A Hat in Time.description: Hat Kid's default color palette in A Hat in Time is inspired by Spyro's color palette.

A Hat in Time features a Brewing Hat flair that makes it resemble Vivian's hat from Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door, as well as color palettes with the color scheme of Princess Peach and Wario. The "Virtual Kid Costume" makes Hat Kid take on the visual style of Super Mario 64, with A Hat in Time Time Rift areas inspired by Super Mario Sunshine; while The Snatcher mentions Luigi in one of his quips in the Death Wish DLC; there are several other minor references to Mario.

A Hat in Time features a color palette with the color scheme of Link from The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker named "Forest Critter", while one of Hat Kid's idle animations is based on Link's victory animation.

In the chapter "Murder on the Owl Express" in A Hat in Time, a TV in the VIP Lounge shows a video game very similar to the title screen of Metal Gear Solid, while a trophy/achievement is named after Punished Snake from Metal Gear Solid V: Phantom Pain.

The "Cookie Dough" color palette in A Hat in Time is inspired in Remix 3 of Rhythm Heaven Fever.
The Train Rush movie poster in A Hat in Time parodies the poster of Blade Runner.

A Hat in Time features a color palette with the color scheme of Niko from OneShot named "Margin of Night", referencing the game's main artist and musician Nightmargin, while an official mod features Niko's clothing and The Sun as an ability.
A Hat in Time features a color palette with the color scheme of Sash Lilac from Freedom Planet named "The Freedom", while an official mod features Lilac's Headpiece and the Dragon Cyclone ability.

An outline of Raz from Psychonauts can be found on the floor of the attic in Vanessa's Manor, a bonus sticker could also be obtained in an update if you owned A Hat in Time and Psychonauts 2 on Steam, the C.A.W. Agents in A Hat in Time are inspired by the G-Men in Psychonauts and an official mod features Raz's Goggles and a PSI-Power ability.

SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS features Phoenix Wright, Mia Fey, Miles Edgeworth and Franziska von Karma as character cards.
The English language version of Ace Attorney: Justice for All features a reference to the Zelda TV show.
The English language version of Ace Attorney: Justice for All features references to Lord of the Rings.
The English language version of Ace Attorney: Justice for All features a reference to Terminator II.
A wallpaper based on Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Justice for All can be obtained in Chick Chick Boom.

The name of the fictional country Borginia appears to have been reused from the Borginian Republic, a fictional country mentioned in Dino Crisis; while characters resembling Regina, Gail and Rick from Dino Crisis appear in episode 10 of the Ace Attorney anime's 2nd season.
Phoenix Wright's clothes can be bought in Pico Sim Date 2.
Episode 3 of the Sayonara, Zetsubou-Sensei anime features an allusion to the Psyche Lock from the Ace Attorney series.
The Lucky Star episode "There is Substance in 2-D" features a reference to Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney.
The English language version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Trials and Tribulations features a reference to the line "This is Sparta" from 300.
The English language version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Trials and Tribulations features a reference to the line "Spoony Bard" from Final Fantasy IV.

The English language version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Trials and Tribulations features a reference to Metal Gear Solid. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney 5 - Dual Destinies features both dialogue and visual references as well.
The English language version of Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney features a reference to Doctor Who.

The "Lawyered Up" path in Escaping the Prison includes a spoof of the Ace Attorney series' trial scene gameplay, with a stick figure Phoenix Wright (later renamed Felix White to avoid copyright issues) serving as counsel.
Characters dressed as Phoenix Wright, Winston Payne and Dick Gumshoe appear in Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective.
Phoenix Wright and Miles Edgeworth make an appearance in She-Hulk's ending in Marvel vs. Capcom 3 and Wright is selectable in Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3.

In the bonus chapter in Nazo Waku Yakata, the living mannequin doll puts on an Apollo Justice head, and later the main character arrives at a courtroom with the judge and Phoenix Wright making cameos.
The list of generic monickers in Dragon's Dogma features "Maya", "Miles", "Pearl" and "Missile" as possible monickers.
Minna to Capcom All Stars and Street Fighter × All Capcom feature characters from Ace Attorney.
Professor Layton vs. Ace Attorney is a crossover between the two series.
Franziska von Karma, Maya Fei and Kay Faraday from Ace Attorney appear in Onimusha Soul as part of the "Capcom Heroines" limited event.
Phoenix Wright, Miles Edgeworth, Franziska von Karma, Maya Fey and other Ace Attorney characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom.
A remix of the Maya Fei - Turnabout Sisters Theme is featured in CROSS×BEATS, while the Ace Attorney 5 remix of "Pursuit" is featured in CROSS×BEATS REV.
Sora tries to interrupt a court hearing using Ace Attorney(Objection theme),The judge in the animé is similar to the game's judge
There's an allusion to the Ace Attorney series in chapter 81 of the Shokugeki no Soma manga.
The comic Plok: The Exploding Man features a reference to Ace Attorney.
Random Encounters has made an Ace Attorney Musical.
As part of a special collaboration event, Puzzle & Dragons featured characters from the Ace Attorney series.
Phoenix Wright is a party member in Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure; the game also features a music track from the Ace Attorney series.
DLC costumes based on Sengoku BASARA characters are featured in the Japanese version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice.
Art books of Ace Attorney appear in the backgrounds of Dead Rising 4, a poster of Ace Attorney: Spirit of Justice is a collectible in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.

DLC costume sets based on Phoenix Wright, Maya Fey, Miles Edgeworth and Franziska von Karma are featured in Monster Hunter Explore, while a Felyne costume based on Phoenix Wright is featured in Monster Hunter XX.
The Avian Attorney is a reference to Ace Attorney.
Phoenix Wright, Maya Fey, Miles Edgeworth and Godot from Ace Attorney are part of a collaboration event in the game LINE Rangers.
Phoenix Wright from Ace Attorney is a playable character in Puzzle Fighter.
A Psyche-Lock from Ace Attorney appears in episode 12 of Pop Team Epic.
Characters from Ace Attorney appear in Dragon Poker as part of a special collaboration.
TEPPEN update 3.2 added characters from the Ace Attorney series.
Ace Attorney is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
A Miles Edgeworth costume appears as a free cosmetic in Among Us.

Ace Combat.description: Ace Combat features images of Pac-Man on billboards, while Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Pac-Man; Ace Combat 2, Ace Combat 5, Ace Combat 6 and Infinity also feature minor references.

Ace Combat 2 features the sister of Reiko Nagase as a selectable pilot, and she also returns in later episodes, while organizations from Ace Combat 3 appear as sponsors in Ridge Racer V and Ridge Racer 6; there also are other minor references between the two series.
A parody of Ace Combat 2 called "Ace Wombat 2" is featured within Segagaga.
In Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail advertising Ace Combat 4.
Smash Court Tennis Pro Tournament 2 features organizations from the Ace Combat series as sponsors.
The beta of New Space Order featured organizations from Ace Combat 3: Electrosphere.
Ace Combat 2 is included in NamCollection.
The Special Flag from Rally-X appears as an item in Ace Combat Zero: The Belkan War.
The setting of the United Galaxy faction in New Space Order featured organizations from Ace Combat 3: Electrosphere.
Ace Combat 6 features a reference to Gears of War.

Ace Combat 6, Assault Horizon, and Infinity feature aircraft paints based on THE iDOLM@STER. The third game expanded the collaboration by including emblems and nicknames based on THE iDOLM@STER characters and songs.
The "Dragon Busters" Squadron from Ace Combat 6: Fires of Liberation is named after Dragon Buster.

The fictional CFA-44 Nosferatu multirole fighter aircraft from the Ace Combat series can be found in the scenario campaign mode of Tekken 6, while various aircraft from the series appear in the Twilight Conflict stage in Tekken 7; additionally Ace Combat: Assault Horizon and Infinity feature aircraft paints based on Tekken; the latter also included emblems and nicknames.

Taiko no Tatsujin: Portable 2 and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Ace Combat series, while Ace Combat Infinity featured emblems from the Taiko no Tatsujin series for a limited period of time.

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 features the XFA-27 from Ace Combat (here called "Ace-con") as a guest player; Kei Nagase and the X-02 Wyvern (called "Ace") were also added in January 2016 in Famista Dream Match; additionally Famista 3 and its sequels include players called "Air-con", "Ace Combat" or other variations.
A map of the Ace Combat world is featured in the Battlefield 4: Second Assault map Operation Métro.
Camilla from Ace Combat Infinity humes the main theme of Mappy during a mission; the game also features nicknames and emblems based on the series.

Bacuras from Xevious started appearing in the Co-Op Mission "Tokyo Martial Law" from Ace Combat Infinity as part of a collaboration event, with Xevious-themed emblems being handed out at a later date; while city structures in Ace Combat 3: Electrosphere resemble the Andor Genesis from Xevious.

The Sword Art Online II anime features references to Ace Combat. Ace Combat Infinity fetures emblems and nicknames based on Sword Art Online: Hollow Realization as part of a limited collaboration event.

The "Quox Armored Battalion" from Ace Combat 6: Fires of Liberation is named after an enemy from The Tower of Druaga, while Ace Combat Infinity features emblems and nicknames based on The Tower of Druaga obtained through Speical Supply tickets.

Ace Combat Infinity features nicknames and emblems based on Galaxian, Galaga and Gaplus gained through Special Supply tickets, while music from the unrelesead Galaxian Heroes was featured in the compilation soundtrack Ace Combat Infinity & Series Music Best.
Ace Combat 6: Fires of Liberation features a building's lights in the shape of a Pooka from Dig Dug in Mission 14, while Ace Combat Infinity features emblems and nicknames based on Dig Dug.
Ace Combat Infinity features emblems based on characters from Soulcalibur Lost Swords as part of a collaboration event.
Ace Combat Infinity features modified aircrafts named and colored after characters from Area 88, as well as nicknames and emblems, as part of a limited collaboration event.

Question Blocks and Power Stars from the Mario series appear in Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy +, and are used to unlock aircraft themed after Nintendo characters, including Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach and Bowser.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Donkey Kong.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features compatibility with the Super Smash Bros. amiibo.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Link from Skyward Sword and Zelda from Twilight Princess.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Samus from Metroid: Other M.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Fox from Star Fox 64 3D.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed Captain Falcon from F-Zero X.
Ace Combat Infinity features emblems based on God Eater 2 Rage Burst and God Eater Resurrection as part of two limited collaboration events.
A parody video game version of Ace Combat titled "Base Combat" appears in Episode 1 of Gamers!.

As part of a limited collaboration event in Ace Combat Infinity for the release of Godzilla-VS, Godzilla and Mechagodzilla would appear in the Tokyo Martial Law Co-Op mission, the event also handed out emblems and nicknames based on the game.
Scanning Olimar's amiibo unlocks a Pikmin-themed aircraft in Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy +.
Ace Combat Infinity features an emblem based on the main character sprite from Baraduke as a Special Supply ticket reward.
Ace Combat Infinity features emblems and nicknames based on Pixels as part of a limited collaboration event.
Ace Combat Infinity features emblems and nicknames based on Doko Demo Issyo as part of a limited collaboration event.
There's a minor reference to Ace Combat's Belka country in the 8th volume of No Game No Life.

The Red Baron and Blue Max aircrafts from Sky Kid were unlockable Special Aircrafts during a limited time tournament event in Ace Combat Infinity, there are several other minor references to the series in Ace Combat 04, 5, 6 and Infinity.
Ace Combat Infinity features emblems and nicknames based on Digimon World -next 0rder- as part of a limited collaboration event.
The R-C01 from the cover of Air Combat appears in Astro's Playroom. A costume based on a pilot from Ace Combat can be found in Astro Bot.
Planes from Top Gun: Maverick appears in Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown as DLC.

The Mystery Gang meet the Addams Family in the New Scooby-Doo Movies episode "Wednesday is Missing".
Mario meets Fester from The Addams Family in the 1989 flyer, Catch the Title Wave. The Addams Family is mentioned in the Swedish dub of the Super Mario Bros. Super Show episode "Mommies Curse".

Fester meets Ryu from Ninja Gaiden in the 1989 flyer, Catch the Title Wave.

In I'm Alan Partridge, a The Addams Family VHS is shown.

The Angry Video Game Nerd talks about Fester's Quest in the episode "Nintendo Power", and reviews it along the Genesis game The Addams Family in the next episode.
Addams Family is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Caught in the Act", while Morticia is mentioned in the episode: "Snip".

Adventure Quiz: Capcom World features Mobi-chan from Side Arms.
The Adventure Quiz series features characters from Kamen no Ninja Hanamaru.

Adventure Time.description: Lady Rainicorn is similar to Haku's dragon form.
Characters from Adventure Time appear in Fusionfall.
In the episode "Slumber Party Panic", a zombie says "Gimme some sugar, baby", quoting Ash Williams from Army of Darkness. Jake's possessed arm from "Bad to Worse" is a reference to Evil Dead II.
There's a reference to Back to the Future in the Adventure Time episode "Memories of Boom Boom Fountain".
A shadow of Batman appears in the Adventure Time episode "City of Thieves". "Holly Jolly Secrets Part II" features a reference to Batman.
The episode "City of Thieves" from Adventure Time feature sound effects from Looney Tunes.
The Adventure Time episode "The Witch's Garden" feature references to Beauty and the Beast.
The title card for "What is Life?" is a reference to Up.
In "What is Life" from Adventure Time, Finn plays a game that is similar to Galaga.
The Adventure Time episode "Dungeon" feature references to Dungeons & Dragons, and there's later references to the series.
Finn and Jake's Battle in the episode "The Duke", references Kenshiro and Shin's battle.
Jake turns into a balloon that resembles Bubbles from Angry Birds in the episode "His Hero".
The title card for "It Came from the Nightosphere" is a reference to a scene from E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial.
Marceline wears Freddy Krueger's sweater in "It Came from the Nightosphere".
In the season 2 episode "Loyalty to the King", Ice King's Nice King appearance is similar to Mister Rogers.
The Adventure Time episode "Crystals Have Power" features a reference to The Princess Bride.
In "Crystals Have Power", Tree Trunks uses her ears to fly which references Dumbo.
An advertisement for Adventure Time is in Poptropica, which allows the player to meet some of the characters.
TKO: Titanic Kungfubot Offensive features a robot based on Finn from Adventure Time, while Jake The Dog appears as part of several of Finn's attacks.
One scene from the episode "The Other Tarts" parodies Who Framed Roger Rabbit.
In the episode "The Chamber of Frozen Blades", there a scene that parodies the cafe scene from Despicable Me.
The Adventure Time episode "The Chamber of Frozen Blades" feature references to Naruto.
There is a reference to Hulk in the episode "The Silent King" from Adventure Time.
In "Guardians of Sunshine" Finn's eyes transform into Pong.
"Guardians of Sunshine" feature sound effects from "Mega Man".
Bomba is a parody of Bob-omb. The Adventure Time episode "Beautopia" features a reference to Mario.

In the episode "Susan Strong" from Adventure Time, the hatch and title card depicting Finn and Jake looking down it are references to Lost. The Lub Glubs from the episode "Beautopia" are similar to the Smoke Monster from Lost.
The episode "Mystery Train" feature sound effects from The Six Million Dollar Man.
The bears in the episode "Belly of the Beast" resemble the Care Bears.
Adventure Time is parodied in the MAD sketch "Avenger Time".
In "Morituri Te Salutamus", when Finn asks the Fight King for a bigger sword, he says the phrase "Finish him!" the same phrase as in the classic fighting series Mortal Kombat.
Blastronaut resembles Samus Aran
Fionna, Cake, and Gumball riding on Lord Monochromicorn and singing in the season 3 episode "Fionna and Cake" spoofs Aladdin".
In the season 3 episode "Fionna and Cake", Fionna's ball gown is a carbon-copy of Princess Serenity's gown from Sailor Moon.

In "Fionna and Cake" from Adventure Time, the ball scene where Fionna and Gumball meet up again, his immeadiate laughter after she states her presence sounds similar to Phil Ken Sebben's infamous laugh from Harvey Birdman: Attourney at Law.
The mask BMO wears in the episode "The Creeps" resembles the bear mask from The Shining.
In season 3 episode "From Bad to Worse" Science's cage is labeled "TS-19."
In the episode From Bad to Worse, a blue-colored Scorpio symbol can be seen in the background inside one of the Candy Castle's rooms. A reference to Homestuck.
In the episode Beautopia, when Susan leaves the Fish People, she says "I'll be back" which is a quote by Arnold Schwarzenegger in the Terminator movies.

In the episode No One Can Hear You, the fact that Stag's lair is down in the sewer (where he meets his demise), the imagery of the balloons Jake wears, and the haunting snippets of carnival music that play are references to It.

In the episode The New Frontier, the scene in which Jake tells Finn to let him go is a parody of the scene in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusadein which Indiana's father tells him to let go of the Grail.

In the Adventure Time episode The New Frontier, the title is a reference to Star Trek. In the intro of the original series of Star Trek, the narrator says "Space, the final frontier." Mr. Spock appears in a poster in Holly Jolly Secrets Part II.
In Holly Jolly Secrets Part I, when the title shows, the design and outline of the title references to A Charlie Brown Christmas.

In Holly Jolly Secrets Part II, Finn's outburst of "What does it mean?" when trying to decipher the Ice King's secrets refers to a catchphrase of Jack Skellington from the movie The Nightmare Before Christmas.
In the episode Paper Pete, when Pete showed Finn the Teddy Bear Joke Book, the characters on the cover resembles Yogi Bear, Boo-Boo and the Ranger from Yogi Bear.
In the episode Incendium, when Jake is fighting the second Iron Owl, his attack resembles one of Monkey D. Luffy's attack Gomu Gomu no Ono (Gum Gum Battle Axe in English) in One Piece.
In the episode Incendium, BMO's game is a parody of Excitebike.
In the episode Incendium, the Iron Owls resemble Bubo from Clash of the Titans.
In Hot to the Touch, the sticker on the right arm of Finn's robot suit resembles the cutie mark on the My Little Pony character Rainbow Dash. The unicorn sticker on his back also has a similar mane.
In Five Short Graybles, BMO wanting to be real is similar to the story of Pinocchio.
In Five Short Graybles, Princess Bubblegum's mouth movements and manner of speech when saying the word "cheese" mimics the character Wallace from Wallace and Gromit.
In the episode Hug Wolf, the table in the library where Jake found the book has a symbol like the Millennium Eye from Yu-Gi-Oh!. The episode Card Wars features a reference to Yu-Gi-Oh.
The episode Princess Monster Wife features a reference to Frankenstein.

In the Adventure Time episode Princess Monster Wife, the family watching TV and sitting on the couch is a reference to The Simpsons. The Simpsons episode Monty Burns' Fleeing Circus has a couch opening which is referencing the Adventure Time opening.
In the episode Princess Cookie, the sign in the hospital saying "You're Special!" has a reference to the book in the post-apocalyptic Fallout 3.
The episode Card Wars features a reference to Pokémon. In the episode Joshua and Margaret Investigations, a Poké Ball can be seen in Margaret's weapon room.
In the episode Card Wars from Adventure Time, BMO saying "B-Mo chop!" is a reference to the manga series Soul Eater in which several characters do the same thing.
The episode Sons of Mars features a reference to 2001: A Space Odyssey.
In the Adventure Time episode All the Little People, the little people and their interactions are similar to the video game The Sims.
Issue 17 of the Adventure Time comic features a reference to The Legend of Zelda.
Finn and Jake make a cameo in the episode Leela and the Genestalk.
Roblox sponsored Adventure Time with clothing and accessories.
An episode of Adventure Time can be seen playing in the episode All Aboard Who's Coming Aboard.
Ice King appears in a flashback in the Axe Cop episode "No More Bad Guys".
Monopoly: Adventure Time Collector's Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
Ian dresses as Finn the human in The Adventure Time Adventure.

A character dressed like the Ice King from Adventure Time appears in the season 2 episode See You There from Regular Show. The Maximum Glove from the Regular Show episode Video Game Wizards appears as an item in Adventure Time: Time Tangle. Mordecai from Regular Show appears in the Adventure Time episode Ketchup. The Adventure Time/Regular Show comic is a crossover between both series.
The Annoying Orange comic "Adventure Lime" is a parody of Adventure Time.
Munchkin Adventure Time is a format crossover between the two series.

The episode "Say Uncle" features a list of names of Cartoon Network characters. One of those names is Finn;characters from Adventure Time are seen in the audience while Uncle Grandpa hosts "The Grampies";in the episode "Cartoon Factory" a cut out of Jake the Dog as well as a poster for a parody of Adventure Time can be seen.
The episode "Say Uncle" features a list of names of Cartoon Network characters. One of those names is Finn.

The Adventure Time Universe appears in Lego Dimensions.

Cloud Strife's sword appears in the Adventure Time episode Jermaine.
Geometry Dash features a skin based on Finn from Adventure Time..

In the episode Jelly Beans Have Power, during the climactic fight, when Princess Bubblegum is transported to Chatsberry, he says "I can open the door for you, but you have to step through it yourself." This is verbatim what Morpheus says to Neo in The Matrix: "I'm trying to free your mind, Neo. But I can only show you the door. You're the one that has to walk through it."

The Lost Cases of Ooo is a crossover episode between Villainous and Adventure Time. Finn's sword can be seen in the Villainous short "The Portrait of Evil". Characters from Adventure Time briefly appear in "The Lost Cases of Boxmore". Many other villain orientation videos use clips from Adventure Time. The Villainous game Maldad Mecanica features enemies based on Finn and Jake, Hunson Abadder appears in a group photo in The Lost Cases of the Future, the Ice King appears in one of the Villainous Comics strips and Gunther appears in Trap-ical Resort.
Jake the Dog and Princess Bubblegum Pop! Vinyls appear in Love, Simon.
In the episode Temple of Mars, King Man calls Jermaine a "cowardly dog". A reference to Courage the Cowardly Dog.
Bloons Adventure Time TD is a crossover between the two series.

In the episode: "Return to the Nightosphere", during the first recording of the Nightosphere, a creature floats by that looks similar to a Ghast from Minecraft. Lumpy Space Princess appears in "FINALMENTE MOSTREI MINHA MÃE!!! O CARTOON ME CONTRATOU?".

Princess Bubblegum's crown, a small sword, and a Night Sword appear in the shop. There is also a BMO large box skin, Finn's flute long plank, Fionna's crystal sword short and long planks and a Lumpy Space Princess anvil skin in the shop.
Finn and Jake appear in a crossover trailer for Immortals Fenyx Rising.

Cheers is mentioned several times throughout Fionna and Cake.
Flapjack, Bubbie, and Captain K'nuckles make an appearance in the Fionna & Cake episode "Prismo the Wishmaster".

Angry Video Game Nerd.description: The first episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of Castlevania II: Simon's Quest; he then reviews many games from the series in the four-part "Castlevania" episode; he also reviews the unofficial game Castlevania II: Simon's Quest - Redaction in the eposode "Desert Bus".
The third episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the NES game The Karate Kid.
The fourth episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the NES game Who Framed Roger Rabbit and he also plays it in the episode "Back to the Future Re-Revisited".

The fifth episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the NES game Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, while the eighteenth and nineteenth are a review of the movie Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III; he then completes the review of the NES game in the episode "Back to the Future Re-revisited".
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews various Back to the Future games in the episodes "Back to the Future" and "Back to the Future Re-revisited".
The eighth episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of Wally Bear and the NO! Gang.
The Angry Video Game Nerd episode "Top Gun" is a review of two Top Gun games; he also plays the NES Top Gun in the episodes "The Power Glove", "NES Accessories" and "Back to the Future Re-Revisited".
The eleventh episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of Double Dragon III.

The Angry Video Game Nerd plays Super Mario Bros. in the video "The Anger Begins" and references the series in many episodes of the series, then reviews Mario's Tennis, Mario Clash, Super Mario Bros. 3, Hotel Mario, Mario is Missing, Mario's Time Machine and Mario Paint in various episodes of the series.
The twelfth episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the NES game Friday the 13th.
The thirteenth episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the NES game Nightmare on Elm Street.
The sixteenth episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the Sega Master System game Rocky; he also reviews Rocky Super Action Boxing in the episode "Double Vision: Part 2".

Animal Crossing.description: Balloon Fight is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Forest and its revisions.
Clu Clu Land is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Forest, with Clu Clu Land D added in its revisions.
Golf is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Forest and its revisions.
Pinball is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Forest and its revisions.
Tennis is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Forest and its revisions.

Rupees from the Zelda series appear in Animal Forest and later games in the series, while Wolf Link, Medli, Ganon and Epona appear in Animal Crossing: New Leaf when scanning Zelda amiibo. Hyrule is also mentioned in various Animal Crossing games while Linebeck is mentioned in New Horizons and there are other minor references as well.
An Arwing from the Star Fox series appears as an item in all Animal Crossing games.

Animal Forest and its sequels mention locations from the Mario series; the downloadable content pack Animal Crossing × Mario Kart 8 for Mario Kart 8 includes elements from the Animal Crossing series; there also are Mario-themed clothes and furnitures in the series as well as other minor references.
Animal Forest and its revisions mention a location from Golden Sun.

The Pokémon Pikachu console makes an appearance in Animal Forest and its sequels; one of the designs in the Animal Crossing e-Reader cards is based on the Pokéball; various Pokémon-themed items appeared in Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp during a special event.
Baseball is featured as an unlockable playable game in Dobutsu no Mori+ and its revisions.
Ice Climber is featured in Dobutsu no Mori+ through special means and in Animal Crossing by scanning the respective e-reader card.
ExciteBike is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Crossing.
Soccer is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Crossing.
Animal Crossing, Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp and Animal Crossing: New Horizons were reviewed by T.O.M. and S.A.R.A. on Toonami.
Elements from the Metroid series appear in many Animal Crossing games as clothes and furnitures.
Music from the Animal Crossing series is featured in Daigasso! Band Brothers.
Files based on Animal Crossing were obtainable by completing a level in UPIXO in Action: Mission in Snowdriftland.

Super Smash Bros. Brawl features a stage, an item and an Assist Trophy from the Animal Crossing series; Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U also feature the Villager as a selectable character, returning in Ultimate alongside Isabelle.
Captain Rainbow features a reference to K. K. Slider from Animal Crossing
The Gold Watering Can from Animal Crossing is an obtainable item in Kirby Super Star Ultra; one of the designs in the Animal Crossing e-Reader cards is based on Kirby.
Puppet versions of Nintendogs are featured in Animal Crossing: City Folk.
The Blue Falcon from F-Zero appears as a forniture item in Animal Crossing: City Folk and New Leaf.

Captain Olimar sends a letter to the player during a special event in the PAL version of Animal Crossing: City Folk. Additionally Animal Crossing games feature items based on the Pikmin series, while scanning Animal Crossing amiibo in Hey! Pikmin, makes the figures appear in the game.

In a DLC for the European version of Animal Crossing: City Folk, Little Mac sends a letter and a gift to the player's character; Punch-Out!! Featuring Mr. Dream is also featured as an unlockable playable game in Dobutsu no Mori+ and its revisions.
Animal Crossing: New Leaf features a reference to the Mother series.
Animal Crossing: New Leaf features a music track originally from Luigi's Mansion.
Animal Crossing: New Leaf features a shrine based on Totoro.
Nintendo Land features a minigame based on the Animal Crossing series.
Mii Plaza includes two Puzzle Swap puzzles based on Animal Crossing games.
Style Savvy: Trendsetters features downloadable clothes based on Animal Crossing: New Leaf, while Girls Mode 3 and 4 feature costumes based on Animal Crossing, unlocked by Animal Crossing amiibo.

Animal Crossing.game: No Matter How I Look at It, It's You Guys' Fault I'm Not Popular!
Animal Crossing.description: The Animal Crossing artstyle is parodied in the WataMote anime episode "Since I'm Not Popular, the Weather's Bad".
There is a reference to Animal Crossing in Tomodachi Life; a few sounds in Tomodachi Life are recycled from Animal Crossing: New Leaf.
A Gyroid from Animal Crossing appears in "MINE THE DIAMOND".
Nintendo Badge Arcade features badges based on the Animal Crossing series.
At the end of the episode "Open Book", there's an Animal Crossing GameCube video game case in Steven's room.

A Felyne appears in Animal Crossing: Happy Home Designer by scanning a Monster Hunter Stories amiibo; additionally Monster Hunter 4G/Ultimate features downloadable outfits based on Isabelle and Mister Resetti from the Animal Crossing series.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumete - Tomodachi Daisakusen! features compatibility with the Animal Crossing amiibos, unlocking a song and two costumes from the series.
The leaf from Animal Crossing: New Leaf, Reese's head and hair, Isabelle's hair, a Molly skin, a Stitches skin and fossil ball skin appear in the shop.
Animal Crossing: New Leaf includes the minigame Animal Forest Panepon/Animal Crossing Puzzle League as well as Lip's clothes and wand, added with the Welcome amiibo update.
Volleyball appears in the Disk Writer furniture item in Animal Crossing: New Leaf - Welcome amiibo!.
Scanning a Hello Kitty amiibo card in Animal Crossing: New Leaf and New Horizons unlocks Hello Kitty themed furniture.
Scanning a Cinnamoroll amiibo card in Animal Crossing: New Leaf unlocks Cinnamoroll themed furniture.
Miitopia features costumes based on Animal Crossing characters, obtainable by scanning the respective amiibo.
Poochi & Yoshi's Woolly World features Yoshi designs based on Animal Crossing characters, unlocked by using the respective amiibo.
Animal Crossing is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Things Look Bad For The Streepster".

Splatoon squids can be collected in an event in Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp; Animal Crossing: New Leaf also features Splatoon-themed items and furniture and the character of Cece cosplays as Callie from Splatoon.

Ant-Man.description: Ant-Man (Hank Pym) and the Wasp (Janet Van Dyne) are founding Avengers members. Ant-Man (Scott Lang, Eric O'Grady), Wasp (Nadia Van Dyne), and Stature have also been members of the Avengers.
Hulk appears alongside Giant-Man in Tales to Astonish #59.
Ant-Man appears in Rom #58 and #59.
Yellowjacket appears in the Marvel: Ultimate Alliance series, with Wasp as a playable character in Marvel Ultimate Alliance 3: The Black Order.
Tigra appears in Ant-Man & Wasp #1 and Unstoppable Wasp (Vol. 2) #7, #9.
Ant-Man makes a cameo appearance as part of Hawkeye's Level 3 Hyper Combo in Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3.
The Wasp appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #41.
A pinball table based on Ant-Man was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX 2 that features characters from the series.
There is a toy of Thomas the Tank Engine in the Ant-Man movie.
The Quantum Realm from the Ant-Man series of movies is based on the Microverse from the Micronauts series but Marvel couldn't get the rights from Hasbro to use it.
Ant-Man is parodied in "How Ant-Man Should Have Ended".
Ant-Man is playable in Disney Infinity 3.0.
Ant-Man appears in Thunder Brother and the Real H.E.R.O.E.S. of Hollywood.
Ant-Man is a playable character in Marvel Strike Force.
Ant-Man is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Tenant Disassociation”.

In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get Ant-Man-themed gear and spawn characters from the series.
Them! is shown on TV in the Ant-Man & The Wasp.
Black Panther appears in Ant-Man & The Wasp Vol. 1 #5.
Ant-Man appears in Fortnite.
Cards based on characters from Ant-Man in Marvel Snap.
Ant-Man is mentioned in the Rick and Morty episode: "JuRicksic Mort".

The Marvel Studios series of Lego Minifigures includes Goliath and Echo.
Ant-Man and the Wasp appear in Godzilla Destroys the Marvel Universe #2.
A building named after Janet Van Dyne appears in Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.

Antarctic Adventure.description: Penta makes an appearance in Konami's Ping Pong.
Penta from Antarctic Adventure appears as an item in Moero TwinBee: Cinnamon-hakase o Sukue!.
Penta from Antarctic Adventure is a hidden character in Nemesis 2.

Penta from Antarctic Adventure makes a cameo in Konami Wai Wai World and Wai Wai World 2, and later becomes a playable character in the first game's mobile port; he also appears in Wai Wai Bingo, Wai Wai Jockey and Wai Wai Pocker.
Characters from Antarctic Adventure are prominently featured in the Parodius series, while the character of Pentarou is the son of Penta and Penko.
Penta from Antarctic Adventure is a playable character in Hai no Majutsushi.

Purchasing a cartridge item at a store in Ganbare Goemon 2 turns certain enemies into Pentarou from Antarctic Adventure. Goemon and Ebisumaru are seen playing Antarctic Adventure in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigenjou no Akumu OVA.
Penta appears sleeping if there's no player 2 playing in Hexion.
Antarctic Adventure is included in Konami GB Collection Vol. 3.
Konami Krazy Racers features a race track based on Antarctic Adventure and several cameos from Penta, while Krazy Kart Racing features Pentarou as a selectable racer.
The character of Mohan from Frogger's Journey: The Forgotten Empire and Frogger: Ancient Shadow is based off Penta from Antarctic Adventure.
Penta from Antarctic Adventure is playable in Airforce Delta Strike.
Dance Dance Revolution: Mario Mix includes a track from Antarctic Adventure.

Pentarou is selectable in New International Track & Field.

The monster "Penta" from Monster Retsuden Oreca Battle references Antarctic Adventure.
Antarctic Adventure puzzles are featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.

Characters from Isekai Quartet appear in Ao Oni Online.

Tejirof in Aoi Sekai no Chushin de is based on Tetris.

Ape Escape.description: A Pipo Ape, Pirate Ape, and Red Shorts Ape all appear in Monster Rancher 4.

The Japanese and European versions of Everybody's Golf 4 feature a Pipo Monkey as an unlockable caddie. Monkeys dressed as Hugo and Emily from Everybody's Tennis Portable appear in PlayStation Move Ape Escape.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumare! Matsuri da!! Yondaime features a music track from Ape Escape.
The "Snake vs. Monkey" minigame in Metal Gear Solid 3 features the apes from Ape Escape, while Solid Snake from Metal Gear makes an appearance in Ape Escape 3.

In the Japanese version of Ratchet & Clank: Up your Arsenal, by entering a code you can unlock a wearable Pipo Suit for Ratchet to wear. Also in many versions of Ape Escape 3, a Ratchet picture can be seen when entering a cheat-code, as well as a monkey wearing Ratchet costume, with a small version of Clank jetpack to fly around and a replica model of the RYNO.
A trio of Pipo Monkeys challenge Toro to a battle in Doko Demo Issyo: Let's Gakkou; Toro and his friends appear hidden throughout the levels of Saru! Get You! Million Monkeys.
A monkey dressed as Jak appears as an unlockable racer in Saru! Get You! Pipo Saru Racer, driving a machine based on the Zoomers from Jak II.
A monkey costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet. A monkey dressed as Sackboy appears in PlayStation Move Ape Escape.
A monkey dressed as Kulche appears in PlayStation Move Ape Escape.
A monkey dressed as a Hatapon appears in PlayStation Move Ape Escape.
A monkey dressed as Sly Cooper appears in PlayStation Move Ape Escape.
A monkey dressed as Wizel the White Knight appears in PlayStation Move Ape Escape.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features Spike from Ape Escape as a playable character.
A PlayStation 4-exclusive DLC bomberman from Super Bomberman R (added in Ver.2.2) known as "Pipo Monkey Bomber" is based off the Pipo Monkey from Ape Escape.
Two bots that reenact Ape Escape appear in Astro's Playroom. Costumes based on various characters from Ape Escape can be found in Astro Bot.

Devolverland Expo features a poster based on Ape Out.
The Big Ape and Baby Ape from Ape Out appear in Devolver Tumble Time.
The Ape from Ape Out will be an assist in Fraymakers.

Apex Legends.description: Apex Legends is a spin-off of Titanfall.
Pathfinder has a skin based off of BD-1 from Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order. Several Star Wars themed charms have also been made avaliable.
Mirage's Strike a Pose finisher recreates a scene from Tim Burton's Batman.

One of Revenant's rare Death Totem animations will have him peform the Summoning: Impure World Reincarnation jutsu from Naruto. Wattson's Legendary Lightning Spirit skin from the Saviors "Gaiden Themed Event" is based on Naruto.
One of Revenant's rare Death Totem animations will have him peform a move similar to Enchantress' transformation in 2016's Suicide Squad.
Pathfinder's Kneeslapper skydive emote recreates the Tin Man's dance from 1939's The Wizard of Oz.
Caustic's kill quip from the Season 7 Battle Pass is a quote from The Princess Bride.
A charm of a Head Crab from Half-Life could be obtained for the Steam release of Apex Legends.
Charms of Potato GLaDOS and a Companion Cube from Portal could be obtained for the Steam release of Apex Legends.

A Nessie plush from Apex Legends can be found in Medal of Honor: Above & Beyond. Additionally, a charm of Manon from Medal of Honor could be obtained in Apex Legends for the launch of Medal of Honor: Above & Beyond. A charm of Sarge was also avaliable for EA Play members.
A charm of Faith Connors from Mirror's Edge could be obtained in Apex Legends by EA Play members.
Charms of the Male and Female Shepard from Mass Effect could be obtained in Apex Legends for the release of Mass Effect Legendary Edition.
Apex Legends is parodied in multiple Siege Tales episodes.
A charm of Dr. Hakim from It Takes Two could be obtained in Apex Legends by EA Play members.
A charm of a Highland Ravager from Dragon Age could be obtained in Apex Legends by EA Play members.
A charm of Isaac Clarke's helmet from Dead Space could be obtained in Apex Legends by EA Play members.
Cosmetics based on Apex Legends appear in FIFA 22 as part of a special collaboration.
Loba's Legendary Supreme Lupin skin from the Saviors "Awakening Collection Event" is based on Ultraman.
Horizon's Legendary Atom Heart Mother skin from the Saviors "Awakening Collection Event" is based on Gypsy Danger fromPacific Rim.
Seer's Legendary Envious Attitude skin from the Saviors "Awakening Collection Event" is based on the Green Ranger from Power Rangers.

Mad Maggie's Legendary Non-State Actor skin from the Saviors "Awakening Collection Event" is based on Godzilla, while Ash's Legendary Existential Threat skin is based on the MUTO from Legendary Pictures' MonsterVerse.
Octane's Legendary Sea Legs skin from the Saviors "Gaiden Themed Event" is based on Luffy from One Piece.
Mirage's Legendary Marked Man skin from the Saviors "Gaiden Themed Event" is based on Deku from My Hero Academia.
Bangalore's Epic Soldier of Justice skin from the Saviors "Gaiden Themed Event" is loosely based on Sailor Moon.
Crypto's Epic Strength and Power skin from the Saviors "Gaiden Themed Event" is based on Goku from Dragon Ball.
In season 2 of Pop Team Epic Popuko and Pipimi play "Poppex Legends" in episode 10, a parody of Apex Legends.
Apex Legends includes several cosmetics based on Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, including Materia items and a Mythic Buster Sword weapon.

Arkanoid.description: Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Doh's Island") based off Arkanoid, with several enemies and DOH as the final boss. DOH is also a boss in Bubble Bobble Part II and Parasol Stars; Bub, Bob and Drunk are among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, while Round 79 in Bubble Bobble and "TV Machine" Round D-7 in Bubble Symphony references Arkanoid; Round 31 in Arkanoid Returns, Zone C-4 and Zone Beta in Arkanoid DS, Round 04L in Arkanoid Plus!, Round B-2 in Arkanoid HD and Round 98 in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders contain references and two wallpapers from the series are unlockable in DS.

Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Doh's Island") based off Arkanoid, with several enemies and DOH as the final boss; Bubby is one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
A mini boss that takes the appearance of DOH appears in Megablast.
The Vaus from Arkanoid is a preset ball in the Ball Edit Mode from the Sharp X68000 port of Cameltry, while a wallpaper based on Labyrinth is unlockable in Arkanoid DS.

Stage 6 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Arkanoid and features a playable Vaus; while Stage 5 in Arkanoid is patterned after an invader alien and Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders is a crossover between both franchises.
One of the players in the "Taito Planets" team from Super Kyuukyoku Harikiri Stadium 2 is named "Arkanoid", after the series.
The Arcade original and Nintendo DS Turn It Around feature Arkanoid as one of its minigames, Furu Furu Park also features an Arkanoid minigame.

A block based on Arkanoid is playable in Blocks That Matter.

The Vaus from Arkanoid is a DLC character in Elevator Action Deluxe, while the Spy from Elevator Action appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, and Stage 141 in the game is patterned after the spy.
Angry Birds Space features a level based on Arkanoid.
The paddles from Arkanoid appear among the videogame characters in the movie Pixels, while the Pixels version of the Invader is an event character in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Nico from Spica Adventure appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.

Ptolemy from The Fairyland Story appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, while Round 41 in the MSX port of The Fairyland Story makes reference to Arkanoid and Zone β-5 in Arkanoid DS bears resemblance to Ptolemy. Arkanoid - Eternal Battle features a The Fairyland Story background as DLC.
Tiki from The NewZealand Story appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.

Arkanoid - Eternal Battle features a Chack'n Pop background as DLC.

The spy Dubbelosix in Asterix and the Black Gold is an homage to Sean Connery and his role James Bond. Additionally, the character Surreptitius, head of Caesar's secret service, resembles Bond's boss M.

The famous dance is parodied in Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra.

In one scene in Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra, General Chorus is seen from behind in a dark helmet and black cloak reminiscent of the character of Darth Vader from the Star Wars franchise. This scene is further enhanced by the fact that the original science fiction soundtrack, "Imperial March", plays during this scene. The allusion is perfected when he announces the attack of the Roman Empire with the words "if the Empire is attacked, the Empire strikes back". When Brutus and his right hand, Pasunmotdeplus, enter Docteurmabus' workshop in Asterix at the Olympic Games, Pasunmotdeplus finds a lightsaber and has nothing better to do than try it out immediately, accompanied by the typical hissing noises from the films, and destroy the interior. In Asterix and Obelix: God Save Britannia, Caesar tries to trick Asterix by telling him that he is his father, followed by heavy breathing.
The alien character Toon in Asterix and the Falling Sky resembles Mickey Mouse.
The superclones in Asterix and the Falling Sky resemble Superman. In the film Asterix: The Secret of the Magic Potion, a centurio flies in a similar manner to Superman after drinking the magic potion

Neo Nyamco-dan, Gilgamesh also appears in Hippari Mappy Daisakusen and Touch the Mappy with 80's Dot Stars; while Mappy is featured in one of the action arts in Dungeon RPG: Druaga Daifugo no Tou.
The Special Flag and Lucky Flag from Rally-X are usable items in The Quest of Ki; the Special Flag also makes a minor appearance in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga.
Princess Ki from Babylonian Castle Saga is a selectable character in the Japanese version of Rock 'n Ball.
The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of Gilgamesh and Ki from The Tower of Druaga.
Ki from The Tower of Druaga is a secret bonus character in Tinkle Pit and she appears on the hi-score screen, and the game features an obstacle based on the series' Blue Crystal Rod.
A picture of Gilgamesh and Ki from Babylonian Castle Saga can be seen in in the "Hyper Glyder" event from Mach Breakers: Numan Athletics 2.

The Tower of Druaga appears in the background of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64, while Gil and Ki appear as players in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match with Druaga also appearing in the Rivals team in Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Gil", "Ishita" and "Ki".

"RT The Tower of Druaga" is one of the racing teams in Rave Racer, while "Ishtar" and "The Return of Ishtar" are car brands and "Druaga", "Quox's" and "Gil&Ki" are part manufacturers, Type 4 features a Tower of Druaga trophy and enemy cars in Ridge Racer 3D sport emblems of Gil, Ki and Quox.

Gilgamesh's armor, sword, shields and the Blue Crystal Rod are featured in Tales of Phantasia and several later games; The Tower of Druaga and Druaga itself appear as part of an EX dungeon in the PlayStation version of Tales of Destiny, and both reappear in Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon and Tales of the World: Narikiri Dungeon 3; Gilgamesh from Tower of Druaga is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, and as a costume in the Narikiri Dungeon sub-series alongside Ki, while the Quox dragon appears as an enemy in Tales of Legendia; Gilgamesh's armor is available as a DLC costume in Tales of the World: Material Dungeon.

The Tower of Druaga is featured in Namco Museum Vol. 3, including an appearance of Druaga himself. The game is also featured in Battle Collection, DS, Mini Player and Namcot Collection, and Gilgamesh appears in the intro for Vol. 3 and Encore.

The Blue Crystal Rod is unlockable in console versions of Soul Edge and SoulCalibur II, SoulCalibur III and SoulCalibur IV, and the Red Crystal Rod is unlockable in console ports of SoulCaibur II. Nightmare and Soul Edge appear as cards in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga. Sophitia received a bonus costume based on Princess Ki in console ports of SoulCalibur II, and Gilgamesh's helmet and sword are available as custom items in SoulCalibur III.
The Tower of Druaga attraction appears in the background of the Amusement Park stage in Tekken 3.
The Tower of Druaga is featured in Namco History Vol.2.
Floor 29 in Neo Babel Mode from Tower of Babel Arrange features moving pixel art of Ki and the Wizard enemy from The Tower of Druaga in the background.

Valkyrie, Sandra and Sabine are playable characters in Sugoroku Adventure: The Tower of Druaga, Valkyrie is playable in Druaga Online: The Story of Aon and appears as a Creature card in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga.

Taira no Kagekiyo appears as a creature in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga, while the default name for the 2nd player in Genpei Toma Den: Computer Boardgame is "Girugame", after Gilgamesh from The Tower of Druaga.
Dr. Don from Point Blank appears as a creature card in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga, while an image of Gilgamesh appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.
Clovis from Dragon Buster appear as a creature card in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga, and his sword is an equipment card.
Gilgamesh and Ki from The Tower of Druaga are selectable characters in Family Tennis Advance.
Babylonian Castle Saga characters appear in Namco Super Wars.
Ki from The Tower of Druaga makes a cameo appearance in Klonoa Heroes: Densetsu no Star Medal.

Mr Driller Drill Land features a stage titled "Hole of Druaga", including cameos from enemies, Gilgamesh and Ki; Mr. Driller Ace features two stages named after the series, "Quox Ruins" and "Druaga Ruins", the latter including depictions of Druaga.

Music from Tower of Druaga is featured in the Taiko March song, debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin DOKI! Shinkyoku Darake no Haru Matsuri, while music from Tower of Druaga and The Quest of Ki is featured in the Namcot Medley debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10; Taiko no Tatsujin 7 and later games also feature music tracks from Tower of Druaga.

There's a recreation of one stage from The Tower of Druaga in the area "Detourne the Mystical Garden" from Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean, and several Magus cards are based on the series.
The Nightmare of Druaga: Fushigi no Dungeon is a format crossover using gameplay elements from Mystery Dungeon.
A song from Tower of Druaga is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
Namco × Capcom features characters from The Tower of Druaga.
QuickSpot features one puzzle image using The Tower of Druaga sprites.

The Xevi language from Xevious is featured as the language of Aon in Druaga Online: The Story of Aon, while a picture of a Terrazi enemy from Xevious appears in the Museum area of The Return of Ishtar.
The Tower of Druaga characters and one location appear in Party Land.
Arino plays The Quest of Ki in episode 54 of GameCenter CX, The Tower of Druaga as the special challenge in the 5th DVD release and The Return of Ishtar in the 19th season 2-hour special.

A remix of The Tower of Druaga is included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 01, a remix of The Return of Ishtar is included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04 while a Tower of Druaga Arcade cabinet appears in episode 17 of THE iDOLM@STER anime.
Momo makes a cameo appearance in episode 1 of The Tower of Druaga: the Aegis of Uruk, while a Crab Fencer appears in Dungeon RPG: Druaga Daifugo no Tou.

Tanks based on Gil and Druid Ghost appear in Tancle.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of Ki from The Tower of Druaga with Gilgamesh assisting the player.
Some levels of Noby Noby Boy feature The Tower of Druaga characters.
3D Dot Game Heroes features loading screens based on the Babylonian Castle Saga.
Gilgamesh and Ki from Tower of Druaga appear as summons in Keroro RPG.
Gilgamesh, Ki and several enemies and bosses from the Babylonian Castle Saga games appear in Namco Chronicle.
A Ki costume from The Tower of Druaga is unlockable in Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha A's Portable: The Gears of Destiny.
The Tower of Druaga is one of the games added to Namco Arcade.
A sprite from The Tower of Druaga appears in Pac-Man's taunt in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U; Gil from Tower of Druaga also appears as a downloadable Mii costume.

The "Quox Armored Battalion" from Ace Combat 6: Fires of Liberation is named after an enemy from The Tower of Druaga, while Ace Combat Infinity features emblems and nicknames based on The Tower of Druaga obtained through Speical Supply tickets.
A cat version of Gilgamesh is featured in Cat Busters as part of a Namco Catalog IP collaboration.
Characters from The Tower of Druaga appear in The Knight of Avalon during the first Namco collaboration event.
Sprites from the Babylonian Castle Saga appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.

Band Stars.description: Band Stars contains The Glee Pack which contains the characters from Glee.
Band Stars contains The Pitch Perfect 2 Pack which contains the characters from Pitch Perfect.
The Fruit Ninja stage was added to Band Stars in celebration of Fruit Ninja series' 5th anniversary.

Banjo-Kazooie.description: Banjo is selectable in Diddy Kong Racing; Tiptup makes appearances in Banjo-Kazooie and Banjo-Tooie; The cancelled Diddy Kong Pilot was remade into Banjo-Pilot.
Banjo's head appears mounted over a fireplace in Conker's Bad Fur Day; Banjo-Kazooie and Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts also feature references to the Conker series.
Bottles from Banjo-Kazooie is featured in the comic Super Mario in Aloha Hawaii; Mario is referenced in Banjo-Tooie.
Characters from the Banjo-Kazooie series appear in "Freeze Frame" and other N-Gang episodes.
Musical instruments from Banjo-Kazooie can be seen in Donkey Kong 64; there also are minor references to the Donkey Kong series in Banjo-Kazooie and Banjo-Tooie.
Posters of Jet Force Gemini appear in Banjo-Tooie.
A frozen Sabreman clutching the Wulf Amulet makes an appearance in Banjo-Tooie.
Banjo-Tooie features two first person zones based on maps from the multiplayer mode of GoldenEye 007.
The Perfect Dark logo appears on a fridge in Banjo-Tooie and Joanna Dark is mentioned in the Tower of Tragedy quiz.
Banjo-Tooie and Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts feature references to Mr. Pants.
Star Fox Adventures features a character possibly based on Kazooie.
Roysten from Banjo-Kazooie makes an appearance in Grabbed by the Ghouls; there also are other minor references between the two series.
Kameo: Elements of Power features a reference to Banjo-Kazooie, while Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts features a reference to Kameo.
Characters from the Banjo-Kazooie series appear in Viva Piñata as statues; Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts also features references to the Viva Piñata series.
In Odd Pirates, when Cosmo becomes an ostrich, he shoots eggs in a similar way Kazooie launched them.
The Lord of Games' face is drawn after the Pong game.
Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts features a reference to the Halo series.

Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts features a reference to the Killer Instinct series, while Rash's "Rarewear" accessories in the 2013 Killer Instinct game include Banjo's shorts, a Jiggy tattoo, and a backpack based on the Lord of Games' face.
Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts features a reference to the Battletoads series.
Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing with Banjo-Kazooie features Banjo and Kazooie as a single Xbox 360 exclusive racer.
Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing with Banjo-Kazooie features Banjo and Kazooie as an Xbox 360 exclusive racer.
Stealing the Diamond features a reference to Banjo-Kazooie, while the Clawpack used in Infiltrating the Airship is similar to Kazooie from Banjo-Kazooie.
In the Dick Figures episode: "Modern Flame War 3", there is an achievement named "Banjo & Kazoo Player", referencing Banjo-Kazooie.
JonTron reviews Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts.
Skin Pack 1 in the Minecraft Legacy Console and Bedrock Editions features skins based off characters from 'Banjo-Kazooie, along with the Minecraft 2nd Birthday Skin Pack.
In the Video Game High School episode "The N64" a character plays the game over theme from Banjo-Kazooie on a banjo.
A team consisting of characters from games by Rare including Banjo-Kazooie appears in #IDARB.
Rare Replay includes Banjo-Kazooie, Banjo-Tooie and Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts as playable games.
Yooka-Laylee is a spiritual successor to Banjo-Kazooie.
Sea of Thieves features a figurehead and some graffiti based on Banjo and Kazooie.
The Seal the Deal DLC added a costume named "Hiking Shorts Costume", based on Banjo's outfit.
Banjo Kazooie is mentioned in Trover Saves The Universe.
Banjo-Kazooie is parodied in Console Wars.
Banjo and Kazooie appear as a playable character in Super Smash Bros Ultimate, with a stage based on the series.
Banjo-Kazooie is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "Perfect Cell Vs Banjo-Kazooie".
A drawing of Banjo-Kazooie can be seen in Jack's room in Lego Hidden Side's "Night of the Harbinger".
A couple of musical horns that can be unlocked in Forza Horizon 5 play "Spiral Mountain" from Banjo-Kazooie.
Two characters that look like Banjo and Kazooie appear in "Surf & Turf Wars (Part 1)".
"Something About Banjo-Kazooie" is a parody of Banjo-Kazooie.
In the Smiling Friends episode: "Gwimbly: Definitive Remastered Enhanced Extended Edition DX 4k (Anniversary Director's Cut)", Gwimbly and his game are loosely based on Banjo-Kazooie.

Baraduke.description: The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of a Paccet from Baraduke.
A Paccet from Baraduke is a secret bonus character in Tinkle Pit.
Baraduke is included in Namco Museum Vol. 5, with actual appearances of a Paccet and Octies; the game is also featured in Namco Museum Virtual Arcade.
Mr Driller 2 reveals Susumu Hori's mother to be the protagonist of Baraduke Tobi "Kissy" Masuyo; she and a Paccet make later appearances in the series.
Namco × Capcom features Toby "Kissy" Masuyo from Baraduke as a playable character.
A tank based on Paccet appears in Tancle.
One of the players in the Bandai Namco team in Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax is based on the alien Octi from Baraduke.
Tobi Masuyo from Baraduke is a playable character in Namco Chronicle, with Octies appearing as enemies.
Kissy from Baraduke appears in strip #7 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic.
A sprite from Baraduke appears in Pac-Man's taunt in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U.
Ace Combat Infinity features an emblem based on the main character sprite from Baraduke as a Special Supply ticket reward.
Toby and Baraduke are mentioned in Ready Player Two.

The "Baganns" enemy in Baraduke resembles Pac-Man, and the layout of Floor 39 resembles the maze from Pac-Man, while Baraduke is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash and a theme with characters from Baraduke appears in Pac-Man 99.

The Tales of Arise artifact "Broken Machine Gun" is the firearm used by Kissy in Baraduke, while there are pictures of a Paccet from Baraduke in the Dragonis of Tales of Destiny, Tales of Vesperia features a Kissy figurine and Elle's backpack in Tales of Xillia 2 is designed after the Paccet enemies and includes a Kissy charm.

Barbarian (Titus).description: Barbarian is released in Japan as Warrior Blade: Rastan vs. Barbarian, changing one of the characters to Rastan while keeping the other elements the same.

Darbie is a parody of Barbie.
Barbie and Ken appear in the Toy Story Franchise.
Barbie is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episodes: "Future Malcolm" and "Mrs. Tri-County".

Ken is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Menzies".
Barbie is mentioned in the Modern Family episodes: "Flip Flop", "Clean for a Day", "Basketball" and "Kids These Days".

An alternate version of "Chiwawa" was released on the Just Dance Unlimited service featuring Barbie as the dancer.
Costumes based on Barbie could be obtained in Love Nikki as part of a special collaboration.

Caddy reviews "Barbie Explorer" and "Barbie Race and Ride" for the PS1.

Characters from Barbie appear in Stumble Guys as part of a special collaboration.
The TMNT interact with Barbie in a promo for Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem.

The Godfather is mentioned in Barbie.
There is a Preminger costume.

Barbie is mentioned in the Ted episode: "Just Say Yes".
The Nostalgia Critic reviews Barbie in the Nutcracker.
The Game of Life: Barbie Edition is a format crossover between the two series.

Barry Steakfries.description: Age of Zombies was originally going to be a part of Halfbrick Fridays series, and PSP version of Halfbrick Rocket Racing has digital billboards advertising it. A Blast Off Jetpack from Jetpack Joyride is based on the rocket from Halfbrick Blast Off. Jetpack Joyride Racing is a spiritual successor to Halfbrick Rocket Racing.

Fruit Ninja and Barry Steakfries series contain references to each other and crossed over multiple times. Sensei makes a cameo appearance in Age of Zombies and interacts with Barry in episode 60 of Barry Vlog. Barry Steakfries appears in Fruit Ninja Classic as part of a special crossover event.

Barry Steakfries is a playable character in Raskulls and an avatar in Magic Brick Wars. The King appears as one of the clothing sets in Jetpack Joyride, interacts with Barry in several episodes of Barry Vlog, and is playable in Jetpack Joyride Racing.
Jetpack Joyride features the Gravity Suit from Gravity Guy.
Skin Pack 4 in the Minecraft Xbox 360 and Xbox One Editions features a skin based off Barry Steakfries.
Chaingun Jetpack in Skiing Fred references Machine Gun Jetpack from various Barry Steakfries games.
Peter Venkman, Slimers and Proton Pack appeared in Monster Dash in 2014. Various characters and locations from Ghostbusters appeared in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event in 2021.
Various characters and locations from Back to the Future appeared in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event.

Mecha Micro vehicle skin for Profit Bird in Jetpack Joyride is directly based on Micro from Fish Out of Water!. Olympus makes an appearance in Jetpack Joyride Rock Opera - Shirt Sleeves and Jetpack Joyride 2 as part of the Fish Tank jetpack.

Barry Steakfries is a playable character in Dan The Man. Professor Brains also appears as an antagonist in Fright Zone DLC. The game had a crossover event with Jetpack Joyride in celebration of its 10th anniversary. Dan and Josie appear as clothing sets in Jetpack Joyride and are playable in Jetpack Joyride Racing.
Barry Steakfries, Zombie T-Rex, Flash and Scientist are playable characters in Battle Racing Stars.

Colossatron appears as a vehicle skin for Mr. Cuddles in Jetpack Joyride, described  by the game as a 1/4 scale replica of the original, created after Scientists played Colossatron: Massive World Threat on their phones. Rick Dalton appears in one of the trailers for Monster Dash reporting on the outbreak. Colossatron's destroyed head appears at the beginning of Neontropolis levels in Jetpack Joyride 2.
Characters and locations from Metal Slug appear in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event.
Characters and locations from Star Trek appear in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event.
Characters and locations from 1987 TV Series appear in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event.
Characters and locations from Masters of the Universe appear in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event.

Bartender.description: Taiko no Tatsujin Mobile features a music track from Bartender.

Baseball (Nintendo).description: Mario and Luigi are the leaders of the teams in the Game Boy version of Baseball.
Baseball is featured as an unlockable playable game in Dobutsu no Mori+ and its revisions.
A microgame version of Baseball is featured in WarioWare: Twisted!
NES Remix includes challenges based on Baseball.
Pitcher & Batter from Baseball appear as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Baseball can be seen in Animation vs. Super Mario Bros.

Basil of Baker Street.description: A toy of Dumbo appears in The Great Mouse Detective.

Characters from The Great Mouse Detective make an appearance in the House of Mouse episode "Donald's Lamp Trade" and in the comic page "lost t op gouden loepie"; Ratigan is also referenced in the House of Mouse episode "Rent Day".
The Goldbergs episode "Mini Murray" features Beverly attempt to have Adam see The Great Mouse Detective.
Professor Ratigan from The Great Mouse Detective is mentioned in the Descendants book The Isle of the Lost.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews “The Great Mouse Detective”.
Basil of Baker Street appears in the credits for Wish.
Cards based on The Great Mouse Detective appear in Lorcana.

Bastion.description: Turrets from Portal appear in Bastion after starting a New Game +.
You can find The Kid in Archer's Pass trapped until you free him.
The narrator of Bastion is in Dota 2.
Red has toys of a Windbag and a Cael Hammer in her apartment.
Dino Run DX features a hat based on The Kid.
Hades features a hammer based off of the hammer from Bastion.
The Kid from Bastion appears as a skin in Riverbond.

Baten Kaitos.description: Pac-Man is referenced as an ancient hero in several Magnus found in the Baten Kaitos series.
The Magnus "Wonder MOMO" in Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean is based on Wonder Momo.
The Magnus "Rare Action Figure" in Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean is based on KOS-MOS from Xenosaga.
Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean features a reference to Tekken.
The top-most room in Zosma Tower from Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean is modeled after the Q*bert game.

There's a recreation of one stage from The Tower of Druaga in the area "Detourne the Mystical Garden" from Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean, and several Magus cards are based on the series.
There's a reference to Donkey Kong in Baten Kaitos Origins.
Sagi and Milly from Baten Kaitos appear as spirits in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate. A music track from Baten Kaitos Originsis also featured in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.

Batgirl.description: Batgirl made her debut in Detective Comics #359.
Batgirl appears in Justice League of America #60.
Batgirl appears in The Joker: Devil's Advocate HC.
Batgirl/Ghost is a crossover between the two series.
Batgirl is a playable character in Injustice: Gods Among Us as a DLC character.
Scribblenauts Unmasked features Aruna from the Batgirl series as a spawnable character.
Batgirl appeared in Puzzle & Dragons during the DC Universe collaboration event.
Lily dresses up as Batgirl in the Modern Family episode: "Halloween 4: The Revenge of Rod Skyhook".
Batgirl appears in "How Wonder Woman Should Have Ended".
Batgirl has been a subject for Death Battle!.
Batgirl and Elektra appear on  a variant cover of Deadpool/Batman.

Batman.description: Catwoman made her debut in Batman #1.
Joker made his debut in Batman #1.

Both series frequently interact. the first time being in World's Finest Comics magazine which included team-up stories from both series. The first in-universe link between both series would be in the Adventures of Superman radio show which occasionally co-starred Batman and Robin.
Batman and Wonder Woman have co-starred in many comics and media together, the first being All-Star Comics #36.

Batman is one of the founding Justice League members. Batgirl (Barbara Gordon, Stephanie Brown and Cassandra Cain), Batman (Commissioner Gordon), Batwoman, Nightwing and Robin (Tim Drake and Damian Wayne) has also been members of the Justice League.
Batman appears in Green Lantern #29.
Robin is one of the founding members of the first Teen Titans team.
Poison Ivy made her debut in Batman #181.

The Green Hornet and Kato appear in the Batman episodes "The Spell of Tut", "A Piece of the Action", and "Batman Satisfaction". Additionally, Batman '66 Meets the Green Hornet is a crossover between the two series.
Chief Screaming Chicken from the 1966 Batman series is a parody of Roaring Chicken from F Troop.
Batgirl made her debut in Detective Comics #359.
Colonel Klink from Hogan's Heroes appears in the Batman episode "It's How You Play The Game".
Lurch from The Addams Family appears in the Batman episode "The Penguin's Nest".
Batman appears in The Flash #175.
Batman and Robin appear in an episode of Sesame Street teaching about how to safely cross the street while trying to catch the joker.

The story in The Brave and the Bold #93 is a crossover between the two series, and the House of Mystery also appears in All-New Batman: The Brave and the Bold #12; additionally a character dressed like Cain appears in Batman #237.

Characters from Batman appear in the The New Scooby-Doo Movies episodes "The Dynamic Scooby-Doo Affair" and "The Caped Crusader Caper" as well as many Scooby-Doo! Team-Up comics and the Scooby-Doo and Guess Who? episode "What a Night, For a Dark Knight!"; characters from Scooby-Doo appear in the Batman: The Brave and the Bold episode "Bat-Mite Presents: Batman's Strangest Cases!"; Shaggy dresses up as Batman in LEGO Scooby-Doo! Haunted Hollywood; Scooby-Doo! & Batman: The Brave and the Bold is part of both series.
The Shadow appears in Batman vol. 1 #253 and #259.
Green Arrow appears in Batman #260.

Roach's "The Cockroach" personality in Cerebus the Aardvark is a parody of Batman, while his "Secret Sacred Wars Roach" personality also has elements of Batman. Additionally, the Cerebus comics Batvark and Cerebus: The Vark Knight Returns are parodies of Batman.
Batman appears in the Dr. Slump chapter "Kids Gone Wild".
Batman vs. The incredible Hulk is a crossover between the two series.
Cyborg appears in Batman and the Outsiders #5.
Batman and Robin are mentioned in a Garfield comic strip on August 27, 1985. Batman's hand appears on the cover of Garfield Vol. 2.
Batman: Year One issue #1 features a Snoopy lamp in one panel.
Bat-Bat, a character in Mighty Mouse: The New Adventures, is a parody of Batman.

In the Calvin and Hobbes comic strip of August 12th 1989, Calvin wonders if he could buy Batman junk.

Batman appears in Deathstroke the Terminator #7.

Following the release of Get Out, various fan theories emerged, including ones linking Get Out to Being John Malkovich. In a December 2017 Vanity Fair interview, Get Out director Jordan Peele discussed these theories. Peele revealed that he and Being John Malkovich director Spike Jonze had discussed the theory, and although the connection wasn't intended, after hearing Jonze's response he now sees both films as set in the same continuity. Peele concluded, "as far as I'm concerned, it's true."

Black Panther.description: Black Panther made his debut in Fantastic Four #52, and would go on to appear in numerous Fantastic Four comics, with him had at one point becoming a member of the Fantastic Four. Additionally, the Fantastic Four and Doctor Doom have appeared in numerous Black Panther comics.

Black Panther/Captain America: Flags of Our Fathers is a crossover between the two series. Additionally, Black Panther appears in various Captain America comics and in Captain America: Civil War, while Captain America appears in Black Panther Vol. 3 #27 and #30 and Batroc the Leaper from Captain America appears in Black Panther Vol. 4 #3-6 and Black Panther (IDW) #5.
Black Panther has been a member of the Avengers, first joining in Avengers #52. The Avengers have appeared in various Black Panther comics.

Black Panther appears in Daredevil #52, #245, #512 and #612, Daredevil Vol. 3 #3, and Daredevil Vol. 4 #7; and appears with Daredevil in Over the Edge #6. Additionally, Black Panther: The Man Without Fear is a continuation of a story that began in Daredevil, and Daredevil appears in Black Panther: The Most Dangerous Man Alive #529.
Captain America appears in Captain Marvel #27.

Spider-Man and Black Panther appear together in Marvel Team-Up #20. Additionally, Black Panther appears in various Spider-Man comics, while Spider-Man appears in Black Panther: The Man Without Fear #516 and Black Panther Vol. 4 #18. Also, Kraven the Hunter from Spider-Man appears in Black Panther Vol. 3 #6 and #7, Rhino from Spider-Man appears in Black Panther Vol. 4 #3-6, and Morlun from Spider-Man appears in Black Panther Vol. 5 #3-6.

Boktai.description: Boktai and the Megaman Battle Network series have had multiple crossovers with eachother. Battle Network 4 features Django at various points, including during a mini-quest to defeat ShadeMan.EXE. in Boktai 2, ShadeMan.EXE becomes a post-game boss. There are also "crossover battles" that can be played by using a wireless adapter to connect to Battle Network 5. Due to declining sales of the Boktai series in the west, English releases began cutting crossovers between games. In Rockman.EXE6 (Battle Network 6) there are various references to Boktai 3 (which never saw an english release). In Lunar Knights, the 4th Boktai game, the Japanese version links with Shooting Star Rockman (Megaman Star Force), allowing players to fight Taurus Fire. Defeating him unlock Omega-Xis as a terrenial to assist the player.

MGS4: Guns of the Patriots allows players to unlock the solar gun and MGS: Peace Walker has a cameo appearance of Otenko, the main character yelling "SUNLIGHT" during their appearance (charging the gun in the former). In the PSP's card-based spinoff AC!D series, there are cards based on Hideo Kojima's other games, including Boktai. There is a mysterious seller in Boktai 2 and 3 that is hinted to be an amnesiac Solid Snake, the main character of MGS.

Merida appears as a playable character in LEGO The Incredibles.
Merida appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Merida from Brave is mentioned in the Descendants book Escape from the Isle of the Lost.
A picture of a location from Brave can be seen on a calendar in Onward.
Merida and Mor'du from Brave are fighters in Disney Sorcerer's Arena.
Disney Magic Kingdoms features characters from Brave.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews the Pixar film ”Brave”.
Characters and items from Brave appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley.
There will be a puzzle in Disney Solitare that shows a scene from Brave.

Characters from Hatsune Miku appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Chain Chronicle appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration and vice versa.
Characters from Brave Frontier appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations and vice versa.
Characters from Tales of Link appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Phantom of the Kill appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration and vice versa.
Characters from The King of Fighters appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Shin Megami Tensei appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Guilty Gear appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Fairy Tail appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Brave Frontier appeared in The Alchemist Code during special collaborations and vice versa.
Characters from My Hero Academia appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Tokyo Ghoul appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Samurai Champloo appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Characters from Trigun appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.

Brave Nine.description: Characters from Destiny Child appeared in Brave Nine as part of a special collaboration.
