Brave Nine.description: Rimuru Tempest from That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime appears in Brave Nine as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from The Legend of Heroes: Hajimari no Kiseki appeared in Brave Nine as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Darling in the Franxx appeared in Brave Nine as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from DJMax Respect appeared in Brave Nine as part of a special collaboration.

BraveStarr.description: Alderaan from Star Wars is mentioned in the BraveStarr episode "Call to Arms".
BraveStarr is mentioned in the Beef episode: "We Draw A Magic Circle".

Braveheart.description: Braveheart is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "The Bully".
In Conker's Bad Fur Day there is a reference to the film Braveheart.
Braveheart is parodied in "How Braveheart Should Have Ended".
Braveheart is mentioned in The Thick of It.
Broheart is based on William Wallace from Braveheart.
Braveheart is parodied in Les Kassos.

Bravely Default.description: Bravely Default is the spiritual successor of Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light and features many of the same elements; additionally Final Fantasy Brave Exvius includes Bravely Default characters, while Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call features downloadable tracks from the game.
Music from Bravely Default is present in Theatrhythm Final Fantasy: Curtain Call and Theatrhythm Final Bar Line. is present in Theatrythm Final Fantasy: Curtain Call.
Characters from Bravely Default appeared in Valkyrie Anatomia: The Origin as part of a special collaboration.
Bravely Default II spirits are featured in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Characters from Bravely Default II appear in Octopath Traveler: Champions of the Continent as part of a collaboration.

Bravest Warriors.description: Bravest Warriors features many references to the Star Trek series.
Chris from Bravest Warriors makes a cameo appearance at the end of the Slamacow video "Advanced Enchanting 101".
The muffin advertises Bravest Warriors at the end of "asdfmovie7".
A toy of Catbug from Bravest Warriors can be found in the episode "Fun Dead".

Bravoman.description: The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of Bravoman and Waya-Hime.
A character resembling Dr. Bakuda/Bomb (named Dr. Bakuta/Bacta) from Bravoman is a minor character in Digital Devil Story: Megami Tensei II, and he makes other references to Bravoman.
Waya-Hime from Bravoman appears on the hi-score screen in Tinkle Pit.
Bravoman is a selectable character in Family Tennis Advance.
Bravoman appears as a playable character in Namco Super Wars.
Taki received a bonus costume based on Waya Hime from Bravoman in console ports of SoulCalibur II.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Appare Sandaime features a music track from Bravoman.
Namco × Capcom features characters from Bravoman.
A diorama machine based on Bravoman can be found in Tales of Vesperia, and a costume of Bravoman is DLC in Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of a Bravoman item with Bravoman assisting the player.
Some levels of Noby Noby Boy feature Bravoman characters.
Bravoman is mentioned in Chapter 6 of High Score Girl.
Bravoman appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.

Famista Online 2010 features Bakuda from Bravoman in the Rivals team, while Pro Baseball Famista 2011, Famista Dream Match and Famista Climax feature Bravoman in the Namco Stars team, with Bakuda, Black Bravo and Pistol Daimyo also appearing in the Rivals team in Climax; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels include players called "Bravoman" and "Waya Hime".
Bravoman and Waya-hime are playable characters in Namco Chronicle, with Pistol Daimyo appearing as an enemy.

Bravoman and Alpha Man appear in strip #2 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic, and then Bravoman makes a cameo in strip #7; Dig Dug makes a cameo in strip #100 of the Bravoman web comic, strip #164 features a Fygar from Dig Dug, several pieces of merchandising and video games related to Dig Dug also appear in other strips and the web series.
Strip #27 from the Bravoman web comic references Batman, while "Bravoman & Alpha Boy" from strip #34 is a straight parody.
The "Bravo the Barbarian" mini-arc in the Bravoman web series is a parody of Conan the Barbarian.
"Bravobots" from strip #32 of the Bravoman web series is a parody of Transformers.
Strip #51 features a reference to "Mrs. Dig Dug", Mr. Driller's mother; while strip #106 features a Mr. Driller video game.
Wonder Momo appears as part of a crossover story in the Bravoman web comic, and makes several cameos in the web series; strip #240 features Waya Hime disguised as Wonder Momo.
Dirk Davies from The Five-Dimentional Adventures of Dirk Davies makes a cameo appearance in strip #81 of the Bravoman web comic.
Valkyrie makes a cameo in strip #100 and #140 of the Bravoman web comic.

Pac-Man and one of his ghost enemies make a cameo in strip #100 of the Bravoman web comic, strip #230 features the ghost Clyde in a cameo as well and costumes and video games related to Pac-Man also appear in other strips; while a theme featuring characters from Bravoman appears in Pac-Man 99.

The Prince from Katamari Damacy makes a cameo in strips #100 and #278 of the Bravoman web comic; the Prince and the King of All Cosmos appear in the episode "Generic Winter Holiday" of the web series.

Klonoa makes a cameo in strip #100 and #222 of the Bravoman web comic, and strips #239/240 feature Alpha Man disguised as Klonoa; Klonoa also appears in the episode "Generic Winter Holiday" of the web series.

The Galaxian spaceship appears in strip #113 of the Bravoman web comic, while the episode "Generic Winter Holiday" of the web series has one of its aliens making a cameo; there are other minor references to Galaxian as well.
The videogame "Bravo Fighter II" from the episode "Couch of Doom" of the Bravoman web series is a parody of Street Fighter II.
Sky Kid makes a cameo in strip #241 of the Bravoman web comic.
Anti-Bravoman from Bravoman is a character in Namco High.

Bravoman appears as a guest character in the final story arc of Mappy: The Beat, while Mappy makes a cameo appearance in the episode "Generic Winter Holiday" of the Bravoman web series; strip #240 features Bravoman disguised as Mappy.
Strip #276 from the Bravoman web comic features a reference to Tekken.
Wagan makes a cameo in strip #280 of the Bravoman web comic, with other references appearing in earlier strips.
A music track from Bravoman is featured in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.

Brawl Stars.description: Various skins for Brawlers based on characters from Clash of Clans appear in Brawl Stars.
The announcement trailer for skins based on LINE appearing in Brawl Stars features characters from both franchises meeting each other.
The Squeakbuster skin for Gale is based on a Ghostbusters outfit, featuring a "No-Ghost" logo parody with the character Squeak.
The Surge Kong skin for Surge is based on King Kong. Promo artwork also shows him climbing buildings just like King Kong.
The B-800 skin for Bull is based on Terminator.
The insert coin to Brawl promo artwork features an arcade machine for the fictional game "Coltra 3".
The insert coin to Brawl promo artwork features an arcade machine for the fictional game "Brockman 7", referencing the Japanese name for the series.

The insert coin to Brawl promo artwork features an arcade machine for the fictional game "Super Megtroid". A poster can also be seen for "Super Surge", referencing a poster for Metroid II: Return of Samus.
The insert coin to Brawl promo artwork features a poster based on the game's dragon symbol.
The insert coin to Brawl promo artwork features a poster for "Spike Invaders", which references the original game's key artwork.
The insert coin to Brawl promo artwork features a poster for "Magnum Special", which references the logo style and a poster for the first game.
Artwork based off The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom's key artwork was released to celebrate the game's release, featuring Bibi with a Triforce head accessory.
The Lunar Janet skin for Janet is based on Usagi Tsukino from Sailor Moon.
The Boy Scout Gus skin for Gus is based on Russell from Up.
Charlie's mastery title is "Amazing" because of her spider-like appearance. Her Amazing Charlie skin is also based on the titular character.
The Toon Spike skin for Spike is based on The Powerpuff Girls art style, including expressions and poses that reference each girl.
The Toon Spike skin for Spike wears shorts that resemble Mickey Mouse's signature shorts. A Hidden Mickey ornament appears in 2024 Brawlidays artwork.
The announcement trailer for Baby Shark cosmetics appearing in Brawl Stars features characters from both franchises meeting each other.
Characters and locations from Godzilla appear in Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Brawl Stars appear in Squad Busters.
Characters and locations from Ultraman appear in the Chinese version of Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.
The Paint Brawl event is based on Splatoon's Turf War mode. Alongside its debut, Splatoon inspired skins of select Brawlers were also released.
Characters and locations from SpongeBob SquarePants appear in Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.
The Rude Lou skin for Lou is based on Eric Cartman.
The Paper Cordelius skin for Cordelius is based on Paper Mario's art style, resembling a Purple Toad.
The Bizarre Maisie skin for Maisie is based on JoJo's Bizarre Adventure.
The Be Less Ash skin for Ash is based on BMO. The Sugarplum Rosa skin for Rosa is also based on the series.
The intro for The Amazing World of Gumball is parodied in a promotional animation for the Starr Toon 2 season.
A promotional animation for the game's Toy Story collab shows Colt dressed as Woody holding back Bibi dressed as Bo Peep, referencing the way Woody does to Sora in Kingdom Hearts 3.
Characters and locations from Toy Story appear in Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.
The Pop-Up Darryl skin for Darryl is based on the game's barrel design.
The promotional animation "Ollie, The King of Starr Park" is a homage to The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air's intro.
A poster for "Brock to the Future" appears in the "Ollie, The King of Starr Park" animation.
A poster for "The Moetrix" appears in the "Ollie, The King of Starr Park" animation.
A poster for "Ferris Buster's Day Off" appears in the "Ollie, The King of Starr Park" animation.
Cards from UNO appear in Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration. The UNO Chester skin for Chester is based off UNO.
Promo artwork for the Ruffesses II skin is based on Indiana Jones.
The Egg Pam skin's profile icon is based on a pose from the character Humpty Dumpty.
Characters and locations from Boonie Bears appear in the Chinese version of Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.
Characters and locations from Neon Genesis Evangelion appear in the Chinese version of Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.
Promo artwork for the Demons Event is based on the HUD menu of Doom.
Characters and locations from Subway Surfers appear in Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration. A Brawl Stars Showdown mode appears in Subway Surfers as part of a special collaboration.
Promo artwork featuring Melodie and Janet in a rap battle is based on Friday Night Funkin'.
Characters and locations from Stranger Things appear in Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.

Brawlhalla.description: Ragnir is an Alternate Skin for Maypul in Rivals of Aether, while Ranno appears as a skin for Wu Shang in Brawlhalla.
Shovel Knight characters and weapons appear in Brawlhalla.
Rayman appears as a playable character in Brawlhalla.
Several Hellboy characters appear as skins in Brawlhalla, the Apocalypse map and the Horde mode are both based on Hellboy.
Finn, Jake and Princess Bubblegum are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.

Garnet, Amethyst, Pearl, Steven and Connie from Steven Universe appear as playable characters in Brawlhalla, Malachite makes a cameo appearance in Brawlhalla, and the Crystal Temple appears as a 1v1 stage in Brawlhalla.
Lara Croft from Tomb Raider appears as a playable character in Brawlhalla; the Temple Ruins map and the Temple Climb game mode are both based on Tomb Raider.
Four Arms, Heatblast, and Diamondhead are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Michonne, Rick, and Daryl are playable crossover skins. Negan and Maggie appear as new playable skins in part 2 of the collaboration with Brawlhalla.
Po, Tigress, and Tai Lung are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Leonardo, Donatello, Raphael, Michelangelo, and Shredder are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Ryu, Chun-Li and Akuma are playable crossover skins. M.Bison, Ken, Sakura, Dhalsim and Luke also appear as new skins in part 2 of the collaboration with Brawlhalla.
Val and Bodvar from Brawlhalla can be found in Growtopia as part of the 2022 UbiWeek event.
Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Ezio appears as a playable character and Eivor appears as a crossover skin in Brawlhalla.
Simon Belmont and Alucard are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Aang, Zuko and Toph from Avatar: The Last Airbender are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Val's hair and Wasteland Ada's hair appear in the shop.
A skin based on Brawlhalla can be found in Hungry Shark World as part of a special collaboration.
Master Chief and the Arbiter appear as playable characters in Brawlhalla.
Devil Jin, Nina Williams, and Yoshimitsu from Tekken appear as crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
SpongeBob, Patrick and Sandy from SpongeBob SquarePants appear as crossover skins in Brawlhalla.

Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, Ahsoka Tano, Darth Vader and Darth Maul from Star Wars appear as crossover skins in Brawlhalla. In the second wave of the collaboration, Han Solo, Chewbacca, Kay, and The Mandalorian appear as playable skins..
Krieg, Lilith and Tiny Tina from Borderlands appear as crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Mega Man, Beat and Rush appear as crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
The Hunter, Warlock and Titan from Destiny 2 appear as crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
Eren, Mikasa and Levi from Attack on Titan appear as crossover skins in Brawlhalla.

Brawlout.description: Juan from Guacamelee! is a playable character in Brawlout.
The Drifter from Hyper Light Drifter is a playable character in Brawlout.
Yooka-Laylee is a playable character in Brawlout.
Travis can wear a Brawlout t-shirt in Travis Strikes Again: No More Heroes.
The Beheaded from Dead Cells is a playable character in Brawlout.

Breadwinners.description: Breadwinners characters are playable in Super Brawl 3.
Breadwinners have many references to SpongeBob.
In the Breadwinners episode Rocket Trouble, the Breadbots' Extermination Mode is a reference to Doctor Who, in which the Doctor's enemies the Daleks keep saying "Exterminate!"
In the episode Rocket Trouble, when Sway3PO says, "Get over here!" and extends his arm to grab SwaySway before delivering an uppercut, it is a parody of Scorpion from Mortal Kombat.
In the episode Rocket Trouble, when SwaySway, Buhdeuce and Ketta jump over the tires in order to hide from the breadbots, the jumping noise made is similar to the one heard in the Mario.
The Brave and the Mold is a pun on Batman: The Brave and the Bold.
In the episode Lost at Pond, the title card is a parody of Jaws.

Breaking Bad.description: The Three Stooges can be seen on TV in the Breaking Bad episodes: "Cat's in the Bag..." and "Hazard Pay".
The Jeffersons is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Cancer Man".
Daddy Warbucks from Annie is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episodes: "Gray Matter" and "Down".
Scarface is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episodes: "Crazy Handful of Nothin'" and "Shotgun", and shown on TV in the episode: "Hazard Pay".

Smurfs are mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "A No-Rough-Stuff-Type Deal".
James Bond is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episodes: "Seven Thirty-Seven" and "Más".
Willy Wonka is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episodes: "Bit by a Dead Bee", "Bullet Points" and "Gliding Over All".
Captain America is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Down".
Lord of the Rings is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Phoenix".
Hank makes a reference to Ferris Bueller's Day Off in the Breaking Bad episode: "ABQ".
In the "Short Fuse" chapter from Angry Birds there is a pig dressed as Walter White.
Walt Jr. and Louis watch Aqua Teen Hunger Force on TV in the Breaking Bad episode: "I.F.T.".
Breaking Bad is mentioned in the English dub of the Highschool of the Dead OVA: "Drifters of the Dead".
Rocky is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episodes: "One Minute" and "Bug".
Darth Vader and the Death Star are mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Kafkaesque".
Tetris is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Full Measure".
Characters discuss Left 4 Dead in the Breaking Bad episode: "Thirty-Eight Snub".
Characters discuss Resident Evil 4 in the Breaking Bad episode: "Thirty-Eight Snub". Breaking Bad is mentioned in Resident Evil: Vendetta.
Characters discuss Call of Duty: World at War in the Breaking Bad episode: "Thirty-Eight Snub".
The Breaking Bad episodes: "Bullet Points", "Crawl Space" and "Hazard Pay" feature clips from Sonic games.
Terminator is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Bug".
Breaking Bad is mentioned in the Community episode "Biology 101".
Mr. Magoo is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Crawl Space".
The A-Team is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Crawl Space".
House is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode "Face Off".
In the Walking Dead episode "Bloodletting", The crystal meth found in Merle's stash of drugs is the same meth produced by Walter White in Breaking Bad.

In the Breaking Bad episode: "Madrigal", one of the fast food restaurants seen at the Madrigal offices is called "Burger-Matic", which is a reference to the film Home Fries, which also featured the burger chain.
A copy of LittleBigPlanet 2 can be seen in the Breaking Bad episode: "Madrigal".
The DVD for Open Season 2 can be seen in the Breaking Bad episode: "Madrigal".
Ratatouille is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Fifty-One".
Star Trek is discussed in the Breaking Bad episode: "Blood Money".
Scrooge McDuck is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Buried".
Jesse Pinkman recieves a Hello Kitty flip phone in the Breaking Bad episode: "Confessions".
Wolverine is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "To'hajiilee".
Hulk is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "To'hajiilee".
Rambo is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "To'hajiilee".
James Bond is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "To'hajiilee".
A DVD copy of Mr. Magorium's Wonder Emporium is seen in the Breaking Bad episode: "Granite State".
On the Breaking Bad complete series DVD box set, there is an alternate ending where it all turns out to be a dream from Hal from Malcolm in the Middle.
Dead Rising 3 features a recreation of Walter White's house from Breaking Bad, including a pizza stamped on the roof and an usable hazmat suit.
Walter White has been a rapper for Epic Rap Battles of History.
The episode "Breaking Dad" from The Thundermans is named after Breaking Bad.
Walter White from Breaking Bad appears in "How Godzilla Should Have Ended".
Breaking Bad is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Hobbit: There and Bennigan's".
Better Call Saul is a spin-off of Breaking Bad.
There are references to Breaking Bad in Zootopia.
Breaking Bad is mentioned in "QUAL É A SÉRIE? ♫ - PARÓDIA "THE NAME GAME"". Any Malu also has a room decoration similar in design to the Breaking Bad logo.
Marcus mentions Breaking Bad in Season 2, Episode 16 of Superstore, “Wellness Fair”.
Breaking Bad is mentioned in the Baywatch movie.
A wanted poster for Walter White from Breaking Bad can be seen in Oh...Sir! The Hollywood Roast.
Characters that look like Walter White and Jesse Pinkman appear in the Camp Camp episode "Cookin' Cookies".
Walter White's house from Breaking Bad can be found in House Flipper.

In Fallout 76, the barrel burial site north of Sugar Grove is a reference to Breaking Bad. It references a scene from the show in which Walter White buries barrels full of money driven by a truck to a remote location in the desert. The skeleton of Walter White can be found there, among other references to the scene from the show.
Badger mentions Miss Daisy in El Camino.
A Battlestar Galactica poster can be seen in El Camino.
Saul Goodman's name from Breaking Bad can be seen on Henry's cellphone in the remastered version of Escaping the Prison.
Monopoly: Breaking Bad is a format crossover between the two series.
Breaking Bad is parodied in Les Kassos.
Breaking Bad is parodied in the Daitomodachi episode "Nessa Hits The Griddy After Ending My Nuzlocke".
The "Chemistry Teacher" face cosmetic in Project: Playtime is a reference to Walter White from Breaking Bad.
Walter White can be seen drawn on a post-it note in the Console Wars episode "DONT JOIN PC MASTER RACE".
Walter White is mentioned in the Rick and Morty episode: "The Jerrick Trap".
Skibidi Toilets based on Walter White and Jesse Pinkman from Breaking Bad appear in "Skibidi Toilet 68".
The "Heisenblast" and "Cap 'N Blast" sprays in Antonblast are based on Walter White and Jesse Pinkman.
Jax makes a reference to Breaking Bad in the The Amazing Digital Circus episode: "Untitled".
Breaking Bad is parodied in the MeatCanyon episode "Walter White's Pregnancy Scare".
A Wayfarer Airlines plane from Breaking Bad appears in the Pluribus episode: "Pirate Lady".

Breath of Fire.description: Chun-Li makes a cameo in Breath of Fire and later with Sakura in Breath of Fire III, while Ryu, Nina, Peco, Teepo and Momo from Breath of Fire III are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Ryu, Chun-Li, Guile and Cammy; Falke got a Katt costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.
Arthur from Ghosts 'n Goblins appears in portraits in Breath of Fire.
"Zenny", the currency from Black Tiger, appears in several games in the Breath of Fire series.
The enemy "Little Ohmu" (Crawler in English) from Breath of Fire is named after the Ohmu from Nausicaä Of The Valley Of The Wind.
The enemy monster "Bill Bull" (Bulla in English) from Breath of Fire is named after an enemy character in Final Fight.
The "Bouncer" enemies from Breath of Fire II are named after characters in Saturday Night Slam Masters.
The Great Bird from Breath of Fire II is named the "Millenium Falcon" in the end credits, a reference to Star Wars.
Two monsters in Breath of Fire II are named after onomatopeias from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure.
Two members of the resistance in Breath of Fire II are named after Mickey Mouse and Peg-Leg Pete.
One of the members of the resistance in Breath of Fire II is named after Donald Duck.
Two members of the resistance in Breath of Fire II are named after Goofy and Max Goof.
Tiga and one of the members of the resistance in Breath of Fire II are named after Tigger and Winnie the Pooh.
Two members of the resistance in Breath of Fire II are named after Chip and Clarice.
One of the members of the resistance in Breath of Fire II is named after Gaston from Beauty and the Beast.
The character Kukuys/Cucuruz and his pet Doan from Breath of Fire III are named after a character in Mobile Suit Gundam. One of Ryu's weapons is named "Heat Shotel".
The technique "Seven Senses" (Celerity in English) from Breath of Fire III and IV references Saint Seiya.
The item "Jigen's Hat" (Artemis Cap in English) from Breath of Fire III is named after Daisuke Jigen from Lupin the Third".
The design and techniques of the boss Stallion from Breath of Fire III references Ultraman.
Two scenes in Breath of Fire III are parodies of the classic "shark approaching" scene from Jaws.
The monster Audrey from Breath of Fire III is named after Audrey II from Little Shop of Horrors.
Characters from Breath of Fire III make cameo appearances in the PlayStation and Saturn ports of Pocket Fighter.
Characters from Breath of Fire are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
The armor "Cyttoraks" (Psychometer in English) from Breath fo Fire IV is named after Cyttorak, the entity who gives power to X-Men villain Juggernaut.
The name of three boss characters in Breath of Fire IV when put together spell out "Joy Mecha Fight".
Auto Modellista features a car sticker of Ryu and Nina from Breath of Fire: Dragon Quarter.
Capcom Black Jack features appearances of Nina from Breath of Fire III.
A character in Power Pro Kun Pocket 7 is named after Nina.
Characters from Breath of Fire make cameo appearances in Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3.
The list of generic monickers in Dragon's Dogma features "Bosch", "Nina" and "Momo" as possible monickers.
Minna to Capcom All Stars and Street Fighter × All Capcom feature characters from Breath of Fire III.
Nina from Breath of Fire appears in Onimusha Soul as part of the "Capcom Heroines" limited event.
Blade Fantasia features the Faerie race and magic spells from the Breath of Fire series.

Nina from Breath of Fire IV is featured as a costume for Annie Greene in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along with her actual moves, while Dead Rising 4 features billboards and art books from Breath of Fire in its backgrounds.

The world of Breath of Fire III is visited in Sonic and Megaman: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Ryu, Nina, Momo, Honey, Peco, Garr and Rei; while a rescuable Reploid in Mega Man X6 is named after Nina from Breath of Fire and Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Mega Man, Roll, Volnutt and Tron Bonne.
The world of Breath of Fire III is visited in Sonic and Megaman: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Ryu, Nina, Momo, Honey, Peco, Garr and Rei.

Breath of Fire 6 features special hunter costumes from Monster Hunter Frontier G, while Frontier G featured costumes of Ryu and Nina from Breath of Fire III; later collaboration events include a Monster Hunter Explore armor set, Rathalos-based weapons, Felyne unlockable character and a special story event in Breath of Fire 6 and a costume set of Ryu and Nina from 6 in Monster Hunter Explore.
Breath of Fire 6 features Madoka and Homura from Puella Magi Madoka Magica: The Movie as part of a special story event, as well as costumes and weapons from the series.
Breath of Fire III enemies Yawn (Foul Weed in English) and Plant42 are named after monsters in Resident Evil, while Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Chris, Jill, HUNK and Claire.
Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Dante, Trish, Vergil and Lady from Devil May Cry, as well as the special weapons Sparda and Force Edge.
Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Morrigan,  Demitri, Felicia and Donovan from Darkstalkers.
Characters from several Breath of Fire games appear in The Knights of Avalon as part of a Capcom limited promotion.
TEPPEN update 3.3 added characters from the Breath of Fire series.

Brickleberry.description: A Kermit puppet appears in a flashback in the Brickleberry episode "Welcome To Brickleberry".
Mario is referenced in the Brickleberry episode "Saved by the Balls".
Tetris is referenced in the Brickleberry episode "Saved by the Balls".
Robocop is mentioned in the Brickleberry episode "Saved by the Balls".
Winnie the Pooh is mentioned in the Brickleberry episode "Squabbits".
V for Vendetta is referenced in the Brickleberry episode "Squabbits".
Cast Away is mentioned in the Brickleberry episode "Dam Show".
In the episode "Paradise PD Meets Brickleberry", The cast of Paradise PD go to Brickleberry National Park.

Bridge Constructor: The Walking Dead is a format crossover between both series.

Bridge Kids.description: Thomas the Tank Engine is mentioned in the Bridge Kids episode “Smokin Butts”.
Goldeneye is mentioned in the Bridge Kids episode “Smokin Butts”.
In the Bridge Kids episode “Halloween”, Fugger is dressed as Morpheus from The Matrix.
Spider-Man is mentioned in the Bridge Kids episode “Halloween”.

Bubble Bobble.description: Monstas and Maitas/Mightas from Chack'n Pop are recurring enemies in the Bubble Bobble series; Chack'n is a recurring character in the Bubble Bobble series having first appeared in Bubble Symphony; he also appears as an item in the original, Memories, Double Shot and Plus! among others, and there are other minor references to him and the series in several Bubble Bobble games.

Bubble Bobble inherits several gameplay elements and many of the same special items seen on The Fairyland Story that'd become recurring in the series, while Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Magical Island") based off the game, with appearances of several enemies and Horned as the area boss, with Ptolemy making a cameo in the Game Boy Color port; Bubble Symphony features Ptolemy as an assist character and she also spawns as an item in Round 57 of Bubble Memories.
Super Qix features images of characters from Bubble Bobble.
The Rainbow Islands series is a spin-off of Bubble Bobble.

Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Doh's Island") based off Arkanoid, with several enemies and DOH as the final boss. DOH is also a boss in Bubble Bobble Part II and Parasol Stars; Bub, Bob and Drunk are among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, while Round 79 in Bubble Bobble and "TV Machine" Round D-7 in Bubble Symphony references Arkanoid; Round 31 in Arkanoid Returns, Zone C-4 and Zone Beta in Arkanoid DS, Round 04L in Arkanoid Plus!, Round B-2 in Arkanoid HD and Round 98 in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders contain references and two wallpapers from the series are unlockable in DS.

The world of Darius is featured as an island ("Darius Island") in Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 and as the setting of Round E ("Sun 'A' Zone") in Bubble Symphony, including appearances of enemies and Electric Fan/King Fossil (former/NES port) and Yamato (latter) as area bosses; the Silver Hawk is also featured as an assist character in Bubble Symphony, spawns as an item in Round 54 of Bubble Memories with Round 63 of Super Mode resembling the Silver Hawk, and Level 86 of the NES port of Bubble Bobble references Darius.
Round 18 Blue in Raimais is patterned after a Zen-chan enemy from Bubble Bobble, while "Raimaiz" is one of the random secret high score screen names in Bubble Symphony.

The world of Kiki KaiKai is featured as an island ("Kiki KaiKai Island") in the NES port of Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 and as the setting of Round B/F ("Kiki KaiKai") in Bubble Symphony, both including appearances of Sayo-chan/Pocky (the latter as an assist character), enemies and Manuke/Rocky as the area boss; Sayo-chan spawns as an item in Round 59 of Bubble Memories, Round 25 of Super Mode references the Puka Puka enemy, and there's an unlockable Kiki KaiKai bubble set in Space Puzzle Bobble.

Bubby from Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 appears in Cameltry holding a 1000 Pts sign if the player reaches the goal with more than 60 seconds on the clock and the ending image from the 4th Plane Master course in the SNES port of Cameltry features Bub and Bob from Bubble Bobble, while its English release On the Ball replaces the Operation Wolf ball with Bub.
A mini boss that takes the appearance of Bub from Bubble Bobble appears in Megablast.
A graffiti of Bub and the Zen-chan enemy from Bubble Bobble appear in the third stage of The Ninja Kids.

The X68000 port of Bubble Bobble features a hidden game titled "Sybubblun", a parody of Syvalion including Bub and Bob redesigned to resemble the eponymous gold dragon and enemies modifed to resemble the game's enemies; while Bubble Bobble Double features "Gald Valion" as one of its bosses.
Enemies resembling Bub from Bubble Bobble appear in The Adventures of Quik and Silva.

The cannon from Space Invaders is an assist character in Bubble Symphony and the series is referenced in "TV Machine" Round D-2, Level 11 of Bubble Bobble and Round 5 of Bubble Memories Super Mode; while the recurring "Invader" enemy is based on the eponymous aliens; Stage 3 and 4 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Bubble Bobble and Rainbow Island respectively and feature a playable Bub in dragon and human form; while he, Bob and Drunk are among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Bob from Don Doko Don is an assist character in Bubble Symphony.

Hipopo from Liquid Kids is an assist character in Bubble Symphony, and he also spawns as an item in Round 55 of Bubble Memories, while the "Water" bubble in the series works similarly to the water bubbles used in Liquid Kids.
The setting of Pu·Li·Ru·La (Raddish Land) is the setting of Round C and G in Bubble Symphony, with Jack O'Colson as the area boss; Mr. Mikata is also one of many assist characters in the game.
"Timegal" is one of the random secret high score screen names in Bubble Symphony.

Bullyparade.description: In one sketch about two boxers in Bullyparade: Episode 1.11, the song Gonny Fly Now is played.

The sub-series "Unser (T)Raumschiff" features parodies of Captain Kirk, Mr. Spock, Scotty, Dr. McCoy and Sulu. These parodies are also part of the films (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 and Bullyparade: The Movie, with the latter parodying the reboot films.
One sketch in Bullyparade season 2, Red Riding Hood does not meet the wolf, but a cat. The two then begin to sing like in Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical.

Darth Vader appears in the Bullyparade sub-series "Unser (T)Raumschiff" and in "Bullys Partnerbörse", where he asks if someone wants to go to the CSD with him. The film (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 features the character Jens Maul who is a parody of Darth Vader, as well as several parodies of the prequel trilogy. Bullyparade: The Movie features a character named King Clone who has an army of clones and is introduced like General Hux in Episode VII, as well as parodies of Han Solo and Chewbacca.
The Bullyparade parodies this franchise.
The name of the "Puder Rosa Ranch" is a parody of the "Ponderosa Ranch".
Der Schuh des Manitu includes a mine cart escape scene similar to that of Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom, as well as a map following the travelling routes of the main characters.
The Shoshone chief Listiger Lurch often holds a white rabbit in his hands, similar to Ernst Stavro Blofeld with his cat.
Hannibal Lecter appears in the Bullyparade sub-series "Bullys Partnerbörse", where he applys lipstick on his mask for carnival.
Der Wixxer uses the well-known quote "Ich bin mit der Gesamtsituation unzufrieden." from Der Schuh des Manitu.
In a space shot in (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 "An der schönen, blauen Donau" is playing.

The display of the time machine (which is also destroyed by a train) in (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 is similar to the display of the DeLorean. The film also includes a frame-to-frame copy of George McFly's punch against Biff. The segment "Zurück in die Zone" in Bullyparade: The Movie is a parody of the first Back to the Future film.
The dialogue between Spucky and Kork in (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 when they have to leave him behind is a parody of the ending of E.T.
The taxi chase scene and the character Rock in (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 are parodies of the film.

In (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1, when Spucky suggests simply painting the damaged taxi pink camouflage, Rock (Til Schweiger) lists his tuning capabilities. This scene is exactly the same as Berti (also Til Schweiger) in Manta, Manta telling the radio reporter about his Opel Manta.
The action sequences are parodied.
The dress and hairstyle of Queen Metapha in the Middle Ages in (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 remind of those of Fiona.
The character Jens Maul has a red light in his eye similar to that of the Terminator. The one-liner of the character Rock is "Ensalada mista, Baby!"
The film parodies the famous scene from Top Gun in which Maverick takes a photo of himself while flying.
The intro scene of (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 is a parody of the series.
Lissi und der wilde Kaiser features a scene in which the Yeti stands on top of a building, looking similar to King Kong.
The characters Tschango and Dr. Schmitz are parodies of Django and Dr. King Schultz.
Like Jack Sparrow and Will Turner in the first film, Abahachi, Ranger and Mary turn around a boat and thus create an air-filled capsule with which they walk along the bottom of a lake.
The character Winnetouch appears dressed similar to Zorro.

Cast Away is mentioned in the Frasier episode "Daphne Does Dinner".
The episode "Splodyhead" from Lilo & Stitch: The Series feature references to Cast Away.
Alex talks to a ball with a hand-painted face in Madagascar.
John Sheppard says "I am pretty sure you cannot hear me, but I do not have a volleyball to talk to, so what the hell" in the Stargate Atlantis episode "Epiphany".
Seeley Booth says "Next thing you know he will be shipwrecked on some island talking to a volleyball" in the Bones episode "Boneless Bride In The River".
In SpongeHenge, the scene where SpongeBob is in a cave hiding from the jellyfish and making a stone companion is a reference to Cast Away.
Clothier says "Being cursed was lonely, so I once made a friend out of leather. I named him Wilson" in Terraria.
Cast Away is mentioned in the Community episode "Competitive Ecology".
Cast Away is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Punctured Jugular".
Cast Away is mentioned in the Brickleberry episode "Dam Show".

A Cast Away dvd is shown in the Always Sunny episode "Gang Squashes Their Beefs".
Cast Away is parodied in Les Kassos.

Garrett mentions Cast Away in Season 2, Episode 10 of Superstore, “Black Friday”.
Idatori reenacts a scene from Cast Away, which Junpei guessed the movie, in chapter 24 of Jujutsu Kaisen.
A person is dressed up as Chuck Noland from Cast Away in the Bojack Horseman episode "Mister Peanutbutter's Boos".
Cast Away is mentioned in Trover Saves The Universe.

Vampires and Lycans from Underworld are mentioned in the Castle episode "Vampire Weekend".
Javier Esposito asks 'Why do you care about some motherfreaking snakes on a motherfreaking plane?' in the Castle episode "Third Man".
American Psycho is mentioned in the Castle episode: "One Man's Treasures".
Avatar is mentioned in the Castle episode "Lucky Stiff".
There is a reference to Saw in the season 4 episode "Cuffed" from Castle.

Castle Corp.description: The wizard appears on the weapon called 'Magic for Dummies' in Castle Corp.
Knights from Castle Corp appear as enemies in Nitrome Must Die, while weapons based on the Dragon Breath and Triple Crossbow weapons from Castle Corp also appear.

You fight the Aliens from "Alien Hominid" in The Spaceship level in Castle Crashers. Alien Hominid: Invasion features references to Castle Crashers.
Blue Castle Crashers is an unlockable character in Meat Boy - Map Pack and Pink Knight is an unlockable character in Super Meat Boy for consoles.

Castle Crashers.game: The 41-Year-Old Virgin Who Knocked Up Sarah Marshall and Felt Superbad About It
Castle Crashers.description: Seth and Sanjay play Castle Crashers in The 41-Year-Old Virgin Who Knocked Up Sarah Marshall and Felt Superbad About It.
In the episode Henchman, Marceline calls Finn a "Castle Crasher" during the party at the Duke of Nuts' castle, which is a reference to Castle Crashers.
Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood features a reference to Castle Crashers in a memory's name.
Skin Pack 2 in the Minecraft Legacy Console and Bedrock Editions features skins based off characters from Castle Crashers, as well as Skin Pack 4 in the Xbox 360 and Xbox One Editions.

The Knight is an unlockable character in BattleBlock Theater. However only for a limited time Giraffey and The Troll were also unlockable. Hatty Hattington from BattleBlock Theater would later become DLC in Castle Crashers.
A Wanted Poster of The Castle Crashers appear in Guacamelee!.
A character based on the peasant from Castle Crashers appears as the gardener in Pico Sim Date <3.
The sandwich option in Fleeing the Complex is a spoof of the Castle Crashers item.
Dino Run DX features hats based on Castle Crashers characters.
The Red and Green Knights makes a cameo appearance in River City Ransom: Underground.
Cards based on Castle Crashers are included in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls Requiem.
Accessories for the Crashers and Kingley as well as a Rammy pet can be obtained as part of the Indie Cosmicube event in Among Us.

Derry, Maine from The Bird and the Album appears in Castle Rock.
Alan Pangborn from The Dark Half appears in Castle Rock.

Cujo is referenced in Castle Rock.
Frank Dodd from The Dead Zone is referenced in Castle Rock.

The Emporium Galorium from Pet Sematary appears in Castle Rock.
Anne Wikens from Misery appears in Castle Rock.

Castle in the Sky.description: A track from Castle in the Sky appears in Karaoke Revolution: Anime Song Collection.
Taiko no Tatsujin Wii: Chogouka-Ban and later games in the series feature a music track from Laputa: Castle in the Sky.
A Laputa Robot appears at the Avengers Tower in Avengers: Age of Ultron.
Maki mentions Castle in the Sky in Extra chapter of Jujutsu Kaisen in Issue 2, 2022 of Weekly Shonen Jump.
Roboco writes a ripoff to Castle in the Sky in Chapter 86 of Me & Roboco.

Castle of Shikigami.description: The character of Sayo Yuuki from Castle of Shikigami is based on Sayo-chan/Pocky.

The PlayStation 2 port of Shikigami no Shiro was first localized as Mobile Light Force 2, with the removal of all story content. Castle Shikigami 2 features a reference to "Mobile Light Force 3" in its manual.
Reika Kirishima from Time Gal is a playable character in Castle of Shikigami III.
In the Japanese version of Castle of Shikigami III, Nagino Ise's backpack features a picture of Bub from Bubble Bobble.

Castlevania.description: Moai heads and the Vic Viper from the Gradius series appear as items in several Castlevania games, while the boss Bat Company from Dawn of Sorrow can assume the form of the giant Moai boss from Gradius.
The cover art of Castlevania II: Simon’s Quest uses art from the Ravenloft module for Advanced Dungeons & Dragons.
Simon Belmont is a playable character in the series.
In episode 3 of the Howard & Nester comic, Nester disguises as Simon and plays through Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
Simon Belmont from Castlevania is one of the opponents in Hai no Majutsushi.
Simon Belmont and Dracula from Castlevania are recurring characters in the Captain N TV show.
GamePro enters the world of Castlevania.
Kid Dracula is a spinoff of Castlevania.

Goemon visits the world of Castlevania in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigenjou no Akumu OVA, Simon Belmont is a playable character in Ganbare Goemon Gaiden 2: Tenka no Zaihō, a vampire hunter look-alike makes a cameo appearance in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu, and Simon's grandfather appears in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigoku-hen manga. Goemon appears as an item in Castlevania: Harmony of Despair.
Zombies Ate My Neighbors features an enemy named "Vlad Belmont the Vampire".
There's a minor reference to Castlevania in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Tournament Fighters for the SNES.

The secret boss Simondo Belmont from Contra: Hard Corps is a parody of Simon Belmont, including the use of a whip and hitting candles for power ups. In Order of Eclessia, the boss Arthroverta is inspired by Shadow Beast Kimkoh from the NES port of Super Contra.
One of the selectable cursors in Tokimeki Memorial is based on Maria Renard, while Tokimeki Idol features a medley of themes from Castlevania.

People dressed like Simon Belmont and Dracula can be seen in "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the Sega CD and later ports of Snatcher, and at one point the main character makes a comment about the gameplay in the first Castlevania.
Sexy Parodius features a stage based off Castlevania, while Aitsu and Koitsu from Parodius make a cameo appearance in Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin and Harmony of Despair.
Richter Belmont from Castlevania is a selectable character in Jikkyō Power Pro Wrestling '96: Max Voltage.

The recurring item "Stone Mask" from Castlevania is a reference to a similar mask in JoJo's Bizarre Adventure. The boss Zephyr from Dawn of Sorrow and Portrait of Ruin has an attack referencing Dio Brando's Time Stop.
Castlevania: The Adventure is included in Konami GB Collection Vol. 1, while Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge is included in Vol. 3.

In Metal Gear Solid, Psycho Mantis can reference Castlevania if a save file for Castlevania: Symphony of the Night is on the memory card. Solid Snake's bandanna and Solid Eye from Metal Gear Solid 4 are hidden items in Castlevania: Lord of Shadows.
A sticker of Alucard from Castlevania can be seen in printstations from Mitsumete Knight R.
Konami Krazy Racers features Dracula from Castlevania as a selectable racer.
The item "Bear Ring" from Castlevania: Circle of the Moon transforms Nathan Graves into Beartank from Rakugakids.
Skulls similar to Crocomire's from Super Metroid can be seen in Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance.

There is a stage called Dracula's Castle which features Dracula, Skeletons, but most important to the series to link these two as type 1 is a Brachyura. The character, Vampire Hunter is unlockable in the game who is similar to Simon Belmont.
Simon Belmont is selectable in DreamMix TV World Fighters.
The first episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of Castlevania 2; he then reviews many games from the series in the four-part "Castlevania" episode.
The Yu-Gi-Oh cards "Infernalvania" and "Vampire Hunter" ("Vampire Killer" in Japan) are references to the Castlevania series.
An outfit based on Leon Belmont can be found in The Sword of Etheria.

The song "Akumajou Dracula Medley" from Dance Dance Revolution Ultramix 3 is a remix of Castlevania themes. Dance Dance Revolution Universe features a remix of the "Vampire Killer" theme. Dance Dance Revolution SuperNOVA 2 features a remix of the "Bloody Tears" theme and background images from the intro of Curse of Darkness.
Haunted Castle was re-released as a part of the Oretachi Gēsen Zoku series.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Castlevania.

Arino plays Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse in Episode 38. He also played the Disk System version of Akumajou Dracula (known as Castlevania outside Japan) later in 2014 as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge, Castlevania: Bloodlines in episode 270 and Akumajou Dracula X: Chi no Rondo (known as Castlevania: Rondo of Blood) in episodes 297 and 298.
The Fedora item from Portrait of Ruin and Harmony of Despair is a reference to Indiana Jones.
There are two techniques in Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin which references techniques from Kinnikuman.
Twinbee appears as an item in three games of the Castlevania series.
Simon Belmont and Trevor Belmont as well as tracks from the Castlevania series appeared multiple times throughout the Pop'n Music series.
Captain S enters the world of Castlevania.
Dracula from Castlevania appears in I Wanna Be The Guy.
Simon Belmont is selectable in New International Track & Field.
The boss Goliath from Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia features references to the Fist of the North Star villain Raoh.
Castlevania is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Maurice Was Caught".
3D Dot Game Heroes features loading screens based on Castlevania and Castlevania 2.
Castlevania: Symphony of the Night is included in Konami Classics Vol. 1.
JonTron reviews Castlevania: Legacy of Darkness.
Shantae: Risky's Revenge features a dialogue reference to one of the obtuse hints in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
Castlevania: Lords of Shadow features a reference to the Zelda series.
The World 2 intro in Super Meat Boy is a parody of the intro from the NES Castlevania.
The Japanese version of Scribblenauts features Alucard from Castlevania as a spawnable object.

A skeleton enemy in Getsu Fuma Den is named Shimon and attacks with a whip, referencing Simon Belmont from Castlevania; while Getsu Fuma and a map based on his game are DLC content in Castlevania: Harmony of Despair.
Kokoro Belmont from Otomedius Excellent is inspired by the Castlevania series.
Rock of Ages features a parody based on the Castlevania series.
When Eve turns to her cursed self the text box and words come out from "Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest" saying "What a Horrible Night To Have A Curse.".
A track from Castlevania can be played in the Sound Voltex series.
Monster Retsuden Oreca Battle features Simon, Alucard, Dracula and Death as playable characters.
The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim – Dawnguard features a display case referencing Dracula's Relics from Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
Frogger: Hyper Arcade Edition features a game mode based on Castlevania.
The item "Red Orb" from Dust: An Elysian Tail is a reference to a similar item found in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
Adventure Time: Hey Ice King! Why'd You Steal Our Garbage?!! features a minor reference to the Castlevania series.
Castlevania: Lords of Shadow - Mirror of Fate features a reference to Luigi.
The fourth season episode "Castle Mane-ia" from My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic is a reference to the Castlevania series.
Kingdom Dragonion featured Simon Belmont and Alucard as playable characters.
The Irate Gamer reviews Castlevania on NES
Alucard has been a subject for DBX.
Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night is a spiritual successor of Castlevania.

A DLC bomberman from Super Bomberman R (added in Ver.1.4) known as "Simon Belmont Bomber" is based off Simon Belmont from Castlevania, while Ver.2.0 added "Dracula Bomber", based on the series' main antagonist, and Ver.2.2 added "Alucard Bomber" and three stages based on the Castlevania series.
"Castlevania" is one themed category of puzzles featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.
"Something About Castlevania" is a parody of Castlevania.
Simon and Richter Belmont appear as playable characters in Super Smash Bros Ultimate, with a stage based on the series.

The "Evangelist of Love Advent Gacha" limited event from Bombergirl features an unlockable new character called Sepia Belmont, with her biography establishing she's a descendant of the Belmont Clan. A later event also included a Rondo of Blood BGM.
Simon Belmont from Castlevania makes an appearance in Kaettekita Pixel Crows.
Dracula has been a subject for Death Battle!
Two bosses from ULTRAKILL are homages to bosses from Castlevania: Curse of Darkness.
Random Encounters has made a Castlevania song.
Simon Belmont and Alucard are crossover skins in Brawlhalla.
A painting of Alucard from Castlevania can be found in Dead Cells.  Also, Castlevania characters will appear as part of the Dead Cells:Return to Castlevania DLC.
A Castlevania: Curse of Darkness game box is seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Characters from Castlevania appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
A bot that resembles Alucard from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night appears in Astro's Playroom. Costumes based on Richter and Alucard from Castlevania can be found in Astro Bot.
Characters and weapons from Castlevania appear in Vampire Survivors as part of the Ode to Castlevania DLC.

Casualty.description: Holby City is a spinoff of Casualty.

Events from Casualty were mentioned in an episode of Emmerdale.

A cat version of the Dig Dug protagonist appeared in Cat Busters during the Namco Catalog IP collaboration event, while Fygar appeared as a boss and a "Pooka" mouse appeared as a minor enemy.

A cat based on the Solvalou from Xevious appears in Cat Busters as part of a Namco Catalog IP collaboration, alongside the Andor Genesis as a boss battle.
A cat version of Wagan from Wagan Land is featured in Cat Busters as part of a Namco Catalog IP collaboration.

The Cat in the Hat appears in Seussical.

A cat who resembles the Cat In The Hat can be seen in the The Lorax movie.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews "The Cat in The Hat movie".

Someone was wearing the Cat's Hat in the Bojack Horseman episode "The Shot".
I Hate Fairyland #9's alternate title: "Splat in the Hat"'s title is a reference to The Cat in the Hat.
Cake based around Cat in the Hat appears as a special kart in the game “Kart Kingdom”.  Also, the Cat appears in “Kart Kingdom” for a special event.
The Cat in the Hat's hat appears in the shop.
Cat In The Hat is parodied in the MeatCanyon episode "Cet in Het".
Cat in the Hat is mentioned in Class of '09: The Re-Up.
A Cat In The Cat game box is seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
The world of Cat In The Hat appears in the Minecraft Dr. Seuss DLC.

CatDog appears in Nickelodeon Extreme Tennis.

Sylvester And Tweety Mysteries shows on a computer in Cats And Dogs 2.

The melody of "Memory" from Cats is heard in Something Rotten!
Jess wears a Cats sweater in the New Girl episode: "Clean Break".
Multiple Jellicle Cats from Cats perform alongside the class from School of Rock in the GMA Andrew Lloyd Webber Musical Mashup.
The musical Cats is mentioned in “Henry Danger: The Musical”.
Ashley mentions Cats in The Boys episode “What I Know”.
Cats is referenced in an episode of Spitting Image.
A poster can be seen of a movie that is a parody of Cats in the episode "Cat-sino Royale".
The Nostalgia Critic reviews the 2019 film “Cats”.

Contra.description: The Contra series takes inspiration from the Alien series.
Several boxarts and images in the Contra series are based on promotional images and stills from Rambo movies.
Bill Rizer's art in the boxart of the NES Contra port is traced from a still of Schwarzenegger's character in Predator.

Bill and Lance are at The Outer Heaven Show Pub. Stage 3 in Contra III: The Alien Wars (Neo Kobe Steel Factory) is set in Neo Kobe, the setting of Snatcher, and feature Snatcher-looking androids as end bosses.
During Jimmy's Training Contra is shown as one of the games he plays.
In episode 13 of the Howard & Nester comic, Nester meets with Bill and Lance from Contra.
Bill Rizer is a playable character in Wai Wai World 2: SOS!! Parsley Jō.

The secret boss Simondo Belmont from Contra: Hard Corps is a parody of Simon Belmont, including the use of a whip and hitting candles for power ups. In Order of Eclessia, the boss Arthroverta is inspired by Shadow Beast Kimkoh from the NES port of Super Contra.

A Pac-Man-themed minigame featuring tanks can be found as an Arcade and played in Contra: Legacy of War.

Danny Phantom appears on a wanted poster in The Fairly OddParents episode "Poltergeeks". In the episode Crash Nebula, an easter egg is shown when Sprig is looking at his comic. If you look closely, you will see that Danny Phantom is shown on the back of the comic. It says "Butch Hartman's Danny Phantom" and a caption that says "Coming Soon". In Cheese & Crockers, the concept of Denzel Crocker becoming half-man, half-cheese due to a machine built by Cosmo and Wanda is similar to Danny Phantom becoming half-ghost when he used his parents' machine. In The Fairly OddParents episode The End of the Universe-ity, Dark Laser making Timmy go to the bad side is a reference to the episode, Control Freaks, where Danny was hypnotized and becomes bad. In Wishology!, Timmy's and Trixie's kiss is similar to Danny's and Sam's kiss in Phantom Planet. Dash Baxter appears in the episode "Flyboy". "The Fairly Odd Phantom" is a crossover between The Fairly OddParents, Danny Phantom, T.U.F.F. Puppy and Bunsen is a Beast. They also have the same crossover in a comic. Morbius appears in Daredevil #324.
Shang-Chi appears in Daredevil Annual #10.
Gambit appears in Daredevil (Vol. 1) #330.

Shi has a comic crossover with Daredevil in Daredevil/Shi.
Daredevil/Batman: Eye for an Eye and Batman/Daredevil: King of New York are crossover between the two series.

Daredevil is a playable character in Marvel Rivals.
Matt Murdock appears in Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.

Daria.description: Daria is a spin off of Beavis and Butt-Head.
E.T. is mentioned in the Daria episode "Pierce Me".
The ending credits of the Daria episode "Speedtrapped" contain an homage to Carrie.
A character looking like Daria makes a cameo appearance in Drawn Together episode "Lost in Parking Space: Part Two Part II".
Daria appears in the Family Guy episode "Peter & Lois' Wedding".

Darius.description: The world of Darius is featured as an island ("Darius Island") in Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 and as the setting of Round E ("Sun 'A' Zone") in Bubble Symphony, including appearances of enemies and Electric Fan/King Fossil (former/NES port) and Yamato (latter) as area bosses; the Silver Hawk is also featured as an assist character in Bubble Symphony, spawns as an item in Round 54 of Bubble Memories with Round 63 of Super Mode resembling the Silver Hawk, and Level 86 of the NES port of Bubble Bobble references Darius.

The world of Darius is featured as an island ("Darius Island") in Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2, including appearances of enemies and Electric Fan and King Fossil (former/NES port) as area bosses.

Characters, the Silver Hawk and plot elements from Darius appear during one of the story paths in Syvalion, while two bosses from Syvalion appear in Darius Force and the Dark Helios from Dariusburst is implied to be the Syvalion itself.

The Silver Hawk from Darius appears in Cameltry holding a 1000 Pts sign if the player reaches the goal with more than 60 seconds on the clock, while in the SNES port of Cameltry, the background of stage 2 in the 2nd Plane Expert course, 3rd Plane Special course and 4th Plane Expert course feature the Silver Hawk fighting Strong Shell.
Michael's gameplay configuration in Gokujo Parodius is inspired by Darius.
One of the players in the "Taito Planets" team from Super Kyuukyoku Harikiri Stadium 2 is named "Darius", after the series.

Stage 8 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Darius and features a playable Silver Hawk; the ship also appears as one of the playable vehicles in Space Invaders '95: The Attack of Lunar Loonies, as DLC in Space Invaders Get Even and Space Invaders: Infinity Gene (version 3.0); while Proco, Riga Pratica, Ti2, Iron Fossil and Great Thing are among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, and Space Invaders 2000 includes a demo of G-Darius.
"Darius" is written above a plane's door in stage 2 of Elevator Action Returns.
One stage in GUNbare! Game Tengoku 2 features a boss parody of the King Fossil from Darius.
The PlayStation port of Pop n' Pop features a trailer for G-Darius.
A parody of Darius called "Darairama" is featured within Segagaga.
A Silver Hawk doll from Darius is one of the items to buy in the "Be a good buyer!" mini-game from Power Shovel.
The Silver Hawk is a graffiti creature in Magic Pengel: The Quest for Color and Graffiti Kingdom, with the Dual Horn and Death Wings appearing as graffiti monsters in the first game as well.
Several Darius games are included in Taito Memories Joukan, Gekan and Memories II Joukan.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Wai Wai Happy! Rokudaime and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Darius series.
Taito Legends 2 includes Darius Gaiden and G-Darius.
Various theme remixes from Darius are featured in Groove Coaster, while several models of Silver Hawk, Ti2 and Iron Fossil appear as avatars as well.

Metal Black was originally planed as a sequel to Darius II, and several enemies and elements in the game are based or related to bosses in Darius; while the Black Fry from Metal Black is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Taito DLC Pack.
The Inter Gray from Night Striker is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Taito DLC Pack.
Opa-Opa from Fantasy Zone is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Sega DLC Pack.
The Space Harrier is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Sega DLC Pack.
The TRY-Z from Galaxy Force is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Sega DLC Pack.
The Delta Sword from DoDonPachi Resurrection is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Cave DLC Pack.
The Miyamoto from Sorcer Striker is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Eighting DLC Pack.
Mobilsuit Alpha from Side Arms is a DLC character in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Capcom DLC Pack.
The Saber from Varth: Operation Thunderstorm is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Capcom DLC Pack.
The Gambler from Progear is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Capcom DLC Pack.

Proco, Riga Pratica, Ti2, Iron Fossil and Great Thing are among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, while several wallpapers based on the Darius series are unlockable in Arkanoid DS and Zone β-2 resembles the Silver Hawk.
Costumes based on Proco and Tiat's uniforms from Darius and several other related items are featured in Spelunker World as part of a Taito collaboration event.
Music from Darius can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix after an update.
A human version of Darius appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.

Dark Cloud.description: A character plays Dark Cloud in the 6th episode of Ghost Stories.
White Knight Chronicles uses the Georama system from Dark Cloud and is considered to be a spiritual successor.
Everybody's Golf features costumes based on Dark Cloud as part of a Level-5 Collaboration event.
Bots based on Maximilian from Dark Cloud 2 and Toan from Dark Cloud can be found in Astro Bot.

Dark Deception.description: Silent Hill characters appear as DLC for Dark Deception: Monsters & Mortals.
Poppy Playtime characters appear as DLC for Dark Deception: Monsters & Mortals.
Piggy characters appear as DLC for Dark Deception: Monsters & Mortals.
DOORS characters appear as DLC for Dark Deception: Monsters & Mortals.

Dark Souls.description: Dark Souls is a spiritual successor to Demon's Souls, featuring similar gameplay and settings. Trusty Patches and Unbreakable Patches from Dark Souls are based on Patches the Hyena from Demon's Souls.
Several elements and characters in Dark Souls and Dark Souls II are inspired by the Berserk manga series.
Some elements in Dark Souls were inspired by the Harry Potter series.
There are minor references to the first arc of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure in Dark Souls.
Dark Souls features a reference to the Hollows from Bleach.
There are several references to Dark Souls in the Borderlands 2 DLC "Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep".
In Yo-Kai Watch, one of the statues in the Gourd Pond Museum features a minor reference to Dark Souls.
The "Dark Wraith" armor set from DOTA 2 features direct references to Dark Souls.
The items "Heart of the Praxic Fire" and "Ghost Angel Cloak" from Destiny feature references to Dark Souls.

The follower "Soulare of Andorhal" from the World of Warcraft: Warlords of Draenor expansion was likely inspired by Solaire of Astora from Dark Souls. There are other minor references to Dark Souls in World of Warcraft.
There are minor references to Dark Souls in Bloodborne.
Outcast Odyssey featured cards based on Dark Souls 2 characters during limited promotions.
The cover to Dark Souls II can be seen in the Black Mirror episode: "Playtest".
Outfits based on Dark Souls III characters are downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 3.
Fafnir tried to play the game during Kobayashi-san's house party
Dark Souls is parodied in the Daitomodachi episode "Solaire: The Cult Leader".
A painting of Solaire from Dark Souls can be found in Dead Cells.
Days Gone features a reference to the Dark Souls bonfire.
One of the skins of Reventure is based on Solaire of Astora, from Dark Souls.
Haiku, the Robot features a quote from Solaire from the Dark Souls series on a gravestone as well as his name.
The Chosen Undead has been a subject for Death Battle!.
A costume referencing Solaire can be found in Another Crab's Treasure.
The opening to My Deer Friend Nokotan includes a reference to the Dark Souls series.
Bosses from the Dark Souls series appear in Elden Ring Nightreign.

Darkest Dungeon.description: A painting of Hamlet from Darkest Dungeon can be found in Dead Cells.
The Ancestor from Darkest Dungeon is an announcer in Dota 2.
Bounty Battle features the Crusader from Darkest Dungeon as a playable character.
The level "Darkish Dungeon" in Baba is You is inspired by Darkest Dungeon.
Cards based on Darkest Dungeon are included in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls Requiem.

Darkman.description: The Darkman vs. Army of Darkness comic is a crossover between the two series.
The 189th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Darkman for the NES.
A poster for Darkman appears in the Ted episode: "Just Say Yes".

Darkstalkers.description: Blanka from Street Fighter II is referenced in the English version of Felicia's ending from Night Warrior: Darkstalkers' Revenge while characters from Darkstalkers appear in Street Fighter × All Capcom and Street Fighter Battle Combination; guests costumed as Darkstalkers characters appear in Street Fighter Alpha 2, "Street Fighter VS Darkstalkers" is a comic crossover between both series and Street Fighter V features several Darkstalkers costumes. There are other minor references between both series.
Anita from Darkstalkers is a hidden playable character in Marvel Super Heroes.
Various Darkstalkers characters are selectable in Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo and Puzzle Fighter.
There's a poster of Vampire Hunter in one of the backgrounds in Quiz Nanairo Dreams.
In the localization of Revelations: Persona, the enemy character "Nekomata" was renamed "Felicia" after the Darkstalkers character.
A sketch from Red Earth shows Darkstalkers' Hsien-ko as a member of Mai-Ling's combat unit, Darkstalkers/Red Earth: Maleficarum is a manga crossover between both series.
Morrigan, Felicia and Hsien-ko from Darkstalkers are selectable in Pocket Fighter.
Darkstalkers characters are playable in all Marvel vs. Capcom games.
Morrigan from Darkstalkers is a selectable character in Gunbird 2.
Darkstalkers characters are featured in several games of the SNK vs. Capcom series.

A Darkstalkers poster can be found in Resident Evil: Survivor, while the stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several Vampire Hunter: Darkstalkers' Revenge Arcade cabinets.
A Darkstalkers poster can be found in Biohazard Gun Survivor.
Baby Bonnie Hood from Darkstalkers is a hidden selectable character in Cannon Spike.
A rescuable Reploid in Mega Man X6 is named after Morrigan from Darkstalkers.
Capcom Black Jack features appearances of B.B. Hood from Darkstalkers.
Capcom Girl's Mind Puzzle features appearances of Morrigan and Felicia from the Darkstalkers series.
Anakaris, Demitri, Felicia and Jedah from Darkstalkers are selectable in Capcom Fighting Evolution.
Characters in Power Pro Kun Pocket 7 are named after Demitri and Lord Raptor.
Namco × Capcom features characters from the Darkstalkers series.
Universal Fighting System includes four sets of cards based on Darkstalkers.
Demitri, Morrigan, Felicia, Lilith, and Jedah from the Darkstalkers series appear in Cross Edge.
Morrigan from Darkstalkers is a selectable character in Tatsunoko vs. Capcom.
Felica and Jon Talbain have been a subject for Death Battle!
Monster Hunter Frontier and Monster Hunter Explore feature downloadable costumes based on Morrigan and Demitri from the Darkstalkers series.
There are several references to the Darkstalkers series in Skullgirls.
The list of generic monickers in Dragon's Dogma features "Anakaris", "Anita", "Demitri", "Donovan", "Felicia" and "Morrigan" as possible monickers.
Morrigan appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.

Morrigan, Felicia and Jedah Dohma appear in Onimusha Soul in individual collaboration events, while the first two and B.B. Hood, Hsien-ko and Felicia appear as part of the "Capcom Heroines" limited event. Felicia and B.B. Hood also appear in their own events at a later date.
Minna to Akashic Heroes features cards of Darkstalkers characters, while Minna to Capcom All Stars and Street Fighter × All Capcom feature characters from Darkstalkers.
Misery is seen wearing a Morrigan costume from Darkstalkers in the Halloween update for Cave Story+.
Chapter 22 of High Score Girl has the main characters playing the Night Warriors: Darkstalkers' Revenge arcade game.
Morrigan, Lilith, Felicia, B.B. Hood and Hsien-ko are featured in Otoranger.

Hood are featured as costumes for Nick Ramos and Frank West in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along their actual techniques; Frank West receives a Morrigan costume in Dead Rising 4 and series artwork and Arcade cabinets also appear on its backgrounds. Darkstalkers characters appeared in Zombie Cafe as part of a special promotion.
Kaku-San-Sei Million Arthur features Darkstalkers characters as part of a special collaboration event.

Godzilla and Ebirah appear in Dave the Diver as DLC.
Characters and items from Guilty Gear Strive appear as a part of Dave the Diver Anniversary Edition.
Characters from Dave the Diver appear in Goddess of Victory: NIKKE as part of a special collaboration.
