Characters from Potion Craft appear in Dave the Diver as part of the "Dave & Friends" update, while Dave the Diver appears in Potion Craft as part of an update.
Ichiban from Yakuza appears in Dave the Diver's Ichiban's Holiday DLC.
Characters from Dave the Diver appeared in MapleStory as part of a special collaboration.

Dave!.description: CommandgirlVideo is in Woah Dave!, and Jr. Melchkin was later added in the Woah Dave! Deluxe update. Jr. Melchkin and CommandgirlVideo are also in Space Dave!. Dave is in Runner3.
A team consisting of characters from Woah Dave! appears in #IDARB.
Dave Lonuts from Woah Dave! is a playable character in Mutant Mudds Super Challenge.

Dawn FM.description: Dawn FM serves as a sequel series to After Hours. Characters and elements from After Hours and Dawn FM appear in The Weeknd: Nightmare Trilogy.
"Take My Breath" by The Weeknd appears in Fortnite as a Jam Track.
Hurry Up Tomorrow serves as a sequel series to Dawn FM. Characters and elements from ''Dawn FM appear in Hurry Up Tomorrow.

Dawson's Creek.description: Pacey and Joey from Dawson's Creek appears in The Muppets From Space.
There's a reference to Crash Bandicoot in the season 3 episode "Four to Tango" from Dawson's Creek.
Dawson's Creek is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Poker #2".
1990s UNO is a format crossover that features Dawson's Creek characters.
The Dawson's Creek theme plays in the Beef episode: "We Draw A Magic Circle".

Day Job.description: Garfield is mentioned in the Day Job episode “Episode 1”.

Days Gone.description: Days Gone features a reference to the Dark Souls bonfire.
Days Gone features the taser used by Gabriel Logan, the protagonist of Syphon Filter.
Days Gone featured items from Death Stranding after an update.
An arrangement of origami figures can be found in Ghost of Tsushima, one of them referencing Days Gone.
An outfit based on Deacon St. John from Days Gone is included as part of the Special Edition of Sackboy: A Big Adventure.
God of War Ragnarök features a poem based on Days Gone.
A bot that references Days Gone appears in Astro's Playroom. A bot based on Deacon St. John from Days Gone can be found in Astro Bot.

Daytona USA.description: Fighters Megamix features the Hornet as a playable character.
One of the curves in the Expert course "Virtua City" in Daytona USA 2 is named after Sarah Bryant.
The Hornet car from Daytona USA appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Samba de Amigo: Ver. 2000 features a playable track from Daytona USA.
The Hornet is an add-on in Ridge Racer for the PlayStation Vita.
Wreck-It Ralph features a game based on Daytona USA.

The Hornet from Daytona USA appears as a transformation of the racer "AGES" in Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed; additionally an image of Sonic is featured on the side of a mountain in Daytona USA.
The Hornet from Daytona USA appears as a transformation of the racer "AGES" in Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed.
Music from Daytona USA was added to maimai in the maimai PLUS version.
A human version of Daytona USA appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.

Dead Cells.description: Scorpion from Mortal Kombat is mentioned in the description for the Grappling Hook item in Dead Cells.
A painting of Solaire from Dark Souls can be found in Dead Cells.
A painting of the the Lookout Station from Firewatch can be found in Dead Cells.
A painting of 2B and 9S from Nier:Automata can be found in Dead Cells.
A painting of Hamlet from Darkest Dungeon can be found in Dead Cells.
Two items called Hayabusa Boots and Hayabusa Gloves can be found in Dead Cells.
Dead Cells has portals that are orange and blue just like the ones from Portal
A painting of the sword from Transistor can be found in Dead Cells.
A skeleton with the clothes of Nathan Drake from Uncharted can be found in Dead Cells.
A painting of the Dueling Peaks from The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild can be found in Dead Cells.
Dead Cells was reviewed by T.O.M. on Toonami.
Travis can wear a Dead Cells t-shirt in Travis Strikes Again: No More Heroes.
The Beheaded from Dead Cells is a playable character in Brawlout.
An HEV Suit, Crowbar and Headcrab can be found in Dead Cells as part of a small update to promote the release of Half-Life: Alyx.
Bounty Battle features the Beheaded from Dead Cells as a playable character.
The Beheaded from Dead Cells appears in Heave Ho after an update.
The King from Dead Cells appears in Skul: The Hero Slayer as part of an update. Items and skins from Skul: The Hero Slayer appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here" update.
A skin based on the Prisoner from Dead Cells appears in Fall Guys.
A painting of the knight from Hollow Knight can be found in Dead Cells. Additionally, items and skins from Hollow Knight appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here" update.
Items and skins from Hyper Light Drifter appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here" update.
Items and skins from Guacamelee! appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here" update.
Items and skins from Blasphemous appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here" update.
Items and skins from Soul Knight appear in Dead Cells. Items and skins from Dead Cells appear in Soul Knight.
Items and skins from Slay the Spire appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here Vol. 2" update.
Items and skins from Shovel Knight appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here Vol. 2" update.
Items and skins from Terraria appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here Vol. 2" update. Additionally, items from Dead Cells appear in Terraria after an update.
Items and skins from Hotline Miami appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here Vol. 2" update.
Items and skins from Katana Zero appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here Vol. 2" update.
Items and skins from Risk of Rain appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here Vol. 2" update.
A painting of Alucard from Castlevania can be found in Dead Cells.  Also, Castlevania characters appear as part of the Dead Cells: Return to Castlevania DLC.
Weapons from Dead Cells appear in Astral Ascent as part of an update.
The Prisoner from Dead Cells appears as a playable character in BlazBlue: Entropy Effect.

Dead Estate.description: Digby has a costume based on the Boyfriend from Friday Night Funkin'. Additionally, there is an item called "Friday Night Pumpkin".

In Dead Estate, there is a weapon called "Revengeance", which is a nod to Metal Gear Rising Revengeance and looks like Jetstream Sam’s weapon from the game. Fuji also has a costume based on Senator Armstrong.
Dead Estate features a skin for Jules that resembles Ashley Graham from Resident Evil 4.
Dead Estate features a skin for Luis that resembles Stan from Nightmare Cops.
Dead Estate features a skin for Lydia that resembles The Bride from Kill Bill.
Cordelia from Dead Estate is a playable character in Solace Inc..

Dead Island.description: A Hostile Surviver with very similar alike to Jason Voorhees (Mask, Machete, Kills People, etc) appears in the game.
Tobuscus and Gabuscus visit Dead Island in "TOBUSCUS ANIMATED ADVENTURES".
Sir Radzig's sword and Zizka's mace from Kingdom Come: Deliverance II were added to Dead Island 2 as downloadable content.

Dead Rising.description: Mega Man's Mega Buster weapon is unlockable in Dead Rising, while costumes based off Mega Man X (normal and first armor), Roll Caskett, Proto Man, Dr. Wily, Sigma, Bass and Zero are featured in several games of the series, together with a multitude of smaller references. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster features costumes based on Mega Man and Lan Hikari from Mega Man Battle Network and Tron Bonne from Mega Man Legends.

Frank West and his "Mega Man suit" are DLC characters in the game Lost Planet: Extreme Condition, Frank West is also playable in Lost Planet 2, and a notebook of Lost Planet 3 is a collectible in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.
A costume inspired by Spencer from Bionic Commando can be unlocked in Dead Rising: Chop Till You Drop; Dead Rising 4 features a t-shirt with the Bionic Commando remake's logo.

Left 4 Dead 2 features a message that says "Otis, out of film, No helicopter, Zombies are too fast, Not going to make it, Frank West"; while Dead Rising 2: Case West features a message on the wall referencing Left 4 Dead. Both series also references each other in the names of certain Achievements.
Frank West from Dead Rising is selectable in Tatsunoko vs. Capcom: Ultimate All-Stars.
Monster Hunter Frontier features downloadable weapons and costumes from Dead Rising 2.
Frank West makes an uncredited appearance in the second trailer of Marvel vs. Capcom 3 and is playable in Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3 and Marvel vs. Capcom: Infinite.
The bonus chapter in Nazo Waku Yakata features a cameo of Frank West from Dead Rising.
The Whored Mode minigame wave "Hank East" from Saints Row: The Third references Dead Rising.
Minna to Capcom All Stars features Frank West from Dead Rising, Frank West later appears in official art for Street Fighter × All Capcom.
The fictional character Ratman from Dead Rising appears in Otoranger as an event character, and his story is expanded on the official site and with new supporting characters.
Dylan Fuentes' mask from Dead Rising 3 appears to be inspired by Ken Kaneki's mask from Tokyo Ghoul.
The "Daisy Dukes Outfit" in Dead Rising 3 is a reference to The Dukes of Hazzard.
Dead Rising 3 features a recreation of Walter White's house from Breaking Bad, including a pizza stamped on the roof and a usable hazmat suit.

Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha features Ryu and Chun-Li costumes, along with the actual moves from Street Fighter, and zombie versions of Akuma and M.Bison as bosses; Dead Rising 2 also features a Blanka mask and the combo weapons "Roaring Thunder" and "Dragon Punch" reference techniques from Street Fighter; Dead Rising 4 features costumes of several Street Fighter characters, and Frank West from Dead Rising appears in official art for Street Fighter × All Capcom. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster features costumes based on Ken and Sodom from the Street Fighter series.

Regina from Dino Crisis is featured as a costume for Annie Greene in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along an actual Pteranodon from the series; a poster of Dino Crisis 3 is a collectible in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.

Edward Falcon's power form from Power Stone is featured as a costume for Nick Ramos in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along his actual moves; Dead Rising 4 features a Power Stone board game and art books in its backgrounds.

Shoma from Rival Schools is featured as a costume for Chuck Greene in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along with his actual moves; Dead Rising 4 features Rival Schools Arcade cabinets, art books and banners in its backgrounds.

Captain Commando is featured as a costume for Chuck Greene in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along with his actual moves, and later as a costume for Frank West in Dead Rising 4.
Kaijin no Soki is featured as a costume for Frank West in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along with his actual moves.

Felicia and B.B. Hood are featured as costumes for Nick Ramos and Frank West in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along their actual techniques; Frank West receives a Morrigan costume in Dead Rising 4 and series artwork and Arcade cabinets also appear on its backgrounds. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster features a costume based on Rikuo from Darkstalkers.

Mike Haggar is featured as a costume for Frank West in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha; Dead Rising 4 features a Mike Haggar costume and Final Fight Arcade cabinets in its backgrounds.

Nina from Breath of Fire IV is featured as a costume for Annie Greene in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along with her actual moves, while Dead Rising 4 features billboards and art books from Breath of Fire in its backgrounds.
The Option A from Strider appears as an item in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha.
The P-38 Lightning biplane from 1942 appears as an item in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha; Dead Rising 4 features a 1943 board game in its background.

Stores in Dead Rising named "Jill's Sandwiches" and "Chris' Fine Foods" references Chris and Jill from Resident Evil, while weapons and the joke character Tofu from Resident Evil 2 appear as items in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha; Dead Rising 4 features several art books in its backgrounds, while its update Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package features a Jill Valentine costume in "Capcom Heroes" mode, along with her actual moves. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster features costumes based on Chris Redfield, Leon S. Kennedy, a Licker, Nemesis, a Chainsaw Villager and Ashley Graham from the Resident Evil series.
"Zenny", the currency from Black Tiger, appears in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition EX + α, a DLC package for Dead Rising 3.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha.
Art books of Ace Attorney appear in the backgrounds of Dead Rising 4, a poster of Ace Attorney: Spirit of Justice is a collectible in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.
Art books of Asura's Wrath appear in the backgrounds of Dead Rising 4.

Frank West and Chuck Greene from Dead Rising are playable characters in Puzzle Fighter, while a poster of Super Puzzle Fighter Turbo II is a collectible in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.
Sissel from Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is featured as a costume for Frank West in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package, along with his actual moves.

Art books of Devil May Cry appear in the backgrounds of Dead Rising 4, while its update Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package features a Dante costume in "Capcom Heroes" mode, along with his actual moves.
Art books of Ōkami appear in the backgrounds of Dead Rising 4, while its update Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package features an Amaterasu costume in "Capcom Heroes" mode, along with her actual moves.

"Arthur's Boxers" is an unlockable item in Dead Rising, and a costume inspired by Arthur from Ghosts 'n Goblins can be found in Dead Rising 2; Dead Rising 4 features a Ghosts 'n Goblins board game in its backgrounds, and its update Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package features an Arthur costume in "Capcom Heroes" mode, along with his actual moves.
Viewtiful Joe is featured as a costume for Frank West in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package, along with his actual moves.
The magic lamp item from Midnight Wanderers is featured as an item in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.
A poster of Zack & Wiki is a collectible in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.
Frank West has been a subject for Death Battle!
TEPPEN update 3.2 added characters from the Dead Rising series.
Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster features a costume of Blodia from CyberBots: Full Metal Madness.

Dead Space.description: A costume based on Isaac Clarke from Dead Space is unlockable in Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 versions of Tiger Woods PGA Tour 10.
Isaac Clarke from Dead Space is playable in the PSP version of Army of Two: The 40th Day; masks from the Dead Space series are also unlockable in Army of Two: The Devil's Cartel.
Dante's Inferno: Death Edition features a costume based on Isaac Clarke from Dead Space.
Isaac Clarke from Dead Space is playable in Skate 3.
Isaac Clarke from Dead Space is unlockable in MySims SkyHeroes.
NBA Jam: On Fire Edition features Isaac Clarke from Dead Space as a selectable character.
In Dragon Age 2 there is a knight armor based on Dead Space's Isaac Clarke Armor.

A dead body looking like Isaac Clarke from Dead Space can be found in Duke Nukem Forever, and Duke quips "That's one dead space marine";  Isaac's helmet is one of three collectable helmets in the game.

In Battlefield 3 you can find the helmet of Isaac Clarke from Dead Space; additionally, two characters are seen playing Dead Space in Battlefield: Hardline. A Dead Space-themed crossover event, Outbreak, was released in Battlefield 2042.
Random Encounters has made a Dead Space song.
In Saints Row: The Third one of the missing ships found on a list is named "USG Ishimura", like a ship from Dead Space.
Dead Space 3 includes a suit based on the N7 Armor from Mass Effect, with its description also mentioning Shepard as a fictional character.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features Isaac Clarke from Dead Space as a downloadable character.
Isaac Clarke's costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 2.
Skin Pack 5 in the Minecraft Xbox 360 and Xbox One Editions features skins based off characters from Dead Space.
Enter the Gungeon features a weapon called the Mine Cutter that resembles the plasma cutter from Dead Space.
The Universalist armor set is based on Isaac Clarke's armor from Dead Space.
The cover to Dead Space 2 can be seen in the Black Mirror episode: "Playtest".
Cosmetics based on Isaac Clarke from Dead Space appear in Knockout City as part of the Holo-Ween event.
A charm of Isaac Clarke's helmet from Dead Space could be obtained in Apex Legends by EA Play members.
The biophages from The Callisto Protocol resemble the Necromorphs from Dead Space.
Isaac Clarke appears in Fortnite.
The Dead Space remake added a beer brand named 'Red Dwarf'.

Dead Zone (SunSoft).description: Carrie from Dead Zone co-hosts the Miss Nazoler Contest in Nazoler Land Dai 3 Gou, and Kirk also makes a cameo in the Nazoler BOX mode.
A Dead Zone card is included in the game Barcode World.
Characters from Dead Zone appear on Mahjong tiles in Shanghai Musume: Mahjong Girls.

Michael Myers (as The Shape) and Laurie Strode appear as DLC for Dead by Daylight.
William "Bill" Overbeck appears as DLC for Dead by Daylight.
Leatherface is a DLC character in Dead by Daylight.
Freddy Krueger and Quentin Smith appear as DLC for Dead by Daylight.
The Pig and David Tapp appear as DLC for Dead by Daylight.
Ash Williams appears as DLC for Dead by Daylight.
Ghostface appears as DLC for Dead by Daylight.
Nancy Wheeler, Steve Harrington, a Demogorgon and Vecna from Stranger Things appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Pyramid Head and Cheryl Mason appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
The Look-See appears in Dead by Daylight as a cosmetic set for The Doctor.
The Birch appears in Dead by Daylight as a cosmetic set for The Hag.
The Mordeo appears in Dead by Daylight as a cosmetic set for The Huntress.
Characters from Resident Evil appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Characters from Hellraiser appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
The Trapper from Dead by Daylight appears in For Honor as DLC.
Characters from The Ring appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Costumes based on Attack on Titan appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Jenny, Trapper, Huntress and Blight from Dead by Daylight appear in Move or Die as part of an update.
The Wassup mask from Scary Movie appears as a cosmetic for The Ghost Face in Dead by Daylight.
Dead by Daylight characters and maps appear in PUBG during a crossover event.
The Xenomorph and Ellen Ripley from Alien appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Chucky and Tiffany Valentine from Child's Play appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
A pinball table based on Dead By Daylight was added to to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball M that features characters from the series.

Tubarão from Rainbow Six: Siege appears as a crossover skin in Dead by Daylight, along with outfits based on Wamai and Blitz, while outfits and other cosmetics based on the Trapper and the Huntress from Dead by Daylight appear in Rainbow Six: Siege.
Alan Wake appears as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Eddie the Head appears in Dead by Daylight as a cosmetic set for The Doctor, The Deathslinger, The Oni, and The Dredge.
Characters from Dungeons and Dragons appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Lara Croft appears as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Characters from Castlevania appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.

Characters from Junji Ito Collection and Junji Ito: Maniac appear in Dead by Daylight as a cosmetic set for The Artist, The Spirit, The Dredge, The Trickster, The Twins, Yun-Jin Lee, Kate Denson, and Yui Kimura.
Cards based on Dead by Daylight appeared in Balatro as part of the "Friends of Jimbo 4" update.
Ken Kaneki appears as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
The Oni from Dead by Daylight appears in Assassin's Creed Shadows during a crossover event.
Characters from The Witcher appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Springtrap from Five Nights at Freddy's appears as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
The Boulet Brothers, Dracmorda and Swanthula, from Dragula appear as a cosmetic set for The Artist in Dead by Daylight.
Rick, Michonne and Daryl from The Walking Dead appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
The Grizzly and Kaoru appear as a cosmetic set for The Oni and Yui Kimura in Dead by Daylight. Also, in various episodes of the anime, many references to Dead by Daylight can be seen.

Dead or Alive.description: Ryu Hayabusa from Ninja Gaiden is a recurring character in the Dead or Alive series, while Muramasa appears in Dead or Alive 4 and 5, Irene Lew appears in Dead or Alive Dimensions, and Momiji and Rachel appear in Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate. Ayane is a recurring character in the modern Ninja Gaiden series, Kasumi is selectable in Ninja Gaiden III: Razor's Edge and several characters from Dead or Alive appear as cards in Ninja Gaiden Clans.

Lei Fang in the PlayStation version of Dead or Alive has a costume based on the pixie from Monster Rancher, while toys of "Suezo" and "False Suezo" can be found in the Survival Mode from Dead or Alive 2: Hardcore and the "Tecmo 50th Anniversary DLC" pack for Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features various costumes based on Monster Rancher; additionally a Pixie-breed monster based on Kasumi from Dead or Alive appears in several Monster Rancher games and another based on Ayame appears on Monster Rancher Advanced 2.
Having saved data of Dead or Alive unlocks the special "Shock" dragon in Dragonseeds.

The PlayStation 2 version of Dead or Alive 2 includes costumes for Ayane and Helena based respectively on Millennia from Kagero: Deception II and Reina from Deception III: Dark Delusion, while Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features a DLC costume set of characters from the series, and also a costume for Helena including a shirt with the Kagero: Deception II logo. The "Butterfly Costume" in Deception IV: Blood Ties is based on Ayane.
The character SPARTAN-458 in Dead or Alive 4 is a SPARTAN-II supersoldier from the Halo series; her stage, called Nassau Station, is also from the series.
Kasumi's costume is an unlockable outfit in Super Swing Golf and Super Swing Golf: Season 2, Ayane's costume is unlockable in Season 2.

Ayane is a guest character in Dynasty Warriors: Strikeforce, where her weapons are selectable, and she's playable in Dynasty Warriors Vs. and Warriors Orochi 3, while Kasumi is playable in Warriors Orochi 3 Ultimate; Naotora Li from Samurai Warriors is a guest character in Dead or Alive 5 Last Round, which also features a DLC costume set of characters from the series; Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate features a costume set based on characters from Warriors Orochi 3 Ultimate; Warriors All-Stars features Kasumi, Marie Rose and Honoka as playable characters.
Kasumi from Dead or Alive received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate and makes a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Dead or Alive: Dimensions features a stage based on Metroid: Other M which also features the appearances of Samus and Ridley.
Dead or Alive 5 features Akira, Sarah and Pai Chan from Virtua Fighter as playable characters, while Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate adds Jacky as another playable character.
Samurai & Dragons features cards based on characters from Dead or Alive 5.
One of Kasumi's costumes in Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate is a promotional outfit bearing the logo of Ragnarok Odyssey ACE.
The Sports Gear DLC pack for Dead or Alive Ultimate and the Tecmo 50th Anniversary DLC pack for Dead or Alive 5 Last Round include costumes based on Tecmo Bowl.

Ayane from Dead or Alive is a bonus playable character in Zero: Nuregarasu no Miko. Costumes based on Kasumi and Ayane from the Dead or Alive series are unlockable in Fatal Frame II: Crimson Butterfly - Director's Cut.

Ayane from Dead or Alive is a DLC character in Senran Kagura Estival Versus, while Honoka, Marie Rose and Ayane are DLCs in Senran Kagura: Peach Beach Splash. Dead or Alive 5 Last Round and Dead or Alive Xtreme 3 feature DLC costume sets based on the Senran Kagura series.
Three alternate color palettes in Skullgirls are based on Dead or Alive.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features DLC costumes of characters from Trails in the Sky and Trails of the Cold Steel as part of the "Falcom Mashup" costume set.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features DLC costumes of characters from the Ys series as part of the "Falcom Mashup" costume set.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features a DLC costume of Mail from Popful Mail as part of the "Falcom Mashup" costume set.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features DLC costumes of Hakushon Daimaoh and Akubi from The Genie Family as part of the "Tatsunoko Mashup" costume set.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features a DLC costume set of characters from Fairy Tail.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features a DLC costume set of characters from Attack on Titan and a stage featuring the eponymous titans.
Mai Shiranui from Fatal Fury is a guest character in Dead or Alive 5 Last Round and in Dead or Alive 6.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features DLC costumes of characters from Utawarerumono as part of the "Aquaplus Mashup" costume set.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features DLC costumes of characters from Guilty Gear as part of the "Arc System Works Mashup" costume set.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features DLC costumes of characters from BlazBlue as part of the "Arc System Works Mashup" costume set.
Phantasy Star Online 2 features costumes based on Dead or Alive during a special promotion.
The Tecmo 50th Anniversary DLC pack for Dead or Alive 5 Last Round includes a costume for Christie featuring a shirt with the Star Force logo.
The Tecmo 50th Anniversary DLC pack for Dead or Alive 5 Last Round includes a costume for Hayate featuring a shirt with art from Rygar.
The Tecmo 50th Anniversary DLC pack for Dead or Alive 5 Last Round includes a costume for Zack featuring a shirt themed after Bomb Jack.
The Tecmo 50th Anniversary DLC pack for Dead or Alive 5 Last Round includes a costume for Zack featuring a shirt themed after Solomon's Key.

Kasumi, Marie Rose, Honoka, Ayane, and Leifang appeared in Destiny Child, while costumes from the game appeared in Dead or Alive Xtreme Venus Vacation with an in-universe reference to "Channel Evil" during special collaboration events.
Costumes based on Haruhi Suzumiya appeared in Dead or Alive Xtreme Venus Vacation during the Kadokawa Sneaker Bunko collaboration event.
Costumes based on Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? appeared in Dead or Alive Xtreme Venus Vacation during a collaboration event.
Scott the Woz once did a review on Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball.

Dead or Alive.game: How Heavy Are the Dumbbells You Lift?
Dead or Alive.description: Costumes based on How Heavy Are the Dumbbells You Lift? appeared in Dead or Alive 6 during an update.

Dead or Alive 5 Last Round and later games in the series feature costumes based on characters from the Atelier series; in the Dead or Alive Xtreme Venus Vacation collaboration events the characters are also seen performing alchemy from Atelier Ryza.
Kasumi and Marie Rose appear in Alice Gear Aegis, while costumes from the game with functioning weapons appeared in Dead or Alive Xtreme Venus Vacation during special collaboration events.
Nanjou mentions Dead or Dead, which might be a parody of Dead or Alive in Chapter 42 of The Dangers in My Heart.

Kula Diamond from The King of Fighters appears in Dead or Alive 6 as a DLC character while Dead or Alive characters appeared in The King of Fighters Allstar during a special collaboration; additionally Dead or Alive 5 Last Round featured DLC costumes of characters from The King of Fighters. Characters from Dead or Alive 6 appear in the Japanese and Chinese versions of The King of Fighters '98 Ultimate Match Online as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Dead or Alive Xtreme Venus Vacation appeared as shipgirls in Azur Lane during the collaboration event "Vacation Lane".
The Nioh 2 DLC "The First Samurai" includes a boss battle against Nyotengu from Dead or Alive, under the name "Ancient Nyotengu".

Kasumi, Ayane, Marie Rose, and Misatoki from the Dead or Alive series appeared in Romance of the Three Kingdoms 14 during a special collaboration; additionally costumes based on Romance of the Three Kingdoms 14 appeared in Dead or Alive Xtreme Venus Vacation during collaboration events.
Kasumi, Nyotengu, Marie Rose, and Honoka from Dead or Alive appear in The King of Fighters: All Star as part of a special event.
Dead or Alive 6 characters make an appearance in Langrisser Mobile as part of a special collaboration.

Deadlock.description: In Deadlock, The Doorman references Portal by having the ability to create door portals that are blue and orange.

Deadpool.description: Deadpool #27 features a reference to Street Fighter and the Shoryuken.

Black Panther vs. Deadpool is a crossover between both series. Additionally, Black Panther has appeared in several Deadpool comics, while Deadpool appears in Black Panther Vol. 3 #22 and #23 and Black Panther and the Agents of Wakanda #5 and #6.
Deadpool is a playable character in the Marvel: Ultimate Alliance series.
Great Lakes Avengers appear in Deadpool - GLI Summer Full Spectacular .
Deadpool appears in Thunderbolts (Vol. 2) #130-131. Deadpool has also been a member of the Thunderbolts, first joining in Thunderbolts (Vol. 3) #1.

Hit-Monkey appears in several Deadpool comics.
A zombie version of Man-Thing appears in Deadpool: Merc with a Mouth #13.
Moon Knight appeared in Deadpool Vol. 4 #28-29 and #49.1, Deadpool's Secret Secret Wars Vol. 1 #1.
Deadpool characters are playable in Marvel vs. Capcom 3 and Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3.
Deadpool costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 2.
There is a pizza with one of Raphael's sais buried in one of the sewer levels of the Deadpool video game.
Geometry Dash features a skin based on Deadpool.
Captain America appears in Deadpool Vol. 3 during the "Good, the Bad, and the Ugly" storyline.
Wolverine and Deadpool have crossed over on many occasions.
A pinball table based on Deadpool was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX 2 that features characters from the series.
Deadpool is mentioned in Armada.
Morbius appears in Deadpool #3.
Deadpool has been a rapper for Epic Rap Battles of History.

A character is referred to as "Mrs. Magoo" in the Deadpool movie.
Blade 2 is mentioned in the Deadpool movie.
Ripley from Alien 3 is mentioned in the Deadpool movie.

The Room is mentioned in Spider-Man/Deadpool #12.

Deadpool is parodied in the Cell Vs episode "Deadpool Vs Cell".
Deadpool is mentioned in Rick and Morty Presents: The Vindicators #1.
Pitch Meeting had episodes on the Deadpool movies.
Deadpool is parodied in multiple Perfect Cell Vs episodes.

Saw 3D is mentioned in Deadpool 2, referred to as "Saw 7."
Sharknado is mentioned in Deadpool 2 and Deadpool is mentioned in The Last Sharknado: It's About Time.
Pinkie Pie from My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic is mentioned in Deadpool 2.
The Teen Titans mistaken Slade for Deadpool in Teen Titans Go! To The Movies.
The Princess Bride is parodied in Once Upon A Deadpool.
A kid dresses up as Deadpool in the Modern Family episode: "The Last Halloween".
Deadpool appears in Fortnite as the Chapter 2 Season 2 Battle Pass secret skin.
Deadpool appeared in Puzzle & Dragons during the Marvel collaboration event.
All Might appears in chapter 9 of the Deadpool: Samurai manga.
A character on a poster bearing a strong resemblance to Deadpool appears in the Monster Lab episode "The Man Trials".
There is crossover merchandise "Marvel x Iron Maiden" collection "Stranger In a Strange Land" featuring Eddie the Head interacting with Deadpool.
Fujiko mentions Deadpool in the JoJo oneshot Fujiko's Bizarre Worldly Wisdom -Whitesnake's Miscalculation-.
A card based on Deadpool appears in Marvel Snap.
Deadpool is mentioned in Entergalactic.
The Nakatomi Plaza from Die Hard can be seen in the Void in Deadpool and Wolverine.
Deadpool appears in the "Secret Lair x Marvel's Deadpool" release for Magic: The Gathering.
Deadpool/Batman and Batman/Deadpool will be crossovers between the two series. Additionally, Batman and Robin are mentioned in the Deadpool movie.
Five Nights at Freddy's is mentioned in Deadpool VR.

Dexter's Laboratory.description: The episode "The Big Sister" features a reference to Godzilla.

In the episode "The Big Sister", when Mom enters Dexter's bedroom and is met by Dexter's robot duplicate, a Power Rangers-like poster can be seen on Dexter's bedroom wall. The episode "Go, Dexter Family! Go!" is a parody of Power Rangers whose vehicles come together to form a giant robot used to fight a huge monster who is wreaking havoc. This includes the family members divided into different squares and the theme song is a parody of Go Go Power Rangers.
The Justice Friend's character Major Glory is a parody of Captain America.
The Infraggable Bulk is a parody of The Incredible Hulk, while the Justice Friend's character the Infraggable Krunk is a parody of Hulk.
The Justice Friend's character Valhallen is a parody of Thor.
The episode "Simion" features a reference to The Jungle Book.
The Dexter's Laboratory episode "Barbequor" is a parody of the Fantastic Four's Galactus Trilogy story arc.
The episode "Jurassic Pooch" is a parody of Jurassic Park.
The episode "Huntor" parodies Predator.

In "Dream Machine", Dexter begins the episode by saying "Dexter's log, star date 1234.5", referencing how most episodes begin in Star Trek: The Original Series. The episode "Star Check Unconventional" parodies Star Trek.
Darbie is a parody of Barbie.
In "Dollhouse Drama", while Dexter's hallucinating the "ghost of his first love", the hand puppet Dee Dee wears is a reference to Pennywise.
In "Way of the Dee Dee", Dee Dee sings "Can you sing with all the colors of the rain", spoofing the song "Colors of the Wind" from Pocahontas.
My Little Unicorn from "Tribe Called Girl" is a parody of My Little Pony.
In "Tribe Called Girl", one of the outfits for Dexter includes a hat that resembles the Cat's hat. Thug 1 & Thug 2 are parodies of Thing 1 & Thing 2.
In "Tribe Called Girl", Dexter jumps into another pile of stuffed animals. One of them resembles Hello Kitty.
In the episode "Can't Nap", Krunk and White Tiger's slapstick shenanigans when he is dressed as a rodent are a reference to Tom and Jerry. Mom and Jerry is a parody of Tom and Jerry.
George Jetson appears in the Dexter's Laboratory episode Beard to be Feared.
An animatronic of Grape Ape appears in the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Chubby Cheese".
In "Dee Dee Locks and the Ness Monster", Dee Dee flying with her enlarged ears references Dumbo.
The episode "Dee Dee Locks and the Ness Monster" parodies Pinocchio.
In the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Backfire", Dee Dee's transformation into a car is a reference to the Gadgetmobile from Inspector Gadget.
In the episode "Book 'Em" Dee Dee gliding along the library floor with accompanying music is a reference to Jaws.
A soundalike of the Mission: Impossible theme music is heard in the episode "Book 'em".

In Shoo, Shoe Gnomes, when the last of the Shoe Gnomes is defeated, he yells "What a world!", a line that's derived from the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz'. In Comedy of Feathers, when Dee Dee said "Lions, tigers and bears" and Dexter said "Oh my", this was a reference to The Wizard of Oz.
R2-D2 is mentioned in the episode "Lab of the Lost".
In "Snowdown" from Dexter's Laboratory Dee Dee references Bugs Bunny's catchphrase. A sound effect from Looney Tunes is used the episode "Road Rash".
In "World's Greatest Mom" , the "M" that appears during the transitions is a parody of the "S" seen on Superman's chest.
The Dexter's Laboratory episode "Sports a Poppin'" features references to Peanuts. In Issue 17 of Dexter's Laboratory by DC Comics, Dexter dresses as Charlie Brown.
Dexter has a box of Scooby snacks in "Dexter's Lab: A Story".
Dexter from Dexter's Laboratory appears in I Am Weasel in the episode "I Am My Lifetime".
Characters from The Flintstones appear in Dexter's Laboratory.
Various scenes of the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Blackfoot and Slim" spoof Die Hard.
The Blue Falcon and Dynomutt appear in the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Dyno-Might".

Dexter makes cameos in many Powerpuff Girls episodes as well as the Powerpuff Girls movie; two of The Justice Friends characters Major Glory and Valhallen appeared in the Powerpuff Girls episode "Members Only". In the Dexter's Laboratory episode Mandarker, one of the elderly judges about to present Dexter with a ribbon is shown wearing a monocle and same exact shoes similar to The Mayor of Townsville from The Powerpuff Girls, both of whom are voiced by Tom Kenny. The Rowdyruff Boys appear in a painting in Dexter's Laboratory Issue 4 of IDW Comics, while the rest of the characters from Dexter's Laboratory appear in the comic Powerpuff Girls: Super Smash-Up!; The Powerpuff Girls also made a cameo appearance as one of many plush toys in the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Star Check Unconventional". In the Dexter's Laboratory episode Germ Warfare, the three talking amoebas found under Dexter's microscope are a reference to the Amoeba Boys, one of the villains on The Powerpuff Girls. In the Dexter's Laboratory episode 2Geniuses 2Gether 4Ever, the Alien on the screen of the Alien Communicator Dexter has is the same alien from the episode of The Powerpuff Girls called Beat Your Greens. In the Dexter's Laboratory episode Babysitter Blues, Lisa's pet name for Jeff is Fuzzy Lumpkins which is the name of a villain from The Powerpuff Girls. Jim from The Powerpuff Girls episode Mime for a Change also makes an appearance in the Dexter's Laboratory episode Bygone Errors. On September 17, 2021, ex-PPG writer Rob Renzetti revealed on his Twitter that he had storyboarded a Powerpuff Girls and Dexter's Lab crossover a decade earlier, which he called a fanfic but this is also considered a reportedly unfinished crossover episode.
Brain's story in the episode "The Contest" parodies Dexter's Laboratory with Brain as Dexter and Arthur as Dee Dee, while Mully and Francine share Dee Dee's tall body and long limbs.
Dexter's Laboratory: Robot Rampage is a redesigned version of Elevator Action EX.

Huntor from Dexter's Laboratory appears in the Samurai Jack episode "Jack vs. Mad Jack" and the game "Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time", while a Samurai Jack toy can be seen in some Dexter's Laboratory episodes. In the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Robo-Dexo 3000", Dexter mentions Samurai Jackson similar to Samurai Jack. In the IDW Comics, Jack and Aku make a cameo appearance in Dexter's Laboratory Issue 2.
In Information Stupor Highway, A.J.'s secret lab is a reference to Dexter's secret lab from Dexter's Laboratory.
The Dexter's Laboratory episode "Copping an Aptitude" features a reference to Mario Kart.
The episode "A Silent Cartoon" parodies Pink Panther.
In the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Oh, Brother", Robot Jones is seen as a toy on a bookshelf in one scene where Dexter walks over to the window and looks outside.

Dexter's Laboratory shows on tv in Signs.
Green Bacon and Eggs is a parody of Green Eggs and Ham.

In the episode Dexter's Library, when Dexter confiscates the library books from kids breaking the rules, he bellows "No book for you!" in a similar manner to the Soup Nazi's "No soup for you!" from the 1995 Seinfeld episode named after him.
The phrases Dexter and Dee Dee use in "D²" are a reference to The All-New Super Friends Hour.
The episode Dexter's Wacky Races parodies Wacky Races.
Dexter makes a cameo appearance in Time Squad episode, Floral Patton / Orphan Substitute.
Dexter from Dexter's Laboratory makes a cameo in the Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends episode Eddie Monster.

Diablo.description: Having saved data of Diablo unlocks the special "Demon" dragon in Dragonseeds.
Dungeons and Dragons: Diablo II Edition is a role playing game using the D&D rules, but set in the Diablo universe, therefore being a format crossover between the two series.

The creatures from Diablo appear in World of Warcraft. Diablo IV includes several cosmetics based on World of Warcraft, including Varian Wrynn and Garrosh Hellscream (for Barbarian), Malfurion Stormrage and Xavius (for Druid), Xal'atath and Lich King (for Necromancer), Illidan Stormrage and Sylvanas Windrunner (for Rogue), and Jaina Proudmoore and Kael'thas Sunstrider (for Sorcerer).
In Starcraft II you can enter the world of Diablo.
The PC re-release of Final Fantasy VII features a reference to Diablo II.
The character Satine from Wreck-It Ralph may be based on Diablo.

The PlayStation 3 version of Diablo III features Journey-themed pauldrons called "The Hero's Journey"; their description also mentions the Travelers from said game as making appearances in Diablo's world.
The PlayStation 3 version of Diablo III features an Uncharted-themed amulet called "Drake's Amulet".
Characters from Once Upon A Time can be seen playing Diablo III in Season 3, Episode 12.
Goat MMO Simulator features an area based on Diablo.
Runner, Stalker, Clicker, and Bloater enemies from The Last of Us make an appearance in the PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4 versions of Diablo III: Ultimate Evil Edition.
The PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4 versions of Diablo III: Ultimate Evil Edition feature a Shadow of the Colossus themed armor.
Diablo characters appear in Heroes of the Storm.
Diablo piñatas appear in the Dorado map in Overwatch.
The Diabuffalo is a reference to Diablo.
The Nintendo Switch version of Diablo III: Eternal Collection features a Ganondorf Transmogrification set, a Cucco pet, and a Triforce portrait frame.
Lilith from Diablo appears as an operator in Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 along with other Diablo cosmetics.
Cosmetics based on Berserk were added to Diablo Immortal and Diablo IV as part of an event. Additionally, Nosferatu Zodd was added to the former as a boss fight during said event.

Diagnosis: Murder.description: Diagnosis: Murder is a spinoff of Jake and the Fatman.
Ben Matlock appears in the two-part Diagnosis: Murder episode "Murder Two".
Joe Mannix appears in the Diagnosis: Murder episode "Hard-Boiled Murder".
Cinnamon Carter from Mission: Impossible appears in the Diagnosis: Murder episode "Discards".
Rob Petrie from The Dick Van Dyke Show appears in the Diagnosis: Murder episode "Obsession: Part 2".

Lt. Ben Keohala, a character introduced in the Diagnosis: Murder novel The Death Merchant, appears in the Monk novel Mr. Monk Goes to Hawaii, while Ian Ludlow, also introduced in The Death Merchant, appears in the Monk novel Mr. Monk and the Two Assistants.

Diary of a Wimpy Kid.description: The students play a stage play based on Wizard of Oz in Diary of a Wimpy Kid.
Ice Age can be seen on TV in Diary of a Wimpy Kid.
Mario Kart DS is seen being played in the first movie. A render from Super Mario 3D World featuring Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Toad are seen in the Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul movie.
Greg and Rowley try to make their own Pac-Man arcade machine.
Diary of a Wimpy Kid-based islands are in Poptropica.
Diary of a Wimpy Kid UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Greg Heffley mentions that Rodrick had The Lord of the Rings on his summer reading list.
In Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Double Down, Greg describes how he saw a movie about "a man whose life is secretly being filmed for a TV show", which is similar to the plot of The Truman Show.
The Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul movie has a scene where a woman can be seen dressed up as Undyne from a fan-created "alternate universe" of Undertale called "Underkeep".
Mad Max is mentioned in Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Long Haul.
Jeff Kinney confirmed in a tweet that Nate has met Greg, but it is yet to be recorded any of the current books.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews the 2010 film “Diary of a Wimpy Kid”.
Clue: Diary of a Wimpy Kid is a format crossover between the two series.

Daisy Duke is mentioned in Live Free or Die Hard.

Bro Hard is based on John McClane from Die Hard.

The Nakatomi Plaza from Die Hard can be seen in the Void in Deadpool and Wolverine.
The Nakatomi Plaza from Die Hard can be seen in the Void in Deadpool and Wolverine.
Die Hard is referenced in The Week Before.

Diff'rent Strokes.description: Arnold from Diff'rent Strokes appears in the Silver Spoons episode "The Great Computer Caper".
Arnold and Dudley from Diff'rent Strokes are fans of Knight Rider; David Hasselhoff, star of Knight Rider, appears alongside KITT in the Diff'rent Strokes episode "Hooray For Hollywood: Part 2".
Arnold Jackson appears in the Amazing Stories episode "Remote Control Man".
There is a minor reference to Diff'rent Strokes in Stay Tuned titled “Different Strokes.”
Arnold and Mr. Drummond from Diff'rent Strokes appear in The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air in the episode "I, Done: Part 2".
Diff'rent Strokes is mentioned in the Freaks and Geeks episode: "Carded and Discarded".
Diff'rent Strokes is mentioned in Final Destination 2.
Diff'rent Strokes is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Infestation Hypothesis".
Diff'rent Strokes is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Junk In The Trunk".
Diff'rent Strokes is mentioned in Ted.
"Whatcha talkin' bout Willis", a quote from Diff'rent Strokes, is spoken in Spiral.

Dig Build Live.description: Dig Build Live is a parody of the Minecraft series.
Mobs watch Felix the Cat in Episode 2 of Dig Build Live.
Dave the Zombie from Slamacow makes a cameo appearance in Episodes 2 and 4 of Dig Build Live.

Dig Dug.description: The Atari upright version of Pole Position features billboards advertising Dig Dug.
Stage 21 in Battle City is shaped after Pooka from Dig Dug. Pookas also appear hidden inside the steel walls in Round 29 of Tank Force. Tanks based on Taizo Hori, Pooka and Fygar appear in Tancle.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in the NES version of Dig Dug II and in Dig Dug Arrangement; Dig Dug: Digging Strike also features a reference to New Rally-X.

Pookas from Dig Dug appear as enemies in special stages in The Quest of Ki, while Dig・Dra・Pac Janken ou is a crossover between the two series; additionally a Gilgamesh costume appears in Dig Dug Island.
The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of Pooka from Dig Dug.
Elements from Dig Dug are featured in the X68000 version of Galaga '88 and in Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition; the Galaxian flagship is an item in Dig Dug.
Tinkle Pit features Pookas and Fygars, Taizo Hori as a secret bonus character and the power up "Dig Dug Rock" summons the rock obstacles from Dig Dug.
Dig Dug makes a cameo appearance in Mach Breakers: Numan Athletics 2.

Elements from Dig Dug appear in the background of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64, while Fygar appears as a player in Famista DS, Famista Online, and the protagonist of Dig Dug (called "Dig Dug") and Pooka appear as guest players in Pro Baseball Famista 2011; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Dig Dug", "Fygar" and "Pooka".
Namco Classic Collection Vol.2 includes Dig Dug.

Namco Museum Vol. 3 features Dig Dug and includes actual appearances of Pookas. Various later entries in the Namco Museum brand include several games from the Dig Dug series. Additionally, characters from Dig Dug can be seen interacting with characters from other series on the boxart of Namco Museum Arcade Pac.
Destroying all Sols in Area 1 and the red Sol in Area 2 of Xevious 3D/G+ makes a large Pooka from Dig Dug appear in Area 7, while Dig Dug: Digging Strike features a reference to Xevious.
In the X-Files episode "Unusual Suspects", a character is seen playing Dig Dug.
Dig Dug and Dig Dug II are featured in Namco History Vol.3.

Mr. Driller is a spin-off of the Dig Dug series; Mr. Driller also makes an appearance in Dig Dug: Digging Strike, and various characters from the series appear in the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic.

Pooka from Dig Dug makes a cameo in Pac-Man World, is a recurring enemy in Pac-Man World 2 and an unlockable character in  Ms. Pac-Man Maze Madness, in Pac-Man World Rally along with Fygar and as part of a theme with other Dig Dug characters in Pac-Man 99, while Taizou Hori is selectable in Pac-Man Kart Rally; Pac-Man appears in strip #9 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic; Dig·Dra·Pac Janken ou is a crossover between the two series.
Pooka is a selectable "car" in Ridge Racer 64; additionally, Ridge Racer features a "Team Dig Dug" while R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 features a reference to Dig Dug.
Dig Dug is one of the players in the "Namco All Stars '80" team in World Kicks.
An image of Pooka from Dig Dug appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.
The main character from Dig Dug appears in Namco Super Wars.
A song from Dig Dug is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
Namco × Capcom features the main character from Dig Dug as a playable character.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Tobikkiri! Anime Special features a music track based on the Dig Dug series; music from Dig Dug is also featured in the Namcot Medley debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10.
A Pooka from Dig Dug makes an appearance in Mario Kart Arcade GP and its sequel.
Dig Dug II characters and one location appear in Party Land.
The PlayStation 2 The Fast and The Furious video game by Namco features drifter charms of Taizo Hori, Fygar and Pooka from Dig Dug: Digging Strike.
A Valkyrie costume appears in Dig Dug Island.
The My Name Is Earl episode "Foreign Exchange Student" features a reference to Dig Dug.
A Wonder Momo costume appears in Dig Dug Island.
A Dig Dug theme song and attraction appear in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04 and 05, while a Pooka-themed phone strip appears in THE iDOLM@STER OVA.
The Robot Chicken episode "President Evil" features a sketch based on Dig Dug.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of a Pooka from Dig Dug with Dig Dug assisting the player.
Some levels of Noby Noby Boy feature Dig Dug characters.
In the episode Chum Caverns, one scene of Mr. Krabs and Plankton digging underground references Dig Dug.
Arino plays Dig Dug II in episode 88 of GameCenter CX.
A character is dressed like a Pooka from Dig Dug in the episode "Doomy Tales of the Macabre" from Homestar Runner.
The main character from Dig Dug appears as a summon alongside a Pooka in Keroro RPG.
Taizou Hori/Dig Dug is a playable character in Namco Chronicle, with Pookas and Fygars appearing as enemies.
Dig Dug has been a subject for Death Battle!
Fry makes a mention of Dig Dug in the season 6 episode "Benderama", while there's a visual gag based on its gameplay in the season 6 episode "Reincarnation".
Dig Dug is mentioned in Ready Player One and Ready Player Two.

Bravoman and Alpha Man appear in strip #2 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic, and then Bravoman makes a cameo in strip #7; Dig Dug makes a cameo in strip #100 of the Bravoman web comic, strip #164 features a Fygar from Dig Dug, several pieces of merchandising and video games related to Dig Dug also appear in other strips and the web series.
Wagan and other characters from Wagan Land appear in strip #2 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic.
Red from the ShiftyLook Sky Kid comic appears in strip #2 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary comic; additionally Pooka from Dig Dug appears as an item in Sky Kid.
Kissy from Baraduke appears in strip #7 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic.
A character dressed like Klonoa appears in strip #7 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary web comic.
A character dressed like the Prince from Katamari makes a cameo in strip #7 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary web comic.
A Creeper from Minecraft appears in strip #23 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary web comic.
Hiromi from Burning Force makes a cameo in strip #28 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic.
A character resembling Heihachi Mishima and another dressed like King appear in strip #7 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic, while King makes a cameo in strip #33.

Mappy makes a cameo in strip #33 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic, while the Dig Dug protagonist is a supporting character in Mappy: The Beat; Dig Dug, Pookas and Fygars appear in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan, Hippari Mappy Daisakusen and Touch the Mappy with 80's Dot Stars; additionally a Mappy costume appears in Dig Dug Island and a Pooka image appears in Mappy Kids.
Wreck-It Ralph features characters from Dig Dug.
Dig Dug from Dig Dug is a character in Namco High.
Dig Dug is parodied in "MINE THE DIAMOND".
Pooka from Dig Dug appears as an enemy in Smash Run mode in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS.
Lloyd mentioned Dig Dug in Dumb and Dumber To.
Ace Combat 6: Fires of Liberation features a building's lights in the shape of a Pooka from Dig Dug in Mission 14, while Ace Combat Infinity features emblems and nicknames based on Dig Dug.
Characters discuss the game Dig Dug in the season 7 episode "Donna and Joe" of Parks and Recreation.
Marge makes a reference to Dig Dug in the season 26 episode "Sky Police" from The Simpsons.
Frygar from Dig Dug appears as one of the videogame characters in the movie, Pixels.
Dino Run DX features a hat based on Dig Dug.
Dig Dug costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 3.
A cat version of the Dig Dug protagonist appeared in Cat Busters during the Namco Catalog IP collaboration event, while Fygar appeared as a boss and a "Pooka" mouse appeared as a minor enemy.
A character resembling Dig Dug appears in the episode "Labor Day".
Dig Dug characters appeared in The Knights of Avalon during the first and third Namco collaboration events.
Dig Dug is shown in Season 2: Chapter 1 of Stranger Things.
The main theme of Dig Dug is part of the "Namcot Medley" BGM featured in Groove Coaster 4: Starlight Road.
