There's an allusion to Attack on Titan during an imagination spot in Chapter 35 of Don't Toy With Me, Miss Nagatoro.
Chapter 27 of Kaguya-sama: Love is War - Official Doujinshi features two minor characters resembling Nagatoro and Senpai.
Don't Toy With Me, Miss Nagatoro x Magical Sempai is a crossover manga chapter between the two series.
The character Yoshi in a fantasy segment of Episode 6 of Don't Toy with Me, Miss Nagatoro appears out of an egg similar to Nintendo’s Yoshi.

DonPachi.description: Star Soldier vs DoDonPachi DaiOuJou CARAVAN'06 is a crossover between both series.
There is a minor reference to DonPachi in Chapter 19 of the Assassination Classroom manga.
The Delta Sword from DoDonPachi Resurrection is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Cave DLC Pack.

Donald Duck.description: The Donald Duck series can be considered a spin-off to the Mickey Mouse series, since it stars Donald in his modernized incarnation from the Mickey Mouse series, as well as featuring various Mickey Mouse characters in its early comic strips; there have been many other cameos and crossovers between the two series through the years.

The Donald and Goofy shorts as well as The Mickey, Donald and Goofy cartoons in Mickey Mouse Works and the movie Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers can be considered crossovers between the two series;Humphrey the Bear from the Goofy short Hold That Pose makes an appearance in the Donald Duck short Rugged Bear and then becomes a regular character in the series.

Donald Duck.game: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (Disney)
Donald Duck.description: In the Donald Duck cartoon The Riveter, Donald sings the song "Heigh Ho" from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
Chip and Dale appear in the Donald Duck short of the same name and become recurring characters afterwards.
Uncle Scrooge is a spin-off of Donald Duck
Bambi and his mother make a brief cameo in the Donald Duck short No Hunting.
Donald Duck appears as a cameo in Hikari. He shouts “What do you do? I’m an American famous duck and-“ at Penkou who proceeds to beat Donald up and then steal his clothes to wear them.
The Italian comic Moldfinger or The Spy Who Ducked-Out On Me is a parody of Goldfinger. The Italian comic Operazione Goldenball is a parody of Thunderball.
The Italian comics Paperino contro Colossor and L'ottava meraviglia del mondo are parodies of the franchise.
In The Twelve Tasks of Asterix, a hen lays an egg that resembles the head of Donald Duck.
A toy of Donnald Duck appears in An American Werewolf in London.

The Brazilian comic Os Caçadores da Pena Perdida and the Italian comic Parodie di grandi film: Paperinik e l'arca dimenticata are parodies of Raiders of the Lost Ark. The Italian comic Paperinik e il tempio indiano is a parody of Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom.
The Brazilian comic Zorro, O Justiceiro Panacão and the Italian comic Don Paperigo e il "sogno" di Zorro are parodies of Zorro.
Donald Duck is mentioned in Stand by Me.
Donald Duck characters appear in DuckTales.
The Italian comics Paperino acchiappafantasmi and Paperino e Paperoga ghostbusters are parodies of the franchise.
The Italian comic Paperino e il mistero delle ombre vaganti is a parody of the first film.
The film is shown on TV in the Italian comic Paperino e la video-sogno avventura.
The Italian comic Zio Paperone e il pianeta proibito is a parody of this film.
The Famicom game Donald Duck was repurposed as Snoopy's Silly Sports Spectacular! in North America.
The Italian Donald Duck comic Paperopoli Graffiti is a parody of American Grafiti.
The Italian comic Zio Paperone e il Grande Papero is a parody of the novel.
Donald Duck is mentioned in Home Alone 2: Lost In New York.
Donald Duck no Mahou no Boushi features compatibility with the Barcode Battler II.
The Italian comic Paperino e il signore del Padello is a parody of The Lord of the Rings. The Danish comic Back to There Again is a parody of The Hobbit.
The Italian comic Soul Papers is a parody of the film.
Donald Duck is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One Where No One's Ready".
A clip from Donald Duck is shown in Flubber.
Donald Duck is the protagonist of the Fantasia 2000 segment Pomp and Circumstance
Donald and Daisy Duck made an appearance in Pop'n Music Mickey Tunes and Pop'n Music Disney Tunes GB.
The Danish comic Cosmic Confrontation is a parody of the novel.
Dance Dance Revolution Disney Mix, Disney Dancing Museum and Disney Grooves feature Donald Duck and other characters from his stories as dancers.
The Donald short "Donald's Goofy World" features a parody of I Love Lucy.
In the first issue, a boy is shown wearing a Donald Duck costume.
The Danish comic The Mummy is a parody of the franchise.
The Kingdom Hearts series features many characters from the Donald Duck series.

At one point in the Sitting Ducks episode "Daredevil Ducks", there is a brick wall near an entrance leading to Swampwood warning about the presence of gators due to their habit of preying on ducks in the series. Among the signs reads "R.I.P Donald", alluding to Donald Duck.
Characters from Donald Duck appear in Toontown Online.
The Danish comic The Quacking is a parody of the film.
Animal Crossing’s Drake’s German name, Gustav, possibly references Gustav Gans, the German name for Gladstone Gander from Donald Duck.
The Danish comic A Space Oddity is based on Stanley Kubrick's film.
Peter Griffin dresses as Donald Duck in the Family Guy episode "Movin' Out (Brian's Song)".
In the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Stanley S. SquarePants", Mr. Krabs' nephews are a parody of Huey, Dewey, and Louie.
Donald Duck is mentioned in 'Party Time.
The Italian comic Quacklight: Bewitching Vampires in Duckburgh is a parody of Twilight.
The Italian comic Pirate's Revenge is a parody of the film series.
Costumes of Donald and Daisy Duck are playable in Disney Universe.
Kinect Disneyland Adventures features characters from the Donald Duck series.
The Italian comic Paperinik e il passato senza futuro is a parody of the first film.
Donald Duck is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Fancyman: Part 2".
Emil Eagle appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #58.
Donald Duck has been a subject for DBX.
Cards based on Donald Duck appear in Lorcana.

Donkey Hodie.description: Donkey Hodie is a spin-off to Mister Rogers' Neighborhood.
The Donkey Hodie episode "Daniel Tiger Visits Someplace Else" is a crossover between the series.

Donkey Kong.description: Donkey Kong takes inspiration from Popeye. Donkey Kong Jr. Math recycles the title screen music from Popeye no Eigo Asobi.
Crazy Kong is a clone of Donkey Kong.
There were multiple Game & Watch games released featuring Donkey Kong characters. Donkey Kong characters also appeared in the Game & Watch Gallery games.
A Donkey Kong cabinet is shown in WarGames.

The Mario series is a spinoff of the Donkey Kong series and characters from Donkey Kong appeared in many Mario games; Mario makes an appearance in Donkey Kong Country 2, while elements from the Mario series are featured in "Modern" versions of Donkey Kong games within the Game & Watch Gallery series; the Mario vs Donkey Kong sub-series is part of both series.
Frogger meets Donkey Kong between the episodes of their shows in the Saturday Supercade.
Donkey Kong characters meet Pitfall! characters between episodes of their shows in the Saturday Supercade.
The Road Runner from Looney Tunes is mentioned in the Donkey Kong Junior episode of Saturday Supercade "Sheep Rustle Hustle".
Mario meets Q*bert between the episodes of Donkey Kong and Q*bert, in the Saturday Supercade, while Q*bert meets Donkey Kong Jr. between the episodes of their respective shows.
The Donkey Kong episode title "Little Orphan Apey" is a reference to Little Orphan Annie.
Mario and Pauline from Donkey Kong make an appearance in a bonus minigame in Nintendo's Pinball.
The Mickey Mouse Panorama screen Game & Watch and Donkey Kong Circus have the same gameplay and got their serial numbers swapped.
The Coleco LCD Tabletop Donkey Kong can be seen in a scene in Gremlins.
Donkey Kong and Donkey Kong Jr. make an appearance in the audience in the arcade game Punch-Out!!; Donkey Kong is a secret opponent in Punch-Out!! for Wii.
Kangaroos Joey and Katy meet Donkey Kong between the episodes of their shows in the Saturday Supercade.
The Donkey Kong TV show was aired with the Space Ace TV show in the Saturday Supercade.
Mario and Pauline from Donkey Kong make an appearance in built-in games in Family Basic - v.3.
Donkey Kong Jr. makes an appearance in the audience in Smash Ping Pong, the Famicom Disk System version of Konami's Ping Pong.
In the first Mother an arcade cabinet for a game very similar to Donkey Kong can be spotted.
Donkey Kong is a recurring character in Captain N: the Game Master.
Donkey Kong makes an appearance in Tetris for NES and in Tetris DS. Tetris 99 held an event in promotion of Donkey Kong Bananza.
The Muppets Babies episode "It's Only Pretendo" features gameplay scenes from Donkey Kong and Donkey Kong Jr.
Donkey Kong makes a cameo in the game boy version of F-1 Race.
Donkey Kong makes a cameo in NES Open Tournament Golf.

Donkey Kong Jr. appears in the comic Kirby und das Geheimnis des Glibbers. The "Kong's Barrel" is an obtainable item in Kirby Super Star; the theme from the Kirby TV show is featured in the Japanese and North American versions of Donkey Konga, while a song from Kirby's Adventure is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
In a scene in Billy Madison, some characters talk about Donkey Kong.
In the Sega CD version of Earthworm Jim, a Donkey Kong mask is unlockable; in Donkey Kong Country 2 a gun looking like Earthworm Jim's can be seen in Cranky Kong's video game hero challenge results.

Wario meets Donkey and Diddy Kong in the comic Warios Weihnachtsmärchen; various microgames in the WarioWare series are based on Donkey Kong games, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "Donkey Kong Country Returns" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; additionally a music track from WarioWare Twisted! is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
Yoshi makes an appearance in Donkey Kong Country 2; a baby version of Donkey Kong, called Baby Donkey Kong, is playable in Yoshi's Island DS.
Link makes an appearance in Donkey Kong Country 2 and is referenced in Donkey Kong Country 3. He is also playable in a minigame version of Donkey Kong within NES Remix.
Arcade cabinets and a poster for Killer Instinct can be seen in Donkey Kong Country 2.
Bart imagines Donkey Kong in The Simpsons episode "Marge Be Not Proud"; there are other Donkey Kong references in other episodes of the series as well as the comics and videogames.
The Crash Bandicoot series features references to Donkey Kong.

La Planète Donkey Kong features an episode titled "Raiders of the Lost Banana", referncing Raiders of the Lost Ark. The German website for Donkey Kong 64 lists Diddy Kong's favorite movie as being "Banana Jones 2", referencing Indiana Jones.
Donkey Kong interviews Salem in an episode of Donkey Kong Planet.
The Donkey Kong Planet skit "Remix Files" parodies The X-Files.
The Donkey Kong Planet skit "Mission: Impossible" parodies the series of the same name.
The Donkey Kong Planet skit "Caspied le gentil fantôme" parodies Casper the Friendly Ghost.
The Donkey Kong Planet skit "Le gros rogue qui tache" uses music from The Nightmare Before Christmas.
Donkey Kong mentions Planet of the Apes in the Donkey Kong Country episode "Legend of the Crystal Coconut".

Donkey Kong mentions having an autographed picture of King Kong in the Donkey Kong Country episode "Legend of the Crystal Coconut". Donkey Kong is partially inspired on King Kong; The King Kong LCD game is based on Donkey Kong.
The music used in the Skerries course was originally the Boss Battle music from Donkey Kong Land. This music was eliminated from the Xbox One version used in Rare Replay.
GoldenEye 007 features a cheat mode called "DK mode" as a reference to Donkey Kong.
Diddy Kong Racing is a spin-off of the Donkey Kong series.
Donkey Kong and Donkey Kong Jr. appears in Game Boy Camera.
Jazz Jackrabbit 2 features a reference to Donkey Kong.
Characters, places and items from the Donkey Kong series are featured in all Super Smash Bros. games; Mr. Game & Watch makes a cameo in Donkey Kong Country Returns.
Characters from the Donkey Kong series appear in "Freeze Frame" and other N-Gang episodes.
Conker plays a tune from Donkey Kong in Conker's Pocket Tales.
Musical instruments from Banjo-Kazooie can be seen in Donkey Kong 64; there also are minor references to the Donkey Kong series in Banjo-Kazooie and Banjo-Tooie.
Donkey Kong 64 features Jetpac as a playable minigame.
The German website for Donkey Kong 64 lists Donkey Kong's favorite movie as "The Konginator 2", referencing Terminator 2: Judgment Day.
The German website for Donkey Kong 64 lists Tiny Kong's favorite movie as "Bananic", referencing Titanic. The Donkey Kong Planet skit "Camembert" parodies Titanic.
The German website for Donkey Kong 64 lists Chunky Kong's favorite movie as "Karate Kong 3", referencing The Karate Kid.
La Planète Donkey Kong features a sketch titled "Toc Story 2", parodying Toy Story 2.
The Donkey Kong Planet skit "La nuit des vivants-morts" features a poster for The Matrix.
The Donkey Kong Planet skit "La nuit des vivants-morts" features a poster for Starship Troopers.
Mr. Bean is mentioned in the Donkey Kong Country episode "Hooray for Holly-Kongo Bongo".
Buffy the Vampire Slayer episode "Doomed" feature a reference to Donkey Kong The Donkey Kong Planet skit "Bouffy contre les vampires" parodies Buffy the Vampire Slayer.
Picross NP Vol. 8 includes images from the Donkey Kong series.
In Pokémon Stadium 2, connecting an NES to a TV can show an image from Donkey Kong; music themes from the Pokémon series are featured in Donkey Konga games.
Donkey Kong appears as one of the video game characters in Futurama's episode Anthology of Interest II.
The Fairly OddParents episode "Fairy Fairy Quite Contrary" features a reference to Donkey Kong.
Sabre Wulf's head appear in Cranky Kong's house in the Game Boy Advance version of Donkey Kong Country.

The ending theme from Bakuryū Sentai Abaranger is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga, while the opening theme from Tokusou Sentai Dekaranger is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga 2.
The opening theme from the Hamtaro TV show is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga.
The Legend of Starfy theme is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga.
"Ai no Uta" and "Tane no Uta", the songs from the Japanese commercials for Pikmin and Pikmin 2, are featured respectively in the Japanese versions of Donkey Konga.
Themes from the Doraemon TV show are featured in the Japanese versions of Donkey Konga and Donkey Konga 2.
Opening themes from the Detective Conan TV show are featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga and in Donkey Konga 3.
The theme from the Galaxy Express 999 TV show is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga.
Nintendo UNO is a format crossover that features Donkey Kong and Diddy Kong's appearance from Donkey Kong 64.
In the Angel episode "You're Welcome", Spike plays a game implied to be Donkey Kong.
Edd imagines himself fighting Purple Kong in the Eddsworld episode "Edd Again", a parody of Donkey Kong.
The theme from the Heidi, Girl of the Alps TV show is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga 2.

The theme from the Mazinger Z TV show is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga 2. The Donkey Kong Planet skit "Le comte de Monte Costaud" has Donkey Kong use a disguise of Koji Kabuto from Mazinger Z.
The theme from Mobile Suit Gundam SEED is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga 2, while the theme from Mobile Suit Gundam SEED Destiny is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
Themes from the Naruto TV show are featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga 2 and in Donkey Konga 3.
Themes from the Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo TV show are featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga 2 and in Donkey Konga 3.
The theme from the Pretty Cure TV show is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga 2.
Songs from the Donkey Kong series are featured in Daigasso! Band Brothers.
The game It's Mr. Pants is based on the never released Donkey Kong Coconut Crackers.
Bubbles from Clu Clu Land is unlockable in DK King of Swing.
The theme from the Fullmetal Alchemist TV show is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Star Fox: Assault is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
The theme from Dragon Ball Z is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
The theme from the Shin-chan TV show is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
The song from the  Fire Emblem: Fuin no Tsurugi commercial is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Balloon Fight is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Kid Icarus is featured in Donkey Konga 3, while Kid Icarus: Uprising features a reference to Donkey Kong.
A song from Nazo no Murasame Jo is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Ice Climber is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Dig Dug is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Xevious is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Mappy is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from The Tower of Druaga is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Sky Kid is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
A song from Pac-Man is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
"The Sack" and other later episodes feature segments parodying Donkey Kong.
Dance Dance Revolution: Mario Mix includes a track from Donkey Kong.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are some references to Donkey Kong.
There's a reference to Donkey Kong in Baten Kaitos Origins.
Scott Pilgrim & The Infinite Sadness features a reference to Donkey Kong.
The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift features a reference to Donkey Kong.

Donkey Kong.game: Super Robot Monkey Team Hyperforce Go!
Donkey Kong.description: The Super Robot Monkey Team Hyper Force Go! episode "Galactic Smash: Space Attack (Part 1)" features a reference to Donkey Kong.
Evan plays Donkey Kong on his tablet in the Supernatural season 2 episode 'Everybody Loves a Clown".
Code Monkeys features references to Donkey Kong.
The Class of 3000 episode "Funky Monkey" features a reference do Donkey Kong.
The My Name Is Earl episode "Foreign Exchange Student" features a reference to Donkey Kong.

The first Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games features a reference to the game Donkey Kong, while Donkey Kong himself is selectable in its sequels; also in Donkey Kong Country 2 a pair of shoes looking like Sonic's can be seen in Cranky Kong's video game hero challenge results.
Braid features a level based on Donkey Kong.
Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People - Episode 5: 8-Bit Is Enough features a fictional game based on Donkey Kong.
The Donkey Kong arcade game is spoofed in the Spliced episode "Octocataclysm". One of Entree's udders in the episode "Juice", Cranky, holds a cane as a reference to Cranky Kong.
The Big Bang Theory episode "The Bozeman Reaction" features a reference to Donkey Kong; characters from the show play Donkey Kong Jenga in the episode "The Shiny Trinket Maneuver".
In the episode "Pinxillated" of the Pink Panther and Pals TV show, there's an arcade game similar to Donkey Kong.
The Fish Hooks episode "Fish Out of Water" features a reference to Donkey Kong.
A scene in the movie Megamind parodies Donkey Kong.

Creatures from the Metroid series appear in the background in Donkey Kong Country Returns, along with other references to the series, while Samus' Gunship and a Metroid appear in Donkey Kong: Tropical Freeze.
The Konkey Dong mini-game is a parody of Donkey Kong.

A character based on Mario can be seen in the American Dad! episode "A Piñata Named Desire", while in "School Lies" a parody of Donkey Kong can be seen; there also are other references to the game in other episodes.
Donkey Kong is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Boys Night".
Donkey Kong is mentioned in the Dick Figures episode: "Camp Anarchy".

In Duke Nukem Forever, Duke walks up a staircase while being attacked by thrown barrels from the top in Chapter 22; Duke mentions wanting a hammer at the beginning in reference to Mario's item in Donkey Kong and quips "Oh, I was expecting a monkey" when reaching the top in reference to Donkey Kong himself.
Donkey Kong is mentioned several times in Ready Player One and once in Ready Player Two.
The Two and a Half Men episode "People Who Love Peepholes" features a cabinet of Donkey Kong.
Pushmo features a level based on a sprite of Donkey Kong Jr.
Minecraft features a picture of Donkey Kong.
Donkey Kong appears in the MAD segment "Celebrity Ape-rentice".
Mii Plaza includes a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Donkey Kong Country Returns.
Once-ler mentioned to Ted about Donkey Kong.
Donkey Kong appears in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
The Gravity Falls episode "Fight Fighters" features a reference to Donkey Kong.
Random Encounters has made multiple Donkey Kong songs.
The Donkey Mong enemy in Borderlands 2 is based on Donkey Kong.
Wreck-It Ralph features some references to Donkey Kong.
Nintendo Land features a minigame based on Donkey Kong.
The videogame Lego City Undercover features a reference to Donkey Kong.
"Grapefruit vs Donkey Kong" is a Annoying Orange parody of Donkey Kong.
One customer of the Sewer Bar turns into an ape after drinking the brew's swill, and starts to hurl barrels at a red clad plumber, who dodges them by jumping in Goodbye Deponia.
NES Remix includes challenges based on Donkey Kong, Donkey Kong Jr. and Donkey Kong 3.
There's a Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker level based on the Donkey Kong Arcade game.
Nintendo Badge Arcade features badges based on Mario vs. Donkey Kong: Tipping Stars.
Johnny avoids barrels and climbs up ladders in like Jump-man in the Donkey Kong arcade games.
Posters of Donkey Kong, Diddy Kong and Cranky Kong appear in One Night at Flumpty's and One Night at Flumpty's 3.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Donkey Kong.
The Family Guy episode "Encyclopedia Griffin" features a skit based on Donkey Kong.
In the Community episode "Queer Studies and Advanced Waxing", the original Donkey Kong game is mentioned, saying that it's the rip-off of a game called "Construction snake".
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of Donkey Kong or Donkey Kong Jr.
Donkey Kong appears as one of the videogame characters in the movie, Pixels.
The Irate Gamer reviews various Donkey Kong Games
Donkey Kong has been a subject for Death Battle!
Donkey Kong appears as a playable character in Skylanders: SuperChargers.
Fallout 4 features a fictional game called "Red Menace", partially based on Donkey Kong.
Mini Mario & Friends: amiibo Challenge features a level based on Luigi's Mansion.
A poster for Donkey Kong Country 2 can be seen in Angry Video Game Nerd II: ASSimilation.
Miitopia features a costume based on Donkey Kong, obtainable by scanning a Donkey Kong amiibo.
Ronnie wears a Donkey Kong shirt in the Baywatch movie.
A poster based on the Donkey Kong series appears in the stage Ancho-V Games in Splatoon 2.

DK Barrels from the Donkey Kong series make an appearance in Mario + Rabbids: Kingdom Battle where there also is a Rabbid Kong enemy. The Donkey Kong Adventure expansion to the game is based on the Donkey Kong series and features Donkey Kong as a selectable character.
There's a minor reference to Donkey Kong Country 2 in episode 4 of Pop Team Epic.
Glenn mentions Donkey Kong in Season 3, Episode 13 of Superstore, “Video Game Release”.
"Something About Donkey Kong Country"  and "Something About Donkey Kong Country 2" are parodies of Donkey Kong Country and Donkey Kong Country 2 respectively.
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Donkey Kong.
Donkey Kong can be seen in Animation vs. Super Mario Bros.
Donkey Kong is mentioned in Into the Pit.
Crocodile Isle from Donkey Kong Country 2 is mentioned in Animal Crossing: New Horizons; there also are other minor references between the two series.
One scene from Completing the Mission uses the cannon barrels from the Donkey Kong Country series, another references the Donkey Kong 64 Rap.
The Disenchantment episode “Bean Falls Down” features a reference to a Donkey Kong level.
Enguarde from Donkey Kong Country appears in the video "berd wins a bet".
Scott the Woz once did a review on Donkey Kong: Barrel Blast.
The Animaniacs episode "WARnerGAMES" features a reference to Donkey Kong.
A Diddy Kong game box is seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
A version of Donkey Kong for the NES is included in Nintendo World Championships: NES Edition.
The "Country Monkey" spray in Antonblast is based on Donkey Kong.
Donkey Kong and other characters from Donkey Kong appear in Super Nintendo World at Universal Epic Universe.
Donkey Kong is mentioned in the version of Undertale used in the official 10th Anniversary Charity Livestream.

Donnie Darko.description: Donnie Darko and his friends has a discussion about The Smurfs.
Donnie Darko and Gretchen watch The Evil Dead.
The "rabbit" in the woods in H3 - Halloween Horror Hostel looks like Frank from Donnie Darko.
Venom mentions Donnie Darko in "How Spider-Man 3 Should Have Ended".
The second episode of Life Is Strange features a reference to Donnie Darko.
Donnie Darko is mentioned in the Community episode: "Basic Email Security".
A Donnie Darko themed icon can be unlocked in Emily is Away.
Donnie Darko is mentioned in the Riverdale episodes: "Chapter Two: A Touch of Evil", "Chapter Twenty-One: House of the Devil" and "Chapter One Hundred and Fifteen: Return to Rivervale".
In the event featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War and Call of Duty: Warzone called "The Haunting", the event features Frank from Donnie Darko.
The protagonist of Unpacking is seen owning a copy of Donnie Darko.
Donnie Darko is mentioned in Leave the World Behind.

Donutella.description: Characters from Donutella interact with characters from Cactus Friends in various web shorts and merchandise collections.
Characters from Moofia interact with characters from Donutella in various web shorts and merchandise collections.
Characters from Punkstar interact with characters from Donutella in various web shorts and merchandise collections.
Characters from Royal Pride interact with characters from Moofia in various web shorts and merchandise collections.
Characters from Donutella interact with characters from 'Til Death in various web shorts and merchandise collections.
Characters from Unicorno interact with characters from Donutella in various web shorts and merchandise collections.
There is crossover merchandise featuring characters from Donutella interacting with characters from Gudetama.
Characters from Tiger Nation interact with characters from Moofia in various web shorts and merchandise collections.

Doodle God.description: In Run Santa Run mode of Doodle God, a character looking like Batman is one of the people you need to give a present to which is The Joker.
In Run Santa Run mode of Doodle God, a character looking like Emperor Palatine is one of the people you need to give a present to which is The Death Star.
In Run Santa Run mode of Doodle God, a character looking like Bender is one of the people you need to give a present to which is different kinds of alcohol you can make in the game.

Doodle Jump.description: The Doodler from Doodle Jump appears in Pocket God mini-game "Ooga Jump". The Pygmies from Pocket God appear in Doodle Jump.
Doodle Jump is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Zarnecki Incursion".
Doodle Jump and Hop have a crossover game with Doodle Jump: HOP The Movie.
Doodle Jump and SpongeBob have a crossover game with Doodle Jump: SpongeBob SquarePants.
Doodle Jump and Batman have a crossover game with Doodle Jump: DC Super Heroes.
The Doodle Jump app can be seen in Animator vs. Animation 4.

Doogie Howser, M.D..description: Doogie Howser appears in The Earth Day Special.
Doogie Howser appears in a dream in the Roseanne episode "Less Is More".
Doogie Howser, M.D. is featured in Stay Tuned.
Doogie Howser, M.D. is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One Hundredth".
Doogie Howser is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Grasshopper Experiment".
The How I Met Your Mother episode "The Bracket" ends with Barney writing in his computerized diary as the Doogie Howser theme music plays, a reference to how episodes of the latter series end.

Doom (ID Software).description: Jazz Jackrabbit and Jazz Jackrabbit 2 feature references to Doom.

In Doom II, there is a secret level that features the world of Wolfenstein and many enemies from Wolfenstein. The final boss of Wolfenstein RPG is a Cyberdemon. Additionally, Doomguy from the Doom series has been confirmed to be the great-grandson of B.J. Blackowicz from Wolfenstein.
Doom is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One with the List".

In Duke Nukem 3D, a corpse similar to the Doomguy can be found in Episde 3, Level 1. Upon finding it, Duke quips "That's one doomed space marine"; one of the books found in the Slayer's office in Doom Eternal is titled "Why I'm So Great Pt II, By Dork Norkem"; one of the control schemes in Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown is based on the scheme of the PlayStation port of Doom and named "Doomed" and the multiplayer DLC map "Inferno" from Forever is inspired by the Doom II map "Entryway".
Chex Quest was originally created as a mod of Doom.
In Quake III Arena, Doom Slayer appears in three levels under the name "Doom".
Doom Slayer is playable in Pro Skater 3.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are Doom references.
Stewie Griffin enters map 5, episode 1 of Doom in the opening of "PTV".
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews the Sega 32X version of Doom in the episode "Sega 32X" and the Jaguar version in the episode "Atari Jaguar Part 2".
Bang, Boom, Splat! features a reference to Doom.
Fry makes a reference to Doom.
3D Dot Game Heroes features a loading screen based on Doom.
Doomguy has been a subject for Death Battle!
Doom I and II are mentioned several times in Armada.

Duke Dashington.description: Duke Dashington makes a cameo in Indie Pogo.

Duke Nukem.description: In Duke Nukem, Dr. Proton taunts Duke Nukem and further brags how Commander Keen cannot escape his mine.

In Duke Nukem 3D, a corpse similar to the Terminator and a hydraulic press can be found in Episode 3, Level 11, referencing the end of the original Terminator. Upon finding it, Duke quips "Terminated".
In Duke Nukem 3D, a corpse similar to Snake Plissken can be found in Episode 4, Level 3. Upon finding it, Duke quips "I guess he didn't escape from L.A.".
In Duke Nukem 3D, a corpse similar to Indiana Jones and a trap that pays homage to Raiders Of The Lost Ark can be found in Episode 4, Level 8. Upon finding it, Duke quips "We meet again, Dr. Jones".

In Duke Nukem 3D, a corpse similar to the Doomguy can be found in Episde 3, Level 1. Upon finding it, Duke quips "That's one doomed space marine"; one of the books found in the Slayer's office in Doom Eternal is titled "Why I'm So Great Pt II, By Dork Norkem"; one of the control schemes in Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown is based on the scheme of the PlayStation port of Doom and named "Doomed" and the multiplayer DLC map "Inferno" from Forever is inspired by the Doom II map "Entryway".

In Duke Nukem 3D, a hanging corpse similar to Luke Skywalker can be found in Episode 2, Level 7. Upon finding it, Duke quips "Now this is a force to be reckoned with". In Duke Nukem 64, Luke is replaced by Yoda.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 2, Level 3 "Warp Factor" is based on the Enterprise from Star Trek and includes recreations of its Bridge and Picard's Ready Room.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 2, Level 7 "Lunar Reactor" features a warp resembling the monolith from 2001: Space Odyssey.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 3, Level 6 "Rabid Transit" features an area based on Lex Luthor's hideout from Superman: The Movie.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 4, Level 5 "Pigsty" features a desk tag for Judge Dredd.

In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 4, Level 5 "Pigsty" features a desk tag for "J.McClane", the main character in Die Hard. Upon finding it, Duke quips "Yippee-ki-yay, motherfucker!", a quote from McClane.

In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 4, Level 5 "Pigsty" features a desk tag for "H.Callahan", the main character in Sudden Impact. Upon finding it, Duke quips "Go ahead, make my day", a quote from Callahan.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 4, Level 1 "It's Impossible" has many refereces to Mission: Impossible, including an exploding tape recorder that can hurt Duke.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 4, Level 1 "It's Impossible" includes a reference to the door opening sequence in Get Smart.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 4, Level 1 "It's Impossible" features an umbrella and hat under a tag reading "Steed", referencing John Steed from The Avengers.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 4, Level 8 "Critical Mass" features an area based on Homer Simpson's working area at the nuclear plant; other levels feature extra minor references to The Simpsons.
One of the songs in Duke Nukem 3D is based on the theme of the Mortal Kombat movie and named "Mortail Wombat".
In Duke Nukem 3D, one of the dog cages in the kennel from Episode 4, Level 2 shows the name "Scrappy Due", a reference to the Scooby-Doo character Scrappy Doo.
Duke Nukem is a playable character in Death Rally, a shareware version was included in Duke Nukem 3D: Kill-A-Ton Collection.
Duke Nukem is mentioned in the ER episode "Homeless for the Holidays".
Whenever a big explosion is triggered in Shadow Warrior, the main character says "Wow! Look like a Duke Nukem".
In Blood, a corpse hanging from a chain resembling Duke Nukem can be found in Episode 1, Level 7.

In Duke Nukem 64, a Hannibal Lecter look-alike in a similar glass prison can be found in Episode 1, Level 3, while the stage "Gates Motel" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features references to The Silence of the Lambs.

The stage "Nightmare Zone" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown is inspired by the Tomb Raider series, while the unseen character Lara from Duke Nukem: Time to Kill and Land of the Babes may be a reference to Lara Croft; Duke can also find Lara Croft's clothing in Stage 2 of Time to Kill.
The stage "Trackside Tragedy" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown is inspired by Wipeout.
The stage "Gates Motel" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features references to Resident Evil.
The stage "Gates Motel" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features references to The Shining.
The stage "Gates Motel" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features references to The Exorcist.
The stage "Duke Royale" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features locations from Reservoir Dogs.
The stage "Duke Royale" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features locations from From Dusk Till Dawn.
The stage "Duke Royale" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features locations from Pulp Fiction.
In stage 3 of the Duke Nukem 3D expansion Duke: Nuclear Winter, one can find a Mario-lookalike playing video games, his back turned to Duke.

In Duke Nukem: Time to Kill, a damaged DeLorean can be found in the underground mine of stage 6, a clear reference to the events of Back to the Future III; Upon finding it, Duke quips "Where's Doc' Brown when Ya need him?".
The secret boss Wozma from Duke Nukem: Manhattan Project is based on Ozma from Final Fantasy IX.

In Serious Sam 2, the blonde, shades-wearing skeleton of Duke Nukem can be found in Stage 10. Upon finding it, Sam quips "Dude, you've been hanging here, like, forever". In Episode 5, Level 4 of Duke Nukem 20th Anniversary World Tour, Sam's body can be found and Duke quips "Why so...serious?". There are many references to Duke Nukem in the dialogue of some Serious Sam games, often calling him "Blondie".

In the second episode of Sam & Max Beyond Time and Space there are crates underwater with an image of Duke Nukem and the initials "D.N.E." parodying the still-unreleased at the time Duke Nukem Forever.

Duke Nukem makes a cameo in the trailer for the Game of the Year Edition of Borderlands, which also included access to the Duke Nukem Forever First Access Club; the weapon Nukem from Borderlands 2 has references to Duke Nukem, while Duke Nukem Forever features Psycho's helmet as one of three collectables.

A dead body looking like Isaac Clarke from Dead Space can be found in Duke Nukem Forever, and Duke quips "That's one dead space marine";  Isaac's helmet is one of three collectable helmets in the game.

In Duke Nukem Forever, Duke is offered a power armor identical to Master Chief's, but Duke refuses saying "Power Armor is for pussies"; the helmet from the armor is one of three collectable helmets in the game and the DLC map "Sandbox" is inspired by the Halo: Combat Evolved map "Bloody Gulch".

In Duke Nukem Forever, Duke walks up a staircase while being attacked by thrown barrels from the top in Chapter 22; Duke mentions wanting a hammer at the beginning in reference to Mario's item in Donkey Kong and quips "Oh, I was expecting a monkey" when reaching the top in reference to Donkey Kong himself.
The DLC multiplayer map "Call of Duke" from Duke Nukem Forever is inspired by the Call of Duty series.
The DLC multiplayer map "2Forts1Bridge" from Duke Nukem Forever is inspired by the Team Fortress 2 map "2Fort".
Duke Nukem appears as a playable character in Choplifter HD.
Duke Nukem appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mica #32.
The Angry Video Game Nerd plays the Game.Com version of Duke Nukem 3D in the episode "Tiger Electronic Games".
In a video of the Shovelwarewolf he plays a Duke Nukem game.
Duke Nukem makes a brief cameo in the Ready Player One movie.
Duke Nukem is a playable character in Rad Rodgers: Radical Edition.

Characters from Duke Nukem appear in World of Tanks, along with cosmetics.

Dumb and Dumber.description: The title of Dumb and Dumberer: When Harry Met Lloyd is an allusion of When Harry Met Sally...
Ian and Anthony make a song parody reflecting Dumb and Dumber.
Jerry Maguire is mentioned in Dumb and Dumber To.
Titanic is mentioned in Dumb and Dumber To.
Lloyd mentioned Dig Dug in Dumb and Dumber To.
James Bond is referenced in Dumb and Dumber To.
Dumb and Dumber is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Space Probe Disintegration”.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews Dumb and Dumber.

Dumbo & Cool.description: Gish has a cameo in Dumbo & Cool.

Dumbo (Disney).description: Dumbo makes an appearance in some Mickey Mouse comics, in the Mickey Mouse Club opening and in the House of Mouse series, while the train Casey Junior appears in Mickey's Racing Adventure and in the Mickey Mouse episode "Tokyo Go"; Clara Cluck makes an appearance in the Dumbo story "Dumbo The Musician".
The stork from Dumbo appears in Lambert the Sheepish Lion.
A toy of Dumbo appears in The Great Mouse Detective.
Dumbo appears in Who Framed Roger Rabbit.
In the episode Dee Dee Locks and the Ness Monster, Dee Dee flying with her enlarged ears references Dumbo.
A clip from Dumbo is shown in Flubber.
Characters from Dumbo appear in Disney's Villains' Revenge.
Dumbo can be summoned in Kingdom Hearts.

A Dumbo plush toy can be seen in Lilo's bedroom in Lilo & Stitch. In the Stitch! episode A Recurring Nightmare, when Remmy shows Yuna the memory of her mother humming a tune to her when she was a baby, the tune she is humming is "Baby Mine" from Dumbo.
In the episode Crystals Have Power, Tree Trunks uses her ears to fly which references Dumbo.
Characters from Dumbo are seen in Kinect Disneyland Adventures.
Gloria and Manny ride the Dumbo the Flying Elephant ride in the Modern Family episode: "Disneyland". Dumbo is also mentioned in the episode: "Halloween 4: The Revenge of Rod Skyhook".
The ride version of Dumbo is a vehicle in Disney Infinity.
Dumbo is mentioned in Grandpa HATES Disneyland.
The Ringmaster has a daughter in the Descendants book Return to the Isle of the Lost.
The melody of the Kyle song and the few Kyles walking in line is a referebce to the pink elephants in the dream sequence of Disney's Dumbo.
Dumbo appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Disney Magic Kingdoms features characters from Dumbo.
Dumbo was referenced in the Henry Danger episode “The Fate of Danger”.
Dumbo is parodied in Les Kassos.
Dumbo is a fighter in Disney Sorcerer's Arena.
Official Squishmallows were released based on Dumbo.
The Dumbo the Flying Elephant ride appears in Disney Dreamlight Valley.
Dumbo appears in the credits for Wish.
Dumbo is mentioned in The Fall Guy.

Dune.description: National Lampoon's Doon is a parody of Dune.
Random Hajime from Snatcher is visually inspired by the appearance of Feyd-Rautha Harkonnen from the 1984 film Dune.
In Conker: Live and Reloaded, the planet Doon is named after the Dune franchise.
Dune is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Adhesive Duck Deficiency".
Arrakis, a planet from Dune, is mentioned in Ready Player One.
Dune is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Disemboweled By An Orphan".
The weirding module from Dune is mentioned in Armada, and the fear mantra is quoted.
Brigador features multiple references to the Dune series.
Paul Atreides and Chani from Dune (2021) appear in Fortnite.
A VHS copy of Dune is shown in Totally Killer.

A Sardaukar, Paul Atreides and Feyd-Rautha Harkonnen from Dune appear as operators in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III and Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0 along with other Dune cosmetics.
Monopoly: Dune is a format crossover between the two series.
Dune is parodied in "How DUNE Should Have Started" and "Previously On - DUNE".
The world of Dune appears in the 2020 version of Microsoft Flight Simulator as a free add-on.
The world of Dune appears in a special event for World of Tanks Blitz!.
Maps from Dune: Part Two appear in RISK: Global Domination as DLC.

Dungeon & Fighter.description: Dungeon Fighter Online had a special collaboration with the Fate/ series, including several Fate/Zero characters.
Rose from Dungeon Fighter Online appears in Elsword as part of a special collaboration.
Hatsune Miku appears in Dungeon Fighter Online for a collaboration event.
Re:Zero characters appear in Dungeon Fighter Online for a collaboration event.
Dungeon Fighter Online is mentioned in the Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episode "Lisa Shocks Us With Her Thiccness (Ft Otaku D Furiku)".
Charcters and locations from The King of Fighters appear in Dungeon Fighter Online during the DFO x SNK event.
Charcters and locations from Samurai Shodown appear in Dungeon Fighter Online during the DFO x SNK event.

Dungeon Defenders.description: The PC version of Dungeon Defenders features Pyro, Heavy, Engineer and Medic from Team Fortress 2.
The PC version of Dungeon Defenders features the Portal Gun and Weighted Companion Cube from Portal.
The PC version of Dungeon Defenders features characters from Penny Arcade.

Various items and characters from Terraria appear in Dungeon Defenders II, including the Dryad, Demon Eyes, and the Eye of Cthulhu, while various items and characters from Dungeon Defenders II appear in Terraria, including the Tavernkeep and the Old One's Army.
Piggles and Magic Dragon Fruit from Wizard101 appear in Dungeon Defenders II, while Propeller Cat from Dungeon Defenders appears in Wizard101 as a pet.

Dungeons & Dragons.description: Dungeons & Dragons features creatures based on species from the Tolkien legendarium.
The Dungeons & Dragons module Conan Unchained! is a format crossover with Conan the Barbarian.
The Dungeons & Dragons module Red Sonja Unconquered is a format crossover with Red Sonja.
Final Fantasy uses some elements from Dungeons & Dragons.
The cover art of Castlevania II: Simon’s Quest uses art from the Ravenloft module for Advanced Dungeons & Dragons.
Makai Toushi SaGa uses some elements from Dungeons & Dragons.
The King of Dragons borrows elements from Dungeons & Dragons.
The innkeeper at the beginning of Dungeons & Dragons: Tower of Doom appears very similar in appearance to Mike Haggar.
There's a poster of Dungeons & Dragons: Shadow over Mystara in one of the backgrounds in Quiz Nanairo Dreams.
Baldur's Gate takes place in the Dungeons & Dragons universe.
Dungeons & Dragons is mentioned in the Freaks and Geeks episodes: "Looks and Books" and "Discos and Dragons".
Dungeons and Dragons: Diablo II Edition is a role playing game using the D&D rules, but set in the Diablo universe, therefore being a format crossover between the two series.
Clue: Dungeons & Dragons is a format crossover between the two series.
In the episode Mid-Life Crustacean, P and P is a parody of Dungeons & Dragons. Dunces and Dragons is another parody of Dungeons & Dragons.
There are several references to Dungeons & Dragons in the Drawn Together episode Hot Tub.
Dungeons And Dragons is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Cracked China".
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews the Intellivision game Advanced Dungeons & Dragons in the episode "Double Vision: Part 1".
Characters from Dungeons & Dragons appear in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
Dungeons & Dragons is mentioned in many episodes of The Big Bang Theory.
The Adventure Time episode Dungeon feature references to Dungeons & Dragons. There are more references to Dungeons & Dragons in the Adventure Time episode What Have You Done?.
The character Peeps from the eponymous season 2 episode is based on the Beholder monster from Dungeons & Dragons.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews "Dungeons & Dragons".
Red, Blue and Pink play Dungeons & Dragons in the Dick Figures episode: "Role Playas".
Ready Player One and Ready Player Two contain several references to Dungeons and Dragons; most prominently, the Tomb of Horrors appears as an important location in the first novel.
Guenhwyvar and Drizzt from Dungeons & Dragons appear in Unit:E.
Overlord includes several references to spells and other elements from Dungeons & Dragons.
Dungeons & Dragons characters appear in the Infestation 2 Crossover event.
The "Wizard Magic" choice in Infiltrating the Airship is a spoof on Dungeons & Dragons.
One of Hiryu's color alts in the 2014 Strider is inspired by Elf from Dungeon & Dragons: Shadow over Mystara.
Vox Machina takes place in the Dungeons & Dragons universe.
Dungeon & Dragons is mentioned in Armada.

Dungeons & Dragons is frequently played by characters in Stranger Things. The comics Stranger Things and Dungeons & Dragons and Dungeons & Dragons: The Rise of Hellfire also center on Stranger Things characters playing Dungeons & Dragons.
The first episode of Life Is Strange: Before the Storm features a reference to Dungeons & Dragons.

Dungeons & Dragons.game: Betrayal at House on the Hill
Dungeons & Dragons.description: Betrayal at Baldur's Gate is a format crossover between the two series.
The Mighty Nein takes place in the Dungeons & Dragons universe. Arkhan the Cruel and Spurt the Kobold appear in Idle Champions of the Forgotten Realms.
Rick and Morty has an official comic crossover with Dungeons & Dragons.

There are official sourcebooks for Dungeons & Dragons featuring Ravnica, Theros, and Strixhaven as campaign settings, locations from Magic: The Gathering. Additionally, downloadable "Plane Shift" supplements exist depicting Magic locations Zendikar, Innistrad, Kaladesh, Amonkhet, Ixalan, and Dominaria. Characters from the Saturday morning "Dungeons & Dragons" cartoon appear depicted on alternate-art cards in limited-edition "Secret Lair Drop Series: Saturday Morning D&D" release. Additionally, Drizzt Do'Urden and many other characters appear as tournament-legal cards in "Dungeons & Dragons: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms" set.
Dungeons And Dragons is mentioned in Later Alligator.
Dice Studz played “Dungeons & Dragons” in the episode “Board Girls”.
The Duel Masters card Beholder, Orderly General features a Beholder from Dungeons & Dragons.
A Beholder and a Gelatinous Cube from Dungeons & Dragons appear in Onward.
Cutie Marks and Dragons is a Crossover Collection using the D&D rules, but set in the My Little Pony universe, therefore being a format crossover between the two series.
Everhood features a section of the game where the main characters play a game very similar to Dungeons & Dragons
A Dragon appears on the board of Monopoly: Hasbro 100th Anniversary Edition.
The world of Dungeons & Dragons appears in the Minecraft Dungeons & Dragons DLC.
Dungeons & Dragons memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Skins and maps from Dungeons & Dragons appear in Stumble Guys as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Dungeons and Dragons appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Cosmetics based on Dungeons and Dragons appear in Destiny 2.
The Dungeons & Dragons collectible minifigures series are considered format crossovers.
Dungeons & Dragons is mentioned in Class of '09: The Flip Side.
The Secret Level episode: "Dungeons & Dragons: The Queen's Cradle" is based off of Dungeons & Dragons.

Dunk Dunk.description: Yooka and Laylee appear as a playable characters in Dunk Dunk.
Beebz from Demon Turf appears as a playable character in Dunk Dunk.
The Onion King and a chef from Overcooked appear as playable characters in Dunk Dunk.

Dunston Checks In.description: The Nostalgia Critic has reviewed Dunston Checks In.

Durarara!!.description: A character dressed like Celty from Durarara!! appears in the season 2 episode "See You There" from Regular Show.
Characters from Durarara!! appear in Shin Megami Tensei IMAGINE as part of a special collaboration event.
One of Ms. Fortune's alternate color palettes in Skullgirls is based on Celty Sturluson from Durarara!!.
Shizuo Heiwajima is a playable character. Celty Sturluson and Izaya Orihara are assist characters

Toaru Majutsu no Index VS Durarara!! Special Collaboration is a crossover between the two series. Additionally, A Certain Magical Index Illusion Convergence features several characters from Durarara!! as part of a special collaboration.
Divine Gate features several characters from Durarara!! as part of a special collaboration, as well as a second one in September 27th 2015.
Characters from Durarara!! appear in Devil Survivor 2 Record Breaker.
Extraordinary Ones asia servers released skins and items from Durarara!!.

Dust: An Elysian Tail.description: The Summer of Arcade Promotional Skin Pack in Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition features skins based on characters from Dust: An Elysian Tail, as well as in Skin Pack 4 in the Xbox One Edition, and the Minecraft 2nd Birthday Skin Pack.
You can find Spelunky Boy and Girl in The Cirromon Caverrns trapped until you free them.
You can find Tim in Blackmoor Mountains trapped until you free him.
You can find Gomez in Blackmoor Mountains trapped until you free him.
You can find Meat Boy in The Glade and Bandage Girl in The Abadis Forrest trapped until you free them.
You can find The Kid in Archer's Pass trapped until you free him.
You can find The Dishwasher and Yuki in The Sorrowing Meadows trapped until you free them.
You can find The Maw in Everdawn Basin trapped until you free him.
The item "Red Orb" from Dust: An Elysian Tail is a reference to a similar item found in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
Dust is a playable character in Cook, Serve, Delicious!.
Dust from Dust: An Elysian Tail appears as a rival boss in Pocket Rumble.
Dust is a playable character in Indie Game Battle.
Dust is a playable character in Indie Pogo.

Dying Light.description: In Dying Light you can find a zombie similar to a Clicker from The Last of Us, and it also drops an item called "Clicker".
In Dying Light you can find a Mario-like pipe which leads to World 1-1 from the Super Mario Bros. game for NES.
In Dying Light, there is a reference to Plants vs. Zombies.
In Dying Light: The Following, a skeleton can be found with a whip and hat nearby. This is a possible reference to Indiana Jones.
Two antennas based on elements from Dying Light were included in Rocket League patch v1.19.
Weapons from Left 4 Dead 2 appear in Dying Light as DLC, as well as Bill and Gnome Chompski appearing in the second DLC pack.
Weapons based on Chivalry appear in Dying Light as part of a collaboration event.
Weapons and armor based on Rust appear in Dying Light as part of a collaboration.
You can find a dog tag for a man named Chris Bluefield in Dying Light 2.
Characters from Dying Light appear in the Siege Tales episodes "DropKick Spam in Dying Light 2" and "Smashing Zombies in Dying Light 2" as part of a sponsorship from Techland.
Weapons and accessories based on The Walking Dead appear in Dying Light 2 as part of a special collaboration.
Weapons and accessories based on Payday 2 appear in Dying Light 2 as part of a special collaboration.
Weapons and accessories based on For Honor appear in Dying Light 2 as part of a special collaboration.
Weapons and accessories based on Balatro appear in Dying Light 2 as part of a special collaboration.

Dynamite Deka.description: Dynamite Deka is a spinoff of Die Hard Arcade.

Death Adder from Golden Axe is the third stage boss in the Sega Saturn version of Dynamite Deka, while Easy mode also features costumes based on Tyris Flame and Ax Battler from Golden Axe. Chicken Leg appears in Dynamite Deka 2.

A Cockatrice enemy from Altered Beast makes a background cameo in the 2nd stage of Dynamite Cop, while the Werewolf and Garuda transformations appear as costumes for Bruno and Cindy in the Sega Ages remake of Dynamite Deka.
Bruno Delinger makes a cameo appearance as a playable character in The House of the Dead 2.
A human version of Dynamite Cop appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.

Dynamix.description: Characters and music from Dynamix appear in Arcaea while music from Arcaea appears in Dynamix as part of a special collaboration.
Characters and music from Dynamix can be found in Paradigm: Reboot as part of a special collaboration.

Dynomutt, Dog Wonder.description: Characters from Scooby-Doo appear in the Dynomutt, Dog Wonder episodes "Everyone Hyde!", "What Now, Lowbrow?" and "The Wizard of Ooze"; characters from Dynomutt, Dog Wonder appear in the Scooby-Doo comic stories "Big House Brouhaha" and "It Was a Dark and Gritty Knight..." as well as the Scooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated episode "Heart of Evil", the Scooby-Doo and Guess Who? episode "Scooby-Doo, Dog Wonder!", and the movie Scoob; Scooby-Doo! Mask of the Blue Falcon is a crossover between the two series.
Characters from Dynomutt, Dog Wonder appear in Laff-A-Lympics.
The Blue Falcon and Dynomutt appear in the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Dyno-Might".
Dynomutt and Blue Falcon (called Azul Falcone in Harvey Birdman) appear in the Harvey Birdman episodes "Deadomutt, Part 1" and "Deadomutt, Part 2".
The Blue Falcon appears in Johnny Makeover/Back on Shaq.
The Blue Falcon appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #24. Dynomutt appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #61.
Blue Falcon and Dynomutt appear in Space Jam: A New Legacy.
Dynomutt and the Blue Falcon appear in the Jellystone! episode "Heroes and Capes".

E.T..description: The character of Michael in E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial wears a Space Invaders t-shirt.
The Tom & Jerry short "The Mouse Comes to Dinner" appeared on T.V. because E.T. doesn't like it.
Indiana Jones makes a cameo in the game E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial for Atari 2600. E.T. appears as one of the tiles in Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull.
A Yar from Yars' Revenge makes a cameo in the game E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial for Atari 2600.
The "phone home" scene from E.T. is parodied in Airplane II: The Sequel.
In E.T. and Friends: Magical Movie Visitors, Beldar and Connie from The Coneheads make a cameo.
The Italian Mickey Mouse story Topolino in... E.B. l'extraterrestre is a parody of E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial.
Brian Tanner calls Alf "E.T." in the ALF episode "ALF".
Many elements of E.T. were used in the movie, Mac and Me.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! live action episode "E.C. The Extra Creepy" is a parody of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial.
E.T. appears in The Earth Day Special.
An E.T. cosplayer appears in issue 6 of the comic Men In Black.
E.T. is mentioned in the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "Out of the Past - Part II".

E.T. is mentioned in the Friends episodes: "The One Where Old Yeller Dies" and "The One with the Ride-Along". Monica, Chandler and Phoebe watch E.T.: The Extraterrestrial in the episode: "The One Where Chandler Can't Cry".
E.T. is mentioned in the Daria episode "Pierce Me".
The Grebleips' species appear in The Phantom Menace.
There are references to E.T. in Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back.
The main character enters the E.T. universe via the E.T. Adventure ride.
A street billboard for E.T. is briefly seen in one panel from Chapter 105 of Stone Ocean.
E.T. is mentioned in the King Of The Hill episode "Of Mice And Little Green Men".
Roger Smith says he does not have an 'ET finger thing' in the American Dad episode "Pilot".

In Fear of a Krabby Patty, in SpongeBob's dream, the Krabby Patty tells him that he will always be with him in his arteries, a reference to E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, complete with the glowing finger.
In the My Name Is Earl episode "Faked My Own Death", E.T. is mentioned.
E.T. is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Cracked China".
E.T. appears in "Ocean's 40 Trailer".
In the second episode of the series, Dave is almost enters the cinema to see E.T..

The Angry Video Game Nerd shows briefly the Atari game E.T. in the episodes "Halloween" and "Spielberg Games", then mentions it in the episode "Schwarzenegger Games"; the plot of The Angry Video Game Nerd: The Movie is centered around the E.T. game and he also reviews it in the 120th episode of the series.
The Irate Gamer reviews E.T. on Atari 2600
E.T. is mentioned in Meet Dave.
Actors play out the flying bike scene from ET in the Oggy And The Cockroaches episode: "Oggywood".
"ET GO HOME" is written on missiles in Monsters VS Aliens.
E.T. is mentioned in the Community episode "Home Economics".
In the Adventure Time episode It Came from the Nightosphere, the title card is a reference to a famous scene from E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial.
E.T. is mentioned in Paul.
E.T. was mentioned in The Smurfs (2011).
The E.T. video game is mentioned in Ready Player One.
An E.T. doll is shown in Thousand Words.
Assets based on E.T. could be obtained in Universal Movie Tycoon.
E.T. is mentioned in Pitch Perfect.
E.T. appears in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
E.T. is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episodes “The Communication Deterioration”, "The Viewing Party Combustion", and "The Convergence Convergence".
Elliot and E.T. cameo in Lego Jurassic World.
E.T. is mentioned twice in Armada.
E.T. is parodied in Les Kassos.
Hank does a shadow puppet recreation of the flying bike scene from E.T. in Swiss Army Man.
The E.T. Universe appears in the game.
A pinball table based on E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX 3 that features characters from the series.
In the Happy! episode "Destroyer of Worlds", Happy describes "that movie where the iguana phoned home", a reference to E.T.
Eddie Brock in Venom does an impression of E.T.
In a video of the Shovelwarewolf he plays an E.T. game.
E.T. is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Putting Down Roots".
A decal based on E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial is available in Rocket League as part of the "Radical Summer" event.
E.T. is mentioned in Into the Pit.
Lydia mentions E.T. in the Solar Opposites episode “The Matter Transfer Array”.
E.T. appears in Funko Pop! Blitz.
Monopoly: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial is a format crossover between the two series.
E.T. appears on TV in Rescue Rangers (2022).
E.T. is mentioned in the Beef episode: "The Birds Don't Sing, They Screech in Pain".
E.T. is mentioned in Leo.
A ride based on E.T.: The Extra Terrestrial is included in Minecraft's "Universal Studios Experience" DLC.
E.T. is mentioned in the Ted episode: "Ejectile Dysfunction".

ER is mentioned in the Joey episode: "Joey and the Valentine's Date".
Ghost is mentioned in the ER episode "Out On A Limb".
ER is mentioned in Bee Movie.
In Persona 5, you can obtain DVD of a parody of ER.

EZ2DJ.description: Groove Coaster Wai Wai Party featured a DLC pack featuring music from EZ2ON as well as characters that are selectable as navigators and avatars while EZ2ON REBOOT : R features music from Groove Coaster as part of a special collaboration.

Sammo Law from Martial Law appears in the Early Edition episode "Play It Again, Sammo".

Earth Defense Force (D3 Publisher).description: A Defense Force soldier appears as a fighter in All-Star Fighters.
An Earth Defense Force 5 trailer promotes Starship Troopers: Traitor of Mars using a news broadcast to link the two series.

The Pale Wing costumes from Earth Defense Force 2017 Portable appear as DLC outfits in Onechanbara Z2: Chaos. Aya and Saki from Onechanbara appear as DLC characters in Earth Defense Force: World Brothers.

Earthworm Jim.description: In the Sega CD version of Earthworm Jim, a Donkey Kong mask is unlockable; in Donkey Kong Country 2 a gun looking like Earthworm Jim's can be seen in Cranky Kong's video game hero challenge results.
Earthworm Jim is a selectable character in the PC version of Battle Arena Toshinden.
In "Clayfighter 63⅓" Earthworm Jim is a playable character.
Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum features a reference to Earthworm Jim.
Enter the Gungeon a features weapon resembling Earthworm Jim's blaster.
The 208th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the Earthworm Jim trilogy.
A replica of Earthworm Jim's blaster can be seen in the music video for FNAF Kids.
The "Blastworm Blast" spray in Antonblast is based on Earthworm Jim.

EastEnders.description: EastEnders and Doctor Who have a television crossover together in "Dimensions in Time".
The Bureau, the show featured within The Day Today, is a parody of EastEnders.
Den Watts and Grant Mitchel's descendants appears in League of Extraordinary Gentlemen.
In Little Britain, Dennis Waterman talks about auditioning for EastEnders. In another episode, the narrator mentions EastEnders.
Lauren Cooper appears in EastEnders as a Children in Need sketch.
EastEnders is mentioned in The Thick of It.
Mr Blobby fights Heather Mills and Phil Mitchell in Harry Hill's TV Burp.
"East Street" is a crossover episode between Coronation Street and EastEnders.
Monopoly: EastEnders is a format crossover between the two series.
