George from Evil and Nick Newman from The Young and the Restless appear together in a commercial for Evil.

Evil Bong.description: The Gingerdead Man appears in Evil Bong and some of its sequels, with Gingerdead Man vs. Evil Bong and the comic The Gingerdead Man Meets Evil Bong being crossovers between the two series.
Elvira smokes from Eebee the Evil Bong in the eleventh episode of 13 Nights of Elvira.
Dollman fights Gingerweed Man in the extra San Diego Comic Con exclusive story in Dollman Kills the Full Moon Universe #1.

Evil Con Carne.description: Evil Con Carne is a spinoff to Grim and Evil.

Evil Con Carne.game: The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy
Evil Con Carne.description: In The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy episode, Chicken Ball Z, Mandy bought Bunny Island from Hector Con Carne from Evil Con Carne, and took charge of becoming it's new, evil dictator, bent on dominating the world. General Skarr would later become a regular character in the series.
In the Evil Con Carne episode “No No Nanook”, a spoof of Gollum named Shlamegal and a Frodo spoof get run over in the snow cave twice.
In the Evil Con Carne episode “Ultimate Evil”, Boskov is forced to watch The Powerpuff Girls. Hector does an impression of Mojo Jojo in the Evil Con Carne episode "Hector, King of the Britons".
Hector does an impression of Huckleberry Hound in the Evil Con Carne episode "Hector, King of the Britons".
Major Dr. Ghastly from Evil Con Carne appears in the OK K.O.! Let's Be Heroes episode Crossover Nexus.
Accessories based on Evil Con Carne appear in KleptoCats: Cartoon Network.
Hector Con Carne, Boskov and Stomach appear in the Jellystone! special "Crisis on Infinite Mirths".

Evil Dead.description: An Evil Dead video case is shown in Video Violence.

The Evil Hand enemy from Splatterhouse is a reference to Evil Dead, and laughing deer heads are featured in Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti and Splatterhouse 2. In the 2010 Splatterhouse Phase Four: "The Meat Factory", Rick finds a shotgun next to a corpse that looks similar to Ashley William, missing hand included.
The Necronomicon and Skull Dagger from the Evil Dead series make an appearance in Jason Goes to Hell; Freddy vs. Jason vs. Ash is a direct crossover between the two series.
In the comic Super Mario in Die Nacht des Grauens - Part 2 Mario receives the Necronomicon book from a skeleton buried under a gravestone with the name "Ash" written on it.
The episode "To Mend and Defend" from ReBoot features a parody of the Evil Dead series.
The name of the game MediEvil comes from the original title of Army of Darkness, The MediEvil Dead. The Severed Hand enemies in MediEvil are also a reference to the Evil Dead films.
Donnie Darko and Gretchen watch The Evil Dead.

Evil Dead.game: The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy
Evil Dead.description: In Billy's Growth Spurt, the part where the growth is first discovered on Billy is a reference to a scene from Army of Darkness from Evil Dead.
The episode Remains to be Seen features a reference to Evil Dead.
Evil Dead is featured in "Evil Dead - Scottman."
Darkman vs. Army of Darkness is a crossover between the two series.
Marvel Zombies vs. Army of Darkness is a crossover between the two series.

A Nightmare on Elm Street features a reference to The Evil Dead, while Evil Dead II features a reference to the Nightmare on Elm Street series; Freddy vs. Jason vs. Ash is a direct crossover between the two series.
The plot of the first Evil Dead film is parodied in H3 – Halloween Horror Hostel.
Army of Darkness / Xena, Xena / Army of Darkness, and Army of Darkness / Xena: Warrior Princess: Forever... And a Day are crossovers between the two series.
Ash from Evil Dead appears in "Spider-Man 3 How It Should Have Ended".
The first Fight Klub set features cards based on Army of Darkness, including a character card of Ash Williams.
The Necronomicon and Skeletal Warriors objects in Scribblenauts are a reference to The Army of Darkness.
Jennifer has an Evil Dead poster in Jennifer's Body.
In the episode "Slumber Party Panic", a zombie says "Gimme some sugar, baby", quoting Ash Williams from Army of Darkness. Jake's possessed arm from "Bad to Worse" is a reference to Evil Dead II.
Evil Dead is mentioned in Ready Player One.
Jake English has a poster for Army of Darkness in Homestuck.
Deadites from Evil Dead make cameos in The Cabin in the Woods.
Juliet has an outfit based on Ash from Army of Darkness.
Poker Night 2 features Ash from the Evil Dead series as one of the main characters.
Borderlands 2 features an unlockable head skin representing Evil Ash from The Army of Darkness.
Ash Brolliams is based on Ash Williams from The Evil Dead.
Army of Darkness vs. Hack/Slash is a crossover between the two series.
Vampirella/Army of Darkness is a crossover between the two series.
A scene in Until Dawn pays homage to Evil Dead.
Ash Williams from Ash vs Evil Dead appears in Family Guy: The Quest for Stuff's The Hauntening event.
The world of Evil Dead takes part of Deploy And Destroy.
Ash Williams appears as DLC for Dead by Daylight.
In "Chibi Tiny Tales Triple Date", a poster similar in design to The Evil Dead poster can be seen.
The Army of Darkness versus Re-Animator: Necronomicon Rising is a crossover between the two series.
Ash Williams from the Evil Dead series appears in Fortnite.
Characters from Evil Dead appear in the "Secret Lair Spookydrop" release for Magic: The Gathering.
Ash Williams from Evil Dead appears as an operator in Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 along with other Evil Dead cosmetics.
Red Sonja vs. the Army of Darkness is a crossover between the two series.
Archie x The Army of Darkness is a crossover between the two series.

Evil Ernie.description: The Final Revenge of Evil Ernie is a crossover between the two series.
Evil Ernie appears in Red Sonja: Age of Chaos.

Evolution Skateboarding.description: Solid Snake and Raiden are selectable in Evolution Skateboarding, while Metal Gear Solid 2: Substance features a minigame with elements from Evolution Skateboarding.
Frogger is selectable in Evolution Skateboarding.

There is a stage called Dracula's Castle which features Dracula, Skeletons, but most important to the series to link these two as type 1 is a Brachyura. The character, Vampire Hunter is unlockable in the game who is similar to Simon Belmont.

Evolve.description: A team consisting of characters from Evolve appears in #IDARB.
Lazarus from Evolve was likely designed after Francis from Left 4 Dead. The Goliath Monster from Evolve borrows gameplay elements of the Tank from Left 4 Dead.

Excel Saga.description: Nabeshin from Excel Saga makes an appearance in Eyeshield 21.
Nabeshin from Excel Saga makes an appearance in To Be Hero.

Excite.description: Excitebike: Bun Bun Mario Battle Stadium is a crossover between the two series; The downloadable content pack The Legend of Zelda × Mario Kart 8 for Mario Kart 8 includes a track based on Excitebike.
ExciteBike is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Crossing.

In the microgame "Unexcite Bike", featured in WarioWare, inc.: Minigame Mania, Wario meets the Excite Bikers; Microgame versions of Excitebike are featured in WarioWare: Twisted! and WarioWare: D.I.Y.
One of the themes in Standard Mode of Tetris DS is based on Excitebike.
Metroid Prime 3: Corruption features an unlockable sticker based on Excite Truck.
The Excitebikers from Excitebike are an Assist Trophy in Super Smash Bros. Brawl; the Beetle from Excitebots: Trick Racing also appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Pushmo features two levels based on sprites from Excitebike.
In the episode Incendium, BMO's game is a parody of Excitebike.
The "High School Video Game" features an Excitebike sprite as the first level icon.
NES Remix includes challenges based on Excite Bike.
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of Excitebike
The Irate Gamer reviews ExciteBike on NES
Music from Excitebike is included in the Famicom Medley, in Taiko no Tatsujin Red Version.
Excitebike can be seen in Animation vs. Super Mario Bros.

Exed Exes.description: The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an enemy in Exed Exes.
" SON SON " is one of the random placeholder names in the hi-score screen in Exed Exes.
"EXED.EXES" is one of the default names in the hi-score screen in Commando.
"EXED.EXES" is one of the default names in the hi-score screen in Legendary Wings.
"EXED.EXES" is one of the default names in the hi-score screen in Side Arms.
"EXED.EXES" is one of the default names in the hi-score screen in Avengers.
Exed Exes is included in Capcom Classics Collection and Capcom Classics Colection Reloaded.
One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of an enemy sprite from Exed Exes.
"Exed Exes" is one of the unlockable Nom de Guerres in Lost Planet 2.
Exed Exes is included in Capcom Arcade Cabinet as part of the "Game Pack 3".
Exed Exes is included in Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium.
Exed Exes is a playable Arcade in the Game Center of Street Fighter 6.

Exist Archive.description: Costumes based on Star Ocean appear in Exist Archive as part of a special collaboration.
Costumes based on Valkyrie Profile appear in Exist Archive as part of a special collaboration.
A Monokuma costume is available as DLC for Exist Archive: The Other Side of the Sky.

Exoprimal.description: Robot versions of Ryu, Guile, and Chun Li from Street Fighter 6 appear in Exoprimal as part of a special collaboration.
Rathalos from Monster Hunter appears in Exoprimal as part of a special collaboration, along with several cosmetics based on Monster Hunter.
Mega Man appears in Exoprimal as part of a special collaboration, along with several cosmetics based on Mega Man.

Expert Wrassling.description: Ref makes a cameo in Indie Pogo, appearing as the judge after a match ends.

Exploding Kittens.description: Exploding Minions is a format crossover between the two series.
A pinball table based on Exploding Kittens was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX that features characters from the series.
Avatars based on Exploding Kittens characters appear as DLC in Walkabout Mini Golf VR.

Extraordinary Ataro.description: Characters from Osomatsu-san have appeared in episodes of Extraordinary Ataro several times throughout the series.
Nyarome and Kemunpas from Extraordinary Ataro appear as the hosts of Mi-Pha-Pu.

Extraordinary Ones.description: My Hero Academia characters are playable in Extraordinary Ones.
Skins for Killer Seven and Thirteen from Scissor Seven were added to the Chinese servers of Extraordinary Ones.
Extraordinary Ones released 7723 from Next Gen as a playable hero.
Mob Psycho 100 characters are playable in Extraordinary Ones.
Durarara!! characters are playable in Extraordinary Ones.
Extraordinary Ones released skins and items from A Certain Scientific Accelerator and A Certain Scientific Railgun T.
KonoSuba characters are playable in Extraordinary Ones.
Re:Zero characters are playable in Extraordinary Ones.

Extreme Dinosaurs.description: Extreme Dinosaurs is a spin-off of Street Sharks.
Extreme Dinosaurs is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Catdog On A Stick".

Eyeshield 21.description: Nabeshin from Excel Saga makes an appearance in Eyeshield 21.
Characters from Eyeshield 21 appear in Jump Super Stars and Jumputi Heroes as playable characters.
Taiko no Tatsujin 9 features a music track from Eyeshield 21.
The Eyeshield 21 episode "3 Brothers Of Texas Ranch" features a game based on Tekken 2.

F Troop.description: Chief Screaming Chicken from the 1966 Batman series is a parody of Roaring Chicken from F Troop.
The F Troop theme song is briefly heard on a television in Rover Dangerfield.
F Troop is mentioned in the Freakazoid! episode "Candle Jack".

F-1 Race.description: Famicom Grand Prix: F-1 Race is part of both series.
Mario is the pilot in Famicom Grand Prix: F-1 Race; Mario, Luigi, Toad, Peach and Bowser appear in F-1 Race for the Game Boy.
Link makes a cameo in the Game Boy version of F-1 Race.
Samus makes a cameo in the Game Boy version of F-1 Race.
Pit makes a cameo in the Game Boy version of F-1 Race.
Donkey Kong makes a cameo in the Game Boy version of F-1 Race.

F-Zero.description: F-Zero takes some stylistic elements from Mach Rider.
The game F-Mega is shown in Chapter 117 of Stardust Crusaders, which is a parody of the game F-Zero.

Captain Falcon makes a cameo in the comic Super Mario: Im Rausch der Geschwindigkeit and in Volume 4 of Super Mario-kun; One of the tracks in F-Zero X is the "Rainbow Road" from Mario Kart 64; The downloadable content pack The Legend of Zelda × Mario Kart 8 for Mario Kart 8 includes a track based on F-Zero.
Captain Falcon's Helmet is an obtainable item in Kirby Super Star.
Jody Summer from F-Zero X is based on Samus from Metroid.

Captain Falcon is selectable in Super Smash Bros. and its sequels, where stages from the series also appear, with Samurai Goroh appearing as an Assist Trophy in Super Smash Bros. Brawl; Captain Falcon performs a Falcon Punch in the last episode of the anime F-Zero: GP Legend.
Captain Falcon appears in the N-Gang episode "Freeze Frame".
In Pokémon Stadium 2, connecting the SNES to a TV can show an image from F-Zero.
A microgame version of F-Zero is featured in WarioWare, inc.: Minigame Mania.
A R.O.B. shaped crane appears in F-Zero GX.
The "Groovy Taxi" vehicle in F-Zero GX is a reference to the Crazy Taxi series.
AiAi from Super Money Ball appears F-Zero GX on Billy's belt and an Emblem in Garage Mode.
Digi-Boy in F-Zero GX may be based on Beat from Jet Set Radio.
One of the emblems in F-Zero GX's Garage Mode represents Sonic the Hedgehog; Aliens looking like Chaos from the Sonic series make an appearance in F-Zero GX.
A trailer for F-Zero GX is included in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Master Quest; One of the emblems in F-Zero GX's Garage Mode represents Tingle from the Zelda series.
Music from the F-Zero series is featured in Daigasso! Band Brothers.
Blue Falcon and Black Bull, the two bosses in the game, are named after the racing cars in F-Zero.

James McCloud from F-Zero X is based on Fox and James McCloud from the StarFox series; Leon from F-Zero GX may be a reference to Wolf O'Donnell; Octoman from the F-Zero series makes an appearance in Star Fox Command; there also are other references between the two series.
X-Scape features a reference to the F-Zero series.
Random Encounters has made multiple F-Zero songs.
Nintendo Land features a minigame based on the F-Zero series.
Tekken Tag Tournament 2: Wii U Edition features a Captain Falcon outfit for the characters.
Jay performs the Falcon Punch in the Deep Space 69 episode “The Galactic Bonesmen: Part 2”.
F-Zero is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of F-Zero
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed Captain Falcon from F-Zero X.
There's a Monstermon card based on Captain Falcon called "Faptain Calcon"
Captain Falcon has been a subject for DBX.
A giant cartridge based on F-Zero appears in Splatoon 2: Octo Expansion.
F-Zero is parodied in multiple Perfect Cell Vs episodes.
Captain Falcon has been a subject for Death Battle!
Captain Falcon has been a subject for Death Race.
Many elements of Star Racer are heavily based on F-Zero.

FAITH.description: A drawing of V1 from ULTRAKILL can be found in Chapter 3 of FAITH: The Unholy Trinity.
A Horror from DUSK can be found outside the Shack in Chapter 3 of FAITH: The Unholy Trinity.
Graffiti of WD Gaster can be found in Chapter 3 of FAITH: The Unholy Trinity.
Graffiti of Uboa can be found in Chapter 3 of FAITH: The Unholy Trinity.
Graffiti of White Face can be found in Chapter 3 of FAITH: The Unholy Trinity.

FIFA.description: George and Will play FIFA 2001 in Stuart Little 2.
The FIFA Street series follows the same formula as the NBA Street series.
In The Sims 2, sims can play FIFA 08.
Captain S enters the world of Fifa International Soccer.
NBA Elite has mode based on "Be a Pro Mode" in FIFA.
A limited-time event in Roblox promoted the FIFA games with FIFA-themed clothing.
Cosmetics based on Apex Legends appear in FIFA 22 as part of a special collaboration.

FLCL.description: A Kenny doll can be seen in the episode "Marquis de Carabas" of FLCL.
One of Valentine's alternate color palettes in Skullgirls is based on Haruko Haruhara from FLCL.
Super Robot Wars X-Ω features units from FLCL.

FLIP.description: Matthew writes Gollum on his hand then does an impression of Gollum in FLIP.

FTL: Faster Than Light.description: The achievements "Tough Little Ship", "The United Federation", "Bird of Prey", "Rule Ten: Greed is Eternal", "Givin' her all she's got Captain!" and "No Redshirts Here" are all references to Star Trek.
The achievement "The guns... They've stopped" is a reference to Star Wars VI: A New Hope.
The achievement "Trustworthy Auto-Pilot" is a reference to 2001: A Space Odyssey.
One of the randomised crew names can be Dr. Jones, a reference to Indiana Jones.
One of the randomised crew names can be Garrus, a reference to Mass Effect.
One of the randomised crew names can be Butters, a reference to South Park.
Rockman is an assist in Fraymakers.

Factory Panic.description: Arino plays Ganbare Gorby! during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.

Fahrenheit (Quantic Dream).description: Characters from Fahrenheit star in the "Little Sister" video of Video Mods.
A "Citizen Cage" poster can be found in Fahrenheit.
Some endings of Heavy Rain takes place in Lucas Kane's apartment from Fahrenheit.
A game cover of Beyond: Two Souls can be found in the remastered version of Fahrenheit.

Fairly OddParents.description: There is multiple references to The Simpsons throughout The Fairly OddParents.
In short "The Fairly OddParents!", the "I am your father" quote is an obvious reference to the iconic Darth Vader quote. There's other references to Star Wars throughout the series.
Titanic is mentioned in the Oh Yeah! Cartoons short "The Fairly OddParents!".
In the short "Party of Three!" from Oh Yeah! Cartoons, Timmy says "Warp speed, Mr. Sulu" while riding a roller coaster.
Voltron is mentioned in the short "The Temp!" from Oh Yeah! Cartoons.
The Partridge Family is mentioned in the short "The Zappys!" from Oh Yeah! Cartoons.
"The Zappys!" features a reference to Friends.
A kid looking like Sid Phillips from Toy Story appears in "The Big Problem".
The show "I Love Wanda" is a parody of I Love Lucy.
The show Cosmo from the episode "Power Mad!" is a parody of Seinfield.
There are several references to The Matrix in The Fairly OddParents.
The Fairly OddParents episode "Power Mad!" is a parody of Tron.
The episode "Power Mad!" feature sound effects from Mario.
The episode "Power Mad!" from The Fairly OddParents feature references to Sonic.

In "Power Mad!" A.J. falls off a ladder and Chester stays on it, referencing Road Runner from Looney Tunes. "Channel Chasers" feature references to Looney Tunes. The Fairly OddParents episode "Back to the Norm" features a reference to Wile E. Coyote and Road Runner.

Fairly OddParents.game: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (Disney)
Fairly OddParents.description: Vicky's kindness portrayal from "Tiny Timmy!" is a satire of Snow White, even the animals helping Vicky clean up the house are a parody of the animals that help Snow White when she needs their help.
Tinklebell is a parody of Tinker Bell.
In "Tiny Timmy!", Timmy and various germs touring Vicky's body is similar to The Magic School Bus episodes "Goes Lunch" and "Goes Cellular".
Cleft the Boy Chin Wonder is a parody of Robin. In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Blackbird and Sparrow, a parody of Batman and Robin.
In "Dog's Day Afternoon", at one point, Timmy (in Doidle's body) does the same wheezing laugh as Muttley.
A.J.'s secret lab from "Information Stupor Highway" is a reference to Dexter's secret lab.
The ending of "Information Stupor Highway" is a reference to Dora the Explorer.
There are several references to Die Hard in The Fairly OddParents episode "Action Packed".
The Fairly OddParents episode "Fairy Fairy Quite Contrary" features a reference to Donkey Kong.
In The Fairly OddParents episode "The Secret Origin of Denzel Crocker!", a DeLorean can be seen time traveling, a reference to Back to the Future.

"Pipe Down" features Timmy somehow managing to misinterpret a rowboat gesture in a game of charades as the entirety of Ghostbusters II. In "Fairly Odd Baby" Chet Ubetcha says "Dogs and Cats living together... It's mass hysteria." This is a reference to the Ghostbusters line "Human sacrifice, dogs and cats living together... Mass hysteria!". "Poltergeeks" parodies Ghostbusters.
In the beginning of "Abra-Catastrophe" Timmy is dressed as Spider-Man.
The beginning of "Abra-Catastrophe!" has a parody of Jurassic Park.
The episodes "Abra-Catastrophe!" and "Just Desserts!" feature references to Popeye. The show "Poke Eye the Longshoreman" is a parody of Popeye.
In The Fairly OddParents episode "The Big Superhero Wish!", Vicky is seen as a villain called The Baby Shredder who resembles Wolverine.
The Power Pals are a parody of the Justice League.

Jimmy, Carl, and Cindy were mentioned in The Fairly OddParents episode "Sleepover and Over". Jimmy Neutron and The Fairly OddParents have a crossover called Jimmy Timmy Power Hour. They also have comic crossovers.
Yogi Bear was mentioned in "Jimmy Timmy Power Hour".
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Maho Mushi, a parody of Dragon Ball.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show The Futurellis, a parody of The Jetsons.

In "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Poppyseed Avenue, a parody of Sesame Street. In the season 6 episode "Odd Pirates", the monsters holding the letters "R" and "C" are a reference to Sesame Street.
In "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Adolescent Genetically Modified Karate Cows, a parody of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Heavy Hal, a parody of Fat Albert.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Johnny Hunt, a parody of Johnny Quest.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Paula Poundcake, a parody of Strawberry Shortcake.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Space Spectre, a parody of Space Ghost.

In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Walnuts, a parody of Peanuts. Charlie Brown, Snoopy, and Lucy appear in The Fairly OddParents episode "Bad Heir Day". Charlie Brown, Snoopy, and Woodstock appear in a flashback from "Let Sleeper Dogs Lie".
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show The Meatflints, a parody of The Flintstones.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Go Racer Go!, a parody of Speed Racer.

In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Snooper Dog and the Clue Crew, a parody of Scooby-Doo. The Scooby-Doo gag is referenced in the episode "Dread 'N' Breakfast", while parodies of Scooby and Shaggy appear in the same episode. The MERF van from "Wishology!" is a parody of the Mystery Machine. Season 9 and 10 of The Fairly OddParents feature many references to Scooby-Doo.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Carpet Critters, a parody of Rugrats. Dill Pickles from Rugrats makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".

In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Ted and Jimmy, a parody of Tom and Jerry. The episode "Mice Capades" features a show called "Sleazy and Cheezy" a parody of Tom and Jerry and the plot of the episode parodies Tom and Jerry.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Clint's Hints, a parody of Blue's Clues. Lookee Lookee's Lunchbox is a reference to Blue's Clues.
In the episode "Channel Chasers", there is a brief reference of a reindeer planning on insulting another reindeer with a glowing red nose.
The Fairly OddParents characters are featured in several Nicktoons games.
The soap opera All My Biceps featured in The Fairly OddParents is a parody of All My Children.
Cosmo and Wanda from The Fairly OddParents appear in Ned's Declassified School Survival Guide.
The episode "The "Good Old Days!"" featur references to Mickey Mouse.
In "When Nerds Collide!" Cindy is holding a Hockey Mask referencing Jason Voorhees. A character resembling Jason appears in "The Big Fairy Share Scare!"
Snap from ChalkZone makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".
Donnie and Darwin make cameos in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".
Krumm from Aaahh!!! Real Monsters makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".
Truman from The X's makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".
Daggett from The Angry Beavers makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".
Appa from Avatar: The Last Airbender makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".

Fairly OddParents.game: My Life as a Teenage Robot
Fairly OddParents.description: Mrs. Wakeman from My Life as a Teenage Robot makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".
Mr. Blik from Catscratch makes a cameo in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".
The Fairly OddParents episode "Mission Responsible" parodies Roger Rabbit.
"Odd Pirates", features a reference to Banjo-Kazooie
The episode "For Emergencies Only" features a reference to Transformers, Transmorphers is a parody of Transformers.
In The Fairly OddParents episode "The End of the Universe-ity", one of the sailors that appeared at the end has a similar appearance to Bandit Keith.
In Wishology!, Timmy is dressed as Harry Potter, Poof takes the form of a golden quidditch snitch, and Vicky is Moldywart, which is Lord Voldemort.
In "Wishology!", Cosmo is fed up with Eliminator 0 constantly attacking his family and godchild, so he transforms into a giant creature named "Cos-zilla", a parody of Godzilla.
Cosmo and Wanda appear in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #15.
At the end of "Super Zero" Wanda is dressed as Wonder Woman.

Posters of The Fairly OddParents can be seen in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Truth or Square". In the FairlyOdd Parents episode "Ruled Out", Mr. Turner says that "pants are for squares", a reference to SpongeBob. Patrick, Mr. Krabs, and Sandy are referenced in The Fairly OddParents episode "Something's Fishy!". SpongeBob was referenced by Timmy Turner in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".  In the Fairly OddParents episode "App Trap", there is a person that looks like SpongeBob.
Garfield is drawn on a cup in "Manic Mom-Day"
The Fairly OddParents characters are playable in Super Brawl.

Poof makes a cameo as a fountain fish in the T.U.F.F. Puppy episode "Mall Rat." Dudley makes cameos in various episodes of The Fairly OddParents as well as one of the head gags. "The Fairly Odd Phantom" is a crossover between The Fairly OddParents, Danny Phantom, T.U.F.F. Puppy and Bunsen is a Beast. They also have the same crossover in a comic.
Pencil Nexus' interior parodies the Chocolate Factory.

Danny Phantom appears on a wanted poster in The Fairly OddParents episode "Poltergeeks". In The Fairly OddParents episode "Crash Nebula" Danny Phantom is shown on the back of Sprig's comic. The concept of Denzel Crocker becoming half-man, half-cheese in "Cheese & Crockers" is similar to Danny Phantom becoming half-ghost when he used his parents' machine. "The Fairly Odd Phantom" is a crossover between The Fairly OddParents, Danny Phantom, T.U.F.F. Puppy and Bunsen is a Beast. They also have the same crossover in a comic. In the Danny Phantom episode "What You Want", Danny and Tucker can be seen playing a Crash Nebula arcade game.
The title card for "Balance of Flour" is a reference to Pac-Man. Ghosts from Pac-Man appear on a poster in "Poltergeeks".
Characters that resemble Wreck-It Ralph and Vanellope appear in The Fairly OddParents episode "Dumbbell Curve".
In the Big Time Rush episode "Big Time Cartoon", The Fairly OddParents episode "I Dream of Cosmo" plays on TV, and Buddha Bob dresses as and acts like Cosmo after falling off his ladder.
"Scary GodCouple" features a reference to Phineas and Ferb".
"Finding Emo" is a parody of Finding Nemo.

Fairly OddParents.game: 100 Things to Do Before High School
Fairly OddParents.description: Wanda from The Fairly OddParents makes an appearance in the 100 Things episode "Be a Fairy Godmother Thing!"

Fairly OddParents.game: Nick's Not So Ultimate Boss Battles
Fairly OddParents.description: The Fairly OddParents characters are playable in Nick's Not So Ultimate Boss Battles.
A pony resembling Twilight Sparkle makes an appearance in The Fairly OddParents episode "Birthday Battle".
The Fair Bears are parodies of the Care Bears.
Timmy Turner appears in Nickelodeon Music Maker.
The Hungry Games is a parody movie of The Hunger Games.
Poof does an imitation of Johnny Bravo near the beginning of "Certifiable Super Sitter."

Fallout.description: In Fallout 2 you can find a phone box looking like the TARDIS, and if the Vault Dweller approaches this strangely-located object, the light on top starts spinning, and the box slowly vanishes into thin air with a whooshing sound, leaving behind only a motion sensor.
A robot says "number five is alive" in Fallout 2.
Stimpacks and radiation chems are mentioned in Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space.
In Fallout 3, there is a side-quest involving giant mutated fire ants titled "Those!" in homage to the film Them!.
The Fallout character "Fawkes" and the "Finding the Garden of Eden" quest contains minor references to V for Vendetta.

The Wild Wasteland trait adds an encounter with a refrigerator containing a fedora and skeleton. This is a reference to the scene in Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull where Indiana Jones saves himself from an atomic bomb explosion by taking cover in a lead-lined fridge.
Team Fortress 2 features a promotional item from Fallout: New Vegas and unlocked by pre-puchasing the game.
Fallout: New Vegas - Gun Runners' Arsenal features a reference to BioShock.
Pip Fred costume from Running Fred and Vault Fred from Clicker Fred are based on Vault Boy.
Jacoren appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
In the episode Princess Cookie, the sign in the hospital saying "You're Special!" has a reference to the book in the post-apocalyptic Fallout 3.
In Primordia a character has a Water Chip and proposes trading it for a G.E.C.K.; this references items from Fallout and Fallout 2.
The armor used in one path from Infiltrating the Airship is based on the T-45 power armor from Fallout.
In Wolfenstein: The New Order and Wolfenstein: The Old Blood, the soda machines feature the Nuka-Cola logo among other in-universe brands.
Posters based on Fallout can be found in The Evil Within. Additionally, one of the Mysterious Objects in The Evil Within 2 is based on Fallout
The comic Plok: The Exploding Man features a reference to Pip-Boy.
An Antenna based on the Vault Boy was included in Rocket League patch v1.08.
In Fallout, one of Codsworth's recognized player character names is "Lain" referencing Serial Experiments Lain.
Fallout 4 features a fictional game called "Pipfall", partially based on Pitfall.
Fallout 4 features a fictional game called "Red Menace", partially based on Donkey Kong.
EZIC's symbol from Papers, Please can be found in Fallout 4.
Mr. Handy from Fallout 4 is an announcer in Dota 2.
Random Encounters has made a Fallout song.
A Fallout themed icon can be unlocked in Emily is Away.
Outfits based on Fallout 4 appear as DLC in Rock Band.
Monopoly: Fallout Collector's Edition is a format crossover between the two series.

In Fallout Zoe's diary contains the entry "Who Protects the Protectron?" This is a reference to Juvenal's "Quis custodiet ipsos custodes?", a phrase popularized as "Who Watches the Watchmen?" from the Watchmen series.
There have been multiple crossovers between Fallout and Doom.
The Chryslus Rocket 69 from Fallout is featured in Forza Motorsport 6.
A pinball table based on Fallout was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX 2 that features characters from the series.
Minecraft features a Fallout mash-up pack for the Bedrock and Legacy Console Editions.
Morgan Yu's spacesuit is available as part of Fallout 4's Creation Club.
The Quake Thunderbolt is available as part of Fallout 4's Creation Club.
There have been multiple crossovers between Fallout and The Elder Scrolls.
Operation - Fallout S.P.E.C.I.A.L. Edition is a format crossover between the two series.

There are two locations that reference to the film Beetlejuice in the Forest area of Appalachia in Fallout 76. Namely, a car wreckage containing the bodies of Adam and Barbara Maitland and the chalk door.
In Fallout 76, at the AVR Medical Center, first floor, one can find a Jangles the Moon Monkey doll lying on a stretcher with a toy alien attached to its face.

In Fallout 76, the barrel burial site north of Sugar Grove is a reference to Breaking Bad. It references a scene from the show in which Walter White buries barrels full of money driven by a truck to a remote location in the desert. The skeleton of Walter White can be found there, among other references to the scene from the show.
Liberty Prime is mentioned in the game Metro Exodus.
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate features a downloadable costume based on Vault Boy from Fallout.
Fallout characters are parodied in Console Wars.
The vault suit from Fallout 4 can be found in Ghostwire: Tokyo.

Goat Simulator 3 contains the quest The Big Red Button which involves detonating an atomic bomb. The quest rewards the player with a Vault 55 suit which is named Fallout Boi. The item description reads "Goat. Goat never changes" in reference to the Fallout series tagline.

In Hi-Fi Rush, if the player completes all the bonus doors within the game they gain access to the lair of the main villain, Kale Vandelay. The room has notes considering different business ideas, each referencing games published by Bethesda Softworks such as The Evil Within, Prey, Deathloop, and Fallout.
"Video Games" by Tenacious D includes a brief segment referencing Fallout 4.
Characters from Fallout appear in the "Magic The Gathering - Fallout" release for Magic: The Gathering.
The T-60 Power Armour from Fallout appears in Fortnite as a part of the Chapter 5 Season 3 Battle Pass.
Professor Chalk sings about Fallout in the music video for Roll Out The Fallout!
Characters from Fallout appear in Stumble Guys as part of a special collaboration.
Vault Dwellers from Fallout appear in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Call of Duty: Warzone as operator skins along with other Fallout cosmetics.
Cards based on Fallout appeared in Balatro as part of the "Friends of Jimbo 4" update.

Famicom Grand Prix.description: Famicom Grand Prix: F-1 Race is part of both series.
Mario is the pilot in Famicom Grand Prix: F-1 Race and its sequel with Luigi as the navigator, while the Monster truck makes an appearance in Super Mario Bros. & Friends: When I Grow Up
The Monster truck from Famicom Grand Prix II appears as a Spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; it's also a trophy in Super Smash Bros. Melee and a sticker in Super Smash Bros. Brawl.

Famicom Robot.description: The Nav-Com robot in StarTropics is based on R.O.B.

A picture of R.O.B. appears in Game Boy Camera.
R.O.B. appears in various microgames in the WarioWare series.
A R.O.B. can be seen in the GameCube version of Viewtiful Joe.
A R.O.B. shaped crane appears in F-Zero GX.
R.O.B.'s head and the Stack-Up blocks are featured as items in Pikmin 2.
R.O.B. is unlockable in Mario Kart DS.
Pofessor Hector from Stack-Up and Gyromite appears in Tetris DS to give instructions to the player.
Some robot characters in the Star Fox series may be based on R.O.B.; UNDIRECT: R.O.B. appears as a boss in the microgame version of Star Fox in WarioWare: Smooth Moves.
R.O.B. is a selectable character in Super Smash Bros. Brawl and its sequels; Brawl also features many ROBs as common enemies.
R.O.B. makes an appearance in The Angry Video Game Nerd episode "NES Accessories" and the Nerd reviews it in the episode "R.O.B. the Robot".
The Irate Gamer reviews R.O.B. The Robot
Picross 3D includes a model of R.O.B. as one of the puzzles.
R.O.B. is one of the "treasures" that can be acquired in Tomodachi Life.
A R.O.B. figure can be seen in the Curosity Shop when viewing from the window in Kafei's Shop in Majora's Mask 3D.
In a video of the Shovelwarewolf he plays Gyromite and Stack-up

Ayumi Tachibana from Famicon Tantei Club Part II appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; she's also a trophy in Super Smash Bros. Melee.

Family Guy.description: Larry and Steve watch Star Trek in The Life of Larry. Star Trek was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "I Never Met The Dead Man"; there are later references to Star Trek.
Characters watch Philadelphia in The Life of Larry and the Family Guy episode "Death Has A Shadow".
Characters watch Brady Bunch in the Family Guy episode "Death Has A Shadow".
GI Jew toys are shown in the Family Guy episode "Death Has A Shadow".
Stewie Griffin uses a Sesame Street phone in the Family Guy episode "I Never Met The Dead Man".

Peter Griffin meets Wile E. Coyote in the Family Guy episode "I Never Met the Dead Man". Bugs Bunny and Elmer Fudd appear in Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story; Taz was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Farmer Guy".
Peter Griffin dreams about meeting Alf in the Family Guy episode "I Never Met The Dead Man".
In the Family Guy episode "Chitty Chitty Death Bang", Bruce is dressed as Spider-Man. Many other episodes feature references to Spider-Man.
Joe Swanson tells the story of how The Grinch handicapped him in the Family Guy episode "A Hero Sits Next Door".  This was later revealed to be a lie in the episode "Joe's Revenge".
Teletubbies is shown on TV in the episode "A Hero Sits Next Door".
Speed Racer appears in the Family Guy episode "The Son Also Draws".
Peter writes a letter to Angus MacGyver in the Family Guy episode "Brian: Portrait of a Dog".
Lois and Brian watch The Dick Van Dyke Show in the Family Guy episode "Holy Crap".
Stewie sees an evil looking clown at a game stand and comments that “it looks like something out of Stephen King.”

Family Guy was shown on TV in The Simpsons episode "Missionary: Impossible", Peter Griffin appears as a clone of Homer Simpson in The Simpsons episode "Treehouse of Horror XIII"; Peter appears in a book in the episode "The Italian Bob". Stewie Griffin talks about The Simpsons in the Family Guy episode "8 Simple Rules for Buying My Teenage Daughter". Homer Simpson appears in the Family Guy episode "PTV"; The Simpsons characters appear in the Family Guy episode "Movin' Out (Brian's Song)"; various episodes of The Simpsons were referenced in the Family Guy episode "Save the Clam". In the episode "The Simpsons Guy", the Griffins go to Springfield and meet The Simpsons characters.
The sign by the NBC building mentions "We Used to Have Seinfeld, Remember?" in the Family Guy episode "If I'm Dyin', I'm Lyin'".
Breakfast cereal mascots are in the role of the Breakfast Club cast in the Family Guy episode "Let's Go To The Hop"; Breakfast Club is mentioned in theFamily Guy episode "Peter Principal".
The season 2 episode “There’s something About Paulie” is a full parody of The Godfather.
There are several references to Peanuts in the Family Guy series.
Lethal Weapon 2 was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "E. Peterbus Unum".
Sam Wheat and Molly Jensen appear in the Family Guy episode "Story On Page One"; Ghost is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Don't Be A Dickens At Christmas".
Peter plays the X-Files theme tune in the Family Guy episode "Wasted Talent".
Characters watch Blair Witch Project at the cinema in the Family Guy episode "Thin White Line".
Stewie Griffin plays with Kermit and Miss Piggy toys in the Family Guy episode "Brian Does Hollywood Part 2".
Leonard Part 6 is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Brian Does Hollywood".
In the episode "And the Weiner is...", Rudolph the Red Nosed Reindeer has a tumor when a doctor arrives to check on his red nose and became Rudolph the Uncircumstanced Reindeer.
Peter Griffin shouts "Wilson" at a ball with a face on a raft in the Family Guy episode "Fish Out Of Water". Cast Away is also mentioned in "Bigfat".
Stewie watches The Smurfs in the Family Guy episode "Emission Impossible".
Pretty Woman is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Screwed The Pooch".
Episodes of The Jeffersons were mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Peter Griffin: Husband, Father...Brother?".
Frosty appears in the episode "A Very Special Family Guy Freakin' Christmas", while Brian's drunken Christmas music rant in "Christmas Guy" includes Frosty the Snowman.
ThunderCats was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Brian Wallows and Peter's Swallows".

Stewie and Brian watch Magnum, P.I. in the Family Guy episode "Stuck Together, Torn Apart".
The Silence of the Lambs is referenced in several episodes of Family Guy.

Stewie Griffin is reading Peter Griffin's copy of "Garfield at Large" in "North by North Quahog".
Barney was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Fast Times at Buddy Cianci Jr. High".
Peter watches Jake and the Fatman in the Family Guy episode "Petarded".

Barney Rubble meets Peter Griffin in the Family Guy episode "Peter's Got Woods".
Tom Tucker is seen playing a handheld Crash Bandicoot racing game in Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story.
Casper appears in Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story.
Jonny Quest appears in Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story.

All in the Family is shown on PTV in the Family Guy episode of the same name.
Characters are dressed up as the A Team in the Family Guy episode "Brian Goes Back To College".
Peter and Lois from Family Guy make an appearance in the Drawn Together episode "The Lemon-AIDS Walk".
Scrat from the Ice Age series makes an official appearance in the Family Guy episode: "Sibling Rivalry". Sid the Sloth also advertises Family Guy in a promo for Fox's Animation Domination block.

Peter Griffin appears in the Robot Chicken episode "Suck It"; Stewie and Brian enter the world of Robot Chicken in the Family Guy episode "Road to the Multiverse". Robot Chicken is mentioned in several Family Guy episodes.

The townspeople from South Park are against Family Guy in the Cartoon Wars duology, there are other references to Family Guy in the series; South Park is mentioned in the Family Guy episodes "Bigfat" and "Family Guy Through the Years", and Kenny appears in the episode "V is for Mystery".

Roger appears in the Family Guy episodes Meet the Quagmires, The Simpsons Guy, Blue Harvest, It's A Trap! and Send in Stewie, Please. Barney appears in the Family Guy episode Killer Queen. Stan and Avery appear in the Family Guy episode Lois Kills Stewie while Stan makes a cameo in the episode Excellence in Broadcasting. Brian makes a cameo in the American Dad episode The People vs. Martin Sugar while he and Stewie make a cameo in the American Dad episode The Worst Stan. Peter appears in the American Dad episode Hurricane!.
Ryu from Street Fighter appears as a character in the browser game American Dad vs. Family Guy Kung-Fu II.
Popeye appears in the episode "You May Now Kiss the...Uh...Guy Who Receives".
The title of the Family Guy season 4 episode "Stu and Stewie's Excellent Adventure" and season 5 episode "Bill and Peter's Bogus Journey" are references to Bill & Ted.

Peter and Brian watch Dora the Explorer in issue 2 of Family Guy. Stewie has Dora on his sled in the episode "How the Griffin Stole Christmas"; a fanfic of Dora the Explorer appears in the Family Guy episode "Peter's Lost Youth".
In the Family Guy episode "Mother Tucker", Tom Tucker asked Peter Griffin if he wants to watch Chicken Little.

Family Guy is shown on TV in "Bad Karma", a DVD bonus feature, which is also an alternate version of "Pilot". My Name Is Earl is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Believe It Or Not, Joe's Walking On Air".
Yogi Bear and Boo-Boo appear in the Family Guy episode "Hell Comes to Quahog".
A person watches Madagascar in the Family Guy episode "Hell Comes to Quahog".
A Tetris cutaway gag was featured in the Family Guy episode "Prick Up Your Ears".

Stewie has a toy of a green SpongeBob in the episode "Prick Up Your Ears". Meg puts on an episode of SpongeBob SquarePants in the Family Guy episode "Road to Rupert". SpongeBob and Squidward were mentioned in "Road to the North Pole". In the episode "Inside Family Guy", a character is dressed as SpongeBob SquarePants.
Mad TV was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Prick Up Your Ears".
Monopoly: Family Guy Collector's Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
There are several references to Cheers throughout Family Guy.
"The Worry Song" from Anchors Aweigh is featured in the Family Guy episode "Road to Rupert", complete with Stewie Griffin inserted over footage of the film.
Mister Rogers' Neighborhood was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "No Chris Left Behind".
Jason From Friday the 13th appears in "It Takes a Village Idiot, and I Married One", where he is interviewed by Quahog 5 News reporter Tricia Takai from Family Guy
The original Star Wars trilogy is parodied in the Family Guy episodes "Blue Harvest", "Something, Something, Something, Dark Side", and "It's A Trap!".
Coach McGuirk from Home Movies appears in the Family Guy episode "Blue Harvest".
Peter Griffin dresses as Donald Duck in the Family Guy episode "Movin' Out (Brian's Song)".
Stitch is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Movin' Out (Brian's Song)".
Sebastian is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Movin Out (Brian's Song)".
The character Pink Panther appears in the Family Guy episodes "Former Life of Brian" and "Halloween on Spooner Street".
Contact is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Former Life of Brian".
The Happiness Booster in Spore is based on the "Intergalactic Proton Powered Electrical Tentacle Advertising Droids" from the Family Guy Special Blue Harvest.
In a flashback from "25ft Under the Seat", Tom is dressed as Stewie Griffin from Family Guy.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "I Dream of Jesus", while Peter plays Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 in the episode "April in Quahog".
A clip from Hook is edited into a fake interview in the Family Guy episode Kiss Seen Round The World.
Calvin appears in a cutaway in the Family Guy episode “Not All Dogs Go To Heaven”.
Stewie Griffin from Family Guy appears during a hallucination in the Bones episode "The Critic in the Cabernet".
A fake promo for 24 was shown in the Family Guy episode "Peter's Progess"; 24 was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Friends of Peter G".
Brian plays Pac-Man in the episode "Road to the Multiverse".

The Cleveland Show is a spinoff of Family Guy. Additionally, a promo for The Cleveland Show appears in the Family Guy episode "The Big Bang Theory", while the episode "He's Bla-ack!" is about Cleveland returning to Family Guy.
There's a spoof of the Super Friends intro in the Family Guy episode "Family Goy".
Stewie watches Hannah Montana in the Family Guy episode "Hannah Banana".
Brian talks to a character from The Family Circus in the Family Guy episode "Dog Gone".
Curious George is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Dog Gone" and later episodes.
Dr. House appears in the Family Guy episode: "Business Guy".
Carter Pewterschmidt watches The Big Bang Theory in the Family Guy episode "Business Guy"; The Big Bang Theory is referenced in later episodes.

Family Stadium.description: One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Bosco".
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Indy", and one in Famista 64 is called "Babel".
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Herohero", referencing the enemy Berobero.
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '87 is called "Luke", after the protagonist of Star Wars, that also appeared in Namco-produced games.

Acha from Toy Pop appears in Famista '88 - '91 as the newscaster, while Pino appears as a player in Famista Online 3, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and along with Acha in Famista Dream Match; additionally players named after Pino and Acha appeared in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels.
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels is called "Bunbun".
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels is called "Tomari".
A player in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium: Pennant Race for MSX is called "Miramon", while one in Super Famista 3 is called "Shiranui".

The Namco Stars team from Family Statium is unlockable in Kyukai Dochuki, while Tarosuke from Shadow Land appears as a player in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '87 and its sequels is called "Tarosuke".
Super Famista and its sequels include players called "Blade" and "GeoSword" in the Namco Stars team.

Pac-Man appears during a homerun in Super Batter Up, then appears alongside other Pac-Man characters in the audience of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64, and as an actual player in Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Pac", while Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax feature a player based on Blinky (as "Akabe") in the Rivals team, and Ms. Pac-Man appears as the mascot of the Namco Stars team in Famista 64; Pac-Man also appears as the logo of the team in Super Famista and its sequels.

The field in the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64 features elements from Xevious, and the Solvalou ship, the Mothership Andor (under the name "Xevious") and the Bacura appear as guest players in Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Solvalou" and "Xevious", while Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax include one in the Rivals team based on the Mothership Andor.

The Meowky from Mappy are among the audience in the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4 and Famista 64, and Mappy himself appears as a player in Famista Online 3, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match, while Nyamco appears in Famista Online 2011, Famista Returns and Famista Climax (here in the Rivals team); additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Mappy" and "Nyamco".

Elements from Dig Dug appear in the background of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64, while Fygar appears as a player in Famista DS, Famista Online, and the protagonist of Dig Dug (called "Dig Dug") and Pooka appear as guest players in Pro Baseball Famista 2011; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Dig Dug", "Fygar" and "Pooka".

The Tower of Druaga appears in the background of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64, while Gil and Ki appear as players in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match with Druaga also appearing in the Rivals team in Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Gil", "Ishita" and "Ki".
Elements from Metro-Cross appear in the background of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4.

The "Sky Kids" appear during a homerun in the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Baron" and "Sky Kid" in the Namco Stars team, while Famista Online 2010 features a player based on the enemy planes from Sky Kid  in the Rivals team.

Elements from Libble Rabble appear in the background of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 5; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Tofukafu".

Amul appears (in dragon form) during a homerun in the Namco stadium in Super Famista 5, and (in human form) as a player in Famista DS, Famista Online 3, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels and Famista Dream Match, while Chaos and Zawell appear in the Rivals team in Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '87 and its sequels include players called "Amul" and "DSUPI" (or "D. Spi").

Valkyrie appears among the audience in the Namco stadium in Famista 64 and as an actual player along with Sandra in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match, and she also appeared as the mascot for the Namco Stars team in Super Famista 3-5; the enemy Zouna also appeared in the Rivals team in Famista Online 2010 and in Famista Climax; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels include players called "Quarkman" and "Sandra".
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Famista 64 is called "Richard", one in Famista Advance is called "Keith", and one in Famista Climax is called "Taikura" (or "Ti-Cri").
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Wonder Stadium and Wonder Stadium '99 is called "Anthology".
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Wonder Stadium and Wonder Stadium '99 is called "Final Furlong".

An image of Yakyuu-kun appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3, while one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Super Famista 4 and its sequels is called "Gun Bullet" (only "Gun-bul" in Wonder Stadium and Wonder Stadium '99).
Pac from Family Stadium appears in Namco Super Wars.

Family Stadium 2003 features a stadium set in the world of Klonoa, and Klonoa himself appears as a player in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match, with the King of Sorrow also appearing in Dream Match; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Famista Advance is called Popka, and an image of Klonoa appears in the Namco stadium.

Family Stadium 2003 features a stadium set in the world of Taiko no Tatsujin and players called "Don Wada" and "Katsu Wada", that also return in later games; Don-chan himself appears as a player in Pro Yakyuu Famista 2011, then alongside Katsu-chan in Famista Dream Match and alongside Tatsu-Don in Famista Climax.
Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature Hitomi Yoshino as a guest player; additionally Famista Advance and Family Stadium 2003 feature a player called "Moto G".

Famista Online, Famista DS, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature KOS-MOS from Xenosaga as a guest player, with Albedo also appearing in Famista Online 2010 and Shion appearing in Famista 2011 and Dream Match.

Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011, Famista Dream Match and Famista Climax feature a racer from Ridge Racer as a player (called "Ridge"), with Reiko Nagase also appearing in Famista 2011 and Dream Match; additionally some games in the series feature players called "RRR" (referencing Ridge Racer Revolution), "R4" (referencing R4: Ridge Racer Type 4), "Rage" (referencing Rage Racer) and "Reiko".

Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011, Famista Dream Match and Famista Climax feature Susumu and Taizo Hori as guest players (altough Taizo appears in 2011 as "Dig Dug"); additionally Famista Advance and its sequels include players called "Susumu", "Taizo" and "Anna", and an image of Puchi appears in the Namco stadium in Famista Advance.
Famista Online 2 features Apollo from Phelios as a guest player; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Famista '89 and its sequels is called "Apollo".
Famista Online, Famista DS, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels  and Famista Dream Match feature The Prince from Katamari as a guest player, with the King also appearing in Dream Match.
One of the players in the Bandai Namco team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium for Wii is called "Digimon".
One of the players in the Bandai Namco team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium for Wii is called "Haseo".
One of the players in the Bandai Namco team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium for Wii is called "Mametchi".

The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of a Famista player with other baseball players as assistants, while Pro Baseball Famista 2011, Famista Dream Match and Famista Climax feature Moji-kun as a guest player.

Famista Online 2010 features Bakuda from Bravoman in the Rivals team, while Pro Baseball Famista 2011, Famista Dream Match and Famista Climax feature Bravoman in the Namco Stars team, with Bakuda, Black Bravo and Pistol Daimyo also appearing in the Rivals team in Climax; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels include players called "Bravoman" and "Waya Hime".

Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax feature Mabu from Rolling Thunder in the Rivals team; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels is called "Albatross".
One of the players in the Bandai Namco team in Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax is based on the alien Octi from Baraduke.

Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax feature Yoritomo from Genpei Toma Den in the Rivals team, while Kagekiyo appears in the Namco Stars team in Famista Online 2011, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '87 and its sequels is called "Kagekiyo".

Famista Online features Heihachi from Tekken as a guest player, with Unknown also appearing in Famista Online 2010 and Nina and Yoshimitsu appearing in Famista Online 2011, while Pro Baseball Famista 2011 features Heihachi, Nina and Panda, and Famista Climax features Heihachi, Devil and Unknown; additionally Super Famista 5 and its sequels include players called "Devil", "Heihachi", "Mokujin" and "Tekken".
Famista Online 2011 features Paco from Marvel Land as a guest player.

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature Wagan as a guest player; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels include players called "Wagan", "Takuto", "Karin" (after the protagonists of Wagan Paradise) and "Hisopiso" (after the character from Wagan Land 3).

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 features the XFA-27 from Ace Combat (here called "Ace-con") as a guest player; Kei Nagase and the X-02 Wyvern (called "Ace") were also added in January 2016 in Famista Dream Match; additionally Famista 3 and its sequels include players called "Air-con", "Ace Combat" or other variations.

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 features Chihaya, Haruka and Miki from THE iDOLM@STER as guest players, while 13 idols from the series appeared in Famista Online 2011 during a special collboration, and Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax features Haruka, Mirai, Uzuki and Tendo.

Famista Online 2011, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match feature the crocodile from Wani Wani Panic as a guest player (called "Wani Wani"); additionally Gear Stadium Heiseiban and its sequels include players called "Wani Wani", "Wani Para" (after Wani Wani Paradise), "Takoika" and "Same Same".

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature an alien from Galaga as a guest player; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Galaga", "Gala 3" (only in Famista 2), "Kyara Hachi" (after Galaga '88), "Dragoon" (after the player's ship from Galaxian 3), "Galboss" and "Zolgear".

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature Mitsurugi and Siegfried from the Soul series as guest players, with Taki, Ivy and Astaroth also added to Famista Dream Match in December 2015, and Mitsurugi also returning in Famista Climax; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Super Famista 5 and its sequels is called "Soul Edge", while one in Family Stadium 2003 is called "Maxi".

One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "P.P.", and he's depicted in Pro Baseball Famista 2011  and Famista Dream Match  as a racer from Pole Position.
Pro Baseball Famista 2011 features Soma and Shio from God Eater as guest players, while Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax features Alisa and Vajra.
Famista Online 2011, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match feature Wonder Momo as a guest player (sometimes simply called "Momo").
Famista Online 2012 features Clovis from Dragon Buster as a guest player; additionally Famista '89 and its sequels include players called "Carl" and "Clovis".
Famista Dream Match features Hiromi from Burning Force as a guest player.

Famista Dream Match and Famista Climax feature Rick from Splatterhouse as a guest player; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels is called "Rick".

One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Famista 2 is called "Tank". Saki, Kaoru, Natasha and Tsubame from Shin-Gun Destroy! Girl's Tank Battalion were added to Famista Dream Match during a special promotion.
Kamen Rider Ex-Aid "Tricks": Kamen Rider Genm features a Famista Gashat.
Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax features Sharon from Numan Athletics as a guest player; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Famista '94 is called "Numan".
Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax features a player called "Tank", who is shown driving a tank from Tank! Tank! Tank!.

Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax features Velvet from Tales of Berseria in the Bandai Namco team, while Barbatos from Tales of Destiny 2 and Dhaos from Tales of Phantasia appear in the Rivals team; addtionally Super Famista 5 and its sequels include players called "Cress", "Mint", "Reid" and "Tales".

The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax; it also makes minor appearances in other games in the series; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Rally-X".

Fantasia.description: Mickey Mouse appears in Fantasia. Little Pan from the Pastoral Symphony segment of Fantasia makes an appearance in the cover story to Mickey Mouse Weekly #521, while The Mushrooms from the Nutcracker Suite segment are enemies in the North American version of Mickey Mousecapade; various characters from Fantasia and Fantasia 2000 also appear in the House of Mouse series.
Donald Duck is the protagonist of the Fantasia 2000 segment Pomp and Circumstance
Chernabog appears as a boss in Kingdom Hearts.
Fantasia is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Tangerine Factor".
Characters from Fantasia appeared in Towers of Saviors during a special collaboration.
Yen Sid appears in the Descendants book The Isle of the Lost.
