Fazbear & Friends is animated in the style of Minecraft. Steve and Alex appear several times throughout the series.
Undertale characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
A parody version of "Strange Things" plays in the Fazbear & Friends episode "Circus Baby VS Freddy!" Toy Story is mentioned in the Fazbear & Friends short "Huggy Wuggy BITES Pro Player!?"
Bendy characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
Friday Night Funkin' characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
Squid Game characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
Among Us characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
Baldi has appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
Doki Doki Literature Club characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
Poppy Playtime characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends. Huggy Wuggy's "Voxel" skin in Project: Playtime originates from Fazbear & Friends.
Tekken 4 is mentioned in the Fazbear & Friends short "HUGGY WUGGY vs. PRO PLAYER".
Elden Ring is mentioned in the Fazbear & Friends short "MOMMY LONG LEGS vs. FOXY!"
Talking Ben has appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
Don't Hug Me I'm Scared characters appear in the Fazbear & Friends short "Rainbow Friends vs. Don't Hug Me I'm Scared".
Chainsaw Man appears in the Fazbear & Friends short "Chainsaw Man is right behind you."
Choo-Choo Charles appears in the Fazbear & Friends short "Choo-Choo Charles vs. Steve".
Garten of Banban characters have appeared several times throughout Fazbear & Friends.
A parody version of "Rainbow Connection" from The Muppets is played in the Fazbear & Friends short "Poppy Playtime VS Garten of Banban".
Characters from The Amazing Digital Circus appear in the Fazbear & Friends episode "Extermination" as part of an official collaboration with Glitch Productions.
An employee from Lethal Company makes a cameo in the Fazbear & Friends episode "Extermination".
Skibidi Toilet makes a cameo in the Fazbear & Friends episode "Extermination".

Jackie's introduction in the Fazbear & Friends episode "Death by Mimic" is a reference to the introductions used in the character trailers for Super Smash Bros. for 3DS/Wii U and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
A portrait of SpongeBob's pineapple can be seen in the Fazbear & Friends episode "The Rage".
A plush of the Knight from Hollow Knight can be found in the Fazbear & Friends episode "The Rage".

Feast (Disney).description: In Big Hero 6, a graffiti tag and paw prints on a wall references Feast.

Felix the Cat.description: Julius the Cat from the Alice Comedies series is based on Felix the Cat.
Betty Boop and Felix is a crossover between both series.

In the Garfield and Friends episode "The Automated, Animated Adventure", Garfield's model transforms into Felix the Cat. In The Twisted Tales of Felix the Cat episode "The Fuzzy Bunny Show", a kid mistook Felix for Garfield.

Felix the Cat.game: The Mystery Files of Shelby Woo
Felix the Cat.description: Shelby Woo wears a Felix the Cat shirt in the Mystery Files of Shelby Woo episode "Fool's Gold".
In The Twisted Tales of Felix the Cat episode "The Fuzzy Bunny Show", Felix says "You wouldn't do this to the Ninja Turtles".
Felix took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews "Felix The Cat".
Mobs watch Felix the Cat in Episode 2 of Dig Build Live.
A character looking like Felix the Cat appears in Heathcliff comic strips.
The Professor appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #58.
Felix the Cat appears in Funko Pop! Blitz.
A Felix  the Cat doll appears in Rescue Rangers (2022).
Characters from Felix the Cat make an appearance in KouKou Love: Tap Blast.

Femme Fatales.description: Creepshow is shown on TV in the Femme Fatales episodes: "Bad Medicine", "Help Me, Rhonda", "The Clinic", "Family Business", and "Libra".
In the Femme Fatales episode: "Angel & Demons", a poster of Blade Runner is seen on a wall above the bed in Charles Solomon's apartment.
In the Femme Fatales episode: "Angel & Demons", a poster of The Lost Boys is seen on a wall in Charles Solomon's apartment.
Jason is mentioned in the Femme Fatales episode: "Till Death Do Us Part".
Bambi is mentioned in the Femme Fatales episode: "Trophy Wife".
Alien is mentioned in the Femme Fatales episode: "Killer Instinct".

In the Femme Fatales episode: "Bad Science", when Matilda West teleports into the alternate universe, she says her serial number is TK-421, the same unit number of the Imperial stormtrooper Han Solo impersonates when taking back the Millennium Falcon in Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope.
King Kong is mentioned in the Femme Fatales episode: "Bad Science".
The Wicked Witch of the West is mentioned in the Femme Fatales episode: "Family Business".

Ferris Bueller's Day Off.description: Ferris Bueller's Day Off takes place in Shermer, Illinois, a fictional suburb that first appeared in Sixteen Candles. Additionally, according to Word of God, Samantha Baker from Sixteen Candles and Ferris Bueller knew each other.
The I Dream of Jeannie theme plays in Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
Alien is mentioned in Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
Dirty Harry is mentioned in Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
The Star Wars theme plays in Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
Ferris Bueller appears in the end credits of She's Having A Baby.
Ferris Bueller is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Kiddie Pool".
Hank makes a reference to Ferris Bueller's Day Off in the Breaking Bad episode: "ABQ".
Ferris Bueller is mentioned in the White Collar episode "Dentist Of Detroit".
Ferris Bueller’s Day Off is mentioned and quoted in Ready Player One and Ready Player Two.
Ferris Bueller's Day Off is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Thanksgiving IV".
The first episode of Life Is Strange features a reference to Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
The Goldbergs episode "Barry's Day Off" features many references to Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
The Scorpion episode "Dam Breakthrough" features a ferret named "Ferret Bueller", named after the titular character of Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
The post-credit scene of the Deadpool movie is a parody of Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
Jameson H.’s father owns a memorabilia of the bat from Ferris Bueller's Day Off in the Bojack Horseman episode “A Horse Walks Into Rehab”.
A DVD cover for Ferris Bueller's Day Off can be seen in the Rick and Morty episode: "Night Family".

Fez.description: You can find Gomez in Blackmoor Mountains trapped until you free him.
You can find the language from Fez in Guacamelee.
Gomez appears as a goat skin in "Toto Temple Deluxe".
Dino Run DX features a hat based on Gomez.
Inputting a secret button input will briefly change your character to look like Gomez from Fez.

Fields of Mistria.description: Three wearable cosmetic items in Fields of Mistria called the 'Farmer's Outfit Set' resembles the clothing of the protagonist in the early Story of Seasons games.

Fight Club.description: Characters from the Fight Club video game star in the "Get Low" video of Video Mods.
Fight Club is mentioned in the Father of the Pride episode "Sarmoti Moves In".
Jude makes a Fight Club reference in the 6teen episode Labour Day - Part 1.
Fight Club is mentioned in Ready Player One.

Fight Club.game: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl
Fight Club.description: Fight Club is mentioned in Me and Earl and the Dying Girl.
A poster for Fight Club can be seen in the New Girl episode: "Lillypads".
Fight Club shows on TV in Baby Driver.
Hashimoto’s girlfriend mentions Brad Pitt from Fight Club in Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan - Episode 9: The Run.
Fight Club is parodied in Les Kassos.
Tyler Durden is mentioned in the Bridge Kids episode “Killer Bars”.
The opening to Chainsaw Man features a reference to Fight Club.
A poster that parodies Fight Club can be seen in the Scott Pilgrim Takes Off episode "Whatever".
Fight Club is mentioned in Class of '09: The Flip Side.
Fight Club is mentioned in Dispatch.

Fight Klub.description: The first Fight Klub set features cards based on Army of Darkness, including a character card of Ash Williams.
The first Fight Klub set features cards based on Rambo, including a character card of John Rambo.
The first Fight Klub set features cards based on Silence of the Lambs, including a character card of Hannibal Lecter.
The first Fight Klub set features cards based on Friday the 13th, including a character card of Jason Voorhees.
The first Fight Klub set features cards based on Saw II, including a character card of Jigsaw.
The second Fight Klub set features cards based on The Lost Boys, including a character card of Michael Emerson.
The second Fight Klub set features cards based on Tank Girl, including a character card of Tank Girl.
The second Fight Klub set features cards based on The Devil's Rejects, including a character card of Captain Spaulding.
The second Fight Klub set features cards based on Reservoir Dogs, including a character card of Mr. Blonde.
The third Fight Klub set features cards based on Robocop, including a character card of Robocop.
The third Fight Klub set features cards based on Terminator 2, including character cards of The Terminator and T-1000 and a partner card of John Connor.

Fight Night.description: Characters from Fight Night Round 2 star in the "What's Happenin'" video of Video Mods.
The GameCube version of Fight Night Round 2 features Little Mac from the SNES game Super Punch-Out!! as an unlockable boxer.
Calvin Garret from Need for Speed: The Run might be based on Andre Bishop from Fight Night Champion.

Fighter's History.description: Karnov is one of two bosses in Fighter's History and Fighter's History Dynamite. The second game was rebranded Karnov's Revenge in English markets.
Mizoguchi from Fighter's History is an enemy in Joe & Mac Returns.
The Bonus stage Ox from Karate Champ is a secret boss character in Fighter's History Dynamite.
Garou Densetsu vs. Fighter's History Dynamite is a crossover between the two series.
Makoto Mizoguchi from Fighter's History appears as a guest character in KOF: Maximum Impact Regulation "A".
Ryu's School Costume from Street Fighter V is inspired by Makoto Mizoguchi from Fighter's History.
Fighter's History characters appear in The Knights of Avalon during the third Namco collaboration event.
Sprites from Fighter's History appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.

Fighters Megamix.description: Fighters Megamix features many characters from Virtua Fighter.
All original characters from Fighting Vipers are selectable in Fighters Megamix.
Fighters Megamix features two characters and two stages from Sonic the Fighters; Deku from Fighters Megamix makes a cameo appearance in the 50th issue of the Archie Sonic the Hedgehog comic.
Fighters Megamix features Janet from Virtua Cop 2 as a playable character.
Fighters Megamix features The Hornet as a playable character.
Fighters Megamix features Rent a Hero as a playable character.
The plane from After Burner makes a cameo in Fighters Megamix. There is also a music track from After Burner in the game.

Fighting Layer.description: Fighting Layer and Fighter EX Layer feature characters originally from the Street Fighter EX series, while Ace from Street Fighter EX3 features three moves lifted from Fighting Layer and five Fighting EX Layer costumes were available in Street Fighter V: Champion Edition in limited events.
SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy features Skullomania from Fighting EX Layer as a DLC guest character.
Fighting EX Layer features Terry Bogard from the Fatal Fury series as a DLC guest character.

Fighting Vipers.description: Toys based on Sonic characters appear in the introduction of the console versions of Fighting Vipers; Sonic and Tails are also included in the game's code, though unused, in the arcade version.
All original characters from Fighting Vipers are selectable in Fighters Megamix.
A character can be seen playing Fighting Vipers 2 in episode 3 of Arcade Gamer Fubuki.
Honey from Fighting Vipers appears in Earth UFO Catcher.
A human version of Fighting Vipers appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.

Figure (Komoe).description: Hatsune Miku appeared in Figure Fantasy and Figure Story during a collaboration event.

Figure (Komoe).game: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
Figure (Komoe).description: Rimuru and Milim from That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime appeared in Figure Fantasy and Figure Story during a collaboration event.
Mikoto Misaka from A Certain Scientific Railgun T appeared in Figure Fantasy during a collaboration event.
Characters from Black Rock Shooter appeared in Figure Fantasy during a special collaboration event.

Fillmore!.description: Kim Possible appears in Fillmore! in the background of the episode Codename: Electric Haircut.
Spinelli from Recess appears in Fillmore! in the background of the episode Codename: Electric Haircut.
Ingrid Third appears in American Dragon: Jake Long in the background of the episode The Halloween Bash.

Final Destination.description: Stuart Little is mentioned in Final Destination.
Diff'rent Strokes is mentioned in Final Destination 2.
Top Gun is mentioned in Final Destination 3.
SpongeBob is mentioned in Final Destination 3.
Final Destination is mentioned in Scre4m.
Final Destination 2 is mentioned in Emily is Away.
The Rick and Morty episode: "Final DeSmithnation"'s title is an allusion to the Final Destination series.

Final Fantasy.description: Final Fantasy uses some elements from Dungeons & Dragons.
The Final Fantasy series features some references to the Zelda series.

Makai Toushi SaGa features enemies from Final Fantasy and the first three SaGa games were released as the Final Fantasy Legend series outside Japan; Final Fantasy Legends: Toki no Suishou features characters from Romancing SaGa 2 as summons, while Adel from Imperial SaGa, and various characters from Romancing Saga 3 appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations; Final Fantasy Record Keeper held crossover events exclusively in Japan with Emperors SaGa, Romancing SaGa 2, and SaGa Scarlet Grace; additionally Unlimited SaGa features a demo version of Final Fantasy X and a Chocobo Card is present, but unused, in the code for Romancing Saga 3, while Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call features downloadable tracks from the SaGa series.

The Mana series started with Seiken Densetsu: Final Fantasy Gaiden; a chocobo is unlockable as a pet in Legend of Mana, while Final Fantasy Legends: Toki no Suishou features Salamander and Undine from the Mana series as a summon called Spirit of Mana, and characters from Secret of Mana and Trias of Mana also appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations; Final Fantasy Record Keeper held a Japan-exclusive crossover event with Rise of Mana; additionally Final Fantasy X-2 features a minor reference to Secret of Mana while Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call features a downloadable track from Seiken Densetsu 3.
The last episode of Captain N: The Game Master features elements from Final Fantasy.

The names of some characters in the Final Fantasy series, starting with Biggs and Wedge from Final Fantasy VI, are based on Star Wars characters; Final Fantasy IX, XIV and XIII-2 also feature references to the Star Wars series.
Sabin's Aura Cannon Blitz attack in Final Fantasy VI is likely based off of the Hadouken from Street Fighter, using the same button combination.
Sabin's Raging Fist Blitz attack in Final Fantasy VI is likely based off of the move from Art of Fighting, using the same button combination.
Secret of Evermore features a cameo of Cecil from Final Fantasy IV and various characters from Final Fantasy VI; there also is an item called Chocobo Egg.
Tobal No. 1 includes demo versions of Final Fantasy VII and Final Fantasy Tactics; Tobal 2 features a Chocobo as an unlockable playable fighter.
A Chocobo makes an appearance in Front Mission Alternative.
The Chocobo series is a spin-off of the Final Fantasy series.
Final Fantasy VII and Final Fantasy X were reviewed by T.O.M. on Toonami.
Ehrgeiz features some characters from Final Fantasy VII; Final Fantasy VIII and Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy feature a weapon called Ehrgeiz.
Having saved data of Final Fantasy VII unlocks the special "Saviour" dragon in Dragonseeds, while having saved data of Final Fantasy Tactics unlocks the special "Stamina" dragon.
In the Japanese version of the debug room in Final Fantasy VIII, the Doomtrain's name is "Devil Thomas", referencing Thomas the Tank Engine.
Final Fantasy IX features a reference to Star Trek.
Final Fantasy IX features the line "Great Scott!"
Kids are seen playing Final Fantasy VIII within the movie Charlie's Angels.
A parody of Final Fantasy VIII called Final Pharmacy VIII is featured within Segagaga.

Many characters, items and general themes from the Final Fantasy series are featured prominently in the Kingdom Hearts series, while characters from Kingdom Hearts appear in World of Final Fantasy, Final Fantasy Record Keeper, and Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special promotions; additionally three costumes from Kingdom Hearts are downloadable in Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy, and Kingdom Hearts Final Mix contains a trailer for Final Fantasy X-2.
Morrowind features a reference to Final Fantasy VI in a dungeon's name; Final Fantasy Dimensions features a reference to the "Arrow in the knee" line from Skyrim.
The secret boss Wozma from Duke Nukem: Manhattan Project is based on Ozma from Final Fantasy IX.
A mission in Final Fantasy XI is called "Inspector's Gadgets!"
Final Fantasy XI features a reference to Charmed.
Final Fantasy X-2 features a reference to Metal Gear Solid.
Final Fantasy X-2 features a reference to Scooby Doo.
The Animatrix features a short clip starring Aki from Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within.
The box for the North American Final Fantasy II can be seen in Dragon Ball Z: The Legacy of Goku II, while Final Fantasy Dimensions features a reference to the Dragon Ball series.
The Scott Pilgrim series features many references to the Final Fantasy series.
There's a song called "Filna Fantasy" played everytime Konata plays an RPG
Itadaki Street Special, Itadaki Street Portable, Itadaki Street Mobile and 30th Anniversary feature characters and maps from the Final Fantasy series.
A scene in the Two and a Half Men episode "Weekend in Bangkok with Two Olympic Gymnasts" features a Final Fantasy X.
Cloud Strife's sword appears in "Zombeh Attack".
In Asterix And Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are references to the Final Fantasy series.
Cait Sith says "number five is alive" in Dirge Of Cerberus.
The Coconut Fred's Fruit Salad Island episode "Sir Nutalot" features references to Final Fantasy VII.
The Robot Chicken episode "Rodigitti" and some later episodes feature sketches based on Final Fantasy VII.

Five characters from the Final Fantasy series are unlockable in Mario Basketball 3on3 and Mario Sports Mix; additionally the boss Culex from Super Mario RPG is based on characters from the Final Fantasy series.
Mortal Kombat Armageddon features the hairstyle of Final Fantasy VII's Sephiroth and Cloud in Kreate a Fighter mode.
The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance references a quote by Kermit the Frog.

The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance references a quote by Homer Simpson. The Simpsons Game features a reference to Final Fantasy VII. The Simpsons episode "Women in Shorts" has a record store named "Vinyl Fantasy".

The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance has Gilgamesh quote "It's morphing time!" from Power Rangers. TheFinal Fantasy XV DLC Booster Pack + was originally scheduled to include The Magitek Exosuit, based on the Power Rangers suits.
The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance possibly references the "You are a Pirate" song from LazyTown.
The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance has a reference to the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance has a reference to the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance has a reference to Reading Rainbow.
The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance has a reference to Superman.
The English version of Final Fantasy V Advance has a reference to the Pokemon anime. Final Fantasy XIII-2 features a reference to the Pokémon series.
Cloud's hair is unlockable in Pico Sim Date 2.
The English version of Final Fantasy's PSP port uses the word "burninate" from Homestar Runner.
The North American version f Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Trials and Tribulations features a reference to the line "Spoony Bard" from Final Fantasy IV.

The Quest in Final Fantasy XI: Wings of the Goddess "A Nation On The Brink" features the dialogue "Then all your Jeuno are belong to us!" and "You are on way to destruction", referencing dialogue from Zero Wing.
In World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King there's a flower vendor named Aerith Primrose, based on Aerith from Final Fantasy VII.
The Siren object from Scribblenauts is based on the Siren from Final Fantasy VIII.
3D Dot Game Heroes features some references to the Final Fantasy series.

Dave Strider's apartment contains numerous swords from the Final Fantasy series. A room in the trolls' meteor is based on a room from Final Fantasy VI. Joey Claire has a poster for Final Fantasy VI in Hiveswap.
The Big Bang Theory episode "The Bozeman Reaction" features a reference to the Final Fantasy games.
No More Heroes 2 features a character based on Cloud from Final Fantasy VII.
There's a dialogue reference to Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children in Episode 11 of the Black Butler season 2 anime.
An achievement in Final Fantasy XIV is "Dragoon Age".
An achievement in Final Fantasy XIV is "Double Dragoon".
Final Fantasy XIV features references to the My Little Pony series.
Final Fantasy XIV features a reference to The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
Final Fantasy XIV features a reference to The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe.
Final Fantasy XIV features a reference to Law & Order.
The Monster Galaxy moga "Peepee" is based on PuPu from Final Fantasy VIII.
The victory theme from Final Fantasy can be heard in "Dick Figures - Teabag Teaser".
Music from Final Fantasy can be found in Toilet in Wonderland.
JonTron reviews Final Fantasy XIII.
The Chuck episode "Chuck Versus the A-Team" features a reference to Final Fantasy IV.
The Orb Battle "Whom Wilt Thou Call" in Final Fantasy XI (added with an update) is based on Ghostbusters.
LittleBigPlanet 2 features downloadable costumes based on Final Fantasy VII characters.
Final Fantasy XIII-2 features a reference to Terminator 2.
Final Fantasy XIII-2 features a reference to Murder, She Wrote.
Commander Shepard armor from Mass Effect 3 is downloadable in Final Fantasy XIII-2.
Theatrhythm Final Fantasy and its sequels are format crossovers between the two series. Final Fantasy characters appear.
Random Encounters has made a Final Fantasy song.
Cloud appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
Cloud Strife, Tifa Lockhart, Sephiroth, and Clive Rosfield have been subjects for Death Battle!
The PC re-release of Final Fantasy VII features a reference to Diablo II.

Bravely Default is the spiritual successor of Final Fantasy: The 4 Heroes of Light and features many of the same elements; additionally Final Fantasy Brave Exvius includes Bravely Default characters, while Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call features downloadable tracks from the game.
Wreck-It Ralph features a reference to Aerith fromFinal Fantasy VII.
There's a spoof of the battle system from Final Fantasy VI in Infiltrating the Airship, Cloud's Buster Sword appears in Completing the Mission.
An official ONaF drawing has Flumpty as Cloud from Final Fantasy.

Slimes from Dragon Quest appeared in Final Fantasy XI as part of a special collaboration. Shantotto from Final Fantasy XI and a Moogle from Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn appear during special events in Dragon Quest X, while various monsters and characters from Dragon Quest of the Stars appeared in Mobius Final Fantasy and Dissidia Final Fantasy Opera Omnia, Brickman appeared in Final Fantasy XIV, and characters from the series appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations; additionally in international versions of Final Fantasy there's the tomb of a character named "Erdrick" and the Wyrmhero Blade in Final Fantasy XII is based on Erdrick's sword from Dragon Quest; a demo version of Final Fantasy XII was included in the North American release of Dragon Quest VII.
A toy resembling Cloud Strife from Final Fantasy VII appears in the Steven Universe episode "Steven the Sword Fighter".
Hyperdevotion Noire: Goddess Black Heart features a character called Ein Al, that is a parody of Final Fantasy characters.

Final Fantasy IX features a reference to Resident Evil 2, while Minna to Biohazard Clan Master features costumes from Final Fantasy Brigade Break the Seal in a special collaboration event, as well as a shared event between both games which gift Final Fantasy character cards.
Dynasty Warriors 8: Empires, Samurai Warriors 4-II and Samurai Warriors 4: Empires feature hairstyles for custom characters based on Cloud Strife's and Lighting's from the Final Fantasy series.
The first episode of Life Is Strange features a reference to Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within.
2 Tracks from The World Ends with You can be downloaded in Theatrhythm Final Fantasy: Curtain Call.
Pure Odio from Live A Live appears as a summon in Final Fantasy Legends: Toki no Suishou. 2 Tracks from Live A Live can be downloaded in Theatrhythm Final Fantasy: Curtain Call.

Characters from Valkyrie Profile appear in Final Fantasy Legends: Toki no Suishou and Final Fantasy Brave Exvius. Additionally, characters from Final Fantasy Record Keeper appeared in Valkyrie Anatomia as part of a collaboration event and vice versa.

Final Fantasy.game: The Irregular at Magic High School
Final Fantasy.description: Costumes based on Final Fantasy Type-0 appeared in The Irregular at Magic High School: Lost Zero as part of a special collaboration.
As part of special collaboration events, Puzzle & Dragons featured characters from the Final Fantasy series.
The comic Plok: The Exploding Man features a reference to Final Fantasy VII.
Final Fantasy XIV: Heavensward features costumes based on Tactics Ogre; additionally the Final Fantasy Tactics sub-series takes elements from Tactics Ogre.
Umaru throws a tantrum to make his brother buy her the game. It's called "Last Fantasy XV" in this universe.
A Chocobo and a Moogle were available for a limited time in Dota 2 by pre-purchasing Final Fantasy Type-0 HD for Steam.

Super Smash Bros. for Wii U and for 3DS feature Cloud Strife from Final Fantasy VII as a downloadable character, along with his own stage, with Sephiroth appearing as DLC in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Characters from Brave Frontier appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations and vice versa.
Items and costumes from Final Fantasy Type-0 appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Mii Plaza includes a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Final Fantasy Explorers.
Enter the Gungeon features a weapon called the Machine Fist that that references Barret's machine gun hand from Final Fantasy VII.

Thirteen Yokai from Yo-Kai Watch appear as minions in Final Fantasy XIV, during an event from July 26th to October 3rd, 2016, while Yo-Kai Watch 3 features a Yokai based on Moogle, and one riding a Chocobo from the Final Fantasy series; characters from Dissidia Final Fantasy also appeared in Yo-Kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Cloud Strife's sword appears in the Adventure Time episode Jermaine.

A special collaboration between Final Fantasy Brave Exvius and Monster Hunter Explore includes a "Hunter" unit, weapons and an exclusive boss battle in the former, and costumes, weapons and a Moogle in the latter; Monster Hunter World features creatures from Final Fantasy XIV and vice versa during a collaboration; Monster Hunter 4G/Ultimate and Monster Hunter X also feature a downloadable costume from Final Fantasy; Rathalos from Monster Hunter appears in Final Fantasy VII: Ever Crisis as part of a crossover event.
Odin from Final Fantasy XIV appears as a boss in Phantasy Star Online 2 as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from the Final Fantasy series appeared in Monster Strike during special collaborations.
When the glam metal pug leader gets defeated the fanfare from Final Fantasy plays in Paradigm.
Cloud, Noctis Lucis Caelum, and Tifa have been subjects for DBX.
Costumes based on Final Fantasy XV appeared in Blue Reflection as part of a special collaboration.
The Regalia from Final Fantasy XV appears as a DLC car in Forza Horizon 3 and Forza Horizon 4.
In West of Loathing, a character named Flo hums the Victory Fanfare theme from Final Fantasy.

Ardyn and Bahamut from Final Fantasy XV appear in Assassins Creed: Origins, unlocking the Ultima Blade, the Ziedrich shield and a Chocobo camel; additionally Ezio's clothes from Assassin's Creed: Revelations are downloadable in Final Fantasy XIII-2, and Final Fantasy XV: Assassin's Festival is an Assassin's Creed-themed event for the game, where the Assassin's Creed series is mentioned as fictional within the game's world; there have also been other minor references between the two series.
A copy of Final Fantasy XV can be seen in Episode 8 of Gamers!

Characters from Star Ocean: Anamnesis appear in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius and vice versa, during special collaborations; additionally Star Ocean: Till the End of Time features a character based on Aerith from Final Fantasy VII.

Characters from NieR:Automata appear in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations and again during an event in War of the Visions: Final Fantasy Brave Exvius; additionally the music of NieR is present in Theatrythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call while music from the NieR series can be heard on the radio in Final Fantasy XV.2B, 9S and 2P appear in Final Fantasy XIV in the YoRHa: Dark Apocalypse questline in the expansion Shadowbringers. 2B appear in Final Fantasy VII: Ever Crisis as a boss in the collab with the NieR Series featured costumes and cosmetics based on NieR Series in November 27, 2025.
Wonderland from Alice in Wonderland is visited in the Final Fantasy Record Keeper event "Key to Another World".
Olympus Coliseum from Hercules is visited in the Final Fantasy Record Keeper event "Key to Another World".
Everybody's Golf features Final Fantasy-themed items, including a Chocobo as a caddie.
Final Fantasy XV Windows Edition features a costume based on Gordon Freeman from Half-Life.

Final Fantasy XV Windows Edition features a costume based on Super Llama Man from The Sims, while The Sims 4 features a costume based on Noctis Lucis Caelum from Final Fantasy XV (added in update 64).
Lara Croft appears in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during a special collaboration; additionally Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII features a downloadable costume based on Lara Croft.

Noctis Lucis Caelum from Final Fantasy XV is a downloadable character in Tekken 7; additionally, Tekken 6 features the hairstyles of Cloud and Sephiroth from Final Fantasy VII as character customization. Clive Rosfield from Final Fantasy XVI appears as a guest character in Tekken 8.

XG from Xenogears appears as a boss in World of Final Fantasy. Characters from Xenogears appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations; there have also been other minor references between the two series.
Minecraft features a Final Fantasy skin pack for Legacy Console and Bedrock Editions.
Characters from Just Cause 3 appear in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during a special collaboration.
Characters from Final Fantasy XV appeared in The Alchemist Code during special collaborations.
Final Fantasy is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "Perfect Cell Vs Sephiroth".

Characters from Octopath Traveler appear in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius and Final Fantasy Record Keeper during special collaborations. Cecil from Final Fantasy IV appears in Octopath Traveler during a special collaboration.
Deus Ex: Human Revolution features a poster for Final Fantasy XXVII. Characters from Deus Ex appear in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during a special collaboration.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within.
One of the endings of Reventure in the spanish traduction have the name Allévoy, referencing a translation error from Final Fantasy 7, where Cloud says exactly the same thing.
Dicey Dungeons features two weapons named after weapons from Final Fantasy VII
Characters from SINoALICE appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during a special collaboration.
"Final Friendcity" is mentioned in Later Alligator.
Characters from Fullmetal Alchemist appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations.

SD Gundam: OVER GALAXIAN is a format crossover between the two series, featuring ships and mechas from Gundam, and gameplay from Galaxian.
In the episode "Amnesio" from Lilo & Stitch: The Series, the arcade games that Lilo/Martha and the little boy were playing had sound effects similar to Galaga.

Taiko no Tatsujin: Appare Sandaime and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Galaxian series; music from Galaxian and Galaga is also featured in the Namcot Medley debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10; additionally, the Galaxian flagship appears in Taiko no Tatsujin 13 as an icon.
Arino plays Galaga through the PS1 game Namco Museum Volume 1 in episode 7.
A microgame in WarioWare: Touched! is inspired on the NES version of Galaga.
Namco × Capcom features the UGSF.
An alien from Galaga makes an appearance as an item in the Mario Kart Arcade GP series.
QuickSpot features one puzzle based on Galaga.
A submarine named "The Galaga" is featured in Lost.
Smash Court Tennis 3 features a Galaga themed court with the actual aliens moving around.
One remix theme based on Gaplus is included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 02, while Sana Miyoshi from THE  iDOLM@STER: Cinderella Girls has shirts with logos based on Galaga.
Futurama: The Beast with a Billion Backs features a videogmae called "Gxlaxian".
In "What is Life" from Adventure Time, Finn plays a game that is similar to Galaga.

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature an alien from Galaga as a guest player; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Galaga", "Gala 3" (only in Famista 2), "Kyara Hachi" (after Galaga '88), "Dragoon" (after the player's ship from Galaxian 3), "Galboss" and "Zolgear".
Galaga is mentioned several times in Ready Player One and once in Ready Player Two.
Katamari Amore features a Galaga-themed level; characters from Katamari appeared in the Galaga webcomic during a four part "Katamari X Galaga" story.
In the movie The Avangers a character is seen playing Galaga.
Galaga is one of the games added to Namco Arcade.
There's a reference to Galaga in strip #13 of the Wonder Momo web comic.

Chiaki's hairpin in Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair resembles the ship from Galaga. In Danganronpa 3: The End of Hope's Peak High School, Chiaki is seen playing a game called Gala Omega that closely resembles Galaga.
The Galaga ship is one of the main characters in Namco High.
Space Galaga is a crossover between the two series.

Stage 35 in Battle City and Stage 43 in Namco Gallery Vol.1 version of the game are shaped after a Galaxian and a flagship respectively. Shin-Gun Destroy! Girl's Tank Battalion features references to the UGSF and Galaga ship appears as one of the tanks.

The Boss Galaga appears as an item in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U, with its tractor beam also appearing as Pac-Man's grab move, while the Galaxian Flagship appears as one of the items in Pac-Man's Bonus Fruit move.

Ace Combat Infinity features nicknames and emblems based on Galaxian, Galaga and Gaplus gained through Special Supply tickets, while music from the unrelesead Galaxian Heroes was featured in the compilation soundtrack Ace Combat Infinity & Series Music Best.

Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition features many characters from the Tekken series; additionally the PlayStation version of Tekken features a minigame version of Galaga and the Galaxian Flagship is featured as a point indicator in Tekken and Tekken 2.
Rick from Splatterhouse makes an appearance in Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition.
Elements from Rolling Thunder are featured in Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition.
Galaxian is mentioned in Armada.
The Boss Galaga appears as one of the videogame characters in the movie, Pixels.
Galaxian and Galaga costumes is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 3.
Kamen Rider × Super Sentai: Chou Super Hero Taisen features a Galaxian Gashat and an army of enemies from Galaxian.
Kamen Rider × Super Sentai: Chou Super Hero Taisen features a Galaxian Gashat and an army of enemies from Galaxian.
A mouse enemy dressed like Boss Galaga appeared in Cat Busters during the Namco Catalog IP collaboration event.
The Fighter from Galaga and the Galaxian alien appeared in The Knights of Avalon during the second Namco collaboration event.
The main theme of Galaga and Galaxian are part of the "Namcot Medley" BGM featured in Groove Coaster 4: Starlight Road.

Various games in the Galaxian series are included in Namco Museum titles. Additionally, characters from Galaxian can be seen interacting with characters from other series on the boxart of Namco Museum Arcade Pac.
Sprites from Galaxian and Galaga appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.
Galaga is mentioned in Into the Pit.
A Galaxian themed emote appears in Fortnite.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Galaxian.
A Galaxian sticker can be seen in the window of Game Over World in A Minecraft Movie.

Galaxy Express 999.description: There is an Easter egg in Virtua Fighter 3 in which a flying train will appear in the background of the stage, referencing Galaxy Express 999.
Captain Harlock appears as a major character throughout the Galaxy Express 999 series.
Pop'n Music Animelo features a track from Galaxy Express 999.
Characters from Galaxy Express 999 make an appearance in Cosmo Warrior Zero.
The theme from the Galaxy Express 999 TV show is featured in the Japanese version of Donkey Konga.
Tracks from Galaxy Express 999 appear in Karaoke Revolution: Anime Song Collection.
Music from Galaxy Express 999 is featured in Daigasso! Band Brothers DX as a downloadable song.
Taiko no Tatsujin 7 and later games in the series feature music tracks from Galaxy Express 999.
Characters from Galaxy Express 999 appear in Dragon Poker as part of a special collaboration.
A track from Galaxy Express 999 appears in D4DJ Groovy Mix.
Maetel from Galaxy Express 999 appears in Shinkalion Z as a supporting character.

Galaxy Fight.description: Bonus-kun is a parody of Ryu from Street Fighter.
Yakopoo from Trip World is a mini-boss in Galaxy Fight.
Bonus-kun is a boss in Waku Waku 7.
A Lutecian (Roomi's race) appears in Albert Odissey: Legend of Eldean as a shopkeeper.

Galaxy Force.description: The spaceship from Galaxy Force appears as a hidden playable unit in Super Daisenryaku for Sega Genesis, named Galaxy F.
The Try-Z from Galaxy Force appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Sega 3D Classics Collection features Galaxy Force II with Galaxy Force characters interacting with other characters in the credits.
The TRY-Z from Galaxy Force is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Sega DLC Pack.
The Galaxy Lady from Galaxy Force II is unlockable in the retail release of 3D Power Drift.
A Galaxy Force arcade machine appears in Earth UFO Catcher.
A human version of Galaxy Force appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.

Galaxy Quest.description: Galaxy Quest DVD appears in Flushed Away.
Galaxy Quest is mentioned in Armada, and the line "By Grabthar's hammer" is quoted.
After ejecting from your Titan, there is a 15% chance of getting the message "NEVER GIVE UP NEVER SURRENDER.", a reference to Galaxy Quest.
Galaxy Quest is a parody of Star Trek. Characters and species from Galaxy Quest appear in Star Trek Fleet Command.

Galidor.description: The BIONICLE and Galidor PC games have been released as a bundle.
From The LEGO Ninjago Movie onwards Rufus McCallister wears a Galidor shirt; a poster of the theme is also included in the set 70620 Ninjago City.
The Dimensional Defender and Realm Raider minifigures in the Lego Minecraft set 21279 Enderman Tower are based on Nick Bluetooth and Gorm from Galidor.

Galtar and the Golden Lance.description: Galtar appears in the Harvey Birdman episode "SPF".

Gambit.description: Gambit made his debut in X-Men Annual #14.
Gambit appears in Wolverine (Vol. 2) #53.
Gambit appears in Marc Spector: Moon Knight (Vol. 2) #42.
Gambit appears in Web of Spider-Man (Vol. 1) #113.
Gambit appears in Daredevil (Vol. 1) #330.
Gambit appears in Iron Man (Vol. 1) #307.
Gambit appears in Ghost Rider (Vol. 3) #67.
Night Man/Gambit is a crossover between the two series.
Gambit is a playable character in Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter.
Gambit is a playable character in Marvel vs. Capcom: Clash of Super Heroes and Marvel vs. Capcom 2: New Age of Heroes.
Blade appears in Gambit (Vol. 3) #4.
Deadpool appears in Gambit (Vol. 3) #18
The Fantastic Four appear in Gambit (Vol. 3) #22
A zombie version of Gambit appears in Marvel Zombies #2, and in several Marvel Zombies comics.
Gambit appears in the Marvel: Ultimate Alliance series.
the Avengers Unity Division appear in Gambit (Vol. 5) #9.
Lego Marvel Super Heroes included a Minifigure of Gambit as a playable character who would later appear in physical form.
Morbius appears in Deadpool v Gambit #2.
She-Hulk appears in Deadpool v Gambit #4.
Thanos appears in Deadpool v Gambit #5.
Doctor Strange appears in Deadpool v Gambit #5.
The Guardians of the Galaxy appear in Deadpool v Gambit #5.
Man-Thing appears in Deadpool v Gambit #5.
Gambit appears in Fortnite.
Gambit appears in Marvel Strike Force.
Gambit appears in Captain Marvel (Vol. 11) #43.
Gambit is a playable character in Marvel Rivals.

Game & Watch.description: There were multiple format crossover games between Popeye and Game & Watch.
There were multiple format crossover games between Mickey Mouse and Game & Watch. Egg also featured elements from the Mickey Mouse Game & Watch game.
There were multiple format crossover games between Peanuts and Game & Watch.
There were multiple Game & Watch games released featuring Donkey Kong characters. Donkey Kong characters also appeared in the Game & Watch Gallery games.
There were multiple Game & Watch games released featuring Mario characters. Mario characters also appeared in the Game & Watch Gallery games.
The Game & Watch Punch-Out!! is a re-release of Boxing.
Urban Champion is an adaptation of Boxing.
There were multiple format crossover games between Balloon Fight and Game & Watch with one game being featured in Game & Watch Gallery 3.

The "Modern" versions of Vermin in Game & Watch Gallery 2, of Egg, Greenhouse, and Turtle Bridge in Game & Watch Gallery 3 and of Mario's Cement Factory in Game & Watch Gallery Advance feature elements from Yoshi games.

The "Modern" versions of Ball in Game & Watch Gallery 2, of Donkey Kong Jr. in Game & Watch Gallery 3 and of Fire Attack in Game & Watch Gallery Advance feature elements from the Wario Land series. Various microgames based on Game & Watch games appear in the WarioWare series.
Pictures of various characters from the Game & Watch series appear in Game Boy Camera.

Characters, stages, and other collectibles from the Game & Watch series appear in every Super Smash Bros. game starting with Super Smash Bros. Melee which introduced Mr. Game & Watch, an amalgamation of various games throughout the series.
A Ball Game & Watch console appears as an item in Pikmin 2.
Nintendo Land features a minigame based on Octopus.
A graffiti of the Octopus appears in the stage Ancho-V Games in Splatoon 2.
The name and aesthetics of Piczle Puzzle & Watch Collection are based on the Game & Watch series.
There were multiple format crossover games between Zelda and Game & Watch. The Legend of Zelda 35th Anniversary Edition also features a playable version of Vermin where you play as Link instead.

Game Boy (Valiant).description: The Game Boy comic series by Valiant is based on Super Mario Land.

Game Boy Camera.description: Arranged musics from Balloon Kid are featured in Game Boy Camera.
Donkey Kong and Donkey Kong Jr. appears in Game Boy Camera.
A picture of R.O.B. appears in Game Boy Camera.
Pictures of various characters from the Game & Watch series appear in Game Boy Camera.

Mario appears in the title screen, including stamps, pictures and frames from Mario characters being featured.The Mario Artist games on Nintendo 64DD can edit pictures taken in Pocket Camera through Transfer Pak.
An arranged version of the Twinkle Elementary School music from EarthBound Beginnings is featured in Game Boy Camera.
Stamps featuring Generation I Pokémon appears in Game Boy Camera.
Sheriff appears in Game Boy Camera.
A picture of Wario from Wario Land II appears in Game Boy Camera.
A picture of Yoshi and Baby Mario referencing Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island appears in Game Boy Camera.
Elements from the Zelda franchise appears in the Gold Edition of Game Boy Camera.
SimCity 64 can interact with photos taken from Pocket Camera through 64GB Pack.
Music from Hello Kitty Pocket Camera is used in Mobile Golf.
The Nerd reviews the Game Boy Camera in episode 147.
Chief Arino uses the Game Boy Camera during the Good-Bye Game Boy segment.

Game Shakers.description: Sky Whale, a character from a fictional video game in Game Shakers is a playable character in Super Brawl 4.
Helen from Drake & Josh appears in the Game Shakers episode "Tiny Pickles".
Rex from Victorious appears in the Game Shakers episodes "Tiny Pickles", "Lost Jacket", "Falling Pigeons" and "Llama Llama Spit Spit".
Babe and Kenzie appear in the online Nickelodeon game Block Party 3.

The Game Shakers track down Nathan Kress to see if his character, Freddie, liked Carly or Sam from ICarly in the Game Shakers episode Game Shippers. Nevel from iCarly makes a cameo in the episode "Llama Llama Spit Spit" in a photo on the wall of people who are banned from eating at Fooders.
The Game Shakers appear in the Henry Danger episode "Danger Games". Henry and Schwoz later appears in the Game Shakers episode "Babe Loves Danger".
Animal from The Muppets makes a cameo in the episode "Llama Llama Spit Spit" in a photo on the wall of people who are banned from eating at Fooders.
Friends was referenced in the Game Shakers episode "The One With the Coffee Shop".

Game Tengoku.description: Stage 5 in Game Tengoku features a parody of Space Invaders.
One of Momoko's outfit in her Momoko Bomber from Game Tengoku has her dressed as Lum from Urusei Yatsura.

Suchie-Pai makes a cameo appearance on the Game Tengoku OVA, while Suchie-Pai Arcade machines are added on Arrange Mode's Stage 1 in the Sega Saturn port, and Selia's ending image has her dressed as the main character.
Stage 5 in the Arrange Mode of Game Tengoku for the Sega Saturn features a parody of Tokimeki Memorial.
Stage 5 in the Arrange Mode of Game Tengoku for the Sega Saturn features a parody of Dragon Quest.
Jeynus's ending image in the Arrange Mode of Game Tengoku for the Sega Saturn shows him and Genius Yamada dressed like Guile and Ryu.
A redesigned "Clarice" from City Connection is one of the playable characters in GUNbare! Game Tengoku 2, while the original "Claris" is a  DLC character in Game Tengoku CruisinMix.
One stage in GUNbare! Game Tengoku 2 features a parody of Tamagotchi.
One stage in GUNbare! Game Tengoku 2 features a boss parody of the Andor Genesis from Xevious.
One stage in GUNbare! Game Tengoku 2 features a boss parody of the Big Core from Gradius.
One stage in GUNbare! Game Tengoku 2 features a boss parody of the King Fossil from Darius.

Game no Kanzume.description: Flicky is a playable game in Game no Kanzume Vol. 1 and Game no Kanzume Otokuyou.
The visual novel games based around Phantasy Star II are playable games in both Game no Kanzume Vol. 1 and Game no Kanzume Vol. 2.
Sonic and Tails appears in the instruction manuals of Game no Kanzume Vol. 1 and Game no Kanzume Vol. 2.
Teddy Boy Blues is a playable game in Game no Kanzume Vol. 2 and Game no Kanzume Otokuyou.
Masami, the host from all compilations, appears as a collectible in SEGA AGES Columns II

Game of Thrones.description: In the Big Bang Theory episode The Russian Rocket Reaction, Sheldon and Leonard purchase a replica of the Longclaw Sword from Game of Thrones, which is seen in their apartment in many other episodes. Additionally, Game of Thrones is mentioned in several other episodes of The Big Bang Theory.
The episode Exit Through the Kwik-E-Mart has a couch opening which is a reference to Game of Thrones opening.
Mr. Garrison talks about Game of Thrones in the South Park episode "Cartman Finds Love".
Game of Thrones is mentioned in The Thick of It.
All Guards of the Shado-Pan are randomly quoting the Night's Watch from the series.
The Princess and the Queen was first released in an anthology, Dangerous Women, which included Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell from The Cosmere
In the episode The Most Interesting Man in the World, Chris mentions that he wants to watch Game of Thrones.
Tyrion Lannister and Jon Snow appear in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #46.
Game of Thrones is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
Monopoly: Game of Thrones Collector's Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
Risk: Game of Thrones is a format crossover between the two.
The Detentionaire episode: "Game of Clones"'s title is a reference to Game of Thrones.
Game of Thrones is parodied in Les Kassos.
Team Dragons' cars found in Rocket League's Season Mode are named Viper, Imp and Hound in reference to characters from Game of Thrones.
Sideshow Bob mentions Game of Thrones in the episode “Treehouse of Horrors XXVI”.
Game of Thrones is mentioned in the Modern Family episodes: "Clean Out Your Junk Drawer" and "Heavy is the Head". The in-universe show "Clash of Swords" is a parody of Game of Thrones.
Game of Thrones is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Helmet".
Clue: Game of Thrones is a format crossover between the two series.
Larry references Game of Thrones in I Hate Fairyland #6.
Game of Thrones is mentioned in "QUAL É A SÉRIE? ♫ - PARÓDIA "THE NAME GAME"" and "50 TONS DE ROSA (PARTE 2) - FATOS SOBRE MIM!!".
Game of Thrones is mentioned in the Camp Camp episode "Quest to Sleepy Peak Peak".
Garrett mentions Game of Thrones in Season 3, Episode 1 of Superstore, “Grand Re-Opening”.
Game of Thrones is mentioned in Love, Simon.
Game of Gnomes in Sherlock Gnomes is a parody of Game of Thrones.
Pitch Meeting had episodes on Game of Thrones.
Reigns: Game of Thrones is a format crossover between the two series.

Rachel watches Game of Thrones in the Titans episode “Hawk and Dove”.  Also, there are many Game of Thrones references to the Teen Titans Go! Episode “ Where Exactly on the Globe Is Carl Sanpedro Part 4”.
Game of Thrones is mentioned in the Shazam! movie.
Game of Chairs is a parody of Game of Thrones.  Also, characters from Game of Thrones appear in the short Sesame Street: Respect is Coming.
A host based on Drogon from Game of Thrones appears in the Westworld episode “The Winter Line”.
Daenerys Targaryen's hair appears in the shop.
There is a Game of Thrones planet that appears in Space Jam: A New Legacy.
In The Ghost and Molly McGee episode: "All Night Plight", Libby mentions she reads a book series called "A Song of Snow and Humidity", a reference to the book series: A Song of Fire and Ice.
Arya Stark is a playable character in MultiVersus. Daenerys Targaryen and The Hound were planned to appear as playable characters, but were scrapped after the game was shut down.
When meeting the dragon in Chantal in Fairyland, Chantal refers to herself as Khaleesi.

GameCenter CX.description: Arino plays the NES game Takeshi no Chōsenjō in episode 1.
Arino plays the PS2 game Angelique Trois in episode 2.
Arino plays the Xbox game Steel Battalion in episode 3.
Arino plays the Dreamcast game Roommania＃203 in episode 4.

Arino plays the Japanese NES port of Star Force in episode 5. He later plays Super Star Force in episode 111 and the original Arcade version through Wii Virtual Console as part of Nintendo Channel promotional episodes. Former AD Shinchiro Toujima also played the Famicom version during the Saitama Super Arena event.
Arino plays the NES port of Sasa in episode 6.
Arino plays the PS1 game Namco Museum Volume 1 in episode 7. He also played Namco Museum Volume 4 during the GameCenter CX in Vietnam special.
Arino plays Galaga through the PS1 game Namco Museum Volume 1 in episode 7.
Arino plays the NES port of Door Door in episode 8.
Arino plays the NES port of Yie Ar Kung-Fu in episode 9. He also made it through a DVD-only revenge years later.
Arino plays the NES port of Gradius in episode 9. He did a full challenge in episode 136. He later plays Moai-kun in episode 370.
Arino plays the NES port of Track & Field (Hyper Olympic) in episode 9.

Arino plays the NES game Super Mario Bros. in episode 10. He also plays Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels in episodes 10 and SP of Season 1. He did a full challenge in a special live from 2013 and revenged against it in the Budokan live event. Other Mario games featured in the show includes Super Mario Bros. 3, Super Mario World, Super Mario 64, Dr. Mario, Super Mario Land, Super Mario Land 2: 6 Golden Coins, Super Mario Kart, Mario Kart 64 Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars and Dance Dance Revolution: Mario Mix. Arino appears as a costume for the Mystery Mushroom in Super Mario Maker through a update. To make him available, the player has to clear either Arino Maker, Arino Maker Returns or New! Arino Maker courses.

Arino plays the NES game Atlantis no Nazo in episode 1 of Season 2, which marks the current format of the TV show. He also tried a revenge through several obstacles in 2018 as part of a Blu-Ray compilation.
Arino plays the NES game Challenger in episode 2.

Arino plays the NES port of Ghosts 'n Goblins in episode 3 of GameCenter CX, the Genesis port of Ghouls 'n Ghosts in episode 34 and Super Ghouls 'n Ghosts in episode 52. He also tried a revenge through several obstacles in 2018 as part of a Blu-Ray compilation.
Arino plays the NES game Konami Wai Wai World in episode 4.
Arino plays the Disk System game Metroid in episode 5. He also did a full play through of Super Metroid in 2010 as part of the Wii Virtual Console promotional episodes.
Arino plays the NES port of Solomon's Key in episode 6.
Arino plays the SNES game Prince of Persia in episodes 7 and 8.
Arino plays the first five games in the classic Mega Man series and the first two Mega Man X games in GameCenter CX.
Arino plays the TurboGrafx-16 game Kato-chan Ken-chan (released in US as J.J. & Jeff with certain elements removed), in episode 11.
Arino plays the NES game of Ganso Saiyūki: Super Monkey Daibōken during the Arino's! Ring-Ring Tactics segment with the hints of viewers through a telephone.
Arino plays the NES game Totsugeki! Fūun Takeshi Jō in episode 12. He later plays Jogging Race in episode 158.
Arino plays the PS1 port of Tokimeki Memorial in episode 13. The PS1 version of Tokimeki Memorial 2 was also played by him as a DVD-exclusive challenge in 2019.
Arino plays the NES game Famicom Jump: Hero Retsuden in episode 14.
Arino plays the Disk System game Yume Kojo: Doki Doki Panic in episode 15.
Arino plays the NES game Milon's Secret Castle in episode 19.

Arino plays the SNES game The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past in episode 20. He later plays The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time in episodes 109 and 110, Zelda II: Link's Adventure in episodes 209, 210 and through a New Year Live Special, and The Legend of Zelda in episodes 317 and 318.
Arino plays the SNES port of Ultraman in episode 20. He also played Ultraseven later in episode 45.
Arino plays the SNES port of Final Fight in Episode 22 of GameCenter CX.
Arino plays the NES port of Adventure Island in episode 23. He also played New Adventure Island later in 2017 as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge.
Arino plays the SNES game ActRaiser in episode 24.
Arino plays the TurboGrafx-CD port of Quiz Tonosama no Yabō in episode 25. He also plays Quiz Tonosama no Yabō 2: Zenkoku-ban in episode 228 by using proper conversion kits.
Arino plays the NES game Transformers: Convoy no Nazo as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge.
Arino plays the NES game Doraemon in episode 26.

Arino plays the NES Ninja Gaiden in Episode 29 of GameCenter CX, and the NES Ninja Gaiden II in Episodes 96 and 97 and Ninja Gaiden III as part of the GameCenter CX in Pacific special episode. The "Robot Ninja Haggleman" fictional video games within Retro Game Challenge for Nintendo DS are inspired in the classic Ninja Gaiden series.
Arino plays the Disk System game Hikari Shinwa: Palutena no Kagami (known outside Japan as Kid Icarus) in episode 30.
Arino plays the SNES game Umihara Kawase in episode 31.
Arino plays the NES port of Contra in Episode 32 of GameCenter CX. He also plays Super C in episode 235 and Contra III: The Alien Wars in episode 360.
Arino plays the Cassette Vision game PakPak Monster during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Arino plays the Cassette Vision game Monster Mansion during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Arino plays the Cassette Vision game Kikori no Yosaku during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Arino plays the NES game Ikki as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge.
Arino plays the Genesis port of Bonanza Bros. in episode 33.
Arino plays the Game Gear game Ganbare Gorby! (released in Europe as Factory Panic with certain elements changed) during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Arino plays the 3DO game Jurassic Park Interactive during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Arino plays the 3DO game Shock Wave during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Arino plays the 3DO game Chiki Chiki Machine Mou Race: Kenken to Black Maou no Ijiwaru Daisakusen during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.

GameCenter CX.game: Princess Tomato in the Salad Kingdom
GameCenter CX.description: Arino plays the NES version of Princess Tomato in the Salad Kingdom in episode 35.
Arino plays the SG-1000 game Girl's Garden during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Arino plays the TurboGrafx-16 port of Yōkai Dōchūki in episode 36 of GameCenter CX.
Arino plays the SNES port of Street Fighter II: The World Warrior in episode 37 of GameCenter CX, and 2010 Street Fighter in episode 95.

Arino plays Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse in Episode 38. He also played the Disk System version of Akumajou Dracula (known as Castlevania outside Japan) later in 2014 as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge, Castlevania: Bloodlines in episode 270 and Akumajou Dracula X: Chi no Rondo (known as Castlevania: Rondo of Blood) in episodes 297 and 298.

Arino plays Mighty Bomb Jack in episode 39. He tried to avenge it in episode 40 and later in a live show. Both episodes and the live show were the basis for GameCenter CX THE MOVIE: 1986 Mighty Bomb Jack, a movie based on the show with a romantic side-story added as new content. The DVD and Blu-Ray releases of the movie also features Arino playing the original Bomb Jack on Wii Virtual Console as a DVD-exclusive challenge.
Arino plays Gargoyle's Quest II in Episode 40 of GameCenter CX and Demon's Crest in Episode 279.
Arino plays the NES port of TwinBee as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge.
Arino plays Adventure Quiz: Capcom World / Hatena? no Daibouken in Episode 42 of GameCenter CX.
Arino plays the SNES game Septentrion (released in US as SOS) in episode 43. He also played it during the Makuhari Messe event in order to get a better ending.
Arino plays the Disk System game Bio Miracle Bokutte Upa in episode 44.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Fire during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Flagman during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Manhole during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Helmet during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.
Arino plays the NES game Wagan Land in episode 47. He later plays Wagan Land 2 in episode 222 and Super Wagan Land in episode 323.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Octopus during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Parachute during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.
Arino plays the SNES port of Out of this World (released as Outer World in Japan) in episode 48.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Oli Panic during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.

Arino plays Legend of the Mystical Ninja in episode 49. He later plays the NES game Ganbare Goemon 2 in 2016 as a DVD-exclusive challenge, and  Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu in episode 276.

Arino had a choice to play the NES game GeGeGe no Kitarō: Yōkai Daimakyō (released in US as Ninja Kid with certain elements removed) for episode 51, but chose Musashi no Ken: Tadaima Shugyō Chū instead. However, he later played the SNES game Gegege No Kitarō: Fukkatsu! Tenma Daiou in episode 104.
Arino plays the SNES game Clock Tower in episode 53. He later plays the PS1 game Clock Tower in episodes 230 and 231 and Clock Tower II: The Struggle Within in episode 342.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Boxing during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.

Arino plays the NES game Kai no Bouken: Quest of Ki in episodes 54 and 55. He later did a revenge against the game within a Live Broadcast in 2007. The NES port of The Tower of Druaga was played by him as a DVD-exclusive challenge in 2008. During the GameCenter CX in Vietnam special, he also played The Return of Ishtar through Namco Museum Volume 4 for PS1.
Arino plays the Game & Watch game Spitball Sparky during the Game & Watch, I Can't Leave You Alone segment.

Arino plays the TurboGrafx-16 game Bikkuriman World in episode 57. The game is a port of the Wonder Boy in Monster Land arcade game but with Bikkuriman characters. The plot and the music were also changed.
Arino plays the NES game Kamen no Ninja Hanamaru (known as Yo! Noid in US) in episode 58.
Arino plays the Genesis game Super Fantasy Zone in episode 59.

Arino plays the NES game Bomberman as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge. In the same episode, he also played the TurboGrafx-16 version of Bomberman with the staff. Later, Super Bomberman was played by him in episode 269 and Bomberman '94 (released as Mega Bomberman on the Genesis) as part of the GameCenter CX mini special.

Ganbare Goemon.description: Goemon is a playable character in the series, while purchasing a cartridge item at a store in Ganbare Goemon 2 turns the money woman into Konami Lady, and Konami Lady appears at the game center in The Legend of the Mystical Ninja.
Goemon and other series' characters appear as playable characters in several games of the Parodius series.
Goemon is a playable character in Hai no Majutsushi.

Purchasing a cartridge item at a store in Ganbare Goemon 2 turns certain enemies into Getsu Fuuma. The stage "Virtual Hell" in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu features enemies from Getsu Fuuma Den.

Purchasing a cartridge item at a store in Ganbare Goemon 2 turns certain enemies into Pentarou from Antarctic Adventure. Goemon and Ebisumaru are seen playing Antarctic Adventure in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigenjou no Akumu OVA.

Goemon visits the world of Gradius in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigenjou no Akumu OVA. The first level of Arcade Gradius can be played at the Amusement Park in Legend of the Mystical Ninja. Ganbare Goemon 2 features a miniature Big Core Mk.II and an holographic, samurai-themed Moai as bosses, and there are references to Gradius in the credits of Ganbare Goemon: Uchuu Kaizoku Akogingu.

Goemon visits the world of Castlevania in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigenjou no Akumu OVA, Simon Belmont is a playable character in Ganbare Goemon Gaiden 2: Tenka no Zaihō, a vampire hunter look-alike makes a cameo appearance in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu, and Simon's grandfather appears in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigoku-hen manga. Goemon appears as an item in Castlevania: Harmony of Despair.

Goemon visits the world of TwinBee in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigenjou no Akumu OVA, a TwinBee plane is found and used in Ganbare Goemon Gaiden 2: Tenka no Zaihō, and Pastel makes a cameo appearance in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu and Ganbare Goemon 3: Shishijūrokubē no Karakuri Manji Gatame; Goemon and Ebisumaru make a cameo appearance in the TwinBee Paradise OVA.
There's an allusion to Daisuke Jigen from Lupin the Third in the Ganbare Goemon: Jigenjou no Akumu OVA.
There's a hidden item shaped like Kid Dracula's head in Legend of the Mystical Ninja.

A person dressed like Goemon can be seen in "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the Sega CD and later ports of Snatcher, and the main characters discusses the Ganbare Goemon series. Gillian Seed makes a cameo in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu.
Sparkster makes a cameo appearance in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu.
The second level of Arcade Xexex appears as a playable game at the Amusement Park in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu.
Shiori Fujisaki from Tokimeki Memorial makes a cameo appearance in Ganbare Goemon 3: Shishijūrokubē no Karakuri Manji Gatame.
Goemon has a Super Saiyan styled transformation in Ganbare Goemon 3: Shishijūrokubē no Karakuri Manji Gatame and Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon.
A mini-game in Ganbare Goemon Kirakira Dōchū: Boku ga Dancer ni Natta Wake is based on Track & Field.
Two robots in Ganbare Goemon Kirakira Dōchū: Boku ga Dancer ni Natta Wake look like Ryu and Guile from Street Fighter II.
The final boss in Ganbare Goemon Kirakira Dōchū: Boku ga Dancer ni Natta Wake throws miniature Death Stars.
An enemy resembling the pistol from Doom and attacking from the foreground can be spotted during Ganbare Goemon Kirakira Dōchū: Boku ga Dancer ni Natta Wake.
A wrestler in Jikkyō Power Pro Wrestling '96: Max Voltage named "The G. Goemon" is inspired in Goemon.
Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon is included in Konami GB Collection Vol. 2.
Stickers of Goemon and Ebisumaru can be seen in printstations from Mitsumete Knight R.
Beartank from Rakugakids appears as a board piece in Goemon Mononoke Sugoroku.
Konami Krazy Racers features Goemon as a selectable racer.
In Reshef of Destruction Pegasus summons a giant mech which is Goemon Impact. Several cards in the actual TCG are based off Ganbare Goemon characters as well.
Goemon is one of the characters in Pop'n Music 12 Iroha and Pop'n Music Portable; there's also a remix medley of themes from the series.
A modified version of Quarth with Goemon Impact replacing the ship can be unlocked in Ganbare Goemon: Tōkai Dōchū Oedo Tengu ri Kaeshi no Maki.
Space Manbow can be unlocked in Ganbare Goemon: Tōkai Dōchū Oedo Tengu ri Kaeshi no Maki.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Ganbare Goemon.
Arino plays The Legend of the Mystical Ninja in Episode 49 of GameCenter CX.
Otomedius characters Emon-5 and Emon-8 are inspired by the Ganbare Goemon series.
The Japanese version of Scribblenauts features spawnable Ganbare Goemon characters.
Monster Retsuden Oreca Battle features Goemon as a playable character.
Kingdom Dragonion featured Goemon as a playable character.

Taisen! Bomberman features "Goemon Bomber", based off the main character from Ganbare Goemon; Goemon Bomber returns as a DLC for Super Bomberman R (added in Ver.2.0), while Ver.2.1 added "Ebisumaru Bomber", based on the series' recurring sidekick.
In Persona 5, you can obtain cartridge of a parody of Ganbare Goemon.
Ganbare Goemon puzzles are featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.
The "Konami 50th Anniversary Wai Wai Collab" limited event from Bombergirl features a Ganbare Goemon 2 BGM.
Goemon makes an appearance in Kaettekita Pixel Crows.
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate features a downloadable costume based on Goemon from Ganbare Goemon.

Get Out.description: Following the release of Get Out, various fan theories emerged, including ones linking Get Out to Being John Malkovich. In a December 2017 Vanity Fair interview, Get Out director Jordan Peele discussed these theories. Peele revealed that he and Being John Malkovich director Spike Jonze had discussed the theory, and although the connection wasn't intended, after hearing Jonze's response he now sees both films as set in the same continuity. Peele concluded, "as far as I'm concerned, it's true."
In the Big Mouth episode "Pillow Talk" there is a billboard parodying Get Out titled "Stay Out". The billboard features Jordan Peele's name and a depiction of the character Chris Washington.

There's a minor reference to Ghosts 'n Goblins in episode 3 of Pop Team Epic.
Characters from Ghouls 'n Ghosts appear in The Knights of Avalon as part of a Capcom limited promotion.
Ghosts 'n Goblins can be seen in Animation vs. Super Mario Bros.
Music from Ghosts 'n Goblins can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix after an update.
Ghosts 'n Goblins and Ghouls 'n Ghosts are included in Capcom Arcade Stadium.
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate features a downloadable costume and spirit based on Arthur from Ghosts 'n Goblins.
TEPPEN update 4.3 added characters from Ghosts 'n Goblins.
A costume based on Arthur from Ghosts 'n Goblins can be found in Astro Bot.

Ghosts (TV).description: Pete mentions Star Trek in CBS’s Ghosts episode “Dinner Party”.

A kid dresses up as a Ghostbuster in CBS’s Ghosts episode “Halloween”.
Legally Blonde was mentioned in CBS’s Ghosts episode “Jay’s Sister”.
Jay mentions Friends in the CBS Ghosts episode "Jay's Friends".

The vault suit from Fallout 4 can be found in Ghostwire: Tokyo.
You can find a set of Blu-rays of fictional movies in Ghostwire: Tokyo called "Serbian Psycho", "White Fog" and "Zom Bomb". These movies also have posters that you can find in The Evil Within.

Giana Sisters.description: The Great Giana Sisters is based on Super Mario Bros.
Hard'n'Heavy was originally planned as Giana 2 – Arthur and Martha in Future World.
Enemies resembling a robot Giana appear in The Adventures of Quik & Silva.
The Cosmonaut Comrade from SpeedRunners appears in the multiplayer mode of Giana Sisters Twisted Dreams.

Gidget.description: Gidget and her family shipwreck on a deserted island in The New Gidget "Gilligidge Island", and actors from Gilligan's Island appear as themselves with many references to the show.

Giftpia.description: Chibi-Robo! features the dog Tao from Giftpia.
Mappo and Tao from Giftpia make an appearance in Captain Rainbow (Tao also appears in Chibi-Robo!! but his page in the official site states him to be from Giftpia).
Mappo from Giftpia appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

GigaBash.description: Godzilla, Gigan, Kiryu and Destoroyah appear in GigaBash as guest characters.
Ultraman, Ultraman Tiga, Alien Baltan and Camearra appear in GigaBash as guest characters.

Gilligan's Island.description: Gidget and her family shipwreck on a deserted island in The New Gidget "Gilligidge Island", and actors from Gilligan's Island appear as themselves with many references to the show.
Gilligan and the Skipper from Gilligan's Island appears in Back to the Beach.
ALF dreams he meets the characters from Gilligan's Island in ALF "Somewhere Over the Rerun".
Gilligan's Island is mentioned in the Rugrats episodes "The Seven Voyages of Cynthia", "Runaway Angelica", and "Angelica's Worst Nightmare".
Gilligan's Island is mentioned in Sister Act 2: Back in the Act.
Roseanne has a dream about Gilligan's Island in the Roseanne episode "Sherwood Schwartz: A Loving Tribute".
Gilligan, the Professor and Mary Ann from Gilligan's Island appear in the Meego episode Mommy 'n' Meego.
Gilligan and Marry Ann from "Gilligan's Island" appear in the "Baywatch" episode "Now Sit Right Back and You'll Hear a Tale".
Gilligan's Island" is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Dinner Out".
Skipper from Gilligan's Island is mentioned in the The King of Queens episode: "Fatty McButterpants".
Gilligan's Island is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Poker".
J.D. mentions naming his kids after Gilligan and Skipper from Gilligan's Island in the Scrubs episode "Her Story II".
Lawrence and Candace make a reference to the Gilligan's Island theme song in the episode "Swiss Family Phineas".
Mary Ann and Ginger from Gilligan's Island are mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "The Wedding (Part 2)".

Gilligan's Island.description: Gilligan's Island is shown on TV in Apollo 10 ½: A Space Age Childhood.

Gingerdead Man.description: The Gingerdead Man appears in Evil Bong and some of its sequels, with Gingerdead Man vs. Evil Bong and the comic The Gingerdead Man Meets Evil Bong being crossovers between the two series.
Dollman fights Gingerweed Man in the extra San Diego Comic Con exclusive story in Dollman Kills the Full Moon Universe #1.

Gintama.description: Gintoki is a playable character in the series.
Ryuk appears as a cameo near the end of an episode of Gintama.
There is a reference to Saint Seiya in Episode 44 of the Gintama anime.
Taiko no Tatsujin 10 and later games in the series feature music tracks from Gintama.
Pop'n Music 18 Sengoku Retsuden, Pop'n Music 19 TUNE STREET and Utacchi feature tracks from Gintama.
The Sket Dance series had a series of crossover episodes with the Gintama.
One of Koro-sensei's clones is seen cosplaying as Takasugi from Gintama in Episode 6 of the Assassination Classroom anime.

Gintama.description: Gintama characters appear in Saiki K as part of a crossover. Additionally, items from Gintama make their way into the world of Saiki K.

Minto appears in episode 9 of the anime.

Characters from Ghost in the Shell appear in Girls' Frontline as part of a collaboration event.

Gish.description: Gish appears in Clubby the Seal.

Glee.description: The song "Defying Gravity" from Wicked is featured in the Glee episodes: “Wheels” and "100".
Pretty Woman is mentioned in the Glee episode "Home".
The Glee episode "Laryngitis" features a reference to Super Mario Bros. 3.

Inception is mentioned in the Glee episode "Rocky Horror Glee Show".

Glee is mentioned in Class of '09: The Anime Pilot.

Glitch Karts.description: Pomni from The Amazing Digital Circus is a playable character in Glitch Karts.
Mel from The Gaslight District is a playable character in Glitch Karts.
Princess Guinevere from Knights of Guinevere is a playable character in Glitch Karts.
Uzi from Murder Drones is a playable character in Glitch Karts.

Official Gloomy Bear merchandise was released featuring characters from VA-11 Hall-A.
Official Gloomy Bear merchandise was released featuring characters from Tokyo Revengers.

Glory of Heracles.description: Archanea from Fire Emblem is mentioned as a fictional place in Glory of Heracles.
JonTron reviews Glory of Heracles games in the episode, Hercules Games.
Glory of Heracles characters appear in The Knights of Avalon during the third Namco collaboration event.
Sprites from Glory of Heracles appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.
The Glory of Heracles Hero and Heracles appear as spirits in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; a music track from Glory of Heracles is also featured in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.

Glove on Fight.description: Glove on Fight features Akiko Minase and Ayu Tsukimiya from Kanon as playable characters.
Glove on Fight features Satsuki Yumizuka and Ciel from Tsukihime as playable characters.

Glover.description: A secret minigame with Frogger appears in Glover.
The 217th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of Glover.

Spider-Man is mentioned in Gnomeo And Juliet and Sherlock Gnomes.
Game of Gnomes is mentioned in Sherlock Gnomes.
Indiana Gnomes is mentioned in Sherlock Gnomes.
The Twilight Gnome is mentioned in Sherlock Gnomes.

Teslakid is a playable character in Go All Out!.
Yandere-chan is a playable character in Go All Out!.
