Klonoa.description: Klonoa has an image of Pac-Man on his hat, and a picture of Pac-Man appears on Klonoa's house in strip #2 of Klonoa: Dream Traveler of Noctis Sol. Additionally, a hat based on Klonoa can be obtained in Pac-Man Mega Tunnel Battle Chomp Champs.
The race course "Phantomile" from R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 is named after one of the locations in Klonoa, and it features billboards of the series; one of the game's trophies is based on Klonoa.
Klonoa is an unlockable character in Alpine Racer 3.
Klonoa is one of the players in the "Namco All Stars '90" team in World Kicks.
Klonoa is an unlockable character in Smash Court 3, while artwork of Klonoa appears as an easter egg in the training mode of Smash Court 2.
An image of Klonoa appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.
Klonoa is an unlockable character in MotoGP.
A parody of Klonoa called "Klonoa of the Cold" is featured within Segagaga.
In Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail with an artwork of Klonoa, purportedly coming from him as well.
Klonoa is a selectable character in Family Tennis Advance.

Taiko no Tatsujin: Tatacon de DODON ga DON and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Klonoa series and Klonoa makes an actual appearance in the Game Over screen, while Katsu and Don make a cameo appearance in Klonoa Heroes: Densetsu no Star Medal.
Susumu Hori from Mr. Driller makes a cameo appearance in Klonoa Heroes: Densetsu no Star Medal, while Mr. Driller Ace features a Pacteria named and based on Klonoa.
Ki from The Tower of Druaga makes a cameo appearance in Klonoa Heroes: Densetsu no Star Medal.

Moji-kun and Moji-chan make a cameo appearance in Klonoa Heroes: Densetsu no Star Medal, while Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Klonoa characters running in the background and a remix of a Klonoa theme in certain puzzles, and Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Encore adds a set of stages based on characters and items from Klonoa.

Family Stadium 2003 features a stadium set in the world of Klonoa, and Klonoa himself appears as a player in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match, with the King of Sorrow also appearing in Dream Match; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Famista Advance is called Popka, and an image of Klonoa appears in the Namco stadium.
Namco × Capcom features characters from the Klonoa series.
Klonoa: Door to Phantomile is included in NamCollection.
QuickSpot and Machigai Museum 2 feature several puzzles based on Klonoa.

Klonoa is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, while a Klonoa plushdoll appears in Tales of Destiny 2, a Klonoa costume is featured in Tales of Symphonia, Tales of Fandom Vol.2 and Tales of Vesperia, and the latter also features a Klonoa diorama machine; while Tales of Phantasia and Vesperia also include a Klonoa statue.
Klonoa and Guntz appear as summons in Keroro RPG.
A Klonoa costume is unlockable in Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha A's Portable: The Gears of Destiny.
A Klonoa keychain is included in the Soul Calibur V downloadable pack Miscellaneous Equipment 1.
A character dressed like Klonoa appears in strip #7 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary web comic.

Klonoa makes a cameo in strip #100 and #222 of the Bravoman web comic, and strips #239/240 feature Alpha Man disguised as Klonoa; Klonoa also appears in the episode "Generic Winter Holiday" of the web series.
Lolo from Klonoa is a character in Namco High.
Klonoa appears in Lee's custom portrait in Tekken 7 (update 1.07).
Arino plays Klonoa: Door to Phantomile in episode 281 of GameCenter CX.
A costume based on Klonoa can be found in Astro Bot.
Costumes based on Klonoa were added to Little Nightmares III as DLC.

Konami Wai Wai World.description: Goemon is a playable character in the series, while purchasing a cartridge item at a store in Ganbare Goemon 2 turns the money woman into Konami Lady, and Konami Lady appears at the game center in The Legend of the Mystical Ninja.

The TwinBee ship is a playable character in the series, and Dr. Cinnamon is established to be the creator of Konami Lady.

In Just One Bite, near the end of the episode, Squidward gluttonously chows down all the Krabby Patties in the Patty Vault, despite SpongeBob's warnings not to do so, to the point that they all go down to his thighs and explode, similar to how Piggy Hamhock explodes from overeating near the end of the Looney Tunes cartoon Pigs is Pigs. In SpongeBob Meets the Strangler, the scene where the Tattletale Strangler jumps out of a plane with a parachute only to find out that the parachute is SpongeBob is a reference to the Looney Tunes cartoon Yankee Doodle Daffy where Porky jumps out of a plane with Daffy as a parachute. In Patrick SmartPants, the scene where Patrick falls from a cliff is just like the Wile E. Coyote and Road Runner cartoons from Looney Tunes. In the episode To Save a Squirrel, SpongeBob sitting in a kettle of hot water and thinking it is a bath plus Patrick cutting up and adding carrots is a nod to a number of classic Bugs Bunny shorts in which an enemy attempts to cook Bugs Bunny in a similar fashion.

Mana.description: The Mana series started with Seiken Densetsu: Final Fantasy Gaiden; a chocobo is unlockable as a pet in Legend of Mana, while Final Fantasy Legends: Toki no Suishou features Salamander and Undine from the Mana series as a summon called Spirit of Mana, and characters from Secret of Mana and Trias of Mana also appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations; Final Fantasy Record Keeper held a Japan-exclusive crossover event with Rise of Mana; additionally Final Fantasy X-2 features a minor reference to Secret of Mana while Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call features a downloadable track from Seiken Densetsu 3.
The Pebbler enemy in Secret of Mana may be based on Sonic.
The final bat boss in Secret of Mana is named Buffy, possibly after Buffy the Vampire Slayer.
Rudolph appears in Secret of Mana.
Secret of Evermore borrows gameplay elements from Secret of Mana.
The box for Secret of Mana can be seen in Dragon Ball Z: The Legacy of Goku II.
3D Dot Game Heroes features loading screens based on Seiken Densetsu 3 and Secret of Mana.
Gamzee's dance in AlterniaBound in Homesstuck is based on the Shopkeepers from the Mana series.
Music from Mana is present in Theatrhythm Final Fantasy: Curtain Call and Theatrhythm Final Bar Line.
Mana characters  appear in Merc Storia for a collaboration event.
Items and costumes from Secret of Mana appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Collection of Mana characters appear in Last Cloudia for a collaboration event.
Trials of Mana spirits are featured in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Arino plays the GB game Final Fantasy Adventure in episodes 357 and 358.

Mandrake the Magician.description: A cardboard cutout of Mandrake the Magician appears in Yellow Submarine.
Mandrake the Magician appears in Popeye Meets The Man Who Hated Laughter.
Mandrake the Magician appears in Defenders of the Earth.
Mandrake the Magician appears in Kings Watch and Kings Quest.

Manhattan Love Story.description: Gandalf is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Pilot", while The Hobbit is mentioned in the episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
Harry Potter is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episodes: "Pilot" and "Love Is a Battlefield".
The Muppets Take Manhattan is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Pilot".
Mary Poppins is mentioned in  the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Gay or British?".
David and Amy watch Mamma Mia! in  the Manhattan Love Story episode: "It's Complicated".
Cloverfield is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually".
Love Actually is mentioned in  the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually".
Ocean's Eleven is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually".
Star Wars is referenced in the Manhattan Love Story episodes: "Sex Actually" and "Empire State of Mind Strikes Back", the latter of which's title is a reference to Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back.
Guardians of the Galaxy is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually".
Magneto is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually".
In the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually", Peter owns a Black Widow poster.
In the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually", Peter owns a Hawkeye poster.
Spock is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
Games of Thrones is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
Wicked is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
Peter makes a Gladiator reference in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
Peter plays Killer Instinct (2013) in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Plus One".
The Ninja Rap from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Secret of the Ooze is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Plus One".
Scandal is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Plus One".
Katniss Everdeen is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Happy Thanksmas".
Sex and the City is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
Sharknado is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Empire State of Mind Strikes Back".
Transformers is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Empire State of Mind Strikes Back".
Peter Parker is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Empire State of Mind Strikes Back".
Mario Kart is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Empire State of Mind Strikes Back".
Pee-wee Herman is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Empire State of Mind Strikes Back".

Maniac Mansion.description: The first notes of the Super Mario Bros. theme are featured in the NES version of Maniac Mansion.
Cobb from Loom appears in The Secret of Monkey Island. The seagull from Loom appears in The Secret of Monkey Island and Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge.
Nester enters the world of Maniac Mansion in a Howard & Nester comic strip.
Purple Tentacles appear in a bonus level in Zombies Ate My Neighbors.
In "Eddsworld Christmas Special", Tord gets a Maniac Mansion 2004 Special Edition game.

Chuck the Plant from Maniac Mansion can be found at the beginning of Tales of Monkey Island; additionally the tentacle from Maniac Mansion: Day of the Tentacle appears as an idol in The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition and as a costume in Monkey Island 2: Special Edition.
Purple Tentacle appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.

Manimal.description: Manimal is mentioned in the Newhart episode "Harris Ankles PIV for Web Post".
Manimal is mentioned in the Fresh Prince of Bel-Air episode "Stress Related".
Manimal is mentioned in the Caroline in the City episode "Caroline and Richard's Mom".
Manimal is mentioned in the Buffy the Vampire Slayer episode "Beauty and the Beasts".
Jonathan Chase from Manimal appears in the Night Man episode "Manimal".
Manimal is mentioned in the King of the Hill episode "DaleTech".

Manimal.game: Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby
Manimal.description: Manimal is mentioned in Talladega Nights.

Mannix.description: Joe Mannix appears in the Here's Lucy episode "Lucy and Mannix Are Held Hostage".
Joe Mannix appears in the Diagnosis: Murder episode "Hard-Boiled Murder".

Manta Manta.description: Jaws is mentioned by one of the characters in Manta, Manta.
The poster of Predator can be seen in Manta, Manta.
The poster of Rocky V can be seen in Manta, Manta. Rocky is mentioned by one of the characters in Manta Manta – Zwoter Teil.

In (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1, when Spucky suggests simply painting the damaged taxi pink camouflage, Rock (Til Schweiger) lists his tuning capabilities. This scene is exactly the same as Berti (also Til Schweiger) in Manta, Manta telling the radio reporter about his Opel Manta.
Terminator is mentioned by one of the characters in Manta Manta: Legacy.

Mao Mao.description: Mao Mao from Mao Mao: Heroes of Pure Heart appears in the OK K.O.! Let's Be Heroes episode "Crossover Nexus".
The name "Ultraclops" is presumably derived from the fictional Japanese tokusatsu character Ultraman.
Mao Mao is dressed as Finn in the episode Popularity Conquest.
Mao Mao is dressed as Robin in the episode Popularity Conquest.
Monica and Friends and Mao Mao: Heroes of Pure Heart crossover in several comic strips.

MapleStory.description: The NPC Casey from MapleStory had a little 8-bit Bub featured as part of a decoration.
Characters from MapleStory appear in Mabinogi as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Sword Art Online make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory.
The Boar Beach secret level in Risk of Rain uses the exact same platform layout as a secret area in MapleStory called The Pig Beach.
Characters from Attack on Titan make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory.
Characters from MapleStory appear in Fantasy War Tactics as part of a collaboration event.
Characters from Re:Zero make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory.
Characters from Evangelion make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory.
Characters from Cardcaptor Sakura make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory.
Characters from MapleStory appear in World of Dragon Nest as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Isekai Quartet make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory.
Hatsune Miku appears in MapleStory M as part of a special collaboration.
Music and skins based on MapleStory appear in DJMax Respect as part of the Respect X Nexon DLC Pack.

MapleStory.game: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
MapleStory.description: Characters from That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory.
Lucid and Pink Bean from MapleStory appear in KartRider: Drift as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from The Haunted House make an appearance in a themed event for MapleStory in the 5th season.
Characters from KonoSuba appeared in MapleStory as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Demon Slayer appeared in MapleStory as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Dave the Diver appeared in MapleStory as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Frieren: Beyond Journey's End appeared in MapleStory as part of a special collaboration.

Mappy.description: Stage 10 in Battle City is shaped after Mappy. Tanks based on Mappy and Nyamco appear in Tancle.

Nyamco from Mappy appears as an enemy in special stages in The Quest of Ki and Ki is featured in one of the images in the "Spot the Difference" minigame in Mappy Kids; a Gilgamesh costume with a special action is featured in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan, Gilgamesh also appears in Hippari Mappy Daisakusen and Touch the Mappy with 80's Dot Stars; while Mappy is featured in one of the action arts in Dungeon RPG: Druaga Daifugo no Tou.
The default name for the 1st player in Genpei Toma Den: Computer Boardgame is "Mappii".
The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of Mappy.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Mappy Kids.

The X68000 version of Galaga '88 features a bonus level with enemies from Mappy, while Mappy himself makes an appearance in Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition; while Galaga characters appear in Touch the Mappy with 80's Dot Stars.

One of the enemy cars in Ridge Racer features Mappy images, "Mappy" is a car brand in later games in the series, R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 features the "Micro Mouse Mappy" team and a Mappy trophy, Ridge Racer 3D sport emblems of Mappy, Goro and Mewkie and Ridge Racer Accelerated features a cup named after Mappy.
Mappy, a Meowky and Goro from Mappy are secret bonus characters in Tinkle Pit, alongside three items.

The Meowky from Mappy are among the audience in the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4 and Famista 64, and Mappy himself appears as a player in Famista Online 3, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match, while Nyamco appears in Famista Online 2011, Famista Returns and Famista Climax (here in the Rivals team); additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Mappy" and "Nyamco".
Namco Classic Collection Vol. 1 includes Mappy and an arranged version.
Mappy is included in Namco Museum Vol. 2, Namco Museum Battle Collection and Namco Museum 50th Anniversary, with Mappy appearing in the intro of Vol. 2 and Encore.
Artwork of Mappy appears in one of the courts in Smash Court.
One of the horses in Final Furlong is named "Mappy".
Mappy is featured in Namco History Vol.1.
Mappy is one of the players in the "Namco All Stars '80" team in World Kicks.
An image of Mappy appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.
Taiko no Tatsujin and later games in the series feature music tracks from Mappy; music from Mappy is also featured in the Namcot Medley, debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10.
Mr Driller Ace: Fushigi no Pacteria features a Pacteria named and based on Mappy.
Mappy appears in Namco Super Wars.

Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Mappy characters running in the background and a remix of the Mappy theme in certain puzzles, Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe features a puzzle based on Goro with Mappy serving as the assistant.
A song from Mappy is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
The item "Mappy's Hat" in Namco × Capcom references Mappy.
Tales of the Abyss features a Mappy display in Nam Cobanda Isle, while Tales of Vesperia features a Mappy figurine and Tales of Destiny II includes a remix medley of music from Mappy.
Mappy characters and one location appear in Party Land.

Mappy is an unlockable racer in the PSP version of Pac-Man World Rally and a theme featuring Mappy characters appears in Pac-Man 99; while Pac-Man characters appear in Mappy Kids (as images), Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan, Hippari Mappy Daisakusen and Touch the Mappy with 80's Dot Stars; Mappy is included in Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man, Pac-Man's Arcade Party and Pac-Man's Pixel Bash alongside Hopping Mappy.
QuickSpot feature one puzzle image using Mappy sprites.
A remix of the main theme from Mappy is featured in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 05, with other remixes included in later releases; while the OVA features a Mappy plushie and phone strap.
Some levels of Noby Noby Boy feature Mappy characters.
Mappy appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Mappy is a playable character in Namco Chronicle.

Mappy makes a cameo in strip #33 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic, while the Dig Dug protagonist is a supporting character in Mappy: The Beat; Dig Dug, Pookas and Fygars appear in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan, Hippari Mappy Daisakusen and Touch the Mappy with 80's Dot Stars; additionally a Mappy costume appears in Dig Dug Island and a Pooka image appears in Mappy Kids.
Sky Kid is a support character in the web series Mappy: The Beat.
Albatross from Rolling Thunder appears in Episode 3 of Mappy: The Beat, while Maskers from Rolling Thunder appear in the "Spot the Difference" minigame image in Mappy Kids.

Wonder Momo is referenced in Episode 4 of Mappy: The Beat, while a Wonder Momo costume with a special action is featured in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan, and she later appears in Hippari Mappy Daisakusen.
The Prince from Katamari Damacy appears in Episode 5 of Mappy: The Beat.
Richard and Keith from Time Crisis appear in Episode 6 of Mappy: The Beat.
Indy Borgnine from Tower of Babel appears in episode 8 of Mappy. The Beat, and a costume of Borgnine with a special action is featured in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan.
Tarosuke from Yōkai Dōchūki appears in Episode 9 of Mappy: The Beat.
Meowkie from Mappy is a character in Namco High.

Bravoman appears as a guest character in the final story arc of Mappy: The Beat, while Mappy makes a cameo appearance in the episode "Generic Winter Holiday" of the Bravoman web series; strip #240 features Bravoman disguised as Mappy.

Valkyrie makes an appearance in Episode 12 of Mappy: The Beat, while a Valkyrie costume with a special action is featured in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan; Valkyrie also appears in Hippari Mappy Daisakusen.
Camilla from Ace Combat Infinity humes the main theme of Mappy during a mission; the game also features nicknames and emblems based on the series.
Pac-Man uses the trampoline from Mappy in his up special in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS, for Wii U, and Ultimate; additionally a sprite of Mappy appears in Pac-Man's taunt.
A costume of Clovis from Dragon Buster with a special action is featured in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan.
A costume of Wagan with a special action is featured in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan.
A Mappy "Police Mouse" costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 3.
Mouse enemies dressed as Mappy appear in Cat Busters as part of a Namco Catalog IP collaboration.
Mappy characters appear in The Knights of Avalon during the first Namco collaboration event.
The main theme of Mappy is part of the "Namcot Medley" BGM featured in Groove Coaster 4: Starlight Road.
Mappy characters appear in Pixel Runner!.
Sprites from Mappy appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.
A human version of Mappy appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.
There is a level in SPY x ANYA: Operation Memories based on Mappy.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Mappy.

Marble Madness.description: The Captain N: The Game Master episode "I Wish I Was a Wombatman" features elements from Marble Madness.
Marble Madness is featured in Arcade's Greatest Hits: The Atari Collection 2
Marble Madness is included in Midway Arcade Treasures and Midway Arcade Treasures: Extended Play.
The Video Game High School episode "Welcome to Varsity" features a reference to Marble Madness.
Elements of Marble Madness are featured in the Midway Arcade level pack for Lego Dimensions.
The season 7 episode "Deez Keys" from Regular Show features an area based on Marble Madness.

Mario.description: There were multiple Game & Watch games released featuring Mario characters. Mario characters also appeared in the Game & Watch Gallery games.
The Mario series is a spinoff of the Donkey Kong series; characters from Donkey Kong also appeared in many Mario games; the Mario vs Donkey Kong sub-series is part of both series.
A commercial for the Atari 2600 port of Mario Bros. features a parody of the Car 54, Where Are You? theme song.
The Wrecking Crew series is a spin-off of the Mario series.
One of the Mario Brothers is the referee in Tennis.
Mario and Luigi make an appearance in the audience in the arcade game Punch-Out!!; Mario is also the referee in Punch-Out!! for the NES.
The level complete sound from the Famicom port of Lode Runner is used as the title screen in Mario Bros. Special.
The Sidesteppers and Fighter Flies from Mario Bros. make an appearance in built-in games in Family Basic - v.3.

The boss Manhandla in The Legend of Zelda is a giant Piranha Plant from the Mario series, with other Mario enemies also appearing in later episodes; the Warp Whistle from The Legend of Zelda is featured in Super Mario Bros. 3 while Mario visits Hyrule in Volume 4 of Super Mario-Kun and Link appears in Super Mario Bros. & Friends: When I Grow Up and Super Mario RPG; The downloadable content pack The Legend of Zelda × Mario Kart 8 for Mario Kart 8 includes elements from the Zelda series.
The Great Giana Sisters is based on Super Mario Bros.
Mario is the player in Golf US Course, Golf Japan Course, the Game Boy Golf and NES Open Tournament Golf; Mario Open Golf is part of both series.
Yume Kojo: Doki Doki Panic features elements from the Mario series; Being a clone of Doki Doki Panic, Super Mario Bros. 2 (USA) features the same enemies and levels from that game.
Doraemon makes small cameos in Super Mario-Kun. UNDIRECT: Characters from Doraemon, Mario, and Little Ghost Q-Taro meet in the October 1987 issue of Shogakukan's Kindergarten.
Mario is the pilot in Famicom Grand Prix: F-1 Race; Mario, Luigi, Toad, Peach and Bowser appear in F-1 Race for the Game Boy.
Mario is the pilot in Famicom Grand Prix: F-1 Race and its sequel with Luigi as the navigator, while the Monster truck makes an appearance in Super Mario Bros. & Friends: When I Grow Up.
Nester comics feature many references to Mario games.
Mario meets Ryu from Ninja Gaiden in the 1989 flyer, Catch the Title Wave.
Mario meets a football player from Tecmo Bowl in the 1989 flyer, Catch the Title Wave.
Mario meets Fester from The Addams Family in the 1989 flyer, Catch the Title Wave. The Addams Family is mentioned in the Swedish dub of the Super Mario Bros. Super Show episode "Mommies Curse".

Mario meets Michelangelo from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles in the 1989 flyer, Catch the Title Wave. The titular characters from The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "Sneaky Lying Cheating Giant Ninja Koopas" as well as The Koopa Bros. from Paper Mario are based on the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles; The episode "The Gaminator" of the 2003 Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles series features a reference to Super Mario Bros.
Mario is the pilot of the spaceship in Alleyway
Mario and Luigi are the leaders of the teams in the Game Boy version of Baseball.
In the episode "Missing Persons" of the Freddy's Nightmares TV series, two children play Super Mario Bros.
Mario and Luigi make an appearance in Tetris for Game Boy and, with Peach and Bowser in Tetris for NES.
In the first Mother, a child talks about Super Mario Bros. 3 and the nonexisting Super Mario Bros. 7; Super Mario Maker features four costumes based on Mother characters.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! live action episode "Slime Busters" is a parody of Ghostbusters.
Captain N: The Game Master features some references to the Mario series; episodes from The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 and Super Mario World were featured in Captain N & the Video Game Masters.
Pee-wee Herman is mentioned in the Super Mario Bros. Super Show episode "Rolling Down the River".
The Flintstones is mentioned in the Latin American Spanish dub of the Super Mario Bros. Super Show episode "Bats in the Basement".
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Toad Warriors" is a parody of The Road Warrior.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! live action episode "E.C. The Extra Creepy" is a parody of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "The Fire of Hercufleas" features a reference to Rocky. An NPC in Mario is Missing! references the name "Italian Stallion" from Rocky.
Elvira guest stars in the live action episodes "Mommies Curse" and "The Ghoul of My Dreams" of The Super Mario Bros. Super Show!
John Rambo from Rambo is mentioned in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Lost Dog".
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! live action episode "Mario Hillbillies" is a parody of The Beverly Hillbillies.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! live action episode "9001: A Mario Odyssey" is a parody of 2001: A Space Odyssey.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "On Her Majesty's Sewer Service" is a parody of the James Bond series.

Luigi plays Duck Hunt in the Super Mario Bros. Super Show episode "Time Out Luigi". Super Mario Maker features a costume based on the Duck Hunt dog and duck; additionally Super Mario Bros. and Duck Hunt have been released in the same cartdrige in 2-in-1 Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt and in 3-in-1 Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt/World Class Track Meet.

The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Mario Meets Koop-zilla", The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "Dadzilla" and the Club Nintendo comic "Mario in Mariozilla" are parodies of Godzilla.
Inspector Gadget guest stars in the live action episode "Defective Gadgetry" of The Super Mario Bros. Super Show!
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Star Koopa" is a parody of Star Wars.
The Muppets Babies episode "It's Only Pretendo" features fictional videogames based on Mario games.
The Wizard features characters playing Super Mario USA and Super Mario Bros. 3.

A version of Super Mario Bros. is included in Nintendo World Championships. Versions of Super Mario Bros., Super Mario Bros. 2, Super Mario Bros. 3, and Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels are included in Nintendo World Championships: NES Edition
Mystery Science Theater 3000 episode 111 and some later episodes feature references to the Mario series.
The Game Boy version of Qix features cameos of Mario, Luigi and Princess Peach.
The Royal Parrot in the The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "Sneaky Lying Cheating Giant Ninja Koopas" mentions having a Big Bird poster.

The Royal Parrot in the The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "Sneaky Lying Cheating Giant Ninja Koopas" mentions having a Woody Woodpecker poster in the Latin American Spanish dub and Castilian Spanish re-dub.
The first notes of the Super Mario Bros. theme are featured in the NES version of Maniac Mansion.

The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "Misadventure of Mighty Plumber" mentions Indiana Jones in the Latin American Spanish dub and Castilian Spanish re-dub. The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Raiders of the Lost Mushroom" is a parody of Raiders of the Lost Ark.
Bowser makes a cameo in SimCity for the SNES, while Bowser's Castle is unlockable in SimCity DS.
The Adventures of Willy Beamish features a fictional game based on Super Mario Bros.
The Game Boy comic series by Valiant is based on Super Mario Land.
The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air episode "Love at First Fight" features a reference to Super Mario Bros.
The Tiny Toon Adventures episode "K-ACME TV" features a videogame based on Super Mario Bros.
Enemies resembling Mario's head appear in The Adventures of Quik & Silva.
The Ren & Stimpy Show episode "Stimpy's Big Day" features a videogame based on Super Mario Bros. in a fake commercial.
Mario appears as a pilot in a European commercial for Top Gun: The Second Mission.
The show "Mister Koopa's Neighborhood" in the Super Mario World episode "Rock TV" is a reference to Mister Rogers' Neighborhood.
The Yoshi series is a spinoff of the Mario series; the games Mario & Yoshi, Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island and Yoshi's Island: Super Mario Advance 3 are part of both series.
The Super Mario World Barcode Battler Cards set is part of both series.
The freeware version of Jill of the Jungle featured a reference to an italian superhero called "Mario".
Mario and Lemmy Koopa have a cameo in Super Scope 6; Sniper Bills from Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga use the Super Scope.
In Beethoven a character is seen playing Super Mario Bros. 3.

Captain Falcon makes a cameo in the comic Super Mario: Im Rausch der Geschwindigkeit and in Volume 4 of Super Mario-kun; One of the tracks in F-Zero X is the "Rainbow Road" from Mario Kart 64; The downloadable content pack The Legend of Zelda × Mario Kart 8 for Mario Kart 8 includes a track based on F-Zero.
Mario fights some Street Fighter II characters in the comic Super Mario Klemp-Won-Do: Muskeln sind nicht alles!

Pit from Kid Icarus is featured in the comic Super Mario: Die Bescherung; UNDIRECT: A challenge for Kid Icarus within NES Remix 2 features elements from Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels and Super Mario Bros. 3.
Mega Man is featured in Super Mario: Die Bescherung and some other Club Nintendo comics.
In a scene of 3 Ninjas, one of the main characters is seen playing Super Mario Bros. 3, while a balloon version of Mario can be seen in 3 Ninjas Kick Back.
The J Son enemy in Super Mario Land 2 references Jason Woorhees; a monster very similar to Jason is also featured in the comic Super Mario in Die Nacht des Grauens - Part 1.
Kirby is featured in Super Mario-Kun and other Mario comics; Mario characters and items have cameos in Kirby Super Star.
Mario is Missing! and the Club Nintendo comic "Mario in Mariozilla" feature references to King Kong.
Super Hornio Brothers is a pornographic parody of the Mario series and specifically the Super Mario Bros. movie.

Fox from Star Fox is featured in the comics Super Mario: Mario im Wunderland and, with other Star Fox characters in Part 3 of Super Mario: Verloren in der Zeit; he also makes a cameo in Super Mario-Kun #7.
The film Super Mario Bros. features references to The Wizard of Oz.
The film Super Mario Bros. features a reference to The Blues Brothers.
Joe and Mac are featured in the comic Super Mario: Verloren in der Zeit Part 1.
Erik, Baleog and Olaf from The Lost Vikings are featured in the comic Super Mario: Verloren in der Zeit Part 2.
The Wario series is a spin-off of the Mario series. The games Mario & Wario and Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3 are part of both series.
The three viruses from Dr. Mario make a cameo in Motoko chan no Wonder Kitchen.
Plok is featured in the comic Super Mario: Verloren in der Zeit Part 3. One panel from the comic is then shown in page 96 of the webcomic Plok: The Exploding Man, and referenced again in page 117.
A Battletoad is featured in the comic Super Mario: Verloren in der Zeit Part 3.
In StarTropics II there's a character riding a Koopa Troopa.
Mario's Face appears on billboards in Stunt Race FX. An F-Type doll can also be found in Super Mario RPG.
One of the tracks in Uniracers is called "Wario Paint".
Mario's Picross and Mario's Super Picross are part of both series.
Toad from the Mario series is the main character in Satella-Q.

Bart Simpson imagines Mario and Luigi in The Simspons episode "Marge Be Not Proud"; there are other Mario references in other episodes of the series as well as the comics and videogames. "Lisa Simpson" is given as an answer to a question in Mario is Missing!.

Mario & Wario can be seen on a TV in Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue; In Pokémon Stadium 2, connecting video game consoles to a TV can show images from Mario games; Super Mario Maker features costumes based on Pokémon.
Samus Aran has a cameo in Super Mario RPG; UNDIRECT: A challenge for Metroid within NES Remix 2 features elements from Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels and Super Mario Bros. 3.
The Axem Rangers in Super Mario RPG are based on the Super Sentai/Power Rangers.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Dragon Ball. The box for Super Mario Kart can be seen in Dragon Ball Z: The Legacy of Goku II.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Lupin III.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Neon Genesis Evangelion.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Sailor Moon.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Virtua Fighter.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Fist of the North Star.
Thoughts in Super Mario RPG reference Mobile Suit Zeta Gundam and Mobile Suit Gundam 0083: Stardust Memory.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Ninja Hattori-kun.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references the tagline to Poltergeist II: The Other Side.
A living doll very similar to Chucky is featured in the comic Super Mario in Die Nacht des Grauens - Part 1.

A monster very similar to Pinhead is featured in the comic Super Mario in Die Nacht des Grauens - Part 1, while in Part 2 there's an object very similar to the Lemarchand's box while Kirby's look assumes some of Pinhead's features.
In Pilotwings 64 Mario's face can be seen on Mount Rushmore, and changes to Wario's when shot; UNDIRECT: the Super Mario Bros. sounds return from Wii Sports Resort in Pilotwingd Resort.
In Crash Bandicoot there are some enemies similar to Piranha Plants and Koopa Troopas; there also are other references in other episodes of the series.
A golden Mario statue appears in BS Shin Onigashima, while Super Mario Maker features costumes based on Donbe and Hikari from Shin Onigashima.
Excitebike: Bun Bun Mario Battle Stadium is a crossover between the two series; The downloadable content pack The Legend of Zelda × Mario Kart 8 for Mario Kart 8 includes a track based on Excitebike.
The Boy Meets World episode "Quiz Show" features a reference to the Mario series.

MediEvil.description: On Albia, a picture of Zarok can be found under a windmill.
The name MediEvil comes from the original title of Army of Darkness, The MediEvil Dead. The Severed Hand enemies are also a reference to the Evil Dead films.

According to MediEvil game designer Jason Wilson, the Harry Potter author named Florean Fortescue in Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban after Sir Daniel Fortesque due to talking to one of the game's developers on a train.
The layout and general gameplay of the Inside the Asylum level was based on the arenas in Smash TV.
The North American and European versions of Everybody's Golf 2 feature Sir Daniel Fortesque as an unlockable golfer.
MediEvil and C-12: Final Resistance were released together in C-12: Final Resistance and MediEvil Twin Pack.
Colonel Freddie Fortesque from Ghosthunter is a reference to Sir Dan.
A ship called Medievil appears in WipEout Pure as a promotion of MediEvil: Resurrection. A WipEout Pure demo can be played in MediEvil: Resurrection.

The cutscene in the Shadow Demon Tomb in MediEvil: Resurrection where Dan tries to swap out the Anubis Stone piece with a pumpkin is based on the famous Golden Idol swapping scene from Raiders of the Lost Ark.
The Shrubbites in MediEvil: Resurrection are a parody of the Ents, while the Fazguls are a parody of the Nazgûl.

The cutscene at the beginning of the Dragon Island level in MediEvil: Resurrection is based on the scene of Jack Sparrow arriving into port on a sinking boat from Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl.
The Mad Axeman's entrance cutscene in MediEvil: Resurrection references the famous "Here's Johnny" scene from The Shining.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features Sir Daniel Fortesque from MediEvil as a playable character.
A portrait of Sir Daniel Fortesque from MediEvil can be found in Guacamelee! 2.
MediEvil was one of the biggest inspirations for Pumpkin Jack.
Clive 'N' Wrench has a plethora of references to MediEvil throughout its levels, including posters, signs, inscriptions on crypts, and so on.
A bot that resembles Sir Daniel Fortesque appears in Astro's Playroom. A costume based on Sir Daniel Fortesque from MediEvil can be found in Astro Bot.
The level Devilled Gardens in Antonblast is inspired by MediEvil. The title card for the level also uses the same font as MediEvil's logo.

Sonic and Mega Man: When Worlds Collide and Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite are crossovers between the two series.

The "High School Video Game" features a level based on Mega Man.
Several characters from Mega Man are featured in Otoranger.
A remix of Cut Man's theme from Mega Man is featured in CROSS×BEATS, while a remix of Wily Castle 1 from Mega Man 2 is featured in CROSS×BEATS REV.

Strider Hiryu is mentioned in the description of the Slash Claw from Mega Man 7, while the Slash Claw may be inspired by Hiryu's basic slash attack. The 2014 Strider features an area with a Light Capsule from the Mega Man X series in the background.
There's a reference to the stage select screen from Mega Man 3 in the Steven Universe episode "Onion Trade".
Mii Plaza includes a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Mega Man.

Mega Man appears as a playable character in Super Smash Bros for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U, with a stage based on the series; issue 42 of the Mega Man comic by Archie features a "Super Smash Variant", referencing Super Smash Bros.; the 3DS version of Mega Man Legacy Collection features compatibility with the Mega Man amiibo from the Super Smash Bros. series and also includes a gold version of that amiibo in the Collector's Edition.
Mega Man characters appeared in Zombie Cafe as part of several special promotions.
Several design elements in the character C-Sha from Megadimension Neptunia VII are references to the Mega Man series.
"Mega Man X" was mentioned in Chapter 48 of My Hero Academia.

The world of Ghosts 'n Goblins is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 9 - Infinite Possibilities, including appearances of Arthur, Astaroth and Firebrand. Roll's "Knight" DLC costume from Mega Man Powered Up is inspired by Arthur, and there's a DLC stage pack based on Ghosts 'n Goblins. There are also minor references to the series in Mega Man 7, Mega Man X6 and Rockman Xover.
The world of Okami is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 9 - Infinite Possibilities, including appearances of Amaterasu and Issun.
The world of Alex Kidd is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 9 - Infinite Possibilities, including appearances of Alex Kidd and Stella.
The world of NiGHTS into Dreams is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 9 - Infinite Possibilities, including appearances of NiGHTS, Reala and Wizeman.
The world of Skies of Arcadia is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 9 - Infinite Possibilities, including appearances of Vyse, Enrique, Gilder, Drachma, Fina and Aika.

The world of Monster Hunter is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Felyne, Palico and Gore Magala. Monster Hunter 4G/Ultimate and Monster Hunter X feature a Mega Man-themed Palico armor set and a Rush-themed weapon.

The world of Breath of Fire III is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Ryu, Nina, Momo, Honey, Peco, Garr and Rei; while a rescuable Reploid in Mega Man X6 is named after Nina from Breath of Fire and Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Mega Man, Roll, Volnutt and Tron Bonne.

The world of Viewtiful Joe is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Viewtiful Joe and Sexy Silvia. A Viewtiful Joe billboard appears in the final issue of the Dreamwave Mega Man comic book. The DLC stage pack "Joe A Go Go!!" from Mega Man Powered Up is named after Viewtiful Joe.

The world of Billy Hatcher is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Billy Hatcher, Rolly Roll, Chick Poacher, Bantam Scrambled and Menie-Funie.
The world of Golden Axe is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Gilius Thunderhead, Ax Battler and Tyris Flare.
The world of Panzer Dragoon is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Kell Fluge and a Blue Dragon.
The Irate Gamer reviews Mega Man on NES.
One of the alternate color palettes in Skullgirls is based on Bass from Mega Man.
Dino Run DX features a hat based on Mega Man.
Enter the Gungeon features a weapon called the Megahand that looks identical to Mega Man's Mega Buster.
Mighty No. 9 is a spiritual successor to Mega Man.

Chapter 35 of High Score Girl features a cameo of Air Man from Mega Man 2.
Geometry Dash features a robot skin based on Zero.
Mega Man X, Mega Man, Zero, and Tron Bonne have been subjects for DBX.
One of the bosses in Cuphead is inspired by Dr. Wily from Mega Man.

Elemental Story features characters from Mega Man X as part of a collaboration event.
Mega Man characters appear in Dragalia Lost during a special collaboration.

Metal Black was originally planed as a sequel to Darius II, and several enemies and elements in the game are based or related to bosses in Darius; while the Black Fry from Metal Black is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Taito DLC Pack.

Metal Gear.description: The boxart image from the NES Metal Gear is traced over a still of Kyle Reese from Terminator, while the Metal Gear enemy Arnold/Bloody Brad is based on the Terminator.
A Metal Gear called Mk. II makes an appearance in Snatcher, and it later returns in Metal Gear Solid 4. There also are other references between the two series.
The character Predator/Jungle Evil from Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake is inspired by the movie Predator.
Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake features a reference to the Minovsky Particles from Mobile Suit Gundam.
A vehicle in Neo Kobe 2045 Speed King is named after Solid Snake of Metal Gear.
In Metal Gear Solid, Psycho Mantis can mention Suikoden.

In Metal Gear Solid, Psycho Mantis can reference Castlevania if a save file for Castlevania: Symphony of the Night is on the memory card. Solid Snake's bandanna and Solid Eye from Metal Gear Solid 4 are hidden items in Castlevania: Lord of Shadows.
In the Japanese version of Metal Gear Solid, Psycho Mantis can detect a save for Tokimeki Memorial: Forever With You on the memory card.
Metal Gear Solid and Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of the Patriots feature the Moai from Gradius as a secret easter egg.
beatmania 3rdMix features METAL GEAR SOLID Main Theme, a remix of the main theme from Metal Gear Solid.

Konami Krazy Racers features the Cyborg Ninja from Metal Gear Solid as a selectable racer.
A parody of Metal Gear Solid called "Otalu Gear Solid" is featured within Segagaga.
Solid Snake's false identity "Iroquois Pliskin" in Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty is based on Snake Plissken from Escape from New York; there are other minor reference to the movie.
Solid Snake and Raiden are selectable in Evolution Skateboarding, while Metal Gear Solid 2: Substance features a minigame with elements from Evolution Skateboarding.
Final Fantasy X-2 features a reference to Metal Gear Solid.
Solid Snake is selectable in DreamMix TV World Fighters.
In Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes there are many references to the Mario series.
In Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes, Psycho Mantis mentions The Legend of Zelda if a save for The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker is detected.
Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes features references Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem, such as Psycho Mantis mentioning the game and a poster of Pious Augustus appearing.
Solid Snake makes a reference to Jurassic Park in Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes.

Solid Snake from Metal Gear makes an appearance in Boktai 2, while Master Otenko from Boktai makes an appearance in Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker. There is also a reference to Boktai in Metal Gear Solid 4.
Metal Gear Solid 3 features a reference to Austin Powers.
Metal Gear Solid 3 features a reference to From Russia with Love.
Metal Gear Solid 3 features a reference to Godzilla.
The "Snake vs. Monkey" minigame in Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater features the apes from Ape Escape, while Solid Snake from Metal Gear makes an appearance in Ape Escape 3.
In Metal Gear Solid 3, Snake mentions "Sam", likely referring to Sam Fisher from Splinter Cell, in "Snake vs Monkey".
In Metal Gear Solid 3, Snake mentions "Gabe", likely referring to Gabe Logan from Syphon Filter, in "Snake vs Monkey".
Several paintings from Silent Hill 3 can be found in Metal Gear Solid 3.

Solid Snake from the Metal Gear series makes an uncredited cameo in Yu-Gi-Oh! 7 Trials to Glory: World Championship Tournament 2005, while the "Tactical Espionage Expert" Yu-Gi-Oh card is based on Solid Snake.
A track from Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater appears in Karaoke Revolution: Volume 3.
Reiko Hinomoto from Rumble Roses is a playable character in the Online mode of Metal Gear Solid 3: Subsistence. EVA and Olga Gurlukovich costumes can be unlocked in Rumble Roses XX.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Metal Gear and Metal Gear 2.
Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops features a reference to Dirty Harry.
Captain S enters the world of Metal Gear.
Big Boss appears in I Wanna Be The Guy.

The english language version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Trials and Tribulations features a reference to Metal Gear Solid. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney 5 - Dual Destinies features both dialogue and visual references as well.

Snake is unlockable in Super Smash Bros. Brawl, with a stage also based on the series and Gray Fox featured as Assist Trophy; Psycho Mantis can mention Super Smash Bros. Melee in Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes.
Sunny can be seen playing Penguin Adventure in Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots.

Altair's clothes from Assassin's Creed are unlockable in Metal Gear Solid 4; Raiden's uniform from Metal Gear Solid 4 is unlockable in Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood; Brotherhood also features a reference to the Metal Gear series in the form of a cardboard box, while Metal Gear Solid Peace Walker features a reference to the "Leap of Faith".
Old Snake makes a reference to Star Wars in Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots.
Solid Snake is selectable in New International Track & Field.
LittleBigPlanet features downloadable clothes based on characters from the Metal Gear series.
3D Dot Game Heroes features a loading screen based on Metal Gear.
Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker features monsters from Monster Hunter, while Monster Hunter Portable 3rd features clothes based on Metal Gear characters.
Front Mission Evolved features sticker decals based on the Metal Gear series.
Risk: Metal Gear Solid is a format crossover between the two.
The Japanese version of Scribblenauts features spawnable Metal Gear characters.
A block based on Metal Gear Solid is playable in Blocks That Matter.
In The Stanley Parable Demo you can find a pic of Metal Gear.
In the Dick Figures episode: "Modern Flame War 3", there is an achievement named "SNAAAAAAAKEEEE!!!", referencing Metal Gear Solid.
Metal Gear Solid: Snake Eater 3D features Yoshi dolls.
Snake appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
An Exclamation Mark from the Metal Gear series makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features Raiden from the Metal Gear series as a playable character.
Lego City Undercover features a reference to Metal Gear.
One of the tutorial chapters in Yo-kai Watch features a minor reference to Metal Gear Solid.
Metal Gear Solid V was mentioned in the first part of the Black Friday Trilogy of South Park.
Hyperdevotion Noire: Goddess Black Heart features a character called Lid, that is a parody of Solid Snake.
In the Sanjay and Craig episode "Hot Sauce Boss", Hector was dressed like Solid Snake.
Metal Gear is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
Cyborg made a noise that resembled the exclamation noise from Metal Gear.
Metal Gear is parodied in Les Kassos.
A character based on Snake from the Metal Gear Awesome series appears as the tech store clerk in Pico Sim Date <3.
Solid Snake and Raiden have been subjects for Death Battle!
The box option in Fleeing the Complex is a spoof of the Metal Gear item, while the "Master Bounty Hunter" route in Completing the Mission features several references to the series.

A book can be found in Firewatch called "The Patriots" which is the name of the enemy organization in the Metal Gear Solid series. Not only that, but the book is written by Donald Anderson, The DARPA Chief from the first Metal Gear Solid.
Enter the Gungeon features several weapons that reference the Metal Gear Solid series.
The cover to Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes can be seen in the Black Mirror episode: "Playtest".
Raiden has been a subject for DBX.

In the chapter "Murder on the Owl Express" in A Hat in Time, a TV in the VIP Lounge shows a video game very similar to the title screen of Metal Gear Solid, while a trophy/achievement is named after Punished Snake from Metal Gear Solid V: Phantom Pain.

Ver.2.1 of Super Bomberman R added three stages from the Metal Gear series as well as Bombermen "Solid Snake Bomber", "Naked Snake Bomber" and "Raiden Bomber" based off characters from the series. The Xbox Series X/S version of Metal Gear Solid △: Snake Eater features a "Snake vs. Bomberman" mode.
CrossCode features a boss based on Metal Gears from the Metal Gear Solid series.
Sam owns "Nintendo Power V179", which has Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes on the cover.
Metal Gear Solid is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "Perfect Cell Vs Snake".
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Metal Gear Solid.
"Spec Ops" in the Glitch Techs episode "Karate Trainer" is a reference to Metal Gear.
Eda has a body pillow resembling Solid Snake in The Owl House episode “Adventures in the Elements”.
The Squirrel from cutscenes in Super Meat Boy Forever adopts an appearance that resembles Venom Snake from Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain.

In Dead Estate, there is a weapon called "Revengeance", which is a nod to Metal Gear Rising Revengeance and looks like Jetstream Sam’s weapon from the game. Fuji also has a costume based on Senator Armstrong.
A character dresses up as Solid Snake in the 23rd episode of Close Enough.
Psycho Mantis and Metal Gear Solid are mentioned in High on Life
Arino plays the PS1 game Metal Gear Solid as part of a DVD-exclusive challenge.
Solid Snake and Raiden appear in Fortnite.

The song "Sneaking" by Mori Calliope of Hololive was created to promote Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 1, and in the music video Mori is seen interacting with the characters and settings of the games.

The Bots from Astro Bot appear in Metal Gear Solid △: Snake Eater's "Snake vs. Monkey" mode, exclusive to the PlayStation 5 version. A bot that resembles Solid Snake appears in Astro's Playroom. Bots based on various characters from Metal Gear can be found in Astro Bot.

Metal Max.description: Pochi from the Metal Max series is a playable character in Umihara Kawase BaZooKa!!.

Metal Slug.description: Various Metal Slug characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games; the mini-game "Target 9" in SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millenium is based on Metal Slug and features Marco Rossi and Fio as playable characters, and a Mars People is a boss character in SVC Chaos.
Fiolina Germi from Metal Slug is playable in several installments of the King of Fighters series; characters from The King of Fighters appear in Metal Slug Defense.
Metal Slug characters are featured in Neo Geo Battle Coliseum.
Ralf Jones and Clark Still from Ikari Warriors appear in several Metal Slug games.
Marco Rossi briefly appears on the TV in Stage 1 of Dan The Man.
Characters from Fatal Fury appear in Metal Slug Defense.
Characters from Art of Fighting appear in Metal Slug Defense.
Characters from Metal Slug Defense appear in The Battle Cats as a part of a collaboration.
Overwatch features references to Metal Slug.
Characters from Metal Slug appear in Army Men Strike as a part of a collaboration.
Music tracks from Metal Slug are featured in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Characters and locations from Metal Slug appear in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event.
Violet from Arena of Valor appears in Metal Slug: Awakening as part of a crossover event.
A Metal Slug game box is seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Marco Rossi is playable in Contra Returns, while Bill Rizer is playable in Metal Slug: Awakening as part of a collaboration between both games.

Metalocalypse.description: "Thunderhorse", a song by Dethklok from Metalocalypse, is a bonus song in Guitar Hero II. "Laser Cannon Deth Sentence" by Dethklok is a downloadable song in Guitar Hero 5. "Bloodlines" by Dethklok is in Guitar Hero: Warriors of Rock.
V for Vendetta is parodied in the Metalocalypse episode "The Revengencers".
Eddie Riggs meets the characters from Metalocalypse in a promotion for their show.
"The Cyborg Slayers", a song by Dethklok from Metalocalypse, is featured in Saints Row: The Third.
John Goblikon announces his tour with Dethklok in the video "Nekrogoblikon on Tour with DETHKLOK", of whom they have done live performances with.

Metaphor: ReFantazio.description: A concept character from Project Re Fantasy, an early version of Metaphor: ReFantazio, appears in Earth UFO Catcher.

An Archetype called "Samurai" appears in Metaphor: ReFantazio which includes the ability to summon demons from the series. Costumes based on Shin Megami Tensei IV and Shin Meegami Tensei V were also added as DLC.

An Archetype called "Persona Master" appears in Metaphor: ReFantazio which includes the ability to summon personas from the game. Costumes based on various games in the Persona series were also added as DLC.
Archetypes called "Devil Summoner" and "Soul Hacker" appears in Metaphor: ReFantazio which includes the ability to summon demons from the game.
The Ariadne Thread from Etrian Odyssey appears in Metaphor: ReFantazio. Costumes based on Etrian Odyssey were also added as DLC.

Meteor Man.description: Spider-Man teams up with Meteor Man in Meteor Man #3.

Metro.description: On D6 level in Metro 2033, on the wall in the Missile Control room to the left from the main screen, there is an old boot with a plant growing out of it, a reference to WALL-E.
Liberty Prime is mentioned in the game Metro Exodus.
Characters and maps based on Metro Exodus appear in PUBG Mobile as part of a crossover event.

Metro-Cross.description: Elements from Metro-Cross appear in the background of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4.
Metro-Cross was featured in multiple Namco Museum titles.
A diorama machine based on Metro-Cross and a figurine of its main character can be found in Tales of Vesperia.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of the Metro-Cross car with characters assisting the player.
Some levels of Noby Noby Boy feature Metro-Cross characters.
The Runner from Metro-Cross appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
A sprite from Metro-Cross appears in Pac-Man's taunt in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.
Metro-Cross is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash, while a theme featuring characters from Metro-Cross appears in Pac-Man 99.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Metro-Cross.

Metroid.description: Samus plays The Legend of Zelda in the 1986 Metroid manga, Victory Techniques for Metroid. Metroid Prime 3 also features a reference to the series.
Samus plays Volleyball in the 1986 Metroid manga, Victory Techniques for Metroid.
Blaster Master features enemies that look like Metroids.
A character resembling Samus makes a cameo in Famicom Wars.
Mother Brain is the main villain in the Captain N TV show, while Samus appears in the comic.
Samus makes an appearance in Tetris for NES; Metroids appear as obstacles in Tetris DS.
In a scene in The Wizard, the main character Jimmy is seen playing Metroid.
Samus makes a cameo in the game boy version of F-1 Race.
Some games in the Metroid series have plot elements similar to the Alien movies.
Various elements from the Metroid series are featured in the "Cosmic" table of Galactic Pinball.
Samus Aran has a cameo in Super Mario RPG; UNDIRECT: A challenge for Metroid within NES Remix 2 features elements from Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels and Super Mario Bros. 3.
The Screw Attack ball is an obtainable item in Kirby Super Star, while Metroids and Samus appear in Kirby's Dream Land 3.
Jody Summer from F-Zero X is based on Samus from Metroid.
Samus and places from the Metroid series are featured in all Super Smash Bros. games.
Samus from Metroid appears in the N-Gang episode "Die Hexe lacht um Mitternacht".
The Federation Army Special Ops Battleship VIXIV IV from the 2002 Metroid manga and the Galactic Federation Battleship VIXIV take their name from the VIXIV spaceship in X.
Skulls similar to Crocomire's from Super Metroid can be seen in Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance.
Elements from the Metroid series appear in many Animal Crossing games as clothes and furnitures.
The box for Super Metroid can be seen in Dragon Ball Z: The Legacy of Goku II.
In 1080° Avalanche there are references to the Metroid series in the game's high scores.
Custom Robo: Battle Revolution features a reference to the Metroid series.
Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little Life features a reference to Metroid.
In the episode "Occam's Razor", Dr. House can be seen playing Metroid: Zero Mission.
Arino plays the Disk System game Metroid in episode 5. He also did a full play through of Super Metroid in 2010 as part of the Wii Virtual Console promotional episodes.
In the Supernatural episode "Wendigo", two characters are seen playing Metroid on the Nintendo DS.
Files based on Metroid Prime Hunters were obtainable by completing a level in UPIXO in Action: Mission in Snowdriftland.
Picross DS includes an image of Samus from Metroid.
Saroid in Aoi Sekai no Chushin de is based on Samus from Metroid.
Metroid Prime 3: Corruption features an unlockable sticker based on Excite Truck.
The "Brinstar" theme from Metroid is a downloadable song in the European version of Jam with the Band.
Samus' Zero Suit is unlockable in Project Zero 4.
The Code Monkeys episode "Valley of the Silicon Dolls" features a reference to Metroid.
Characters and locations from Metroid appear in I Wanna Be The Guy.
Samus' Arm Cannon is an unlockable weapon in Phantasy Star 0.
Shadow Complex features various gameplay elements from Super Metroid.
Cave Story features enemies similar to Metroids.
StarCraft II features a cameo by a creature resembling a Metroid.

Creatures from the Metroid series appear in the background in Donkey Kong Country Returns, along with other references to the series, while Samus' Gunship and a Metroid appear in Donkey Kong: Tropical Freeze.
Samus Aran has been a subject for Death Battle!
The video game Catherine features a character nemed Justin Bailey.
The Star Pics AR game uses a Samus card, and there also are Metroid refereneces in Graffiti.
Mii Plaza features unlockable hats based on Metroid and includes two Puzzle Swap puzzles based on Metroid games.
Samus' helmet is featured in Nintendogs + Cats.
Samus Aran is parodied in the MAD sketch "Gaming's Next Top Princess".
Dead or Alive: Dimensions features a stage based on Metroid: Other M which also features the appearances of Samus and Ridley.
A Metroid (later turned into a generic alien to avoid copyright issues) appears in Stealing the Diamond.
In the episode Hitman, Blastronaut resembles Samus Aran from Metroid.
Pushmo features a level based on a sprite from Metroid.
Kiki Trick features a scene from Super Metroid in a minigame.
The Komayto enemies in the Kid Icarus series are based on metroids; Kid Icaurus: Uprising features a direct reference to the Metroid series.
Dynasty Warriors Vs features a Zero Suit Samus costume.
Samus appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
Curly is seen wearing a Samus Aran costume in the Halloween update for Cave Story+.
Nintendo Land features a minigame based on the Metroid series.
Tekken Tag Tournament 2: Wii U Edition features a Zero Suit Samus outfit for the characters.
Zero Suit Frida costume from Skiing Fred is based on Samus Aran's Zero Suit.
Geometry Dash features a wave skin based on a Metroid and a skin based on Samus Aran.
Elements looking respectively like a Chozo Statue and Samus's helmet from Metroid appear in Teslagrad.
In one of the areas in the 2014 Strider there's a large brain in a containment tube shaped like the one holding Mother Brain from Metroid.
NES Remix 2 includes challenges based on Metroid.
The Wii U version of Bayonetta and Bayonetta 2 features the Power Suit from Metroid as a costume, also including the Arm Cannon and Morph Ball functionality.
Monster Hunter 4G/Ultimate features the Varia Suit and Zero Suit costumes from Metroid, along with the Arm Cannon weapon.
Metroid is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
Metroids appear on the wallpaper in One Night at Flumpty's.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Samus from Metroid: Other M.
Axiom Verge features a secret outfit based on Samus from Metroid.
One of the skins for Lt. Morales in Heroes of the Storm is based on Samus Aran.
Nintendo Badge Arcade features badges based on the Metroid series.
Dino Run DX features a hat based on Samus Aran.
Random Encounters has made a Metroid song.
Enter the Gungeon features a weapon called the Heroine that looks like Samus' arm cannon.
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of Metroid or Super Metroid.
An item similar to the Morph Ball from Metroid makes an appearance in Starbound.
Miitomo featured Metroid-themed items to promote the release of Metroid Prime: Federation Force.
In the episode "Terror Tales of the Park VI" from Regular Show, Eileen is dressed as Samus Aran from Metroid.
Miitopia features costumes based on Metroid characters, obtainable by scanning the respective amiibo.
Samus has been a subject for DBX.
Joey Claire has a poster for Super Metroid in Hiveswap.
Rocket League for Switch features a car based Samus's Gunship from Metroid.
Sam owns "Nintendo Power V31", which has Samus from Metroid II: Return of Samus on the cover.
The cover of the "Space Game" included with the Video Game Champ minifigure is based on Metroid Prime.
A Metroid Prime: Federation Force poster appears in Luigi's Mansion 3.
"Something About Super Metroid" is a parody of Super Metroid.
A Samus costume was added to Jump Rope Challenge with Update 1.1.0.
Samus and Metroid are mentioned in Ready Player Two.
The Chapter 4 introduction cutscene in Super Meat Boy Forever is a parody of the intro cutscene from Super Metroid.
Metroid is parodied in multiple Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episodes.

A silhouette resembling Samus from Metroid appears in the background of Batman/Fortnite: Zero Point #3. Samus was also originally supposed to be one of the Hunters in Fortnite Chapter 2 Season 5, but due to Nintendo wanting the skin to be a Nintendo Switch Exclusive, the skin was cancelled.

Microgame versions of Metroid games are featured in the WarioWare series, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "Super Metroid" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; there also are other minor references between the two series.
Haiku, the Robot features a statue that looks very similar to the Chozo statues from the Metroid series.
A Metroid poster can be seen in the music video for FNAF Kids.
A version of Metroid for the NES is included in Nintendo World Championships: NES Edition.
The "Sams" and "Meteor Oid" sprays in Antonblast are based on Samus and a Metroid.
The 225th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of Metroid, Metroid II: Return of Samus, and Super Metroid.

Mewgenics.description: The Mewgenics release date trailer features a crossover with MeatCanyon.
Mewgenics is a spin-off of The Binding of Isaac and is set in the same universe, as stated by Edmund McMillen (word of god.)

Mi-Pha-Pu.description: Nyarome and Kemunpas from Extraordinary Ataro appear as the hosts of Mi-Pha-Pu.

Michael Jackson's Moonwalker.description: GamePro enters the world of Michael Jackson's Moonwalker.
The sixty-third episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the Genesis game Michael Jackson's Moonwalker.

Mickey Mouse.description: Pegleg Pete from Oswald the Lucky Rabbit is one of the main characters in the Mickey Mouse series. Oswald himself is featured in Epic Mickey games, including its comic adaptations, in the Italian story Topolino e il surreale viaggio nel destino and makes cameos in the short Get a Horse! and in the Mickey Mouse 2013 tv series.
Julius the Cat from Alice Comedies appears as a villain in the first Italian Mickey Mouse stories, published on the newspaper "Il Popolo di Roma".
Madelon Claudet appears in the short Mickey Mouse Presents Parade of the Award Nominees.
Dr. Jekyll, transforming into Mr. Hyde, from the 1931 movie Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde appears in the short Mickey Mouse Presents Parade of the Award Nominees.
A Mickey Mouse doll appears in the Our Gang episodes For Pete's Sake and Night 'N' Gales.
Mickey Mouse makes an appearance in the movie "Hollywood Party".

The Goofy series is a spin-off of the Mickey Mouse series, Mickey also makes an appearance in the Donald and Goofy short The Fox Hunt and in A Goofy Movie. Goofy's nephew Gilbert then makes an appearace in a Mickey Mouse sunday page from May 30, 1954 and in some other stories, while Goofy's son Max from Goof Troop is featured in Mickey's Once Upon a Christmas and the House of Mouse series, The Mickey, Donald and Goofy cartoons in Mickey Mouse Works and the movie Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers can be considered crossovers between the two series, the Mickey Mouse episode "Good Sports" is based on the Goofy sports shorts.

The Donald Duck series can be considered a spin-off to the Mickey Mouse series, since it stars Donald in his modernized incarnation from the Mickey Mouse series, as well as featuring various Mickey Mouse characters in its early comic strips, there have been many other cameos and crossovers between the two series through the years.

Mickey Mouse.game: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (Disney)
Mickey Mouse.description: Snow White characters appear alongside Mickey Mouse characters in the promotional shorts The Standard Parade and All Together, in many comic stories, in the House of Mouse series, in Epic Mickey: Power of Illusion and in the Mickey Mouse episodes "Wish Upon a Coin" and "Sock Burglar"; the story Seven Dwarfs and Mickey Mouse: Diamond Mine Dilemma is a crossover between the two series; Mickey Mouse is also seen playing a Snow White fighting game in the short Runaway Brain, additionally Mizrabel from Castle of Illusion is likely based on the Queen from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.

Pinocchio and Geppetto appear alongside Mickey Mouse characters in the short "All Together", while Pinocchio characters appear in the comic stories "Clara Cluck", "L'inferno di Topolino", the strip arc "Li'l Davy", "Topolino allo Zecchino D'Oro", "Donald and Mickey in Disneyland", "Mickey's Toontown" and some other stories, in the Mickey Mouse Club opening, in On Vacation with Mickey Mouse and Friends, Mickey's Christmas Carol, the Mickey Mouse episode "Wonders of the Deep" in the House of Mouse series, in the Game Boy game Mickey Mouse II, in Epic Mickey: Power of Illusion; additionally Goofy appears dressed as Pinocchio in Mickey Mouse Holiday Special #4 while Mickey appears dressed as Pinocchio on the cover of Topolino #1948, an animatronic version of Stromboli from Pinocchio is also featured in Epic Mickey 2.

Dumbo makes an appearance in some Mickey Mouse comics, in the Mickey Mouse Club opening and in the House of Mouse series, while the train Casey Junior appears in Mickey's Racing Adventure and in the Mickey Mouse episode "Tokyo Go", Clara Cluck makes an appearance in the Dumbo story "Dumbo The Musician".
Mickey appears as a cameo in the manga The Lost World.

Little Pan from the Pastoral Symphony segment of Fantasia makes an appearance in the cover story to Mickey Mouse Weekly #521, while The Mushrooms from the Nutcracker Suite segment are enemies in the North American version of Mickey Mousecapade; various characters from Fantasia and Fantasia 2000 also appear in the House of Mouse series, while Chernabog appears in the Mickey Mouse episode "Touchdown and Out", additionally graffiti reading "Fantasia 2000" can be seen in the Mickey Mouse episode "No Reservation".

Characters from Bambi appear in the cover story to Mickey Mouse Weekly #521, in the promotional story "Man at Work", in the Mickey Mouse story Battle of Wits and Witches, in Duck the Halls: A Mickey Mouse Christmas Special and in the House of Mouse series, the Mickey Mouse episode "Swimmin' Hole" also features a reference to Bambi.

Gus and Jaq from Cinderella make an appearance in Mickey Mouse's comic strip arcs Mousepotamia and Land Beneath the Sea, while other Cinderella characters appear in the stories Fantasyland: Mickey and Goofy in The Captured Castle, Topolino allo Zecchino D'Oro, Topolino e il favoloso sogno, in the House of Mouse series, in the shorts Mickey's April Fools and Croissant de Triomphe, and in Epic Mickey: Power of Illusion.

Peter Pan Treasure Chest and Mickey Mouse in Fantasyland feature crossover stories between the two series, Peter Pan characters also appear in the Mickey Mouse stories 20,000 Weeds Under The Sea, Treasure Island A-Yo-Ho, Classy Castle Hassle, Topolino allo Zecchino D'Oro, O Sumiço Das Vozes Na Terra Do Nunca and Le capitaine Crochet est de retour !, as well as in Mickey Mousecapade, the Epic Mickey series and the House of Mouse series, additionally a Mary Blair drawing from the production of Peter Pan is shown on a book in the Mickey Mouse episode "Wonders of the Deep".

Peg Leg Pete makes an appearance in the Chip 'n' Dale short The Lone Chipmunks and Mickey Mouse characters appear in some Chip 'n' Dale comic stories as well as on the cover of Chip 'n' Dale #56, while Chip 'n' Dale appear in their "Rescue Rangers" outfits in the story Mickey's Toowntown and in the company logo at the beginning of Castle of Illusion Starring Mickey Mouse.

Characters from Alice in Wonderland appear in the Mickey Mouse stories Topolino e il doppio segreto di Macchia Nera, The Mystery Machine and Topolino e il grande colpo di Macchia Nera, the video games Mickey Mousecapade, Mickey Mouse, Mickey Mouse II, World of Illusion Starring Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck, Epic Mickey: Power of Illusion and in the House of Mouse series, with the Mad Hatter also appearing in the short Pit Crew.
Some Peanuts strips feature references to Mickey Mouse.

Characters from the Mickey Mouse series appear in the stories Uncle Scrooge goes to Disneyland, Showboat, A Fine Featherless Friend, Passing The Olympic Torch To Scrooge, Il segreto del totem decapitato, Grandma's Birthday Surprise, Zio Paperone e le carte Disney, Zio Paperone e la festa dei 2500 and Plastic bloem, while Uncle Scrooge appears in the Clara Cluck story The Windy Warpath and Magica De Spell appears in some Mickey Mouse stories and in Mickey's Racing Adventure and the family from Il Papero del Mistero also appears in Topokolossal; Mickey, Goofy and Pluto also appear on a comic in the Scrooge story "Nobody's Business", while a Mickey Mouse mask appears in Il Papero del Mistero and a puppet Mickey in The Dutchman's Secret.
Characters from Lady and the Tramp appear in a Mickey Mouse Sunday comic page from April 12, 1959, in the House of Mouse series and in the Mickey Mouse episode "Third Wheel".
Mickey Mouse is referenced on Beany and Cecil in various ways.
The comic 20,000 Weeds Under The Sea is a parody of the film.
In a Jon comic strip from October 7, 1976, Garfield watches the Mickey Mouse Club on TV. There's other references to Mickey Mouse throughout the comics.

The comic story Operação P.I. 1820 can be considered a crossover between the two series. A character dressed as Zorro, called Little Zorro is featured in some Mickey Mouse strips from 1958 and Zorro can also be seen on TV in a Mickey Mouse comic strip from April 24, 1958 and one from May 15, 1958.
Toys of Mickey and Minnie Mouse appear in An American Werewolf in London.
There were multiple format crossover games between Mickey Mouse and Game & Watch. Egg also featured elements from the Mickey Mouse Game & Watch game.
Egg is adapted from the Game & Watch Mickey Mouse and features the same setting.
Mickey, Donald and Goofy appear in the promotional comic page for The Fox and the Hound O Cão E A Raposa - Shopping Disney, while Tod and Copper make an appearance in the House of Mouse series.
Characters from The Sword in the Stone appear in the Mickey Mouse story Le miroir magique, in the game World of Illusion Starring Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck and in the House of Mouse series.
The Italian Mickey Mouse story Topolino in... E.B. l'extraterrestre is a parody of E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial; Topostorie Disney #39, is also titled "E.B. l’extra-terrestre".
Mickey Mouse was mentioned in Pet Sematary.
Many characters from Robin Hood make an appearance in Mickey's Christmas Carol and the House of Mouse series.
The Secretary Bird from Bedknobs and Broomsticks makes an appearance in Mickey's Christmas Carol and along with other characters in the House of Mouse series.
The Mickey Mouse Panorama screen Game & Watch and Donkey Kong Circus have the same gameplay and got their serial numbers swapped.
The Italian Mickey Mouse story Topolino & Pippo ghostbusters (cacciatori di fantasmi) is a parody of Ghostbusters.
Statues of Mickey and Donald appear in the Adventures of the Gummi Bears episode "The Sinister Sculptor".
The Italian comic Pluto e l'invasione dei replicanti is inspired by the first film.
Chief O'Hara and Red Wasp are recurring characters in the Club of Heroes series.
The Mickey Mouse Club is mentioned in Stand by Me.
In a Calvin and Hobbes comic strip on October 1, 1986, Hobbes dresses as Mickey Mouse.

Mojipittan.description: Moji-kun and Moji-chan make a cameo appearance in Klonoa Heroes: Densetsu no Star Medal, while Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Klonoa characters running in the background and a remix of a Klonoa theme in certain puzzles, and Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Encore adds a set of stages based on characters and items from Klonoa.

Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Taiko no Tatsujin characters running in the background and a remix of a Taito no Tatsujin theme in certain puzzles, and the characters return in later Mojipittan games; Taiko no Tatsujin 4 and later games in the series feature music tracks from Kotoba no Puzzle: Mojipittan.
Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Pac-Man characters running in the background and a remix of a Pac-Man theme in certain puzzles.

Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Mappy characters running in the background and a remix of the Mappy theme in certain puzzles, Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe features a puzzle based on Goro with Mappy serving as the assistant.

Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Mr. Driller characters running in the background and a remix of a Mr. Driller theme in certain puzzles, while Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Encore features a set of stages based on characters and items from Mr. Driller.
Xenosaga Freaks includes a parody of the game titled Kotoba no Puzzle: Xenopittan.

The remix theme Futari no Mojipittan is featured in the music CD THE iDOLM@STER Your Song and other later releases, the Vocal Lesson interface from THE IDOLM@STER Dearly Stars is based on Mojipittan and features Erabu-kun; while Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Encore features a set of stages based on THE iDOLM@STER characters.
Unou no Tatsukin: Soukai! Machigai Museum 2 features one puzzle based on Mojipittan.

Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of the Prince from Katamari Damacy with the King of All Cosmos assisting the player, while Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Encore features a set of stages based on characters and items from Katamari.
