In a scene in The Karate Kid characters are seen playing Pac-Man.
The sound of a video game being played at the comic book store in Santa Carla is Pac-Man.

Ghosts from Pac-Man appear as enemies in special stages in The Quest of Ki, and Pac-Man appears as a creature card in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga, while Pac-Man Monsters featured characters from Tower of Druaga during a timed promotion and two themes featuring characters from The Tower of Druaga and The Return of Ishtar appear in Pac-Man 99; Dig·Dra·Pac Janken ou is a crossover between the two series and The Tower of Druaga is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash.
Pac-Man is a selectable character in the Japanese version of Rock 'n Ball.
Pac-Man appears in the PC Engine/TurboGrafx-16 version of Ordyne when using the "Stock bomber shot" power up.
A scene in The Wizard features a Baby Pac-Man cabinet.

The X68000 version of Galaga '88 features a bonus level with the ghosts from Pac-Man, while the fighter from Galaxian is unlockable in Pac-Man Kart Rally and a theme with Galaga characters appears in Pac-Man 99; Pac-Man also appears in Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition and a Pac-Man-themed level appears in Galaga Wars; The flagship from Galaxian is a collectable item in various Pac-Man games; games from the Galaxian series are also included in Pac-Man Arcade Gold, Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man, Pac-Man Party, Pac-Man Connect and Play. Pac-Man's Pixel Bash and Pac-Man's anniversary arcade cabinets; Pac-Man & Galaga Dimensions is a collection of both Pac-Man and Galaga games.
Magicland Dizzy features a reference to Pac-Man.
Jill of the Jungle features enemies based on the Ghost Monsters from Pac-Man; the freeware version of the game also features a reference to Pac-Man himself.

Ace Combat features images of Pac-Man on billboards, while Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Pac-Man; Ace Combat 2, Ace Combat 5 and Ace Combat 6 also feature minor references.
Wolfenstein 3D features a secret level based on Pac-Man.

Pac-Man appears during a homerun in Super Batter Up, then appears alongside other Pac-Man characters in the audience of the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64, and as an actual player in Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Pac", while Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax feature a player based on Blinky (as "Akabe") in the Rivals team, and Ms. Pac-Man appears as the mascot of the Namco Stars team in Famista 64; Pac-Man also appears as the logo of the team in Super Famista and its sequels.
Pac-Man and Inky appear in the comic Kirby und das Geheimnis des Glibbers. Pacto is based on Pac-Man.

The power-up "Pac Power" in Tinkle Pit transform the players into Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man, and the enemies into scared ghosts. Ms. Pac-Man also appears in the hi-score screen and the enemy "Blinky Clones" is based on Blinky from Pac-Man.
Point Blank features images of characters from Pac-Man.
A billboard of a christmas-themed Pac-Man can be seen in the Intermediate Course in Alpine Racer.

Various games in the Pac-Man series are included in Namco Museum titles, and the player controls Pac-Man in the hub world. Additionally, characters from Pac-Man can be seen interacting with characters from other series on the boxart of Namco Museum Arcade Pac.
Namco Classic Collection Vol.2 includes Pac-Man.
A Pac-Man-themed minigame featuring tanks can be found as an Arcade and played in Contra: Legacy of War.
Blast Corps features a level based on Pac-Man.

Klonoa has an image of Pac-Man on his hat, and a picture of Pac-Man appears on Klonoa's house in strip #2 of Klonoa: Dream Traveler of Noctis Sol. Additionally, a hat based on Klonoa can be obtained in Pac-Man Mega Tunnel Battle Chomp Champs.
Pac-Man, Ms. Pac-Man, Super Pac-Man and Pac & Pal are featured in Namco History Vol.3.
Namco Anthology Vel.2 includes Pac-Attack.
A pizza banner found in the Food Court area of the Rickety Town level in CarnEvil resembles Pac-Man.

Pac-Man appears as a guest player in Anna Kournikova's Smash Court Tennis and Smash Court 3, Smash Court Tennis 3 features a Pac-Man themed court with Pac-Man and the ghosts moving around and artwork of Pac-Man appears in one of the courts in Smash Court and as part of an easter egg in the training mode of Smash Court 2.
Pacman is mentioned in the Crash Zone episode "Identity Crisis".

Pooka from Dig Dug makes a cameo in Pac-Man World, is a recurring enemy in Pac-Man World 2 and an unlockable character in  Ms. Pac-Man Maze Madness, in Pac-Man World Rally along with Fygar and as part of a theme with other Dig Dug characters in Pac-Man 99, while Taizou Hori is selectable in Pac-Man Kart Rally; Pac-Man appears in strip #9 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic; Dig·Dra·Pac Janken ou is a crossover between the two series.
The ghost Blinky from Pac-Man appears as an unlockable "car" in Ridge Racer 64, while Reiko Nagase is selectable in Pac-Man Fever
Pac-Man is one of the players in the "Namco All Stars '80" team in World Kicks, and the ghosts are part of the audience.

A costume of Pac-Man is featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with his actual techniques, the Tales of Arise artifacts "Glutton's Maze", "Glutton's Code" and "Glutton's Guidebook" feature references to Pac-Man; Pac-Man makes other minor cameos in the series.
Monica, Phoebe and Chandler play Ms. Pac-Man in the Friends episode: "The One Where Joey Dates Rachel".
Pac Man and Ms. Pac Man arcade machines appears in many episodes of Scrubs.
Pac-Man appears as one of the video game characters in Futurama's episode Anthology of Interest II.
In Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail advertising a Pac-Man game.
Pac-Man is a selectable character in Family Tennis Advance.

Heihachi Mishima and Tiger Jackson are selectable in Pac-Man Fever; Pac-Man is selectable in PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita versions of Street Fighter X Tekken, and to celebrate Pac-Man's 40th anniversary the Arena stage in Tekken 7 was briefly turned into "Pac-Man Arena" for its Season 4 release with a Pac-Man statue and series imagery around it.
Astaroth from SoulCalibur is selectable in Pac-Man Fever
Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan for PlayStation 2 features Pac-Man characters running in the background and a remix of a Pac-Man theme in certain puzzles.
Pac-Man is referenced as an ancient hero in several Magnus found in the Baten Kaitos series.
Pacman is referenced when the extremeasaur chases Bloo in a maze in the FHFIF episode "House Of Bloo's".
One of the games that the employee plays in Whack Your Boss is Pac-Man.
Pac-Man is mentioned in Are We There Yet?
The Simpsons episode "Homer and Ned's Hail Mary Pass" and some later episodes feature references to Pac-Man.
A song from Pac-Man is featured in Donkey Konga 3.

The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Pac 'n Roll and appears alongside the Rally-X racers during a timed promotion in Pac-Man Monsters, while Pac-Man is selectable in Rally-X Remix and a theme featuring Rally-X cars appears in Pac-Man 99; additionally a car from Rally-X appears as a collectable item in Pac & Pal; also New Rally-X is included in Pac-Man Arcade Gold and Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man while Rally-X is included in Pac-Man's Arcade Party, and Rally-X S is included in Pac-Man Games; Pac-Man Championship DX+ includes a map based on Rally-X, while Pac'N-Jump includes a Rally-X mode.
Pac-Man is mentioned in The Mighty Boosh.
Space Invaders × Pac-Man is a crossover between the two series.
Pac-Man and other characters from the series are selectable in the Mario Kart Arcade GP series, along with items and race tracks.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are some references to Pac-Man.
Pac-Man and the ghosts make appearances as guest AI drivers in Wangan Might Maximum Tune 2 and Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune 3 DX+. Pac-Man images appear in all the Wangan Midnight games by Namco.
QuickSpot and Machigai Museum 2 feature a puzzle based on Pac-Man.
The Prince from Katamari Damacy is an unlockable racer in Pac-Man World Rally and along with Ichigo in Pac-Man Kart Rally; Katamari Amore also features a Pac-Man-themed level.

Mappy is an unlockable racer in the PSP version of Pac-Man World Rally and a theme featuring Mappy characters appears in Pac-Man 99; while Pac-Man characters appear in Mappy Kids (as images), Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan, Hippari Mappy Daisakusen and Touch the Mappy with 80's Dot Stars; Mappy is included in Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man, Pac-Man's Arcade Party and Pac-Man's Pixel Bash alongside Hopping Mappy.
Mr. Driller is an unlockable racer in the PSP version of Pac-Man World Rally and in Pac-Man Kart Rally.
A graffiti drawing of Pacman is shown in the Torchwood episode "Everything Changes".
Bosconian is included in Pac-Man Arcade Gold, Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man, Pac-Man's Arcade Party, Pac-Man Connect and Play and Pac-Man's Pixel Bash.

At the end of The Gift of Gum, during the cleaning of the gum, Patrick eats some of the gum like Pac-Man. In The Cent of Money, when the scene shows the fish playing the arcade games, one of them has a character and game similar to Pac-Man. In the episode Krusty Kleaners, the scene where SpongeBob and Patrick are trying to find a way out of the maze references Pac-Man. In the episode Treats!, at the beginning of the Snail Bites commercial, there is an allusion to Pac-Man.
One possible map arrangement in New Space Order is based on the maze from Pac-Man.
The My Name Is Earl episode "Foreign Exchange Student" features a reference to Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man.
There is a bloon with an image of Pac-Man on it, that releases a character looking like Pac-Man when popped in Bloons and its expansions.
BioShock and its sequel feature references to Pac-Man.
Pole Position is included in Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man.

The theme "Labyrinth" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 01 is based on Pac-Man, Pac-Man based costume parts are featured as DLC for THE iDOLM@STER: Live for You!, while Pac-Man merchandise appear in episodes 17 and 19 of THE iDOLM@STER anime.
The Robot Chicken episode "Tubba-Bubba's Now Hubba-Hubba" and some later episodes feature sketches based on Pac-Man.
The iCarly episode "iStage an Intervention" features a game called "Pak-Rat", which is a parody of Pac-Man.
Some levels of Noby Noby Boy feature Pac-Man characters.
The arcade game is spoofed briefly in the Spliced episode "Honorary Freak".
The PlayStation 2 The Fast and The Furious video game by Namco features drifter charms of Pac-Man and all the ghosts.
Brian plays Pac-Man in the episode "Road to the Multiverse".

The Big Bang Theory episode "The Bozeman Reaction" features a reference to Ms. Pac-Man. Stuart wears a Pac-Man shirt in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Wheaton Occurence". In the episode "The Hot Troll Deviation", Howard wears a Pac-Man belt.
Pac-Man appears as a summon alongside the ghosts in Keroro RPG.
In the episode "Pinxillated" of the Pink Panther and Pals TV show, there's an arcade game similar to Pac-Man.
Pacmania is a parody of Pacman. Ms. Pac-Man is mentioned in Grapefruit's Revenge and characters play Pacman games in later episodes.
The movie Scott Pilgrim vs. The World features a reference to Pac-Man.
Sound effects from Pac-Man can be heard in "Dick Figures - Teabag Teaser".
Pac-Man appears on the cover of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32. Inky appears in several issues of the comic.
The American Dad! episodes "A Piñata Named Desire" and "School Lies" feature references to Pac-Man.
The Fairly OddParents episode "Balance of Flour" title card is a reference to Pac-Man. Ghosts from Pac-Man appear on a poster in "Poltergeeks".
In a logo panel, Garfield is in a box eating dots while chasing a ghost-like creature in the comic strip on April 24, 2011.
Pacman is featured in Hangover Part 2.
Ms. Pac Man is mentioned in Ready Player One, Wade later plays a perfect game of Pac Man. Pac-Man is mentioned in Ready Player Two.
Random Encounters has made a Pac-Man song.
In "Skyrim" you can find a cheese in the shape of Pac-Man chasing food similar to the pellets.
Greg and Rowley try to make their own Pac-Man Arcade Machine.
The North American and European versions of Everybody's Golf: World Invitational feature Pac-Man as a DLC golfer.
Pac-Man is selectable in PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita versions of Street Fighter X Tekken.
Pac-Man and Pac-Land are some of the games added to Namco Arcade.
A version of Gator Panic titled Gator Panic S is included in Pac-Man Games.
The Gravity Falls episode "Fight Fighters" features a fictional game based on Pac-Man. Pac-Mabel, a Pac-Man version of Mabel, appears in Gravity Falls: Lost Legends.
Wreck-It Ralph features characters from Pac-Man, while Pac-Man: Ralph Breaks the Maze includes several characters and themed mazes from Wreck-It Ralph.

Pac-Man and one of his ghost enemies make a cameo in strip #100 of the Bravoman web comic, strip #230 features the ghost Clyde in a cameo as well and costumes and video games related to Pac-Man also appear in other strips; while a theme featuring characters from Bravoman appears in Pac-Man 99.
Angry Birds Space features a level based on Pac-Man
Ms. Pac-Man is mentioned in the Zombieland: The Series pilot
Pac-Man is a secondary character in Namco High.

Pac-Man Monsters features Rick from Splatterhouse, and a theme featuring characters from Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti appears in Pac-Man 99; additionally Splatterhouse is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash.
Pac-Man is parodied in Les Kassos.
Hyperdevotion Noire: Goddess Black Heart features a character called Lady Wac, that is a parody of Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man.
An advertisement in Poptropica for Disney XD Animacation has some cardboard cutouts of some Pac-Man and the Ghostly Adventures characters.
The Roblox Disney XD Mystery Morphing Mask included Pac-Man.
Pac-Man Monsters featured Kagekiyo from Genpei Toma Den during a timed promotion, while a theme with characters from Genpei Toma Den appears in Pac-Man 99.

Pac-Man Monsters featured Clovis and the Buster Dragon from Dragon Buster during a timed promotion, while Dragon Buster is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash and a theme with Dragon Buster characters appears in Pac-Man 99.

Pac-Man Monsters featured Siria, 3-Headed Dragon and Zawell from the Dragon Spirit series during timed promotions; additionally Dragon Spirit is included in Pac-Man's Arcade Party and Pac-Man's Pixel Bash and a theme featuring Dragon Spirit characters appears in Pac-Man 99.
Beardo from Total Drama makes the Pac-Man gameover sound when he was eliminated.
Pac-Man appears as a playable character in Super Smash Bros for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U, with a different stage in each game.
The minigame "Mrs. Spook" from Spooky's Jump Scare Mansion is inspired by Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man.
Ms. Pac-Man is mentioned in the Modern Family episodes: "Queer Eyes, Full Hearts" and "Integrity".
Pac-Man and Blinky appear in One Night at Flumpty's 2.
There's a Pac-Man reference in the episode Video Game References.
A cartridge titled “Pac-Laudy 2” is shown in Episode 41 of Stardust Crusaders, which is a parody of Pac-Man.
Pac-Man appears as one of the videogame characters in the movie, Pixels.
Crossy Road features Pac-Man, Inky, Blinky, Pinky and Clyde as unlockable characters after an update.
Board James reviews the board games Pac-Man Game and Pac Man Magnetic Maze in the episode "Video Games!!"
Dino Run DX features a hat based on Pac-Man.
Outcast Odyssey featured cards based on Pac-Man characters during a limited promotion.

Pac-Man is selectable in Project Fardraut: Secondary Work of Xevious; additionally Xevious is included in Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man, Pac-Man's Arcade Party, Pac-Man Connect and Play and Pac-Man's Pixel Bash; and a theme featuring Xevious characters appears in Pac-Man 99.
Quicksilver was playing Ms. Pac-Man in X-Men: Apocalypse.
There is a title achievement called "Pac-mouse". Short and long plank skins of Pac-Man appear in the shop.
Pac-Man is mentioned in the Black Mirror episode: "Playtest".
In one mission "Haum Sweet Haum", four robots can be found named after the Pacman ghosts in Watch Dogs 2.
Pac-Man appears as a virus in the movie,  Kamen Rider Heisei Generations: Dr. Pac-Man vs. Ex-Aid & Ghost with Legend Riders .
Pac-Man costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 3.
A cat version of Pac-Man appeared in Cat Busters during the Namco Catalog IP collaboration event, while Pac-Man himself appeared as a boss and a "ghost" mouse appeared as a minor enemy.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 features references to Pac-Man. Star Lord has a Pac-Man cake in Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy.
Pac-Man appears in the Off the Mark comic strip "OverPac-Man".

The Hello Kitty ♥ Pac-Man line is a crossover between the two series and includes a Pac-Man ghost Hello Kitty; as part of the promotion the smartphone version of Pac-Man featured Hello Kitty-themed levels and items for a limited period.
Pac-Man appeared in The Knights of Avalon during the first Namco collaboration event.
There's a segment in Golf Story that plays identically to classic Pac-Man.

Pac-Man appears as a challenger in Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don!; Music from Pac-Man is featured in the Namcot Medley debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10; Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumete - Tomodachi Daisakusen! also features a costume and theme based on Pac-Man, while Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version!and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Pac-Man series.

Characters from the Pac-Man series appear in Sonic Dash and Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds, while Sonic appears in the iOS and Android Pac-Man during a special collaboration. Pac-Man World 2 Re-Pac also includes a Sonic the Hedgehog themed DLC.
Pacman is referenced in Chuchel.
The main theme of Pac-Man is part of the "Namcot Medley" BGM featured in Groove Coaster 4: Starlight Road.
Pac-Man characters appear in Pixel Runner!
Pac-Man has been a subject for DBX.
Motos is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash.
The Pac-Man world appears as a location in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers and various sprites from Pac-Man appear as treasures.
Just Dance Now, Just Dance 2019, Just Dance Unlimited, and Just Dance+ feature the song "Pac-Man" with dancers dressed as Pac-Man characters.
Head gear based on Pac-Man is part of a free Namco DLC for Sword Art Online: Fatal Bullet.
One Piece Pac-Man Stampede Ver. is a crossover between the two series.
Ms. Pac-Man is mentioned in Into the Pit.
Pac-Man Tamagotchi is a crossover between the two series.
A Pac-Man DLC was added to Minecraft to celebrate the 40th Anniversary of Pac-Man.
Pac-Man is referenced in the Gorillaz song "PAC-MAN", and 2D is seen playing Pac-Man in the music video.
"Something About Pac-Man" is a parody of Pac-Man.
Monopoly Arcade: Pac-Man is a format crossover between the two series.
Posters of Pac-Man can be seen in Sky Kid, Sky Kid and Sky Kid Deluxe are included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash and a theme featuring Sky Kid characters appears in Pac-Man 99.

A banner ad featuring Pac-Man appears in the Japan League stadiums from Kyukai Dochuki, and images of Pac-Man with a purple tie appear in after-match results; while a theme featuring characters from Yōkai Dōchūki appears in Pac-Man 99.
A theme featuring characters from Valkyrie no Densetsu appears in Pac-Man 99.
Metro-Cross is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash, while a theme featuring characters from Metro-Cross appears in Pac-Man 99.
Rolling Thunder is included in Pac-Man's Arcade Party and Pac-Man's Pixel Bash, while a theme featuring Rolling Thunder characters appears in Pac-Man 99.

A Pac-Man themed baby carriage appears in strip #38 of the Wonder Momo web comic, a Pac-Man poster appears in episode 2 of the anime, while a theme featuring Wonder Momo characters appears in Pac-Man 99.

The "Baganns" enemy in Baraduke resembles Pac-Man, and the layout of Floor 39 resembles the maze from Pac-Man, while Baraduke is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash and a theme with characters from Baraduke appears in Pac-Man 99.
A theme featuring characters from Toy Pop appears in Pac-Man 99.
The 195th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Pac-Man 2: The New Adventures for the Sega Genesis.
A lamp that looks like Blinky can be found in Free Guy'.

Round 21 in Tank Force is shaped after Pac-Man. Pac-Man, Blinky and Inky also appear hidden inside the steel walls in Round 29. The second world in Pac-Man Arrangement Plus+ is based on Battle City, and a theme featuring characters from Tank Battalion appears in Pac-Man 99.

A theme featuring characters from Tower of Babel appears in Pac-Man 99; additionally one of the eight symbols from Tower of Babel is an image of Pac-Man, while Floor 32 in the arranged version of the game features moving pixel art of Pac-Man in the background.
Pacman is mentioned in Ron's Gone Wrong.
Bero Bero enemy from Pac-Pix is possibly a reference to Berobero from Warp & Warp. A theme featuring characters from Warp & Warp appears in Pac-Man 99.
A theme featuring characters from Wagan Land appears in Pac-Man 99.
Pac-Man can be seen in Animation vs. Arcade Games.
Super Robot Wars DD features Pac-Man as a unit.

Pac-Man.game: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
Pac-Man.description: Characters from Pac-Man and original event stories are featured in That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime: ISEKAI Memories as part of a special collaboration event.
A Pac-Man themed emote and back bling appear in Fortnite.
Pac-Man makes an appearance in 404 GAME RE:SET.
One of the levels of Suicide Guy: The Lost Dreams is a reference to Pac-Man.
Skins based on Pac-Man appear in Fall Guys.
There is a level in SPY x ANYA: Operation Memories based on Pac-Man.
Pac-Man memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Skins and maps from Pac-Man appear in Stumble Guys as part of a special collaboration.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Pac-Man.
Pac-Man can be seen on a tv screen in the music video for FNAF Kids.
The Secret Level episode: "PAC-MAN: Circle" is based off of Shadow Labyrinth.
Plushies of Pac-Man and Blinky appear in Class of '09: The Anime Pilot.
Pac-Man appears as a playable character in Super Monkey Ball: Banana Rumble as DLC.

Pacific Rim.description: There is a category system called 'Serizawa Scale' referencing Doctor Serizawa from Godzilla in Pacific Rim and Muto is listed in the PPDC database in Pacific Rim Uprising.
The AI voice in Pacific Rim is based on GLaDOS' voice.
Pacific Rim is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Snarfer Image".
Pacific Rim is mentioned in Armada.
Pitch Meeting had an episode on Pacific Rim.
Clover is listed in the PPDC database in Pacific Rim Uprising.
Several Gamera monsters are listed in the PPDC database in Pacific Rim Uprising.
Horizon's Legendary Atom Heart Mother skin from the Saviors "Awakening Collection Event" is based on Gypsy Danger from Pacific Rim.
Characters from Pacific Rim appeared in Top War as part of a special collaboration.
A pinball table based on Pacific Rim was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX that features characters from the series.
Characters from Pacific Rim appear in a special collab with State of Survival.
Characters from Pacific Rim appeared in Lords Mobile as part of a special collaboration.

Paddington.description: Somebody in a Paddington costume appears in Jingle All the Way.
A Paddington plush toy can be seen in the toy store.
Paddington appears in Children's Party at the Palace.
Paddington is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Fancyman: Part 2".
The head of Paddington appears in the Deep Space 69 episode “Pride and Predator Juice”.

There is a scene in Paddington where it is implied that Mr Curry (played by Peter Capaldi) stole flowers from a roadside memorial. This mirrors a scene in The Thick of It where his character does a similar thing, claiming that "it's one of the many advantages of living near an accident blackspot".
Paddington appeared in the 2014 version of Cut the Rope: Holiday Gift.
Paddington is mentioned in The Big Bang Theory episode "The Maternal Conclusion".
There is a bear dressed like Paddington in the Solar Opposites episode “The Booster Manifold”.  Also, Yumyulack mentions Paddington 2 in the Solar Opposites episode “The Lake House Device”.

Paddington.game: The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent
Paddington.description: Paddington 2 is mentioned in The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent.
Paddington is mentioned in Knock at the Cabin.
Paddington 2 is mentioned in the MeatCanyon episode "SNEAKO MEETS CHARLIE".
Paddington is mentioned in the Ted episode "Just Say Yes".

Pain.description: The Buzz! Host appears in the game Pain.
Daxter is a downloadable character in the game Pain.
Pain includes a costume for George Takei based on Sulu from Star Trek.
Elvira is a downloadable character in the game Pain.
Fat Princess is a downloadable character in the game Pain.
A bot that references Pain appears in Astro's Playroom as well as the Pain logo.

Painkiller Jane.description: Painkiller Jane and The Darkness had a comic book crossover together.
Painkiller Jane appears in Vampirella Crossover Gallery.
There was a crossover comic between Painkiller Jane and Hellboy.
The Punisher has a crossover with Painkiller Jane.

Pair of Kings.description: An advertisement for Pair of Kings is in Poptropica, which allows the player to meet some of the characters.
The Pair of Kings episode: "Where the Wild Kings Are"'s title is a reference to Where the Wild Things Are.
Dale Davis from Zeke and Luther appears in the Pair of Kings episode "An Ice Girl for Boomer".

PakPak Monster.description: PakPak Monster is a clone of Pac-Man.
Arino plays the Cassette Vision game PakPak Monster during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.

Paladins.description: To celebrate open beta on Steam, a skin was made available based on the Engineer as well as voice lines for it.
Skins have been dropped multiple times in Paladins based on characters from Smite.
Amelia Watson was added as a match announcer in Paladins.
Rambo appears as a skin in Paladins.
RWBY characters appeared in Paladins for a collaboration event.

Palworld.description: Palworld features many references to Pokémon.

Near the Sea Breeze Archipelago Castaway Beach fast travel point, you can encounter a "Mercenary With a Wounded Knee" sitting by a campfire. She references the "arrow in the knee" line from Skyrim: "I used to be a tough trainer like you... Then I took an attack to the knee from that giant Pal."
Palworld is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "Perfect Cell Vs Palworld".
Items and creatures from Terraria were added to Palworld after an update.
Pals from Palworld appear in Once Human as part of a collaboration event.
V1 and V2 from ULTRAKILL were added to Palworld after an update.

Pan's Labyrinth.description: Fairies from Pan's Labyrinth appear in the Troll Market in Hellboy II: The Golden Army.
Pale Man appears in the Robot Chicken episode "Schindler's Bucket List".
The protagonist of Unpacking is seen owning a copy of Pan's Labyrinth.

Pandemonium.description: Nikki from Pandemonium appears in the ending cutscene of Gex 2.
Nikki from Pandemonium appears as an opponent in Lara Croft's Poker Party.

Panel de Pon.description: Yoshi no Panepon is a crossover between the two series.
The Western release of Yoshi no Panepon uses the name "Tetris Attack".
Pokémon Puzzle Challenge and Pokémon Puzzle League are crossovers between the two series.
Lip's Stick from Panel de Pon is a usable item in Super Smash Bros. Melee and its sequels; Lip also appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, where her Mii costume is also available.
Nintendo Puzzle Collection includes a remake of Panel de Pon.
Dr. Mario & Panel de Pon is a bundle including games from both series.
Lip from Panel de Pon makes an appearance in Captain Rainbow.
In Poker Night at the Inventory, Tycho talks about Tetris Attack.
Animal Crossing: New Leaf includes the minigame Animal Forest Panepon/Animal Crossing Puzzle League as well as Lip's clothes and wand, added with the Welcome amiibo update.

PangYa.description: Kasumi's costume from Dead or Alive is an unlockable outfit in Super Swing Golf and Super Swing Golf: Season 2; Ayane's costume is unlockable in Season 2.
A costume based on Miku Hinasaki from Fatal Frame is an unlockable outfit in Super Swing Golf.
Konata from Lucky Star owns a statue of Kooh from PangYa.
Ryu Hayabusa's costume is an unlockable outfit in Super Swing Golf: Season 2.
A costume based on Pixie from Monster Rancher appears in Super Swing Golf: Season 2.
A costume based on Tecmo Bowl appears in Super Swing Golf: Season 2.
A costume based on Mighty Bomb Jack appears in Super Swing Golf: Season 2.
A costume based on Dana from Solomon's Key appears in Super Swing Golf: Season 2.
A costume based on Rygar appears in Super Swing Golf: Season 2.

Panic in Nakayoshi World.description: Sailor Moon and Chibi Moon are playable characters in Panic in Nakayoshi World

Panty & Stocking with Garterbelt.description: A stamp of Katz appears in the Panty & Stocking episode "The Diet Syndrome".
Transformers is parodied in the Panty And Stocking episode "Trans-homers".
There's a minor reference to Resident Evil in the 8th episode of Panty & Stocking with Garterbelt.
The designs of Wife and Husband Petter resemble Ren and Stimpy.
The title of "Chuck To The Future" is a reference to Back To The Future.
In "HELP! We are Angels", Chuck is dressed as Kenny.
"Chuck To The Future Part 4" is a homage to Mario.
Blossom and Bubbles are mentioned in the English version of "Sex and the Daten City".
The female Succubus from Scribblenauts Unlimited resembles Kneesocks Daemon.

Panzer Dragoon.description: The Solo Wing from Panzer Dragoon Zwei appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Orta and her dragon from Panzer Dragoon makes a cameo appearance in OutRun 2 SP.
Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed features a track based on Panzer Dragoon.

Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed features a track based on Panzer Dragoon; the world of Panzer Dragoon is visited in Sonic and Megaman: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Kell Fluge and a Blue Dragon.
The world of Panzer Dragoon is visited in Sonic and Megaman: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Kell Fluge and a Blue Dragon.
A dragon from Panzer Dragoon appears in Earth UFO Catcher.

Papa Louie.description: As of Papa's Cupcakeria, Tohru can be seen wearing a costume based on Mario on Halloween.

Papa Pear Saga.description: In the Candy Crush Saga level "Meringue Moor", there is a pear that hangs over a pot as a reference to Papa Pear Saga.

Paper Plane.description: Paper Plane was originally a videogame within the Wario series, and it features characters from the game.

Paperboy.description: The Captain N: The Game Master episode "The Invasion Of The Paper Pedalers" features elements from Paperboy.
Paperboy is featured in Arcade's Greatest Hits: The Atari Collection 2 and Midway's Greatest Arcade Hits
Paperboy is included in Midway Arcade Treasures and Midway Arcade Treasures: Extended Play.
Paperboy makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
Random Encounters has made a Paperboy song.
Paper Boy appears as one of the videogame characters in the movie, Pixels.
Elements of Paperboy are featured in the Midway Arcade level pack for Lego Dimensions.
The 140th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of the NES version of Paperboy.
The comic Spy Hunter & Paper Boy is a crossover between the two series.
Characters in 8-Bit Christmas can be seen playing Paperboy.

Paperman (Disney).description: The piece of paper with the lipstick mark from Paperman can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.

Papers, Please.description: In The Stanley Parable, papers from Papers, Please can be found in the colored doors room.
A stamp similar to the one from Papers, Please appears in The Talos Principle.
There is a Passport for Arstotzka in Please, Don't Touch Anything.
EZIC's symbol from Papers, Please can be found in Fallout 4.
Nate and Sully can be heard talking about Arstotzka in chapter 11 of Uncharted 4.
Random Encounters has made a Papers Please song.
Travis can wear a Papers, Please t-shirt in Travis Strikes Again: No More Heroes.
An ad of "Please, Paper" pops up in There Is No Game: Wrong Dimension, a parody of Papers, Please.

ParaNorman.description: In ParaNorman, Norman's ringtone is the theme music from Halloween.
ParaNorman is mentioned in the 30 Rock episode "The Beginning of the End".
The Story Book from ParaNorman appears in Missing Link.

Paradigm (Jacob Janerka).description: One of the dialogue options with John 3000 in Paradigm is "Hey dude, do your HAL 9000 impression."
The phrase "These are not the droids you are looking for" from Star Wars is spoken in Paradigm.
The war pipe is a reference to the warp pipes from the Mario series in Paradigm.
The glam nun has a tattoo of Max the rabbit in Paradigm.
When the glam metal pug leader gets defeated the fanfare from Final Fantasy plays in Paradigm.

Paradigm: Reboot.description: Characters and music from Dynamix can be found in Paradigm: Reboot as part of a special collaboration.
Characters and music from WACCA can be found in Paradigm: Reboot as part of a special collaboration.
Characters and music from Phigros can be found in Paradigm: Reboot while music from Paradigm: Reboot can be found in Phigros all as part of a special collaboration.
Characters and music from Lanota can be found in Paradigm: Reboot while music from Paradigm: Reboot can be found in Lanota all as part of a special collaboration.
Characters and music from Paradigm: Reboot can be found in Rotaeno as part of a collaboration event  and vice versa.
Music from Paradigm: Reboot appears in Cytus II as part of a collaboration.

Paradise PD.description: In "Welcome to Paradise", Kevin had a plush doll of Kermit the Frog.
In "Welcome to Paradise" a poster for the movie Titanic is seen on the wall of a VHS store.
A poster for the movie Jaws is also visible.
A poster for a Superman movie is visible in one episode, and in the episode "PARAD-ISIS" characters watch Superman 2.
A VHS tape of Mean Girls is also seen on a shelf in the store.
There's also a VHS of Child's Play.
Randall tells Kevin not to expect any "Mickey Mouse Shit", when dealing with hardened criminals. Mickey Mouse is also mentioned in the episode ""The Father, The Son, and the Holy Post-It Note".
In "Black & Blue", Robby and Delbert tell a Russian black marketer that he sounds like Count Von Count from Sesame Street.
Fitz watched Rocky & Bullwinkle cartoons as a kid.
Kevin plays Dungeons & Dragons with his friends in several episodes.
In "Dungeons & Dragnet", Fitz arrests the four main kids of Stranger Things. In another episode, Demigorgons from Stranger Things are mentioned.
Brooklyn Nine-Nine is referenced in several episodes of Paradise PD.
In "Tucker Carlson is a Huge Dick", Scrooge McDuck was a member of Bullet's cartoon animal police force.
Heathcliff was a member of Bullet's cartoon animal police force.
Droopy Dog was a member of Bullet's cartoon animal police force.
Porky Pig was a member of Bullet's cartoon animal police force.
Woody Woodpecker was a member of Bullet's cartoon animal police force.
The Disney vault is blown open, releasing all of the racist characters from their old movies and shows, including Sunflower from Fantasia.
Another racist character is Shun-Gun from The Aristocats.
Great Big Little Panther from Peter Pan also comes out.
The Jim Crows from Dumbo also fly out.
Donald Duck comes out of the Disney vault in a Nazi uniform.
Uncle Remus comes out last, talking jive with Mr. Bluebird.
Although he doesn't appear on screen, Bullet says he just got back from doing blow with Scrappy Doo, implying the latter to be a real person in the Paradise PD universe.
Agent Dunfore drives the Eagle 5.
One of the prizes in MethDonald's tweaky meals are action figures of Pinky Pie, which Dusty wanted really bad.
Brickleberry and Paradise PD do a full-length crossover episode in "Paradise PD Meets Brickleberry". Additionally, Brickleberry is mentioned in several episodes of Paradise PD.
Malloy says that their series finale was even worse than the finale for The Sopranos.
Bobby gets so high he thinks he's Vegeta from Dragon Ball Z.
Denzel gets high with Snoopy and Woodstock.
Dusty and Connie both have The Golden Girls as their favorite show and sing the theme song. Dusty later makes sculptures of all the character out of his own feces.
Denzel gets to ask an omnipotent god one question and chooses to ask if he's ever seen The Dark Crystal before.
Bullet and Denzel talk about the Thanksgiving special of Friends.
Karen wishes they had crossover over with Big Mouth in the previous episode instead of Brickleberry.
Karen calls Brickleberry a knockoff of Family Guy.
Karen says that she wrote the highly disappointing Game of Thrones finale.
Kevin talks about how My Hero Academia is one of the better animes of the new Japanese renaissance.
Dusty says that Season 2 of Westworld is only slightly better than watching two flies fuck on a fresh turd.
Kevin believes that Alan Moore's The Watchmen is a deconstructionist parable about the superhero paradigm.
Hopson gets a job working as an actor on The Boss Baby: Back in Business, which is portrayed as a live-action show in this universe.
Hopson gets a job working as an actor on Rick & Morty, which is also portrayed as a live-action show.
Hopson gets a job working as an actor on DuckTales, which, one again, is also portrayed as a live-action show.
In "Blind Drunk", Dusty and Hopson did a Dukes of Hazzard parody, with Dusty being Boss Hogg and Hopson being Enos. Bullet also steals the actual General Lee from a museum.

Paradroid.description: Robot model 883 in Paradroid looks like a Dalekfrom Doctor Who.

Parahumans.description: In the chapter Agitation 3.4, Taylor talks about being able to watch an Earth Aleph's version of Star Wars episodes one and two.

In the chapter Shell 4.5, the schtick of Leet and Über is described as an ever-changing video game theme, one of the examples given being "Leet in a Mario costume throwing fireballs while Über was dressed up as Bowser, the two of them breaking into a mint to collect ‘coins’.".

In the chapter Shell 4.5, the schtick of Leet and Über is described as an ever-changing video game theme, one of the examples given being that "they would have a Grand Theft Auto theme, and they would be driving through the city in a souped up car, ripping off the ABB and beating up hookers.".

The chapter Plague 12.3 ends with Jack Slash stating "This is not an exit", the last words of the novel American Psycho. The following chapter begins with Tattletale giving him kudos for the reference.

In the chapter Monarch 16.6, Taylor tries to shut down the mech Azazel using the paradox "This statement is false", to which it replies "I’ll go with true. There, that was easy", referencing Wheatley's response to the same paradox. Taylor thinks that perhaps the designer "had a liking for popular culture I wasn’t aware of".

In the chapter Imago 21.7, a brainstorming board is seen with some people's names and trigger events listed. The first name read is 'Jadeite', whose trigger event is listed as "post-brainwashing dissonance".

In the chapter Sting 26.6, Taylor thinks to herself "Out of the frying pan and into the fire". This chapter also has protagonists fighting Nilbog's 'goblins', reminiscent of the protagonists of The Hobbit having fought off goblins just before Chapter 6, 'Out of the Frying-Pan into the Fire'. Later in Ward's chapter Glare Interlude 3, Ratcatcher declares "You thall not path" when encountering Dot.

In the chapter Teneral e.2, Imp continues to use fish related puns when mocking Nero, soon after which he is blatantly corrected "Nero, not Nemo". He is later annoyed that emperor Nero is also not the name of a famous fish.
In the chapter Teneral e.5, Ingenue appends the title Beauty and The Beast to her brief summary of Stockholm syndrome, adding “I always did like the princess movies.”.

The skill Pressure Points in Slay the Spire was originally named Path to Victory, and The Woman in Blue is actually the Worm character Contessa, a parahuman in the business of selling vials of powers, whose own power is called Path to Victory. Additionally, a story described similarly to Worm can be encountered in the library about an insect-controlling teenage girl who aspires to be a hero.

Parasite Eve.description: Aya Brea from Parasite Eve appears as a playable character in Chocobo Racing.

Aya Brea from Parasite Eve appears in Final Fantasy: Brave Exvius as part of a collaboration event. Additionally, in Parasite Eve there's a poster of characters from Final Fantasy VII and a poster of a Chocobo; Aya Brea's Costume from The 3rd Birthday is downloadable in Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy; there also are minor references to Final Fantasy VII in Parasite Eve II and to Parasite Eve in Final Fantasy IX.

Parenthood (NBC).description: Pretty Woman is mentioned in the Parenthood episode "What's Goin On Down There?".
Assets based on Parenthood could be obtained in Universal Movie Tycoon.
An episode of Adventure Time can be seen playing in the Parenthood episode "All Aboard Who's Coming Aboard".

Parker Lewis Can't Lose.description: Bud Bundy from Married... with Children appears in the Parker Lewis Can't Lose episode "Musso & Frank".
Eddie Haskell appears in the Parker Lewis Can't Lose episode Father Knows Less.
Andrew Keaton from Family Ties appears in the Parker Lewis Can't Lose episode "Civil Wars".
Elvira makes an appearance in the Parker Lewis Can't Lose episode "Boy Meets Girl II".

Parks and Recreation.description: District 9 is mentioned in the Parks and Recreation episode: "The Set Up".
Love Actually is mentioned in the Parks And Recreation episode "Fancy Party".
Jane Crocker has a poster of Ron Swanson from Parks and Recreation in Homestuck.
Pretty Woman is mentioned in the Parks And Recreation episode "Road Trip".
Unbreakable is mentioned in the Parks And Recreation episode "Sex Education".
The gorilla statue from the Parks and Recreation episode, Swing Vote, is the same gorilla statue from the 30 Rock episode, Jack-Tor.
Mister Bean is mentioned in the Parks and Recreation episode "Filibuster".
Characters discuss the game Dig Dug in the season 7 episode "Donna and Joe" of Parks and Recreation.
A printer made by the fictional company "Sabre" from The Office appears in the Parks and Recreation episode "Meet 'N' Greet".

Jean-Ralphio's champagne brand from Parks and Recreation was shown in a magazine on The Good Place and later in the episode of The Good Place, Chapter 11: What's My Motivation, Jason hides in a safe from Swanson Safe Company owned by Parks and Rec character, Ron Swanson, which was proven in Good Place the Podcast where a fake ad by Ron Swanson has to warn people not to hide in a safe.
Characters from Parks and Recreation appear in Funko Pop! Blitz.
April Ludgate and Leslie Knope from Parks and Recreation appeared on an episode of Weekend Update.
Monopoly: Parks and Recreation is a format crossover between the two series.

Parodius.description: Parodius is a spin-off of Gradius.
Goemon and other series' characters appear as playable characters in several games of the Parodius series.
Characters from Antarctic Adventure are prominently featured in the Parodius series, while the character of Pentarou is the son of Penta and Penko.
Popolon from Knightmare appears as a playable character in Parodius.
The TwinBee ship and characters from the series are playable in several entries of the Parodius series.
The Octopus gameplay configuration in Parodius Da! is based on Salamander.
Mambo and Sambo from Gokujo Parodius and Sexy Parodius are inspired by Space Manbow.
Michael's gameplay configuration in Gokujo Parodius is inspired by Darius.

Takosuke from Parodius appears in Wai Wai Bingo and Wai Wai Pocker, Hanako from Gokujo Parodius replaces Penta in his functions on the mobile port of Konami Wai Wai World, and Konami Lady makes a minor cameo in Parodius Da! for the SNES.
Mahamba from Martial Champion makes a cameo appearance in Stage 1 of Gokujō Parodius!
Kid Dracula is a playable character in the SNES port of Gokujou Parodius and the PlayStation/Saturn port of Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius.
Upa is a playable character in the SNES port of Gokujou Parodius and Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius.
Aitsu from Parodius is a secret playable character in Neo Kobe 2045 Speed King.
The stage "School" in Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius is based on Tokimeki Memorial, while Parodius characters Koitsu and Doitsu appear on a book in Tokimeki Memorial: Forever with You.
The stage "Sweet Land" in Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius is based on stage 2 of Xexex.
A Koitsu Mask based on the Parodius character can be found at the Joy Division store in the PlayStation/Saturn port of Snatcher, while Hikaru appears on a television ad in Alton Plaza.
Sexy Parodius features a stage based off Castlevania, while Aitsu and Koitsu from Parodius make a cameo appearance in Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin and Harmony of Despair.
Sexy Parodius features a stage based off Yie Ar Kung-Fu, including a cameo of its protagonist, Oolong.
Aitsu and Koitsu from Parodius appear as wrestlers in Jikkyō Power Pro Wrestling '96: Max Voltage under the names Mr. Gel and Dr. Mist.
Parodius Da! is included in Konami GB Collection Vol. 4.
Stickers of Takosuke and Koitsu from Parodius can be seen in printstations from Mitsumete Knight R.
Konami Krazy Racers features Takosuke from Parodius as a selectable racer.
Aitsu, Koitsu, Doitsu and Soitsu from Parodius appear as Yu-Gi-Oh cards.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Parodius.
Eliza from Parodius appears as an antagonist in Otomedius.
Tako/Octopus from Parodius appears as an elebit in Elebits: The Adventures of Kai and Zero.
A DLC bomberman "Octopus Bomber" (available by preordering the official soundtrack) is based off a character from Parodius.
"Parodius" is one themed category of puzzles featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.
The "Fantastic Shooting Gacha" limited event from Bombergirl features the outfits of Akane & Hikaru from Parodius as unlockable Dress Up Parts and a BGM from Fantastic Parodius.

Part Time UFO.description: Part Time UFO includes a level with dolls of Kirby characters.
Qbby makes appearances in various levels in Part Time UFO. Additionally, Part Time UFO features a costume based on Qbby. Accessories based on Part Time UFO can be obtained in BoxBoy! + BoxGirl!.
Part Time UFO includes a costume based on Goku from Yuyuki.

Party Animals.description: Skins referencing Star Wars can be found in Party Animals.
A skin referencing Harry Potter can be found in Party Animals.
A skin based on Gordon Freeman appears in Party Animals.
Naru and Ori appear in Party Animals as part of a special collaboration.
The Lamb from Cult of the Lamb appears in Party Animals as part of a special collaboration.
Om Nom from Cut the Rope appears in Party Animals as part of a special collaboration.
Skins based on Bill Rizer and Lance Bean from Contra appear in Party Animals as part of a special collaboration.

Party Land.description: Mappy characters and one location appear in Party Land.
The Tower of Druaga characters and one location appear in Party Land.
Dig Dug II characters and one location appear in Party Land.
Valkyrie no Densetsu characters and one location appear in Party Land.
Sky Kid characters and one location appear in Party Land.

Passions.description: Dr. Bombay from Bewitched appears in two episodes of Passions.
Passions is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One with Joey's Award".
Passions is mentioned in the Joey episode: "Joey and the Wrong Name".
Two episodes of Passions take place in the Montecito Resort and Casino from Las Vegas, and Mary Connell from Las Vegas appears in both episodes.

Patapon.description: Patapon costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet.
A monkey dressed as a Hatapon appears in PlayStation Move Ape Escape.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features a secondary representation based on Patapon.
Several "Patapon 3" summons were available during a special collaboration.
Cave art of bots reenacting Patapon appears Astro's Playroom. Costumes based on a Warrior, Archer and Flagbearer from Patapon can be found in Astro Bot.

Path to Nowhere.description: Langley from Path to Nowhere is added to Call of Duty: Mobile as an operator skin for Rin Yoshida. Along with other Path to Nowhere cosmetics.
Jolyne Cujoh, Foo Fighters and Weather Report from JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure: Stone Ocean are added to Path to Nowhere.

Pathfinder (Paizo Inc.).description: Munchkin Pathfinder is a crossover between both series.
Red Sonja appears in a Pathfinder: Worldscape one-shot.
Vampirella appears in a Pathfinder: Worldscape one-shot.

Patlabor.description: The Super Robot Wars series features units from the Patlabor series.
Patlabor characters appear in the game City Shrouded in Shadow.
ZOIDS × PATLABOR Code Name BUDDY is a crossover between the two series.

Paul (Universal).description: Graeme Willy wears a Flash t-shirt in Paul.
Clive Gollings wears a Creature From The Black Lagoon t-shirt in Paul.
Paul includes several references to Star Wars.
Graeme Willy wears an Invincible t-shirt in Paul.
Dirty Harry is mentioned in Paul.
Paul does a Predator impersonation in Paul.
The titular character says the 'draw me like one of your French girls' line in Paul.
Agent Mulder is mentioned in Paul.
Peter Parker is mentioned in Paul.
Mac and Me is mentioned in Paul.
Clive Gollings and Graeme Willy get nicknamed Rocky and Bullwinkle in Paul.
Wonder Woman is mentioned in Paul.
Star Trek is shown on TV in Paul.
The titular character gets nicknamed as "Short Round" in Paul.
Paul is shown on OnDemand in Ted.
The son of the Mochizuki Family mentions Paul in Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan - Episode 4: The Harvest Moon.

Paul Blart: Mall Cop.description: A picture or poster of Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction is used in Paul Blart: Mall Cop.
Paul Blart: Mall Cop is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Closure Alternative".
RoboCop was mentioned in Paul Blart: Mall Cop 2.
Paul Blart is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Where the Road Goes".
A character mentions Paul Blart: Mall Cop in Spooky Month episode “Unwanted Guest”.

Payday.description: Bill Overbeck from the Left 4 Dead Series makes an appearance in Payday: The Heist and Payday 2 in No Mercy a heist takes place in Mercy Hospital, a location from the Left 4 Dead game and takes place before the events of Left 4 Dead. The heist was remade for Payday 2 in late 2018
In the Confusion Ending of The Stanley Parable, Dallas's Mask from Payday 2 can be found.
The primary target of the heist "Transport: Train Heist" from Payday 2 is a prototype turret made to resemble the Sentry Gun from Team Fortress 2.

The map "Bank" from Counter-Strike:  Global Offensive was adapted into the heist "GO Bank" in Payday 2 as part of a collaboration between Valve and Overkill; in response, the masks of Dallas, Wolf, and Houston were added to the map after an update.
A Sweet Tooth mask was available as a free DLC for the PlayStation 3 version of Payday 2.

A heist taking place in the world of Hotline Miami was added in Payday 2. Later, A character based on the Hotline Miami character "Jacket" Was added to the game as a playable character, gained if you bought Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number - Digital Special Edition, bought Payday 2: Crimewave Edition, or sent Overkill proof of citizenship in places where Hotline Miami 2 is banned.

John Wick was added as a playable character in Payday 2. Later, Downloadable Content would be released to add John Wick Weapons and masks to commemorate the game, John Wick Chronicles VR and another pack that added a few heists, some masks, and a few more weapons to commemorate the release of John Wick: Chapter Two.
Characters from Payday are playable characters in SpeedRunners. Masks based on SpeedRunners characters were added to Payday 2.
The Gage Chivalry Pack DLC adds weapons from Chivalry. The trailer confirms Chivalry is part of the Payday universe.
A heist taking place in the world of Goat Simulator was added in Payday 2, while a Payday-themed expansion was added to Goat Simulator.
Masks based on Dead by Daylight can be obtained in Payday 2 by joining the former game's Steam Community Group.
The pre-order "All-Stars" pack for Worms W.M.D. includes masks of Payday 2 characters.
The events of the 1983 film Scarface happened in Payday 2's timeline. An imposter named "Scarface" is playable in the game.
The Kazaguruma and several demon masks from Shadow Warrior 2 are usable in Payday 2, while a Dallas skin, the AMCAR Rifle, and the Money Bundle from Payday 2 are usable in Shadow Warrior 2.
Enter the Gungeon and Payday 2 had a collaboration in which items based on one game would be available in the other.
A heist based on Reservoir Dogs was added to Payday 2.
Clothing based on Saints Row can be obtained in Payday 2 to promote the release of Saints Row The Third Remastered
Payday 3 is parodied in the Siege Tales episode "Spider-Man vs Payday 3".
Weapons and accessories based on Payday 2 appear in Dying Light 2 as part of a special collaboration.
Outfits based on Dallas and Chains from Payday 3 appear in Rainbow Six: Siege as part of a bundle.
Costumes based on Payday can be obtained in The Division 2 as part of a collaboration.

Peanuts.description: Some Peanuts strips feature references to Mickey Mouse.
Betty and Veronica issue #144 features a poster of Peanuts.
Snoopy has a sled with "rosebud" written on it in a comic strip from 1968/12/18; Citizen Kane is mentioned in a comic strip from 1971/9/12.
Tintin and the Picaros features masks of Charlie Brown in a carnival parade.
A character sings "Just One Person" from Snoopy The Musical in the Muppets Show episode "Bernadette Peters"; Kermit the frog is mentined in one Peanuts comic strip.
The Garfield comic strip June 23, 1978 features a reference to Peanuts. There's other references to Peanuts throughout the comics. Garfield is mentioned in a Peanuts comic strip on April 29, 1988.
Charlie Brown, Lucy, and Snoppy appear in The Fantastic Funnies.
There are several references to The Great Gatsby in the Peanuts comic strips.
Snoopy is mentioned in Who Censored Roger Rabbit?.
There were multiple format crossover games between Game & Watch and Popeye.
Batman: Year One issue #1 features a Snoopy lamp in one panel.
Characters from Peanuts appear in Off the Mark.
There are several references to Peanuts in the Simpsons series.
The Famicom game Donald Duck was repurposed as Snoopy's Silly Sports Spectacular! in North America.
The Tiny Toon Adventures episodes "Pledge Week" and "It's a Wonderful Tiny Toons Christmas Special" feature references to Peanuts.
A Snoopy balloon appears in We're Back! A Dinosaur's Story.
Snoopy is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One Where Rachel Quits". Gunther dresses up as Charlie Brown in the episode: "The One with the Halloween Party".
Charlie Brown from Peanuts appears in the Big Nate strip.
The Dexter's Laboratory episode "Sports a Poppin'" features references to Peanuts.
In the Buffy the Vampire Slayer episode "Passion", Willow and Xander say they watch A Charlie Brown Christmas as a christmas tradition.
Peanuts is mentioned in the The King of Queens episode: "Dog Days".
The Arthur episode "A Long, Dull Christmas" features a minor reference to Charlie Brown and Snoopy.
In one Peanuts strip, Sally writes fan letters to Harry Potter, unaware he's fictional.

In the episode Walking Small, when Plankton is seen packing his suitcase, one of the items his puts in is a shirt that looks similar to the one Charlie Brown wears in Peanuts. SpongeBob is mentioned in the Peanuts episode School Chums.
Snoopy from Peanuts appears in a Mother Goose & Grimm comic strip.
Linus Van Pelt and Snoopy from Peanuts appear in a Marvin comic strip.
Tom and Jazmine watch a Charlie Brown TV special in a Boondocks comic strip; The Boondocks episode "A Huey Freeman Christmas" features several references to A Charlie Brown Christmas.
Peanuts is mentioned in a Blondie comic strip.
Charlie Brown from Peanuts is mentioned in a Dilbert comic strip.
Charlie Brown from Peanuts is mentioned in a Hi and Lois comic strip.
Snoopy from Peanuts is mentioned in a Marmaduke comic strip.
Peanuts is referenced in a Hagar comic strip.
Dennis is seen reading a Peanuts book in a Dennis The Menace comic strip.
Snoopy from Peanuts is mentioned in a Family Circus comic strip.
A character is seen wearing a jacket with Snoopy from Peanuts on it in a Crankshaft comic strip.
Charlie Brown from Peanuts is mentioned in a Funky Winkerbean comic strip.
The faces of several Peanuts characters appear in a Luann comic strip.
There are several references to Peanuts in the Family Guy series.

Schroeder from Peanuts appears in the South Park "Something You Can Do With Your Finger"; they watch a parody of Peanuts in the South Park "Very Crappy Christmas"; the cast of South Park watch and criticize A Charlie Brown Christmas in the episode "A Very Crappy Christmas".
The West Wing episode "The Drop-In" features a reference to Charlie Brown, Lucy and her football prank.
The Johnny Bravo episode "Freudian Dip" features a minor reference to Peanuts.
Linus from Peanuts is mentioned in the Scrubs episode "My Bad".
The That '70s Show episode "An Eric Forman Christmas" features references to A Charlie Brown Christmas.
There are many format crossover UNO games between the two series.
Snoopy is mentioned in Chapter 110 of Stone Ocean.
In Eyes Cold Lemonade, the way Giggles and Petunia lean on the lemonade stand at the beginning of the episode is a reference to Peanuts when Charlie Brown and Linus lean on a brick wall.
There are many Peanuts themed Monopoly boards.
Peanuts is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Grandma Sues".
Kill Bill: Volume 1 features a character nicknamed Charlie Brown, whose appearance is simialr to the Peanuts character.

In The Fairly OddParents episode "Fouled Balled", when Chester pitches the ball at a world series game, the ball hits him and makes him spin around, causing his clothes, except his shorts, to come off. This is a running gag in Peanuts, that always happens to Charlie Brown when he is pitching. In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Walnuts, a parody of Peanuts. In The Fairly OddParents episode "Bad Heir Day", Crocker walks by two children one pulling a football away and the other one falling on his back. A dog lying on top of a purple doghouse is also seen. In Wishology!, while people are laughing at Timmy, there is "Hahahas" around him which is a nod to Peanuts. In the episode "Let Sleeper Dogs Lie", in a flashback, Sparky is Snoopy with Charlie Brown and Woodstock there.
A sound effect from Peanuts is used the Drawn Together episode Hot Tub.
There are several minor references to Peanuts in Arrested Development.

Peanuts.game: My Life as a Teenage Robot
Peanuts.description: In the My Life as a Teenage Robot episode "A Robot for All Seasons" there's a kid looking like Charlie Brown.
The Robot Chicken episodes "Vegetable Funfest" and !1987" feature segments parodying Peanuts.
Charlie Brown from Peanuts is mentioned on the news in "This World of Edd".
A background character resembles Charlie Brown in The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen: The Black Dossier.
The episode title It's The Great Pumpkin, Sam Winchester is an allusion to the short film title It's The Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown.
Snoopy is mentioned in Dork Diaries, Party Time, Pop Star, Dear Dork and Holiday Heartbreaker.
Charlie Brown is mentioned in Trick 'r Treat.
A tree resembling the one from A Charlie Brown Christmas appears in Prep & Landing.
A Peanuts based island is in Poptropica.
In Holly Jolly Secrets Part I, when the title shows, the design and outline of the title references to A Charlie Brown Christmas.
Characters turn into the style of Peanuts in the Eureka episode "Do You See What I See".

Peppermint Patty from Peanuts is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Schooled". Snoopy is mentioned in the episodes: "Connection Lost" and "New Kids On The Blog". The Modern Family episode: "It's the Great Pumpkin, Phil Dunphy"'s title is an allusion to "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown". Someone dresses up as Charlie Brown in the episode: "The Last Halloween".

Phineas and Ferb.description: Lawrence and Candace make a reference to the Gilligan's Island theme song in the episode "Swiss Family Phineas".

In No More Bunny Business, when Phineas pops out of the mailbox and scares the mailman, it is a reference to whenever Spongebob camps in his mailbox waiting for the mail. In Phineas and Ferb: Summer Belongs to You!, while stranded on a desert island, Phineas finds a square yellow kitchen sponge and a pink starfish and says "Look! A sponge and a starfish! There's gotta be something we can make out of this! No, that's ridiculous." which is a reference to SpongeBob SquarePants. In Squid Plus One, SpongeBob asking "Whatcha' dooooin'?" is the famous catchphrase used for the character Isabella Garcia-Shapiro in Phineas and Ferb.

A cartridge for The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX appears as a treasure in Hey! Pikmin, while another treasure is an ocarina similar to the one from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time; additionally the Goddesses statues in The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker are likely based on Pikmin. There might also be other references in the series.
Scanning Splatoon amiibo in Hey! Pikmin, makes the figures appear in the game.
"Something About Pikmin is a parody of Pikmin.

Microgame versions of Pikmin games are featured in the WarioWare series, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "Pikmin 2" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; additionally Wario can draw a sketch of Pikmin in WarioWare Gold by scanning the respective amiibo.

Pinocchio, Jiminy Cricket, and Lampwick appear in Who Framed Roger Rabbit.
Genie's head transforms into Pinocchio in Aladdin.
The episode Dee Dee Locks and the Ness Monster parodies Pinocchio.

Planet Terror.description: Planet Terror is one of the films in Grindhouse.

Planet of the Apes.description: Stage 3 from the Arcade version is a parody of Planet of the Apes series, featuring a boss fight against a monkey in one spacesuit.
The head of the Mega Maid crashes into a planet and a pair of apes discover it in Spaceballs, resembling the ending scene of Planet Of The Apes.

Planet of the Apes is mentioned in When Harry Met Sally...
The characters of Alien Nation meet Planet of the Apes in "Ape Nation".
Planet of the Apes is mentioned in Mrs. Doubtfire.
Planet of the Apes is mentioned in the Friends episodes: "The One with Ross's New Girlfriend" and "The One with Barry and Mindy's Wedding".
Donkey Kong mentions Planet of the Apes in the Donkey Kong Country episode "Legend of the Crystal Coconut".
In I'm Alan Partridge, Alan refers to his wife Carol's lover as "Mr. Planet of the Apes Man."
Planet of the Apes is mentioned in the The King of Queens episode "Roamin' Holiday".
Hal quotes Planet of the Apes in the Malcolm in the Middle episode "Monkey".
Characters recreate a scene from Planet of the Apes in the Cartoon Monsoon pilot Oh, Shoot!
In the Father of the Pride episode "Possession", the members of the chimpanzee orchestra are referred to as "damn dirty apes", a reference to a line in Planet of the Apes
Alex says "You maniac! You burned it up! Darn you! Darn you all to heck" at the ruins of his Liberty Statue copy in Madagascar, a reference to a similar line from Planet of the Apes.

In SpongeHenge, when the Krusty Krab is buried in the sand, it is a reference to the ending of Planet of the Apes when Taylor, having survived and escaped imprisonment, wanders along a coastline in search of shelter. He finds a partially destroyed Statue of Liberty buried in the sand and finally realizes what planet he is on. In addition, SpongeBob's hair and beard are strikingly similar to Charlton Heston's in the same movie. Planet of the Jellyfish is a parody of Planet of the Apes.
Leonard, Howard and Raj go to a Planet of the Apes marathon in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Pancake Batter Anomaly".
Rise of the Planet of the Apes is shown on TV in the New Girl episode: "Valentine's Day".
Planet of the Apes is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "The Late Show".
The Simian Flu from Rise of the Planet of the Apes is a disease in Plague Inc.

The Nostalgia Critic reviews "Planet of the Apes (2001)".

Bjorn's Skeleton and pegs appear in the achievement menu from Plants vs. Zombies: Game of the Year Edition. Gnorman from Peggle appears in Plants vs. Zombies 2: Its About Time when unlocking Terror from Tomorrow; there are minor references to the series in Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare. In Peggle 2, there are DLC costumes for Plants vs. Zombies Garden Warfare Costume Pack.
Plants vs. Zombies features a mini-game called "Portal Combat".

Pocket Fighter.description: Pocket Fighter is a spin-off of Puzzle Fighter.
Pocket Fighter features various characters from Street Fighter; Asuka is seen playing the game in Street Fighter Alpha: The Movie, and the game was included in the Street Fighter Alpha Anthology.
Morrigan, Felicia and Hsien-ko from Darkstalkers are selectable in Pocket Fighter.
Tessa from Red Earth is selectable in Pocket Fighter.
Guy, Rolento and Sodom make cameo appearances in Pocket Fighter, while Tessa's quiz in the English version of the console version includes two references to Final Fight.
Zombies from Resident Evil appear in Akuma's ending from Pocket Fighter. Chun-Li also cosplays as Jill Valentine in some of her attacks.

In Pocket Fighter, Felicia dresses like Mega Man and performs his Charged Buster and Slide attacks, while characters from the Mega Man series make cameo appearances in the PlayStation and Saturn ports.
Tessa dresses as Kyouko Minazuki from Rival Schools in one of her Hypers from Pocket Fighter.
Sonson, Tonton and Suisui make a cameo appearance in Pocket Fighter.
Blodia from Cyberbots makes a cameo appearance in Pocket Fighter, while Devilot makes a cameo appearance in the PlayStation and Saturn ports.

Various Star Gladiator characters make cameo appearances in Pocket Fighter, while Chun-Li cosplays as June Lin Milliam in some of her attacks and Felicia cosplays as Gamof and Rimgal in some of her attacks.
Pocket Fighter features Arthur's "turn-into-bones" death animation from the Ghosts 'n Goblins series.
In Pocket Fighter, the appearance of Dan's father is a parody of Art of Fighting character Takuma Sakazaki when disguised as Mr. Karate.

Super Gem Fighter Minimix is included in Capcom Fighting Collection.
Super Gem Fighter Mini Mix is included in Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium.

The modules Surble, Micemon and Pokelua are based on Pokémon. There is a defilante title achievement called "Catch Them All", which is based on the franchise's original slogan, "Gotta catch 'em all!". The shaman markings are based on Sentret and Furret. Ash's cap, Decidueye's hood, Umbreon hat, Slowking's shell, Selene's hat, May's bandana, Lillie's hat, Magikarp hat, Floria's hat, Dawn's beanie, Sawsbuck's spring antlers and Espeon hood appear in the shop as head items. Selene's hair, May's hair, Lillie's hair, Dawn's hair, N's hair, Primarina's hair, Keldeo's mane, Adaman's hair and Rika's hair appear in the shop as hair styles. Selene's hibiscus, Primarina's tiara and Gracidea flower appear in the shop as ear items. Cubone's skull appears in the shop as an eye item. Dawn's scarf and Meganium's flower appear in the shop as neck items. Drifloon appears in the shop as a tail item. Sylveon's eyes appear in the contact lenses section in four colors: pink, green, blue and yellow, and Obstagoon's eyes in four colors: blue, green, purple and pink. Poké Ball, Zacian's sword and Alolan Marowak's bone appear in the shop as hand items. The Trainer belt appears in the shop as a tattoo item. Poké Ball appears in the shop as a ball skin. Eevee, Marill, Furret, Litten, Vaporeon, Mega Charizard X, Mega Audino, Dewott, Wooloo, Lycanroc, Sylveon, Shaymin, Spring Sawsbuck, Glaceon, Jolteon, Umbreon, Espeon, Meowth and Flareon appear in the shop as furs. Detective Pikachu is mentioned in the Scott Pilgrim Takes Off episode "2 Scott 2 Pilgrim".
Squirtle from Leo is named after Squirtle from Pokémon.
Pokémon memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Palworld features many references to Pokémon.
In Sonic the Hedgehog 3, Detective Pikachu is mentioned.

Pole Position (Namco).description: The Atari upright version of Pole Position features billboards advertising Dig Dug.
Pole Position games are featured in multiple Namco Museum titles.
Pole Position is included in Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man.

One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "P.P.", and he's depicted in Pro Baseball Famista 2011  and Famista Dream Match  as a racer from Pole Position.
An arcade cabinet for Pole Position can be seen in the movie, Pixels.

Police Quest.description: Space Quest is mentioned many times in the Police Quest series.
The Black Cauldron is mentioned in Police Quest: In Pursuit of the Death Angel.
A picture of King Graham appears in a newspaper in Police Quest II: The Vengeance. Additionally, both series contain several minor references to one another.
Larry from Leisure Suit Larry appears at the Lytton Airport in Police Quest II. Additionally, both series contain several minor references to one another.
Sonny Bonds from Police Quest appears as an opponent in Hoyle's Official Book of Games: Volume 1 and Volume 3.
Characters from SWAT 4 star in the "Take It Away" video of Video Mods.

Poltergeist.description: A Poltergeist video case is shown in Video Violence.
The Treehouse of Horror segment "Bad Dream House" parodies Poltergeist.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references the tagline to Poltergeist II: The Other Side.
Poltergiest is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One with the Giant Poking Device".
Poltergeist is mentioned in Supernatural season 1 episode "Phantom Traveler".
Poltergeist is mentioned in the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia episode: "Mac and Charlie Die - Part 2".
Luigi's Mansion 2 features a reference to Poltergeist.
The Goldbergs episode "Mini Murray" features Adam watching Poltergeist.
There is a title achievement called "Poltergeist".
Poltergeist is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Viewing Party Combustion”.
Poltergeist is shown in "ESPECIAL DE HALLOWEEN - CLICHÊS MAIS PERTURBADORES DOS FILMES DE TERROR".
In an ad for Halloween Horror Nights 28 Carol Anne from Poltergeist  appears along with a Demogorgon from Stranger Things
In an ad for Halloween Horror Nights 28 Carol Anne from Poltergeist appears along with Michael Meyers from Halloween

Pong.description: Light Tennis is a clone of Pong.
Pong is referenced in Friday the 13th Part 2.
Doug and Arthur play Pong in the The King of Queens episode: "Fixer Upper".
One of the games that the employee plays in Whack Your Boss is Pong.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are references to Pong.
Pong is displayed in WALL-E.
The Lord of Games' face is drawn after the Pong game.
In the episode Guardians of Sunshine, when Finn is singing his computer song, his eyes start moving up and down and bounce his mouth back and forth. This is a reference to the game Pong.
A block based on Pong is playable in Blocks That Matter.
Some of the agents in T.U.F.F. slack-off while playing Pong in Super Duper Crime Busters!
Angry Birds Space features a level based on Pong.
The Season 1 opening of Video Game High School features a reference to Pong.
Pong appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
The paddles and ball from Pong make an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
Characters play Pong in the episode "The Snogre".
"Annoying Orange vs Pong" is a parody of Pong.
Pong has been a noticeable cameo in Monsters Vs. Aliens episodes.
Pong makes an appearance in The Emoji Movie.
In the stage "The Arctic Cruise" from A Hat in Time: Seal the Deal there's a monitor displaying a game of Pong.
"PING" in the Glitch Techs episode "Ping" is a reference to Pong.
Pong can be seen in Animation vs. Arcade Games.

Pony Island.description: In Pony Island one corrupted file is called "missingno", referencing the infamous glitch from Pokemon Red and Blue.
The infamous glitch "I AM ERROR" from Zelda 2 is referenced in Pony Island.
The character from the "I AM ERROR" room in Binding Of Isaac can be found in Pony Island.
One reply option screen has a list of "YES", "NO", "MAYBE", "I DON'T CARE" and "CAN YOU REPEAT THE QUESTION?" in Pony Island, referencing the lyrics of the Malcolm In The Middle theme.
The coin from Pony Island appears as the Strange Coin in The Hex, and Asmodeus.exe and Louey from Pony Island make cameo appearances in The Hex.
The coin from Pony Island appears as the Ancient Obol in Inscryption.

Ponyo.description: Ponyo features a miniature toy of the Bird God from Spirited Away.
Footage from Ponyo appears in Kaku Spring Festival Gala 2010.
Taiko no Tatsujin DS: Dororon! Yokai Daikessen!! and later games in the series feature a music track from Ponyo.
Machi Omakawa watches Panyo, a parody of Ponyo, in Chapter 331 of Komi Can’t Communicate.

Two characters dressed as Popuko and Pipimi can be found in Spooky Month episode “Tender Treats”.
