Mario meets Q*bert between the episodes of Donkey Kong and Q*bert, in the Saturday Supercade, while Q*bert meets Donkey Kong Jr. between the episodes of their respective shows.
The Kangaroo TV show was aired with the Q*bert TV show in the Saturday Supercade.
Q*bert meets Space Ace and Kimberly between the episodes of their shows in the Saturday Supercade.
The Simpsons episode "The Twisted World of Marge Simpson" and "In the Name of the Grandfather" feature references to Q*bert.
The Futurama episodes "A Clone of My Own" and "Anthology of Interest II" feature references to Q*bert.
The Family Guy episodes "Stuck Together, Torn Apart" and "Chick Cancer" feature references to Q*bert.
The top-most room in Zosma Tower from Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean is modeled after the Q*bert game.
Qbert is mentioned in the Pure Pwnage episode "Life Of A Pro Gamer".
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Q-Bert.
The Irate Gamer reviews Q*bert on NES.
Q*bert is mentioned in Ready Player One.
The Regular Show episode "Busted Cart" features a fictional game based on Q*bert.
Wreck-It Ralph features characters from Q*bert, while Ralph appears as a guest in Q*bert for iOS and Android.
Q*bert appears as one of the videogame characters in the movie, Pixels.
Q*bert appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #52.
Glenn mentions Q*bert in Season 3, Episode 13 of Superstore, “Video Game Release”.
Q*bert is mentioned in Into the Pit.
Q*bert can be seen in Animation vs. Arcade Games.

QWOP.description: Several characters play QWOP in the Office episode "New Guys".
In Octodad: Dadliest Catch, a poster in Gervason's Grocery contains a phrase with the acronym "QWOP".
Qwop is a playable character in SpeedRunners.
A video about QWOP can be seen in Animation vs. YouTube.
Cards based on QWOP are included in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls Requiem.

Qi Jiguang (Kaku Kids).description: Qi Jiguang, Qi Jimei, Hu Shouren, Chen Dacheng, Wang Rulong and Yu Dayou from Qi Jiguang appear in Kaku Spring Festival Gala 2015.

Qix.description: Super Qix features images of characters from Bubble Bobble.
The Game Boy version of Qix features cameos of Mario, Luigi and Princess Peach.
Multiplayer mode in the Game Boy version of Qix is based on Multiplayer mode from the Game Boy version of Tetris.
Qix is included in Taito Memories Volume 2 and Taito Memories Pocket, while Super Qix is included in Taito Memories II Volume 1.
Super Qix is included in Taito Legends, while Qix is included in Taito Legends 2 and Taito Legends Power-Up.
The "Art Class" minigame in Bully is based on Qix.
The Qix makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.

Quake.description: In Quake II, Dopefish appears partly disemboweled, hanging on a hook.
In Quake III Arena, Doomguy appears in three levels under the name "Doom".
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are Quake references.
The Team Fortress series spawned from a Quake mod; Team Fortress 2 features a promotional item from Quake and unlocked by pre-purchasing Quake 4 on Steam.
Quake is mentioned in Ready Player One.
A Shambler appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
Jazzpunk features a hidden minigame called "Wedding Cake" which is a parody of Quake and plays very similarly but replaces the weapons with wedding cakes.
The Quake Thunderbolt is available as part of Fallout 4's Creation Club.
One of the Mysterious Objects in The Evil Within 2 is based on Quake
B.J. Blackowicz from Wolfenstein appears as a playable character in Quake Champions.
An edit style for The Doom Slayer based on Phobos from Quake appears in Fortnite.

Quantum Break.description: A chalkboard in Quantum Break features references to the mystery of Alan Wake. Additionally, a TV show in Alan Wake called "Night Springs" also appears in Quantum Break.
The town of Ordinary, Maine which is seen in Quantum Break is also where the protagonist of Control grew up.

Quantum Leap.description: It is said that Anji Kapoor was once forced to watch the entire Quantum Leap series in the novel Slow Empire by Dave Stone.
Sam and Al appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #35.
Quantum Leap is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Focus Attenuation”.
Tim can be seen watching Quantum Leap in Season 2, Episode 17 of Superstore, “Integrity Award”.
Quantum Leap is mentioned in Avengers: Endgame.
Quantum Leap is mentioned in "Last Annihilation: Wiccan & Hulkling #1".

Quartet (Sega).description: Alex Kidd and Prince Egle make a cameo appearances in the sound test of Quartet.
Opa-Opa makes a cameo appearance in the sound test of Quartet.
Teddy Boy makes a cameo appearance in the sound test of Quartet.
A remix of the theme from Quartet appears in Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade and several subsequent Project DIVA games.
The Heroes from Quarter appear in Earth UFO Catcher.
Picross S Genesis & Master System Edition includes puzzles based off Quartet.

Quarth.description: Quarth is included in Konami GB Collection Vol. 4.
The Block Shooter from Quarth is playable in Airforce Delta Strike.
A modified version of Quarth with Goemon Impact replacing the ship can be unlocked in Ganbare Goemon: Tōkai Dōchū Oedo Tengu ri Kaeshi no Maki.
Quarth was re-released as a part of the Oretachi Gēsen Zoku series.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Quarth.
Quarth puzzles are featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.

Queen's Blade.description: Iroha, Mina Majikina and Cham Cham from Samurai Shodown received visual combat books for Queen's Gate and makes a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Mai Shiranui from Fatal Fury received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate and makes a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Dizzy from Guilty Gear received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate and makes a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Kasumi from Dead or Alive received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate and makes a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Lili from Tekken received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate and makes a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Ivy, Taki and Pyrrha from the Soul series received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate and make a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Noel Vermillion from BlazBlue received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate and makes a guest appearance in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Wonder Momo appears as a character in Queen's Gate: Spiral Chaos.
Suchie-Pai from Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai received a visual combat book for Queen's Gate.
Characters from Queen's Blade are guest characters in Shinobi Master Senran Kagura: New Link.
Characters from Queen's Blade Unlimited appear in Ikki Tousen Extra Burst as part of a collaboration.
Characters from High School of the Dead appear in Queen's Blade Limit Break as part of a collaboration.
Characters from Darkstalkers appear in Queen's Blade Limit Break as part of a collaboration.

Quick Draw McGraw.description: In the Top Cat episode "A Visit from Mother", the gang walks past graffiti that reads "El Kabong", the name of Quick Draw's alter ego in The Quick Draw McGraw Show.
Quick Draw McGraw has appeared in several Yogi Bear shows.
Characters from Quick Draw McGraw appear in Laff-A-Lympics.
Quick Draw McGraw, Augie Doggy and Doggie Daddy from The Quick Draw McGraw show appear in Casper's First Christmas.
Quick Draw McGraw, Baba Looey, Augie Doggy and Doggie Daddy from The Quick Draw McGraw Show appear in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Snooper and Blabber appear in the Super Secret Secret Squirrel episode "Agent Penny".
Characters from Quick Draw McGraw appear in I Am Weasel in the episode "I Am My Lifetime".
Quick Draw McGraw and Baba Looey appear in the Samurai Jack  episode ""Episode XXIX: Couple on a Train".
Snuffles appears in the Johnny Bravo episode "Double Vision".
Augie Doggie and Doggie Daddy appear in the Harvey Birdman episode "Peanut Puberty"; Quick Draw McGraw and Baba Looey appear in the Harvey Birdman episode "Guitar Control".
Characters looking like Quick Draw McGraw and Baba Looey appear in a Heathcliff comic strip.
Quick Draw McGraw appears in the Wacky Races episode "Much Ado About Wacky".
Augie Doggie and Doggie Daddy from Quick Draw McGraw are mentioned in Ready Player Two.
El Kabong, Bobbie Looey, and many other characters from Quick Draw McGraw appear in Jellystone!
Quick Draw McGraw is mentioned in Licorice Pizza.
Quick Draw McGraw appears in the Teen Titans Go! episode: "Warner Bros 100th Anniversary".

QuickSpot.description: QuickSpot and Machigai Museum 2 feature a puzzle based on Pac-Man.
QuickSpot features puzzles based on Taiko no Tatsujin.
QuickSpot and Machigai Museum 2 feature several puzzles based on Klonoa.
QuickSpot features a puzzle based on Katamari.
QuickSpot feature one puzzle image using Mappy sprites.
QuickSpot features three puzzles with images showing Susumu Hori from Mr. Driller.
QuickSpot features one puzzle with the Solvalou from Xevious.
QuickSpot features one puzzle based on Galaga.
QuickSpot features one puzzle image using The Tower of Druaga sprites.
QuickSpot features one puzzle based on Libble Rabble.
QuickSpot features one puzzle based on Ridge Racer.
Point Blank DS is a format crossover with Unou no Tatsujin.
Unou no Tatsukin: Soukai! Machigai Museum 2 features several puzzle using images from SoulCalibur III.
Unou no Tatsukin: Soukai! Machigai Museum 2 features one puzzle based on Mojipittan.

Quiz Caravan Cult Q.description: A Bomberman world is featured in Quiz Caravan Cult Q, with Bomberman himself and Red Bomberman also appearing.

Quiz Caravan Cult Q.game: Princess Tomato in the Salad Kingdom
Quiz Caravan Cult Q.description: Princess Tomato appears as a playable character in Quiz Caravan Cult Q.
One of the four worlds in Quiz Caravan Cult Q is based on Star Soldier.

Quiz Magic Academy.description: Aloe from Quiz Magic Academy makes an appearance in Pop'n Music 13, Pop'n Music Sunny Park and Pop'n Music Kaimei Riddles; tracks from Quiz Magic Academy also appear in the game. Additionally, Mimi from Pop'n Music makes a cameo appearance during the Bemani exam in Quiz Magic Academy: Kenja no Tobira.
Sharon and Medea make a cameo appearance in LovePlus during the Moeru! Taisen Puzzle-Dama minigame. Additionally, LovePlus features a cosplay outfit based on Quiz Magic Academy.
Tracks from Quiz Magic Academy can be played in the Sound Voltex series.
The "Grim Aloe Explosive Battle" limited event from Bombergirl features Grim Aloe from Quiz Magic Academy as a playable character, as well as an Academy uniform as a Dress-Up Part.
An outfit based on Konami Lady appears in Quiz Magic Academy: Kiseki no Kōsa -Xross Voyage- as part of a collaboration event.
Malariya from Quiz Magic Academy appears as a guest character in Chase Chase Jokers as part of a collaboration event.

Quiz Nanairo Dreams.description: Ryu's Japan stage from Street Fighter Alpha: Warrior's Dream appears in one of the character scenarios in Quiz Nanairo Dreams, as well as merchandising based on the series. Quiz Nanairos Dreams was planned to be featured in Street Fighter × All Capcom, with Saki appearing in official art.
Saki Omokane and other girls from Quiz Nanairo Dreams were based on characters from Neon Genesis Evangelion.
There's a poster of Vampire Hunter in one of the backgrounds in Quiz Nanairo Dreams.
There's a poster of Dungeons & Dragons: Shadow over Mystara in one of the backgrounds in Quiz Nanairo Dreams.
Charlotte from Quiz Nanairo Dreams was based on Devilot from Cyberbots.
Charlotte's dungeon from Quiz Nanairo Dreams uses an edited version of the background from Devilot's stage in Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo.
Quiz Nanairo Dreams features a giant monster inspired in Godzilla.
Saki Omokane is an assist character in Marvel vs. Capcom.
Characters from Quiz Nanairo Dreams make cameo appearances in the PlayStation and Saturn ports of Pocket Fighter.
Various Quiz Nanairo Dreams characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Saki Omokane is selectable in the Wii ports of Tatsunoko vs. Capcom.
Minna to Capcom All Stars features Saki Omokane from Quiz Nanairo Dreams, and she later appears in official art for Street Fighter × All Capcom.
Saki from Quiz Nanairo Dreams appears in Onimusha Soul as part of the "Capcom Heroines" limited event.
Arino plays the PlayStation port of Quiz Nanairo Dreams in episode 199 of GameCenter CX.

Quiz Tonosama no Yab\u014d.description: Mega Man appears in Quiz Tonosama no Yabō.
Arino plays the TurboGrafx-CD port of Quiz Tonosama no Yabō in episode 25. He also plays Quiz Tonosama no Yabō 2: Zenkoku-ban in episode 228 by using proper conversion kits.

During the active period of the Onimusha Soul game, Haruo Yaguchi from High Score Girl mentions Quiz Tonosama no Yabō by wondering if he and his friends were warped to the game's universe rather than Onimusha.

R-Type.description: GamePro enters the world of R-Type.
Enemies resembling the ship from R-Type appear in The Adventures of Quik & Silva.
Various characters from R-Type appears in Shuyaku Sentai Irem Fighter.
A Bydo from R-Type appears in Superior Soldiers.
Mr. Heli from Battle Chopper appears in R-Type Final.
The OF-1 Daedalus from Image Fight appears in R-Type Final.
There's a minor reference to R-Type in episode 3 of Pop Team Epic.
Music from R-Type can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix after an update.

RAID: Shadow Legends.description: RAID: Shadow Legends is mentioned in multiple Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episodes.
Xena appears in Raid: Shadow Legends.

Champions with weapons and armor from Monster Hunter appear in RAID: Shadow Legends as part of a collaboration event. Additionally, during this event, several trailers were released that explain how the creatures of Monster Hunter came to the world of Teleria from RAID: Shadow Legends.
Characters from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles appear in Raid: Shadow Legends as part of a collaboration event.
A Xenomorph appears in Raid: Shadow Legends as part of a collaboration event.
A Predator appears in Raid: Shadow Legends as part of a collaboration event.

RESEARCH and DESTROY.description: Costumes based on Date Kaname, Iris Sagan, and Aiba from AI: The Somnium Files appear in RESEARCH and DESTROY as part of the Costume Bundle DLC.
Costumes based on Monokuma, Nagito Komaeda, and Chiaki Nanami from Danganronpa 2 appear in RESEARCH and DESTROY as part of the Costume Bundle DLC.
Costumes based on Rintarou Okabe, Kurisu Makise, and Daru from Steins;Gate appear in RESEARCH and DESTROY as part of the Costume Bundle DLC.
Costumes based on Sigma Klin, Phi and Zero III from Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward appear in RESEARCH and DESTROY as part of the Costume Bundle DLC.

RPG World.description: Hero and Galgarion appear in the OK K.O.! episode A Hero's Fate.

RWBY.description: Episode 1 features a reference to to Fullmetal Alchemist.
Episodes 1 and 9 feature references to Yu-Gi-Oh.
RWBY features many references to Red vs. Blue.
A team consisting of characters from series by Rooster Teeth including RWBY appears in #IDARB.
RWBY characters appear in Crusaders Quest for a collaboration event.
Characters from RWBY are playable characters in BlazBlue: Cross Tag Battle.
RWBY is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
Ruby, Blake, and Yang have been subjects for DBX.
The Relic of Knowledge from RWBY can be found in the Camp Camp episode "The Quarter-Moon Convergence". Additionally, the two series makes several other references to each other all of the time.
Yang Xiao Long, Weiss Schnee, and Blake Belladonna have been subjects for Death Battle! alongside the Crescent Rose is an official card in Death Battle: The Game.
Smite features skins that change the gods into RWBY characters.
One Step From Eden features a reference to RWBY
RWBY/Justice League is an crossover between the two series.
RWBY characters appeared in Paladins for a collaboration event.
RWBY characters appeared in Black Rock Shooter for a collaboration event.
Crunchyroll-Hime appeared alongside Ruby from RWBY in multiple videos on the Crunchyroll-Hime YouTube channel.
RWBY is parodied in multiple Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episodes.
There's a series of Weiß Schwarz cards based around characters and items from 'RWBY.

Rabbids.description: Rabbids is a spinoff of Rayman.
The Clark Superbunny is based on Superman.
A rabbid appears in a trailer for Far Cry Vengeance.
A picture of a Rabbid can be seen on a purchasable cot in Imagine: Babyz.
The Rabbinator rabbid from Rayman Raving Rabbids 2 is based on the Terminator.
The poster for a parody of Pirates of the Caribbean was shown on rabbids.com to promote Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
The poster for a parody of X-Men was shown on rabbids.com to promote Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
The poster for a parody of Ghost Recon 2 was shown on rabbids.com to promote Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
The poster for a parody of Dark Messiah of Might and Magic was shown on rabbids.com to promote Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
The poster for a parody of Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Vegas was shown on rabbids.com to promote Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
A costume based on Jason Voorhees from Friday the 13th can be unlocked in Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
A costume based on Ken Masters from Street Fighter can be unlocked in Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
A costume based on Naruto Uzumaki can be unlocked in the Japanese version of Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
Raving Rabbids make an appearance in Academy of Champions: Football.
In Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Smash Up, The Rabbids are unlockable characters; additionally Rayman Raving Rabbids 2 features Rabbids based on the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
Rabbid Plush Toys can be found in Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Conviction; additionally the Bunny Fisher rabbid and the Sam Kingfisher Grenaduck are based on Sam Fisher.

Rabbids appear during the song "Here Comes The Hotstepper", downloadable in Just Dance 2, and featured in Just Dance: Summer Party, and during the song "Make The Party (Don’t Stop)" in Just Dance 4, while Just Dance 2018 features a version of "Naughty Girl" with Rabbid Peach as a dancer.
Rabbids are playable characters in Super Brawl 3.
Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag features a cheat code which turns all the enemies into Rabbids scarecrows.
Rabbid Plush Toys can be found in Watch Dogs.
Rabbids characters/map appears as DLC for Monopoly Plus.
A "Rayman Raving Rabbids" board game can be found in Tom Clancy's The Division.
The Uno Rabbids DLC for UNO features Rabbids characters interacting with the main game.
A Rabbid dressed as a shark appears in Hungry Shark Evolution as part of a special collaboration.
Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle is a crossover between the two series; additionally the Rayman Raving Rabbids series features minor references to the Mario series.

DK Barrels from the Donkey Kong series make an appearance in Mario + Rabbids: Kingdom Battle where there also is a Rabbid Kong enemy. The Donkey Kong Adventure expansion to the game is based on the Donkey Kong series and features Donkey Kong as a selectable character.
Rabbid Peach, Rabbid Mario and Rabbid Kong appear as spirits in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Rabbids replace the generic minions in For Honor for April Fool's Day.
A Rabbid can be obtained in Growtopia as part of the 2022 UbiWeek event while a Rabbid Buddy can be found in Growtopia as part of the 2023 UbiWeek event..
Rabbids appear in Stumble Guys.
Rabbids appear in Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix.

Rad Mobile.description: Sonic the Hedgehog appears as a car ornament in Rad Mobile; its port Gale Racer features ornaments based on other Sonic characters as well.
A Rad Mobile arcade machine appears in Earth UFO Catcher.

Rad Rodgers.description: Duke Nukem is a playable character in Rad Rodgers: Radical Edition.
Lo Wang is a playable character in Rad Rodgers: Radical Edition.

Radar Scope.description: Radar Scope has elements inspired from Space Invaders.
Radar Scope has elements inspired from Galaxian.

Rage of Bahamut.description: Shadowverse is considered to be a spiritual successor of Rage of Bahamut with many characters and illustrations from Rage of Bahamut appearing in the game.
Characters from Yuri on Ice appeared in Rage of Bahamut as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Granblue Fantasy appeared in Rage of Bahamut as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Hatsune Miku appeared in Rage of Bahamut as part of a special collaboration.
Princess Connect! Re:Dive characters appear in Rage of Bahamut as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Zombie Land Saga appear in Rage of Bahamut during a collaboration event.

Ragnarok (Daewon CI).description: As part of special collaboration events, Puzzle & Dragons featured dungeons with creatures from Ragnarok Online and Ragnarok Odyssey Ace.
A Kat and Alias costume appear as a free dlc in Ragnarok Odyssey Ace.
One of Kasumi's costumes in Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate is a promotional outfit bearing the logo of Ragnarok Odyssey ACE.
Ragnarok Clicker has the same gameplay as Clicker Heroes.
An item similar to The Dead Branch from Ragnarok Online can be found in Slay the Spire
Characters from Neon Genesis Evangelion made an appearance in Ragnarok M: Eternal Guardians of Love as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Ultraman made an appearance in Ragnarok M: Eternal Guardians of Love as part of a special collaboration.
Ragnarok partnership items and skins added for a limited time.

Ragnarok (Daewon CI).game: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
Ragnarok (Daewon CI).description: Characters from That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime made an appearance in Ragnarok X as part of a special collaboration.

Raimais.description: Round 18 Blue in Raimais is patterned after a Zen-chan enemy from Bubble Bobble, while "Raimaiz" is one of the random secret high score screen names replacing banned words in Bubble Symphony.
Three endings in one of the story paths in Syvalion reveal Makoto from Raimais is the pilot of the Syvalion, with Mika and Dr. Molto being referenced as well.
A mini boss that takes the appearance of the Organizer from Raimais appears in Megablast.
Taito Memories Gekan  and Pocket include Raimais.
Taito Legends 2 and Taito Legends: Power-Up include Raimais.

Rain World.description: Slugcat makes a cameo in Indie Pogo.
A poster for Rain World can be found in Professor Chalk's room in the music video for A Songus Amongus.

Rainbow (ITV).description: George and Zippy appear in the premiere episode of Ashes to Ashes.
Zippy appears in the CBeebies House episode "Dodge Time".
Zippy, George and Bungle sing in Children in Need's Puppet Aid. Zippy and George appear in the Children in Need special Puppets take over the Masterchef kitchen.

Rainbow Bubblegem.description: An animated web short on the official Rainbow Bubblegem social media accounts, "What Should Indigo Wear for Halloween? 🎃👻", features Indigo Keen dressed up as CatNap from Poppy Playtime.
An animated web short on the official Rainbow Bubblegem social media accounts, "What Should Indigo Wear for Halloween? 🎃👻", features Indigo Keen dressed up as Pomni from The Amazing Digital Circus.

Rainbow Islands.description: The Rainbow Islands series is a spin-off of Bubble Bobble.

Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Doh's Island") based off Arkanoid, with several enemies and DOH as the final boss; Bubby is one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.

The world of Darius is featured as an island ("Darius Island") in Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2, including appearances of enemies and Electric Fan and King Fossil (former/NES port) as area bosses.

Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Magical Island") based off The Fairyland Story, with appearances of several enemies and Horned as the final boss, with Ptolemy making a cameo in the Game Boy Color port.

The world of Kiki KaiKai is featured as an island ("Kiki KaiKai Island") in the NES port of Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2, including appearances of Sayo-chan/Pocky, enemies and Manuke/Rocky as the area boss.
Bubby from Rainbow Islands appears in Cameltry holding a 1000 Pts sign if the player reaches the goal with more than 60 seconds on the clock.
Stage 4 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Rainbow Islands and features a playable Bubby; and Bubby is one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Characters from Rainbow Islands appear in Pop n' Pop.
Taito Memories Pocket, II Gekan and II Joukan include Rainbow Islands.
Bob, Bub, Mike and Violet from Rainbow Islands Revolutions appear as captured friends in The NewZealand Story Revolution.

Rainbow Sea (Kaku Kids).description: Characters from Rainbow Sea appear in Kaku Spring Festival Gala 2010.

Rainbow Six.description: The Rainbow Six series spun off from the Jack Ryan novel of the same name.
Operatives from the Rainbow appear in EndWar; "The End Begins: Rainbow Six" is a crossover between the two series.
The ERS System from H.A.W.X appears in Rainbow Six: Shadow Vanguard.
A costume based on Rainbow Six: Siege appears in Tom Clancy's The Division as a Ubisoft Club reward. Cosmetics based on The Division appear in Rainbow Six: Siege as Ubisoft Club rewards.
Operators from Rainbow Six Siege appear in Special Operation 2 from Ghost Recon: Wildlands and in the Amber Sky event from Ghost Recon: Breakpoint.

Siege Tales is based on Rainbow Six: Siege. Characters from Rainbow Six appear in multiple Siege Tales episodes as part of sponsorships from Ubisoft. Outfits based on Siege Tales appear in Rainbow Six: Siege as part of a bundle.
Characters from Rainbow Six appear in Elite Squad.
Sam Fisher appears as an operator under the name "Zero" in Rainbow Six: Siege as part of the Operation Shadow Legacy expansion.
Ash, Blitz, Frost and Tachanka from Rainbow Six: Siege appears in a collab for Arknights.
Outfits based on Jill Valentine and Leon S. Kennedy appear in Rainbow Six: Siege.
Outfits based on Smoke Pickle Rick and gromflomites appear in Rainbow Six: Siege as part of a bundle.
Outfits based on Kiryu, Majima and Kaoru and Cosmetics from Yakuza appears in Rainbow Six: Siege.
Cosmetics based on NieR appear in Rainbow Six: Siege as part of a special collaboration.
The Spartan 117 armor from Halo appears as a skin for Sledge in Rainbow Six: Siege, along with several other cosmetics based on Halo.
Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix features many elements from the Rainbow Six series.
Ezio Auditore from Assassin's Creed appears in the Ubisoft advertisement "What is Rainbow Six Siege x @SiegeTales" alongside characters from Rainbow Six.

Tubarão from Rainbow Six: Siege appears as a crossover skin in Dead by Daylight, along with outfits based on Wamai and Blitz, while outfits and other cosmetics based on the Trapper and the Huntress from Dead by Daylight appear in Rainbow Six: Siege.
GS-Kommando from Rainbow Six appears as a faction in XDefiant.
Outfits based on Dallas and Chains from Payday 3 appear in Rainbow Six: Siege as part of a bundle.

Rakugakids.description: Beartank from Rakugakids appears as a board piece in Goemon Mononoke Sugoroku.
Beartank as well as music from Rakugakids appear in Pop'n Music GB and Pop'n Music 10.
The item "Bear Ring" from Castlevania: Circle of the Moon transforms Nathan Graves into Beartank from Rakugakids.
Konami Krazy Racers features Bear Tank from Rakugakids as a selectable racer.

Rally-X.description: The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Xevious and its sequels.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Libble Rabble.

The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Gaplus while the X68000 version of Galaga '88 features a bonus level with cars and flags from Rally-X; the cars from Rally-X are featured in Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Sky Kid.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Toy Pop.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in the NES version of Dig Dug II and in Dig Dug Arrangement; Dig Dug: Digging Strike also features a reference to New Rally-X.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is an item in Genpei Toma Den.
The Special Flag and Lucky Flag from Rally-X are usable items in The Quest of Ki; the Special Flag also makes a minor appearance in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Dragon Buster II.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Marvel Land.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Mappy Kids.
The car and flags from Rally-X appear as special items in Tinkle Pit.
Games in the X-Rally series are featured in multiple Namco Museum titles.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a usable item in Tales of Phantasia, Tales of the Abyss and Tales of Vesperia.
Namco Classic Collection Vol. 2 includes Rally-X, New Rally-X and Rally-X Arrangement.
Stage 47 in Namco Gallery Vol.1 version of Battle City is shaped after a Special Flag from Rally-X.
Rally-X and New Rally-X are featured in Namco History Vol.2.
Floor 28 in Neo Babel Mode from Tower of Babel Arrange features moving pixel art of the Rally-X car in the background.
A parody of Rally-X called "Lolly-X" is featured within Segagaga.
Taiko no Tatsujin 2 and later games in the series feature a music track from Rally-X.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Wangan Midnight and Wangan Midnight R.
The Special Flag from Rally-X appears as an item in console versions of Tekken 4 and Tekken 6 and as an icon in Tekken Tag Tournament 2.

Ridge Racers, Ridge Racers 2 and Ridge Racer 3D features the Rally-X car as a selectable car; additionally, Ridge Racer features a "Team Rally-X", while Ridge Racers features a minigame version of Rally-X as loading screen.
The Special Flag from Rally-X makes an appearance in Star Fox: Assault.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Namco × Capcom.

The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Pac 'n Roll and appears alongside the Rally-X racers during a timed promotion in Pac-Man Monsters, while Pac-Man is selectable in Rally-X Remix and a theme featuring Rally-X cars appears in Pac-Man 99; additionally a car from Rally-X appears as a collectable item in Pac & Pal; also New Rally-X is included in Pac-Man Arcade Gold and Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man while Rally-X is included in Pac-Man's Arcade Party, and Rally-X S is included in Pac-Man Games; Pac-Man Championship DX+ includes a map based on Rally-X, while Pac'N-Jump includes a Rally-X mode.
Namco Museum: 50th Anniversary includes Rally-X, while Namco Museum Remix includes Rally-X Remix and Namco Museum Megamix includes New Rally-X.
A racer from Rally-X appears as an item in Mario Kart Arcade GP and its sequels, and also is a selectable kart in Arcade GP DX.
The Special Flag from Rally-X appears as an item in Ace Combat Zero: The Belkan War.
Music from New Rally-X is featured in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of the Rally-X Special Flag with characters appearing in the background.
The game TurboTime from Wreck-It Ralph is based on Rally-X.
The Special Flag appears as an item.

The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax; it also makes minor appearances in other games in the series; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels is called "Rally-X".

In the episode Cartman Joins NAMBLA is present one remix of the Rambo's theme song.

John Rambo is mentioned in Kick-Ass #4.
Rambo is mentioned in the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia episode: "Mac And Dennis: Manhunters".
The first Fight Klub set features cards based on Rambo, including a character card of John Rambo.

The character Rookie in Rookie - Fast platt is parody of Rocky Balboa and John Rambo.
Rambro is based on John Rambo from Rambo.
Rambo is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "To'hajiilee".

A poster for Rambo can be seen in the New Girl episode: "San Diego".
There is a title achievement called "Rambo Mouse".
Rambo is parodied in Les Kassos.
John Rambo is a DLC character in the second Kombat Pack for Mortal Kombat 11.
In the event featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, Call of Duty: Warzone and Call of Duty: Mobile called '80s Action Heroes, the event features Rambo.

Characters from Rambo appear in World of Tanks, along with cosmetics.

Characters from  Randy Cunningham: 9th Grade Ninja appear in Disney XD Villains Unite!.

Raskulls.description: Halfbrick Rocket Racing Trial Mode! demo and PSP version of Halfbrick Rocket Racing have digital billboards advertising Raskulls. A rocket from Halfbrick Blast Off appears on the background menu in Magic Brick Wars.
Raskulls and ilomilo crossed over with each other as part of Microsoft's 2010 "Games for the Holidays" promotion.

Barry Steakfries is a playable character in Raskulls and an avatar in Magic Brick Wars. The King appears as one of the clothing sets in Jetpack Joyride, interacts with Barry in several episodes of Barry Vlog, and is playable in Jetpack Joyride Racing.
The King is a playable character in Battle Racing Stars.

Truffles, Sensei, Watermelon Ninja and Koya are available as an avatars in Magic Brick Wars. The game later featured a Fruit Ninja 10th Anniversary Season, which included various elements from Fruit Ninja. Fruit Ninja 2 would later reuse most of the emotes from Magic Brick Wars, including the ones of a Raskull character.
Micro is available as an avatar in Magic Brick Wars.
Colossatron appears on the background of the menu and on one of the banners in Magic Brick Wars.
Dan is available as an avatar in Magic Brick Wars.

Rastan.description: The ending image from the 4th Plane Beginner course in the SNES port of Cameltry features Rastan holding the fire sword, while the head of Rastan is a preset ball in the Ball Edit Mode from the Sharp X68000 port of Cameltry.
The beast master is revealed to be Rastan in the ending of Dino Rex.
"Rastansa" (for Rastan Saga) and "Warriorb" (for Warrior Blade: Rastan Saga Episode III) are two of the random secret high score screen names in Bubble Symphony.
One of the players in the "Taito Planets" team from Super Kyuukyoku Harikiri Stadium 2 is named "Rastan", after the series.
Barbarian is released in Japan as Warrior Blade: Rastan vs. Barbarian, changing one of the characters to Rastan while keeping the other elements the same.
Taito Memories Joukan and Taito Pocket Memories include Rastan, Taito Memories Gekan includes Rastan Saga II and Taito Memories Gekan II includes Warrior Blade: Rastan Saga Episode III.
Taito Legends and Taito Legends Power-Up include Rastan, Taito Legends 2 includes Rastan Saga II.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure and Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don! feature a music track from Warrior Blade: Rastan Saga Episode III.
Arino plays the Genesis port of Rastan Saga II in episode 328.

Ratatouille.description: The Pizza Planet Truck appears in Ratatouille.
Dug appears as a shadow that barks at Remy in Ratatouille.
Ratatouille UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Remy appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #29.
The player enters the world of Ratatouille in Kinect Rush: A Disney/Pixar Adventure.
Ratatouille is mentioned in the Breaking Bad episode: "Fifty-One".
Ratatouille is mentioned in the White Collar episode "Vested Interest".
Ratatouille is parodied in several episodes of Robot Chicken.
Gusteau's Sign appears in Disney Infinity 2.0.
Colette from "Ratatouille" makes a cameo in "Inside Out"
There is a Cooking event, which is based on Ratatouille. The Cooking event's title achievement called "Ratatouille" is also based on Ratatouille.
Characters from Ratatouille appear in Disney Heroes: Battle Mode
Linguini appears as a playable character in LEGO The Incredibles.
Remy makes his debut in Kingdom Hearts III.
Characters and Items from Ratatouille appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley.
Ratatouille is parodied in Les Kassos.
Official Squishmallows were released based on Ratatouille.
There is a puzzle in Disney Solitare that shows a scene from Ratatouille.
Zootopia 2 has a reference to Ratatouille.

Ratchet & Clank.description: The North American and European versions of Everybody's Golf 4 feature Ratchet and Clank as an unlockable golfer.

In the Japanese version of Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal, by entering a code you can unlock a wearable Pipo Suit for Ratchet to wear. Also in many versions of Ape Escape 3, a Ratchet picture can be seen when entering a cheat-code, as well as a monkey wearing a Ratchet costume with a small version of Clank jetpack to fly around and a replica model of the RYNO.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are Ratchet & Clank references.

You could find an image of Jak and Daxter inside Clank's apartment in Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando. Jak is playable in Ratchet: Deadlocked and Ratchet is playable in Jak X by having a save file on Ratchet: Deadlocked. Jak and Daxter and a Precursor orb can sometimes appear when using the RYNO 8 in Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart.
In Ratchet: Deadlocked, there is a superficial superhero who goes by Ace Hardlight, a reference both to Arnold Rimmer's superficial persona Ace Rimmer and the term "hard-light hologram".
Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage! features two enemies that serve a basis for Ratchet & Clank. Also, the Rank-O-Meter features a character named Agent Zero from Spyro 2.
There are Ratchet & Clank references in the Resistance games.
In Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction, a skill point under the name "Gotta Catch 'Em All" is a possible reference to Pokémon.
A picture or poster of Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction is used in Paul Blart: Mall Cop.
Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time features a reference to Mario.
Ratchet & Clank are downloadable in ModNation Racers.
Ratchet and Clank are playable in PlayStation Move Heroes.
Ratchet and Clank costumes are downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 2.
InFamous 2 features a reference to Ratchet & Clank in a movie title and a mission's name.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features Ratchet and Clank as a single playable character.

Sly Cooper can steal the medieval metal man from Sly Cooper: Thieves in Time which resembles Clank. Ratchet's Wrench is also an unlockable in the same game. Sly Cooper, Bentley and the Cooper Van can sometimes appear when using the RYNO 8 in Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart.
The PlayStation 3 version of Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare features a Ratchet hat only available by pre-ordering the game.
Skin Pack 2 in the PlayStation versions of Minecraft Legacy Console and Bedrock Editions features skins based off characters from Ratchet & Clank, along with the Minecraft 2nd Birthday Skin Pack.
Clank appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #48.
A Ratchet mask is a preorder bonus in PlayStation versions of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 5.
Ratchet & Clank have been subjects for Death Battle!
A bomberman exclusive to the PlayStation 4 version of Super Bomberman R known as "Ratchet & Clank Bomber" is based off the main characters from Ratchet & Clank.

In the PS4 Spider-Man game when Spider-Man performs the Spidy McMarx when he performs four aerials in a single free fall. This is a reference to Skid McMarx, as well as the Tricky McMarx move when Ratchet performs every trick in a single jump.
The Peacemonger weapon that fires a barrage of rockets in Borderlands 3 is a reference to the Warmonger and Peacemaker weapons in later Ratchet & Clank games.
An arrangement of origami figures can be found in Ghost of Tsushima, one of them referencing Ratchet and Clank.
One of the weapons that can be obtained in Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart looks similar to the Keyblade from Kingdom Hearts.

A Sawtooth and Thunderjaw from Horizon can sometimes appear when using the RYNO 8 in Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart. Outfits based on Ratchet and Rivet from Ratchet & Clank appear in LEGO Horizon Adventures.

In Sunset Overdrive, the intro features a refrigerator with parody titles of Insomanic titles, including different Ratchet & Clank titles. Fizzie and barrels of Overcharge from Sunset Overdrive can sometimes appear when using the RYNO 8 in Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart.
The Hog Wild and a jeep from Uncharted can sometimes appear when using the RYNO 8 in Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart.
Skins based on Ratchet and Clank are available in Fall Guys.
A Ratchet costume and Clank pet are available for the PS4 and PS5 versions of Among Us.
God of War Ragnarök features a poem based on Ratchet & Clank.
A bot that resembles Ratchet appears in Astro's Playroom. Bots based on Ratchet and Rivet from Ratchet & Clank can be found in Astro Bot.

A Tanchimo appears in Digitalis at Chapter 30 of Eden's Zero.
Rave characters appear in the mini-series Hero's.

Raven (Disney).description: Both Saved by the Bell and That's So Raven take place at a school called Bayside High School.
That's So Raven characters and The Suite Life of Zack & Cody characters cross over in the crossover special That's So Suite Life of Hannah Montana.
That's So Raven characters and Hannah Montana characters cross over in the crossover special That's So Suite Life of Hannah Montana.
That's So Raven is mentioned in the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia episode: "The Gang Gets Invincible".

Eddie Thomas and Cory Baxter are selectable dancers in Dance Dance Revolution Disney Channel Edition.

Bunk'd and Raven's Home characters appear in the crossover special “Raven about Bunk'd“.

Raven appears in "Happy Birthday, Disney Channel!".

Additionally a character dressed as Rayman makes an appearance in Tonic Trouble and Ed appears in jack-in-a-box form in the Rayman: The Animated Series episode "No Parking".
A mosquito from the Rayman series makes a cameo appearance in Beyond Good and Evil.
Rayman's glove can be used as a weapon in Prince of Persia: Warrior Within. The PSVita version of Rayman Legends features an exclusive costume based on Prince of Persia.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are Rayman references.
Rabbids is a spinoff of Rayman.
Rayman makes an appearance in Academy of Champions: Football.
The Eddsworld episodes "Climate Change" and "WTFuture" feature references to Rayman.
A block based on Rayman is playable in Blocks That Matter.
Rayman is parodied in the MAD sketch "Everybody Loves Rayman".
Rayman appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
The Xbox 360 version of Rayman Legends features exclusive costumes based on Splinter Cell.
The PS3/PS4 version of Rayman Legends features exclusive costumes based on Assassin's Creed.
Skin Pack 5 in the Minecraft Xbox 360 and Xbox One Editions features skins based off characters from Rayman.
The comic Plok: The Exploding Man features a reference to Rayman.
A "Rayman Raving Rabbids" board game can be found in Tom Clancy's The Division.
The Uno Rayman DLC for UNO features Rayman characters interacting with the main game.
Rayman is a playable character in Brawlhalla.
Rayman appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; Rayman, Globox and Barbara appear as trophies in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.
Caddy reviews "Rayman Junior" for the PS1.
Grunderbite and Seabreather from Rayman Legends can be unlocked in Hungry Dragon.
Items from Rayman can be found in Growtopia as part of the 2023 UbiWeek event.

Rayman appears as a playable character in the the third DLC pack for Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope. Additionally, the Wii U and Nintendo Switch version of Rayman Legends features exclusive costumes based on Mario & Luigi; there also are minor Mario references in Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
Rayman appears in Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix.
A bot based on Rayman can be found in Astro Bot after an update.
In XDefiant, the Enchanted Forest Map, as well as the game mode "Lum Hunt", are based on the Rayman series.

Red Dead.description: Red Dead is a spiritual successor to Gun.Smoke.

Sheldon plays Red Dead Redemption in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Shiny Trinket Maneuver" and "The D & D Vortex".

In Grand Theft Auto V there is a possibility of a family relationship with John Marston from Red Dead Redemption; the double-action Revolver and Stone Hatchet from Red Dead is also featured in the game as promotion for Red Dead Redemption 2.
A recreation of ManBearPig can be found in Red Dead Redemption 2 and also RDR2 has been referenced a lot in the South Park episode “Time to Get Cereal”.
Red Dead memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".

Red Dwarf.description: A tavern is named "The Red Dwarf" and one of the Thieves Guild leaders is named The Cat.
The Red Dwarf episode "Meltdown" is heavily inspired by Westworld.
The TARDIS from Doctor Who appears in the Red Dwarf episode “Demons & Angels”.
The character Lazarus has the real name Todd Hunter, a reference to Second Officer Frank Todhunter.

A Klingon Bird of Prey is seen in a spaceship graveyard in Red Dwarf "Psirens". In Star Trek, the story "Stone and Anvil" has a hologram character suggest that they wear a large H on their head, and in "Time Lock" the Gemini 12's Time Drive is stored in the Eridian Vault.
A Weyland-Yutani ship from Aliens appears in the Red Dwarf episode “Psirens”.
The names of neighbouring cities can include Rimmer, Lister, Cat's Corner, and Krighton, after the four main characters Of the show.

Grouped together along Route 2 are three Bug Catchers. The two closest together are named Rob and Doug after Red Dwarf's primary writers Rob Grant and Doug Naylor, and the third is named Ed after director and producer Ed Bye.

In Kingdom of Loathing, there are various traffic cone items, all of which quote The Cat from "Last Day": "It's not a good night unless you get a traffic cone!". It was once possible to see a dog's milk asteroid, and an axe wound monster can poke you with a red-hot red dwarf star, which is "smegging hot!"
In Little Britain, Kenny Craig sells the first season of Red Dwarf to a customer.
In Ratchet: Deadlocked, there is a superficial superhero who goes by Ace Hardlight, a reference both to Arnold Rimmer's superficial persona Ace Rimmer and the term "hard-light hologram".
"Tord's Adventure" ends with the music, fonts, stars and scrawl from the Red Dwarf credits. Also Edd is often seen wearing a white shirt which says "Smeg Head" under his hoodie.
Two technicians in an isolated outpost report the UFO using the callsign "Red Dwarf", a reference both to the title of the show and the focal duo.
There are multiple "Everybody's dead, Dave" conversations and a character who plays pool with planets, both references to Lister.
Red Dwarf is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Friendship Contraction".

Far Cry 3's traffic cones are described in your inventory as "The sign of a good night", referencing Cat's sentiment when Lister discovers one in his bed: "Hey! It's not a good night unless you get a traffic cone!"

Lance Corporal Vatslav and Private Kleiner are characteristic homages to Rimmer and Lister, with Vatslav mimicking closely a line from Red Dwarf's first episode by stating "Need I remind you of the penalty for insulting a superior?!" immediately before a dwarf in red enters the scene.
A character resembling Rimmer from Red Dwarf appears in a crowd scene in the story "Hail to the Cat" from Simpsons Comics #87.
Using the TARDIS in a Fantastic Beasts story pack level gives access to an area from Red Dwarf.

In the Madonna Of Sasau quest in the A Woman's Lot DLC, Henry can ask a guard about Inquisitor Jaroslav. The guard will launch into an almost exact copy of the speech used by Kryten when asked about the Inquisitor.

In Marvel's Spider-Man, the logo of the fictional donut brand Frosted Halos bares a striking resemblance to the Red Dwarf logo. Additionally, the use of donuts as halos references Lister's use of a golden donut as part of a holy disguise in "Waiting for God".
The Dead Space remake added a beer brand named 'Red Dwarf'.

Reservoir Dogs.description: According to Word of God (Tarantino), Mr. White (Reservoir Dogs) and Alabama (True Romance) were former partners.

According to Word of God (Tarantino), Vic Vega (Reservoir Dogs) and Vincent Vega (Pulp Fiction) are brothers. Additionally, the Big Kahuna restaurant chain from Pulp Fiction first appeared in Reservoir Dogs.
A Silver Surfer poster can be seen in Reservoir Dogs.
The stage "Duke Royale" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features locations from Reservoir Dogs.
In Conker's Bad Fur Day there is a reference to the film Reservoir Dogs.
The second Fight Klub set features cards based on Reservoir Dogs, including a character card of Mr. Blonde.
A heist based on Reservoir Dogs was added to Payday 2.

The opening to Chainsaw Man features a reference to Reservoir Dogs.

Resident Evil.description: Zombies from Resident Evil appear in Akuma's ending from Pocket Fighter. Chun-Li also cosplays as Jill Valentine in some of her attacks.
The stage "Gates Motel" from Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown features references to Resident Evil.
Having saved data of Resident Evil 2 unlocks the special "Zombie" dragon in Dragonseeds.

Crates in Dino Crisis are marked with Umbrella's logo. One of the costumes found in Resident Evil 3: Nemesis Boutique room includes a costume based on Regina from Dino Crisis. Additionally, a Dino Crisis poster can be found in Resident Evil: Survivor.
In several episodes of Spaced, the characters can be seen playing Resident Evil 2 and making references to the series.

An attraction designed after the Spencer Mansion is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters Cards, including an actor dressed as Chris Redfield and several zombies one can duel with. Several characters also appear as cards in the series.
Gun Survivor, Gun Survivor 2, and Gun Survivor 4 are format crossovers between the two series.

A Darkstalkers poster can be found in Resident Evil: Survivor, the stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several Vampire Hunter: Darkstalkers' Revenge Arcade cabinets and a statue of Victor appears in one map from Resident Evil Resistance.

A Ghosts 'n Goblins poster can be found in Resident Evil: Survivor and Resident Evil 3, while the stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several Makai Mura Arcade cabinets and Umbrella Corps features several decals based on Ghost 'n Goblins.
Resident Evil characters are playable in all games following Marvel vs. Capcom 2.
The Cannon Spike stage "The Unholy Dwelling" is inspired by Resident Evil, including an appearance of Cerberus zombie dogs as enemies.
The first Devil May Cry was originally developed as an entry in the Resident Evil series.

Resident Evil.game: The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy
Resident Evil.description: The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy episode "Brown Evil" features "President Evil", a video game parody of Resident Evil.
Capcom Black Jack features appearances of Claire Redfield from Resident Evil.
Under the Skin features a stage based on Raccoon City from Resident Evil.
Capcom Girl no Mind Puzzle features appearances of Jill Valentine from the Resident Evil series.
The weapon Killer7 from Resident Evil 4 is named after and based on a weapon from Killer7.
Namco × Capcom features Bruce and Fong-Ling from Resident Evil: Dead Aim as playable characters.
"Horror World" from Viewtiful Joe: Double Trouble! features several references to the Resident Evil series, including an appearance of Cerberus zombie dogs as enemies.
A Resident Evil 4 poster can be spotted in the 2006 film Grandma's Boy.
A dog greatly resembling Hewie from Haunting Ground appears in Resident Evil 4.
Resident Pico is a parody of Resident Evil.
There's a Resident Evil reference in the Robot Chicken season 2 episode "Lost for Puppets".
Boxes and banners with the TriCell logo from Resident Evil 5 appear in the 2009 Bionic Commando.
There are several references to Resident Evil in the Smallville season 9 episode "Rabid".
Bayonetta features a reference to Resident Evil 4.

Lost Planet 2 features Albert Wesker from Resident Evil as a selectable character, while "BSAA" is one of the unlockable Nom de Guerres in Lost Planet 2. HUNK appears as a downloadable guest character in Lost Planet 3.
There's a minor reference to Resident Evil in the 8th episode of Panty & Stocking with Garterbelt.
Characters discuss Resident Evil 4 in the Breaking Bad episode: "Thirty-Eight Snub". Breaking Bad is mentioned in Resident Evil: Vendetta.
The name of one trophy/achievement in Dead Island is a reference to Resident Evil.
Jaws is referenced by name in Resident Evil: Revelations.

The Xbox 360 version of Dragon's Dogma included a download code for a Resident Evil 6 demo. The list of generic monickers in Dragon's Dogma features "Barry", "Claire, "Chris", "Jill", "Leon", "Rebecca", "Tyrant" and "Wesker" as possible monickers.
Jill Valentine appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
The "Infection" gun from Borderlands 2 features a minor reference to Resident Evil.
Resident Evil 6 characters appeared in Zombie Cafe as part of several special promotions.

The stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several Senjou no Ookami Arcade cabinets, Billy's pre-order costume for the Resident Evil Zero HD Remaster is a "Wolf Force" uniform from Mercs and a poster referencing Wolf of the Battlefield appears in Resident Evil 3.
The stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several SonSon Arcade cabinets and Umbrella Corps features a decal of Son Son's sprite.
The stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several Star Gladiator Arcade cabinets.

Minna to Biohazard Clan Members and Minna to Biohazard Team Survive are format crossovers between the two series, while Minna to Capcom All Stars and Street Fighter × All Capcom feature characters from the Resident Evil series.

A number of creatures from Resident Evil appear in Onimusha Soul as part of a "Capcom Title Collaboration" limited event quest, while Jill, Claire and Ada appear as part of the "Capcom Heroines" limited event.
Characters from Left 4 Dead 2 are playable in Resident Evil 6 as DLC. Enemies from Resident Evil 6 are seen in Left 4 Dead 2 as DLC.
The name of one trophy in The Last of Us is a reference to Resident Evil.
The Angry Video Game Nerd plays the Game.Com version of Resident Evil 2 in the episode "Tiger Electronic Games".

As part of a crossover collaboration, playing Minna to Biohazard Team Survive unlocks a card of Masamune Date in Sengoku BASARA Card Heroes Matsuri, while playing the latter unlocks cards of Leon Kennedy and Claire Redfield in the former; additionally Sengoku BASARA 4 Sumeragi features a DLC costume pack based on characters from Resident Evil.

Several Resident Evil characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom and also appear in Street Fighter Battle Combination; additionally a Street Fighter poster can be found in Resident Evil Survivor, the HD version of Resident Evil 0 features a costume based on Cody from the Street Fighter series and costumes of Resident Evil characters are DLC in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.
The name of one trophy/achievement in the 2014 Strider references Resident Evil.
In "Fun Dead" from Eddsworld, the Umbrella Corporation from Resident Evil is seen under the "Eggs" poster.
Hyperdevotion Noire: Goddess Black Heart features a character called Vio, that parodies the Resident Evil series.

Stores in Dead Rising named "Jill's Sandwiches" and "Chris' Fine Foods" references Chris and Jill from Resident Evil, while weapons and the joke character Tofu from Resident Evil 2 appear as items in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha; Dead Rising 4 features several art books in its backgrounds, while its update Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package features a Jill Valentine costume in "Capcom Heroes" mode, along with her actual moves. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster features costumes based on Chris Redfield, Leon S. Kennedy, a Licker, Nemesis, a Chainsaw Villager and Ashley Graham from the Resident Evil series.

Final Fantasy IX features a reference to Resident Evil 2, while Minna to Biohazard Clan Master features costumes from Final Fantasy Brigade Break the Seal in a special collaboration event, as well as a shared event between both games which gift Final Fantasy character cards.
The Mansion used by Specimen 12 in Spooky's Jump Scare Mansion is inspired by Resident Evil.
There's a Resident Evil 4 poster in the Clarence episode "Belson's Sleepover".

MonHun Big Game Hunting Quest features characters and a story event from Resident Evil Revelations 2 as part of a special collaboration, while Monster Hunter Explore features two collaborations including costumes of a zombie, Jill, Rebecca and Tyrant as well as weapons and monsters designed after the Resident Evil HD Remaster.
Umbrella Corps features a decal of the Yashichi, and a TV brand in Resident Evil 6 is named after the Yashichi enemy from Vulgus.
Umbrella Corps features two decals of airships from the 194X series, while a poster referencing 1942 appears in Resident Evil 3.
Umbrella Corps features a decal of Mobi-chan from Side Arms: Hyper Dyne.
Breath of Fire III enemies Yawn (Foul Weed in English) and Plant 42 are named after monsters in Resident Evil, while Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Chris, Jill, HUNK and Claire.
Several Resident Evil characters and monsters are featured in Dragon Poker as part of two collaboration events.
The covers to Resident Evil: Code Veronica and Resident Evil: Revelations 2 can be seen in the Black Mirror episode: "Playtest".
Resident Evil is mentioned in Bear With Me.
Jill Valentine from Resident Evil 5 and Ada Wong from Resident Evil 6 are playable characters in Puzzle Fighter.
Jill Valentine has been a subject for DBX.
Leon Kennedy has been a subject for Death Battle!
A collaboration event with the Resident Evil 2 remake is included with Update 0.11.0 of PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds Mobile, featuring costume sets, weapons and enemies from the game.
Scott the Woz once did a review on Resident Evil 4.
Resident Evil is parodied in multiple Perfect Cell Vs episodes.
TEPPEN features characters from the Resident Evil series.

Resident Evil spirits are featured in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; additionally the Nintendo Switch versions of Resident Evil Revelations and Revelations 2 feature compatibility with the Mega Man and Ryu amiibo from the Super Smash Bros. series.

There is a reference to Dr. Wily and Dr. Light in the Resident Evil 3 remake, plus a set of toys based on "Bad Box Art" Mega Man; while there are many small references to Resident Evil in Mega Man games.
A movie poster referencing Captain Commando appears in Resident Evil 3.
A movie poster referencing Terminator appears in Resident Evil 3.
A movie poster referencing Alien appears in Resident Evil 3.
Korvo mentions Resident Evil in the Solar Opposites episode “ The Lavatic Reactor”.
In Neon Abyss, the B-Virus Item is a reference to the T-Virus from Resident Evil.
Characters from Resident Evil appear in LifeAfter during a collaboration event.
Weapons and costumes based on Resident Evil appear in The Division 2.
Outfits based on Jill Valentine and Leon S. Kennedy appear in Rainbow Six: Siege.
Resident Evil is parodied in multiple Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episodes.
Characters from Resident Evil appear as DLC for Dead By Daylight.
Dead Estate features a skin for Jules that resembles Ashley Graham from Resident Evil 4.
Chris Redfield, Jill Valentine, Leon S. Kennedy, Claire Redfield and Grace Ashcroft from Resident Evil appear in Fortnite.
You can find a dog tag for a man named Chris Bluefield in Dying Light 2.
Resident Evil is mentioned in Chapter 66 of Sakamoto Days.
Lady Dimitrescu's hat appears in the shop.
A poster of a parody of Resident Evil can be found in The Owl House episode “Thanks to Them”.
Resident Evil 2 is mentioned in High on Life
Characters from Higemaru appear as dummy targets in the Shooting Range mini-game from Resident Evil 4.
"Something About Resident Evil 4 Remake" is a parody of Resident Evil 4.
Characters from Resident Evil appear in a special collab with State of Survival.
Resident Evil memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Skibidi Nemesis is based on Nemesis from Resident Evil. Additionally, the Mutated Fleshling Skibidi Toilet is inspired by the "Licker".
Three bots that resemble characters from Resident Evil appear in Astro's Playroom. Costumes based on various characters from Resident Evil can be found in Astro Bot.
Jill Valentine, Ada Wong, and Claire Redfield from Resident Evil appear in Goddess of Victory: NIKKE as part of a collaboration event.

The Hybird outfit is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet.
Nathan Hale and a Chimera Hybrid are downloadable in Uncharted 2.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features an arena based on Resistance. The Satan Chimera also appears in one of the other arenas.

Where?" including characters from the WarioWare series; characters from Rhythm Paradise appear in WarioWare: Smooth Moves and Game & Wario.

Rhythm Knights is a playable character in Ortheo's Interdimensional Jam Session.

Rick and Morty characters are playable in Move or Die.

Riddle School.description: Phil from Riddle School is featured as a playable character.
Characters from Riddle School appear in the One Night at Flumpty's series.

Ridge Racer.description: Gameplay scenes from Galaxian can be seen on screen in Ridge Racer, and the game also features a "Team Gaplus", while the PlayStation version also features a minigame version of Galaxian; a car called "Galaxian Paradise" is available in Ridge Racer 64 and Ridge Racer DS. A nitrous brand called "Galaxian" is featured in Ridge Racer 7, specializing in nitrous recharge rates.

One of the enemy cars in Ridge Racer features Mappy images, "Mappy" is a car brand in later games in the series, R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 features the "Micro Mouse Mappy" team and a Mappy trophy, Ridge Racer 3D sport emblems of Mappy, Goro and Mewkie and Ridge Racer Accelerated features a cup named after Mappy.
"Sky Kid" is a car brand first seen in Ridge Racer for PlayStation, while enemy cars in Ridge Racer 3D sport emblems of Baron and Max from Sky Kid.
"Time Crisis" ads are visible in race tracks in Rage Racer.

Ace Combat 2 features the sister of Reiko Nagase as a selectable pilot, and she also returns in later episodes, while organizations from Ace Combat 3 appear as sponsors in Ridge Racer V and Ridge Racer 6; there also are other minor references between the two series.
"Dragon Buster" is a car brand first seen in Rave Racer, and billboards of the game can be seen in several of the series' race tracks, Ridge Racer 3D features emblems based on Clovis.
"Phelios" is a car brand first seen in Rave Racer.
"Dragon Spirit" is a car brand first seen in Rave Racer; there are also ads visible on the race tracks.
"Toy Pop" is a car brand first seen in Rave Racer; there are also ads visible on the race tracks.
"Wonder Momo" is a car brand first seen in Rave Racer.

Reiko Nagase from Ridge Racer appear as a guest player in Anna Kournikova's Smash Court Tennis, while Ai Fukami from Ridge Racer V appears in Smash Court 3 and an artwork of Reiko Nagase appears as part of an easter egg in the training mode of Anna Kournikova's Smash Court Tennis.
The race course "Phantomile" from R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 is named after one of the locations in Klonoa, and it features billboards of the series; one of the game's trophies is based on Klonoa.
The ghost Blinky from Pac-Man appears as an unlockable "car" in Ridge Racer 64, while Reiko Nagase is selectable in Pac-Man Fever
Pooka is a selectable "car" in Ridge Racer 64; additionally, Ridge Racer features a "Team Dig Dug" while R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 features a reference to Dig Dug.
A costume of Reiko Nagase from Ridge Racer is featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with her actual techniques.
Taiko no Tatsujin 6 and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Ridge Racer series.
Ridge Racer DS features some Mario-themed bonus cars.

Ridge Racers, Ridge Racers 2 and Ridge Racer 3D features the Rally-X car as a selectable car; additionally, Ridge Racer features a "Team Rally-X", while Ridge Racers features a minigame version of Rally-X as loading screen.
Heihachi Mishima makes a guest appearance as a DJ in Ridge Racer 6; the Ridge Racer series also features other minor references to the Tekken series.
QuickSpot features one puzzle based on Ridge Racer.

Pac-Man drives a modified Andor Genesis from Xevious in Ridge Racer 7 and a scaled-down Solvalou in Ridge Racer 3D, the Solvalou and Baracuda enemies can be seen flying by in the Mist Falls race track and the player can play a minigame of Xevious during loading screens. There are other minor references in several Ridge Racer games.
Enemy cars in Ridge Racer 3D sport emblems of Valkyrie, Sandra and Sabine; R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 has cups named after Valkyrie and Sandra and a Valkyrie trophy.
Music and cars based on THE iDOLM@STER can be obtained in Ridge Racer for the PlayStation Vita.
The Hornet is an add-on in Ridge Racer for the PlayStation Vita.
Music from Ridge Racer was added to maimai in the maimai GreeN PLUS version.
A human version of Ridge Racer appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.
Bots can be found playing a game similar to Ridge Racer called "Bot Racer" in Astro's Playroom. A costume based on Reiko Nagase from Ridge Racer can be found in Astro Bot.

A weapon similar to Doom's BFG can be found as an equipment called the Preon Accumulator in Risk of Rain 2.

Ristar.description: Ristar makes cameo appearances in the 50th issue of the Archie Sonic the Hedgehog comic, in Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing and in Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing Transformed.

Picross S Genesis & Master System Edition includes puzzles based off Ristar.

Rival Schools.description: Tessa dress as Kyouko Minazuki from Rival Schools in one of her Hypers from Pocket Fighter.

Sakura from Street Fighter is selectable in Rival Schools, Batsu and Akira are selectable in Street Fighter Online: Mouse Generation and many Rival Schools characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; Hinata and Tiffany make a background cameo in Street Fighter V, with Akira becoming a playable character in Season 5. Many characters are also recurring in the Street Fighter UDON comic book series.
There's a Dino Crisis ad in the background screen of the "Drive-In Theater" stage from Shiritsu Justice Gakuen: Nekketsu Seisyun Nikki 2.
There's a Power Stone 2 ad visible in the background of the "Gorin Dome" stage from Project Justice.

Various Rival Schools characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while Kyosuke Kagami is selectable in Capcom vs SNK 2: Mark of the Millenium 2001;. There's also a Capcom vs. SNK ad visible in the background of the "Gorin Dome" stage from Project Justice.
A rescuable Reploid in Mega Man X6 is named after Batsu from Rival Schools.
Capcom Black Jack features appearances of Kyoko Minazuki from Rival Schools.
Capcom Girl no Mind Puzzle features appearances of Hinata from the Rival Schools series.
Characters from Rival Schools make cameo appearances in Capcom Fighting Evolution.
Kyoko and Hideo from Rival Schools are selectable in Namco × Capcom.
Batsu is selectable in Tatsunoko vs. Capcom.
Characters from Rival Schools make cameo appearances in Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3.
The list of generic monickers in Dragon's Dogma features "Hideo", "Kyouko", "Momo", "Roy" and "Kyousuke" as possible monickers, while Dragon's Dogma Online features costumes of Batsu and Hinata.
Minna to Capcom All Stars and Street Fighter × All Capcom feature characters from Rival Schools.
Hinata and Akira from Rival Schools appear in Onimusha Soul as part of the "Capcom Heroines" limited event.
Natsu and Tiffany are featured in Otoranger.

Shoma from Rival Schools is featured as a costume for Chuck Greene in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha, along with his actual moves; Dead Rising 4 features Rival Schools Arcade cabinets, art books and banners in its backgrounds.
The "Blanka Delgado" skin from Fortnite is based on Boman Delgado from Rival Schools.
Project Justice is included in Capcom Fighting Collection 2.

Rivals of Aether.description: Zetterburn from Rivals of Aether makes a cameo appearance in River City Ransom: Underground.

Rivals of Aether takes heavy inspiration from Super Smash Bros. Melee, and borrows many of the techniques from said game. One of the characters in Rivals of Aether, Zetterburn, even has a skin that "includes" Fox's shine move.
Ori and Sein from Ori and the Blind Forest are playable in Rivals of Aether, while the Spirit Tree from Ori and the Blind Forest appears as a stage.
Ragnir is an Alternate Skin for Maypul in Rivals of Aether, while Ranno appears as a skin for Wu Shang in Brawlhalla.
Orcane is a playable character in Indie Pogo.
Shovel Knight is a downloadable fighter in Rivals of Aether.
An arcade cabinet for Rivals of Aether can be found in Katana Zero.
Forsburn from Lovers of Aether appears in an official mod for Monster Prom.
Sylvanos from Rivals of Aether appears as a playable character in Russian Subway Dogs.
An outfit based on Zetterburn from Rivals of Aether can be worn in Mago.
Orcane is a playable character in Fraymakers. Additionally, Merchant Port appears as a stage, with Kragg as an assist.
Maypul makes an appearance as a fighter in Duelist of Eden.
A Forsburn costume can be found in Another Crab's Treasure.
Cosmetics based on Rivals of Aether appear in Spiritfall as part of an update.
A stage based on Rock Wall from Rivals of Aether II is planned to appear in Animation VERSUS.
Ranno from Rivals of Aether will appear as a playable character in Samurai Gunn 2.

River City Ransom.description: All entries in the River City Ransom series are reworkings of games from the Kunio-kun series, and as such, share characters and other elements.
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews River City Ransom during Pat the NES Punk's 2nd NES Marathon.

Abobo has appeared as an enemy in River City: Tokyo Rumble, River City Ransom: Underground and River City Girls, and several other characters have appeared together with him as enemies, shopkeepers or story NPCs, with Miriam becoming playable in River City Girls 2. The characters Ryuji, Ryuichi, Jimmy and Murdov from Kunio-Kun are based on Billy Lee, Jimmy Lee and Abobo respectively. There are other minor references between the two series.
The "High School Video Game" features a level based on River City Ransom.
Me from Dad 'n Me appears as a boss in River City Ransom: Underground.
Zetterburn from Rivals of Aether makes a cameo appearance in River City Ransom: Underground.
The Red and Green Knights from Castle Crashers make a cameo appearance in River City Ransom: Underground.
The Drifter from Hyper Light Drifter makes a cameo appearance in River City Ransom: Underground.
Characters from Hotline Miami makes cameo appearances in River City Ransom: Undergound.
Several characters in River City Ransom: Underground have moves loosely based on characters from the Street Fighter series.
Paul from River City Ransom: Underground bears a resemblance to Little Mac from Punch-Out!!.
A billboard in Guacamelee! 2 reads "Rivera City Ransom" in a spoof of the River City Ransom logo.
River City Ransom can be seen in Animation vs. Super Mario Bros.
River City spirits are featured in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Characters from River City Ransom are playable in Code Shifter.
Characters from River City Ransom appear in The Battle Cats as part of a collaboration.
Kunio and Riki from River City Ransom appear as DLC guest characters in Mighty Fight Federation.
Sol Badguy and Jam Kuradoberi from Guilty Gear appear as secret assist characters in River City Girls 2.

Riverbond.description: Lover Mu from Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime appears as a skin in Riverbond.

Raz Aquato from Psychonauts appears as a skin in Riverbond.
Shovel Knight appears as a skin in Riverbond.
Bullet Kin from Enter the Gungeon appears as a skin in Riverbond.
Spelunky Guy appears as a skin in Riverbond.

The Road Rovers theme briefly plays as BGM in the Histeria! episode "Big Fat Baby Theatre".
The Teen Titans Go! episode: "Huggbees" features a Road Rovers film reel.

Road Warriors.description: Cluck makes a cameo in Indie Pogo.

RoadBlasters (Atari).description: RoadBlasters is featured in Arcade's Greatest Hits: The Atari Collection 2 and Midway's Greatest Arcade Hits
RoadBlasters is included in Midway Arcade Treasures.
In Wreck-It Ralph, the character Turbo visits the game RoadBlasters.
RoadBlasters is playable in Lego Dimensions.

Robeats!.description: RoBeats! was released as a Roblox experience and the player's Roblox Avatar can be used in it. DJ Matsune Hiku has an official Roblox toy.
DJ Matsune Hiku is based upon Hatsune Miku.
Before Friday Night Funkin' had its surge in popularity, RoBeats! had added 6 songs from the game as the second featured artist in collaboration with Kawai Sprite.
RoBeats! partnered with Ubisoft to add 12 original soundtracks from the game in order to promote the release of Just Dance 2022.
The Robeats Crossover was an event that was an official collaboration between Robeats! and Tower Heroes.
Make a Cake Update was an event that was an official collaboration between Make a Cake! and Robeats!.

Robin Hood (Disney).description: Many characters from Robin Hood make an appearance in Mickey's Christmas Carol and the House of Mouse series.
A costume of Robin Hood is playable in Disney Universe.
Dylan dresses up as Little John is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Disneyland".
Rhino Guards from Robin Hood are enemies in Disney Infinity.
Characters from Robin Hood appeared in Towers of Saviors during a special collaboration.
Disney Magic Kingdoms features characters from Disney's Peter Pan.
Robin Hood is parodied in Les Kassos.
Characters from Robin Hood appear in Disney Heroes: Battle Mode
Robin Hood has a son in the Descendants book Escape from the Isle of the Lost.
Robin and the Sheriff from Robin Hood are fighters in Disney Sorcerer's Arena.
The Disney series of Lego Minifigures includes Robin Hood and Prince John.
Cards based on Robin Hood appear in Lorcana.
Robin Hood appears in the credits for Wish.
There is a puzzle in Disney Solitare that shows a scene from Robin Hood.

Roblox.description: The "oof" sound which originally came from Messiah is used as a death sound effect in Roblox until they took it down.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, there was a Zeke and Luther-themed skate park and some skateboards.
In multiple limited-time events in Roblox, players could work for the Autobots or the Deceptions and even play as characters from Transformers.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could enter the world of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, play as the characters, and get items from the series.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get The Three Stooges-themed gear and play as characters from the series.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could enter the world of Lab Rats and get items from the series.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could enter the world of Battleship and get Battleship-themed items.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could spawn Crash from Crash & Bernstein.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get Percy Jackson-themed gear and weapons.
Roblox sponsored Adventure Time with clothing and accessories.
Roblox promoted How to Train Your Dragon with gear and characters from the series.
The Roblox Disney XD Mystery Morphing Mask included Pac-Man.
The Roblox Disney XD Mystery Morphing Mask included Wander.
The Roblox Disney XD Mystery Morphing Mask included Perry.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get a ruby from The 7D.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could enter the world of The Boxtrolls and get The Boxtrolls-themed gear.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could use weapons from Kirby Buckets.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get Night at the Museum-themed items, such as Larry's flashlight.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get Big Hero 6-themed gear and spawn Baymax.

Roblox sponsored SpongeBob with clothing and accessories; The Roblox gear Slime Potion is modeled after SpongeBob's pineapple. Additionally, SpongeBob appears in TMNT Battle Tycoon for a limited-time event. SpongeBob Simulator was released as a Roblox experience and the player's Roblox Avatar can be used in it.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could meet Future-Worm! characters.

In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get Dipper's hat. The description says that this was actually borrowed from Dipper himself.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get Teen Titans-themed gear and spawn Beast Boy as a companion.
In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could use weapons and items from Minions.

In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get We Bare Bears-themed gear, spawn the bears, and use Panda's cellphone.

In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get Hotel Transylvania-themed gear and spawn characters from the series.

In a limited-time event in Roblox, players could get items with the logo of The Good Dinosaur.

Mario enters a parody version of the world of Baldi's Basics in Education and Learning in "If Mario was in... Baldi's Basics".

Mario enters a parody version of the world of Scooby-Doo in "Scooby Mario, Where'd You Go!".
