SNK Heroines.description: Athena from Psycho Soldier is a playable character in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy.

Kula Diamond, Leona, Shermie, Sylvie Paula Paula, Zarina, Mian, and Luong from The King of Fighters are playable characters in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy, while Kukri appears as a boss. Female Terry from SNK Heroines appears in The King of Fighters '98 Ultimate Match Online.
Mai Shiranui and a female version of Terry Bogard from Fatal Fury are playable characters in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy.
Yuri Sakazaki from Art of Fighting is a playable character in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy.
Nakoruru from Samurai Shodown is a playable character in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy.
Thief Arthur from Million Arthur is a DLC character in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy.
A female version of Skullomania from Fighting Layer is a DLC character in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy.
Jeanne D'Arc from World Heroes is a DLC character in SNK Heroines: Tag Team Frenzy.

SNK vs. Capcom.description: Sylphie from Forgotten Worlds appears as a shop owner in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters' Clash, the "Lost World" store is based off the game and has enemies and weapons in display; and the character Foh/Foru Gotton from SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters Clash and Card Fighters 2 is named after the series.

An attraction designed after the Spencer Mansion is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters Cards, including an actor dressed as Chris Redfield and several zombies one can duel with. Several characters also appear as cards in the series.
The P-38 Lightning biplane from 194X is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters' Clash.
Jin Saotome, Blodia, Mary Miyabe and Devilot from Cyberbots are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Various Captain Commando characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Ryu, Nina and Momo from Breath of Fire are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Various Strider characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Super Joe from Commando is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Pure & Fur are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while the character Haruna Hatena from SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 is named after the series.
Michelle Heart from Legendary Wings appears as a card in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.

Various Quiz Nanairo Dreams characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while the character Nanako Nijiiro from SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 is designed after Momoko from Quiz Nanairo Dreams.
Characters from Buriki One are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Characters from Robo Army are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.
Various Street Fighter characters are selectable in all SNK vs. Capcom games; Violent Ken from SNK vs. Capcom: SVC Chaos is a selectable character in Ultra Street Fighter II: The Final Challengers.
Various Darkstalkers characters are selectable in all SNK vs. Capcom games.

Various Star Gladiator characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games; while Gore Gajah and June Lin Milliam make cameo appearances in SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millenium and Capcom vs. SNK 2 respectively.
Various The King of Fighters characters are selectable in all SNK vs. Capcom games.
Various Fatal Fury characters are selectable in all SNK vs. Capcom games.
Various Art of Fighting characters are selectable in all SNK vs. Capcom games.
Athena Asamiya from Psycho Soldier is selectable in SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millenium and Capcom vs. SNK 2.
Various Samurai Shodown characters are selectable in all SNK vs. Capcom games.

Various The Last Blade characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while Akari Ichijou and Hibiki Takane are selectable in SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millenium and Capcom vs. SNK 2 respectively.

Various Ghosts 'n Goblins characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games; the mini-game "Ghost Trick" in SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millenium is based on Ghosts 'n Goblins and features Arthur as its playable character, and a Red Arremer is a boss character in SVC Chaos.

Various Metal Slug characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games; the mini-game "Target 9" in SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millenium is based on Metal Slug and features Marco Rossi and Fio as playable characters, and a Mars People is a boss character in SVC Chaos.

Various Rival Schools characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while Kyosuke Kagami is selectable in Capcom vs SNK 2: Mark of the Millenium 2001; There's also a Capcom vs. SNK ad visible in the background of the "Gorin Dome" stage from Project Justice.

Various Final Fight characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while Rolento and Maki are selectable in Capcom vs SNK 2: Mark of the Millenium 2001 and the "Slum Alleyway" theme can be unlocked in Capcom vs. SNK Millenium Fight 2000.
Various Power Stone characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while Edward Falcon and Rouge make a cameo appearance in Capcom vs. SNK 2: Mark of the Millenium 2001.
Ralf and Clark from Ikari Warriors are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, and make a cameo appearance in Capcom vs. SNK 2: Mark of the Millenium 2001.

Various Red Earth characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while Mai-Ling makes a cameo appearance in Capcom vs. SNK 2: Mark of the Millenium 2001 and Tessa is selectable in SVC Chaos.
Lou and Siva from Three Wonders are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2.
Ruby Heart, Sonson and Amingo appear as cards in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 and SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Sammanosuke and Kaede from Onimusha appear in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2.
Regina from Dino Crisis is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 and SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Characters from Tech Romancer are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 and SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Sonson and Tonton from SonSon are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2.
The character Yashichi Fuwa from SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 is named after the Yashichi from Vulgus.
The character Asoh Shuuko from SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 is named after the Japanese name of the game Alpha Mission.
Various Mega Man characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, while Zero is selectable in SVC Chaos.
Athena is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games, and can be fought as a boss character in SVC Chaos.
Characters from Devil May Cry are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS features Phoenix Wright, Mia Fey, Miles Edgeworth and Franziska von Karma as character cards.
Fiona Belli from Haunting Grounds is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Cyber Blue and Master Program from Battle Circuit are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
The main character from Trojan is featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Character from World Heroes are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Characters from Aggressors of Dark Kombat are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Characters from Ninja Commando are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Yuki and Ai from Neo Geo Battle Coliseum are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters DS.
Capcom vs. SNK: Millennium Fight 2000 and Capcom vs. SNK 2: Mark of the Millennium 2001 are included in Capcom Fighting Collection 2.

SSX.description: NBA Street features two characters from SSX in "Team BIG", while Stretch from NBA Street is unlockable in SSX 3.
In The Sims 2, sims can play SSX3; UNDIRECT: characters from SSX 3 meet characters from The Urbz and The Sims 2 in the Video Mods video "Let's Get It Started".
Characters from SSX 3 appear in the Video Mods original video "Stand and Choose"; they also star in the "Gossip Folks" and "Let's Get It Started" videos.
Mario, Luigi and Peach are unlockable in the GameCube version of SSX on Tour.
DJ Atomika from SSX appears as the commentator in Burnout Paradise.
NBA Jam: On Fire Edition features Elise, Kaori and Mac from SSX as selectable characters.

SUPERHOT.description: The protagonist from Superhot is a playable character in Cook, Serve, Delicious!.
Travis can wear a SUPERHOT t-shirt in Travis Strikes Again: No More Heroes.
One of the worlds of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to SUPERHOT.
An ad of "SUPERCOLD" pops up in There Is No Game: Wrong Dimension, a parody of SUPERHOT.

SWAT Kats.description: Several elements from SWAT Kats appear in ATHF, such as several backgrounds, the Pastimer's Time Vortex, and an Enforcer Chopper.
The episode "Say Uncle" features a list of names of Cartoon Network characters. One of those names is SWAT Kats.
The episode "Say Uncle" features a list of names of Cartoon Network characters. One of those names is SWAT Kats.
SWAT Kats is mentioned in the Craig of the Creek episode "Kelsey the Elder".

SaGa.description: Makai Toushi SaGa features enemies from Final Fantasy and the first three SaGa games were released as the Final Fantasy Legend series outside Japan; Final Fantasy Legends: Toki no Suishou features characters from Romancing SaGa 2 as summons, while Adel from Imperial SaGa, and various characters from Romancing Saga 3 appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations; Final Fantasy Record Keeper held crossover events exclusively in Japan with Emperors SaGa, Romancing SaGa 2, and SaGa Scarlet Grace; additionally Unlimited SaGa features a demo version of Final Fantasy X and a Chocobo Card is present, but unused, in the code for Romancing Saga 3, while Theatrhythm Final Fantasy Curtain Call features downloadable tracks from the SaGa series.
The enemy "Fly Man" in The Final Fantasy Legend is possibly based off The Fly.
The enemy "Condorman" in Makai Toushi SaGa is possibly based off Condorman.
The enemies "Rat Man" and Cat Girl in Makai Toushi SaGa are possibly based off GeGeGe no Kitarō.
Makai Toushi SaGa uses some elements from Dungeons & Dragons.
Makai Toushi SaGa features an NPC class named Mobile Suit, referencing Mobile Suit Gundam.
Captain Kirk is mentioned in SaGa Frontier.
Music from SaGa is present in Theatrhythm Final Fantasy: Curtain Call and Theatrhythm Final Bar Line.
Dragon's Dogma Online features armor sets and weapons from Imperial SaGa as part of a special collaboration.
Monster Hunter Frontier Z and Monster Hunter Explore feature characters, weapons and a story event from Imperial SaGa as part of special collaborations.
Characters and weapons from SaGa Emerald Beyond appear in Vampire Survivors as part of the Emerald Diorama DLC.

Sabreman.description: The character Sabrewulf from the Killer Instinct series is based on the Wulf from the Sabreman series.
A frozen Sabreman clutching the Wulf Amulet makes an appearance in Banjo-Tooie.
Sabre Wulf's head appear in Cranky Kong's house in the Game Boy Advance version of Donkey Kong Country.
The Sabre Wulf amulet makes an appearance in Viva Piñata.
A team consisting of characters from games by Rare including Sabreman appears in #IDARB.
Rare Replay includes Sabre Wulf, Underwurlde and Knight Lore as playable games.

Sabrina the Teenage Witch.description: Archie and Sabrina crossover with each other many times.
Groovie Goolies is a spin-off of Sabrina the Teenage Witch.
Donkey Kong interviews Salem in an episode of Donkey Kong Planet.
Sabrina appears in the Clueless episode "Mr. Wright".
Sabrina appears in the Boy Meets World episode "The Witches of Pennbrook" and Salem appears in the Boy Meets World episode "No Guts, No Cory".
Josie and the Pussycats appear in Sabrina the Teenage Witch (2nd series) #17.
The 28th issue of Sabrina the Teenage Witch guest stars Sonic the Hedgehog. That story was later published in Sonic Super Special issue 10.
The episodes “Rumor Mill” and “The Wild, Wild Witch” feature several references to The Godfather.
In the Sabrina the Teenage Witch episode "Sabrina Unplugged", Sabrina interacts with Shaggy and Scooby Doo after being transported into a computer.
Potsie from Happy Days makes a cameo in the Sabrina the Teenage Witch episode Sabrina in Wonderland.
There was a single page crossover story between Hellboy and Chilling Adventures of Sabrina entitled Sabrina Meets Hellboy.
Caddy reviews Sabrina the Teenage Witch for the PS1.
Sabrina the Teenage Witch is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Where the Road Goes".
Clue: Chilling Adventures of Sabrina is a format crossover between the two series.
There is official crossover art featuring Michael Myers from Halloween and Sabrina the Teenage Witch.

Sailor Moon.description: Sailor Moon and Chibi Moon are playable characters in Panic in Nakayoshi World
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Sailor Moon.
In the game you can find a woman looking like Sailor Moon in a bed.
Sonic Super Special issue 8 features a parody of Sailor Moon.
Taiko no Tatsujin 3 and Taiko no Tatsujin: Waku Waku anime Matsuri feature a music track from Sailor Moon.
Sailor Moon is mentioned in Core

Rohan mentions he used to own Sailor Moon figures in Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan - Episode 2: Mutsu-kabe Hill.
In certain versions of Punch-Out!! Wii, the manga Piston Hondo reads is Sailor Moon.
Sailor Moon is parodied in the MAD sketch "Grey's in Anime".
In Fionna and Cake, Fionna's ball gown is a carbon-copy of Princess Serenity's gown from Sailor Moon.
Characters from Sailor Moon make a guest appearance in Girls RPG: Cinderella Life.
Sailor Moon is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episodes “The Stag Convergence” and the “The Gorilla Dissolution”.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews Sailor Moon.
There's a dialogue reference to Sailor Moon in Chapter 68 of The Seven Deadly Sins manga.
Alluka Zoldyck is seen playing with Sailor Moon and Tuxedo Mask dolls in Episode 138 of the 2011 Hunter × Hunter anime.
A Sailor Moon comic book is visible at the end of the Steven Universe episode "House Guest".
Characters from Sailor Moon appeared in LINE Pokopang during a collaboration event.
A doll that looks similar to Luna from Sailor Moon can be seen in the Bee and PuppyCat episode "Beach".
Princess uses a dialogue reference to Sailor Moon in the episode Princess is Better Than You.
Ell references Sailor Moon in "Mirror Mirror".
Sailor Spoon is a spoof on Sailor Moon.
A background pony is dressed up as Sailor Moon in the MLPFIM episode "Scare Master".
There's a parody of the transformation sequence from Sailor Moon in episode 8 of the One-Punch Man anime.

Sailor Moon.game: Star vs. the Forces of Evil
Sailor Moon.description: Mina Loveberry from Star vs. the Forces of Evil is a parody of Sailor Moon.
Sailor Moon posters are shown in the Class episode "For Tonight We Might Die”.

Monster Hunter XX features a downloadable Palico costume based on Luna from Sailor Moon, as well as the Cutie Moon Rod as a weapon; a Felyne is also shown transforming the same way as Sailor Moon in the trailer for the DLC.
Bennett The Sage reviews “Sailor Moon R: The Movie”.
Chibiusa's hair appears in the shop.
Monopoly: Sailor Moon Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
Characters from  from the Sailor Moon series appeared in Puyo Puyo!! Quest during collaboration events.
Sailor Moon appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #65.
Music from Sailor Moon can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix.
Starlight Blue is a parody of Sailor Moon.
Characters from Sailor Moon appeared in Monster Strike during a special collaboration.
Sailor Galaxia has been a subject for Death Battle!.
Sailor Moon is mentioned in Ready Player Two.
Sailor Moon Eternal characters appear in LINE Bubble 2 as part of a collaboration event.
Sailor Mercury has been a subject for DBX.

In the episode Face of the Town, there’s a transformation sequence that’s similar to Sailor Moon, with Huckleberry Hound; When Yogi Bear checks Augie Doggie’s mouth during her checkup in the episode Catanooga Cheese Explosion, she is somewhat saying Ahhh to the tune of Watashitachi Ni Naritakute from Sailor Moon SuperS, the fourth season of the Sailor Moon anime series. This is in honor of Sailor Moon Eternal, which has elements that are based off this season.
A Fan Con attendee dressed as Sailor Moon can be seen in Rescue Rangers (2022).
Bangalore's Epic Soldier of Justice skin from the Saviors "Gaiden Themed Event" is loosely based on Sailor Moon.
Sailor Moon is mentioned in the Rick and Morty episode: "Final DeSmithnation".
Characters from Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon appeared in Towers of Saviors during a special collaboration.
Sailor Moon is parodied in the MeatCanyon episode "youtube is killing me...".
Characters from Sailor Moon appeared in Arena of Valor as part of a special collaboration.

Saint Seiya.description: Pegasus is a playable character in the series.
The technique "Seven Senses" (Celerity in English) from Breath of Fire III and IV references Saint Seiya.
Pop'n Music Animelo, Pop'n Music Animelo 2 and Pop'n Music 10 feature tracks from Saint Seiya.
Characters with Shiryu and Seiya's likeness make a brief appearance in Episode 54 of the Yu-Gi-Oh! anime.
Chapter 98 of the Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo manga features a parody of Saint Seiya. The scene is later adapted in Episode 38 of the anime.
A track from Saint Seiya appears in Karaoke Revolution: Anime Song Collection.
There is a reference to Saint Seiya in Episode 44 of the Gintama anime.
Mao's "Shine Beam" from Disgaea 3 and Disgaea 4 is based off Leo Aiolia's "Lightning Plasma" from Saint Seiya.
Taiko no Tatsujin (C/N: KATSU-DON) and later games in the series feature a music track from Saint Seiya.
A Saint Seiya figurine appears in Episode 26 of Smile Pretty Cure!.
The Duelist's weapon "Scarlet Needle" from Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag is a reference to Scorpio Milo from Saint Seiya.
As part of special collaboration events, Puzzle & Dragons featured a dungeon with creatures from Saint Seiya.
Episode 11 of the Assassination Classroom anime features a visual allusion to Andromeda Shun and Phoenix Ikki of Saint Seiya.
Episode 68 of Yo-Kai Watch features a reference to Saint Seiya.
Dragon Shiryū's shield appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #48. Pegasus Seiya appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #68.
Saint Seiya is parodied in Les Kassos.
There is a title achievement called "Gold Saint".
Characters from Saint Seiya appeared in Towers of Saviors during a special collaboration.
Characters from Saint Seiya appeared in Puyo Puyo!! Quest during a collaboration event.
Characters from Saint Seiya appear in Lords Mobile during a collaboration event.
Symphogear has a collaboration event with Saint Seiya.
Monopoly: Saint Seiya is a format crossover between the two series.
Characters from Saint Seiya: Awakening appeared in Contra Returns during a collaboration event.
Characters from Saint Seiya appear as crossover skins in Mobile Legends: Bang Bang as part of a collaboration event.
Characters from Saint Seiya appeared in Honor of Kings as part of a special collaboration.

Saints Row.description: "The Cyborg Slayers", a song by Dethklok from Metalocalypse, is featured in Saints Row: The Third.
In Saints Row: The Third one of the missing ships found on a list is named "USG Ishimura", like a ship from Dead Space.
In Saints Row: The Third one of the missing ships found on a list is named "Borealis", like a ship from Half-Life 2: Episode Two.
In Saints Row: The Third one of the missing ships found on a list is named "Axiom", like a ship from Wall-E.
The Whored Mode minigame wave "Hank East" from Saints Row: The Third references Dead Rising.

Team Fortress 2 features three promotional items based on Saints Row: The Third and unlocked by pre-ordering the game. Saints Row: The Third features headwear based on the cast of Team Fortress 2, while Saints Row IV features weapon skins based on the Flamethrower, Rainblower and Rocket Launcher.
At one point in Saints Row IV a number of spaceships imitate the formation and movement of the aliens in Space Invaders.
The Penetrator from Saints Row IV appears as a skin for the Katana in Shadow Warrior.
Johnny Gat appears in Divekick: Addition Edition + as a playable guest fighter.
The pre-order "All-Stars" pack for Worms W.M.D. includes Dubstep Gun from Saints Row IV as a mounted gun.
Clothing based on Saints Row can be obtained in Payday 2 to promote the release of Saints Row The Third Remastered

Sakamoto Days.description: Sakamoto Days is mentioned in Chapter 46 of Me & Roboco.
Spider-Man is mentioned in Chapter 47 of Sakamoto Days.
Resident Evil is mentioned in Chapter 66 of Sakamoto Days.
Terminator 2 is mentioned in Chapter 89 of Sakamoto Days.
Characters from Sakamoto Days appear in Jumputi Heroes as playable characters.
Union Arena features cards based on Sakamoto Days.

Sakuna: Of Rice and Ruin.description: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate features three spirits from Sakuna: Of Rice and Ruin.
A costume based on Sakuna from Sakuna: Of Rice and Ruin was available in Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town for a limited time.
Princess Sakuna appears in Rune Factory: Guardians of Azuma as DLC.

Sakura Samurai.description: Sakura Samurai appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; he's also a trophy in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS.

Sakura Wars.description: Hanagumi Taisen Columns and Hanagumi Taisen Columns II are format crossovers featuring storyline elements from the Sakura Wars series and gameplay elements from the Columns series.
Puyo Puyo Fever: Carnival Edition included Sakura Shinguji as a guest character, while Puyo Puyo!! Quest featured various characters from Sakura Wars during collaboration events.
Sega Splash! Golf features Sakura Shinguji from Sakura Wars as a caddie.
Music from Sakura Wars was added to maimai in the maimai version.
Sakura Shinjui from Sakura Wars appears in the Sega Hard Girls episode "Connect Your Passions into a Combo".
Characters from Sakura Wars appear in Granblue Fantasy as a part of a collaboration.
Sakura Wars characters appear in Chain Chronicle for a collaboration event.
Super Robot Wars X-Ω features units from Sakura Wars during special events.
Music from Sakura Wars can be played in O.N.G.E.K.I.
Sakura Shinguji from Sakura Wars appear as a playable character in Toaru Majutsu no Index MMO during a collaboration event.
Characters from Sakura Wars appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration.
Sakura Wars characters make an appearance in Langrisser Mobile as part of a special collaboration.
Sakura Shinguji and Sakura Amamiya from Sakura Wars appear in Earth UFO Catcher.
Characters from Sakura Wars appear in Revue Starlight Re LIVE as part of a special collaboration.
Taiko no Tatsujin (Nijiro Version) features a music track from Sakura Wars.
Music from Sakura Wars can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix after an update.

Salad Fingers.description: Salad Fingers is a playable character in Newgrounds Rumble.
A character based on Salad Fingers appears as the junk store clerk in Pico Sim Date <3.
Salad Fingers is a playable character in Indie Game Battle.
Salad Fingers appears in Umbilical World.
Cards based on Salad Fingers are included in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls Requiem.
Salad Fingers memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".

Salamander (Konami).description: Salamander is a spinoff of Gradius.
Areas in the shooting stages from Konami Wai Wai World are based off Salamander.
The Octopus gameplay configuration in Parodius Da! is based on Salamander.
Brain Golem from Salamander appears in Monster Maulers.
A wrestler in Jikkyō Power Pro Wrestling '96: Max Voltage named "Mill Salamander" is inspired in the Lord British from Salamander.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Salamander.
The Lord British ship from Salamander appears as a Yu-Gi-Oh card.

Saltburn.description: Harry Potter is read by multiple characters in Saltburn.
The Ring is shown on TV in Saltburn.
Superbad is shown on TV in Saltburn.

Sam & Cat.description: Sam & Cat is a spin off of both iCarly and Victorious.
Sam & Cat is a spin off of both iCarly and Victorious.
Cat mentions SpongeBob's pineapple in the Sam & Cat episode "#TextingCompetition.
The Laverne & Shirley opening is parodied in the Sam & Cat episode: "#SalmonCat".
Stacey Dillsen from Zoey 101 appears in the Sam & Cat episode "#MadAboutShoe", while Coco and Carl appear in the episode: "#FirstClassProblems".
A parody of Curly from The Three Stooges appears in the Sam & Cat episode "#Twinfection".
Brain Crush, a game in Sam & Cat, is a parody of Candy Crush.
Sam & Cat appear in the online Nickelodeon game Block Party.
Crazy Steve makes a cameo in the Sam and Cat episode #SuperPsycho.
Herb from Sam & Cat appears in the Henry Danger episode "Secret Beef".  Also Goomer from Sam and Cat is an assistant to Frankini from Henry Danger.

Sam & Max.description: Sam and Max make appearances as an idol, as costumes and as shadows in the first three episodes of Monkey Island, and are referenced in Escape from Monkey Island; the Sam & Max: Freelance Police stories on issues 1 and 14 of The Adventurer are parodies of The Secret of Monkey Island, and there also is a reference to the game in Sam & Max Hit the Road.

The Sam & Max: Freelance Police story on issue 3 of The Adventurer is a parody of Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis and there also are references to Indiana Jones movies in Sam & Max Hit the Road.
The game  Star Wars Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II features Max The Bunny, who can team up with the player. Before, both series have made various references to each other.
A parody of Cecil is seen in The Adventures of Sam & Max: Freelance Police episode "It's Dangly Deever Time".
Stimpacks and radiation chems are mentioned in Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space.

In the second episode of Sam & Max Beyond Time and Space there are crates underwater with an image of Duke Nukem and the initials "D.N.E." parodying the still-unreleased at the time Duke Nukem Forever.
The Sam & Max video games "Chariots of the Gods" and "What's New Beelzebub" feature references to Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure.
Team Fortress 2 features three promotional items  based on Sam & Max: The Devil's Playhouse and unlocked by pre-purchasing the game.

Se7en" is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Therapy".

Sengoku Ace.description: Aine from the Sengoku Ace series is one of the pilots featured in Strikers 1945, several other characters appear as Operators in Strikers 1945: World War and as characters and elements in Strikers 1945 Collection.

Aine (Kain) and Koyori (Koyomi) from Sengoku Ace are secret characters in Taisen Hot Gimmick and Taisen Hot Gimmick Kairakuten, the character Melty cosplays as Aine in Taisen Hot Gimmick 3: Digital Surfing and Junis (Jumis) from Sengoku Blade is a secret character in Taisen Hot Gimmick 4 Ever.
Aine from the Sengoku Ace series is a playable character in Gunbird 2, while Marion is a playable character in the Sega Saturn port of Sengoku Blade.
Several characters from the Sengoku Ace series are featured in Taisen Net Gimmick: Capcom & Psikyo All Stars.

Sengoku BASARA.description: Weapons from the Devil May Cry series are featured in the Sengoku BASARA series and Devil Kings was loosely inspired by the series; while Sengoku BASARA 4 features costumes based off Dante and Vergil from Devil May Cry, the Sengoku BASARA VS Devil May Cry stage play is a crossover between the two series and Sengoku BASARA Battle Party features Dante and Lady from Devil May Cry 4 as part of a collaboration event.
Honda Tadakatsu from Sengoku BASARA features several references to the Gundam series.
’’Sengoku BASARA’’ billboards are visible in ‘’Final Fight: Streetwise’’.
There's a series of Weiß Schwarz cards based around characters and items from Sengoku BASARA.
Pop'n Music 18 Sengoku Retsuden features a track from Sengoku BASARA.
"Zenny", the currency from Black Tiger, appears in Sengoku BASARA: Samurai Heroes and Sengoku BASARA 3 Utage.
Minna to Capcom All Stars and Street Fighter × All Capcom feature characters from Sengoku BASARA.

Yukimura Sanada, Tadakatsu Honda, Shingen Takeda, Mitsunari Ishida and Kenshin Uesugi from Sengoku BASARA appear in Onimusha Soul as part of a limited event quest; as part of a crossover collaboration, playing Minna to Onimusha Card Master unlocks cards of Date Masamune and Yukimura Sanada in Sengoku BASARA Card Heroes Matsuri, while playing the latter unlocks cards of Samanosuke Akechi and Princess Sarashina in the former.

As part of a crossover collaboration, playing Minna to Biohazard Team Survive unlocks a card of Masamune Date in Sengoku BASARA Card Heroes Matsuri, while playing the latter unlocks cards of Leon Kennedy and Claire Redfield in the former; additionally Sengoku BASARA 4 Sumeragi features a DLC costume pack based on characters from Resident Evil.

Monster Hunter Frontier and Monster Hunter Explorer feature downloadable weapons and costumes from Sengoku BASARA; while Sengoku BASARA 4 Sumeragi features a DLC costume pack based on characters and armor from Monster Hunter.

Date Masamune, Yukimura Sanada and other Sengoku BASARA characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; while Sengoku BASARA 4 Sumeragi features a DLC costume pack based on characters from Street Fighter.
A remix of the Sengoku BASARA theme is featured in CROSS×BEATS.
Tales of Zestiria features a DLC costume pack based on Sengoku BASARA 4, while Sengoku BASARA 4 Sumeragi features a DLC costume pack based on Tales of Zestiria.
Taiko no Tatsujin V Version features a downloadable music track from Sengoku BASARA.
The Sengoku BASARA version of Yukimura Sanada makes a guest appearance on Q-Transformers: The Road to Additional Popularity.
DLC costumes based on Sengoku BASARA characters are featured in Ace Attorney 6: Spirits of Justice.
TEPPEN update 2.7 added characters from the Sengoku BASARA series.

Serious Sam.description: In Serious Sam 2, the blonde, shades-wearing skeleton of Duke Nukem can be found in Stage 10. Upon finding it, Sam quips "Dude, you've been hanging here, like, forever". In Episode 5, Level 4 of Duke Nukem 20th Anniversary World Tour, Sam's body can be found and Duke quips "Why so...serious?". There are many references to Duke Nukem in the dialogue of some Serious Sam games, often calling him "Blondie".

The main character from Dig Dug appears as a summon alongside a Pooka in Keroro RPG.
Clovis from Dragon Buster appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Red Baron from Sky Kid appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
The main character from Genpei Toma Den appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Torosuke from Shadow Land appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Mappy appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Valkyrie and Kurino Sandra appear as summons in Keroro RPG.
The Mothership from Xevious appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Wonder Momo appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Bravoman appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Mr. Driller appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Don-chan from Taiko no Tatsujin appears as a summon in Keroro RPG; many games in the Taiko no Tatsujin series also feature songs from Keroro Gunsō.
The Prince from Katamari appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Klonoa and Guntz appear as summons in Keroro RPG.
Wagan appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
The Runner from Metro-Cross appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Haseo from .hack//G.U. appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Pac-Man appears as a summon alongside the ghosts in Keroro RPG.
Keroro Gunsō X Transformers is a crossover between the two series.
Characters from Sgt. Frog appeared in Heroes Phantasia.
The Super Robot Wars series features units from the Keroro Gunsou series.
Sgt Frog characters appear in Kemono Friends for a collaboration event.
Sgt. Keroro from Sgt. Frog appears in White Cat Tennis as part of its 1st Anniversary Gacha.

Shadow Complex.description: The WSA2 Tarantulas from Shadow Complex resemble the think tanks from Ghost in the Shell, with the third WSA2 Tarantula boss fight paying homage to a scene in the Ghost in the Shell film.
A Shadow Complex poster can be found in some locations in Fortnite.

Shadow Warrior.description: In Shadow Warrior you can find a character looking like Lara Croft in a prison cell chained to a wall as your character say "She's raided her last tomb".
In the game you can find a woman looking like Sailor Moon in a bed.
The Mach 5 from Speed Racer appears in Shadow Warrior.
Whenever a big explosion is triggered in Shadow Warrior, the main character says "Wow! Look like a Duke Nukem".
The Katana from Hotline Miami appears in Shadow Warrior as a skin for the Katana.
The Penetrator from Saints Row IV appears as a skin for the Katana in Shadow Warrior.
The Sledgehammer from Serious Sam 3: BFE appears as a skin for the Katana in Shadow Warrior. Lo Wang from Shadow Warrior is a playable character in I Hate Running Backwards.
A silhouette of Godzilla makes an appearance in Shadow Warrior.
Lo Wang from Shadow Warrior appears as a guest character in Oh...Sir!! The Insult Simulator.
Enter the Gungeon features several weapons that make references to Shadow Warrior (2013).
The Kazaguruma and several demon masks from Shadow Warrior 2 are usable in Payday 2, while a Dallas skin, the AMCAR Rifle, and the Money Bundle from Payday 2 are usable in Shadow Warrior 2.
A mask based on Shadow Warrior 2 was added to Absolver as part of an update.
Lo Wang is a playable character in Rad Rodgers: Radical Edition.
Devolverland Expo features a booth based around Shadow Warrior 3 including the Oni Hamna from the game.
Hoji and Lo Wang from Shadow Warrior appear in Devolver Tumble Time.
The Hoji Mask and Shuriken Spitter from Shadow Warrior 3 can be used in Naraka: Bladepoint, while the Raikou from Naraka: Bladepoint can be used in Shadow Warrior 3.

Shadow of the Colossus.description: Shadow of the Colossus serves as a spiritual successor to Ico
Colossus II and III costumes are downloadable in LittleBigPlanet.
The episode "The Colossus" of The Amazing World of Gumball features a minor reference to Shadow of the Colossus.
The PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4 versions of Diablo III: Ultimate Evil Edition feature a Shadow of the Colossus themed armor.
Shadow of the Colossus is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Expedition Approximation”.

The remaster of Shadow of the Colossus features one of the barrels that can be seen in The Last Guardian. Additionally you can find an outfit in The Last Guardian based on the outfit of the protagonist from Shadow of the Colossus

An arrangement of origami figures can be found in Ghost of Tsushima, one of them referencing Shadow of the Colossus. Additionally, an outfit based on Shadow of the Colossus can be obtained in Ghost of Tsushima.
A Shadow of the Colossus game box is seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Bots that reference Shadow of the Colossus appear in Astro's Playroom. Costumes based on Wander, Mono, and Agro from 'Shadow of the Colossus can be found in Astro Bot.
Characters from Shadow of the Colossus appear in the Secret Level episode "Playtime: Fulfillment".

Shadow the Hedgehog.description: Shadow the Hedgehog and Shadow Shoot are spin-offs of the Sonic series. Sonic X Shadow Generations is part of both series.
Black Doom from Shadow the Hedgehog might be based on Wizeman the Wicked from NiGHTS
Blue Falcon and Black Bull, the two bosses in the game, are named after the racing cars in F-Zero.
The Egg Vacuum is a weapon based on the game Billy Hatcher and the Giant Egg.
Shadow's trophy in Super Smash Bros. Brawl references Shadow the Hedgehog.
Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing features the Dark Rider from Shadow the Hedgehog as shadow's vehicle.
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Shadow the Hedgehog in the episode "Wish List (Part 1)".
"Something About Shadow the Hedgehog" was created as part of a sponsored video to promote the release of Sonic X Shadow Generations.

Shadowverse.description: Shadowverse is considered to be a spiritual successor of Rage of Bahamut with many characters and illustrations from Rage of Bahamut appearing in the game.
Several characters from Street Fighter V are part of a collaboration event in the game Shadowverse.
Characters from Shadowverse appear in Granblue Fantasy as a part of a collaboration.
Music from Shadowverse was added to maimai in the maimai FiNALE version.
Music from Shadowverse can be played in O.N.G.E.K.I. Plus.
One-Punch Man characters appear in Shadowverse for a collaboration event.
Love Live! School Idol Festival held a collaboration with Shadowverse.
Haruhi Suzumiya characters appear in Shadowverse for a collaboration event.
Shadowverse characters appear in World Flipper for a collaboration event.
Code Geass characters appear in Shadowverse for a collaboration event.
Jujutsu Kaisen characters appear in Shadowverse: Champion Battle for a collaboration event.
Shadowverse characters appear in Sevens Story as part of a special collaboration.
Kaguya-sama: Love Is War characters appear in Shadowverse for a collaboration event.
Characters from Uma Musume appear in Shadowverse as part of a collaboration event; Uma Musume cards have also been released for the Shadowverse TCG.
Characters from Hololive are featured in Shadowverse Evolve as part of two collaboration events.
Spy × Family characters appear in Shadowverse for a collaboration event.

Shady Lewd Kart.description: Talia and Faye are playable characters in Shady Lewd Kart.
ZONE-Tan is a playable character in Shady Lewd Kart.
Cameilla is a playable character in Shady Lewd Kart.
Projekt Melody is a playable character in Shady Lewd Kart.
Jane is a playable character in Shady Lewd Kart.
Arma is a kart in Shady Lewd Kart.
Wild Woody is a free DLC character in Shady Lewd Kart voiced by the original voice actor.

Shake It Up.description: CeCe, Rocky, Flynn and Deuce from Shake It Up appear in the Good Luck Charlie episode Charlie Shakes It Up.
CeCe and Rocky appeared as part of the Make Your Mark: Ultimate Jam party
Just Dance: Disney Party features the songs "Shake It Up" and "Twist My Hips (Watch Me)" from Shake It Up.

Shakugan no Shana.description: Yoshida Kazumi from the Shakugan no Shana appears in the A Certain Scientific Railgun episode, Electromaster
Shana is a playable character. Wilhelmina Carmel is an assist character
Shana appeared in Hyaku Nen Senki: Euro Historia as part of a collaboration event with Dengeki Bunko ranobes.
The OP from Shakugan no Shana III - Final is featured in CROSS×BEATS REV.
Divine Gate features several characters from Shakugan no Shana as part of a special collaboration.
Shana appeared in Monster Strike during the Dengeki collaboration.

Shaman King.description: Yoh is a playable character in the series.
Characters from Shaman King appeared in Boku & Dragons as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Shaman King appeared in Puzzle & Dragons and Puzzle & Dragons Radar (with Yoh Asakura appearing as leader) during special collaborations.
Shaman King characters appear in Last Period for a collaboration event.
Characters from Shaman King appear in Dragon Egg as part of a collaboration.
Shaman King characters appear in Kotodaman for a collaboration event.
Shaman King characters appear in Grand Summoners for a collaboration event.
Characters from Shaman King appear in White Cat Project as part of a collaboration.
Shaman King characters appear in Chain Chronicle for a collaboration event.
Hiro Gomon wears a similar outfit to Iron Maiden Jeanne from Shaman King.

Shang-Chi.description: Man-Thing appears in Master of Kung Fu #19.

Doctor Doom from Fantastic Four appears in Master of Kung Fu #60. Shang-Chi appears in Fantastic Four Roast and Ultimate Fantastic Four #23, #52, and #53. The Fantastic Four appear in Shang-Chi Vol. 2 #4.
Shang-Chi appears in Thor Vol. 1 #271. Thor appears in Shang-Chi Vol. 2 #6.

”Spider-Man and Master of Kung Fu” from Ultimate Marvel Team-Up is a crossover between the two series. Shang-Chi appears in numerous Spider-Man comics and in the Spider-Man cartoon episode “Wrath of the Sub-Mariner”. White Dragon from Spider-Man appears in Deadly Hands of Kung Fu Vol. 2 #2 and #3. Spider-Man appears in Shang-Chi Vol. 2 #1.
Shang-Chi appears in Rom #38 and #39. Brynocki from Master of Kung-Fu appears in Rom #47.
Shang-Chi appears in Captain America Vol. 1 #302 and #412-414. Captain America appears in Deadly Hands of Kung Fu Vol. 2 #1 and Shang-Chi Vol. 2 #2.
Shang-Chi appears in Daredevil Annual #10.
Shang-Chi appears in The Incredible Hulk #434 and The Totally Awesome Hulk #15-18. Abomination from The Incredible Hulk appears in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.
Shang-Chi appears in X-Men Vol. 2 #62-64 and Uncanny X-Men Vol. 5 #4. Nightcrawler from X-Men appears in Master of Kung Fu Vol. 2 #1.
Shang-Chi appears in Elektra Vol. 2 #9, #10 and #16. Elektra appears in Master of Kung Fu Vol. 2.
Shang-Chi appears in Black Panther Vol. 4 #11 and #18. Black Panther appears in Master of Kung Fu #3 and #4.
Shang-Chi appears in Wolverine: First Class #9 and Wolverine Vol. 6 #8-9.
Deadpool appears in Shang-Chi: Master of Kung Fu Vol. 2 #1. Shang-Chi appears in Deadpool Kills the Marvel Universe #4 and Deadpool Kills the Marvel Universe Again #3 and #4.
Shang-Chi appears in Black Widow: Deadly Origin #4.
Shang-Chi has been a member of both the Secret Avengers and the Avengers.
Shang-Chi appears in Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur #39.
Alvin and the Chipmunks are mentioned in Shang-Chi Vol. 2 #2.
Shang-Chi appears in Fortnite.
Characters play Dance Dance Revolution in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.
Trevor Slattery mentions Planet of the Apes in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.
Katy Chen mentions a "Kamehameha" attack from Dragon Ball in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.
Iron Man appears in Shang-Chi Vol. 2 #5.
A card based on Shang-Chi appears in Marvel Snap.

Shanghai (Sunsoft).description: Hebereke characters appear as the players' characters in the i-mode version of Shanghai and on Mahjong tiles in Shanghai Musume: Mahjong Girls.
Characters from Dead Zone appear on Mahjong tiles in Shanghai Musume: Mahjong Girls.
The Metal Attacker/Sophia the 3rd from Metafight/Blaster Master appears on Mahjong tiles in Shanghai Musume: Mahjong Girls.
Lucia from The Wing of Madoola appears on Mahjong tiles in Shanghai Musume: Mahjong Girls.
Yumetaro from Gimmick! appears on Mahjong tiles in Shanghai Musume: Mahjong Girls.
Gonbe from Ikki appears on Mahjong tiles in Shanghai Musume: Mahjong Girls.

Shangri-La Frontier.description: Sunraku, Arthur Pencilgon, and Oikatzo from Shangri-La Frontier appear in The Eminence of Shaow: Master of Garden as part of a special collaboration.
Seven Knights: Idle Adventure features characters from Shangri-La Frontier as part of a special collaboration.
Union Arena features cards based on Shangri-La Frontier.
Characters from Shangri-La Frontier are playable characters in Isekai∞Isekai.

Shantae.description: The DLC microgame "Shantae NAB!" from WarioWare: D.I.Y. is based on the Shantae series.
Shantae: Risky's Revenge features a dialogue reference to the intro of Super Contra.
Shantae: Risky's Revenge features a dialogue reference to one of the obtuse hints in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest.
The nameless warrior from Shantae and the Pirate's Curse references Karnov in his shape, vague backstory details and a very similar music theme.
The character Bran-Son from Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is a parody of He-Man.
Shantae and the Pirate's Curse features a dialogue reference to Ghostbusters.
The "space princess" outfit Shantae and other characters wear during a part of Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is based on Leia's slave costume from Star Wars: The Return of the Jedi.
A team consisting of characters from Shantae appears in #IDARB.
One of the alternate color palettes in Skullgirls is based on Shantae.
Shantae is a playable character in Mutant Mudds Super Challenge.
A ghost named “Ikki” in the game Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is a reference to Nikki.
Shantae is a downloadable character in Runbow.
Shantae is a downloadable character for Blaster Master Zero, while a free update in Shantae: Half-Genie Hero added a Sophia the 3rd transformation to Shantae's repertoire.
Shantae and Risky Boots appear as spirits in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Shantae is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
The Dagron Ball items from Shantae and the Seven Sirens are a reference to the Dragon Balls.
Shantae has been a subject for DBX.
Accessories based on Shantae appear in Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night as part of a free update.

Shark Tale.description: Characters hum the Jaws theme in Shark Tale.
Shark Tale is a spoof of The Godfather.
There is a reference to Die Hard in Shark Tale.
Oscar says "Are you not entertained" referencing Gladiator in Shark Tale.
Oscar says "You had me at hello" referencing Jerry Maguire in Shark Tale.
Don Feinberg wanted to sing “My Heart Will Go On” from Titanic in Shark Tale.
Shark Tale DVD set appears in Flushed Away.
Various Shark Tale characters appear in DreamWorks Movie Trivia DVD Game.
Footage from Shark Tale appears in Kaku Spring Festival Gala 2010.
Shark Tale is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Soldier Excursion Diversion”.
Caddy reviews the Shark Tale video game in the video "The Nightmare World of Dreamworks Games".
Characters from Shark Tale make an appearance in KouKou Love: Tap Blast.
A Shark Tale game box is seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".

Sharkboy and Lavagirl.description: A Big Kahuna bag from Pulp Fiction can be seen during the dream in which Max meets Sharkboy in The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl.
A DVD cover for Sharkboy and Lavagirl can be seen in the Modern Family episodes: "And One to Grow On".
The Nostalgia Critic reviews "The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl".

Sharknado.description: Sharknado is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Empire State of Mind Strikes Back".
Archie and Sharknado meet in a comic crossover.
The character from Sharknado, Fin Sheppard, makes a cameo appearance in Lavalantula.
Sharknado is mentioned in Deadpool 2 and Deadpool is mentioned in The Last Sharknado: It's About Time.

Shattered Angels.description: Kū's personality and characteristics resemble Himeko in Kannazuki no Miko.

Shaun the Sheep.description: Shaun The Sheep is a spinoff of Wallace & Gromit.
Home Sheep Home was a playable game in the Moshi Fun Park in Moshi Monsters.
A Shaun the Sheep toy appears in Arthur Christmas.
The special episode of Shaun the Sheep called "Shaun Goes Old School" features references to Super Mario Bros.; Super Mario Maker features a costume based on Shaun the Sheep.
Creature Comforts animals can be seen as captured animals in Shaun the Sheep Movie.
Vince can be seen as a captured animal in Shaun the Sheep Movie.
Shaun the Sheep is parodied in multiple Perfect Cell Vs episodes.
Shaun the Sheep characters appear in Playtime Island.
There are several references to Doctor Who in Shaun The Sheep Movie: Farmageddon.
Shaun the Sheep characters appear in Get Creative.

Shazam!.description: Shazam appears in Justice League #136.
Captain Everything from normalman has elements that parody Shazam!
Megaton Man parodies elements of Shazam!.
Shazam is a playable character in Injustice: Gods Among Us.
Scribblenauts Unmasked features spawnable objects from the Shazam! series.
Shazam appears in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
Shazam's costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 2.
The Shazam Family appears in Scooby Doo Team Up #16.
Shazam and Shazam! Fury of the Gods have been parodied on "How Shazam Should Have Ended".
A character based on Billy Batson appears in The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen: The Tempest #4.
Shazam appears in Doomsday Clock #9.
Annabelle appears in the Shazam! movie as an easter egg.
Billy and Freddy play Mortal Kombat X in Shazam!. Additionally, a Mortal Kombat II arcade cabinet can be found in Shazam! Fury of the Gods.
Harry Potter is mentioned in Shazam!.
Game of Thrones is mentioned in Shazam!.
Watch Dogs is mentioned in Shazam!.
Emma Glover from Lights Out appears in Shazam!
Shazam has been a subject for Death Battle!
Black Adam is a spinoff of Shazam!
The Fast and The Furious is mentioned in Shazam! Fury of the Gods.
Billy Batson wears a The Goonies shirts in Shazam! Fury of the Gods.
A Shazam themed Ringout effect is an unlockable item in MultiVersus.
Thor/Shazam! is a crossover between the two series.

Shazzan.description: Characters from Shazzan appear in the Space Ghost episode "The Final Encounter".
Shazzan appears in the Harvey Birdman episode "Shazzan".
B'wana Beast rides a creature that strongly resembles Kaboobie from Shazzan in the Batman: The Brave and the Bold episode "The Siege of Starro!: Part 1".
Shazzan and Kazoobie appear in several episodes of Jellystone!

She's Having a Baby.description: Jake watches The Dick Van Dyke Show in She's Having a Baby.
Ferris Bueller appears in the end credits of She's Having A Baby.
A billboard for a movie called She's Having a Baby...Again appears in the Simpsons episode "Beyond Blunderdome".
She's Having a Baby is mentioned in the Glee episode "Girls (and Boys) on Film".
She's Having A Baby is mentioned in Ready Player Two.

She's the Man.description: Bambi is mentioned in She's the Man.

She-Hulk.description: The She-Hulk series is a spin-off of the Hulk series.
She-Hulk has been a member of the Avengers, first joining in Avengers #221.
She-Hulk has been a member of the Fantastic Four, first joining the team in Fantastic Four #265.
Tigra appears in Sensational She-Hulk in Ceremony #1, She-Hulk (Vol. 2) #3, #7, #15, and She-Hulk (Vol. 3) #5-6, #12.
Moon Knight appeared in Sensational She-Hulk (Vol. 1) #58 and She-Hulk (Vol. 4) #4.
A doppelganger of She-Hulk is an enemy in Marvel Super Heroes in War of the Gems, while She-Hulk makes a cameo appearance in Marvel Super Heroes.
Black Panther appears in She-Hulk (Vol. 2) #3, while She-Hulk appears in Black Panther (Vol. 3) #22 and Black Panther (Vol. 4) #18.
A Zombie version of She-Huk appears in Marvel Zombies: Dead Days.
She-Hulk appears in Marvel: Ultimate Alliance 2.
A card based on She-Hulk appears in Marvel Snap.
She-Hulk is parodied in the Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episode: "She Hulk Smash ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) ".
The "Marvel Studios" series of Lego Minifigures includes She-Hulk from She-Hulk: Attorney at Law.
She-Hulk is a playable character in Marvel Cosmic Invasion.

She-Ra.description: She-Ra is a spin off of Masters of the Universe.
She-Ra is mentioned in Ready Player One.
One journal entry mentions She-Ra in Gone Home.
She-Ra appears in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
She-Ra is one of Any's contacts.
She-Ra has been a subject for Death Battle!.
Chilli dresses up as She-Ra in the Bluey episode "Fairytale".
A skin based on She-Ra appears for Adora in Bloons TD 6.

Shenmue.description: Hang-On is featured as a fully playable Arcade game within Shenmue and Shenmue II.
OutRun is featured as a fully playable Arcade game within Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Space Harrier is featured as a fully playable Arcade game and a set of Capsule Toys within Shenmue and Shenmue II.
The Bonanza Brothers appear as Capsule Toys in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Rent a Hero appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
The Try-Z from Galaxy Force appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Opa Opa and several enemies from Fantazy Zone appear as Capsule Toys in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
The Solo Wing from Panzer Dragoon Zwei appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Myau from Phantasy Star appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
A Chicken Leg from Golden Axe appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Ristar appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Alex Kidd appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
NiGHTS appears as Capsule Toys in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
A poster for Flicky appears in Shenmue.
The Hornet car from Daytona USA appears as a Capsule Toy in Shenmue and Shenmue II.
The Dreamcast port of Virtua Cop 2 features billboards with Shenmue artwork.
Several robots from Virtual On appears as Capsule Toys in Shenmue II.
Several characters from Power Jet Racing 2001 appear as Capsule Toys in Shenmue II.
Several characters from 18-Wheeler: American Pro Trucker appear as Capsule Toys in Shenmue II.
After Burner II is featured as a fully playable Arcade game in Shenmue II, and there's also a Capsule Toy of the game's F14-XX.
Ryo Hazuki from Shenmue is an unlockable player in ESPN NFL Football.

Shenmue was initially planned to be part of the Virtua Fighter series; Shenmue and Shenmue II feature Toy Capsules based on Virtua Fighter and Virtua Fighter Kids, while the Virtua Fighter 5 stage "Aurora" features the "MJQ" jazz bar from Shenmue in the background.

Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing features Ryo from Shenmue as a playable racer; additionally, Shenmue and Shenmue II feature Capsule Toys based on characters from Sonic and a Shenmue billboard can be seen in the "'90s Boulevard" stage from Sonic Riders: Zero Gravity.
Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing features Ryo from Shenmue as a playable racer.
There's a minor reference to Ryo Hazuki in Yakuza 4.
The mission "Shore Leave" from Crazy Taxi City Rush features a number of nods to Ryo's sailor search in Shenmue.
Ryo Hazuki from Shenmue appears in Kyoutou Kotoba RPG: Kotodaman during a "Sega All Stars" collaboration.
Characters from Shenmue appear in Sega Heroes.
Ryo Hazuki from Shenmue appears in Earth UFO Catcher.
Ryo Hazuki from Shenmue appeared in Puyo Puyo!! Quest during the Gintama collaboration boss event "Dream Satan challenge" and in the second Sega collaboration event.
Ryo Hazuki from Shenmue appears in the background of a stage in Shinobi: Art of Vengeance.
In Do You Know Gaming?, a card featuring a parody of Shenmue named "Shen-Moo" can be found.

Sheriff (Nintendo).description: A built-in game in Family Basic - v.3 features a possible reference to Sheriff.
Sheriff appears in Game Boy Camera.
The minigame Wario's Sheriff, featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!, can be considered a crossover between the two series.
The Sheriff appears as an Assist Trophy in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U.

Shi (Crusade Comics).description: Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents is a crossover between the two series.
Sara Pezzini from Witchblade appears in Cyblade/Shi: The Battle for Independents.
Cerebus appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Fone Bone appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Mr. Spook from Tales of the Beanworld appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Hellboy appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Johnny the Homicidal Maniac appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Madman appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Megaton Man appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
The Tick appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Usagi appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Spider-Man appears in Shi/Cyblade: The Battle for Independents.
Tomoe is a spin-off of Shi.
Daredevil/Shi is a crossover between the two series.
Shi/Vampirella is a crossover between the two series. Shi appears in Vampirella Monthly #7-9.
Wolverine/Shi is a crossover between the two series.
Shi vs. 10th Muse is a crossover between the two series.
Shi took part in the War of the Independents event.

Shimajiro.description: Taiko no Tatsujin: Wai Wai Happy! Rokudaime features a music track from Shima Shima Tora no Shimajiro.
There is a exercise video with Shimajiro and Hello Kitty.

Shimmer and Shine.description: Shimmer and Shine characters appear in Nick Jr. Music Maker.
Shimmer & Shine were mascots in the episode “Hummels & Heroin.”
Footage from Shimmer and Shine is shown in the Black Mirror episode "Arkangel".

Shin Megami Tensei.description: The Shin Megami Tensei series is a spin off of Megami Tensei.
The Devil Summoner series is a spin-off of Shin Megami Tensei.
The Persona series is a spin-off of the Shin Megami Tensei series.
The Devil Children series is a spin-off of Shin Megami Tensei.
Dante from Devil May Cry appears in Shin Megami Tensei: Nocturne.
The Digital Devil Saga series is a spin-off of Shin Megami Tensei.
The Devil Survivor series is a spin-off of Shin Megami Tensei.
3D Dot Game Heroes features loading screens based on Shin Megami Tensei II.
Characters from Durarara!! appear in Shin Megami Tensei IMAGINE as part of a special collaboration event.
There's a series of Weiß Schwarz cards based around characters and items from Shin Megami Tensei.
Undertale has a references to Shin Megami Tensei.
Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE is a crossover between Shin Megami Tensei and Fire Emblem.
Characters from Shin Megami Tensei appear in Brave Frontier during a special collaboration.
Bayonetta characters appear in Shin Megami Tensei: Liberation Dx2 for a special collaboration.
Joker's moves Tetrakarn and Makarakarn first appeared in Shin Megami Tensei. Tsubasa Oribe from Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Berserk characters appear in Shin Megami Tensei: Liberation Dx2 for a special collaboration.
Jack Frost and Megakin from Shin Megami Tensei appear in Earth UFO Catcher.
Ghost in the Shell characters appear in Shin Megami Tensei: Liberation Dx2 for a special collaboration.
Characters from the Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne appear in The Alchemist Code as a part of a collaboration.
Shin Megami Tensei: Liberation Dx2 featured Sonic during a collaboration event.
The Seven Deadly Sins characters appear in Shin Megami Tensei: Liberation Dx2 for a special collaboration.
Dragon Poker features several characters from Shin Megami Tensei V as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Shin Megami Tensei V appeared in Boku & Dragons as part of a special collaboration.
A plush of Jack Frost from Shin Megami Tensei can be found in Professor Chalk's room in the music video for A Songus Amongus.
Etrian Odyssey II HD features a character portrait of Demi-Fiend from Shin Megami Tensei III as DLC while Etrian Odyssey III HD features a character portrait of Nahobino from Shin Megami Tensei V.
Evangelion characters appear in Shin Megami Tensei: Liberation Dx2 for a special collaboration.
Overlord characters appear in Shin Megami Tensei: Liberation Dx2 for a special collaboration.

A scene in the Sitting Ducks episode "Daredevil Ducks" references The Blair Witch Project.

Sixteen Candles.description: A Top Cat cartoon can be seen on TV in Sixteen Candles.
The Breakfast Club takes place in Shermer, Illinois, a fictional suburb that first appeared in Sixteen Candles.
Weird Science takes place in Shermer, Illinois, a fictional suburb that first appeared in Sixteen Candles.

Skibidi Toilet contains references to Team Fortress, such as the character names and other various character models and locations.
Skibidi Toilet contains references to Counter-Strike, such as the character names and other various character models and locations.
Skibidi Toilet contains references to Garry's Mod. And features other various character models and locations.
Spider-Man can be spotted in "Skibidi Toilet 6".
Skibidi Toilet is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "Perfect Cell Vs Skibidi Toilet".

Characters from Skibidi Toilet appear in the SMG4 episode "Mario vs Skibidi Toilet".

Upgraded Titan TV Man faces Godzilla in the video "godzilla get humbled".
Skibidi Toilets based on Walter White and Jesse Pinkman from Breaking Bad appear in "Skibidi Toilet 68".
Free Fire released the Toiletman emote based on Skibidi Toilet.

A Skibidi Toilet DLC was added to Minecraft.

Characters from Skibidi Toilet appear in Stumble Guys as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Skibidi Toilet appear in PUBG Mobile during a crossover event.

Patrick Bateman from American Psycho can be seen in Skibidi Toilet Multiverse bloopers.

Sky Kid.description: The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Sky Kid.
One of the chairs in the carousel has a picture of a Red Baron from Sky Kid.
An Ohaka and Red Baron from Sky Kid are secret bonus characters in Tinkle Pit.
"Sky Kid" is a car brand first seen in Ridge Racer for PlayStation, while enemy cars in Ridge Racer 3D sport emblems of Baron and Max from Sky Kid.

The "Sky Kids" appear during a homerun in the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Baron" and "Sky Kid" in the Namco Stars team, while Famista Online 2010 features a player based on the enemy planes from Sky Kid  in the Rivals team.

Sky Kid is featured in Namco Museum Encore, Namco Museum 50th Anniversary, Namco Museum Virtual Arcade alongside Sky Kid Deluxe, Namco Museum for Nintendo Switch, Namco Museum Mini Player and Namcot Collection/Namco Museum Archives Vol. 1.
Artwork of Blue Max and Red Baron from Sky Kid appears as part of an easter egg in the training mode of Smash Court 2.
An image of Red Baron from Sky Kid appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.

Music from Sky Kid is featured in the Taiko March song, debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin DOKI! Shinkyoku Darake no Haru Matsuri, and in the Namcot Medley, debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10; the two Medal no Tatsujin also feature a song from Sky Kid.
A song from Sky Kid is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
The back of the jackets worn by Noelle and Ginji in Tales of the Abyss have artwork of Blue Max and Red Baron from Sky Kid.
Sky Kid characters and one location appear in Party Land.
Two remixes of the Sky Kid main theme are featured in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03  and Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER BEST ALBUM + LIVE DVD.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of Red Baron from Sky Kid with characters assisting the player.
Red Baron from Sky Kid appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Red from the ShiftyLook Sky Kid comic appears in strip #2 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary comic; additionally Pooka from Dig Dug appears as an item in Sky Kid.
A Sky Kid plushie appears in strip #38 of the Wonder Momo web comic.
Sky Kid is a support character in the web series Mappy: The Beat.
Arino plays Sky Kid in episode 167 of GameCenter CX.
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Sky Kid during Pat the NES Punk's 4th NES Marathon.
Blue Max from Sky Kid makes a cameo in strip #241 of the Bravoman web comic.
Blue Max from Sky Kid is a character in Namco High.
A sprite of Sky Kid appears in Pac-Man's taunt in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U.

The Red Baron and Blue Max aircrafts from Sky Kid were unlockable Special Aircrafts during a limited time tournament event in Ace Combat Infinity, there are several other minor references to the series in Ace Combat 04, 5, 6 and Infinity.
Red Baron and Blue Max from Sky Kid occasionally appear on the map screen in Battle City Dengeki Operation Offline.
Sky Kid characters appear in The Knights of Avalon during the second Namco collaboration event.
Red Baron from Sky Kid is one of the playable characters in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers, sprites also appear as treasures.
Posters of Pac-Man can be seen in Sky Kid, Sky Kid and Sky Kid Deluxe are included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash and a theme featuring Sky Kid characters appears in Pac-Man 99.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Sky Kid.

Sky: Children of the Light.description: In the secret office area of Sky: Children of the Light, 3 posters can be found hung up on the wall. One of them includes a poster for Flower.

In the secret office area of Sky: Children of the Light, 3 posters can be found hung up on the wall. One of them includes a poster for Journey. Outfits based on the traveler from Journey were later added as downloadable content.
Link's hair and ocarina from The Legend of Zelda appears in Sky: Children of the Light as content exclusive to the Nintendo Switch version.
A costume based on Kizuna AI appears in Sky: Children of the Light as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Sky: Children of the Light appear in Eggy Party.
A Companion Cube from Portal appears in Sky: Children of the Light as content exclusive to the Steam version.
Cinnamoroll appeared in Sky: Children of the Light as part of a special collaboration.
The world of Moomin appeared in Sky: Children of the Light as part of a special collaboration.

Skyhook.description: Finn makes a cameo in Indie Pogo.

Skylanders.description: Skylanders is a spin-off to the Spyro series.
Monopoly: Skylanders is a format crossover between the two series.
Bowser appears as a playable amiibo in Skylanders: SuperChargers.
Donkey Kong appears as a playable amiibo in Skylanders: SuperChargers.

Crash Bandicoot and Dr. Neo Cortex appear as playable characters in Skylanders: Imaginators and Crash later appears in three episodes of Skylanders Academy; while Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time features a parade float of Eruptor from Skylanders.
Roblox sponsored Skylanders with clothing and accessories.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 features graffiti art based on the Skylanders series.

Slam Masters.description: Haggar is a playable character in the Slam Masters series.

The Slam Masters characters King Rasta Mon and Gunloc may be based on Blanka and Guile from Street Fighter; Zangief and Guile are referenced in Slam Masters, while Chun Li, Ryu, and E. Honda make cameos in the audience; Slam Masters characters are referenced and make cameos occasionally in the Street Fighter series.
The "Bouncer" enemies from Breath of Fire II are named after characters in Saturday Night Slam Masters.
There are minor references to Slam Masters in Haggar's movelist in Namco × Capcom.
"Saturday Night Slam Masters" is one of the unlockable Nom de Guerres in Lost Planet 2.
Haggar makes some references to Slam Masters in Marvel vs. Capcom 3.
Saturday Night Slam Masters is included in Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium.

Slamacow.description: Slamacow is a parody of the Minecraft series.
Bart and Dave travel through the Town of Solitude from Skyrim in the Slamacow video "Solitude Entertainment".
The Slamacow video "Earthbending in Minecraft" is a parody of the Avatar series.
A player with a Spy skin appears in the Slamacow video "Emerald Trading".
A player with a Sonic the Hedgehog skin appears in the Slamacow video "Emerald Trading".
Chris from Bravest Warriors makes a cameo appearance at the end of the Slamacow video "Advanced Enchanting 101".
Dave the Zombie from Slamacow makes a cameo appearance in Episodes 2 and 4 of Dig Build Live.

Slap City.description: Many elements of Slap City are heavily inspired by Super Smash Bros..
Ittle Dew, Masked Ruby, Jenny Fox, and Ultra Fishbunjin 3000 from Ittle Dew appear as playable characters in Slap City. Additionally, several stages based on Ittle Dew appear in Slap City.
Princess Remedy and Frallan from Princess Remedy appear as playable characters in Slap City. Additionally, several stages based on Princess Remedy appear in Slap City.
Harbor Street, Bear Mine, and Turnip Corp. from Card City Nights appear as stages in Slap City. Additionally, characters from Slap City were added in Card City Nights 2.
Asha from Iji appears as a playable character in Slap City. Additionally, several stages based on Iji appear in Slap City.
Ultra Fishbunjin 3000's moveset and Pepperpain's layout in Fraymakers are based on their appearances in Slap City.
Creatures from Slap City can be found in Abomi Nation: Monster Rifts.

Slap Fight.description: The power-up bar system is the same as Gradius, albeit with different power-ups.
A white Invader from Space Invaders makes a cameo in Slap Fight, and many appear as enemies in Slap Fight Tiger.
KiKi KaiKai is included in Let's! TV Play Classic: Taito Nostalgia 2 alongside Slap Fight and Slap Fight Tiger.
The helicopter from Tiger-Heli appears in Slap Fight Tiger, a game included in Let's! TV Play Classic: Taito Nostalgia 2.

Slay the Princess.description: Cards based on Slay the Princess appeared in Balatro as part of the "Friends of Jimbo 4" update.
Random Encounters has made a Slay the Princess song.

Slay the Spire.description: The Blue Candle relic and Fairy in a Bottle potion in Slay the Spire are similar to items of the same name from The Legend of Zelda.
The Bowling Bash attack and Dead Branch relic in Slay the Spire are similar to a skill and item of the same name, respectively, in Ragnarok Online.
The Chemical X relic in Slay the Spire is based on the substance of the same name from The Powerpuff Girls.

The skill Pressure Points in Slay the Spire was originally named Path to Victory, and The Woman in Blue is actually the Worm character Contessa, a parahuman in the business of selling vials of powers, whose own power is called Path to Victory. Additionally, a story described similarly to Worm can be encountered in the library about an insect-controlling teenage girl who aspires to be a hero.
The Golden Idol relic in Slay the Spire is based on the item of the same name from Spelunky.
A costume of the Ironclad can be obtained in Imposter Mode in Going Under.
Items and skins from Slay the Spire appear in Dead Cells as part of the "Everyone Is Here" update.
The Watcher is a playable character in Fraymakers. Additionally, The Silent appears as an assist.
Cards based on Slay the Spire are included in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls Requiem.
A Spyreling from Slay the Spire appears in Moonstone Island.
Cosmetics based on Slay the Spire appear in Spiritfall as part of an update.
Cards based on Slay the Spire appeared in Balatro as part of the "Friends of Jimbo 2" update.

Slayaway Camp.description: The character Bob is influenced by the Twin Peaks character of the same name.
Slayaway Camp feature many references to Friday the 13th most notably killers dressed as Jason appear in the game.
The character Frankie is a reference to Five Nights at Freddy's.
The character Bucky Doll is influenced by Chucky.

An outfit based on Agent 47 from Hitman that gives Agent 47's weapon and abilities is available in Sleeping Dogs as part of the Square Enix Character Pack.

A Portal-themed t-shirt is available in Sleeping Dogs as part of the Valve T-Shirt Pack.
