Penny says 'Snakes On A Train' in the Inspector Gadget episode "Train-ing Day".

Snatcher.description: Snatcher is heavily inspired by Blade Runner in aesthetics and plot elements.
Random Hajime from Snatcher is visually inspired by the appearance of Feyd-Rautha Harkonnen from the 1984 film Dune.
The Snatchers are visually inspired by the appearance of The Terminator's robot skeleton.

A Metal Gear called Mk. II makes an appearance in Snatcher, and it later returns in Metal Gear Solid 4, while the Snatchers appear as enemies in the DLC mission Jamais Vu from Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes. There also are other references between the two series.
A person dressed as H2O from Allstar Wars, a parody of C-3PO from Star Wars, can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the original versions of Snatcher.
A person dressed as Omen Rider, a parody of Kamen Rider, can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the original versions of Snatcher.
A person dressed as Korneliussan from Stuffing of the Ape, a parody of Cornelius from Planet of the Apes, can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the original versions of Snatcher.
A person dressed as Eiliyan, a parody of the Xenomorph from Alien, can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the original versions of Snatcher.

A person dressed as Okanesan, a parody of Kanegon from Ultra Q, can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the original versions of Snatcher; there's also a mask based on Ultraman and the "Dadada Mask" is based on the Dada Alien from Ultraman.
A Moai mask from Gradius can be bought at the Joy Division store in all versions of Snatcher.
A Snatcher is a playable character in Hai no Majutsushi.

People dressed as Bill and Lance can be seen in "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the Sega CD version of Snatcher, Stage 3 in Contra III: The Alien Wars (Neo Kobe Steel Factory) is set in Neo Kobe, the setting of Snatcher, and features Snatcher-looking androids as end bosses.
A person dressed as Gullyver, a parody of Guyver, can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the PC Engine port of Snatcher.
A mask that resembles Kinnikuman's mask can be seen at the Joy Division store in the PC Engine and later ports of Snatcher.

A person dressed as Goemon can be seen in "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the Sega CD and later ports of Snatcher, and the main characters discusses the Ganbare Goemon series. Gillian Seed makes a cameo in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu.

People dressed as Simon Belmont and Dracula can be seen in "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the Sega CD and later ports of Snatcher, and at one point the main character makes a comment about the gameplay in the first Castlevania.
A person dressed as Sparkster can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the Sega CD port of Snatcher, and the main characters briefly discuss the Rocket Knight series.
The "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" bartender wears a mask based on Brainy from Monster Maulers in the Sega CD and later ports of Snatcher.
Neo Kobe 2045 Speed King is set in Neo Kobe, the setting of Snatcher, and the Tri-Cycle is a secret playable vehicle.

TwinBee and Madoka appear on a television ad in Alton Plaza, people dressed as Light and Pastel from TwinBee appear at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" and a Pastel image appears on a disconnected call in the PlayStation/Saturn port of Snatcher.
A person dressed as Power Pro-kun can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the PlayStation/Saturn port of Snatcher.
A Koitsu Mask based on the Parodius character can be found at the Joy Division store in the PlayStation/Saturn port of Snatcher, while Hikaru appears on a television ad in Alton Plaza.
A Snatcher is a selectable character in Jikkyō Power Pro Wrestling '96: Max Voltage under the name "Mister Snatcher".
The theme "Snatcher -Dual Vacuum Mix-" from Beatmania Append ClubMIX is from Snatcher.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Snatcher and SD Snatcher.

One can find a dead man named Gibson in Fallout 3, found decapitated and in the same pose as the Snatcher character Jean Jack Gibson. The body holds a note stating "Search the House!", another nod to Snatcher.

Snipperclips.description: Snip and Clip appear as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

Snorks.description: The Snorks appear in Laugh Busters.
Posters with creatures resembling the Snorks appear in The Further Adventures of SuperTed episode "Bubbles, Bubbles Everywhere".
A bootleg Snork appears in Rescue Rangers (2022).

Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (Disney).description: Snow White characters appear alongside Mickey Mouse characters in the promotional shorts The Standard Parade and All Together, in many comic stories, in the House of Mouse series, in Epic Mickey: Power of Illusion and in the Mickey Mouse episode "Wish Upon a Coin"; the story Seven Dwarfs and Mickey Mouse: Diamond Mine Dilemma is a crossover between the two series; Mickey Mouse is also seen playing a Snow White fighting game in the short Runaway Brain; additionally Mizrabel from Castle of Illusion is likely based on the Queen from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
In the Donald Duck cartoon The Riveter, Donald sings the song "Heigh Ho" from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
Thumper and the Seven Dwarfs is a crossover between Bambi and Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
Snow White, the Witch, and the Seven Dwarfs appear in Who Framed Roger Rabbit.
A clip from Snow White and the Seven Dwarves is shown in Gremlins.
A clip from Snow White and the Seven Dwarves is shown in Flubber.
Characters from Snow White appear in Disney's Villains' Revenge.
Vicky's kindness portrayal from "Tiny Timmy!" is a satire of Snow White, even the animals helping Vicky clean up the house are a parody of the animals that help Snow White when she needs their help.
Snow White makes her debut in Kingdom Hearts.  Also, Dwarf Woodlands is a stage in Kingdom Hearts: Birth by Sleep which also features characters from Snow White.
Snow White is mentioned in jokes in Toontown.
Snow White and the seven dwarfs appear in Lion King 1½.
The first film is a parody of the fairytale Snow White. The dwarf march and some names from the Disney version are parodied in all three films.
Kilala travels to the world of Snow White in Kilala Princess.
Snow White is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Grasshopper Experiment", while Amy is seen dressed up as Snow White in "The Contractual Obligation Implementation".
A background character resembles Snow White in The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen: Black Dossier.
Grimhilde appears in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
Tony Field says "Snow White was not created by Disney" in the White Collar episode "Pilot".
Accessories based on Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs appeared in Webkinz as part of a special collaboration.
Someone dresses up as Snow White in the Dan Vs. episode: "The Wolf Man".
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs is parodied in the MAD sketch "Snott Pilgrim vs. the Wonderful World of Disney".
A costume of the Evil Queen is playable in Disney Universe.
Snow White appears in Kinect Disneyland Adventures.
Princess Snow White costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 2.
Rufus sings the "Heigh Ho" song from Snow White to taunt the dwarf he finds in the jukebox in Chaos On Deponia.

In Kirby: Triple Deluxe, Queen Sectonia is said to have been bewitched by a magic mirror and driven mad with the desire for perfect beauty and power. This is a nod to the tale of Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
Princess Snow White was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor.
Characters from Snow White and the Seven Dwarves appeared in Towers of Saviors during a special collaboration.
The 7D is a spinoff to Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarves.
Objects from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs appear in Disney Infinity 2.0.
The Evil Queen has a daughter in Disney Channel's movie Descendants.

In Squid Plus One, the scene where the scallops take Squidward's apron references the scene in Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs where the birds take Snow White's cloak and hang it on a coat rack.
A character looking like the dwarf Grumpy appears in a Heathcliff comic strip.
Any Malu tries a Poison apple from Popeye in "PROVANDO COMIDA DE FAMOSOS DESENHOS ANIMADOS!".
Disney Magic Kingdoms features characters from Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
Characters from Snow White appear in Disney Heroes: Battle Mode
Snow White and Grumpy appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Characters from Snow White appear in Disney Sorcerer's Arena.
In Neon Abyss, the Toffee Apple Item is a reference to Snow White.
The Magic Mirror from Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs appears in "Date Night at the Museum".
Snow White is parodied in Les Kassos.
Snow White appears in Cookie Run: Kingdom as part of the Disney Cookie World event.
Items from Snow White appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley.
The Disney series of Lego Minifigures includes Evil Queen.
Cards based on Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs appear in Lorcana.
The world of Snow White appears in the Minecraft Disney Worlds DLC.
Snow White appears in the credits for Wish.
Snow White appears in Disney Speedstorm.
The Evil Queen from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs appears in Disney Villains Cursed Cafe.
There is a puzzle in Disney Solitare that shows a scene from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews Snow White.

Snowpiercer.description: Snowpiercer is mentioned in The Simpsons episode: "Let's Go Fly a Coot". In the episode: "Treehouse of Horror XXXII", the Itchy & Scratchy short "D'oh Piercer" parodies Snowpiercer. The "Wild Bart's Can't Be Token" segment in the episode: "Treehouse of Horror XXXIV" parodies Snowpiercer.
Snowpiercer is parodied in the Robot Chicken episodes: "Robot Chicken Christmas Special: X-Mas United" and "Fila Ogden in: Maggie's Got a Full Load".
Snowpiercer is mentioned in the Riverdale episode: "Chapter Twenty-Four: The Wrestler".
Snowpiercer is mentioned in the Solar Opposites episode: "Hululand".

So Random!.description: So Random! is a spin-off of Sonny with a Chance.
The "Sparrow Family" sketches from So Random! reference Jack Sparrow from Pirates of the Caribbean.
Harry Potter is referenced in several sketches from So Random!.
Miss Piggy from The Muppets appears in an episode of So Random!.
The Suite Life on Deck is referenced in the So Random! sketch "The Lost Episode of 'The Suite Life on Deck'".

Soccer (Nintendo).description: Soccer is featured as an unlockable playable game in Animal Crossing.
The soccer ball from the NES game Soccer is a usable item in Super Smash Bros. Brawl and its sequels.
Soccer can be seen in Animation vs. Super Mario Bros.

Social Monsters.description: 50 First Dates is mentioned in "How to be Internet Famous?".
Slimemantha and Vanity from Social Monsters appear in an official mod for Monster Prom.
Slimemantha and Vanity from Social Monsters make a cameo appearance in Demon Turf.

Sock.description: Characters from Sock appear in Umbilical World.

Sofia the First.description: Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather appear as recurring characters in Sofia the First.  Also, Princess Aurora was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode Holiday in Enchancia. Maleficent's Staff is one of the Wicked Nine.
Cinderella was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode Once Upon a Princess. Lady Tremaine's Key is one of the Wicked Nine.
Accessories based on Sofia the First appeared in Webkinz as part of a special collaboration.

Princess Jasmine and the Magic Carpet were summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode Two to Tangu. Genie's lamp appears in the episode New Genie On The Block. Jafar's Snake Staff is one of the Wicked Nine.
Princess Belle was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode The Amulet and the Anthem.
Princess Ariel was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode The Floating Palace. Ursula's Necklace is one of the Wicked Nine.
Monopoly Junior: Sofia the First is a format crossover between the two series.

Sofia the First.game: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (Disney)
Sofia the First.description: Princess Snow White was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode The Enchanted Feast. The Evil Queen's Crown and Heart Box are one of the Wicked Nine.
Princess Fa Mulan was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode Princesses to the Rescue!. Sword of Shan Yu is one of the Wicked Nine.
Princess Rapunzel was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode The Curse of Princess Ivy. Mother Gothel's Sundrop Flower is one of the Wicked Nine.
Princess Tiana was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode Winter's Gift. Dr. Facilier's Hat is one of the Wicked Nine.
Sofia the First UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Miss Piggy makes an audition for Sofia The First in Muppets Audition For Disney Junior.
The episode In a Tizzy featured Amber in the race dressed like Penelope Pittstop.
The Mountain and the Wind can be seen in the background of the river ride in Sofia the First: The Secret Library.
Princess Merida was summoned by the Amulet of Avalor in the episode The Secret Library. Mor'du's Claw is one of the Wicked Nine.
Winter, a faun, heard about a princess that can freeze anything she touches.  She is most likely referring to Elsa.  Also, Sofia meets Olaf in the episode "Olaf and the Tale of Miss Nettle".
Merlin appears in the episode Gone with the Wand.
Sofia appears in "Big Air Adventure".
Elena of Avalor is a spin-off of Sofia the First.
Sofia and James makes a cameo on the TV in the Mickey Mouse Funhouse episode "Daisy in Movie Magic Land".
Sofia from "Sofia The First" appears as a drawing in Abigail's princess book during the episode "If I Were a Princess".

Gladwell mentioned him writing Luigi's Mansion fanfics in the Solar Opposites episode "The Extremity Triangulator".
Snowpiercer is mentioned in the Solar Opposites episode: "Hululand".

Solar, Man of the Atom.description: The X-O Manowar armor first appears in Solar, Man of the Atom #6. Solar, Man of the Atom and X-O Manowar have appeared in many comics together.
Mothergod from Solar, Man of the Atom appears in several Turok, Dinosaur Hunter comics, while Solar is referenced several times. Turok appears in Solar, Man of the Atom: Hell on Earth #2-4.
Solar appears in Iron Man/X-O Manowar in Heavy Metal.
Solar appears in Gold Key: Alliance.

Solo Leveling.description: The prologue of Solo Leveling mentions a daily quest of 100 push-ups, 100 sit-ups, 100 squats, and running distance of 10 km, a reference to Saitama's daily training in One-Punch Man.
The Ants in Solo Leveling act similarly to the Chimera Ants in Hunter × Hunter.
Seven Knights: Idle Adventure features characters from Solo Leveling as part of a special collaboration.
UniVersus includes a set of cards based on Solo Leveling.
Characters from Solo Leveling appear in Nanatsu no Taizai: Grand Cross as part of a special collaboration.
Jinwoo and Hae-In from Solo Leveling appear as characters in AFK Arena as part of a collaboration event.
Characters from Frieren appear in Solo Leveling: ARISE as part of a collaboration event.

Solomon's Key.description: Bomb Jack can appear in the NES version of Solomon's Key.
Monster Rancher Explorer is a repurposed version of the Japanese original, Solomon's Key. Solomon's Key included references to Monster Rancher.
Arino plays the NES port of Solomon's Key in episode 6.
A costume based on Dana from Solomon's Key appears in Super Swing Golf: Season 2.
3D Dot Game Heroes features two loading screens based on Solomon's Key.
Blocks based on the Solomon's Key series are playable in Blocks That Matter.
The Tecmo 50th Anniversary DLC pack for Dead or Alive 5 Last Round includes a costume for Zack featuring a shirt themed after Solomon's Key.

Soma Bringer.description: Statues resembling the Zohar from Xenogears appear in Soma Bringer.
Idea and Welt from Soma Bringer appear as spirits in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; a music track from the game is also featured in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.

Something About.description: The Monster Hunter series is parodied in several episodes of Something About.
"Something About Yoshi's Island"  and "Something About Yoshi's Story" are parodies of Yoshi's Island and Yoshi's Story respectively.
The Super Smash Bros. series is parodied in several episodes of Something About.
"Something About Fortnite" is a parody of Fortnite.
The Kirby series is parodied in several episodes of Something About.
The Pokémon series is parodied in several episodes of Something About.
The Mario series is parodied in several episodes of Something About.
"Something About Luigi's Mansion" is a parody of Luigi's Mansion.
"Something About Castlevania" is a parody of Castlevania.
"Something About Donkey Kong Country"  and "Something About Donkey Kong Country 2" are parodies of Donkey Kong Country and Donkey Kong Country 2 respectively.
"Something About Star Fox 64" is a parody of Star Fox 64.
The Zelda series is parodied in several episodes of Something About.
"Something About The Typing of the Dead" is a parody of The Typing of the Dead.
"Something About Super Metroid" is a parody of Super Metroid.
"Something About Mega Man X" is a parody of Mega Man X.
"Something About Pac-Man" is a parody of Pac-Man.
"Something About Pikmin is a parody of Pikmin.
"Something About Undertale" is a parody of Undertale.
"Something About Street Fighter II" is a parody of Street Fighter II.
"Something About Resident Evil 4 Remake" is a parody of Resident Evil 4.
"Something About Helldivers 2" is a parody of Helldivers 2.
"Something About Banjo-Kazooie" is a parody of Banjo-Kazooie.

The Sonic series is parodied in several episodes of Something About. "Something About Shadow the Hedgehog" was created as part of a sponsored video to promote the release of Sonic X Shadow Generations.
"Something About Shadow the Hedgehog" was created as part of a sponsored video to promote the release of Sonic X Shadow Generations.
"Something About Left 4 Dead 2" is a parody of Left 4 Dead 2.
"Something About Crash Bandicoot" is a parody of Crash Bandicoot.

Something Rotten!.description: The melody of "Memory" from Cats is heard in Something Rotten!
Seussical is mentioned in Something Rotten!.
Scar from The Lion King features on the fictional cast list in Something Rotten!.
"It's A Hard Knock Life" from Annie is referenced in Something Rotten!
Nostradamus mixes up Hair with Hairspray in Something Rotten!.
A Wicked song is used as the medley of "A Musical" from Something Rotten!.

Something Special.description: Something Special characters appear in Playtime and Playtime Island.
Mr. Tumble appears in CBeebies Storytime.
Mr. Tumble appears in the Justin's House episode "Cat's Lost Bag".
Something Special characters appear in Get Creative.
Mr. Tumble appears in CBeebies Little Learners.
Mr. Tumble appears frequently in CBeebies House.

Son of Zorn.description: Homer Simpson meets Zorn in promotional art for Son of Zorn.
Peter Griffin meets Zorn in promotional art for Son of Zorn. Son of Zorn is mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Married with Cancer".
Bob Belcher meets Zorn in promotional art for Son of Zorn.

SonSon.description: The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in SonSon.
" SON SON " is one of the random placeholder names in the hi-score screen in Exed Exes.
"SON.SON" is one of the default names in the hi-score screen in Commando.
The Dragonfly enemy from SonSon appears as an item in Gun.Smoke.
"SONSON" is one of the default names in the hi-score screen in Side Arms.
The dragonfly and bamboo sprout from SonSon appear as items in several games of the 194X series.
A golden bamboo sprout from SonSon appears as an item in Forgotten Worlds.
Black Tiger features the Spin Skull enemy from SonSon; Black Tiger was later used as the basis for SonSon II, and thus both games share some gameplay elements and enemies.
One of the players in the "Capcom Games" team is named "Sonson", after the series.
Sonson makes a cameo in Chun-Li's stage from Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo.
Sonson, Tonton and Suisui make a cameo appearance in Pocket Fighter.
Capcom Generations 3 includes SonSon.
Sonson appears as an item in Strider 2.
Sonson from Marvel vs. Capcom 2 is the granddaughter of the first game's Sonson.
Sonson and Tonton from SonSon are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2.
A character in Power Pro Kun Pocket 7 is named after Sonson.
SonSon is included in Capcom Classics Collection and Capcom Classics Colection Reloaded.

Three of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure are trophies of the Son Son, Ton Ton and Sui Sui sprites from SonSon, and one of the Bonelich's minigames songs is the game's stage 1 theme.
3D Dot Game Heroes features a loading screen based on SonSon.
"Son Son" is one of the unlockable Nom de Guerres in Lost Planet 2.
Sonson's sprite is part of Arcade Man's attack in Rockman Xover.
The stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several SonSon Arcade cabinets.
Minna to Capcom All Stars and Street Fighter × All Capcom feature characters from SonSon.

Sonson and Tonton are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; a store named "Sonson" also appears in the background of Ryu's and Guy's stages in Street Fighter Alpha and in Luke's story in Street Fighter V.
SonSon is included in Capcom Arcade Cabinet as part of the "Game Pack 5".
The logo and artwork for the "Winter Superhuman Festival" event in Otoranger is inspired by SonSon.
SonSon is included in Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium.

Song of the South.description: Mr. Bluebird from Song of the South makes an appearance in the House of Mouse episode "Pete's One-Man Show".
Br'er Bear appears in Lion King 1½.
Kinect Disneyland Adventures features characters from Song of the South.
Uncle Remus comes out last, talking jive with Mr. Bluebird.

Sonic.description: Sonic the Hedgehog appears as a car ornament in Rad Mobile; its port Gale Racer features ornaments based on other Sonic characters as well.
Enemies resembling Sonic the Hedgehog appear in The Adventures of Quik and Silva.
Flicky appears as a species in the Sonic series.
Sonic posters are featured in the background of the Sega Master System game Tom & Jerry: The Movie.
A picture of Sonic appears in the Arcade game Wally wo Sagase!
In the ending of Zool: Ninja of the Nth Dimension, Zool kicks a blue hedgehog with red sneakers meant to represent Sonic.

The Super Sonic form from the Sonic series resembles the Super Saiyan transformation;The Special Stage in Sonic the Hedgehog 3 & Knuckles as well as a bonus stage in Sonic Mania are based on King Kai's planet;Silver The Hedgehog is based on Future Trunks;The  Sonic Boom episode "Dude, Where's My Eggman?" features a reference to Dragon Ball.
The Pebbler enemy in Secret of Mana may be based on Sonic.
Shining Force II features a secret arena shaped after Sonic.

The ending of the Mega-CD version of The Amazing Spider-Man vs. The Kingpin features an image of Sonic carved on a wall while Stealth The Hedgehog and Professor Egg from Sonic the Hedgehog Issue 149 parody Spiderman and the Green Goblin respectively
Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine is a spin-off of the Sonic series.
Mel Joseph plays Sonic The Hedgehog in the novel Conundrum by Steve Lyons.

In Sonic The Hedgehog #10 from Archie Comics, The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles make a brief cameo. Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is set to include content from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem.
The Mega-CD version of Popful Mail features a small Sonic drawing in a cutscene.
Sonic and Tails appears in the instruction manuals of Game no Kanzume Vol. 1 and Game no Kanzume Vol. 2.
A casino called "Sega SonicS" and a statue of Sonic appear in Stack Columns. Additionally Sonic Pinball Party and Columns Crown were released together in a "2 games in 1" cartridge.
Jazz Jackrabbit's instruction manual features the appearance of a character based on Sonic; also the boss Zoonik is partially based on Sonic.
The Knuckles series is a spin-off of the Sonic series.
Sonic & Knuckles uses some edited sprites borrowed from the Mega Drive port of Strider, which was developed internally by Sega.
In the Space Ghost Coast to Coast episode "Gum, Disease" Space Ghost is seen playing Sonic 3 & Knuckles.
Uniracers features a reference to Sonic.

The Golden Axe appears in the Sonic the Comic story Megadroid. Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed features Gilius from Golden Axe as a selectable racer; the world of Golden Axe is visited in Sonic and Mega Man: Worlds Unite Part 10 - Justice Across Worlds, including appearances of Gillius Thunderhead, Ax Battler and Tyris Flare.
The trident of Trident appears in the Sonic the Comic story Megadroid.
A glyph from Ecco the Dolphin appears in the Sonic the Comic story Megadroid.
In SimCity 2000 for the Sega Saturn a statue of Sonic is unlockable.
A six-part comic book arc based on Rocket Knight Adventures is featured in issues 53 to 58 of Sonic the Comic.

Bart Simpson imagines Sonic in The Simspons episode "Marge Be Not Proud", while a Sonic billboard is featured in the episode "That 90's show" and a charachter based on Sonic can be seen in the episode "The Food Wife".
Toys based on Sonic characters appear in the introduction of the console versions of Fighting Vipers; Sonic and Tails are also included in the game's code, though unused, in the arcade version.
Somebody in a Sonic the Hedgehog costume appears in Jingle All the Way.

Soulcalibur.description: Valkyrie's sword and shield are unlockable in console versions of Soul Edge and SoulCalibur II,  SoulCalibur III and SoulCalibur IV. Cassandra received a bonus costume based on Valkyrie in console ports of SoulCalibur II, and several pieces of her costume are available as custom items in SoulCalibur III and downloadable in SoulCalibur V.

The Blue Crystal Rod is unlockable in console versions of Soul Edge and SoulCalibur II, SoulCalibur III and SoulCalibur IV, and the Red Crystal Rod is unlockable in console ports of SoulCaibur II. Nightmare and Soul Edge appear as cards in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga. Sophitia received a bonus costume based on Princess Ki in console ports of SoulCalibur II, and Gilgamesh's helmet and sword are available as custom items in SoulCalibur III.
One of the horses in Final Furlong is named "Soul Blade".

Yoshimitsu is selectable in SoulCalibur and most later episodes in the series; Heihachi is a guest character in the PlayStation version of SoulCalibur II and Devil Jin's style is usable in SoulCalibur V; there also are other minor references between the two series.
An image of Yoshimitsu from SoulCalibur appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.
Ivy Valentine from SoulCalibur is one of the players in the "Namco All Stars '90" team in World Kicks.
Astaroth from SoulCalibur is selectable in Pac-Man Fever, while a Pac-Man keychain appears as a downloadable item in Soul Calibur V.
Link is a guest character in the GameCube version of SoulCalibur II.
Spawn is a guest character in the Xbox version of SoulCalibur II.
Taki received a bonus costume based on Waya Hime from Bravoman in console ports of SoulCalibur II.
One of Yoshimitsu's swords introduced in SoulCalibur II is named Shiranui, after the main character of Mirai Ninja.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Appare Sandaime and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Soul series.

Raphael and Cassandra from SoulCalibur II are playable characters in Smash Court Tennis Pro Tournament 2, while artwork of the cast of SoulCalibur appears as part of an easter egg in the training mode of Anna Kournikova's Smash Court Tennis.

Veigue from Tales of Rebirth is based on Siegfried from SoulCalibur, he is seen wielding Siegfried's Requiem sword as his strongest weapon, and his "Celsius Calibur" attack summons the Soul Calibur, which can also be obtained as a weapon in Tales of the Heroes: Twin Brave and Tales of the Abyss; a costume of Mitsurugi is DLC in Tales of Vesperia and again with Taki in Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2; Radiant Mythology 2 also features the Soul Edge and Soul Calibur as EX Challenge DLC weapons and the Tales of Arise "Blade of Sealing" artifact is the Soul Embrace from SoulCalibur III; while Lloyd Irving from Tales of Symphonia is a guest character in SoulCalibur Legends.
Namco × Capcom features characters from the Soul series.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are references to the Soul series.

Create-A-Soul mode in SoulCalibur III features Kagekiyo's armor and mask from Genpei Toma Den, and a sword for Yoshimitsu named "Kagekiyo" in reference to its protagonist has existed since SoulCalibur II.
Universal Fighting System includes six sets of cards based on Soul Calibur III and two sets based on Soul Calibur IV.

Characters from The Herculoids appear in the Space Ghost episode "The Molten Monsters of Moltar". Additionally, characters and locations from The Herculoids are frequently mentioned on Space Ghost Coast to Coast.
Characters from Shazzan appear in the Space Ghost episode "The Final Encounter".
Space Ghost and Frankenstein Jr. segments aired together as Space Ghost and Frankenstein Jr.
Space Ghost appears in the Fantastic Max episode "The Big Sleep".
In the Space Ghost Coast to Coast episode "Gum, Disease" Space Ghost is seen playing Sonic 3 & Knuckles.
Joel Hodgson appears in the Space Ghost Coast to Coast episode "$20.01" talking about Mystery Sience Theatre 3000.
Elvira is a guest in the Space Ghost Coast to Coast episode "Switcharoo".
Red Green appears in the Space Ghost Coast to Coast episode "Pavement".
In the Space Ghost episode "Waiting for Edward" Denis Leary mentions Dr. Katz, referencing his appearance as a guest in the Dr. Katz, Professional Therapist episode "Fanny Pack".
The Brak Show is a spin-off of Space Ghost Coast to Coast.
Space Ghost from Space Ghost appears in the Powerpuff Girls episode "Members Only".

Space Ghost appears in the Aqua Teen Hunger Force episodes "The Dressing" and "Multiple Meat". Carl and Carl Jr. from the Space Ghost Coast to Coast episode "Chambraigne" appear in the Aqua Teen Hunger Force episode "Carl Wash". Meatwad and the Cybernetic Ghost of Christmas Past from the Future appear in the Space Ghost special Adult Swim Brain Trust.
Triumph the Insult Comic Dog appears in Space Ghost Coast to Coast episode "Dreams".
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Space Spectre, a parody of Space Ghost.
Space Ghost characters appear in the Season 4 episode "Adam West's Date-O-Rama" from Johnny Bravo.
Early Cuyler appears in the Space Ghost special Adult Swim Brain Trust.
Sharko appears in the Space Ghost special Adult Swim Brain Trust.
Perfect Hair Forever is a spin-off of Space Ghost Coast to Coast.
Space Ghost is the announcer in Cartoon Network: Punch Time Explosion.
Space Ghost appears in the Batman: The Brave and The Bold episode "Bold Beginnings".
Space Ghost appears in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica. Zorak appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #53.
Space Ghost appears in the Wacky Races episode "The Wack Stuff".
Space Ghost appears in Space Jam: A New Legacy.
Several characters from Space Ghost appear in Jellystone!
Space Ghost is mentioned in the Teen Titans Go! episode: "Warner Bros 100th Anniversary".

Space Goofs.description: Etno Polino from Space Goofs meets Hank Hill in a King of the Hill promo on Fox Kids.

Jackie Nacho from Oggy and the Cockroaches appears in the Space Goofs episode Get Off My Couch!, while several other Oggy characters appear in "Space Sailors". Both shows feature several other minor references to each other.
Etno, Gorgious, Bud and Candy appear in the Daltons episode "The Secret Passage".

Space Harrier.description: Fantasy Zone and Space Harrier share a universe. The Sharp X68000 version of Fantasy Zone contains a secret level, Dragon Land, which contains enemies from Space Harrier; Opa-Opa appears as a playable character in Planet Harriers; Space Harrier and Uriah are mentioned in the bad ending of Fantasy Zone II DX.
A picture of Harrier from Space Harrier can be found in the Comet Museum level of Bonanza Bros.
Space Harrier is featured as a fully playable Arcade game and a set of Capsule Toys within Shenmue and Shenmue II.
Enemies from Space Harrier II make an appearance in Segagaga.
Sega Superstars Tennis features a minigame based on Space Harrier.
Bayonetta features a minigame based on Space Harrier, also including a music track from the game.
3D Dot Game Heroes features a loading screen based on Space Harrier.
Music from Space Harrier was added to maimai in the maimai PLUS version.
Sega 3D Reprint Archives features Space Harrier and Space Harrier 3-D with Harrier interacting with other characters in the credits.
The Sega Hard Girls view the world of Space Harrier in the fifth episode of Sega Hard Girls.  Also, the girls enter the world of Space Harrier in the episode “I Heard We're Graduating Sehaga”.
The Space Harrier is a DLC plane in Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours as part of the Sega DLC Pack.
Harrier and Binsbein are unlockable in the retail release of 3D Power Drift. Additionally, course A of the Special Mode of 3D Power Drift has a medley of Space Harrier tracks as its music.
The protagonist from Space Harrier appears in Kyoutou Kotoba RPG: Kotodaman during a "Sega All Stars" collaboration.
Wi Wi Wumbo from Space Harrier appears as a collectible in SEGA AGES Columns II.
A Space Harrier arcade machine appears in Earth UFO Catcher.
Harrier from Space Harrier appears in the Herzog Academy mode of SEGA AGES Herzog Zwei.
A decoration of a mammoth from Space Harrier can be obtained in Two Point Hospital as part of the SEGA 60th Items DLC.
Music from Space Harrier can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix after an update.
Picross S Genesis & Master System Edition includes puzzles based off Space Harrier.
Arino plays the SMS and Sega Saturn ports of Space Harrier in episode 332.
A human version of Space Harrier appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.
In C.H.A.I.N.G.E.D., "Time Harrier" is an homage to Space Harrier.

Space Invaders.description: The 111th episode of the Lupin the Third Part II anime features the Space Invaders Arcade game prominently.
Radar Scope has elements inspired from Space Invaders.
Characters from Space Invaders appears in the game Gorf.
The 1st episode of the 2nd season and the 3rd episode of the 5th season of Danger Mouse feature references to Space Invaders.
The character of Michael in E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial wears a Space Invaders t-shirt.
A white Invader from Space Invaders makes a cameo in Slap Fight, and many appear as enemies in Slap Fight Tiger.
ALF plays the Atari 2600 version of Space Invaders in the episode "Border Song".
A Space Invaders arcade cabinet can be found in Spaceballs.
The player's ball in Calmetry can be changed to a space invader from Space Invaders.
Space Invaders is mentioned in issue 2 of the comic Men In Black.
Battletoads features enemies based on the aliens from Space Invaders.
The Arcade Space Invaders is featured in Terminator 2: Judgment Day, and it is also referenced in Terminator: The Sarah Connor Chronicles.

The cannon from Space Invaders is an assist character in Bubble Symphony and the "Invader" enemy is based on the eponymous aliens; Stage 3 and 4 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Bubble Bobble and Rainbow Island respectively and feature a playable Bub in dragon and human form; while he, Bob and Drunk are among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
One of the players in the "Taito Planets" team from Super Kyuukyoku Harikiri Stadium 2 is named "Invader", after the series.

Stage 1 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on The New Zealand Story and features a playable Tiki; he's also one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.

Stage 2 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on The Fairyland Story and features a playable Ptolemy; she's also one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Stage 4 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Rainbow Islands and features a playable Bubby; and Bubby is one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Stage 5 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Liquid Kids and features a playable Hipopo.

Stage 6 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Arkanoid and features a playable Vaus; while Stage 5 in Arkanoid is patterned after an invader alien and Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders is a crossover between both franchises.

Stage 7 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Kiki KaiKai and features a playable Sayo-chan/Pocky; she's also one of the playable characters in Space Invaders '95: The Attack of Lunar Loonies and is one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.

Stage 8 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Darius and features a playable Silver Hawk; the ship also appears as one of the playable vehicles in Space Invaders '95: The Attack of Lunar Loonies, as DLC in Space Invaders Get Even and Space Invaders: Infinity Gene (version 3.0); while Proco, Iron Fossil and Great Thing are among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, and Space Invaders 2000 includes a demo of G-Darius.
Stage 9 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on Don Doko Don and features a playable Bob.
There's a reference to Space Invaders in the 2nd half of the Who Shot Mr. Burns? special from The Simpsons.
Stage 5 in Game Tengoku features a parody of Space Invaders.
The 6th episode of the 2nd season of ReBoot features a reference to Space Invaders.
PD Ultraman Invaders is a format crossover between both series.
There's a reference to Space Invaders in the live action Inspector Gadget film.
Space Invaders is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One with Ross's Denial".
Space Invaders is mentioned in the Freaks and Geeks episode: "The Garage Door".
An Invader alien doll is one of the items to buy in the "Be a good buyer!" mini-game from Power Shovel.
Space Invaders appear as some of the video game characters in Futurama's episode Anthology of Interest II, while Hermes can be seen playing the game in Attack of the Killer App.
The Space Invaders appear as graffiti creatures in Magic Pengel: The Quest for Color and Graffiti Kingdom.
Space Invaders/Qix - Silver Anniversary Edition is a compilation of both series.

The boss in Area D and E of Spica Adventure is the shadowy figure seen in cabinet and flyer artwork for Space Invaders imitating the way invaders attack and behave in the series, while Nico from Spica Adventure appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Several Space Invaders games are included in Taito Memories Joukan, Gekan and Memories II Joukan.
Space Invaders × Pac-Man is a crossover between the two series.
Several Space Invaders games are included in Taito Memories Legends, Legends 2 and Legends Power-Up.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are Space Invaders references.
Space Invaders gets spoofed several times in Robot Chicken.
Sheldon is seen wearing a Space Invaders t-shirt in several episodes of The Big Bang Theory, first seen on the 10th episode of Season 1, "The Loobenfeld Decay".

Space Invaders.game: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
Space Invaders.description: Flint Lockwood from Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs wears a t-shirt with a drawing resembling the Space Invaders.
Space Invaders can be played in Machinarium.
Stage 6 in Touhou Seirensen~ Undefined Fantastic Object features references to Space Invaders.

In The Cent of Money, when the scene shows the fish playing the arcade games, one of them has creatures that look and move like the aliens from Space Invaders. In the episode That Sinking Feeling, the underground chase is a reference to the arcade game Dig Dug.
The Black Fry ship and a stage pack based on Metal Black are DLC in version 3.0 of Space Invaders: Infinity Gene.
Space Invaders is referenced several times in Ready Player One and Ready Player Two; Halliday wears a Space Invaders t-shirt in the movie.
Groove Coaster is a spin-off of Space Invaders.
Angry Birds Space features a level based on Space Invaders.
The aliens from Space Invaders appear in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
The episode "The Phone" of The Amazing World of Gumball features several references to Space Invaders. The character Ocho is also designed after the titular aliens.
An arcade cabinet for Space Invaders can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
At one point in Guacamelee! there are bricks forming the shape of the aliens in Space Invaders.
At one point in Saints Row IV a number of spaceships imitate the formation and movement of the aliens in Space Invaders.
Aliens from Space Invaders appeared in Puzzle & Dragons during the GROOVE COASTER collab event.
In the Rick and Morty Pilot, during the Interdimensional Customs scene, a silhouette of an Alien Invader appears.
Jazzpunk features a hidden minigame that plays identically to Space Invaders.
A picture of an alien from Space Invaders appears in Please, Don't Touch Anything.
Space Invaders is mentioned several times in Armada.
The Space Invaders ships appear among the many videogame characters in the movie Pixels, while the Pixels version of the Invader is an event character in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
In the 2nd episode of the 5th season of American Horror Story Holden can be seen playing Space Invaders for the Atari.
In Night Blights, there is a game about shooting Night Blights in space, a reference to Space Invaders.
The title card for Space Invader gives a reference to the game it is named after.
A Space Invaders arcade cabiet can be seen in the Black Mirror episode: "San Junipero".
Chack'n and Monsta from Chack'n Pop appear among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Kage from The Legend of Kage appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
The Spy from Elevator Action appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
The main characters from The Ninja Warriors appear among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Reika Kirishima from Time Gal appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Nancy from Chase H.Q. appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Sonic Blast Man appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Zac from Pu·Li·Ru·La appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Lufia from Lufia & the Fortress of Doom appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Burn, Emilio, Keith and Wendy from Psychic Force appear among the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
C-Mond from Puchi Carat appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Patrako from Cleopatra Fortune appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Space Invaders is referenced in Chuchel.
In the stage "The Arctic Cruise" from A Hat in Time: Seal the Deal there's a monitor displaying a game of Space Invaders.
In a video of the Shovelwarewolf he plays a Space Invaders game.
The invaders appeared in SINoALICE during a special collaboration.
The level "Baba Invaders" is inspired by Space Invaders.
Space Invaders can be seen in Animation vs. Arcade Games.
An anvil skin of the alien appears in the shop.
Space Invaders memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".

Space Manbow.description: Mambo and Sambo from Gokujo Parodius and Sexy Parodius are inspired by Space Manbow.
The MANBOU-J from Space Manbow is playable in Airforce Delta Storm and Airforce Delta Strike.
The Space Manbow enemy ship appears in the background of the "Space Manbo" Yu-Gi-Oh card, itself a reference as well.
Space Manbow can be unlocked in Ganbare Goemon: Tōkai Dōchū Oedo Tengu ri Kaeshi no Maki.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Space Manbow.
Space Manbow puzzles are featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.

Space Odyssey.description: The soundtrack album of 2001 is displayed in Clockwork Orange.
R.O.K. from Airplane II: The Sequel is a parody of HAL-9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey.
A Space Odyssey video case is shown in Video Violence.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! live action episode "9001: A Mario Odyssey" is a parody of 2001: A Space Odyssey.
A monolith looking like the one in 2001: Space Odissey is featured in SimEarth.
2010 video case appears in Last Action Hero.
Koichi mentions 2001: A Space Odyssey in the first chapter of Vento Aurero.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 2, Level 7 "Lunar Reactor" features a warp resembling the monolith from 2001: Space Odyssey.
A giant domino resembling the monolith appears in Men In White.
In the PJs episode "House Potty" a robot toilet resembles HAL 9000 from Space Odyssey.

The SpongeBob episodes Sandy's Rocket and Ugh feature references to 2001: A Space Odyssey. In the episode Squidward in Clarinetland, SpongeBob and Squidward tumbling through space to classical music is a reference to 2001: A Space Odyssey.
AL from Dr. Muto is a parody of HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey.
In a space shot in (T)Raumschiff Surprise - Periode 1 "An der schönen, blauen Donau" is playing.
A monolith from Space Odyssey appears in Tom And Jerry: Blast Off To Mars.
HAL 9000 from Space Odyssey can be read on the papers in the Robot Chicken episode "Kiddie Pool".
2001 and 2010 are recreated by the characters in Be Kind Rewind.
A monolith looking like the one in 2001: Space Odyssey is featured in Spore.
2001: A Space Odyssey is referenced in several episodes of The Big Bang Theory.
Space Odyssey is parodied in the Phineas And Ferb episode "Mommy Can You Hear Me".
2010 is mentioned in Ready Player One, while HAL-9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey is mentioned in Ready Player Two.

Space Odyssey.game: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl
Space Odyssey.description: Earl and Greg create a spoof of 2001: A Space Odyssey in Me and Earl and the Dying Girl (book).
HAL 9000 has been a rapper for Epic Rap Battles of History.
The Monolith is mentioned in The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen: Century - 2009.
The achievement "Trustworthy Auto-Pilot" is a reference to 2001: A Space Odyssey.
Lil Hal in Homestuck references HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey.
A 2001: A Space Odyssey VHS can be found in Gone Home.
Linkara reviews 2001: A Space Odyssey #1.
The Discovery appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #41. HAL 9000 appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #53.
Gumball and Darwin time travel to when the ape found his weapon in the AWOG episode "The Countdown".
2001: A Space Odyssey and 2010: The Year We Make Contact are mentioned several times in Armada.
HAL 9000 appears in the game.
One of the dialogue options with John 3000 in Paradigm is "Hey dude, do your HAL 9000 impression."
In Lego Movie 2 the door resembles the Monolith from Space Odyssey.
It is mentioned 2001's BOWMAN expedition have discovered a monolith on Jupiter in the fifth issue of Tempest.
A poster for 2001: A Space Odyssey can be seen in Harley Quinn: Breaking Glass.
An AI is referred to as "HAL" in AI: The Somnium Files, referencing HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey.
HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey is mentioned in Murder by Numbers.
PAL and Mark Bowman are direct references to HAL 9000 and David Bowman.

Space Odyssey.game: Apollo 10 ½: A Space Age Childhood
Space Odyssey.description: Stanley watches 2001: A Space Odyssey in cinemas in Apollo 10 ½: A Space Age Childhood.

Space Patrol Luluco.description: Wooser makes multiple cameo appearances throughout Space Patrol Luluco.
Luluco and Nova visit the planet of Little Witch Academia in the Space Patrol Luluco episode "Mysterious Power's Trap".
Luluco visits the world of Inferno Cop and meets Inferno Cop himself in Space Patrol Luluco.

Space Quest.description: The Space Quest series frequently references Star Trek.
The Space Quest series frequently references Star Wars.
Space Quest is mentioned many times in the Police Quest series.
Roger Wilco can appear in the piano lounge in Leisure Suit Larry 3. Both series also contain numerous minor references to each other.

Roger Wilco from Space Quest appears as an opponent in Hoyle's Official Book of Games: Volume 1, Volume 3, and Hoyle Classic Card Games. Arnoid and Vohaul from Space Quest appear as opponents in Volume 3.
A game called "SimSim" is mentioned in Space Quest.
The Planet Pinball tables in Take a Break! Pinball are based on Space Quest IV.
Cedric from King's Quest V makes a cameo in Space Quest 6. Additionally, both series make several other minor references to one another.

Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator.description: Content based on Among Us is included in the Bean Bone update for Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator.
The boxes from Unpacking appear in Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator as part of the Omega Update.
The Journalist from Bugsnax appear in Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator as part of the Omega Update.
Leshy from Inscryption appear in Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator as part of the Omega Update.

Spaceballs.description: Spaceballs is a parody of the Star Wars series.
Max Headroom is parodied in Spaceballs.
Rocky VHS tapes appear in Spaceballs.
A Space Invaders arcade cabinet can be found in Spaceballs.
Star Trek is mentioned in Spaceballs.
Transformers is mentioned in Spaceballs.
The head of the Mega Maid crashes into a planet and a pair of apes discover it in Spaceballs, resembling the ending scene of Planet Of The Apes.
A chestburster appears in Spaceballs.
Lone Starr and Barf appear in the Deep Space 69 episode “License to Bone”.
Spaceballs is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Double Date".
Eagle 5 from Spaceballs appears in Ready Player One.
Agent Dunfore drives the Eagle 5.
Dune is mentioned in Spaceballs 2 Teaser.
Jurassic Park is mentioned in Spaceballs 2 Teaser.
Avatar is mentioned in Spaceballs 2 Teaser.
the MCU is mentioned in Spaceballs 2 Teaser.
The Lion King is mentioned in Spaceballs 2 Teaser.
Harry Potter is mentioned in Spaceballs 2 Teaser.
Predator is mentioned in Spaceballs 2 Teaser.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews Spaceballs.

Spaced.description: A Sixth Sense poster is shown in the Spaced episode "Dissolution".
In several episodes of Spaced, the characters can be seen playing Resident Evil 2 and making references to the series.
Tomb Raider 3 is played in the Spaced episode "Battles".
In the Spaced episode "Ends", one of the main characters is seen playing Tekken 3.
Spaced is mentioned several times in Ready Player One.

Spark the Electric Jester.description: Spark the Electric Jester's gameplay takes a lot of inspiration from the Sonic the Hedgehog series and features many references to the series.
Spark from Spark the Electric Jester is featured as a playable character.
Spark makes a cameo in Indie Pogo.
Spark the Electric Jester 2 features a jester power based on Corazon from Freedom Planet.
Fark from Spark the Electric Jester is a playable character in Cross Impact.

Spawn.description: Spawn and Savage Dragon appears in several issues of each other's comics.
Cerebus appears in Spawn #10.
Batman and Spawn had a comic book crossover together.
Medieval Spawn/Witchblade is a crossover between both series.
Spawn appears in Mars Attacks Image #1, #3 and #4.
In Gen¹³ #13, many characters make an appearance including Spawn.
In Sonic Super Special Issue #7 Spawn appears in a panel and confuses Sonic and Knuckles for kids in costumes.
A parody of Spawn called "Sppon" is featured within Segagaga.
Spawn is a guest character in the Xbox version of SoulCalibur II.
Spawn appears in Invincible #60.
Linkara reviews Spawn #1.
Spawn has been a subject for Death Battle!
The Necroplasmic Mantle from Volume 2 of Overlord is implied to be based on the cape of Spawn.
Spawn's antagonist Angela, was integrated into the Marvel Universe in the story "Age of Ultron". She was later established to be the lost sister of Thor.
Spawn toys are shown in Cooties
The Nostalgia Critic reviews "Spawn (film)".
Spawn has been a subject for DBX.
Spawn and Chapel appear in I Hate Image.
Spawn appears as an OASIS player avatar in Ready Player One.
A Spawn toy can be seen in Comic Man's room.
The 174th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Spawn games.
Spawn is a DLC character in the first Kombat Pack for Mortal Kombat 11.
Spawn appears in Crossover #2 and #10.
Spawn appears in Killadelphia #30 and #31.
Spawn appears as an operator in Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 along with other Spawn cosmetics.

Special Agent Oso.description: Manny, The Tools and Kelly appears in the Special Agent Oso episode "The Manny with the Golden Bear".

Spectre (DC Comics).description: Bionicle characters Tahu, Gali, Lewa and Pohatu make a background cameo in Spectre Vol 4 10.
Scribblenauts Unmasked features spawnable characters from the Spectre series.
The Spectre appears in Scooby Doo Team Up #13.
The Spectre appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #52.

Speed (20th Century Studios).description: Speed is parodied in the Animaniacs episode "Gimme A Break".
Speed is mentioned by Edgar in the Red Green Show episode "Men's Night on the Mountain".
Speed is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Citation Negation”.
Speed 2 is mentioned in the Supernatural episode "Werther Project".
Several characters are seen watching Speed in Sonic The Hedgehog (2020). Ivo Robotnik mentions Speed in Sonic the Hedgehog 3.
Terry mentions Speed and Speed 2 in the Solar Opposites episode "The Earth Eraser".

Speed Buggy.description: Scooby-Doo meets Speed Buggy in The New Scooby-Doo Movies. Characters from Speedy Buggy appear in the Scooby-Doo: Mystery Incorporated episode "Mystery Solvers Club State Finals" and the Scooby Doo and Guess Who? episode "A Mystery Solving Gang Divided".
Speed Buggy and Tinker from Speed Buggy appear in Laff-A-Lympics.
Speed Buggy appears as a cameo in the Johnny Bravo episode "Bravo Dooby Doo".
Several Speed Buggy characters appear in the Harvey Birdman episode "High Speed Buggy Chase".
Speed Buggy is mentioned in the Futurama episode "Law and Oracle".
The Flash/Speed Buggy Special is a crossover between the two series.
Speed Buggy, Mark, Debbie and Tinker appear in the Animaniacs reboot episode "Suffragette City".
Speed Buggy and Tinker appear in Jellystone!

Speed Racer.description: Speed Racer is parodied in Adolescent Radioactive Black Belt Hamsters Massacre The Japanese Invasion.
Speed Racer has a comic book crossover with Ninja High School.

A Speed Racer poster can be seen in the Friends episodes: "The One Where Monica Gets a Roommate" and "The One with All the Poker". Chandler wears a Speed Racer shirt in the episodes: "The One with the Boobies" and "The One That Could Have Been: Part 2". Speed Racer is mentioned in the episode: "The One Where Dr. Ramoray Dies".
The Speed Racer car appears in Shadow Warrior.
Having saved data of Speed Racer unlocks the special "Speed" dragon in Dragonseeds.
Speed Racer appears in the Family Guy episode "The Son Also Draws".
Reese sings the Speed Racer theme in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Forwards Backwards".
In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Go Racer Go!, a parody of Speed Racer.
Speed Racer UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Speed Racer Characters appear as U.B. Funkeys.
Speed Racer is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Bath Item Gift Hypothesis".
Speed Racer is mentioned in Ready Player One.
The Mach 5 appears in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
Speed Racer appears in the movie.
Characters from Speed Racer appeared in LINE Pokopang during a collaboration event.

SpeedRunners.description: Pilgor from Goat Simulator is a playable character in SpeedRunners.
The Scout from Team Fortress 2 is a playable character in SpeedRunners.
SpeedRunner is a playable character in Cook, Serve, Delicious!.
The Cosmonaut Comrade from SpeedRunners appears in the multiplayer mode of Giana Sisters Twisted Dreams.
The Gang Beasts are playable characters in SpeedRunners.
Characters from Payday are playable characters in SpeedRunners. Masks based on SpeedRunners characters were added to Payday 2.
Qwop is a playable character in SpeedRunners.
Octodad is a playable character in SpeedRunners.
Characters from SpeedRunners appear in Toto Temple Deluxe.

Spelunker.description: Taiko no Tatsujin 11, Taiko no Tatsujin DS: Nanatsu no Shima no Daibouken and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track from Spelunker.
3D Dot Game Heroes features an unlockable "Spelunker Mode" where the player controls the Spelunker; there also are two loading screens based on Spelunker.
Arino plays the NES port of Spelunker as part of a DVD-exclusive GameCenter CX challenge.
Backpacks based on Turo and Kuro could be worn in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.

Characters from Hyperdimension Neptunia Victory II appear in Spelunker as part of a special collaboration. Additionally, the "Neplunker" mode in Hyperdimension Neptunia Victory II is based on Spelunker.
Costumes based on Atlantis no Nazo appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Items and costumes from Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Items and costumes from Secret of Mana appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Items and costumes from Final Fantasy Type-0 appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Costumes from Lode Runner appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Costumes from Just Cause appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.
Costumes based on Thief Arthur and Uathach from Million Arthur appear in Spelunker World as part of a collaboration event.

Several Bubble Bobble character costumes are featured in Spelunker World as part of a Taito collaboration event.
Costume parts and the Exorcism Wand of Sayo-chan/Pocky are featured in Spelunker World as part of a Taito collaboration event.
Costumes based on Proco and Tiat's uniforms from Darius and several other related items are featured in Spelunker World as part of a Taito collaboration event.
There are references to Spelunker in episode 4 of Pop Team Epic.

Spelunky.description: Spelunky Explorer is an unlockable character in Super Crate Box.
Spelunky is an unlockable character in Super Meat Boy for consoles and later Meat Boy is unlockable in the HD remake of Spelunky.
A block based on Spelunky is playable in Blocks That Matter.
