Splatoon squids can be collected in an event in Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp; Animal Crossing: New Leaf also features Splatoon-themed items and furniture and the character of Cece cosplays as Callie from Splatoon.
Inkling costumes for Miis are downloadable in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U and for 3DS. Also, Inklings are playable in Super Smash Bros. for Switch.
Tetris 99 featured a Splatoon 2 theme during a limited event.
Splatoon characters are parodied in Console Wars.
A music track from Splatoon 2 appears in the Rhythm Game mode of Ring Fit Adventure.
Costumes based on Inkling Girl and Inkling Boy were added to Jump Rope Challenge with Update 1.1.0.
Meggy from Sunset Paradise is designed off of an Inkling from Splatoon.

A microgame version of Splatoon 2 is featured in WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with its on-screen instructions; additionally Wario can draw a sketch of Splatoon characters in WarioWare Gold by scanning the respective amiibo.
A squid from Splatoon appears in Zanta's stone tablet in "The Chronicles of Santa".

Splatterhouse.description: The Terror Mask was originally designed after Jason's iconic hockey mask. One achievement/trophy in the 2010 Splatterhouse references Jason Vorhees.

The Evil Hand enemy from Splatterhouse is a reference to Evil Dead, and laughing deer heads are featured in Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti and Splatterhouse 2. In the 2010 Splatterhouse Phase Four: "The Meat Factory", Rick finds a shotgun next to a corpse that looks similar to Ashley William, missing hand included.
The Stage 1, Area 2 boss in Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti is a parody of the film The Exorcist.

The Stage 3, Area 1 boss in Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti is a parody of the film Alien. On the North American and European Splatterhouse 2 boxart, there's a monster that strongly resembles an adult Xenomorph.
The Stage 3, Area 3 boss in Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti is a parody of the film The Fly.
Rick Taylor from Splatterhouse appears among the crowd in Japan League stadiums from Kyūkai Dōchūki.
A theme park attraction based on the West Mansion from Splatterhouse can be seen at the Theme Park course in Anna Kournikova's Smash Court Tennis.
An image of Rick from Splatterhouse appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.
Rick from Splatterhouse makes a cameo appearance in Tales of Eternia, while Tales of Phantasia features a place called "The Splatterhouse Inn".
Rick from Splatterhouse is a selectable character in Family Tennis Advance.
The item "Rick's Mask" in Namco × Capcom references Splatterhouse.
A remix of the ending theme from Splatterhouse is featured in We Love Katamari.
The Terror Mask from Splatterhouse is a customization item (named "Splatter Mask") for Craig Marduk in the PSP port of Tekken 5: Dark Ressurection.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of the Splatterhouse Terror Mask with Rick assisting the player.
In the 2010 Splatterhouse Phase Six: "Beast With a Human Heart", a burnt corpse wearing Freddy's glove is seen near a boiler. Nearby it is Freddy's red and green sweater.
In the 2010 Splatterhouse Phase Two: "The Meat Factory", Rick can spot an inanimate Chucky-like toy under a bed, next to a bloodied knife.
Rick Taylor from Splatterhouse is a playable character in Namco Chronicle, with Biggy Man, Revival Dead and Jennifer appearing as enemies.
The Terror Mask from Splatterhouse is included in the SoulCalibur V donwloadable pack Miscellaneous Equipment 1.

Pac-Man Monsters features Rick from Splatterhouse, and a theme featuring characters from Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti appears in Pac-Man 99; additionally Splatterhouse is included in Pac-Man's Pixel Bash!.

Famista Dream Match and Famista Climax feature Rick from Splatterhouse as a guest player; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels is called "Rick".
Rick from Splatterhouse makes an appearance in Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition.
Splatterhouse is included in Namco Museum for the Nintendo Switch and Namco Museum Mini Player alongside Splatterhouse II, while Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Grafitti is included in Namcot Collection.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Splatterhouse.

Splice.description: Splice is mentioned in the Family Guy episode: "Baby Stewie".

Spliced.description: One of Peri's quotes in the Spliced episode "Bowled Over" is a reference to He-Man and the Masters of the Universe.
Jason's mask appears briefly in the Spliced episode "Cleaning Up".
The arcade game is spoofed briefly in the Spliced episode "Honorary Freak".
The Donkey Kong arcade game is spoofed in the Spliced episode "Octocataclysm". One of Entree's udders in the episode "Juice", Cranky, holds a cane as a reference to Cranky Kong.
The title of the Spliced episode "Nightmare on Condemned Street" is a reference to Nightmare on Elm Street.
One of Entree's quotes in the Spliced episode "Nightmare on Condemned Street" is a reference to Star Wars.
The title card of the Spliced episode "One Joe Wingus" is a reference to For the Birds.

Splinter Cell.description: Sam Fisher appears in the Video Mods original video "Stand and Choose".
In Metal Gear Solid 3, Snake mentions "Sam", likely referring to Sam Fisher from Splinter Cell, in "Snake vs Monkey".

The USS Clarence E. Walsh from Ghost Recon 2 appears in the PlayStation 2 version of Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory; Third Echelon from Splinter Cell is mentioned in Ghost Recon: Advanced Warfighter 2; Sam Fisher's stealth suit from Spinter Cell appears in Ghost Recon Online; Sam Fisher from Splinter Cell appears in Ghost Recon: Wildlands and Ghost Recon: Breakpoint.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are Splinter Cell references.
Third Echelon from Splinter Cell is mentioned in H.A.W.X.
Sam Fisher from the Splinter Cell game series makes an appearance in Academy of Champions: Football.
Rabbid Plush Toys can be found in Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Conviction; additionally the Bunny Fisher rabbid and the Sam Kingfisher Grenaduck are based on Sam Fisher.
Anna Grimsdottir from Splinter Cell appears in EndWar: The Hunted; "The End Begins: Splinter Cell" is a crossover between the two series.
The design of the Lez's night vision suit in "BIRTHDAY BASH" is based on Sam fisher's signature trifocal goggles and suit from Splinter Cell.
The Xbox 360 version of Rayman Legends features exclusive costumes based on Splinter Cell.
Skin Pack 5 in the Minecraft Xbox 360 and Xbox One Editions features skins based off characters from Splinter Cell.
A costume based on Splinter Cell appears in Tom Clancy's The Division as a Ubisoft Club reward. A costume based on Sam Fisher from Splinter Cell appears in The Division 2.
Sam Fisher's stealth suit can be obtained in Far Cry New Dawn.
Characters and locations from Splinter Cell appear in Tom Clancy's Elite Squad.
Sam Fisher appears as an operator under the name "Zero" in Rainbow Six: Siege as part of the Operation Shadow Legacy expansion.
Sam Fisher can be found in Growtopia as part of the 2022 UbiWeek event.
Sarah Fisher and Sam Fisher from Splinter Cell appear in Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix.
Echelon from Splinter Cell appears as a faction in XDefiant.

Spoilsbury Toast Boy.description: Characters from Spoilsbury Toast Boy appear in Umbilical World.

SpongeBob SquarePants.description: There's a comic book based on SpongeBob SquarePants in the Hey Arnold episode "Weighing Harold".

In the episode Plankton!, Plankton saying "You weak-minded fool!" is a reference to Star Wars: Return of the Jedi. In Sandy, SpongeBob, and the Worm, the scene where Sandy enters the worm, she thinks the tongue is a worm. This is a reference to The Empire Strikes Back, where the Millennium Falcon flies into the worm's mouth, thinking it is a cave. In Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy V, when Barnacle Boy claims he will turn to the "dark side", this is a reference to Star Wars.
In the episode Pizza Delivery, SpongeBob is called "Jethro" twice by Squidward. This is a reference to The Beverly Hillbillies.
Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy are parodies of Aquaman and Aqualad.
Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy are parodies of Batman and Robin.
The Invisible Boatmobile is a parody of Wonder Woman's Invisible Jet.

In the episode Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy, Reflecto is a parody of Electro from Spider-Man. In Mermaid Man Begins, the radioactive ant biting Ernie's forehead mirrors Peter Parker getting bitten by a radioactive spider.
In the episode Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy, Reflecto is a parody of Reducto from Birdman.
The episode Sandy's Rocket feature sound effects from Tetris.

The SpongeBob episodes Sandy's Rocket and Ugh feature references to 2001: A Space Odyssey. In the episode Squidward in Clarinetland, SpongeBob and Squidward tumbling through space to classical music is a reference to 2001: A Space Odyssey.
The SpongeBob episode Sandy's Rocket feature references to Alien.
SpongeBob characters appear in every Nicktoons game.
Squidward the Unfriendly Ghost is a pun on Casper the Friendly Ghost.

The episode Scaredy Pants feature sound effects from Frankenstein. Frankendoodle is a pun on Frankenstein. In Patrick! The Game, Patrick finishing his game is a parody of the scientist creating the monster in Frankenstein.

In SB-129, the shot of Squidward's face after being in the freezer for 2,000 years is similar to the shot of Jack Torrance's face after freezing to death in The Shining. In The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water, the two popsicles saying "Come play with us, Plankton!" references the Grady twins from The Shining.

In the episode Arrgh!, certain elements of the Flying Dutchman's Treasure Hunt board resemble the game Monopoly, particularly the concept of players going to jail. In the episode Patrick! The Game, Bottomopoly is a parody of Monopoly.
In the episode Rock Bottom, the clock in Rock Bottom looks like a Poké Ball from Pokémon. In the episode The Card, the Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy cards are similar to Pokémon cards.
In the CatDog episode "Cliff's Little Secret", there is a character on a movie poster that resembles SpongeBob.

In the episode Walking Small, when Plankton is seen packing his suitcase, one of the items his puts in is a shirt that looks similar to the one Charlie Brown wears in Peanuts. SpongeBob is mentioned in the Peanuts episode School Chums.

Jimmy Neutron and Goddard have interacted with episodes of SpongeBob with cross promotions. SpongeBob's pineapple house makes a cameo in the episode Jet Fusion. SpongeBob was referenced by Timmy Turner in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic Dimension Intervention.

In Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy II, the Atomic Flounder's radioactive breath is a reference to Godzilla. In the episode Krusty Towers, Patrick's drawing is a reference to Godzilla. In Sing a Song of Patrick, one of the comics in Near Mint Comic Books contains an image of a creature that looks similar to Godzilla.

In the SpongeBob episode "Artist Unknown", SpongeBob sings the dump song, remeniscient to when Heffer sang it in Rocko's Modern Life. The SpongeBob episode Clams is similar to the Rocko's Modern Life episode Fish-N-Chumps.
In The Fry Cook Games, when SpongeBob and Patrick fly straight in the air and both yelling together is similar to a common motif found in Dragon Ball.

In Just One Bite, near the end of the episode, Squidward gluttonously chows down all the Krabby Patties in the Patty Vault, despite SpongeBob's warnings not to do so, to the point that they all go down to his thighs and explode, similar to how Piggy Hamhock explodes from overeating near the end of the Looney Tunes cartoon Pigs is Pigs. In SpongeBob Meets the Strangler, the scene where the Tattletale Strangler jumps out of a plane with a parachute only to find out that the parachute is SpongeBob is a reference to the Looney Tunes cartoon Yankee Doodle Daffy where Porky jumps out of a plane with Daffy as a parachute. In Patrick SmartPants, the scene where Patrick falls from a cliff is just like the Wile E. Coyote and Road Runner cartoons from Looney Tunes. In the episode To Save a Squirrel, SpongeBob sitting in a kettle of hot water and thinking it is a bath plus Patrick cutting up and adding carrots is a nod to a number of classic Bugs Bunny shorts in which an enemy attempts to cook Bugs Bunny in a similar fashion.
In the episode Procrastination, SpongeBob says "Hey, hey, hey" to Gary. This is a reference to Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids.
There are many format crossover UNO games between the two series.
In a bumper ad for Blue's Clues, Squidward and Joe fight over who's the new host of Blue's Clues.

In the episode Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy IV, Patrick mentions Wumborama, a parody of Futurama. In the episode Yo Leela Leela, there is a robot called SpongeBolt SquareBots which is a parody of SpongeBob SquarePants.
In Graveyard Shift, the sign about the telephone ringing is similar to a scene from Scream.

In the episode Wet Painters, a picture of Popeye is visible among the pictures in Mr. Krabs' house. In The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, when SpongeBob and Patrick are at Goofy Goober's Ice Cream Party Boat, a picture of Popeye can be seen. In the episode Enemy In-Law, Mama Krabs' fighting muscle arm with the battle ship guns is similar to the Popeye cartoons. A person dressed as Popeye appears in Truth or Square and Popeye is mentioned in the same episode.
The Quickster from Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy V is a parody of The Flash.
The eagle wings on the side of The Quickster's mask from Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy V resembles Captain America.
In My Pretty Seahorse, during the montage, Mystery paints SpongeBob à la Titanic. The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water features a reference to Titanic.
The SpongeBob episode "Clams" is a spoof of Jaws.
In the episode Mid-Life Crustacean, P and P is a parody of Dungeons & Dragons. Dunces and Dragons is another parody of Dungeons & Dragons.
Spongebob slippers are shown in Daddy Day Care.
In the logo panel for the Garfield comic strip of November 16 2003, Garfield is dressed as SpongeBob.
A girl sings the SpongeBob SquarePants theme in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Malcolm Visits College".
A painting of a character resembling SpongeBob can be seen in a child’s bedroom in the Cartoon Monsoon pilot Boogies.
Characters from Spongebob videogames appear in the Video Mods original video "Stand and Choose"; they also star in the "All the Small Things" videos.
Floyd and Lloyd from The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie resemble Mario and Luigi. There's other references to Mario throughout the series.
In The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, King Neptune's trident being accidentally set to "Real Boy" is a reference to Pinocchio.

In The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, there are two fish headbanging to Goofy Goober Rock. They are a reference to the characters from Beavis and Butt-Head, as the two fish have the same color scheme and hair color as them.
In The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, a picture of Krazy Kat is at the Goofy Goober bar.

In the SpongeBob episode "Welcome to the Chum Bucket", the brain switching part of this episode is similar to The Simpsons episode "Treehouse of Horror Ⅱ". Krabby the Clown from the SpongeBob episode" Krabby Land" is a parody of Krusty the Clown from The Simpsons. In The Simpsons episode "She Used to Be My Girl", SpongeBob appears with Jesus and Buddha in Heaven. In the SpongeBob episode "Karate Island", the painting of a boat inside Gary's shell is a replica of the painting over the Simpson family's couch. Frankenstein's monster is in a SpongeBob costume in the Simpsons episode "Treehouse of Horror XX". In the Simpsons episode "Fat Man and Little Boy", there's a SpongeBob/Itchy hybrid in one of the T-shirt designs. In the Simpsons episode "The Wife Aquatic", "The Science of SpongeBob" is one of the exhibits in the museum.
SpongeBob SquarePants is mentioned in Ocean's Twelve.
SpongeBob is mentioned in Are We There Yet?

In Fear of a Krabby Patty, in SpongeBob's dream, the Krabby Patty tells him that he will always be with him in his arteries, a reference to E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, complete with the glowing finger.
SpongeBob SquarePants is parodied several episodes of Robot Chicken.
Characters from SpongeBob SquarePants appear in Off the Mark.
Spongebob is mentioned in the Ghost Whisperer episode "Crossing".
Spongebob shows on TV in Zathura.
SpongeBob is mentioned in Final Destination 3.
In Dunces and Dragons, Planktonamor's Tower resembles the Eye of Sauron from The Lord of the Rings.
In the episode Krusty Towers, Patrick's drawing is a reference to King Kong.

Edd, Tom, Tord, and Paul sing the "F.U.N. Song" in "F is for Friends". Edd and Matt sing "Now That We're Men" in "SpongeBob Test". King Neptune's crown appears in the volcano's treasure in "Beaster Bunny".
Spongebob is mentioned in the novel Stone Rose by Jacqueline Rayner.
The SpongeBob episode Karate Island feature references to Enter the Dragon.
The SpongeBob episode Karate Island feature references to Kill Bill.
In the episode Karate Island, Sandy's and Udon's muscle growth is loosely based on Toguro's 100% muscle growth in the manga and anime series Yu Yu Hakusho.
The SpongeBob episode Karate Island feature references to Naruto.
A person is dressed up as Spongebob in the South Park episode "Hell on Earth 2006".

Stewie has a toy of a green SpongeBob in the episode "Prick Up Your Ears". Meg puts on an episode of SpongeBob SquarePants in the Family Guy episode "Road to Rupert". SpongeBob and Squidward were mentioned in "Road to the North Pole". In the episode "Inside Family Guy", a character is dressed as SpongeBob SquarePants.

In the episode Squid Wood, the song Squidward plays on the clarinet to Milo at the end of the episode sounds very similar to Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo from Cinderella. Cinderella was referenced by Pearl in the season 9 episode Married to Money.

In the episode The Thing, when Squidward is taken in by the other animals at the end, SpongeBob says to Patrick "But he's with his own kind now, where he belongs, and with that, let us go back to where we belong." This is a reference to the ending of The Jungle Book.

In the episode Hocus Pocus, the Brown Tile Road is an homage to the Yellow Brick Road in The Wizard of Oz. Additionally, SpongeBob and Patrick entering Mr. Magic's room and Patrick revealing that it is actually a man voicing him with a machine behind a curtain are direct parodies of the Wizard's scenes from that film. In Atlantis SquarePantis, when Patchy taps his peg leg to his other boot stating "There's no place like home", it is a reference of The Wizard of Oz. The tornado directly after this scene is also a reference to the The Wizard of Oz.

At the end of The Gift of Gum, during the cleaning of the gum, Patrick eats some of the gum like Pac-Man. In The Cent of Money, when the scene shows the fish playing the arcade games, one of them has a character and game similar to Pac-Man. In the episode Krusty Kleaners, the scene where SpongeBob and Patrick are trying to find a way out of the maze references Pac-Man. In the episode Treats!, at the beginning of the Snail Bites commercial, there is an allusion to Pac-Man.
Spongebob is mentioned in the Supernatural episode "Houses Of The Holy".

In the episode Spy Buddies, when SpongeBob and Patrick get their mission through a recorded message in a Krabby Patty and then the object self-destructs, it is a parody of the self destruct message object used in the Mission: Impossible movies.
In the beginning of The Donut of Shame, the scene where Patrick wakes up next to a pipe is a reference to Saw III.

In The Krusty Plate, when SpongeBob says "It may end life as we know it, but I am crossing the beams!", it is a reference to Ghostbusters, in which it is revealed that crossing the beam of their proton-pack lasers will end life as they know it.
Operation - SpongeBob SquarePants Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
Atlantis SquarePantis feature many references to Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.
In Atlantis SquarePantis, the way Sandy warps into the video game is similar to the way some of the characters in the Mega Man franchise of video games enter or exit levels.

In the video game Mission Start: The Germ Warrior from Atlantis SquarePantis, one can see a code that says 1991 © Nickelodeon Inc. The title screen and title are a parody of Street Fighter II: The World Warrior.
In Atlantis SquarePantis, when Sandy is dancing with a germ, the moves she does is a parody of Dance Dance Revolution.
The Season 5 episode "Atlantis SquarePantis" of SpongeBob SquarePants features a parody of the Bubble Launcher from Puzzle Bobble.
Al Gristlepuss from Banned in Bikini Bottom resembles Duke Nukem.
In SpongeHenge, the scene where SpongeBob is in a cave hiding from the jellyfish and making a stone companion is a reference to Cast Away.

In SpongeHenge, when the Krusty Krab is buried in the sand, it is a reference to the ending of Planet of the Apes when Taylor, having survived and escaped imprisonment, wanders along a coastline in search of shelter. He finds a partially destroyed Statue of Liberty buried in the sand and finally realizes what planet he is on. In addition, SpongeBob's hair and beard are strikingly similar to Charlton Heston's in the same movie. Planet of the Jellyfish is a parody of Planet of the Apes.
In the episode Stanley S. SquarePants, Mr. Krabs' nephews are a parody of Donald Duck's nephews, Huey, Dewey, and Louie, and they solve mysteries, a parody of their role in the show DuckTales.

SpongeBob is mentioned in the King Of The Hill episode "Tears Of An Inflatable Clown". In the SpongeBob episode Pest of the West, when Sandy says, "That boy ain’t hooked up right", it is a reference to the quote "That boy ain’t right" from King of the Hill.
SpongeBob SquarePants can be seen playing on a tv in Alvin and the Chipmunks.
Spongebob shows on TV in Cloverfield.

In A Life in a Day, SpongeBob accidentally knocking over the bikers' motorcycles is a reference to a scene from Pee-wee's Big Adventure where Pee-wee Herman knocks over a biker gang's motorcycles outside of a biker bar.
In Boating Buddies, when SpongeBob drives through the Costume Supplies shop, Mrs. Puff is dressed as Jason Voorhees from Friday the 13th.
Spongebob shows on TV in the Fringe episode "Pilot".
Drawn To Life: SpongeBob Squarepants Edition is a crossover between the two series.
A character resembling Squidward appears in the Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann episode "Let's Go, Comrades".
A reference to Mary Poppins is shown in Grooming Gary when Charles and Foofie glide via an umbrella.
In Sand Castles in the Sand, the large robot that Patrick controls resembles Gundam from the anime of the same name.
Multiple songs from the SpongeBob SquarePants album The Best Day Ever appear in Rock Band.
SpongeBob SquarePants is mentioned in Dork Diaries, Pop Star, Skating Sensation and Dear Dork.
In the episode Chum Caverns, one scene of Mr. Krabs and Plankton digging underground references Dig Dug.

In No More Bunny Business, when Phineas pops out of the mailbox and scares the mailman, it is a reference to whenever Spongebob camps in his mailbox waiting for the mail. In Phineas and Ferb: Summer Belongs to You!, while stranded on a desert island, Phineas finds a square yellow kitchen sponge and a pink starfish and says "Look! A sponge and a starfish! There's gotta be something we can make out of this! No, that's ridiculous." which is a reference to SpongeBob SquarePants. In Squid Plus One, SpongeBob asking "Whatcha' dooooin'?" is the famous catchphrase used for the character Isabella Garcia-Shapiro in Phineas and Ferb.

Posters of The Fairly OddParents can be seen in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Truth or Square". In the FairlyOdd Parents episode "Ruled Out", Mr. Turner says that "pants are for squares", a reference to SpongeBob. Patrick, Mr. Krabs, and Sandy are referenced in The Fairly OddParents episode "Something's Fishy!". SpongeBob was referenced by Timmy Turner in the Jimmy Timmy Power Hour comic "Dimension Intervention".  In the Fairly OddParents episode "App Trap", there is a person that looks like SpongeBob.
Posters of Avatar can be seen in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Truth or Square".
Posters of The Mighty B! can be seen in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Truth or Square".
Posters of Dora the Explorer can be seen in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Truth or Square" and Dora appeared at Super Bowl LVIII in Bikini Bottom.
Triumph the Insult Comic Dog appears in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Truth or Square".
Back to the Past is a parody of Back to the Future.
Squidward in Clarinetland is a parody of Alice in Wonderland.

SpongeBob shows on TV in The Karate Kid (2010). In Squid Defense, the way Squidward did the chores is similar to a scene in The Karate Kid in which Daniel was tricked by Mr. Miyagi into doing chores at his house.
The Clash of Triton is a parody of Clash of the Titans.

In The Cent of Money, when the scene shows the fish playing the arcade games, one of them has creatures that look and move like the aliens from Space Invaders. In the episode That Sinking Feeling, the underground chase is a reference to the arcade game Dig Dug.
Spongebob characters are playable in Super Brawl.
Patrick from SpongeBob Squarepants is referenced in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Justice League Recombination". SpongeBob is also mentioned in several other episodes of The Big Bang Theory.
Clue Jr: SpongeBob SquarePants Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
Patchy The Pirate appears in the episode, Big Time Beach Party.

In the Adventure Time episode Go With Me, the scene where the wolves rip the screen in half after the characters say that nothing can tear them apart is similar to the SpongeBob SquarePants episode F.U.N. when Plankton ripped the screen apart after a couple said exactly the same thing.
SpongeBob appears in the online Nickelodeon game Block Party.

SpongeBob SquigglePants is similar to the WarioWare games. Both contain minigames that are split into sections, each of the sections on both games contain themes, and a main character associated them, and both games contain lives.
Robbie wears SpongeBob underwear in the Victorious episode "Tori Gets Stuck".
In "The Stanley Parable" on Leadership board you can find a pic of Squidward.
In Mermaid Man Begins, the bomb that explodes on Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy is a reference to how Bruce Banner became Hulk. Plank-Ton is a parody of Hulk.
SpongeBob is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Phil on Wire". A kid dresses up as SpongeBob in the episode: "Halloween 3: AwesomeLand".
Fred wears a SpongeBob costume in FЯED 2: Night of the Living Fred.

In The Way of the Sponge, SpongeBob's training montage is a parody of Rocky. What's Eating Patrick? feature references to Rocky. In the season 9 episode Two Thumbs Down, the music that plays while SpongeBob trains his thumb is similar to the song "Eye of the Tiger" from Rocky 3.
A Mr. Potato Head toy was released featuring Mr. Potato Head dressed as SpongeBob SquarePants.
Ian has a SpongeBob watch in REAL DEATH NOTE!.
SpongeBob's Pineapple Home makes an appearance in the episode "Aquatic Conflict".
A Spongebob doll is shown in Thousand Words.
Spongebob is shown on TV in Ted.
In License to Milkshake, the training montage is a parody of the movie Top Gun with SpongeBob riding a motorcycle, flying in a fighter jet and playing beach volleyball.
SpongeBob appears in the MAD segment "Taking Nemo", and there's a SpongeWow commercial (ShamWow/SpongeBob parody).
In the episode Patrick-Man!, Patrick trying to unmask people references the villain unmasks from Scooby Doo.
A person can be seen dressed as SpongeBob in the Oggy and the Cockroaches episode  "Run Olivia Run".
In the episode It's a SpongeBob Christmas!, Randolph the Red-Nosed Seahorse is a parody of Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer.
In Scribblenauts Unlimited at The Lost Kingdom of Parentheses there is a pinapple, a tiki, and a rock. pressing use will spawn a starfish (Patrick), a squid (Squidward), and a sponge (Spongebob).
There are minor references to SpongeBob in Infiltrating the Airship and later games.
Cat mentions SpongeBob's pineapple in the Sam & Cat episode "#TextingCompetition.
SpongeBob and Patrick from SpongeBob appear in Kaku Spring Festival Gala 2014.
Breadwinners have many references to SpongeBob.
Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare features a reference to SpongeBob.
The character Kenny the Cat from the eponymous season 9 episode resembles Tom Cat from Tom and Jerry.
Doodle Jump and SpongeBob have a crossover game with Doodle Jump: SpongeBob SquarePants.
A kid imagines himself working as a fry cook in what looks like the Krusty Krab kitchen.
In The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water, Burger Beard going through death traps to grab the magic book is a parody of Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom.
Sir Pinch-a-Lot is a parody of Iron Man.

Roblox sponsored SpongeBob with clothing and accessories; The Roblox gear Slime Potion is modeled after SpongeBob's pineapple. Additionally, SpongeBob appears in TMNT Battle Tycoon for a limited-time event. SpongeBob Simulator was released as a Roblox experience and the player's Roblox Avatar can be used in it.

SpongeBob SquarePants.game: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (Disney)
SpongeBob SquarePants.description: In Squid Plus One, the scene where the scallops take Squidward's apron references the scene in Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs where the birds take Snow White's cloak and hang it on a coat rack.
In the SpongeBob episode The Executive Treatment, the scene where Patrick and Marv are stamping each other with no-symbol stamp is similar to a scene from the Chowder episode Banned from the Stand.

In Sanctuary!, when SpongeBob counts his pet snails, one of the names mentioned is "He Who Shall Not Be Named." This is a reference to "He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named", one of Lord Voldermort's nicknames in the Harry Potter novel series.
There are several references to The Hunchback of Notre-Dame in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode Sanctuary!.
SpongeBob characters appear in Nickelodeon Music Maker.

SpongeBob SquarePants.game: Nick's Not So Ultimate Boss Battles
SpongeBob SquarePants.description: Spongebob characters are playable in Nick's Not So Ultimate Boss Battles.
A SpongeBob toy is visible in Whack Your Boss: Superhero Style.
Outfits based on SpongeBob characters are downloadable in "LittleBigPlanet 3".

He later plays Super Star Force in episode 111 and the original Arcade version through Wii Virtual Console as part of Nintendo Channel promotional episodes. Former AD Shinchiro Toujima also played the Famicom version during the Saitama Super Arena event.
In Persona 5, you can obtain cartridge of a parody of Star Force.
Re-arranged music from Star Force appears in Warriors All-Stars.

Star Fox.description: Fox from Star Fox is featured in the comics Super Mario: Mario im Wunderland and, with other Star Fox characters in Part 3 of Super Mario: Verloren in der Zeit; he also makes a cameo in Super Mario-Kun #7.
An Arwing from Star Fox makes an appearance in Stunt Race FX.
Mother 2: Giygas Strikes Back - Ness’s Adventure features a panel depicting characters watching Star Fox on the TV.
Characters and places from the Star Fox series are featured in all Super Smash Bros. games.
Fox McCloud appears in the N-Gang episode "Freeze Frame".
Picross NP Vol. 4 and Vol. 6 include images from the Star Fox series.
Five masks in The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask seem to reference the Star Fox team.
In Pokémon Stadium 2, connecting video game consoles to a TV can show an image from Star Fox 64.
An Arwing from the Star Fox series appears as an item in all Animal Crossing games.
Star Fox Adventures features a character possibly based on Kazooie.
Music from Star Fox 64 is featured in Daigasso! Band Brothers.
The Special Flag from Rally-X makes an appearance in Star Fox: Assault.
Star Fox: Assault features Xevious as an unlockable game.
Japanese version of Star Fox: Assault features Battle City as an unlockable game.
A song from Star Fox: Assault is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there's a reference to the Star Fox series.

James McCloud from F-Zero X is based on Fox and James McCloud from the StarFox series; Leon from F-Zero GX may be a reference to Wolf O'Donnell; Octoman from the F-Zero series makes an appearance in Star Fox Command; there also are other references between the two series.
Microgame versions of Star Fox are featured in WarioWare: Smooth Moves and WarioWare: D.I.Y.
Some robot characters in the Star Fox series may be based on R.O.B.; UNDIRECT: R.O.B. appears as a boss in the microgame version of Star Fox in WarioWare: Smooth Moves.
Foster in Aoi Sekai no Chushin de is based on Fox from Star Fox.
Characters resembling Fox, Peppy and Slippy make a cameo in the issue "The Fry and the Furious!" of the Futurama Comic.
Mii Plaza features four unlockable hats based on Star Fox and includes a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Star Fox 64 3D.
Star Fox characters appear in Star Fox TV Show!.
Mii Plaza includes a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Star Fox 64 3D.
Fox appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
Tekken Tag Tournament 2: Wii U Edition features a Fox McCloud outfit for the characters.
Fox McCloud has been a subject for Death Battle!
Peppy Hare makes a cameo in Steel Diver: Sub Wars; The Blue Marine submarine from Star Fox 64 was also added to the game in an update.
In a level of Monument Valley, you can find debris that looks like an Arwing from Star Fox.
Hacked signs can read "Do a barrel roll" in Watch Dogs.
A sleeping Mii in Tomodachi Life will sometimes say "Do a barrel roll!", a reference to Star Fox.
Bayonetta 2 features a costume based on Fox McCloud with Arwing-shaped guns and an Arwing actually appearing in the game.
Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Fox from Star Fox 64 3D.
Star Fox is mentioned in Armada.
Four planets from Kirby Super Star, Floria, Aqualiss, Mecheye, and Halfmoon, are mentioned on the cover of a travel magazine in Star Fox Zero: The Battle Begins.
The Foxy Fighters minigame in FNaF World Update 2 is a reference to Star Fox.
Nintendo Badge Arcade features badges from the Star Fox series.
In Persona 5, you can obtain cartridge of a parody of Star Fox.
Monster Hunter X features a downloadable costume from Star Fox.
Scott the Woz once did a review on Star Fox Zero.
Fox, Falco, Slippy, Peppy, and Wolf appear in the Switch version of Starlink: Battle for Atlas. Leon, Pigma and Andrew also appear in one of the game’s DLC.
"Something About Star Fox 64" is a parody of Star Fox 64.
Fox McCloud and an Arwing has been a subject for DBX.
One of the options in Completing the Mission spoof the gameplay of Star Fox.
Fox McCloud and Peppy Hare appear in "How Eternals Should Have Ended".
The "Floating Hands Boss" spray in Antonblast are based on Andross from Star Fox.

Star Gladiator.description: Star Gladiator was originally planned to be a Star Wars game.
A sketch from Red Earth shows Star Gladiator's June Lin Milliam as a member of Mai-Ling's combat unit.

Various Star Gladiator characters make cameo appearances in Pocket Fighter, while Chun-Li cosplays as June Lin Milliam in some of her attacks and Felicia cosplays as Gamof and Rimgal in some of her attacks.

Ryu makes a minor cameo appearance in Gantetsu's normal ending from Plasma Sword, while Saturn Dyer from Star Gladiator makes a cameo in Paul Phoenix's artwork from Street Fighter X Tekken, watching him punch an alien and Chun Li receives a June Lin Millian costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.

Characters from Star Gladiator are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games; while Gore Gajah and June Lin Milliam make cameo appearances in SNK vs. Capcom: Match of the Millenium and Capcom vs. SNK 2 respectively.
Hayato Kanzaki is playable in Marvel vs. Capcom 2.
Capcom Girl no Mind Puzzle features appearances of June Lin Milliam from the Star Gladiator series.
June Lin Milliam and Ellie from Star Gladiator make cameos in Felicia's ending in Capcom Fighting Evolution.
Various Star Gladiator characters make cameo appearances in Tatsunoko vs. Capcom.
Saturn Dyer from Star Gladiator makes a cameo in Paul Phoenix's artwork from Street Fighter X Tekken, watching him punch an alien.
The list of generic monickers in Dragon's Dogma features "Hayato" as a possible monicker.
The stage "Urban Chaos" from the Mercenaries mode in Resident Evil 6 features several Star Gladiator Arcade cabinets.
June Lin Milliam, Black Hayato, Gamon and Blistein are featured in Otoranger.
One of Hiryu's color alts in the 2014 Strider is inspired by Hayato Kanzaki from Star Gladiator.
Plasma Sword is included in Capcom Fighting Collection 2.

Star Ocean.description: Lenneth Valkyrie appears in Star Ocean: Blue Sphere as a transformation for Rival, and in Star Ocean: Till the End of Time as a superboss. Characters from Valkyrie Profile appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration. Additionally, characters from Star Ocean appeared in Valkyrie Anatomia as part of a collaboration event.
Phantasy Star Nova features downloadable costumes from Star Ocean: The Last Hope.
Costumes based on Star Ocean appear in Exist Archive as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Resonance of Fate appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration.

Characters from Star Ocean: Anamnesis appear in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius and vice versa, during special collaborations; additionally Star Ocean: Till the End of Time features a character based on Aerith from Final Fantasy VII.
Characters from NieR: Automata appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration.
Characters from Sakura Wars appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration.
Characters from Attack on Titan appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration.
Characters from Guilty Gear appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration.
Claude and Rena from Star Ocean appear in Tales of the Rays and Cress and Mint from Tales of the Rays appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis, both as part of a cross collaboration.
Characters from Persona appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis as a collaboration.
Star Ocean: The Second Story characters appear in Last Cloudia as a collaboration.

Star Racer.description: Many elements of Star Racer are heavily based on F-Zero.

Star Raiders.description: Atari Force #3 features the Zylons from Star Raiders.
Star Raiders is mentioned in Armada.

Star Soldier.description: The whale enemy from Challenger appear as a bonus panel in Star Soldier.
Milon is featured as a bonus panel in Star Soldier.
Bomberman is a selectable character in Star Parodier, while Ver.2.2 of Super Bomberman R added a bomberman known as "Caesar Bomber", based off the playable spaceship from Star Soldier.
One of the four worlds in Quiz Caravan Cult Q is based on Star Soldier.
The stage "Floating Continent" in DreamMix TV World Fighters is based on the first stage of Star Soldier.
Star Soldier vs DoDonPachi DaiOuJou CARAVAN'06 is a crossover between both series.
Taiko no Tatsujin 12 and Taiko no Tatsujin Wii feature a music track from Star Soldier.
Star Soldier puzzles are featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.
Caesar from Star Soldier makes an appearance in Kaettekita Pixel Crows.

Star Trek.description: In Farm Fresh Food, the automated farm's control room is a copy of the Enterprise bridge. Later in Invasion of the Moon Creatures, while Graeme attempts to regain contact with Bill and Tim, Spock briefly appears on his monitor. Soon after, Graeme begins recording a log in the style of Captain Kirk; "Captain's log, stardate..." etc.
The Enterprise from Star Trek appears in a scene in Airplane II: The Sequel.
The Characters of Here Comes The Brides appear in the Star Trek book, Ishmael.
Marty McFly lies about being from the planet Vulcan in Back To The Future.
The Space Quest series frequently references Star Trek.
Star Trek is mentioned in Spaceballs.
Kirk sees characters from Bloom County during a hallucination in DC's Star Trek (Volume 2) #51.
A episode of Reading Rainbow shows a behind the scenes of Star Trek: The Next Generation.
Mr. Spock is mentioned in the Garfield and Friends episode Nighty Nightmare.
The shuttlecraft Indiana Jones is shown on Star Trek: The Next Generation "Evolution"
Spock is mentioned in Look Who's Talking. Vulcans are also mentioned in Look Who's Talking Now.
The Captain N: The Game Master episode "Simon the Ape-Man" features a reference to Star Trek.
Star Trek is mentioned in issue 2 of the comic Men In Black.
A line in The Raccoons episode "The Wrong Stuff!" is a reference to Star Trek.
In Bill & Ted's Bogus Journey, Bill and Ted watch the Star Trek episode "Arena" and later references it.
Star Trek is mentioned in Wayne's World.
Stay Tuned parodies Star Trek: The Next Generation in a section of the movie.
Star Trek VHS sets appear in Last Action Hero.

A Klingon Bird of Prey is seen in a spaceship graveyard in Red Dwarf "Psirens". In Star Trek, the story "Stone and Anvil" has a hologram character suggest that they wear a large H on their head, and in "Time Lock" the Gemini 12's Time Drive is stored in the Eridian Vault.
The Eek! The Cat episode "Star TrEek" is a parody of Star Trek.
Star Trek is mentioned in Ace Venture: Pet Detective.
The Avenger Penguins episode "The 23rd Century" features a Star Trek parody.
In Knowing Me Knowing You with Alan Partridge, Alan's joke "It's a chat show Jim, but not as we know it" is a spoof of the famously misquoted line from Star Trek: ‘no life as we know it’.
Chandler mentions the Starship Enterprise in the Friends episode: "The One with the Sonogram at the End". Star Trek is also mentioned in the episode: "The One with the List".
The Star Trek Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles action figures have the Ninja Turtles in the universe of Star Trek, mentioning ships, locations and alien races.

The Star Trek Encyclopedia makes reference to rumours that Dr. Katherine Pulaski's ancestor died by falling down an elevator shaft at a prestigious Los Angeles law firm. This is a reference to the L.A. Law episode "Good to the Last Drop" in which Rosalind Shays dies in such a way (both characters were portrayed by actress Diana Maldaur).
Cardassian and Ferengi action figures come to life in The Indian in the Cupboard.
In Duke Nukem 3D, the Episode 2, Level 3 "Warp Factor" is based on the Enterprise from Star Trek and includes recreations of its Bridge and Picard's Ready Room.
Star Trek is mentioned in The Cable Guy. Jean-Luc Picard is also one of the fake names used by the Cable Guy.
The Millennium Falcon appears on Star Trek: First Contact. Also R2-D2 appears in Star Trek (2009) and Star Trek Into Darkness.

In Dream Machine, Dexter begins the episode by saying "Dexter's log, star date 1234.5", referencing how most episodes begin in Star Trek: The Original Series. The episode Star Check Unconventional parodies Star Trek.
A Klingon from Star Trek is mentioned in the Everybody Loves Raymond episode: "The Ball".
Star Trek/X-Men is a crossover between the two series.
Star Trek is referenced in the Channel Umptee-3 episode "Just Add Water".
Captain Kirk is mentioned in SaGa Frontier.
Dr. Jackson Roykirk, a character that is mentioned in the Star Trek episode "The Changeling" also appears in the Team Knight Rider episode "Apocalypse Maybe".
There are many Star Trek themed Monopoly boards.
In the short "Party of Three!" from Oh Yeah! Cartoons, Timmy says "Warp speed, Mr. Sulu" while riding a roller coaster.
Star Trek is mentioned in the The King of Queens episode: "S'aint Valentine's".
Spock is mentioned in the Charmed episode "That 70s Episode".
Star Trek was mentioned in the South Park episode "Spontaneous Combustion".
Star Trek is mentioned in the Freaks and Geeks episodes: "Pilot" and "Tests and Breasts". Spock is mentioned in the episode: "The Diary".
Star Trek UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Final Fantasy IX features a reference to Star Trek.
Star Trek is mentioned in Clockstoppers.

Star Trek toys are seen in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Monkey". Captain Piccard is mentioned in the episode: "Garage Sale", while Star Trek is mentioned in the episode: "Ida Loses a Leg" and "Hal Grieves".
Star Trek is mentioned in Daddy Day Care.
Sniffles dresses as Vulcan in the episode Remains to be Seen.
Henry Roth talks into a fake Captain’s Log
Star Trek is mentioned in the Joey episode: "Joey and the Premiere".
Star Trek is mentioned in Doogal.
Star Trek is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "Junk In The Trunk".
Dean Winchester mentions the "Vulcan Mind Meld" from Star Trek in the season 1 Supernatural episode "Skin".
Star Trek is mentioned in the English dub of the 4th episode of Ghost Stories.

In the episode Have You Seen This Snail?, when Gary and Granny are riding in the latter's car, Granny says "Set phasers on fun!", a pun on the Star Trek line "Set phasers on stun." In Patrick SmartPants, the first thing Patrick says after having his brain connected is "I find all this laughter highly illogical", a tribute to Spock's famous phrase on the original Star Trek series.
A line from the Star Trek: Deep Space Nine episode "Far Beyond the Stars" is quoted in V for Vendetta.
Star Trek is referenced in many episodes of The Big Bang Theory.
Nikki's mother mistakes Darth for a Vulcan in the 6teen episode How the Rent-A-Cop Stole Christmas.
The Angry Video Game Nerd episode "Star Trek" is a review of some Star Trek games.
Linkara reviews Star Trek #1.
A Constellation class starship is seen in Battlestar Galactica (2004) "Daybreak".
Slusho from Alias is seen in Star Trek (2009).
The company 'Tagruato' from the marketing campaigns of Cloverfield is shown in Star Trek (2009).
Pain includes a costume for George Takei based on Sulu from Star Trek.
Star Trek is mentioned in The Thick of It.
Star Trek is mentioned in the White Collar episode "Book Of Hours".
Star Trek has been parodied multiple times on HISHE, with Kahn appearing frequently in "Villain Pub".
Star Trek is parodied in the MAD sketch "Star Blecch".

One splash text used to read "Cooler than Spock!" (later changed to "Not as cool as Spock!"); an allusion to the Star Trek character. "There are four lights!" is one of the witty comments that can appear at the top of crash reports of Minecraft; an allusion to the Star Trek: Next Generation episode "Chain Of Command" part 2. tlhIngan Hol, a fictional language from Star Trek, was added among the language settings of Minecraft.
Star Trek appears in the Infestation crossover event.
Star Trek shows on TV in Paul.
Star Trek is mentioned in the Community episode "Intermediate Documentary Filmmaking".

Star Trek is mentioned several times in Ready Player One. Locutus, Klingons, Rura Penthe, and Khan from Star Trek are mentioned in Ready Player Two, as are Star Trek V: The Final Frontier and Star Trek: The Next Generation.
Blue dresses up as Picard in the Dick Figures episode: "Terminate-Her".
Captain Kirk has been a rapper for Epic Rap Battles of History.
The characters of Star Trek meet The Legion of Super-Heroes.

In the Adventure Time episode The New Frontier, the title is a reference to Star Trek. In the intro of the original series of Star Trek, the narrator says "Space, the final frontier." Mr. Spock appears in a poster in Holly Jolly Secrets Part II.
Mr. Potato Head toys were released featuring Mr. Potato Head dressed as Kirk and Kor.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews a few "Star Trek" movies.

In the novel Rings Of Time by Greg Cox, Zoe Querez says she replaced a time capsule with her food in the spaceship she is traveling in, it is mentioned the time capsule contained a complete set of Harry Potter books.

Star Trek: The Next Generation / Doctor Who: Assimilation² is a crossover between both series. Characters from Doctor Who: Lost in Time and Star Trek: Lower Decks - The Badgey Directive appear in each other's games during a crossover event.
A item from Star Trek appears in "Space Face". Nog from Star Trek appears in "Beaster Bunny".
Deep Space 69 parodies Star Trek: Deep Space Nine. Spock, Captain Kirk, Captain Picard and Worf appear in the Deep Space 69 episode “License to Bone”.
Spock is mentioned in Hotel Transylvanias end credits.

The achievements "Tough Little Ship", "The United Federation", "Bird of Prey", "Rule Ten: Greed is Eternal", "Givin' her all she's got Captain!" and "No Redshirts Here" are all references to Star Trek.
Star Trek is parodied and has cameos in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
The Irate Gamer reviews Star Trek on NES
Star Trek is discussed in the Breaking Bad episode: "Blood Money".
"Harcourt Fenton Books" is written on the back of the book "Killing Of JFK: A Theory", named after the character from Star Trek.
Star Trek was mentioned in the episode Brain-A-Rooney.
Star Trek is parodied in Veggies in Space: The Fennel Frontier.
The comic Plok: The Exploding Man features a reference to Star Trek.
Star Trek is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "The Wedding (Part 1)". The Starship Enterprise is mentioned in the episodes: "Five Minutes" and "SuperShowerBabyBowl".
A sub fictional character named CAPTEN Kirk appears in Numeric Con.
The episode "Alien Craig" features a reference to Star Trek.
Spock is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Love Is a Battlefield".
The Starship Enterprise  was mentioned in the 2014 Annie movie.
Star Trek & Planet Of The Apes: The Primate Directive is a crossover between the two series.

Characters from Star Trek appear in Family Guy: The Quest for Stuff. Larry and Steve watch Star Trek in The Life of Larry. Star Trek was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "I Never Met The Dead Man"; there are later references to Star Trek.
Ben mentioned Captain Kirk in the Talking Tom & Friends episode "Friendly Customer Service".
People are dressed up as Star Trek characters in Ted 2.
Star Trek/Green Lantern: The Spectrum War and Star Trek/Green Lantern: Stranger Worlds are crossovers between the two series.
There are many references to Star Trek throughout Armada.
Star Trek was mentioned in the Bojack Horseman episode "Let's Find Out".
A whiteboard with names on it features The Borg in Season 1, Episode 10 of Superstore, “Labor”.
A theater marquee with the "Star Trunk" title is shown next to Jumbeaux's Cafe in Zootopia.
The Space Uniform armor set is based on the Federation Uniform from Star Trek.

After ejecting from your Titan, there is a 15% chance of getting the messages "IT WAS FUN.", "MAKE IT SO.", "DESTRUCT SEQUENCE ENGAGED.", "CODE ZERO ZERO ZERO DESTRUCT ZERO." and "AUTHORIZATION ALPHA-ALPHA 3-0-5.", all references to Star Trek.
In the episode: "USS Callister", the show "USS Callister" is a parody of Star Trek.
A Star Trek tshirt is shown in Brigsby Bear.
The characters of Star Trek meet The Transformers.
Star Trek is mentioned in Avengers: Endgame.
The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen: The Tempest #6 has references to Star Trek.
Characters and locations from Star Trek appear in Jetpack Joyride as part of a special crossover event.
An achievement was added in Version 1.3 of Genshin Impact called "...Lizard-Spock".
Pete mentions Star Trek in CBS’s Ghosts episode “Dinner Party”.
Star Trek is mentioned in the Warped! episode "Recorded!".
Uncle Dale from 12 Monkeys appears in the Star Trek: Picard episode Watcher.

Star Trek.game: Apollo 10 ½: A Space Age Childhood
Star Trek.description: Star Trek is shown on TV in Apollo 10 ½: A Space Age Childhood.
Characters from Star Trek: Prodigy appeared in Growtopia as part of a special collaboration.
Spock from Star Trek appears in Fall Guys, as a part of the Season 2 (2022) premium season pass.
The Space Academy DLC of Two Point Campus features many elements that reference Star Trek.
Star Trek is mentioned in the Doom Patrol episode "Nostalgia Patrol".
Star Trek is mentioned in the Invincible episode: "This Must Come as a Shock".
Galaxy Quest is a parody of Star Trek. Characters and species from Galaxy Quest appear in Star Trek Fleet Command.
Commanders and ships based on Star Trek characters appear in World of Warships.
UniVersus includes a set of cards based on Star Trek: Lower Decks.
Characters from SpongeBob SquarePants and Star Trek appear together in a Paramount+  Commercial.
Star Trek is mentioned in the Pluribus episode: "We Is Us".
Characters from Star Trek will appear in an upcoming Magic: The Gathering release.

Star Wars.description: Luke Skywalker, C-3PO , R2D2, and Chewbacca all appear in an episode of The Muppet Show.
The pirate ship in Gamera: Super Monster is based on the Imperial Star Destroyer.
Arale and Senbei dress up as R2-D2 and C-3PO in the Dr. Slump chapter "The Invader from Space".
C-3PO and R2D2 appear in an episode of Sesame Street.
The Kapi enemy from Xevious is based on the Millenium Falcon from Star Wars.
The opening text crawl of Airplane II: The Sequel is a parody of the opening of Star Wars.
Marty McFly calls himself Darth Vader in Back To The Future.
The Star Wars theme plays in Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
The Space Quest series frequently references Star Wars.
Star Wars is mentioned in Max Headroom's Giant Christmas Turkey.
Star Wars is mentioned in The Raccoons episode "The Sweet Smell of Success!".
A Star Wars video case is shown in Video Violence.
The Star Tours merchandise includes minifigures of characters from the Mickey Mouse series portraying Star Wars characters; Mickey Mouse is also seen fighting Darth Vader in promotional material.
Spaceballs is a parody of the Star Wars series.
Alderaan from Star Wars is mentioned in the BraveStarr episode "Call to Arms".
One of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '87 is called "Luke", after the protagonist of Star Wars, that also appeared in Namco-produced games.
A parody of Darth Vader appears in The New Adventures of Beany and Cecil episode "The Framed Freep".
A person dressed as H2O from Allstar Wars, a parody of C-3PO from Star Wars, can be seen at "The Outer Heaven Show Pub" in the original versions of Snatcher.
There's a reference to Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back in Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure.
Several characters were inspired by the scene from The Empire Strikes Back where Darth Vader contracts bounty hunters. Other elements from Strider may have been inspired by elements in Star Wars.
The Captain N: The Game Master episode "Simon the Ape-Man" features a reference to Princess Leia.
A character gets nicknamed 'Darth Vader' in part 1 of Survival from Doctor Who.
The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Star Koopa" is a parody of Star Wars.
Star Wars cosplayers appear in issue 6 of the comic Men In Black.
Off the Mark feature many references to Star Wars.
The Italian comic series Topolino e i signori della galassia is a Star Wars parody.
The Star Wars universe is one of the worlds visited.

Putt-Putt goes to the Moon has several references to Star Wars, including an area (Cosmic Dust Diner) inspired by the Mos Eisley Cantina, and a bunch of rocks that, when clicked on, turn into an R2-D2 look-alike.
The Avenger Penguins episode "Star Struck" features a Star Wars parody.

The names of some characters in the Final Fantay series, starting with Biggs and Wedge from Final Fantasy VI, are based on Star Wars characters; Final Fantasy IX, XIV and XIII-2 also feature references to the Star Wars series.
Mega Man V and Mega Man Zero feature references to the Star Wars movies.
The Eek! The Cat episode "Paw Sores" is a parody of Star Wars.
The Great Bird from Breath of Fire II is named the "Millenium Falcon" in the end credits, a reference to Star Wars.
The characters Vicks (Biggs), Wedge and Piette from Chrono Trigger are named after Star Wars characters.

Gex sometimes says "Obi Wan has taught you well", "What do you mean Darth Vader is my father?" and "Hey, it is Darth Vader's younger brother, Myron" in Gex; he dons a Stormtrooper costume and says "Aren't you a little short for a storm trooper?" in Gex: Enter the Gecko and imitates C3P-O and Luke Skywalker in Gex 3: Deep Cover Gecko.

Kabal from Mortal Kombat 3 is based on the Tusken Raiders from the Star Wars series, while he also shares some traits with Darth Vader; some of Sektor's moves in Mortal Kombat games may be based on Boba Fett from the Star Wars series, while his and Cyrax's Pulse Blades in Deadly Alliance and Armageddon are based on Lightsabers; The slave girl shown in Shao Kahn's vicrory pose in the 2011 game Mortal Kombat, is likely besed on the slaved Princess Leia from Return of the Jedi.
A Darth Vader action figure comes to life in The Indian in the Cupboard.
Yoda is mentioned in Se7en.
The final boss in Ganbare Goemon Kirakira Dōchū: Boku ga Dancer ni Natta Wake throws miniature Death Stars.

In Duke Nukem 3D, a hanging corpse similar to Luke Skywalker can be found in Episode 2, Level 7. Upon finding it, Duke quips "Now this is a force to be reckoned with". In Duke Nukem 64, Luke is replaced by Yoda.
'Star Wars is mentioned in the Friends episodes: "The One with the Prom Video", "The One with the Princess Leia Fantasy", "The One with Ross and Monica's Cousin" and "The One in Barbados: Part 1".
Star Gladiator was originally planned to be a Star Wars game.
The Millennium Falcon appears on Star Trek: First Contact. Also, R2-D2 appears in Star Trek (2009) and Star Trek Into Darkness.
The Lost Vikings II features many references to the Star Wars movies.

Indiana Jones and Star Wars crossover and reference each other various times. First one being Indiana Jones making a cameo in the game Star Wars: Yoda Stories. Indiana Jones and a trailer for LEGO Indiana Jones: The Original Adventures are unlockable in LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga and LEGO Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Out includes references to Indiana Jones. Also, Star Wars characters are unlockable in Lego Indiana Jones while Han Solo appears frozen in carbonite is in the sequel. An exclusive set was also released that featured both Indiana Jones and Han Solo called "Han Solo/Indiana Jones Transformation Chamber"
R2-D2 is mentioned in the episode "Lab of the Lost".
The game Star Wars Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II features Max The Bunny, who can team up with the player. Before, both series have made various references to each other.
There are many Star Wars themed Monopoly boards. Star Wars characters appear in Monopoly Go!.
Most of the kids wore Chewbacca masks in the South Park episode "Pinkeye". Also, the memberberries mention multiple references in Season 20 of South Park.
In I'm Alan Partridge, Alan compares Susan to R2-D2. In another episode, Alan walks while bending over and holding his ankles and says "I could have been R2-D2.
Star Wars is mentioned in Armageddon.
In short "The Fairly OddParents!", the "I am your father" quote is an obvious reference to the iconic Darth Vader quote. There's other references to Star Wars throughout the series.
The Powerpuff Girls episode: "Boogie Frights" features a scene that homages Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope. Star Wars is also referenced in the episode: "Beat Your Greens".
The Beam Sword in the Super Smash Bros. series is based on the Lightsabers from the Star Wars series.
A Star Wars poster is seen in the Home Movies episode "Brendon Gets Rabies".
the Grebleips' species that E.T. is a part of appear in The Phantom Menace additionally A kid in a Yoda costume appears in E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial.
A Star Wars magazine can be found in the Researcher Rest Room area from Dino Crisis.

In the episode Plankton!, Plankton saying "You weak-minded fool!" is a reference to Star Wars: Return of the Jedi. In Sandy, SpongeBob, and the Worm, the scene where Sandy enters the worm, she thinks the tongue is a worm. This is a reference to The Empire Strikes Back, where the Millennium Falcon flies into the worm's mouth, thinking it is a cave. In Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy V, when Barnacle Boy claims he will turn to the "dark side", this is a reference to Star Wars.

Captain Underpants and the Invasion of the Incredibly Naughty Cafeteria Ladies from Outer Space (and the Subsequent Assault of the Equally Evil Lunchroom Zombie Nerds) features a reference to Star Wars.

Star Wars is mentioned in the Freaks and Geeks episodes: "Pilot", "Beers and Weirs", "Tricks and Treats", "Girlfriends and Boyfriends" and "We've Got Spirit". The Empire Strikes Back is mentioned in the episode: "Carded and Discarded". Sam and Gordon dress up as Star Wars characters in the episode: "Chokin' and Tokin'". Yoda is mentioned in the episode: "The Little Things".
Obiwan is mentioned in the Charmed episode "That Old Black Magic".

Stay Tuned.description: At the beginning of the film, Roy can be seen watching a Tom and Jerry cartoon (one animated by Chuck Jones) while he shaves. Note, later on while Roy and Helen are in Hell Vision, they end up in a cartoon where they become mice, which is also animated by Chuck Jones.
Roy can  be seen watching The Maltese Falcon while reciting lines from it. Later on, he ends up in a black-and-white detective movie. Where he mentions the film.
In Stay Tuned there is a there is a reference to Yogi Bear in the form of “Yogi Beer”, a commercial concerning beer for children.
Stay Tuned parodies Driving Miss Daisy in a movie called “Driving Over Miss Daisy.”
There is a minor reference to Diff'rent Strokes in Stay Tuned titled “Different Strokes.”
Stay Tuned references The Exorcist when an exercise instructor does the ‘Exorcist head spin’ an exercise show called "The Exorcisist."
Stay Tuned parodies Wayne’s World in a sketch called Duane’s Underworld where Wayne and Garth are undead satan worshipping zombies.
Doogie Howser, M.D. is featured in Stay Tuned.
There is a minor reference to Frankenstein’s Monster seen when the Knables' kids change channels.
Stay Tuned parodies Star Trek: The Next Generation in a section of the movie.
Stay Tuned is featured in True Romance.
Stay Tuned is featured in Ace Ventura: Pet Detective. "You Can't Win" game show is being watched by Ace's landlord.

Steel Diver.description: A Mario decal appears in Steel Diver; additionally the Steel Driver kart from Mario Kart 8 is based on the game Steel Diver.
Peppy Hare makes a cameo in Steel Diver: Sub Wars; The Blue Marine submarine from Star Fox 64 was also added to the game in an update.

A gun called the Steel Diver is featured as an item in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U, and the BlueShark submarine appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate. Also, submarines from Steel Diver appear as a trophy in the 3DS version.

Steel Jeeg.description: Grendizer vs Steel Jeeg is a crossover between the two series.
The Super Robot Wars series features units from the Steel Jeeg series.

Stellar Blade.description: A bot based on Eve from Stellar Blade can be found in Astro Bot after an update.

Eve from Stellar Blade appears in Goddess of Victory: NIKKE as part of a collaboration event and a DLC expansion for Stellar Blade was released that featured costumes and cosmetics based on Goddess of Victory: NIKKE.

Dana from Step by Step appears on the Boy Meets World episode "The Happiest Show on Earth".

There are reference to Akira in the Steven Universe episodes "Cat Fingers" and "Garnet's Universe", as well as Steven Universe: The Movie.

The Arcade game "Teens of Rage" from the Steven Universe episode "Arcade Mania" is a parody of Streets of Rage.

A giant penny similar to the one found in Batman's Batcave can be seen in the Steven Universe episode "Lion 2: The Movie".

There's a minor reerence to Howl's Moving Castle in the Steven Universe episode "House Guest".

There's a reference to the movie The Fly in the  Steven Universe episode "Island Adventure".
In issue #5 of the Steven Universe comic book, one panel features three plush dolls of the main animatronics from Five Nights at Freddy's.
The character Hoppy from the Steven Universe episode "Garnet's Universe" is likely inspired by the main character in Usagi Yojimbo.
There are several references to Dragon Ball Z in the Steven Universe episode "Garnet's Universe".
There is a minor reference to Tengen Toppa Gurren-Lagan in the Steven Universe episode "Garnet's Universe".
There is a minor reference to Fist of the North Star in the Steven Universe episode "Garnet's Universe".

At the end of the Steven Universe episode "Open Book", there's a Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker video game case in Steven's room. The temple in the episode "Serious Steven" may have been inspired by the ones in The Legend of Zelda. The videogame "Mini Golf Quest" from the Steven Universe episode "Rose's Room" is partly inspired by The Legend of Zelda.
At the end of the episode "Open Book", there's an Animal Crossing GameCube video game case in Steven's room.

A wallpaper based on Harvest Moon DS can be obtained in Chick Chick Boom.
The international release of Harvest Moon DS: Island of Happiness features a possible reference to the Zelda series.

A poster of the protagonist from Harvest Moon can be found in Sebastian's bedroom.
Hamtaro pets are available in Story of Seasons: Trio of Towns as part of a special collaboration.

Piczle Cross: Story of Seasons is a crossover between the two series.

In the Strange Luck episode "Brothers Grim", Chance's brother tells him that if he ever gets in any trouble he should contact Fox Mulder of the FBI, one of the main characters in The X-Files. The producers of Strange Luck got permission from Chris Carter to use the name.

Dustin plays Dragon's Lair in the Stranger Things episode: "CHAPTER ONE: MADMAX".
Dig Dug is shown in Season 2: Chapter 1 of Stranger Things.

the Demogorgon appears in The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen: The Tempest #5.

Dustin talks to Erica about My Little Pony in Season 3: Chapter 6 of Stranger Things.
