Steve and Robin talk about Back to the Future in Season 3: Chapter 7 of Stranger Things.
In an ad for Halloween Horror Nights 29, the Upside Down from Stranger Things appears along with the doppelgangers from Us.
In an ad for Halloween Horror Nights 29, the Upside Down from Stranger Things appears along with The Wolfman.
Nancy Wheeler, Steve Harrington, a Demogorgon and Vecna from Stranger Things appear as DLC in Dead by Daylight.
Haunted Hallows appears as a stage in Rocket League as part of a special collaboration.
Stranger Things is mentioned in "The Joker vs Pennywise".
Stranger Things is parodied in Les Kassos.
Stranger Things: Starcourt Mall was released as a Roblox experience and the player's Roblox Avatar can be used in it.
Stranger Things characters appear in Nanatsu no Taizai: Grand Cross as part of a special collaboration.
Eleven and Hopper are playable characters in Smite for a special collaboration.

Mind Flayer, Jim Hopper, Dustin Henderson, Eleven, Lucas Sinclair, Max Mayfield, Mike Wheeler, Will Byers, and Joyce Byers appear as non-tournament-legal card in the "Secret Lair Drop Series: Stranger Things" release for Magic: The Gathering.
Marky dresses as a Demogorgon in the That Girl Lay Lay episode “Ha-Lay-Lay-Ween”.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles x Stranger Things is a crossover toyline between both franchises. There is also an upcoming Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles x Stranger Things crossover comic book.
Characters that resemble Mike, Will, Dustin and Lucas from Stranger Things appear in I Hate Fairyland #2.
Official Squishmallows were released based on Stranger Things.
Risk: Stranger Things is a format crossover between the two.
Bert and Ernie dressed up as Dustin and Steve to promote the Sesame Street’s appearance on Netflix. "Sharing Things" is a parody of Stranger Things.
Characters and locations from Stranger Things appear in Brawl Stars as part of a special collaboration.
The world of Stranger Things appears in Microsoft Flight Simulator 24.

Strawberry Shortcake.description: In the episode "Channel Chasers", they go to the show Paula Poundcake, a parody of Strawberry Shortcake.
Dance Dance Revolution Strawberry Shortcake is a format crossover between the two series.
In South Park's episode "Imaginationland Episode I" there's a character resembling Strawberry Shortcake.
In The Middle episode "The Trip" Strawberry Shortcake is mentioned.
In a commercial for The Hub's Naughty Or Nice contest, Strawberry Shortcake says Pinkie is the nicest, while Pinkie argues Strawberry is nicer.
Strawberry Shortcake's hat and hair appears in the shop.
Strawberry Shortcake is mentioned in the Doom Patrol episode "Pain Patrol".
Strawberry Shortcake is parodied in Les Kassos.
Strawberry Shortcake: Berry in the Big City is shown on TV in Knock at the Cabin.
Strawberry Shortcake appears alongside Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.
The Care Berry Switch is a crossover special between the two series.

Stray.description: A book can be found in Stray that looks similar to the journals from Gravity Falls except with a paw print instead of a hand.
Two robots that look like Marty and Doc Brown can be found in Stray.
You can find a robot in Stray that looks similar and shares a name with Sojiro from Persona 5.
In Midtown, Sojiro says, "I used to own a bar. It was the coziest place around here. Until I took a screwdriver in the knee, and it's closed now."
A poster for Stray can be found in Professor Chalk's room in the music video for A Songus Amongus.
Stray was reviewed by T.O.M. on Toonami.
A costume based on the cat from Stray can be found in Astro Bot.

Street Fighter.description: A graffiti referencing Legendary Wings appears in Street Fighter, while the Arcade game is playable in the Game Center of Street Fighter 6.
A graffiti referencing Section Z appears in Street Fighter.
A graffiti referencing Avengers appears in Street Fighter; Dan's technique "Hisshou Buraiken" may be named after Hissatsu Buraiken.
A graffiti referencing Trojan appears in Street Fighter.
A graffiti referencing Commando appears in Street Fighter, and a Senjou no Ookami poster can be seen in the "Urban War Zone" stage from Street Fighter X Tekken.
Human Killing Machine is an unofficial sequel to home computer versions of Street Fighter.
One of the players in the "Capcom Games" team is named "Street", after the series.
In the Japanese version of Street Fighter 2010 the planets "Dagobah" and "Tatooine" are named after planets from Star Wars.

It is confirmed that Guile from Street Fighter II was modeled after Jean Pierre Polnareff from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Seth in Street Fighter V imitates special moves used by Dio and Jotaro in JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Heritage for the Future, and there are other minor references.
Mario fights some Street Fighter II characters in the comic Super Mario Klemp-Won-Do: Muskeln sind nicht alles!

Mobichan from Side Arms appears as the cursor in Super Nintendo versions of Street Fighter games and as a special victory symbol (Victory achieved by an attacking taunt) in Street Fighter Zero 2 Alpha; the Side Arms Arcade is playable in the Game Center of Street Fighter 6.
Adventure Quiz: Capcom World 2 features characters from Street Fighter II. Pure from Adventure Quiz: Capcom World 2 makes a came as a party guest in Street Fighter Alpha 2.
Ryu makes an appearance in the fourth stage and credits roll of Varth: Operation Thunderstorm.
Various characters from Art of Fighting resemble characters from Street Fighter, while the Street Fighter character Dan is a parody of Art of Fighting characters.
In the special ending of Tenchi wo Kurau II, the Side Arms Mobilsuits appear dressed as Ryu and Ken and perform their signature moves.
Characters similar to Street Fighter characters appear in the crowd in Yu Yu Hakusho's episode "The Search Begins".
Duke from G.I. Joe meets the characters from Street Fighter II in the G.I. Joe Street Fighter II toyline commercial, while Street Fighter X G.I. Joe is a comic crossover between both series.
Street Fighter II/Streets of Rage II contained one short story based on Street Fighter and another based on Streets of Rage.
The movie City Hunter features a scene based on Street Fighter II.

Chun-Li makes a cameo in Breath of Fire and later with Sakura in Breath of Fire III, while Ryu, Nina, Peco, Teepo and Momo from Breath of Fire III are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, Breath of Fire 6 features special costumes of Ryu, Chun-Li, Guile and Cammy; Falke got a Katt costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition and several Breath of Fire-inspired characters make cameos in Street Fighter 6.
Characters from Street Fighter make cameos in various Final Fight games; various Final Fight characters are recurring characters in the Street Fighter series.

The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as a cursor in the Super Nintendo version of Street Fighter II Turbo, Chelsey from Street Fighter x All Capcom wears a Yashichi hairpin and Vulgus is a playable Arcade game in the Game Center of Street Fighter 6.

The Slam Masters characters King Rasta Mon and Gunloc may be based on Blanka and Guile from Street Fighter; Zangief and Guile are referenced in Slam Masters, while Chun Li, Ryu, and E. Honda make cameos in the audience; Slam Masters characters are referenced and make cameos occasionally in the Street Fighter series.
Characters resembling Chun-Li and Blanka from Street Fighter appear in an ad for Clayfighter, being crushed by Bad Mr. Frosty.

The Hadouken and Shoryuken are unlockable in Mega Man X games; Chun-li and Charlie make cameos in Mega Man media; "Bad Box Art" Mega Man is playable in the PlayStation 3/Vita version of Street Fighter X Tekken; Mega Man characters appear in Street Fighter × All Capcom and Street Fighter Battle Combination; Street Fighter X Mega Man is a crossover between both series; The world of Street Fighter is visited in Sonic and Megaman: Worlds Unite; Dr. Wily makes a cameo in UDON's Street Fighter II comic; several Mega Man costumes are featured in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition, and there are other minor references between both series.
All New World of Lemmings features a "Hadoken" tool based on the move from the Street Fighter series.
The Ferret appears in volume 3 of the Street Fighter comic by Malibu.
Sabin's Aura Cannon Blitz attack in Final Fantasy VI is likely based off of the Hadouken from Street Fighter, using the same button combination.
Eyedol's ending in the first Killer Instinct is a parody of Blanka's ending from Street Fighter II.
Akuma appears as a secret character in X-Men: Children of the Atom; X-Men vs. Street Fighter is a crossover between the two series.
Bonus-kun and Rouwe from Galaxy Fight are parodies of Ryu from Street Fighter.

Blanka from Street Fighter II is referenced in the English version of Felicia's ending from Night Warrior: Darkstalkers' Revenge while characters from Darkstalkers appear in Street Fighter × All Capcom and Street Fighter Battle Combination; Darkstalkers characters appear in Street Fighter Alpha 2 and Street Fighter III; "Street Fighter VS Darkstalkers" is a comic crossover between both series and Street Fighter V features several Darkstalkers costumes. There are other minor references between both series.
Two robots in Ganbare Goemon Kirakira Dōchū: Boku ga Dancer ni Natta Wake look like Ryu and Guile from Street Fighter II.

Strider Hiryu makes a cameo as a party guest in Street Fighter Alpha 2 and he alongside Strider Hien, Tong Pooh, Solo and Lago are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; while one of Hiryu's color alts in the 2014 Strider is inspired by Ibuki from Street Fighter III; Zeku from Street Fighter V has several nods and references to Hiryu and the Strider series.

Captain Commando makes a cameo appearance in the intro of Street Fighter × All Capcom and as a party guest with Ginzu and Carol in Street Fighter Alpha 2, the moves and combat armor of Crimson Viper from Street Fighter IV are inspired by Captain Commando's and Nash receives a costume of the Captain in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.

The two unknown soldiers from Forgotten Worlds appear as party guests in Street Fighter Alpha 2, Two.P's profile in the online Street Fighter V character encyclopedia features further references to the red Unknown Soldier and Guile receives an Unknown Soldier 1P costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.

Lynn Kurosawa from Alien vs. Predator makes a background appearance in Ryu's stage in Street Fighter III and as a party guest in Street Fighter Alpha 2, while there's a Street Fighter billboard in Alien vs. Predator.

Lynn Kurosawa from Alien vs. Predator makes a background appearance in Ryu's stage in Street Fighter III and as a party guest in Street Fighter Alpha 2, while there's a Street Fighter billboard in Alien vs. Predator.
The second season episode "Old Grey Whistle Theft" of Father Ted features characters playing Street Fighter II.

Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo and Puzzle Fighter feature various characters from Street Fighter, while a man can be seen playing the game in the 3rd issue of the Street Fighter Legends: Sakura comic book.

Ryu's Japan stage from Street Fighter Alpha: Warrior's Dream appears in one of the character scenarios in Quiz Nanairo Dreams, as well as merchandising based on the series. Quiz Nanairos Dreams was planned to be featured in Street Fighter × All Capcom, with Saki appearing in official art.
Musashi in Puzzle Bobble 3 is designed and uses similar moves to Ryu of Street Fighter.
The Warrior King from the Street Fighter cartoon episode "The Warrior King" appears in the Savage Dragon cartoon episode "Endgame".

The Warrior King from the Street Fighter cartoon episode "The Warrior King" appears in the Mortal Kombat: Defenders of the Realm cartoon episode "Resurrection". Additionally, the character Kobra in Mortal Kombat: Deception may be inspired on Ken from Street Fighter; Mortal Kombat Armageddon features various elements from Street Fighter in Kreate a Fighter mode.
The Warrior King from the Street Fighter cartoon episode "The Warrior King" appears in the Wing Commander Academy cartoon episode "Recreation".
Bonus-kun's moveset in Waku Waku 7 is a parody of Ryu's moveset from Street Fighter.

A sketch from Red Earth shows Street Fighter's Chun-Li as a member of Mai-Ling's combat unit, Menat's design in Street Fighter V includes a reference to Red Earth, while Alex and Zeku received a Leo and Kenji costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.
Jeynus's ending image in the Arrange Mode of Game Tengoku for the Sega Saturn shows him and Genius Yamada dressed like Guile and Ryu.
Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter is a crossover between the two series. Akuma appears in one of Anita's attacks in Marvel Super Heroes.
Pocket Fighter features various characters from Street Fighter; Asuka is seen playing the game in Street Fighter Alpha: The Movie, and the game was included in the Street Fighter Alpha Anthology.

Sakura from Street Fighter is selectable in Rival Schools, Batsu and Akira are selectable in Street Fighter Online: Mouse Generation and many Rival Schools characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; Hinata and Tiffany make a background cameo in Street Fighter V, with Akira becoming a playable character in Season 5. Many characters are also recurring in the Street Fighter UDON comic book series.

Fighting Layer and Fighter EX Layer feature characters originally from the Street Fighter EX series, while Ace from Street Fighter EX3 features three moves lifted from Fighting Layer and five Fighting EX Layer costumes were available in Street Fighter V: Champion Edition in limited events.

Various Street Fighter characters are selectable in all Marvel vs. Capcom games; SonSon from Marvel vs. Capcom 2 is selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom and Ruby Heart is reimagined as new character "Ruby" in the Street Fighter universe via the online Street Fighter V character encyclopedia as well as given as a costume for Rose in Champion Edition.

Ryu makes a minor cameo appearance in Gantetsu's normal ending from Plasma Sword, while Saturn Dyer from Star Gladiator makes a cameo in Paul Phoenix's artwork from Street Fighter X Tekken, watching him punch an alien and Chun Li receives a June Lin Millian costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.
Having saved data of Street Fighter EX unlocks the special "Dragon" dragon in Dragonseeds.
Capcom Generations 5 has been released as Street Fighter Collection 2 outside Japan.
Deadpool #27 features a reference to Street Fighter and the Shoryuken.
Q's ending in Street Fighter III: Third Strike features references to the X-Files series.
A Street Fighter Alpha artwork can be found in the Researcher Rest Room area from Dino Crisis; while Dino Crisis was one of the planned series to be featured in Street Fighter × All Capcom.
Various Street Fighter characters are selectable in all SNK vs. Capcom games; Violent Ken from SNK vs. Capcom: SVC Chaos is a selectable character in Ultra Street Fighter II: The Final Challengers.
A Street Fighter poster can be found in Biohazard Gun Survivor.

Cammy and Charlie from Street Fighter are selectable characters in Cannon Spike, and Vega/Balrog/Claw also appears as boss character "Fallen/Revenger Balrog"; while Simone and Shiba Shintaro were introduced in the Street Fighter universe via the online Street Fighter V character encyclopedia, with Cammy and Nash receiving their Cannon Spike costumes in Arcade Edition.
Taisen Net Gimmick: Capcom & Psikyo All Stars features characters from the Street Fighter series.
A Street Fighter II arcade cabinet appears in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Company Picnic".
Auto Modellista features car decals referencing the Street Fighter series.
Street Fighter and Street Fighter II: Champion Edition are included in Capcom Arcade Hits: Volume 1. Street Fighter II, Champion Edition and Turbo are included in Capcom Arcade.
Capcom Black Jack features appearances of Chun-Li from Street Fighter.
In the episode "Amnesio" from Lilo & Stitch: The Series, the arcade games that Lilo/Martha and the little boy were playing had sound effects similar to Street Fighter.
A track from Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie appears in Karaoke Revolution: Anime Song Collection.
An Arcade parody of Street Fighter Alpha 3 titled "Super Turbo Turkey Puncher 3" can be found and interacted with in Doom 3.
The Scott Pilgrim series features many references to the Street Fighter series.

Twelve Street Fighter characters are selectable in Capcom Fighting Evolution; Ingrid is selectable in Street Fighter Alpha 3 MAX and the three original characters from Capcom Fighting All-Stars have been included in the online Street Fighter V character encyclopedia and Karin is given an Ingrid costume in Arcade Edition.
Four characters in Power Pro Kun Pocket 7 are named after Ryu, Chun-Li, Sagat and Zangief.
Namco × Capcom features characters from the Street Fighter series.
Various Street Fighter games are included in the various Capcom Classics Collection titles.
The episode "Bato of the Water Tribe" of Avatar: The Last Airbender features a character likely based on Ryu from Street Fighter.
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there's a reference to the Street Fighter series.
Universal Fighting System includes nine sets of cards based on Street Fighter.
Ryu from Street Fighter appears as a character in the browser game American Dad vs. Family Guy Kung-Fu II.

Ryu from Street Fighter appears as a character in the browser game American Dad vs. Family Guy Kung-Fu II; Akiko appears dressed as Chun-Li in the American Dad! episode "Best Little Horror House in Langley Falls".
One of Gene's moves and a minor enemy in God Hand references the Street Fighter series, one of Cody's costume colors in Street Fighter V is based on Gene.
Arino plays the SNES port of Street Fighter II: The World Warrior in episode 37 of GameCenter CX, and 2010 Street Fighter in episode 95.

Captain Sawada from Street Fighter: The Movie appears in Mainichi Issho, while Toro and Kuro from Doko Demo Issyo are selectable in PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita versions of Street Fighter X Tekken.
Capcom Girl no Mind Puzzle features appearances of Chun-Li and other Street Fighter girls.
Konata explains how she met Tsukasa who was afraid from a foreigner (cameo of Guile) who was just asking for directions
The character Chan Lee in Bakugan Battle Brawlers is based on Chun-Li.
Characters from Street Fighter appear in I Wanna Be The Guy.
The Simpsons Game features an enemy based on Ryu from Street Fighter.

In the video game Mission Start: The Germ Warrior from Atlantis SquarePantis, one can see a code that says 1991 © Nickelodeon Inc. The title screen and title are a parody of Street Fighter II: The World Warrior.
A costume based on Ken Masters from Street Fighter can be unlocked in Rayman Raving Rabbids 2.
Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix UNO is a format crossover add-on for the Xbox 360 version of UNO.
Several Street Fighter characters appear in the Capcom-published Harvey Birdman: Attorney at Law video game.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews "Street Fighter" in The Street Fighter + Mortal Kombat Movie Review
One of Pyro's taunts is based on the Hadouken from Street Fighter.
Hu Fei from Flying Fox of Snowy Mountain is selectable in Street Fighter Online: Mouse Generation.
He Tieshou from Sword Stained with Royal Blood is selectable in Street Fighter Online: Mouse Generation.
"Zenny", the currency from Black Tiger, appears in Street Fighter IV and originally appeared inStreet Fighter V.

Cammy is featured in artworks for 1942: Joint Strike, while planes from 1942 are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom. 2019: World President Challenges an STG is a format crossover between both series.
Cyborgs 004, 005, 006 and 009 from Cyborg 009 are selectable in Street Fighter Online: Mouse Generation.
Various Street Fighter characters are selectable in the two Tatsunoko vs. Capcom games.
Outfits based on Street Fighter characters are downloadable in LittleBigPlanet.
The UDON comic Street Fighter II Turbo #6 features references to The Terminator.
Street Fighter II Tribute is an expansion pack for Zen Pinball that includes locations and characters from Street Fighter.
3D Dot Game Heroes features two loading screens based on Street Fighter II.
A pinball table based on Street Fighter 2 was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX.
The Street Fighter II arcade game is heavily featured in High Score Girl.

The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Street Fighter 2010, Fighting Street and Street Fighter: The Movie in the episode "Street Fighter 2010"; he also talks about the Tiger LCD version of Street Fighter II in the episode "Tiger Electronic Games".
Pop'n Music 18 Sengoku Retsuden features a track from Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie.
In the episode "Pinxillated" of the Pink Panther and Pals TV show, there's an arcade game similar to Street Fighter II.
Zangief and El Fuerte's Ultra Combos from Super Street Fighter IV references finishing moves from the Kinnikuman series.
A character heavily resembling Zangief from Street Fighter makes a cameo in episode 13 of Beyblade: Metal Masters.
The World 1 intro in Super Meat Boy is a parody of the intro from Street Fighter II, while the Chapter 1 warp zone from Super Meat Boy Forever is a parody of the car mini-game from the same game.
Street Fighter is parodied in the MAD sketch "MAD's Guide to Video Game Cheats".
Sound effects from Street Fighter can be heard in "Dick Figures - Teabag Teaser".
Akuma, Zangief, Chun-Li, Blanka, M. Bison, Ryu, Dan Hibiki, Cammy White, Ken Masters, and Balrog have been subjects for Death Battle!
The bonus chapter in Nazo Waku Yakata features a cameo of Ryu and a boss battle against M.Bison.
Street Fighter II is mentioned in the Ready Player One novel, while several characters make cameos as OASIS player avatars in the movie.
Linkara reviews Street Fighter #1.

Sagat from Street Fighter makes a cameo appearance during Interlude 10 in Asura's Wrath; Chun-li makes a cameo in Interlude 22 and Ryu/Evil Ryu and Akuma/Oni are enemies in DLC content for Asura's Wrath; while several characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom and Kage received an Asura costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.
Street Fighter X Tekken and Tekken X Street Fighter are crossovers between the two series; Akuma is a selectable character in Tekken 7: Fated Retribution.
Pac-Man is selectable in PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita versions of Street Fighter X Tekken.
Cole from Infamous is selectable in PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita versions of Street Fighter X Tekken.
There are several references to Street Fighter in Skullgirls.

The list of generic monickers in Dragon's Dogma features the names of several Street Fighter characters as possible monickers, while Dragon's Dogma Online features some head gear and hairstyles from the series as accessories, and later Ryu's theme from Street Fighter II as part of a special event.
Chun Li appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32. M. Bison appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #53.
The titular video game in the Gravity Falls episode "Fight Fighters" is based on Street Fighter II.
Minna to Capcom All Stars features characters from the Street Fighter series, while Street Fighter X All Capcom is part of both series.
Wreck-It Ralph features various characters from Street Fighter II.
The episode "The Words" of The Amazing World of Gumball features several references to the Street Fighter series.
There is crossover merchandise featuring characters from Cactus Friends interacting with characters from Street Fighter.
There is crossover merchandise featuring characters from Moofia interacting with characters from Street Fighter.
There is crossover merchandise featuring characters from Royal Pride interacting with characters from Street Fighter.
Monopoly: Street Fighter Collector's Edition is a format crossover between the two series.

Onimusha Soul features Ryu and Chun-Li in a "Capcom Title Collaboration" event and C.Viper, Rose, Cammy, Ibuki and Sakura in a "Capcom Heroines" event; Several Onimusha characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, Onimusha: Dawn Of Dreams features unlockable costumes of Street Fighter characters and Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition features an Akane costume for Ibuki.
Stick figures of Ryu and Ken (later named Rai U. and Kent) appear in Infiltrating the Airship.
The videogame "Bravo Fighter II" from the episode "Couch of Doom" of the Bravoman web series is a parody of Street Fighter II.
One journal entry mentions Street Fighter in Gone Home.
Divekick features various parodies of the Street Fighter series.
"Annoying Orange vs Street Fighter" is a parody Street Fighter.
The introduction image to chapter 29 of the Shokugeki no Soma manga is drawn as a parody of Street Fighter characters Ryu, M. Bison, Chun Li and Cammy.
Ryu, Ken, Chun-Li and Blanka appear as playable characters in Combo Crew.

Several monsters from Monster Hunter and cats from the MonHan Diary subseries are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; while Monster Hunter Frontier G features downloadable costumes based on Ryu, Chun-Li, Cammy and Ken, Monster Hunter X features Palico armor sets based on Chun-Li and Blanka, Monster Hunter Explore features costumes of Ryu, Chun-li, Rashid, Karin, Akuma, Sakura, Cammy and Ken and weapons based on M.Bison, Guile, Vega and Dhalsim; Monster Hunter World features Ryu and Sakura's costumes with their voices and techniques, Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition features costumes based on Monster Hunter armors, and Cammy's codename "Killer Bee" is a title given to the player in Monster Hunter Tri. The Gore Magala from Monster Hunter appears as a boss in Street Fighter: Duel during a collaboration event.

A Mecha version of Akuma is selectable in the console versions of Cyberbots, while Jin Saotome, Devilotte, Arieta, Blodia and Riot are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom and Ryu, Sagat and Menat received a Jin, Shade and Devilotte costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.

Arthur, Red Arremer, Astaroth, Princess Prin-Prin and other Ghosts 'n Goblins characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; Arthur and Red Arremer are featured in Street Fighter Battle Combination, and Arthur and Astaroth costumes are featured in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition. There are other minor references between both series.

Phoenix Wright, Miles Edgeworth, Franziska von Karma, Maya Fey and other Ace Attorney characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, while Cody got several colors based on Ace Attorney characters in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.
Amaterasu, Issun, Susano, Waka, Oki, Sakuya and Yami from Ōkami are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, while there's a reference to Akuma's "Shun Goku Satsu" in Ōkami.

Sonson and Tonton are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; a store named "Sonson" also appears in the background of Ryu's and Guy's stages in Street Fighter Alpha and in Luke's story in Street Fighter V; and SonSon is a playable Arcade in the Game Center of Street Fighter 6.

Wayne Holden, PTX-140, a Mountain Pirate and other Lost Planet chracters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, while "Street Fighter" is one of the unlockable Nom de Guerres in Lost Planet 2.
Viewtiful Joe, Sexy Silvia, Captain Blue, Alastor and Another Joe are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, while Rashid has a Viewtiful Joe costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.

Several Resident Evil characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom and also appear in Street Fighter Battle Combination; additionally a Street Fighter poster can be found in Resident Evil Survivor, the HD version of Resident Evil 0 features a costume based on Cody from the Street Fighter series and costumes of Resident Evil characters are DLC in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.

Dante, Vergil, Nero, Trish, Lady and Nelo Angelo from Devil May Cry are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; while several Devil May Cry costumes appear in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition. Dante appears as a playable character in Street Fighter: Duel during a collaboration event. There are other minor references between both series.

Date Masamune, Yukimura Sanada and other Sengoku BASARA characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; while Sengoku BASARA 4 Sumeragi features a DLC costume pack based on characters from Street Fighter.
Sissel, Lynne, Cabanela, Kamila, Jeego and Ray from Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom.
G.Kaiser from Tech Romancer makes a cameo appearance in the intro of Street Fighter × All Capcom.
Jazzpunk features a minigame where you beat up a Honda which also includes sound effects ripped straight from Street Fighter.

Kou, G.Red, Usagi, Kakeru and other Gotcha Force characters are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom, while the borg Cyber Hero and Orochi from Gotcha Force feature references to the Street Fighter series
Hyperdevotion Noire: Goddess Black Heart features a character called Lee-Fi, that is a parody of Chun-Li.

Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha features Ryu and Chun-Li costumes, along with the actual moves from Street Fighter, and zombie versions of Akuma and M.Bison as bosses; Dead Rising 2 also features a Blanka mask and the combo weapons "Roaring Thunder" and "Dragon Punch" reference techniques from Street Fighter; Dead Rising 4 features costumes of several Street Fighter characters, and Frank West from Dead Rising appears in official art for Street Fighter × All Capcom. Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster features costumes based on Ken and Sodom from the Street Fighter series.
Bennett The Sage reviews “Street Fighter II The Animated Movie”.
Kengan Ashura vs. Street Fighter is a two-part crossover manga between the two series.
Street Fighter is parodied in Les Kassos.
Super Smash Bros. for Wii U and for 3DS feature Ryu from Street Fighter as a downloadable character, along with his own stage, while Super Smash Bros. Ultimate adds Ken as an Echo Fighter.
The world of Street Fighter is visited in Sonic and Megaman: Worlds Unite Part 8 - Holes in Reality, including appearances of Ryu, Chun-li, Ken, Guile and M.Bison.
Ryu, Chun-li and others from Street Fighter characters appeared in Monster Strike as part of a collaboration event, and a second collaboration with Street Fighter V characters including Ken in 2016.
Several theme songs from Street Fighter IV, Ultra Street Fighter IV and Street Fighter V are featured in CROSS×BEATS REV.
A poster referencing Street Fighter can be seen in Himouto! Umaru-chan.
Board James reviews the Street Fighter II board game in the episode "Video Games!!"
In the episode "Terror Tales of the Park V" from Regular Show, Rigby is dressed as M. Bison from Street Fighter, while the episode "Bad Portrait" features references to Street Fighter II.
There are several references to Street Fighter II in the Pop Team Epic manga and episode 8 of the anime.

The logo for the "Fall Superhuman Festival II" and "Fall Superhuman Festival II Dash" events in Otoranger are inspired by Street Fighter II and Street Fighter II Turbo, while a banner in the “Union Station” stage in Street Fighter V features Eisbahn from Otoranger
Characters from Street Fighter appear in Granblue Fantasy as a part of a collaboration.

One of Edward Falcon's moves in Power Stone resembles Ken's Shinryuken, Power Stone was one of the planned series to be featured in Street Fighter × All Capcom, the logo from Edward Falcon's airplane appears in the Street Fighter Unlimited comic book and Ken receives a Falcon costume in Street Fighter V: Champion Edition.
There's a reference to Don't Pull and Three Wonders in the online Street Fighter V character encyclopedia.
Momotaro, Bows and Captain Beard from Higemaru are reimagined as new characters in the Street Fighter universe via the online Street Fighter V character encyclopedia.
Ryu, Fei Long, Guile, Akuma, Ken, Dhalsim, Chun-Li, Juri, and Karin Kanzuki have been subjects for DBX.
Street Fighter is mentioned in the Black Mirror episode: "Playtest".
Ryu and Ken from Street Fighter are parodied in the Cell Vs episode "Cell Vs Ryu & Ken".
Several characters in River City Ransom: Underground have moves loosely based on characters from the Street Fighter series.
Seven Knights features Ryu, Chun-li, Akuma, Karin and Necalli from Street Fighter V as part of a special collaboration.
Ryu's School Costume from Street Fighter V is inspired by Makoto Mizoguchi from Fighter's History.
Several characters from Street Fighter V are part of a collaboration event in the game Shadowverse.
Ryu, Chun-li, Guile and M.Bison from Street Fighter V are part of a collaboration event in the game LINE Rangers.
Hadou Fred from Clicker Fred is based on Ryu.
Characters from Street Fighter V appear in #COMPASS as part of a collaboration.
Richie Tozier plays Street Fighter in It and It: Chapter Two.
In South Park's episode "Imaginationland Episode II" there's a character resembling Akuma. Chung Lee’s thighs were mentioned by Memberberries in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don! features a music track from Street Fighter V.
Ryu, Chun-li, Cammy, Akuma, Ken, Karin and Evil Ryu from Street Fighter, as well as a quest with other characters and references, are part of a collaboration event in the game Valkyrie Connect.
Spencer Gilpin plays Street Fighter V in Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle.
Destiny Child features Chun-li and Cammy as part of a special collaboration.
Cammy's hair and cap, Guile's hair, Kage fur, and a Hadoken cannonball skin appear in the shop.
Street Fighter II × Transformers is a special toyline made of Transformers toys repainted to resemble Street Fighter II characters.

Several Street Fighter V characters are featured in Power Rangers: Legacy Wars as part of a special collaboration; a Ryu Ranger character was included in the short film Power Rangers: Legacy Wars: Street Fighter Showdown, and Ryu (as the Crimson Hawk Ranger) and Chun-Li (as the Blue Phoenix Ranger) are playable DLC characters in Power Rangers: Battle for the Grid.
Color 14 of G's Story Costume in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition is a reference to the Mask.
Cammy receives a costume of Fiona Belli from Haunting Ground in Street Fighter V: Arcade Edition.
Street Fighter toys of Ryu and Ken are brought to life in Goosebumps 2.

Ryu, Chun-li, Ken, Sakura and others from Street Fighter V: Champion Edition appeared in Puzzle & Dragons and Puzzle & Dragons Radar (with various characters appearing as leaders) during a special collaboration.
Street Fighter is parodied in in multiple Perfect Cell Vs episodes.
TEPPEN features various characters from the Street Fighter series.
A "Street Kiter" game can be found in an arcade in Later Alligator.
Ryu, Ken, Chun-li and The World Warriors from Street Fighter V appear in The Battle Cats as a part of a collaboration.
The "Red General Tiny" skin in Crash Team Racing Nitro-Fueled is a reference to M. Bison from Street Fighter.
Ryu, Ken, M.Bison, Dhalsim and Chun-li from Street Fighter V appear in Summoners War as part of a special collaboration.
Music from Street Fighter II can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix.

Street Fighter II: The World Warriors, Hyper Fighting and Super Street Fighter II Turbo are included in Capcom Arcade Stadium, Street Fighter and the 3 Street Fighter Alpha games are included in Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium.
Ryu, Chun-Li, Cammy, Guile, Sakura and Blanka from Street Fighter appear in Fortnite.

In the Total Dramarama episode "Shock & AWW", Duncan preforms an electric projectile while saying "Ha-duncan", a reference to the Hadouken from Street Fighter. Courtney even mentions the move being similar to one from a video game from over 30 years ago.
Characters from Street Fighter V appear in Fist of the North Star: Legends ReVIVE as part of a collaboration event.
One of the eight promotional posters for Free Guy released on August 9th is based on the cover of Street Fighter.

Street Fighter.description: Veldora uses Hadouken, Shoryuken, and Tatsumaki Senpukyaku in Episode 47 of That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime.
Ryu, Akuma and Chun-li from Street Fighter appear in Brawlhalla as part of a crossover event. Later, M.Bison, Ken, Sakura, Dhalsim and Luke appear in the second round of the event.
One of Ame's social media posts in Needy Streamer Overload refernces Akuma from Street Fighter IV.
Ryu, Ken, E. Honda, Blanka, Chun Li, Dhalsim, Guile, and Zangief appear as non-tournament-legal cards in the "Secret Lair Drop Series: Street Fighter" release for Magic: The Gathering.
Minecraft features a Street Fighter skin pack for Bedrock Edition.
Several characters from Street Fighter appear in The King of Fighters: All Star as part of two special events.
"Something About Street Fighter II" is a parody of Street Fighter II.

Unused sprites of Ryu, Chun-li and Guile from Street Fighter II can be found within the code of Armored Warriors, while Street Fighter V: Champion Edition features a minor reference to the key art of Armored Warriors.
Chun Li has a star on The Hollywood Walk of Fame in Rescue Rangers (2022).
Hyper Street Fighter II is included in Capcom Fighting Collection, while Street Fighter Alpha 3 UPPER is included in Capcom Fighting Collection 2.
A game similar to Street Fighter appears in the Rick and Morty episode: "Bethic Twinstinct".
Skins based on Ryu, Cammy and Akuma from Street Fighter appear in Fall Guys.
The Animaniacs episode "WARnerGAMES" features a reference to Street Fighter.
A YouTube video was uploaded by Tooniverse's official channel, Street Ghost Fighter (스트릿 고스트 파이터) which references Street Fighter.
"Video Games" by Tenacious D includes a brief segment referencing Street Fighter.
Exed Exes is a playable Arcade in the Game Center of Street Fighter 6.
Magic Sword: Heroic Fantasy is a playable Arcade in the Game Center of Street Fighter 6.
Street Fighter is parodied in the Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episode "I Like Cammy More".

The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles episode "The Gaminator" features a character based on Akuma from Street Fighter, while Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles vs. Street Fighter is a comic book crossover between both franchises. Cosmetics based on Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles appear in Street Fighter 6.
Street Fighter characters appear as skins in PUBG during a crossover event.
A human version of Street Fighter II appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.
Robot versions of Ryu, Guile, and Chun Li from Street Fighter 6 appear in Exoprimal as part of a special collaboration.
Yor Forger from Spy × Family fights Chun-Li in a trailer for Street Fighter 6. Additionally, cosmetics based on Spy x Family appear in Street Fighter 6 as part of a collaboration event.
Cosmetics based on Baki the Grappler appear in Street Fighter 6 as part of a collaboration event.
Yuuki and Shushu play Super Street Fighter II in Episode 2 of Chained Soldier.
The cover to Street Fighter 2010: The Final Fight appears in the Ted episode: "Loud Night".
Street Fighter characters appear in Last Cloudia for a collaboration event.
A Street Fighter arcade cabinet can be seen in the music video for FNAF Kids.
Bots can be found playing a game similar to Street Fighter called "Bot Fighter in Astro's Playroom. Costumes based on Ken and Ryu from Street Fighter can be found in Astro Bot.
Terry and Mai from Fatal Fury appear in Street Fighter 6 as playable DLC characters. Ken and Chun-Li frn Street Fighter appear in Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves as playable DLC characters.
Zangief, Dhalsim, and Blanka from Street Fighter appear in the couch gag for the Simpsons episode "Treehouse of Horror XXXV".

Overwatch 2 includes several cosmetics based on Street Fighter 6, including Ryu Hanzo, Chun-Li Juno, Cammy Widowmaker, Juri Kiriko, Guile Soldier: 76, M. Bison Sigma, Blanka Winston, and Dhalsim Zenyatta skins.
Characters from Street Fighter appear as Operators in Call of Duty: Mobile, along with other Street Fighter cosmetics.

Street Sharks.description: Extreme Dinosaurs is a spin-off of Street Sharks.
Street Sharks is parodied in the Robot Chicken episodes: "Butchured in Burbank" and "Catdog on a Stick".

Streets of Fury.description: The Nostalgia Critic is a playable character in Streets of Fury EX.

Streets of Rage.description: Street Fighter II/Streets of Rage II contained one short story based on Street Fighter and another based on Streets of Rage.
Sega Smash Pack Volume 1 includes Streets Of Rage 2.
Axel Stone from Streets of Rage is an unlockable player in ESPN NFL Football.
The three Streets of Rage games are included in the Japanese version of Sonic Gems Collection; additionally a beta version of Streets of Rage 3 featured an image of Sonic on billboards.
Captain S enters the world of Streets of Rage.
The arcade game "Teens of Rage" from the Steven Universe episode "Arcade Mania" is a parody of Streets of Rage.

Sega 3D Reprint Archives features Streets of Rage with Streets of Rage characters interacting with other characters in the credits. Sega 3D Reprint Archives 3: Final Stage features Streets of Rage 2 with Streets of Rage characters interacting with other characters in the credits.
Axel, Blaze and Adam from the Streets of Rage series are unlockable in the retail release of 3D Power Drift.
Characters from Streets of Rage appear in Sega Heroes.
Graffiti of Joe Musashi from Shinobi appears in Stage 5 of Streets of Rage 4.
Security Breach: Fury's Rage is inspired by Streets of Rage.
Picross S Genesis & Master System Edition includes puzzles based off Streets of Rage.
Arino plays the Genesis game Streets of Rage 2 in episode 368.
A Streets of Rage box can be seen in the Ted episode: "My Two Dads".

Stretch Dungeon.description: The Prisoner from Stretch Dungeon appears as a contestant on Leap Day.
The Prisoner is part of Yolk's moves in Indie Pogo.

Strider.description: Several characters were inspired by the scene from The Empire Strikes Back where Darth Vader contracts bounty hunters. Other elements from Strider may have been inspired by elements in Star Wars.
The final boss Grandmaster Meio was inspired by Sauron. The flying battleship Balrog is named after the demon of the same name.
Mecha Pon from Strider was inspired by Mechani-Kong from The King Kong Show.
The NES Strider is part of the Captain Commando Challenge Series.
Strider Hiryu is pictured in a newspaper ad in Capcom Baseball. One of the players in the "Capcom Games" team is named "Stri", after the series.

Stage 4 in Strider II bears similar design to areas in the Alien movies, as well as enemies resembling the Xenomorphs, while one of Hiryu's color alts in the 2014 Strider may be inspired by Lt. Linn Kurosawa from Alien vs. Predator.
The Adventure Quiz series features characters from Strider.
A sword weapon in Tenchi wo Kurau 2 is named after Hiryu from Strider, while the female assassin trio may be inspired by the Kuniang Team from Strider.
The ledges and climbing mechanic in Zool: Ninja of the Nth Dimension are inspired by Strider.
Sonic & Knuckles uses some edited sprites borrowed from the Mega Drive port of Strider, which was developed internally by Sega.

Strider Hiryu makes a cameo as a party guest in Street Fighter Alpha 2 and he alongside Strider Hien, Tong Pooh, Solo and Lago are selectable in Street Fighter × All Capcom; while one of Hiryu's color alts in the 2014 Strider is inspired by Ibuki from Street Fighter III; Zeku from Street Fighter V has several nods and references to Hiryu and the Strider series.
A sketch from Red Earth shows Strider's Tong Pooh as a member of Mai-Ling's combat unit, one of Hiryu's color alts in the 2014 Strider is inspired by Kenji from Red Earth.
Tessa's quiz in the English version of Pocket Fighter for consoles includes 2 references to Strider.

Strider Hiryu is a recurring playable character in the Marvel vs. Capcom series. Tong Pooh is an assist character in Marvel vs. Capcom and Grandmaster Meio is part of the story in Marvel vs. Capcom Infinite. Elements from Hiryu's portrayal were later carried over into the Strider series.
Various Strider characters are featured in SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.

THE iDOLM@STER.description: The bio for Junichirou Takagi in the strategy guide THE iDOLM@STER Platinum Album states that the first idol he worked with as Producer was Namco's Wonder Momo, while a Wonder Momo costume is part of the Catalogue 4 DLC for THE iDOLM@STER Live for You! and the music theme "GO MY WAY!!" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 01 is a remix of a theme from Wonder Momo.

The remix theme Futari no Mojipittan is featured in the music CD THE iDOLM@STER Your Song and other later releases, the Vocal Lesson interface from THE IDOLM@STER Dearly Stars is based on Mojipittan and features Erabu-kun; while Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Encore features a set of stages based on THE iDOLM@STER characters.

Beautiful Katamari stage Cloud Nine Forest features the song "Danketsu", sung by four idols from The iDOLM@STER series, while a set of accessories based on The Prince is DLC in THE iDOLM@STER: Live for You!, The Prince made a guest appearance in the 10th broadcast of THE IDOLM@STER STATION!!! and the cover song for THE IDOLM@STER STATION!!! SECOND TRAVEL is based on the opening theme from We Love Katamari.

Ace Combat 6, Assault Horizon, and Infinity feature aircraft paints based on THE iDOLM@STER. The third game expanded the collaboration by including emblems and nicknames based on THE iDOLM@STER characters and songs.
The costume "Marchen Maid" from Catalogue 11 in the Xbox 360 version of THE iDOLM@STER is based on Alice's dress from Märchen Maze.

A Valkyrie costume is part of the Catalogue 1 DLC for THE iDOLM@STER Live for You!, a Valkyrie-themed phone background and strap appear in THE iDOLM@STER OVA and the music theme "Tabi no Tochuu de" is a remix of the main theme from Valkyrie no Densetsu.

A remix of The Tower of Druaga is included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 01, a remix of The Return of Ishtar is included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04 while a Tower of Druaga Arcade cabinet appears in episode 17 of THE iDOLM@STER anime.
Two remix themes based on Libbe Rabble are included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 01.

The theme "Labyrinth" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 01 is based on Pac-Man, Pac-Man based costume parts are featured as DLC for THE iDOLM@STER: Live for You!, while Pac-Man merchandise appear in episodes 17 and 19 of THE iDOLM@STER anime.
A Susumu Hori costume is part of the Catalogue 2 DLC for THE iDOLM@STER Live for You!, while episodes 6 and 12 of the anime include a Mr. Driller t-shirt and video game.
One remix theme based on Gaplus is included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 02, while Sana Miyoshi from The  iDOLM@STER: Cinderella Girls has shirts with logos based on Galaga.
The music theme "Taiyou no Jealousy" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 02 is a remix of a theme from Ordyne.
Two remixes of the Sky Kid main theme are featured in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03  and Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER BEST ALBUM + LIVE DVD.
The music theme "Kin Renka" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03 is a remix of the main theme from Genpei Toma Den.
The music theme "Tower of Adventure" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03 is a remix of the main theme from Tower of Babel.
The music theme "Mahou o Kakete!" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03 is a remix of the main theme from Yōkai Dōchūki.
The music theme "Massugu" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03 is a remix of the main theme from Phelios.
The music theme "9.02pm" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03 is a remix of the main theme from Dragon Buster.
The music theme "Agent Yoru o Yuku" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04 is a remix of a theme from Rolling Thunder.
The music theme "First Stage" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04 is a remix of a theme from Xevious.
A Dig Dug theme song and attraction appear in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04 and 05, while a Pooka-themed phone strip appears in THE iDOLM@STER OVA.
Music from New Rally-X is featured in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04.
The music theme "Omoide o Arigatou" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 05 is a remix of the main theme from Toy Pop.
A remix of the main theme from Mappy is featured in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 01, with other remixes included in later releases; while the OVA features a Mappy plushie and phone strap.
The theme "Aoi Tori" included in Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 05 is a remix of a theme from Dragon Spirit.

Yayoi Takatsuki from THE iDOLM@STER is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, while Narakiri Dungeon X features a costume for Haruka Amami, Tales of Asteria features 8 idols as playable DLC characters, with one returning in Tales of the Rays; several costumes are also featured in many Tales of games.
There's a series of Weiß Schwarz cards based around characters and items from THE iDOLM@STER.

THE iDOLM@STER SP features a downloadable costume of Xiaoyu with a Panda plushie based on Tekken 5, THE iDOLM@STER Million Live! features cards based on Tekken characters and one of Sana Miyoshi from The  iDOLM@STER: Cinderella Girls has her playing Tekken Tag Tournament 2, while Tekken 7 features costumes based on iDOLM@STER.

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 features Chihaya, Haruka and Miki from THE iDOLM@STER as guest players, while 13 idols from the series appeared in Famista Online 2011 during a special collboration, and Pro Yakyuu Famista Climax features Haruka, Mirai, Uzuki and Tendo.

Costumes based on characters from THE iDOLM@STER SP can be obtained in Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA 2nd; Hatsune Miku appears as an in-game rival in the PS3 version of THE iDOLM@STER 2; Senbonzakura, a song originally sung by Miku, was covered by Azusa Miura in the twelfth album of the THE iDOLM@STER MASTER ARTIST 3 series.
A Hibiki Ganaha costume is unlockable in Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha A's Portable: The Gears of Destiny.
Music and cars based on THE iDOLM@STER can be obtained in Ridge Racer for the PlayStation Vita.
Chihaya Kisaragi makes a guest appearance in the Wooser's Hand-to-mouth Life episode "Cheers ~A Time for Blessings, Keep Common Sense in Mind, Because Wooser Won't~"
Costumes based on THE iDOLM@STER can be obtained in God Eater 2 as DLC.
Characters from THE iDOLM@STER appear in Granblue Fantasy as a part of a collaboration.
Music from THE iDOLM@STER was added to maimai in the maimai GreeN PLUS version.

Taiko characters appear in THE iDOLM@STER Must Songs Red/Blue; additionally music from THE iDOLM@STER series is featured in many Taiko no Tatsujin games, while Idolm@ster SideM features Taiko-themed costumes, and THE iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls and THE iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls Starlight Stage feature playable Taiko no Tatsujin minigames; Taiko no Tatsujin 13 also appears in an episode of THE iDOLM@STER anime.

Characters from THE iDOLM@STER appear in Azur Lane as part of a collaboration event.

Music from THE iDOLM@STER can be played in O.N.G.E.K.I. Bright.

Characters from Uma Musume appear in  The iDOLM@STER: Cinderella Girls Starlight Stage as part of a collaboration event.

Taiko no Tatsujin Shinkyoku Tori Houdai! featured songs from Puyo Puyo Fever Touch and vice versa, as part of two different timed events.
Donko from Taiko no Tatsujin is a character in Namco High.
Taiko no Tatsujin Momoiro Version with its updates and Taiko no Tatsujin V Version feature music tracks from Love Live!
Taiko no Tatsujin Wii U Version features a music track from Balloon Fight, and music from the game is also included in the Famicom Medley, in Taiko no Tatsujin Red Version.
Taiko no Tatsujin Wii U Version and Taiko no Tatsujin Yellow Version feature music tracks from The Legend of Zelda series.
Taiko no Tatsujin Wii U Version features a music track from Famicom Remix
Taiko no Tatsujin Momoiro Version and Taiko no Tatsujin V Version feature a music track from Fantasy Zone, part of the "Game Music Triangle" collaboration.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Don to Katsu no Jikuu Daibouken and later games in the series feature music tracks from Frozen and Frozen 2.

Jibanyan from Yokai Watch is a party member in Taiko no Tatsujin: Don to Katsu no Jikuu Daibouken and Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure, while Don-Chan appears in Yo-Kai Watch 2 and Yo-Kai Watch 3; additionally Taiko no Tatsujin Momoiro Version and later games in the series feature music tracks from Yokai Watch.

Two felyne from the MonHan Diary series are party members in Taiko no Tatsujin: Don to Katsu no Jikuu Daibouken and Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure; various games in the Taiko no Tatsujin series also feature music tracks from the Monster Hunter series, with Taiko no Tatsujin: Wii U Version also featuring a Felyne costume for Don-chan, while Monster Hunter 4g/Ultimate features a Don-chan-themed weapon.
Taiko no Tatsujin Kimidori Version and later games in the series feature music tracks from Haikyu!!; Taiko no Tatsujin Red Version also features a costume based the series.
Taiko no Tatsujin Kimidori Version and later games in the series feature a music track from Bakemonogatari.

A sprite from Taiko no Tatsujin appears in Pac-Man's taunt in Super Smash Bros for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U; Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumete - Tomodachi Daisakusen! features compatibility with the Pac-Man amiibo from the Super Smash Bros. series.
Music from Taiko no Tatsujin was added to maimai in the maimai ORANGE version.
Taiko no Tatsujin V Version and later games in the series feature music tracks from Sword Art Online.
Taiko no Tatsujin V Version features a music track from Fate/Stay night.

Taiko no Tatsujin V Version and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature music tracks from The Legend of Heroes series.
Taiko no Tatsujin V Version features a downloadable music track from Sengoku Basara.

During two different collaboration events, characters from Taiko no Tatsujin appeared in Chain Chronicle: Ties of a New World and Chain Chronicle V, while Taiko no Tatsujin Murasaki Version, V Version and Plus feature music tracks from Chain Chronicle and also costumes based on characters from the game for Don-Chan.

Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumete - Tomodachi Daisakusen! and Taiko no Tatsujin Dokodon! Mystery Adventure feature a music track from World Trigger.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumete - Tomodachi Daisakusen!, V Version and Blue Version feature a music track from Rolling Thunder 2.

Taiko characters appear in THE iDOLM@STER Must Songs Red/Blue; additionally music from THE iDOLM@STER series is featured in many Taiko no Tatsujin games, while Idolm@ster SideM features Taiko-themed costumes, and THE iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls and THE iDOLM@STER Cinderella Girls Starlight Stage feature playable Taiko no Tatsujin minigames; Taiko no Tatsujin 13 also appears in an episode of THE iDOLM@STER anime.
Taiko no Tatsujin V Version and Taiko no Tatsujin White Version with its updates feature a song from Himouto! Umaru-chan; Himouto! Umaru-chan also features an arcade game based on Taiko no Tatsujin.
Taiko no Tatsujin White Version features music tracks from Granblue Fantasy; additionally for April Fool's 2018 a Granblue Fantasy game called Oira based on Taiko no Tatsujin was released.
Phoenix Wright is a party member in Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure; the game also features a music track from the Ace Attorney series.

Kirby and King Dedede are party members in Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure and Kirby also returns in Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version!; Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure and Red Version also feature songs from the Kirby series, with a Meta Knight costume also available in Arcade games.

Reimu Hakurei, Marisa Kirisame and Sakuya Izayoi from Touhou are party members in Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure; additionally Taiko no Tatsujin Momoiro Version and later games in the series feature music tracks from Touhou Project, with items based on the series also appearing in Murasaki Version and V Version.

Korosensei from Assassination Classroom makes an appearance in Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure; additionally Taiko no Tatsujin Plus and later games in the series feature music tracks from Assassination Classroom.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure, Blue Version, Plus, and Nintendo Switch Version! feature songs from Kiki's Delivery Service.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure and Taiko no Tatsujin: The Drum Master! features a music track from Ghosts 'n Goblins.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure features a music track from Super Hang-On.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure and Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don! feature a music track from Warrior Blade: Rastan Saga Episode III.
Taiko no Tatsujin Red version and later games in the series feature a music track from Spirited Away.
A theme song from Taiko no Tatsujin Red Version is featured in CROSS×BEATS REV. SUNRISE.
Taiko no Tatsujin Red version with its updates, Session de Dodon ga Don!, and Nintendo Switch Version! feature a music track from Zootopia.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure features a downloadable music track from My Hero Academia.
Taiko no Tatsujin Red version and other games in the series feature music tracks from Re:Zero.

Mystery Adventure; the game also features a downloadable music track from the anime, while the game Saiki Kusuo no Psi-nan: Shijou Psi-dai no Psi-nan!? features a costume based on Taiko no Tatsujin.

Taiko no Tatsujin Plus and later games in the series feature a music track from Your Name.
Taiko no Tatsujin costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 3.

Taiko no Tatsujin Yellow Version, Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don! and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track and costumes from Osomatsu-san, including drum versions of the characters.
Taiko no Tatsujin Yellow Version, Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don!, and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track and a costume from Kemono Friends.
Taiko no Tatsujin Yellow Version and Nintendo Switch Version! feature a music track from Moana.
Taiko no Tatsujin Yellow Version, Taiko no Tatsujin Plus, and Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version! feature a music track from Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid.
Taiko no Tatsujin Yellow Version and its updates feature a music track from Beauty and the Beast.
Taiko no Tatsujin and later games in the series feature music tracks from Doraemon, with Doraemon himself appearing as a challenger in Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don!.

Heihachi appears as a challenger in Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don!; Taiko no Tatsujin: Wai Wai Happy! Rokudaime and later games in the series feature music tracks from the Tekken series, while Tekken 7: Fated Retribution featured Taiko no Tatsujin-themed items during a limited promotion.

Pac-Man appears as a challenger in Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don!; Music from Pac-Man is featured in the Namcot Medley debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10; Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumete - Tomodachi Daisakusen! also features a costume and theme based on Pac-Man, while Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version! and other games in the series feature music tracks from the Pac-Man series.

The Shinkalion E5 Hayabusa appears in Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version! as a downloadable performance character alongside a song from Shinkansen Henkei Robo Shinkalion.

Taiko no Tatsujin Plus features two songs from Batman Ninja.

Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don! features a music track from Hi Score Girl.
Taiko no Tatsujin Green Version and other games in the series feature a music track from Cells at Work!
Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version! features a downloadable music track from Howl's Moving Castle.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don! and Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version! feature a downloadable music track from The Promised Neverland.
Taiko no Tatsujin Green Version and other games in the series feature music tracks from Kimetsu no Yaiba.
Taiko no Tatsujin Green Version with its updates and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track from the movie Ni no Kuni.
Taiko no Tatsujin Green Version features two music tracks from the anime Gudetama, and the character also interacts with Don-chan and Kat-chan in promotional material.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version! and other games in the series feature music tracks from Undertale.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don!, Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version!, and Taiko no Tatsujin: The Drum Master! feature a music track from Fire Force.

The Duel Masters card Bachio Sensei, Unforgiving of Shakapachi features characters from Taiko no Tatsujin. Additionally, Taiko no Tatsujin Yellow Version and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track from Duel Masters.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Nintendo Switch Version!, Taiko no Tatsujin (Nijiro Version), and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature music tracks from Weathering with You.

Taiko no Tatsujin: Pop Tap Beat features a music track from Baby Shark.

Members of Nijisanji appeared in Taiko no Tatsujin: Rhythm Festival as part of a special collaboration.

Taiko no Tatsujin 5 and later games in the series feature music tracks from One Piece; Taiko no Tatsujin Red Version and Taiko no Tatsujin (Nijiro Version) also feature a Luffy doll for the player's avatar. Characters from One Piece appear in Taiko no Tatsujin: Rhythm Festival.

Several Black Lagoon characters make cameo appearances in the Taimanin RPGX special crossover event, "GUNSLINGER and TAIMANIN".
Several Highschool of the Dead characters make cameo appearances in the Taimanin RPGX special crossover event, "TAIMANIN OF THE DEATH".

Taisen Hot Gimmick.description: Marion (Mirion) is a secret character in Taisen Hot Gimmick and Taisen Hot Gimmick Kairakuten, the character Melty cosplays as Marion in Taisen Hot Gimmick 3: Digital Surfing and Yuan Nang (Ran Nang) is a secret character in Taisen Hot Gimmick 4 Ever, while the Yanken dog from the series replaces the Elephant God in the Dreamcast port of Gunbird 2.

Aine (Kain) and Koyori (Koyomi) from Sengoku Ace are secret characters in Taisen Hot Gimmick and Taisen Hot Gimmick Kairakuten, the character Melty cosplays as Aine in Taisen Hot Gimmick 3: Digital Surfing and Junis (Jumis) from Sengoku Blade is a secret character in Taisen Hot Gimmick 4 Ever.
Taisen Net Gimmick: Capcom & Psikyo All Stars is a spin-off of the Taisen Hot Gimmick series.

Several characters from Gunbird are featured in Taisen Net Gimmick: Capcom & Psikyo All Stars.
Several characters from the Sengoku Ace series are featured in Taisen Net Gimmick: Capcom & Psikyo All Stars.
Nebiros from Dragon Blaze is featured in Taisen Net Gimmick: Capcom & Psikyo All Stars.

Patrako from Cleopatra Fortune is one of the characters in Taito Harikiri Daifugo.
Sayo-chan/Pocky is one of the characters in Taito Harikiri Daifugo.
Mawasu-kun from the Arcade version of Turn it Around is one of the characters in Taito Harikiri Daifugo.

Taito Legends 2 includes Syvalion.

Taito Memories.description: The Fairyland Story was included in Taito Memories Joukan.
Cleopatra Fortune was included in Taito Memories Joukan.
Puchi Carat was included in Taito Memories Joukan.
Qix is included in Taito Memories Volume 2 and Taito Memories Pocket, while Super Qix is included in Taito Memories II Volume 1.
Taito Memories Gekan  and Pocket include Raimais.
Taito Memories II Joukan includes The Ninja Kids.

Tak.description: Tak from Tak and the Power of Juju makes four cameos in the game Rocket Power: Beach Bandits.
Tak from Tak and the Power of Juju makes a cameo in the game Rugrats: Royal Ransom.
Tak characters appear in Nicktoons games.
Tak appears in the Video Mods original video "Stand and Choose".
In Tak 2: The Staff of Dreams, Tak, Jibolba, Lok and Dead Juju fall asleep in a flower field as a spoof to a similar scene in The Wizard of Oz.

Take a Break! Pinball.description: The Quest for Daventry table in Take a Break! Pinball is based on King's Quest V.
The Planet Pinball tables in Take a Break! Pinball are based on Space Quest IV.
The Larry's Big Score table in Take A Break! Pinball is based on Leisure Suit Larry 5: Passionate Patti Does a Little Undercover Work.
The "Flipped Out Willy" board in Take a Break! Pinball is based on The Adventures of Willy Beamish.

Taken.description: Taken characters appear in Taken 3 - TRAILER.
Taken is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Christmas".
The episode "The Kids" of The Amazing World of Gumball features a reference to the cellphone scene from the first Taken movie.
Taken is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Crying Out Loud".
The plot of Taken is mentioned in the Deadpool movie.
An image macro can be found reading "I DONT KNOW WHO YOU ARE BUT I WILL FIND YOU AND I WILL ADD YOU ON INVITE" on the walls in Watch Dogs 2.
Taken was mentioned in the Bojack Horseman episode "Hooray! Todd Episode!"
Taken is mentioned in the Rick and Morty episodes: "The Jerrick Trap" and "Wet Kuat Amortican Summer".

Takeshi no Ch\u014dsenj\u014d.description: Arino plays the NES game Takeshi no Chōsenjō in episode 1.
The game over screen from Takeshi no Chōsenjō can be found in Toilet in Wonderland
There's a minor reference to Takeshi no Chōsenjō in episode 5 of Pop Team Epic.

Tales From The Crypt.description: The Grim Reaper from Bill & Ted's Bogus Journey appears as a co-host in the season 6 episode "The Assassin" from Tales from the Crypt.
The Crypt Keeper from Tales From The Crypt appears in the film Casper.
Elvira met the Crypt Keeper from Tales From The Crypt in a promotional image for Knott's Scary Farm's 1999 Halloween Haunt.
Tales from the Crypt is parodied in the MAD sketch "VeggieTales from the Crypt".
The Detentionaire episode: "Tales from Decrypt"'s title is a reference to Tales From The Crypt.

Tales of (Namco).description: The Special Flag from Rally-X is a usable item in Tales of Phantasia, Tales of the Abyss and Tales of Vesperia.

Gilgamesh's armor, sword, shields and the Blue Crystal Rod are featured in Tales of Phantasia and later games; The Tower of Druaga and Druaga itself appear as part of an EX dungeon in the PlayStation version of Tales of Destiny, and both reappear in Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon and Tales of the World: Narikiri Dungeon 3; Gilgamesh from Tower of Druaga is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, and as a costume alongside Ki in the Narikiri Dungeon sub-series, while the Quox dragon appears as an enemy in Tales of Legendia; Gilgamesh's armor is available as a DLC costume in Tales of the World: Material Dungeon.

Valkyrie appears as a character in Tales of Destiny and ports of Tales of Phantasia, is a bonus boss character in Tales of Eternia and a support character in Tales of Hearts; her costume is accessible in several Tales of games and she makes appearances in other minor games of the series, while the Tales of Arise artifacts "Battle Maiden's Shield" and "Trident" are Valkyrie's shield and Xandra's weapon.

Heihachi Mishima makes a cameo appearance in Tales of Destiny, and the game features minor references to Tekken 3; a Heihachi costume with his moves appears in Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon and as DLC in Tales of Vesperia, an Asuka costume is found in Narikiri Dungeon X; a doll based on Heihachi with his moves is featured in Tales of the Abyss, Heihachi returns as a support character in Tales of Hearts, four Tekken 7 costumes are featured in Tales of Link and Tales of Arise features a statue of Devil Jin as an artifact and a Nina Williams costume as DLC.
The item Gnome in Tales of Destiny summons characters from Libble Rabble.

A costume of Momo and Wonder Momo are featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon and Narikiri Dungeon X with her actual techniques; while a doll based on Wonder Momo is featured in Tales of the Abyss and a costume of Wonder Momo is DLC in Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2.

A costume of Kagekiyo from Genpei Toma Den is featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with his actual techniques; Kagekiyo also makes a cameo appearance in Tales of Eternia and the Tales of Arise artifact "Quivering Candles" is based on the candles representing Kagekiyo's health.
A costume of Pino and Acha from Toy Pop are featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with their actual techniques.

A costume of Pac-Man is featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with his actual techniques, the Tales of Arise artifacts "Glutton's Maze", "Glutton's Code" and "Glutton's Guidebook" feature references to Pac-Man; Pac-Man makes other minor cameos in the series.

A costume of a Grobda and a Bacuda from Xevious are featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with their actual techniques, the Bacura appears as an enemy in Tales of Symphonia and Tales of Legendia while Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2 includes a DLC floating Solvalou hat.

A costume of Reiko Nagase from Ridge Racer is featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with her actual techniques, while in Tales of Phantasia playing the Mach Race event a second time has its music replaced with the main theme of Ridge Racer.

A costume of Clovis from Dragon Buster is featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with his actual techniques, while Tales of the Abyss features a sidequest designed after Dragon Buster with a Clovis costume as reward, and a Clovis figurine can be obtained in Tales of Vesperia.
Rick from Splatterhouse makes a cameo appearance in Tales of Eternia, while Tales of Phantasia features a place called "The Splatterhouse Inn".
Statues from the Spirit World in Yōkai Dōchūki make an appearance in Tales of Eternia.

A costume of Susumu Hori is featured in Tales of the World: Narikiri Dungeon 2 and 3 with his actual techniques, while a DLC costume of Susumu is included in Tales of Vesperia and the Tales of Arise artifact "Ancient Excavator" is the drill from Mr. Driller.

Veigue from Tales of Rebirth is based on Siegfried from SoulCalibur, he is seen wielding Siegfried's Requiem sword as his strongest weapon, and his "Celsius Calibur" attack summons the Soul Calibur, which can also be obtained as a weapon in Tales of the Heroes: Twin Brave and Tales of the Abyss; a costume of Mitsurugi is DLC in Tales of Vesperia and again with Taki in Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2; Radiant Mythology 2 also features the Soul Edge and Soul Calibur as EX Challenge DLC weapons and the Tales of Arise "Blade of Sealing" artifact is the Soul Embrace from SoulCalibur III; while Lloyd Irving from Tales of Symphonia is a guest character in SoulCalibur Legends.

A costume of KOS-MOS from Xenosaga is featured in Tales of the World: Narakiri Dungeon 3 with her actual attacks, Tales of the Abyss features a doll of KOS-MOS with her attacks as well, KOS-MOS appears as a support character in Tales of Hearts, Tales of Destiny for PlayStation has a "Gentleman" enemy wearing KOS-MOS's head gear while KOS-MOS's head gear also appears as the "Mechanical Doll Accessory" artifact in Tales of Arise.
Namco × Capcom features characters from the Tales of Destiny series.
Tales of the Abyss features a Mappy display in Nam Cobanda Isle, while Tales of Vesperia features a Mappy figurine and Tales of Destiny II includes a remix medley of music from Mappy.
The back of the jackets worn by Noelle and Ginji in Tales of the Abyss have artwork of Blue Max and Red Baron from Sky Kid.

Two of the nations in New Space Order -Link of Life- employ the Melnics language from Tales of Eternia and the Sacred Religious State faction has ties to indicate it is the distant future of the world in Eternia.
Tales of Vesperia features an Apollo figurine from Phelios.
A diorama machine based on Bravoman can be found in Tales of Vesperia, and a costume of Bravoman is DLC in Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2.
A diorama machine based on Metro-Cross and a figurine of its main character can be found in Tales of Vesperia.
A costume of Sgt. Keroro is featured in Tales of Vesperia.

Klonoa is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, while a Klonoa plushdoll appears in Tales of Destiny 2, a Klonoa costume is featured in Tales of Symphonia and DLC in Tales of Vesperia, and the latter also features a Klonoa diorama machine and figurine.

Wagan is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, while a figurine of Wagan is featured in Tales of Vesperia and the Tales of Arise artifact "Machine Beast Statue" is a bronze statue of Wagan.

Yayoi Takatsuki from THE iDOLM@STER is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, while Narakiri Dungeon X features a costume for Haruka Amami, Tales of Asteria features 8 idols as playable DLC characters, with one returning in Tales of the Rays; several costumes are also featured in many Tales of games.
Pop'n Music Portable features a track from Tales of the Abyss.

.hack//LINK includes a bonus pre-order DVD featuring a crossover between Haseo and Asbel from Tales of Graces, and Haseo also gets an Asbel costume in the game while Asbel gets a DLC costume of Haseo's Xth Form in Tales of Graces ƒ; a Haseo costume with his actual techniques is also featured in Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon X. Haseo and Atoli from .hack appear in Tales of the Rays.

A costume of the Prince from Katamari Damacy is featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon X with his actual techniques; while a doll based on the Prince is featured in Tales of the Abyss and Tales of Graces and the Tales of Arise artifact "Vivid Sphere" is a Katamari ball.

A DLC costume based on Hatsune Miku is featured on Tales of Graces ƒ.
Three costumes based on characters from Puella Magi Madoka Magica and a Kyubei attachment are DLC in Tales of Xillia 2.

Characters from Taiko no Tatsujin appear in Tales of the World: Tactics Union and Tales of Asteria, while Tales of the World: Narikiri Dungeon 3 features a minigame version of Taiko no Tatsujin, Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2 features DLC fans with Taiko no Tatsujin artwork and the Tales of Arise artifact "Drums of the Master" is based on Taiko no Tatsujin drums; Taiko no Tatsujin 2011 and later games in the series also feature music tracks from the Tales of series.
Toro appears in the PlayStation Vita version of Tales of Hearts, while a DLC costume based on Toro is featured on Tales of Graces ƒ and Tales of Hearts R, the latter alongside a Kuro costume.

Kirito and Asuna from Sword Art Online appear in Tales of Link and Tales of the Rays as part of collaboration events, Sword Art Online: Memory Defrag featured Milla Maxwell from Xillia and Sorey from Zestiria in a limited collaboration event; additionally, costumes based on Kirito and Asuna appear as DLC in Tales of Arise.

Claude and Rena from Star Ocean appear in Tales of the Rays and Cress and Mint from Tales of the Rays appear in Star Ocean: Anamnesis, both as part of a cross collaboration.
Gintoki, Kagura, Toushirou, and Sougo from Gintama appear in Tales of the Rays as part of two collaboration events.
Tales of Symphonia characters appear in Symphogear XD as part of a special collaboration.
Several characters from Slayers appear in Tales of the Rays as part of three special collaborations.

Black Clover characters appear in Tales of the Rays as part of a collaboration event.

Wild Tiger and Barnaby Brooks Jr. from Tiger & Bunny appear in Tales of the Rays as part of a collaboration event.

Tales of characters appear in Chain Chronicle for a collaboration event.
Items and costumes based on Scarlet Nexus appear in Tales of Arise as DLC and vice versa.

The Atelier Sophie 2 Collaboration Pack for Tales of Arise will feature multiple items based on Atelier Sophie 2, while the Tales of Arise Collaboration Accessories Set for Atelier Sophie 2 will feature multiple items based on Tales of Arise.
Tales of characters appear in Last Cloudia for a collaboration event.
Union Arena features cards based on Tales of Arise.

Hatsune Mikutchi is a Vocaloid-themed Tamagotchi therefore being a format crossover between the two series.

Princess Rapunzel costume is downloadable in LittleBigPlanet 2.

Tank Battalion.description: Stage 4 in Battle City is shaped after Hoblin from Libble Rabble.
Stage 10 in Battle City is shaped after Mappy. Tanks based on Mappy and Nyamco appear in Tancle.
Stage 21 in Battle City is shaped after Pooka from Dig Dug. Pookas also appear hidden inside the steel walls in Round 29 of Tank Force. Tanks based on Taizo Hori, Pooka and Fygar appear in Tancle.
The Shirei-Bu from Tank Battalion is a secret bonus character in Tinkle Pit.
One of the enemies in Super Xevious resembles the tanks from Tank Battalion series. Stage 42 in Namco Gallery Vol.1 version of Battle City is shaped after the Solvalou from Xevious.
Stage 47 in Namco Gallery Vol.1 version of Battle City is shaped after a Special Flag from Rally-X.
Tank Battalion is featured in Namco History Vol.2.
Japanese version of Star Fox: Assault features Battle City as an unlockable game.

Music from Battle City is featured in the Namcot Medley debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10. Taiko no Tatsujin V Version, Taiko no Tatsujin White Version and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track from Shin-Gun Destroy! Girl's Tank Battalion.
A tank based on Paccet appears in Tancle.
Tanks based on Gil and Druid Ghost appear in Tancle.

Stage 35 in Battle City and Stage 43 in Namco Gallery Vol.1 version of the game are shaped after a Galaxian and a flagship respectively. Galaga ship appears as one of the tanks in Shin-Gun Destroy! Girl's Tank Battalion.
Ami, Mami and Miki from "Mujin Gattai Kisaragi", a series from the 15th episode of THE iDOLM@STER anime, appear in Shin-Gun Destroy! Girl's Tank Battalion as a part of a collaboration.
Neptune and Tekken appear in Shin-Gun Destroy! Girl's Tank Battalion as a part of a collaboration.
Alisa and Ciel appear in Shin-Gun Destroy! Girl's Tank Battalion as a part of a collaboration.

Red Baron and Blue Max from Sky Kid occasionally appear on the map screen in Battle City Dengeki Operation Offline.

Battle City characters appear in The Knights of Avalon during the second Namco collaboration event.
Sprites from Battle City appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.

Round 21 in Tank Force is shaped after Pac-Man. Pac-Man, Blinky and Inky also appear hidden inside the steel walls in Round 29. The second world in Pac-Man Arrangement Plus+ is based on Battle City, and a theme featuring characters from Tank Battalion appears in Pac-Man 99.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Battle City.
