The Fairyland Story.description: The Wraith enemy from The Fairyland Story is inspired on the Mightas from Chack'n Pop, while Round 37 in the MSX port of The Fairyland Story is patterned after Chack'n.

Bubble Bobble inherits several gameplay elements and many of the same special items seen on The Fairyland Story that'd become recurring in the series, while Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Magical Island") based off the game, with appearances of several enemies and Horned as the final boss, with Ptolemy making a cameo in the Game Boy Color port; Bubble Symphony features Ptolemy as an assist character and she also spawns as an item in Round 57 of Bubble Memories.
Round 42 in the MSX port of The Fairyland Story is patterned after the Puka Puka ghosts from Pocky & Rocky.

Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2 includes an island ("Magical Island") based off The Fairyland Story, with appearances of several enemies and Horned as the final boss, with Ptolemy making a cameo in the Game Boy Color port.
A secret warp room in The NewZealand Story features an arrangement of blocks resembling Ptolemy from The Fairyland Story, and both games have a similar red devil enemy.
The Worm and red devil enemies from The Fairyland Story appear as enemies in Don Doko Don.

Stage 2 in the Parody Mode of Space Invaders DX is based on The Fairyland Story and features a playable Ptolemy; she's also one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Characters from The Fairyland Story appear in the PlayStation and Game Boy Color ports of Pop n' Pop.
Taito Memories Joukan and Taito Pocket Memories include The Fairyland Story.
Taito Legends 2 and Taito Legends: Power-Up include The Fairyland Story.
Ptolemy from The Fairyland Story is a playable character in Daifugo Party.

Ptolemy from The Fairyland Story appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, while Round 41 in the MSX port of The Fairyland Story makes reference to Arkanoid and Zone β-5 in Arkanoid DS bears resemblance to Ptolemy. The Goodies.description: The premise of the episode Kitten Kong is that a small cat has grown to colossal proportions and is terrorising the city. The solution requires that they fly their bike as close as possible without being in reach. This, the episode title, and the imagery of Bill in the paw of the beast all parody King Kong.
In Kitten Kong, the Goodies rush into an office dressed as mice, to which the cleaning lady leaps up onto a nearby stool and starts shouting "Thomas!".

In Farm Fresh Food, the automated farm's control room is a copy of the Enterprise bridge. Later in Invasion of the Moon Creatures, while Graeme attempts to regain contact with Bill and Tim, Spock briefly appears on his monitor. Soon after, Graeme begins recording a log in the style of Captain Kirk; "Captain's log, stardate..." etc.

When Bill and Tim are flying through space in Invasion of the Moon Creatures, the TARDIS is seen hovering across the front window. Later in the episode U-Friend or UFO?, Graeme's EB-GB exclaims "Exterminate!" in a Dalek voice while wielding a plunger. Bill's speech in Robot suggests melting K9, among others, for scrap metal.

In Invasion of the Moon Creatures, Bill and Tim are transformed into rabbit people, now doing voices akin to Bugs Bunny and repeating "What's up, Doc?". Later in the episode The Movies, "That's all folks!" is shown after the credits.

In Invasion of the Moon Creatures, Bill and Tim cover the title on a poster for the film A Clockwork Orange, replacing it with "A Transistorised Carrot" before wreaking similar havoc around London dressed in part as Alex's 'droogs'.
In The Movies, Frankenstein's creature is briefly sat next to Tim in a movie theatre.
In The Goodies Rule - O.K.?, Big Ears is a member of parliament.
In The Goodies Rule - O.K.?, Padington Bear is a member of parliament.
In The Goodies Rule - O.K.?, Andy Pandy, Teddy, and Looby Loo intercept their escape.
In The Goodies Rule - O.K.?, A green muppet-like mascot emerges from the dumpster, resembling Oscar the Grouch.
In The Goodies Rule - O.K.?, Bill and Ben engage in an extended swordfight against Graeme and Tim. Later, Weed surprises them but is swiftly trimmed.
In The Goodies Rule - O.K.?, Bill is jumped by four of the Wombles.
In The Goodies Rule - O.K.?, the now oversized Dougal and Zebedee chase after the trio before destroying Chequers.
In Earthanasia, Graeme aggravates Tim by destroying his belief that the Muppets are real using improvised laundry puppets.

The episode Saturday Night Grease makes numerous references to the film Grease, including mimicking Danny Zuko and singing or parodying the musical sequences while also making fun of John Travolta and acknowledging their own parodies.
In Saturday Night Grease, the trio find themselves suddenly on the yellow brick road as 'Follow The Yellow Brick Road' plays in the background. They then link arms and begin skipping along it.

In U-Friend or UFO?, Graeme builds a replica R2 unit for domestic tasks which he instead names EB-GB. Later in Snow White 2, Tim and Graeme engage in a fight using what are essentially lightsabres. Bill's speech in Robot suggests melting R2D2 and C3P0, among others, for scrap metal.

In U-Friend or UFO?, The trio try to impress the aliens by proving they are "super-men", rushing to a line of telephone booths and quick-changing into versions of the Superman costume, after which they fail at various attempts to prove that they're incredibly strong and can fly. After reconsidering, they put out a broadcast showing off "Supernun" who is "faster than an express Herse" and "leaps tall churches in a single bound". At the end of the episode the crowd exclaims in turns "It's a bird! It's a plane! It's a nun.".

In U-Friend or UFO?, Bill and the Aliens fly in space smacking Tim back and forth with rackets. Graeme watches through the computer monitor which displays the activity as a game of Pong, complete with floating scoreboard.

The special episode Snow White 2 begins with an introduction about the horror of pantomime, part of which involves dwarfs creeping between the seats with only their hats visible deliberately to resemble shark fins, accompanied by the Jaws theme music.

The Legend of Heroes.description: The Legend of Heroes series is a spin-off of the Dragon Slayer series.
Jurio and Chris from The Legend of Heroes III: White Witch appear as characters in Vantage Master Online.
Ys vs. Trails in the Sky: Alternative Saga is a crossover between Ys and The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky.

Taiko no Tatsujin V Version and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature music tracks from The Legend of Heroes series.

The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky characters make an appearance in Langrisser Mobile as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from The Legend of Heroes: Hajimari no Kiseki appeared in Brave Nine as part of a special collaboration.
Music and skins based on The Legend of Heroes appears in DJMAX RESPECT V as part of the Falcom Pack DLC.

The Legend of Isis (Blue Water Comics).description: Isis appears in issue 10 of The 10th Muse. 10th Muse vs. Legend of Isis is a crossover between the two series.
The comic Legend of Isis/Black Scorpion is a crossover between the two series.
Isis took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.

The Legend of Kage.description: The theme "The Legend of KAGE" from Touhou Reiiden~ The Highly Responsive to Prayers is inspired by The Legend of Kage.
Taito Memories Gekan and Pocket Memories include The Legend of Kage, the latter also includes an enhanced version.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Wai Wai Happy! Rokudaime and Taiko no Tatsujin 8 feature a music track from The Legend of Kage.
Taito Legends 2 and Taito Legends: Power-Up include The Legend of Kage, the latter also includes an enhanced version.
Kage from The Legend of Kage is a playable character in Daifugo Party.
Kage from The Legend of Kage appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders.
Kage from The Legend of Kage appears as one of the characters providing assist attacks in Arkanoid vs. Space Invaders, while a wallpaper based on The Legend of Kage 2 is unlockable in Arkanoid DS.
A remixed theme of The Legend of Kage is featured in Groove Coaster 3EX.
Music from The Legend of Kage can be played in D4DJ Groovy Mix after an update.
The 185th episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews The Legend of Kage for the NES.
A human version of The Legend of Kage appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.

The Legend of Qin.game: Nine Songs of the Moving Heavens
The Legend of Qin.description: Nine Songs of the Moving Heavens is a prequel series to The Legend of Qin.
Characters from The King's Woman, including Ying Zheng and Jing Ke, appear in The Legend of Qin animated series, adapted from the same novel universe.

The Legend of Zelda.description: The boss Manhandla in The Legend of Zelda is a giant Piranha Plant from the Mario series, with other Mario enemies also appearing in later episodes; the Warp Whistle from The Legend of Zelda is featured in Super Mario Bros. 3 while Mario visits Hyrule in Volume 4 of Super Mario-Kun and Link appears in Super Mario Bros. & Friends: When I Grow Up and Super Mario RPG; The downloadable content pack The Legend of Zelda × Mario Kart 8 for Mario Kart 8 includes elements from the Zelda series.
The boss Digdogger in The Legend of Zelda is a giant Unira from Clu Clu Land.
Samus plays The Legend of Zelda in the 1986 Metroid manga, Victory Techniques for Metroid. Metroid Prime 3 also features a reference to the series.
Zelda II features a reference to the Dragon Quest series.
The Final Fantasy series features some references to the Zelda series.
One of the Howard & Nester comics talks about Zelda II: The Adventure of Link.
Link makes an appearance in Tetris for NES.
The Wizard features characters playing Zelda II.
Arkista's Ring is a clone of Zelda series.
Link and Zelda guest star in three episodes of Captain N.
Link makes a cameo in the game boy version of F-1 Race.
The Legend of Zelda Barcode Battler Cards set is part of both series.

The Legend of Zelda.game: Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru
The Legend of Zelda.description: Prince Richard from Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru, makes an appearance in The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening.
Dr. Wright from the SNES version of SimCity makes an appearance in The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening.
Kirby appears as an enemy in The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening, while the Triforce is an obtainable item in Kirby Super Star. There also are other references between the two series.

The Legend of Zelda.game: BS-X: Sore wa Namae o Nusumareta Machi no Monogatari
The Legend of Zelda.description: The main characters from BS-X: Sore wa Namae o Nusumareta Machi no Monogatari are also the main characters in the two Zelda Satellaview games.
Link makes an appearance in Donkey Kong Country 2 and is referenced in Donkey Kong Country 3. He is also playable in a minigame version of Donkey Kong within NES Remix.
There are references to the Zelda series in Warcraft II, Warcraft III and World of Warcraft.
Elements from the Zelda franchise appears in the Gold Edition of Game Boy Camera.
The Boo Blah from Yoshi's Island appears as an enemy in The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX.
Characters, places and items from the Zelda series are featured in all Super Smash Bros. games.
Link from the Zelda series appear in N-Gang episodes "Freeze Frame" and "Die Hexe lacht um Mitternacht".
Five masks in The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask seem to reference the Star Fox team.
In The Powerpuff Girls episode "Child Fearing" the major plays a game similar to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
In Pokémon Stadium 2, connecting video game consoles to a TV can show images from Zelda games.

Rupees from the Zelda series appear in Animal Forest and later games in the series, while Wolf Link, Medli, Ganon and Epona appear in Animal Crossing: New Leaf when scanning Zelda amiibo. Hyrule is also mentioned in various Animal Crossing games while Linebeck is mentioned in New Horizons and there are other minor references as well.
The videogame Hamtaro: Ham-Ham Heartbreak features references to the Zelda series.
A trailer for 1080° Avalanche is included in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Master Quest; In 1080° Avalanche there's a reference to The Legend of Zelda.
The Homestar Runner series features many references to the Zelda series.
Link is the GameCube exclusive character for SoulCalibur II.

Dragon Ball Z: The Legacy of Goku II features an appearance of a The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past cartridge; Dragon Ball Z: Attack of the Saiyans also features a reference to the Secret Moblin from The Legend of Zelda.
A trailer for F-Zero GX is included in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Master Quest; One of the emblems in F-Zero GX's Garage Mode represents Tingle from the Zelda series.
In Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes, Psycho Mantis mentions The Legend of Zelda if a save for The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker is detected.

The Navi Tracker mode in the Japanese version of The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures is based on the Satellaview Marvelous games. Characters from the games are also present as leftover in the code of Four Swords Adventures.
Link and Navi appear in "Edds Legend of Zelda". There's other references throughout the series.
Xandir, one of the main characters in Drawn Together, is a parody of Link from the Zelda series, and there also are other references to the series in some episodes.
Daigasso! Band Brothers features music tracks from the Zelda series.
One of the images in Big Brain Academy's puzzles is the Triforce from the Zelda series.

Arino plays the SNES game The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past in episode 20. He later plays The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time in episodes 109 and 110, Zelda II: Link's Adventure in episodes 209, 210 and through a New Year Live Special, and The Legend of Zelda in episodes 317 and 318.
Trace Memory features a book called '"The Legend of Zelda Chronology".
In Asterix & Obelix XXL 2: Mission: Las Vegum there are some references to the Zelda series.
The Rope Snake in Mother 3 might be based on the Rope enemy from Zelda, while the Whip in The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks is based on the Rope Snake.
The Coconut Fred's Fruit Salad Island episode "Sir Nutalot" features references to the Zelda series.
The Tingle series is a spinoff of the Zelda series.

Link's hat and hair, the Deku Mask and the Master Sword are in the shop. There is also a Minish costume.

a Zelda zone and Link appears as a DLC in Sonic Lost World.

Princess Zelda's dress is unlockable in Maiden of Black Water.

Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy + features unlockable aircraft themed after Link from Skyward Sword and Zelda from Twilight Princess.
A R.O.B. figure can be seen in the Curosity Shop when viewing from the window in Kafei's Shop in Majora's Mask 3D.
The Triforce symbol is embossed on a tree trunk in the Thornfelt Swamp in Ori And The Blind Forest.

At the end of the Steven Universe episode "Open Book", there's a Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker video game case in Steven's room. The temple in the episode "Serious Steven" may have been inspired by the ones in The Legend of Zelda. The videogame "Mini Golf Quest" from the Steven Universe episode "Rose's Room" is partly inspired by The Legend of Zelda.
There's a Zelda reference in the episode Video Game References.
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of The Legend of Zelda, Zelda II: The Adventure of Link, or The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past.
The comic Plok: The Exploding Man features a reference to Zelda.
A picture of an 8-bit Octorok can be found in Splatoon and Splatoon 2; a giant cartridge based on Ocarina of Time appears in Splatoon 2: Octo Expansion.
The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask is mentioned in the Rick and Morty episode "Total Rickall".

Dino Run DX features hats based on Link and Ganondorf.
A Zelda themed icon can be unlocked in Emily is Away.
The infamous glitch "I AM ERROR" from Zelda 2 is referenced in Pony Island.
My Nintendo Picross - The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess is a crossover between the two series; additionally Picross NP Vol. 5 and Picross DS include images from the Zelda series.
A pony that looks like Link appears in the episode Flutter Brutter.
Miitomo featured Zelda-themed items.
Zelda is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
A hat similar to Link’s hat from The Legend of Zelda makes an appearance in Starbound.
The Legend of Zebra is a reference to The Legend of Zelda.
Miitopia features costumes based on Zelda characters, obtainable by scanning the respective amiibo.
The Legend of Zelda UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Mario enters a parody version of the world of The Legend of Zelda in "If Mario was in... Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time".
Link has been a subject for DBX.
A parody of Zelda 2 called "Legend of Bat 2" can be found in Macbat 64.

A cartridge for The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX can appears as a treasure in Hey! Pikmin, while another treasure is an ocarina similar to the one from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time; additionally the Goddesses statues in The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker are likely based on Pikmin. There might also be other references in the series.

A Hat in Time features a color palette with the color scheme of Link from The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker named "Forest Critter", while one of Hat Kid's idle animations is based on Link's victory animation.

In South Park's Imaginationland episodes there are characters resembling Link and Ganondorf; Kenny's princess costume in South Park: the Stick of Truth is based on Princess Zelda.  Legend of Zelda was mentioned in South Park: The Fractured But Whole.
Girls Mode 4 features clothing items based on the Zelda series, unlocked by using Zelda amiibo.
Scott the Woz once did a review on The Legend of Zelda.
Rex's salvager suit from Xenoblade Chronicles 2 is obtainable in The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.
The Master Sword, Hylian Shield, and Champion's Tunic are unlockable in the Switch version of Skyrim by scanning The Legend of Zelda amiibo.
One of the plants in Among Us looks like a Korok from Zelda.
The Nintendo Switch version of Diablo III: Eternal Collection features a Ganondorf Transmogrification set, a Cucco pet, and a Triforce portrait frame.
A painting of the Dueling Peaks from The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild can be found in Dead Cells.
CrossCode features multiple references to the Zelda series.
Zelda is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "Perfect Cell Vs Link."
An item similar to the Blue Candle from The Legend of Zelda can be found in Slay the Spire.

The sword called "Sword of Masters" is a reference to the Master Sword from the Zelda series and functions identically.
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is compatible with the Nintendo Labo VR Kit.
Comic Man owns several Zelda merchandise, including a Hylian Shield. Sam also owns Nintendo Power V1, which features a page dedicated to The Legend of Zelda.
Zelda is mentioned in Trover Saves The Universe.
There's a lot of references to the Zelda franchise in Reventure.
Cadence of Hyrule is a crossover between the two series.

The Legend of Zelda is parodied in Les Kassos.
A Link costume was added to Jump Rope Challenge with Update 1.1.0.
A room based on the pot room from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time can be found in It Takes Two, and it unlocks the achievement "Force Triangulated".
Link's hair and ocarina from The Legend of Zelda appears in Sky: Children of the Light as content exclusive to the Nintendo Switch version.
Zelda is parodied in multiple Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episodes.

Microgame versions of Zelda games are featured in the WarioWare series, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; additionally Wario can draw a sketch of Zelda characters in WarioWare Gold by scanning the respective amiibo.
Midgi sings the item fanfare from The Legend of Zelda in Demon Turf.

The Master Sword from The Legend of Zelda can be found on display in a training hall in Nobody Saves the World.

Brett mentioned Zelda in the Inside Job episode "Brettwork".
"Video Games" by Tenacious D includes a brief segment referencing Zelda.
"The Legend of Zelda One-Shot: Lookout, Here We Come!" is a special one-shot episode promoting The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.
In Class of '09: The Re-Up, Jeffery wears a Zelda shirt.
Zelda is mentioned in the Rick and Morty episode: "Rickfending Your Mort".
Geometry Dash features a UFO skin based on Majora's Mask as part of a 2.2 update.
Zelda memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".

A figure of Link from The Legend of Zelda can be seen in the music video for FNAF Kids.
Versions of The Legend of Zelda and Zelda II: The Adventure of Link for the NES are included in Nintendo World Championships: NES Edition.
"The Legend of Tenna" in Chapter 3 of Deltarune is a reference to The Legend of Zelda.
In Do You Know Gaming?, a card featuring a parody of Ganon from The Legend of Zelda named "Calamity Gammon" can be found.
In a One Night at Flumpty's comic, Kevin Jr. puts on "Majora's Hat".

The Powerpuff Girls.description: Dexter makes cameos in many Powerpuff Girls episodes as well as the Powerpuff Girls movie; two of The Justice Friendscharacters Major Glory and Valhallen appeared in the Powerpuff Girls episode "Members Only". In the Dexter's Laboratory episode Mandarker, one of the elderly judges about to present Dexter with a ribbon is shown wearing a monocle and same exact shoes similar to The Mayor of Townsville from The Powerpuff Girls, both of whom are voiced by Tom Kenny. The Rowdyruff Boys appear in a painting in Dexter's Laboratory Issue 4 of IDW Comics, while the rest of the characters from Dexter's Laboratory appear in the comic Powerpuff Girls: Super Smash-Up!; The Powerpuff Girls also made a cameo appearance as one of many plush toys in the Dexter's Laboratory episode "Star Check Unconventional". In the Dexter's Laboratory episode Germ Warfare, the three talking amoebas found under Dexter's microscope are a reference to the Amoeba Boys, one of the villains on The Powerpuff Girls. Tower of Babel (Namco).description: There are several references to Indiana Jones in Tower of Babel.

Namco Anthology Vol. 1 features Tower of Babel and an arranged version.

Floor 27 in Neo Babel Mode from Tower of Babel Arrange features moving pixel art of the Galaxian ship shooting an enemy in the background, while floor 31 features similar art of the Galaga ship getting captured.
Floor 28 in Neo Babel Mode from in Tower of Babel Arrange features moving pixel art of the Rally-X car in the background.
Floor 29 in Neo Babel Mode from Tower of Babel Arrange features moving pixel art of Ki and the Wizard enemy from The Tower of Druaga in the background.
Floor 30 in Neo Babel Mode from Tower of Babel Arrange features moving pixel art of Pino and Acha from Toy Pop in the background.
One of the endings in the Neo Babel Mode from Tower of Babel Arrange features statues of Valkyrie on the tower's top.

A theme featuring characters from Tower of Babel appears in Pac-Man 99; additionally one of the eight symbols from Tower of Babel is an image of Pac-Man, while Floor 32 in the arranged version of the game features moving pixel art of Pac-Man in the background.

Toy Story.description: Luxo, Jr. and the Luxo ball make many cameos in the Toy Story series.

A Mickey Mouse wall clock makes an appearance in Toy Story also, in the House of Mouse episode "House Ghosts", Donald dresses up as Woody, Buzz Lightyear, and a Alien from the Toy Story series.

Andy's mother plays the song Hakuna Matata in the car.
Mr. Potato Head and Mrs. Potato Head appears in the Toy Story franchise.

Buzz makes the Vulcan salute in Toy Story.
Two animatronics resembling the Cylons appear in Toy Story.
Mister Bauer recounts a scene from Toy Story as if he had experienced it himself in the Two Guys And A Girl episode "Two Guys, A Girl And A Presentation".

The Pizza Planet Truck appears in A Bugs Life as well as Woody and the phrase "to infinity and beyond" during the credits; A Bug's Life merchandise appears in Toy Story 2. Red Rocker and Blue Bomber from Rock 'Em Sock 'Em Robots appear in Toy Story 2.
Mr. Potato Head calls Rex Godzilla in Toy Story 2.

Toy Story 2 is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One Where Chandler Can't Cry".
A kid looking like Sid Phillips from Toy Story appears in "The Big Problem".

The Pizza Planet Truck appears in Ratatouille.
A Little Green Man from Toy Story appears in Disney Friends.

Us (Jordan Peele).description: In Us, Jason is first seen wearing a Jaws logo t-shirt.

There is a reference to the filming of The Lost Boys. Adelaide and her parents are walking down the boardwalk and Adelaide's mother says, “They're filming something by the carousel.” The scene in Us is shot on Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk and is also set in 1986, around the time when The Lost Boys was filmed; director Jordan Peele confirmed this connection.
In an ad for Halloween Horror Nights 29, the Upside Down from Stranger Things appears along with the doppelgangers from Us.

A costume based on Alicia Melchiott from Valkyria Chronicles can be obtained in Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA, while costumes based on Imca and Kurt Irving from Valkyria Chronicles III can be obtained in Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Extend and Arcade; a cover of the opening theme song of Valkyria Chronicles III, "If You Wish For...", is also included in the album Hatsune Miku -Project DIVA- extend Special Collaboration Album VOCALOID extend REMIXIES.
An image of Sonic appears in Valkyria Chronicles II.
Samurai & Dragons features cards based on characters from Valkyria Chronicles.
Vyse and more characters from Skies of Arcadia are playable in Valkirya Chronicles.
Selvaria Bles is a playable character. Alicia Mechiott is an assist character

Characters from Valkyria Chronicles appear in Sega Heroes

Valkyrie (Namco).description: Valkyrie is a selectable character in the Japanese version of Rock 'n Ball.
The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features floats of Valkyrie and Sandra.
Valkyrie appears as an announcer in Kyūkai Dōchūki.
Valkyrie appears on the hi-score screen and a Sandra from Valkyrie is a secret bonus character in Tinkle Pit.
A picture of Valkyrie can be seen in the "Hyper Glyder" event from Mach Breakers: Numan Athletics 2.
A billboard of a christmas-themed Valkyrie can be seen in the Intermediate Course in Alpine Racer.

Valkyrie's sword and shield are unlockable in console versions of Soul Edge and SoulCalibur II,  SoulCalibur III and SoulCalibur IV. Cassandra received a bonus costume based on Valkyrie in console ports of SoulCalibur II, and several pieces of her costume are available as custom items in SoulCalibur III and downloadable in SoulCalibur V.
The Legend of Valkyrie is part of Namco Museum Vol. 5, with Valkyrie and Sandra making an actual appearance.

Valkyrie appears among the audience in the Namco stadium in Famista 64 and as an actual player along with Sandra in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match, and she also appeared as the mascot for the Namco Stars team in Super Famista 3-5; the enemy Zouna also appeared in the Rivals team in Famista Online 2010 and in Famista Climax; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels include players called "Quarkman" and "Sandra".

Valkyrie appears as a character in Tales of Destiny and ports of Tales of Phantasia, is a bonus boss character in Tales of Eternia and a support character in Tales of Hearts; her costume is accessible in several Tales of games and she makes appearances in other minor games of the series, while the Tales of Arise artifacts "Battle Maiden's Shield" and "Trident" are Valkyrie's shield and Xandra's weapon.
One of the endings in the Neo Babel Mode from Tower of Babel Arrange features statues of Valkyrie on the tower's top.
Namco Anthology 2 features a remake of Valkyrie no Bouken: Toki no Kagi Densetsu.

Valkyrie, Sandra and Sabine are playable characters in Sugoroku Adventure: The Tower of Druaga, Valkyrie is playable in Druaga Online: The Story of Aon and appears as a Creature card in Seme COM Dungeon: Drururuaga.
Valkyrie is one of the players in the "Namco All Stars '80" team in World Kicks.
An image of Valkyrie appears as a possible target in Point Blank 3.
Valkyrie is a selectable character in Family Tennis Advance.
Mr Driller Ace: Fushigi no Pacteria features two stages named after the series, "Sandra Ruins" and "Valkyrie Ruins", the two dungeons depicted as statues looking like their respective character.
Valkyrie is one of the playable characters in Namco Super Wars.

Music from Legend of Valkyrie is featured in the Taiko March song, debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin DOKI! Shinkyoku Darake no Haru Matsuri and in the Namcot Medley, debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10; Taiko no Tatsujin DS: Dororon! Yokai Daikessen!! and later games also feature music tracks from Legend of Valkyrie.

Valkyrie no Densetsu characters and one location appear in Party Land.
A Valkyrie costume appears in Dig Dug Island.

The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of Sandra from Valkyrie no Densetsu with Valkyrie assisting the player.
Valkyrie and Kurino Sandra appear as summons in Keroro RPG.
Enemy cars in Ridge Racer 3D sport emblems of Valkyrie, Sandra and Sabine; R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 has cups named after Valkyrie and Sandra and a Valkyrie trophy.
Valkyrie, Sandra, Sabine and several enemies and bosses from Valkyrie no Densetsu appear in Namco Chronicle.

Viewtiful Joe.description: The "Confession" theme in Viewtiful Joe is a remix of the "Classroom Trial" theme from Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney.
In the GameCube version of Viewtiful Joe, the titular character can be heard whistleing the Super Mario Bros. theme.
A R.O.B. can be seen in the GameCube version of Viewtiful Joe.
Viewtiful Joe contains a reference to the "I am your Father" line from Star Wars. One of the poster in the end credits is a reference to a Star Wars poster.
The episode "2.000.000 Leagues Under The Sea" from Viewtiful Joe is named after the 1954 film 20.000 Leagues Under the Sea.
One of the posters in the end credits of Viewtiful Joe is a reference to the poster of the film King Kong.
One of the posters in the end credits of Viewtiful Joe is a reference to the poster of the film Jaws 2.

Dante from Devil May Cry is playable in the PlayStation 2 version of Viewtiful Joe and the PSP version of Red Hot Rumble, and Alastor is implied to be the spirit inside Dante's sword of the same name; there are also other minor references to Devil May Cry in the first Viewtiful Joe.
The first stage from Viewtiful Joe 2 features references to Jurassic Park.
The stage "Viewtiful Heroes and the Statue of Doom" from Viewtiful Joe 2 is named after Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom.

"Horror World" from Viewtiful Joe: Double Trouble! features statues of Red Arremers from Ghosts 'n Goblins.

The episode "Viewtiful Joe Begins" from Viewtiful Joe: Double Trouble! is named after the film Batman Begins.
The episode "Nightmare on X'mas" from Viewtiful Joe: Double Trouble! is named after the Nightmare on Elm Street film series.
Ōkami makes several references to Viewtiful Joe.

Bayonetta features a references to Viewtiful Joe.

Villainous (Cartoon Network).description: There's an allusion to Angry Bird in the episode "Bad Security" of Villainous Phase One.

The Lost Cases of Ooo is a crossover episode between Villainous and Adventure Time. Finn's sword can be seen in the Villainous short "The Portrait of Evil". Characters from Adventure Time briefly appear in "The Lost Cases of Boxmore". Many other villain orientation videos use clips from Adventure Time. The Villainous game Maldad Mecanica features enemies based on Finn and Jake, Hunson Abadder appears in a group photo in The Lost Cases of the Future, the Ice King appears in one of the Villainous Comics strips and Gunther appears in Trap-ical Resort.
Lex Luthor is in the special thanks list at the end of The Lost Cases of Ooo.
Top Cat is in the special thanks list at the end of The Lost Cases of Ooo.
Brain is in the special thanks list at the end of The Lost Cases of Ooo.

Sinestro is in the special thanks list at the end of The Lost Cases of Ooo.
Black Manta is in the special thanks list at the end of The Lost Cases of Ooo.
The Kanker Sisters are in the special thanks list at the end of The Lost Cases of Ooo.

The Lost Cases of Rhyboflavin is a crossover episode between Villainous and Mighty Magiswords, while the Black Hat Magisword featured in this episode can be seen in the background of several episodes in the final season.

The Lost Cases of Boxmore is a crossover episode between Villainous and OK K.O!. Black Hat from Villainous appears in the OK K.O.! Let's Be Heroes episode "Crossover Nexus". Several villains from OK K.O.! appear in the Villainous episode "The VVV".

The Lost Cases of Townsville is a crossover episode between Villainous and The Powerpuff Girls, Him appears in a group photo in The Lost Cases of the Future, "The Dreadful Dawn" features a doll of Buttercup, Mojo Jojo and Him are in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo", Mojo Jojo appears in "Trap-ical Resort", enemies resembling the Powerpuff Girls appear in Maldad Mecánica, a Broccoloid appears in the episode "BH's Bizarre Bad-Venture" and Blossom makes a cameo appearance in the episode "The Heedeous Heart".
There is an allusion to the Super Saiyan transformation in The Lost Cases of Townsville.
Badaxtra from Dexter's Laboratory appears in a tube in the background of the Villainous episode "The Foul Flower", Val Hallen and The Krunk make a cameo in the episode "BH's Bizarre Bad-Venture".

The Lost Cases of Elmore is a crossover episode between Villainous and The Amazing World of Gumball, a Gumball doll appears in "The Dreadful Dawn" and the monster clown appears in a painting in "Boo!-Ldozing".
Guide for an Evil Conquest is a crossover episode between Villainous and Ben 10, while Vilgax is in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo".
The Beast is in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo", and his head appears as a mounted trophy in the episode "Demencia wuz here".

The Lost Cases of the Future is a crossover episode between Villainous and Samurai Jack, The Creature makes a cameo appearance in the episode "BH's Bizarre Bad-Venture" and Aku is in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo".
The Red Guy appears in a group photo in The Lost Cases of the Future and he's in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo".

Anti-Pops appears in a group photo in The Lost Cases of the Future, The Lost Cases of the Park is a crossover episode between Villainous and Regular Show, enemies resembling Mordecai and Rigby appear in Maldad Mecánica, Hi-Five Ghost makes a cameo in the episode "Boo!-Ldozing" and a scene in the episode "BH's Bizarre Bad-Venture" references the "Power Tower" episode of Regular Show.
In The Lost Cases of the Future, Aku disappearing from a photo is a parody of the same scene in Back to the Future.

The Lost Cases of Beach City is a crossover episode between Villainous and Steven Universe, while the painting in the episode "The Portrait of Evil" shows Steven's shirt and one of the Villainous Comics strips has a cameo appearance of Steven Universe, while Yellow Diamond is in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo" and enemies resembling Steven appear in Maldad Mecánica.

Courage appears in the episode "Trap-ical Resort" and the violin girl makes a cameo in the episode "Boo!-Ldozer", while Katz and King Ramses are in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo".

The Lost Cases of the Tree House is a crossover episode between Villainous and Codename: Kids Next Door and the painting in the episode "The Portrait of Evil" shows the treehouse base; Father, Salmonella Fitzgerald and Toiletnator are in the special thanks list at the end of "The Lost Cases of Ooo".
The Villainous episode "The Black Hat Challenge I" is a parody of The Blair Witch Project.
The Villainous episode "The Black Hat Challenge II" is a parody of The Ring.
Several of Dr. Flug's lines in the Spanish version of Villainous are references to Team Rocket and James from Pokémon, owing to the fact both characters share the same voice actor.
Characters resembling Shaggy, Velma and Fred from Scooby Doo appear in the Villainous episode "Boo!-Ldozer", while Scooby and Shaggy appear as enemies in Maldad Mecánica.
Dr. Flug and Demencia from Villainous appear in the Victor and Valentino episode “Villainy In Monte Macabre”.
