Sega Smash Pack Volume 1 includes Virtua Cop 2.
Virtua Cop 3 features a puppet Sonic in a scene.
Sega Superstars Tennis features a minigame based on Virtua Cop.
An arcade cabinet for Virtua Cop and the access to it can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
A human version of Virtua Cop appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.

Virtua Fighter.description: There is a minor visual reference to the polygonal look of early Virtua Fighter titles in chapter 168 of the Yu Yu Hakusho manga.
There's a statue of Sarah from Virtua Fighter in Virtua Cop, while the Virtua Fighter anime features a parody of Virtua Cop's gameplay in the 22th episode, "Evil Hong Kong".
The season 3 episode 3 of X-Files, "D.P.O.", features a Virtua Fighter 2 Arcade cabinet.
A thought in Super Mario RPG references Virtua Fighter.
In chapter 298 of the Hajime no Ippo manga, two characters can be seen playing Virtua Fighter.
There is an Easter egg in Virtua Fighter 3 in which a flying train will appear in the background of the stage, referencing Galaxy Express 999.
The character Deral from Saturn Bomberman Fight!! is a parody of Dural from Virtua Fighter.
Fighters Megamix features many characters from Virtua Fighter.
The manga and anime Arcade Gamer Fubuki features the Virtua Fighter Arcade games.
One of the curves in the Expert course "Virtua City" in Daytona USA 2 is named after Sarah Bryant.
A Virtua Fighter arcade cabinet can be seen in the The King of Queens episode: "Big Dougie".
Jacky Bryant, Jeffery McWild, Kage-Maru, Taka-Arashi, and Wolf Hawkfield from Virtua Fighter are unlockable players in ESPN NFL Football.
Puyo Puyo Fever: Carnival Edition included Akira Yuki as a guest character.

Shenmue was initially planned to be part of the Virtua Fighter series; Shenmue and Shenmue II feature Toy Capsules based on Virtua Fighter and Virtua Fighter Kids, while the Virtua Fighter 5 stage "Aurora" features the "MJQ" jazz bar from Shenmue in the background.
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Virtua Fighter in the episode "Sega 32X".
Virtua Fighter 5 R features a Ulala costume for Sarah Bryant.
Virtua Fighter 5 R features a costume for El Blaze based on Samba de Amigo.
Virtua Fighter 5 R features a costume for Jeffry based on Virtual-On.
Virtua Fighter 5 R features a costume for Lion based on Picky and one for Eileen based on Emi from Fighting Vipers.

Yakuza 3 features a Virtua Fighter cabinet in one of its areas, while Yakuza 4 features a playable Virtual Fighter pachinko machine, Yakuza 5 features a playable Virtua Fighter pachislot machine and Yakuza 6 features a fully playable Virtua Fighter 5: Final Showdown Arcade machine. Several character costumes and music from Yakuza are included in Virtua Fighter 5: Ultimate Showdown as part of the DLC "Yakuza Series Collaboration Pack".
A premium Xbox 360 theme of Bayonetta shows the protagonist fighting inside an Arcade fighting game parodying the classic Virtua Fighter titles. Bayonetta also performs one of Akira Yuki's moves.
Sega Superstars features a game mode based on Virtua Fighter, while Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing features Jacky Bryant and Akira Yuki as a single playable racer.

Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing features Jacky Bryant and Akira Yuki as a single playable racer; Sonic is also featured as a drawing in Virtua Fighter 2, as pictures in "Sega World" in Virtua Fighter 4: Evolution and as a statue in Virtua Quest.

Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA 2nd features a Sarah Bryant costume for Megurine Luka, while Project DIVA Extend features a Kage-Maru costume for KAITO; a Virtua Fighter 2 arcade machine appears as a decoration in Hatsune Miku: Project Mirai DX.
Chapter 21 and 22 of High Score Girl feature the characters discussing and playing Virtua Fighter, while the character Numata resembles Lau Chan from the series.
Music from Virtua Fighter was added to maimai in the maimai version.
Dead or Alive 5 features Akira, Sarah and Pai Chan from Virtua Fighter as playable characters, while Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate adds Jacky as another playable character.
The Sega All-Star Pack for Samurai & Dragons includes a card based on Akira from Virtua Fighter.
Akira Yuki is a playable character. Pai Chan is an assist character
Virtua Fighter characters appear in the Sega Hard Girls episode "It'll Always Be 10 Years Too Early for You!"
Persona 3: Dancing in Moonlight features several costumes based on Virtua Fighter characters.
Akira and Dural from Virtua Fighter appear in Kyoutou Kotoba RPG: Kotodaman during a "Sega All Stars" collaboration.
Characters from Virtua Fighter appear in Sega Heroes
Super Smash Bros. for Wii U and for 3DS features two downloadable costumes based on Virtua Fighter.  Also, Akira appears as an Assist Trophy in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Akira Yuki from Virtua Fighter appears in Earth UFO Catcher.
Characters from Virtua Fighter appear in Fist of the North Star: Legends ReVIVE as part of a collaboration event.
Several character costumes, music and the health bars from Tekken 7 are included in Virtua Fighter 5: Ultimate Showdown as part of the DLC "Tekken 7 Collaboration Pack".
A human version of Virtua Fighter appears in 404 GAME RE:SET and fights alongside Akira.
Several characters from Virtua Fighter appear in The King of Fighters: All Star as a part of a special event.

Virtua Striker.description: Bean the Dynamite from Sonic the Fighters is featured in Virtua Striker 2's secret MVP Yuki Chan team, while the "F.C. Sonic" team in Virtua Striker 3 is comprised exclusively of Sonic characters.
Sega Superstars features a game mode based on Virtua Striker.
The song "Opa-Opa!" is a crowd chant in Virtua Striker 4.

Virtual On.description: The Super Robot Wars series features units from the Virtual On series.
Virtua Fighter 5 R features a costume for Jeffry based on Virtual-On.

A costume based on Fei-Yen from Virtual On can be obtained in Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Extend; a cover of Fei-Yen's stage BGM, "LOVE14", is also included in the album Hatsune Miku -Project DIVA- extend Special Collaboration Album VOCALOID extend REMIXIES.
Dengeki Bunko Fighting Climax features a stage set in the Cyber Troopers Virtual-On universe.
Costumes based on Virtual On appeared in Phantasy Star Online 2 as part of a special collaboration.
Toaru Majutsu no Virtual-On as well as its video game adaptation called A Certain Magical Virtual-On are a crossover between the two series.
An arcade cabinet of Virtual On can be played in Yakuza Kiwami 2.

Vision (Marvel).description: Vision made his first appearance in Avengers #57, and joined the team in Avengers #58.
Tigra appears in Vision and the Scarlet Witch (Vol. 2) #1-2.
Thanos appears alongside Vision in Infinity Gauntlet #3.
A doppelganger of Vision is an enemy in Marvel Super Heroes in War of the Gems.
Vision appears in the Marvel: Ultimate Alliance series.
Vision appears in Unbeatable Squirrel Girl Beats Up the Marvel Universe!
Vision is one of the main characters in WandaVision.
Yo Gabba Gabba! is seen on TV in the WandaVision episode: "Breaking the Fourth Wall".
Wanda and her family were watching The Dick Van Dyke Show in the WandaVision episode “Previously On”. Wanda also bases her hex off of the Dick Van Dyke Show.
Wanda watches Malcolm in the Middle in the WandaVision episode "Previously On".
The Marvel Studios series of Lego Minifigures includes The Scarlet Witch, Vision and Agatha Harkness.

Vitamin Connection.description: MC Mimimi from Vitamin Connection resembles PaRappa the rapper except she's a female.

Viva Pi\u00f1ata.description: The Sabre Wulf amulet makes an appearance in Viva Piñata.
Characters from the Banjo-Kazooie series appear in Viva Piñata as statues; Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts also features references to the Viva Piñata series.
In both Viva Piñata and Viva Piñata: Trouble in Paradise, one of the accessories that the player's Piñatas can wear is the "Mr. Pants Hat".
There is an homage to The Silence of the Lambs in the Viva Piñata episode "Candibalism".
A set of six Killer Instinct characters were made into Piñata Vision cards and respective piñatas in Viva Piñata: Trouble in Paradise.
A set of four Halo characters were made into Piñata Vision cards and respective piñatas in Viva Piñata: Trouble in Paradise.
Skin Pack 2 in the Minecraft Legacy Console and Bedrock Editions features skins based off characters from Viva Piñata, along with the Minecraft 2nd Birthday Skin Pack.
A team consisting of characters from games by Rare including Viva Piñata appears in #IDARB.
Rare Replay includes Viva Piñata and Viva Piñata: Trouble in Paradise as playable games.

Vocaloid.description: Hatsune Miku is a spinoff of the Vocaloid series.

Taiko no Tatsujin 12 Don! to Zoryoban and later games in the series feature music tracks sung by Vocaloids, also featuring costumes for the characters; the Vocaloids also appear dancing with Taiko characters during the songs in some games, while Hatsune Miku appears as a challenger in Taiko no Tatsujin: Session de Dodon ga Don! and along with Mirai Komachi as a Performance Character in Nintendo Switch Version!
Phantasy Star Portable 2 features costumes based on Vocaloid.
A Vocaloid based on Gachapin named "Ryuto" was released.
Gumi made an appearance in Pop'n Music Sunny Park; many vocaloid tracks also appeared throughout the series.
Hatsune Miku, Rin and MEIKA Hime's hairs appear in the shop. Kagamine Rin's collar also appears in the shop.
Music from Vocaloid was added to maimai in the maimai PLUS version.
Divine Gate features Vocaloid characters as part of a special collaboration.
Several theme songs from Vocaloid are featured in CROSS×BEATS REV and REV. SUNRISE.

Vocaloid Hatsune Miku appears as a dancer in Just Dance 2016, 2017 and 2018 respectively with the song "Ievan Polkka", "PoPiPo" and "Love Ward"; a Hatsune Miku song, "Tell Your World" is also featured in Just Dance Wii U; "Ievan Polkka" and "PoPiPo" are also available in Just Dance Now.
A Xingchen costume from VOCALOID4 appears as a skin for Unicorn in Azur Lane.
Various Vocaloids appeared in Puyo Puyo!! Quest during collaboration events.
Characters from Vocaloid appear in Kaku Spring Festival Gala 2019.
Various Vocaloids appeared in LINE Pokopang during a collaboration event.
Groove Coaster Wai Wai Party featured multiple DLC packs featuring music from Vocaloid artists as well as characters that are selectable as navigators and avatars
Megurine Luka, and Kabamine Rin & Len are playable characters in Dengeki Bunko: Crossing Void.
Characters from Fate/kaleid liner Prisma Illya appear in D4DJ Groovy Mix as part of a special collaboration.
Hatsune Mikutchi is a Vocaloid-themed Tamagotchi therefore being a format crossover between the two series.
Various Vocaloids appear in Project VOLTAGE illustrations.
Kagamine Rin and Len appear as playable characters in Muse Dash as part of the 2nd Hatsune Miku collaboration event.
Vocaloid items and characters appear in Onmyoji Arena.
Lucky Cyan from To Be Hero X and Luo Tianyi made an official collaborative song together.

Volleyball (Nintendo).description: Samus plays Volleyball in the 1986 Metroid manga, Victory Techniques for Metroid.
Super Mario Maker features a costume based on the volleyball player from Volleyball.
Volleyball appears in the Disk Writer furniture item in Animal Crossing: New Leaf - Welcome amiibo!.
A volleyball player appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

Voltage Fighter Gowcaizer.description: Burnov appears in Captain Atlantis's ending in Voltage Fighter Gowcaizer.

Voltron.description: Voltron is mentioned in the short "The Temp!" from Oh Yeah! Cartoons.
Voltron is mentioned in the Bones episode "Boy in the Time Capsule".
A Voltron set was released for Monsterpocalypse.
Voltron is parodied in the MAD sketch "Grey's in Anime".
Todd Zarnecki wears a Voltron t-shirt in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Zarnecki Incursion".
Several IOI employees pilot robots from Voltron during the final battle of Ready Player One.
Voltron is mentioned in the Deadpool movie.
In multiple limited-time events in Roblox, players could get Voltron-themed gear and weapons.
The Vulture-on is a reference to Voltron.
A Voltron figure appears in The Boss Baby.
As part of a special collaboration event, the North American edition of Puzzle & Dragons featured characters and items from Voltron: Legendary Defender.
Items based on Voltron are available in Rocket League as part of the "Radical Summer" event.
Characters from Voltron appear in Funko Pop! Blitz.
A Voltron statue appears in Rescue Rangers (2022).
Lion Voltron is a playable character in Funko Fusion.

Voodoo Vince.description: A store in Voodoo Vince is named “Risky Burlesque” which is a play on the title of Risky Business.

Vox Machina.description: Vox Machina takes place in the Dungeons & Dragons universe.
Vox Machina vs. Mighty Nein is a one-shot special crossing over the two series.
Garrison and Red Monika from Battle Chasers appear in The Legend of Vox Machina episode: "The Trials of Vasselheim".
Many cosmetics based on Critical Role appear in Among Us as part of a special collaboration, including cosmetics based on the Vox Machina campaign.
Cards based on Vox Machina appeared in Balatro as part of the "Friends of Jimbo 4" update.
UniVersus includes a set of cards based on Critical Role: Heroes of Exandria, with characters from Vox Machina also appearing.

Vulgus.description: The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in SonSon and SonSon II.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Pirate Ship Higemaru.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in games of the 194X series.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an enemy in Exed Exes.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Gun.Smoke.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Ghosts 'n Goblins.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in the NES port of Trojan.
A blue Yashichi from Vulgus appears as a secret item in the NES port of Commando, while "VULGUS" is one of the default names in the hi-score screen.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Side Arms.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Black Tiger.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in several games from the Mega Man series.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Forgotten Worlds.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in U.N. Squadron.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Kamen no Ninja Hanamaru.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Magic Sword: Heroic Fantasy.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in The King of Dragons.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Varth: Opeation Thunderstorm.

The Yashichi from Vulgus appears as a cursor in the Super Nintendo version of Street Fighter II Turbo, as a match icon in Street Fighter Alpha 2, and Chelsea from Street Fighter x All Capcom wears a Yashichi hairpin.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an attack in the Japanese version of Marvel Super Heroes.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Final Fight 3.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as a password symbol in Red Earth.
There are dialogue references to Vulgus in Marvel vs. Capcom and Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3.
Capcom Generations 3 includes Vulgus.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Strider 2.
The character Yashichi Fuwa from SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2 is named after the Yashichi from Vulgus.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears in Hydron's ending from  Capcom Fighting Evolution.
A character in Power Pro Kun Pocket 7 is named after the Yashichi.
Three of Sylphie's skills in Namco × Capcom references Vulgus.
Vulgus is included in Capcom Classics Collection and Capcom Classics Colection Reloaded.
One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the Vulgus sprite from Vulgus.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Persona 4.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as a collectable in Bionic Commando: Rearmed and Bionic Commando : Rearmed 2.
"Yashichi" and "Vulgus" are unlockable Nom de Guerres in Lost Planet 2.
The Yashichi from Vulgus makes a cameo appearance during Interlude 2 in Asura's Wrath.
Vulgus is included in Capcom Arcade Cabinet as one of two bonus games.
Chelsea from Street Fighter × All Capcom wears a Yashichi hairpin.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus appears as an item in Super Ultra Dead Rising 3' Arcade Remix Hyper Edition Ex Plus Alpha.
The Yashichi enemy from Vulgus is visible in the "E-mail" evidence from Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirits of Justice .
Umbrella Corps features a decal of the Yashichi, and a TV brand in Resident Evil 6 is named after the Yashichi enemy from Vulgus.
Vulgus is included in Capcom Arcade Stadium.

W.I.T.C.H..description: In the first issue, a boy is shown wearing a Donald Duck costume.

WACCA.description: Music from Kemono Friends can be played in WACCA.
Music from KonoSuba can be played in WACCA.
Music from Pop Team Epic can be played in WACCA.
Music from Steins:Gate can be played in WACCA.

WACCA.game: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
WACCA.description: Music from That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime can be played in WACCA.
Music from The Quintessential Quintuplets can be played in WACCA.
Music from Zombie Land Saga can be played in WACCA.
Music from Touhou can be found in WACCA after various updates.
Music by Kizuna AI can be played in WACCA.
Music from Evangelion can be played in WACCA.
Music from Yuri on Ice can be played in WACCA.
Music from Himouto! Umaru-chan can be played in WACCA.
Music by Hatsune Miku can be played in WACCA.
Music from A Certain Scientific Railgun can be played in WACCA.
Music based around Hololive can be found in WACCA as part of a collaboration event.
Music from Blend-S can be played in WACCA.
Music from DanMachi can be played in WACCA.

WACCA.game: How Heavy Are the Dumbbells You Lift?
WACCA.description: Music from How Heavy Are the Dumbbells You Lift? can be played in WACCA.
Music from WACCA can be found in Muse Dash as part of a collaboration event.
Groove Coaster Wai Wai Party featured a DLC pack featuring music from WACCA as well as characters that are selectable as navigators and avatars
Music from WACCA can be found in Lanota as part of a collaboration event and vice versa.
Music from Azur Lane can be played in WACCA.
Music and characters from WACCA can be found in Arcaea as part of a collaboration event.
Characters from WACCA appear in crossover cards in D4DJ Groovy Mix as part of a special collaboration while music from D4DJ appeared in WACCA for the same collaboration.
Elizabeth and music from WACCA can be found in Rotaeno as part of a collaboration event.
Music from WACCA was added to maimai in the maimai FESTiVAL PLUS version.
Music from WACCA can be played in O.N.G.E.K.I. Bright Memory.
Characters and music from WACCA can be found in Paradigm: Reboot as part of a special collaboration.

WALL-E.description: The Pizza Planet Truck appears in WALL-E.
Pong is displayed in WALL-E.
WALL-E interacts with Luxo Jr after the credits.
Mary has a poster of Eve from WALL-E in Monsters, Inc.: Laugh Factory Issue 2.
WALL-E is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Adhesive Duck Deficiency" and "The Space Probe Disintegration".
On D6 level in Metro 2033, on the wall in the Missile Control room to the left from the main screen, there is an old boot with a plant growing out of it, a reference to WALL-E.
WALL-E is parodied in the MAD sketch "WALL·E·NATOR".
A virtual WALL-E world appears in Disney Universe. Costumes of BURN-E, Hal, EVE, M-O and WALL-E are also playable.
In Saints Row: The Third one of the missing ships found on a list is named "Axiom", like a ship from Wall-E.
WALL-E and EVE appear in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #29.
WALL-E appears in the garbage disposal unit in "Space Face".
WALL-E's fire extinguisher appears in Disney Infinity.
Disney Magic Kingdoms features characters from WALL-E.
Characters from WALL-E appear in Disney Heroes: Battle Mode
WALL-E appears in LEGO The Incredibles.
An image of EVE from WALL-E appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
The Robot pet in Among Us is based on WALL-E.
Characters from WALL-E appear in Disney Sorcerer's Arena.
WALL-E is parodied in Les Kassos.
EVE from WALL-E appears in Disney Melee Mania.
Official Squishmallows were released based on WALL-E.
Haiku, the Robot features an NPC that looks like and acts similarly to Wall-E.
Characters and Items from WALL-E appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley
Characters from WALL-E appear in Disney Speedstorm.
A WALL-E game box is seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Jamil's favorite character is WALL-E.
There will be a puzzle in Disney Solitare that shows a scene from WALL-E.

WHAT THE GAMES?.description: There's a lot of references to the Mario franchise in WHAT THE GOLF?.
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Donkey Kong.
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Flappy Bird.
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Guitar Hero.
One of the worlds of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Super Meat Boy.
One of the worlds of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Portal.
One of the bosses of WHAT THE GOLF? have a gameplay inspired by Frogger.
One of the worlds of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to SUPERHOT.
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Angry Birds, and one of the worlds is a reference to Angry Birds Space.
On a wall of the hubworld of the space world of WHAT THE GOLF? there is a drawing of a character similar to a Cromulon from Rick and Morty.
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Metal Gear Solid.
One of the levels of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Katamari.
One of the victory messages of WHAT THE GOLF? is a reference to Spider-Man.
Stages based on Among Us featuring Crewmates and Imposters from the game appear in WHAT THE GOLF? and WHAT THE CAR?.

WWE 2K.description: A wrestler called "Arnold "The Terminator" Schwarzenegger" is available as a pre-order bonus for WWE 2K16.

WWE Immortals.description: Johnny Cage was added as a new fighter in WWE Immortals. Raiden is added as a new fighter and based on WWE Superstar Xavier Woods in the game.

Wacky Races.description: A gorilla called King Klong, a clear parody of King Kong, appears in the Wacky Races episode "Real Gone Ape".
Dastardly and Muttley in Their Flying Machines is a spin-off of Wacky Races.
Captain Caveman's design is based on the Slag Brothers from Wacky Races.
Dread Baron, a major character in Laff-A-Lympics, was confirmed to be the brother of Dick Dastardly from  Wacky Races in issue #13 of the Laff-A-Lympics comic.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races appear as antagonists in Yogi's Treasure Hunt and Yo Yogi!.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races appear in the "Fender Bender 500" shorts in Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
In Dog's Day Afternoon, at one point, Timmy (in Doidle's body) does the same wheezing laugh as Muttley.
The episode Dexter's Wacky Races parodies Wacky Races.
Arino plays the 3DO game Chiki Chiki Machine Mou Race: Kenken to Black Maou no Ijiwaru Daisakusen during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races are seen in the South Park episode "Handicar".
The Sofia the First episode "In a Tizzy featured Amber in the race dressed like Penelope Pitstop from Wacky Races.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races are in the Uncle Grandpa episode "Uncle Grandpa Retires".
Dick Dastardly and the Hooded Claw appear in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #53.
Top Cat and Benny appear in the Wacky Races episode "Off Track".
Characters resembling Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races appear in episode 4 of Pop Team Epic.
Hong Kong Phooey appears in the Wacky Races episode "Hong Kong Screwy".
Huckleberry Hound appears in the Wacky Races episodes "Hong Kong Screwy" and "Slow and Steady".
The Buzz Wagon from Wacky Races can be seen in the OK K.O. episode "Crossover Nexus".
Quick Draw McGraw appears in the Wacky Races episode "Much Ado About Wacky".
Jabberjaw and The Neptunes appear in the Wacky Races episode "Far Away in Old Bombay".
Space Ghost appears in the Wacky Races episode "The Wack Stuff".
Characters from Wacky Races appear in the Scooby-Doo: Team-Up story "Just Plane Scared"; Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races appear in Scoob!.
Ricochet Rabbit from The Magilla Gorilla Show appears in the Wacky Races episode "Slow and Steady".
Touché Turtle appears in the Wacky Races episode "Slow and Steady".
Penelope Pitstop appears in the Animaniacs reboot episode "Suffragette City".
Muttley and Penelope from Wacky Races appear in Space Jam: A New Legacy.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races appear in Jellystone!

Waffle the Wonder Dog.description: Waffle the Wonder Dog characters appear in Playtime Island.
Waffle the Wonder Dog characters appear in Get Creative.
Mrs Hobbs from Waffle the Wonder Dog appears in This Time with Alan Partridge episode 2.

Wagan Land.description: The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of Wagan.
A banner ad featuring Wagan appears in the Japan League stadiums from Kyūkai Dōchūki.
R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 features a trophy based on Wagan, while  Ridge Racer Accellerated features the "Wagyan Cup".
Wagan is one of the players in the "Namco All Stars '80" team in World Kicks.
The items "Wagancopter" and "Waganizer" in Namco × Capcom reference Wagan Land.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of Wagan Land items with Wagan assisting the player.

Wagan is featured as a support character in Tales of Hearts, while a figurine of Wagan is featured in Tales of Vesperia and the Tales of Arise artifact "Machine Beast Statue" is a bronze statue of Wagan.
Wagan appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.

Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature Wagan as a guest player; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '88 and its sequels include players called "Wagan", "Takuto", "Karin" (after the protagonists of Wagan Paradise) and "Hisopiso" (after the character from Wagan Land 3).
Wagan is a playable character in Namco Chronicle.
Wagan and other characters from Wagan Land appear in strip #2 of the Dig Dug 30th Anniversary webcomic.
Wagan makes a cameo in strip #280 of the Bravoman web comic, with other references appearing in earlier strips.
A costume of Wagan with a special action is featured in Mappy Taiketsu! Neo Nyamco-dan.
A cat version of Wagan from Wagan Land is featured in Cat Busters as part of a Namco Catalog IP collaboration.
Wagan appears in The Knights of Avalon during the first Namco collaboration event.
Sprites from Wagan Land appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.
A theme featuring characters from Wagan Land appears in Pac-Man 99.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Wagan Land.

Wait Till Your Father Gets Home.description: Wait Till Your Father Gets Home is based on All in the Family.
The Wait Till Your Father Gets Home episode "Car 54" is a crossover with Car 54, Where Are You?.

Wake, Rattle, and Roll.description: Quick Draw McGraw, Baba Looey, Augie Doggy and Doggie Daddy from The Quick Draw McGraw Show appear in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races appear in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Huckleberry Hound, Pixie and Dixie from The Huckleberry Hound Show appear in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Yogi, Boo Boo, and Snagglepuss from Yogi Bear appear in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Top Cat and Choo-Choo from Top Cat appear in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Wally Gator appears in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Magilla Gorilla appears in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
The Winsome Witch and her cat Lucky appear in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
"Dino and Cavemouse" segments from The Flintstone Comedy Show occasionally aired during Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
"Undercover Elephant" segments from CB Bears occasionally aired during Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Axel from Wake, Rattle, and Roll appears in the Jellystone! episode "Face of the Town".

Waku Waku 7.description: Bonus-kun is a boss in Waku Waku 7.
Bonus-kun's moveset in Waku Waku 7 is a parody of Ryu's moveset from Street Fighter.

Walkabout Mini Golf.description: A course based on Labyrinth appears as DLC in Walkabout Mini Golf VR.
A course based on Myst appears as DLC in Walkabout Mini Golf VR.
A course based on Wallace & Gromit appears as DLC in Walkabout Mini Golf VR.
Avatars based on Fraggle Rock characters appear as DLC in Walkabout Mini Golf VR.
Avatars based on The Dark Crystal characters appear as DLC in Walkabout Mini Golf VR.
Avatars based on Exploding Kittens characters appear as DLC in Walkabout Mini Golf VR.

Walker, Texas Ranger.description: Walker, Texas Ranger is mentioned in the Friends episode: "The One with the Hypnosis Tape".
Cordell Walker from Walker, Texas Ranger appears in the Martial Law episode "Honor Among Strangers", while Sammo Law appears in the Walker, Texas Ranger episode "The Day of Cleansing".

Walker, Texas Ranger.game: Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby
Walker, Texas Ranger.description: In Talladega Nights, Ricky Bobby's children are named "Walker" and "Texas Ranger".
Brodell Walker is based on Cordell Walker from Walker, Texas Ranger.
Walker, Texas Ranger is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episode “The Proton Transmogrification”.

Walkure Romanze.description: Walkure Romanze characters appear in Kamihime Project for a collaboration event.
Walkure Romanze characters appear in Mist Train Girls for a collaboration event.

Wallace & Gromit.description: A sled with "rosebud" written on it is shown in Grand Day Out and a 2008 BBC One Christmas ident.
The puma from Creature Comforts is shown stuffed in Wrong Trousers and photos of the characters can be found in Wallace & Gromit In Project Zoo.
Wallace appears in the episode Adventure's on Telly, Part 1.
Wallace & Gromit toys and photos are shown in Flushed Away. A newspaper also references the events of Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit.
Shaun the Sheep is a spinoff of Wallace & Gromit.
Wallace and Gromit appear with Dennis the Menace on the cover of The Beano, celebrating The Beanos 70th birthday.
Monty Muzzle from Wallace & Gromit's Grand Adventures makes a cameo appearance in Poker Night at the Inventory.

Wallace & Gromit.game: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl
Wallace & Gromit.description: Wallace & Gromit is mentioned in Me and Earl and the Dying Girl (book).
In Five Short Graybles, Princess Bubblegum's mouth movements and manner of speech when saying the word "cheese" mimics the character Wallace from Wallace & Gromit.
The Techno Trousers (later renamed "Robo Pants" to avoid copyright issues) appears in Infiltrating the Airship.
Lola Woolfe says "You are my Wallace to my Gromit" in Afterparty.
A wanted poster for Feathers McGraw can be seen in the Amphibia episode "Fight at the Museum".
Wallace & Gromit is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "Perfect Cell Vs Wallace and Gromit".
Cooker from A Grand Day Out appears in the Star Wars: Visions episode: "I Am Your Mother".
Feathers McGraw from The Wrong Trousers appears in Chicken Run: Dawn of the Nugget.
Walkabout Mini Golf VR has DLC that allows you to play on a course based on Wallace & Gromit.
PowerWash Simulator features DLC that allows you to clean locations from Wallace & Gromit.
a statue of Gromit dressed as Woody from Toy Story was made in official collaboration between Aardman and Pixar.

Wally Bear.description: The eighth episode of The Angry Video Game Nerd is a review of Wally Bear and the NO! Gang.
JonTron reviews the arcade game, Wally Bear and the NO! Gang in the episode, Anti Drug Games.

Wally Gator.description: Characters from Wally Gator appear in Laff-A-Lympics.
Wally Gator appears in the Fender Bender 500 segment of Wake, Rattle, and Roll.
Wally Gator appears in Brak Presents the Brak Show Starring Brak.
Wally Gator from Wally Gator appears in the Powerpuff Girls episode "Knock It Off".
Wally Gator makes a cameo in the Duck Dodgers episode "K-9 Quarry".
Wally Gator appears in the Harvey Birdman episode "Booty Noir".
Wally Gator appears in the Teen Titans Go! episode: "Warner Bros 100th Anniversary".

Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing.description: Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour is a spin off of Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers.
Jiminy Cricket is a racer in Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour.
The racers enter the world of Dinosaur via the DINOSAUR attraction.
The racers enter the world of The Haunted Mansion via the The Haunted Mansion attraction.
The racers enter the world of Tomorrowland via the Tomorrowland attraction.
The racers enter the world of Pirates of the Caribbean via the Pirates of the Caribbean attraction.
The racers enter the world of Jungle Cruise via the Jungle Cruise attraction.

WandaVision.description: Vision is one of the main characters in WandaVision.
Yo Gabba Gabba! is seen on TV in the WandaVision episode: "Breaking the Fourth Wall".
Wanda and her family were watching The Dick Van Dyke Show in the WandaVision episode “Previously On”. Wanda also bases her hex off of the Dick Van Dyke Show.
Wanda watches Malcolm in the Middle in the WandaVision episode "Previously On".
The Marvel Studios series of Lego Minifigures includes The Scarlet Witch, Vision and Agatha Harkness.
A Hulu promo has Agatha Harkness speak to characters from Only Murders in the Building via radio.

A  Westview sign promoting Westview, New Jersey, which is outside of New York and was the setting in WandaVision appears in The Fantastic Four: First Steps. additionally, Matt Shakman directed both WandaVision and The Fantastic Four: First Steps which explains the reference and both being Marvel adaptations as well.

Wander Over Yonder.description: There are several references to Star Wars in Wander Over Yonder.
A katamari-like object makes a brief cameo in the first episode of Wander Over Yonder.
There are references to Peanuts in Wander Over Yonder.
The episode "The Pet" from Wander Over Yonder features several references to Alien.
The episode "The Prisoner" from Wander Over Yonder features a reference to He-Man.
There are references to The Powerpuff Girls in Wander Over Yonder.
An advertisement in Poptropica for Disney XD Animacation has some cardboard cutouts of some Wander Over Yonder characters.
The Roblox Disney XD Mystery Morphing Mask included Wander.
Characters from  Wander Over Yonder appear in Disney XD Villains Unite!.

Wander Over Yonder.game: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
Wander Over Yonder.description: The episode "The Big Day" from Wander Over Yonder feature a reference to Monty Python and the Holy Grail.
The episodes "The Fremergency Fronfract" and "The Boy Wander" from Wander Over Yonder feature references to several Batman series.
The episode "The Fremergency Fronfract" from Wander Over Yonder feature a reference to Superman: The Movie.
The episode "The It" from Wander Over Yonder feature a reference to Terminator 2.
Bloo from Fosters Home for Imaginary Friends makes a cameo in the Wander Over Yonder episode The End of the Galaxy.
The final episode of Future-Worm! featured cameos of Disney XD characters, including Wander and Sylvia from Wander Over Yonder.
A Wander doll appears in the Big City Greens episode "Present Tense".
Wander's hat appears in the shop.
Wander and Lord Hater from Wander Over Yonder appear in the Chibiverse episode "Pizza vs. Fireworks".

Wandersong.description: Mr. Oshiro from Celeste makes a cameo appearance in Wandersong.
The character Kiwi in Chicory: A Colorful Tale is directly based on the Bard from Wandersong, sharing their canon name and voice.
The Bard is an assist in Fraymakers.

Wangan Midnight.description: The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Wangan Midnight and Wangan Midnight R.
Pac-Man and the ghosts make appearances as guest AI drivers in Wangan Might Maximum Tune 2 and Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune 3 DX+. Pac-Man images appear in all the Wangan Midnight games by Namco.

Cahracters from Taiko no Tatsujin appear as guest characters in the Japanese version of Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune 2. Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure, Taiko no Tatsujin Red Version and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track from Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune.
Characters from Wangan Midnight appeared in Initial D: The Arcade as part of a special collaboration.

Wanted.description: Characters from Wanted, including Wesley Gibson, appear in the Millarworld crossover comic series Big Game.

War Thunder.description: Accessories and weapons based on Friday the 13th appeared in War Thunder as part of a special collaboration.
Skins and a game mode based on Area 88 appeared in War Thunder as part of a special collaboration exclusive to Japan.
Accessories and combat robots based on Atomic Heart appeared in War Thunder as part of a special collaboration.

War of the Independents.description: The Toxic Avenger took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Gumby and Pokey took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Cerebus the Aardvark took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
The Tick took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Shi took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Felix took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Madman took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Usagi took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Flaming Carrot took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Fone Bone took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Cassie Hack took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
The Maxx took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Mercy Sparx took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Tiger Wraith from BloodRayne: Dark Soul took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
The 10th Muse took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Megaton Man took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Pinocchio took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Orion took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Unbelievable Laundry Detergent Man took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.

War of the Independents.game: The Legend of Isis (Blue Water Comics)
War of the Independents.description: Isis took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.
Sylvia took part in the War of the Independents crossover comic event.

WarGames.description: An Asteroids cabinet is shown in WarGames.
A Centipede cabinet is shown in WarGames.
A Donkey Kong cabinet is shown in WarGames.
In the movie WarGames a Galaga cabinet can be seen.
A Tron cabinet is shown in WarGames.
WarGames is mentioned in the BTVS episode "Villains".
AL from Dr. Muto says “A strange game. The only winning move is not to play." which originated from WarGames.
WarGames is mentioned in the Alias episode "Out Of The Box".
WarGames is mentioned in the HIMYM episode "First Time In New York".
Stargate Worlds is played in WarGames: Dead Code.
Warcraft is mentioned in WarGames: Dead Code.
WarGames is mentioned in the NCIS episode "Cloak".
One of the floppy disks is labelled "WOPR" in the third episode of Back To The Future: The Game, referencing the supercomputer from WarGames.
WarGames is mentioned several times in Ready Player One, a recreation of the movie appears in the book. WOPR from WarGames is mentioned in Ready Player Two.
A computer displays the name 'David Lightman' in the Lethal Weapon episode "Fools Rush In".
WarGames is mentioned in the Young Sheldon episode "Pongo Pygmaeus And A Culture That Encourages Spitting".
The name of the Animaniacs episode "WARnerGAMES" is a reference to WarGames.

Warcraft.description: There are references to the Zelda series in Warcraft II, Warcraft III and World of Warcraft.
A level of The Lost Vikings II takes place in the Swamps of Sorrow, a location from Warcraft: Orcs and Humans; The three Vikings make a cameo appearance in World of Warcraft.
Characters from Starcraft appear in Warcraft III.

The creatures from Diablo appear in World of Warcraft. Diablo IV includes several cosmetics based on World of Warcraft, including Varian Wrynn and Garrosh Hellscream (for Barbarian), Malfurion Stormrage and Xavius (for Druid), Xal'atath and Lich King (for Necromancer), Illidan Stormrage and Sylvanas Windrunner (for Rogue), and Jaina Proudmoore and Kael'thas Sunstrider (for Sorcerer).
In World of Warcraft there are two characters named Larion and Muigin, that are parodies of Mario and Luigi.
In Warcraft you could find The Hatch from LOST in Bittertide lake where when you have the curser over the hatchet the numbers show  5 9 16 17 24 43.
Characters play World Of Warcraft in the Pure Pwnage "Imapwnu Of Azeroth".

South Park featured an entire episode based around the game World of Warcraft with the episode "Make Love, Not Warcraft", with permission from Blizzard. The sword that originated from South Park, the "Sword of a Thousand Truths", was later added to Warcraft and the Warcraft trading card game.
Warcraft is mentioned in Daddy Day Camp.
A World of Warcraft sticker is shown in Superbad.
Warcraft is mentioned in WarGames: Dead Code.
In X-Men Origins Wolverine you could find The Lich King's Sword.
Linkara reviews World of Warcraft #2 and #3.
Peggle: World of Warcraft Edition is a crossover between the two series.
A synonym for the Knight object in Scribblenauts is "Leeroy Jenkins".
World of Warcraft appears in Zombieland.
World of Warcraft is mentioned in Kick-Ass #8.
The Lich King is an unlockable character in Guitar Hero: Warriors of Rock.
World of Warcraft is mentioned in the Big Bang Theory episodes "The Hot Troll Deviation" and "The Apology Insufficiency".
The Sunflower from Plants vs. Zombies appear in World of Warcraft which also features a quest which is a reference to Plants vs. Zombies.
World of Warcraft: Cataclysm features a reference to BioShock.
There is an homage to Joust in World of Warcraft: Cataclysm.
World of Warcraft is mentioned in Ready Player One.
World of Warcraft is mentioned in the Dick Figures episode: "Modern Flame War 3".
An orc appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
All Guards of the Shado-Pan are randomly quoting the Night's Watch from the series.
Wreck-It Ralph features a reference to the "Jenkins" meme from World of Warcraft.
Monopoly: World of Warcraft Collector's Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
The Video Game High School episode "OMGWTFPS!?" features a reference to World of Warcraft.

The follower "Soulare of Andorhal" from the World of Warcraft: Warlords of Draenor expansion was likely inspired by Solaire of Astora from Dark Souls. There are other minor references to Dark Souls in World of Warcraft.
World of Warcraft was mentioned in Night at the Museum 3.
Warcraft characters appear in Heroes of the Storm.
World of Warcraft and the "Leeroy Jenkins" meme associated with it are mentioned in Armada.
"Kobolds, Catacombs and Dragons (Oh My!)" is a special one-shot episode promoting Hearthstone.
In Stormsong Valley of Warcraft: Battle of Azeroth, there are NPCs resembling Sora, Kairi, and Riku from Kingdom Hearts.
There is a tombstone asset in Warcraft III: Reforged, with what appears to be "FUCK OU" written in the Daedric script. The line follows the rule of the Daedric Alphabet to omit any "X" or "Y".
World of Warcraft is mentioned in "WORLD OF ANY MALU - ESPECIAL".
The Archlich skull is based on Kel'Thuzad from World of Warcraft.
Lich King has been a subject for Death Battle!.
Overwatch 2 includes several cosmetics based on World of Warcraft, including Sylvanas Windrunner Widowmaker, Lich King Reinhardt, Thrall Zenyatta, and Diamond Magni Torbjorn skins.

Warehouse 13.description: Daniel Dickenson mentions Flash Gordon in the Warehouse 13 episode "Resonance".
Douglas Fargo cameos in the Warehouse 13 episode "13.1" and Claudia Donovan cameos in the Eureka episode "Crossing Over".
Keyser Soze is mentioned in the Warehouse Thirteen episode "Around The Bend".
Dr. Vanessa Calder, a recurring character on Warehouse 13, appears in the Alphas episode "Never Let Me Go".
Pete mentions Contact in the Warehouse 13 episode "3...2...1".

Warframe.description: Several decorative items referencing Warframe are unlockable in Rocket League.
Lotus and Natah from Warframe have spirits in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Weapon skins based on Unreal Tournament were available in Warframe for a limited time.
Warframe characters appear as skins in PUBG Mobile during a crossover event.
Excalibur Bullet has been a subject for Death Battle!, with the series sponsoring it.
Cards based on Warframe appeared in Balatro as part of the "Friends of Jimbo 3" update.

Wargroove.description: Travis can wear a Wargroove t-shirt in Travis Strikes Again: No More Heroes.
Nuru and the Floran race from Starbound make an appearance in Wargroove.

Warhammer.description: Geneviève Dieudonne, a character from several Warhammer novels, also appears in Anno Dracula. However, the Anno Dracula version has a different middle name.
"Dakka," a term from Warhammer, is mentioned in Armada.
Total War: Warhammer is a format crossover between Warhammer and Total War.

The Vindicator and Predator tanks from Warhammer 40,000 appear in World of Tanks Blitz as well as a map based on the series. Several tanks from Warhammer 40,000 also appear in the console version of World of Tanks, along with the characters Volusad Thassius and Patricia Laserian. Characters and ships from Warhammer 40,000 also appear in World of Warships.
Monopoly: Warhammer 40,000 Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
The Furry Crusades is a parody of Warhammer 40k.
Risk: Warhammer 40,000 is a format crossover between the two.
Multiple Space Marine models can be seen throughout The Last of Us Part II.
Soldiers wearing armors resembling those on Warhammer 40000 can be seen in the Helltaker comic strip "Gloomhaven Comic".
Characters from Warhammer 40,000 appear in the "Warhammer 40,000 Commander Decks" release for Magic: The Gathering.
Kyle mentions “Darktide” in the South Park episode “The World-Wide Privacy Tour”.
Warhammer memorabilia can be seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
PowerWash Simulator features DLC that allows you to clean locations from Warhammer.
Call of Duty collaborates with Warhammer for Season Two of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, along with other Warhammer cosmetics.
The Secret Level episode: "Warhammer 40,000: And They Shall Know No Fear" is based off of Warhammer 40,000.
In the Smiling Friends episode: "Mole Man", Glep paints Warhammer figures.
Weapons and armor based on the Death Korps of Krieg from Warhammer 40,000 appear in Rust as part of a collaboration.
Warhammer Survivors is a format crossover between Warhammer and Vampire Survivors.

Warhawk.description: A Warhawk is the final boss in Twisted Metal: Black.
Starhawk is a spinoff to Warhawk.
PlayStation All-Stars Battle Royale features Warhawk ships as secondary representation in Time Station.

Wario.description: The Wario series is a spin-off of the Mario series. The games Mario & Wario and Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3 are part of both series.
Wario Blast: Featuring Bomberman! is a crossover between the two series.
One of the tracks in Uniracers is called "Wario Paint".
Wario meets Kid Klown in the comic Warios Weihnachtsmärchen.
Wario meets Kirby in the comic Warios Weihnachtsmärchen; the bucket from Mario & Wario is an obtainable item in Kirby Super Star.

Wario meets Donkey and Diddy Kong in the comic Warios Weihnachtsmärchen; various microgames in the WarioWare series are based on Donkey Kong games, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "Donkey Kong Country Returns" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; additionally a music track from WarioWare Twisted! is featured in Donkey Konga 3.
Mario & Wario can be seen on a TV in Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue; a Pokémon Pikachu console is a treasure in Wario Land 3, while a Pokémon Mini console can be seen in WarioWare: Touched!

The "Modern" versions of Ball in Game & Watch Gallery 2, of Donkey Kong Jr. in Game & Watch Gallery 3 and of Fire Attack in Game & Watch Gallery 4 feature elements from the Wario Land series. A remake of Flagman featuring D-D as the protagonist is unlockable in Wario Land II. Various microgames based on Game & Watch games appear in the WarioWare series.
A picture of Wario from Wario Land II appears in Game Boy Camera.
Wario Land II features a treasure based on the Big Face item from Yume Kojo: Doki Doki Panic.
Wario appears in "Jagdszenen aus der unteren Oberstufe" and other N-Gang episodes.
Picross NP Vol. 7 includes images from the Wario series.

Wario.game: Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru
Wario.description: Dr. Arewo Stein from Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru makes an appearance in Wario Land 4, and music from the game is unlockable in WarioWare: D.I.Y.
Microgame versions of Balloon Fight are featured in the WarioWare series.
Microgame versions of Duck Hunt are featured in the WarioWare series.
A microgame version of F-Zero is featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!.
A microgame version of Family Basic is featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!.
Microgame versions of Hogan's Alley are featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$! and WarioWare: Touched!
Microgame versions of Urban Champion are featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$! and WarioWare: D.I.Y.
R.O.B. appears in various microgames in the WarioWare series.
A microgame version of Super Scope 6's "LazerBlazer" mode is featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!.
Microgame versions of Wild Gunman are featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$! and WarioWare: D.I.Y. Showcase.

In the microgame "Unexcite Bike", featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!, Wario meets the Excite Bikers; Microgame versions of Excitebike are featured in WarioWare: Twisted! and WarioWare: D.I.Y.
The minigame Wario's Sheriff, featured in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!, can be considered a crossover between the two series.
Wario makes an appearance in Densetsu no Starfy 3.
A microgame version of Tennis is featured in WarioWare: Twisted!
Microgame versions of Wrecking Crew are featured in WarioWare: Twisted!, WarioWare: D.I.Y. Showcase and WarioWare Gold.
Microgame versions of Pinball are featured in WarioWare: Twisted! and WarioWare Gold.
Microgame versions of Golf and NES Open Tournament Golf are featured in WarioWare: Twisted!
Microgame versions of Clu Clu Land are featured in the WarioWare series.
A microgame version of Baseball is featured in WarioWare: Twisted!
A microgame version of Mach Rider is featured in WarioWare: Twisted!
Microgame versions of Kid Icarus are featured in WarioWare: Twisted!, WarioWare: D.I.Y. Showcase and WarioWare Gold.
A microgame version of Ice Hockey is featured in WarioWare: Twisted!
A microgame version of Famicom Tantei Club II is featured in the Japanese version of WarioWare: Touched!
A microgame in WarioWare: Touched! is inspired on the NES version of Galaga.
The "Were's Wario" microgame in WarioWare: Touched! is a parody of Where's Waldo?
Music from the WarioWare series is featured in Daigasso! Band Brothers.
Dance Dance Revolution: Mario Mix includes a track from Wario World.
Andy Stitzer reads a Wario World guide book in The 40-Year-Old Virgin.
In the movie Stormbreaker, Alex Rider has a copy of WarioWare: Touched!.

The Alien Bunnies from WarioWare, inc.: Minigame Mania appear in the original Rhythm Tengoku and in Rhythm Tengoku Gold, while Rhythm Heaven Megamix features a challenge train called "Wario... Where?" including characters from the WarioWare series; characters from Rhythm Paradise appear in WarioWare: Smooth Moves and Game & Wario.

Baby Wario is playable in Yoshi's Island DS, while Wario characters directly interact with the "Yoshi's Story" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; there also are other minor references between the two series.
Files based on WarioWare: Smoothe Moves were obtainable by completing a level in UPIXO in Action: Mission in Snowdriftland.
A microgame version of Light Tennis is featured in WarioWare: Smooth Moves.
Microgame versions of Nintendogs are featured in WarioWare: Smooth Moves and WarioWare Gold.
Microgame versions of the NES Punch-Out!! are featured in WarioWare: Smooth Moves and WarioWare: D.I.Y. Showcase.
A microgame version of Brain Age is featured in WarioWare: Smooth Moves; additionally in the "Rude Awakening" microgame Wario's face is similar to Dr. Kawashima's.
Microgame versions of Star Fox are featured in WarioWare: Smooth Moves and WarioWare: D.I.Y.
A wallpaper based on WarioWare: Smooth Moves can be obtained in Chick Chick Boom.
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews Virtual Boy Wario Land in the episode "Virtual Boy".
Wario is a selectable character in Super Smash Bros. Brawl and its sequels, with stages and Assist Trophies from the series.
Pyoro was originally a videogame within the Wario series.
Paper Plane was originally a videogame within the Wario series, and it features characters from the game.
A microgame version of Nazo no Murasame Jo is featured in the Japanese version of WarioWare: D.I.Y.
A microgame version of Advance Wars is featured in WarioWare: D.I.Y. Showcase.
A microgame version of Freshly-Picked Tingle's Rosy Rupeeland is featured in WarioWare: D.I.Y. Showcase.
The title of a Eddsworld comic is called Warioware.
The DLC microgame "Suck Goo!" from WarioWare: D.I.Y. is based on World of Goo.
The DLC microgame "Fire Bad!" from WarioWare: D.I.Y. is based on the Bit.Trip series.
The DLC microgame "Shantae NAB!" from WarioWare: D.I.Y. is based on the Shantae series.
The DLC microgame "MEAT BOY" from WarioWare: D.I.Y. is based on Super Meat Boy.
The DLC microgame "Fly Home!" from WarioWare: D.I.Y. has Maxwell from Scribblenauts make a cameo appearance.

SpongeBob SquigglePants is similar to the WarioWare games. Both contain minigames that are split into sections, each of the sections on both games contain themes, and a main character associated them, and both games contain lives.

Arino plays the SNES game Mario & Wario as part of the GameCenter CX in Paris special episode. He also played the Game Boy game Super Mario Land 2: 6 Golden Coins in episode 216 and played both WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgames! and WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Party Games! in episode 369.
NES Remix 2 includes challenges based on Wario's Woods.
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of Wario's Woods
A sound effect from WarioWare: Touched is used in Doki Doki Literature Club.
A microgame version of Fire Emblem Awakening is featured in WarioWare Gold.
A microgame version of Pushmo is featured in WarioWare Gold.

A microgame version of Tomodachi Life is featured in WarioWare Gold. Additionally, if a Mii is given a Wii U in Tomodachi Life, they will sometimes play games that sounds like and resemble a minigame in Game & Wario.
Wario has been a subject for Death Battle!

Captain Syrup from the Wario Land series is mentioned by Gullivarrr in Animal Crossing: New Horizons (added with update 1.3.0), while Wario characters directly interact with the "Animal Crossing: New Leaf" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; there also are other minor references between the two series.

Microgame versions of Metroid games are featured in the WarioWare series, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "Super Metroid" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; there also are other minor references between the two series.

A microgame version of Nintendo Badge Arcade is featured in WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with it; Nintendo Badge Arcade also features badges based on the WarioWare series.

Microgame versions of Pikmin games are featured in the WarioWare series, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "Pikmin 2" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; additionally Wario can draw a sketch of Pikmin in WarioWare Gold by scanning the respective amiibo.
Microgame versions of Big Brain Academy are featured in WarioWare: D.I.Y. and WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with the latter.
Microgame versions of Fire Emblem games are featured in WarioWare Gold and WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with on-screen instructions in the latter.
Microgame versions of Ice Climber are featured in the WarioWare series, with Wario characters directly interacting with the one in WarioWare: Get It Together!.

A microgame version of Splatoon 2 is featured in WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with its on-screen instructions; additionally Wario can draw a sketch of Splatoon characters in WarioWare Gold by scanning the respective amiibo.
A microgame version of Devil World is featured in WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with it.

Microgame versions of Zelda games are featured in the WarioWare series, with Wario characters directly interacting with the "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; additionally Wario can draw a sketch of Zelda characters in WarioWare Gold by scanning the respective amiibo.

A microgame version of Luigi's Mansion is featured in WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with it; additionally the ending of Luigi's Mansion might be based on the ending of Wario Land.
A microgame version of Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker is featured in WarioWare: Get It Together!, with Wario characters directly interacting with it.

Ryu's costume is also available as DLC in Dynasty Warriors Online and Ninja Gaiden Sigma 2 features four costumes from Warriors characters.

Ayane is a guest character in Dynasty Warriors: Strikeforce, where her weapons are selectable, and she's playable in Dynasty Warriors Vs. and Warriors Orochi 3, while Kasumi is playable in Warriors Orochi 3 Ultimate; Naotora Li from Samurai Warriors is a guest character in Dead or Alive 5 Last Round, which also features a DLC costume set of characters from the series; Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate features a costume set based on characters from Warriors Orochi 3 Ultimate; Warriors All-Stars features Kasumi, Marie Rose and Honoka as playable characters.
