Worms from Worms can be found in Monster Sanctuary.
A bot based on a Worm from Worms can be found in Astro Bot after an update.

Wreck-It Ralph.description: Wreck-It Ralph features some references to Donkey Kong.
Yuni from Dance Dance Revolution X2 makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
Wreck-It Ralph features characters from the Sonic series; Ralph is selectable in Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed.
Wreck-It Ralph features characters from Pac-Man, while Pac-Man: Ralph Breaks the Maze includes several characters and themed mazes from Wreck-It Ralph.
Wreck-It Ralph features various characters from Street Fighter II.
Wreck-It Ralph features a zombie based on Cyril from The House of the Dead, but the arcade cabinet for The House of the Dead can also be seen.
Wreck-It Ralph features a character based on Kano from Mortal Kombat.
The character Satine from Wreck-It Ralph may be based on Diablo.
Bowser makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph along with other references to the Mario series.
Neff from Altered Beast makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
A flyer from Bolt can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
The piece of paper with the lipstick mark from Paperman can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
Wreck-It Ralph features characters from Q*bert, while Ralph appears as a guest in Q*bert for iOS and Android.
In Wreck-It Ralph, Ralph visits the game Tapper.
An Exlamation Mark from the Metal Gear series makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
The game TurboTime from Wreck-It Ralph is based on Rally-X.
In Wreck-It Ralph, the character Turbo visits the game RoadBlasters.
Wreck-It Ralph features a reference to Lara Croft.
An arcade cabinet for Centipede can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph along with some other references to the game.
An arcade cabinet for Asteroids can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph and the game is cited by Ralph himself.
Paperboy makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
Wreck-It Ralph features a character based on the knights from Joust.
Frogger makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
Wreck-It Ralph features characters from Dig Dug.
Peter Pepper from BurgerTime makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
The paddles and ball from Pong make an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
Tiny from Meet the Robinsons makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
Vladimir from Tangled makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph, while Rapunzel appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
An access to the arcade game Tron can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
Wreck-It Ralph features a character possibly based on Link from the Zelda series.
The Qix makes an appearance in Wreck-It Ralph.
An arcade cabinet for Battlezone can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
An arcade cabinet for Space Invaders can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
Bentley Bear from Crystal Castles appears in Wreck-It Ralph.
An arcade cabinet for the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles game can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
An arcade cabinet for Dragon's Lair can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
An arcade cabinet for Virtua Cop and the access to it can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
Wreck-It Ralph features a game based on Daytona USA.
Wreck-It Ralph features a reference to Aerith from Final Fantasy VII.
Wreck-It Ralph features a reference to the "Jenkins" meme from World of Warcraft.
Wreck-It Ralph features a reference to the phrase "All your base are belong to us" from Zero Wing.
Ralph from Wreck-It Ralph is selectable in Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed.
Characters looking like Wreck-It Ralph and Vanellope appear in The Fairly OddParents episode "Dumbbell Curve".
Characters from Wreck-It Ralph appear in Disney Infinity.
Wreck-It Ralph is referenced in the Big Bang Theory episode "The Relationship Diremption".
Disney Crossy Road has Wreck-It Ralph characters.
Game Central Station is a stage in Kingdom Hearts Union χ which also features characters from Wreck-It Ralph.  Also, Ralph can be summoned in Kingdom Hearts III.
Disney Heroes: Battle Mode features characters from Wreck-It Ralph.
Pitch Meeting had episodes on the Wreck-It Ralph movies.
Iron Man appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Dumbo appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
The house from Up appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
An image of The Mupper Show appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
An image of EVE from WALL-E appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
A Cars image appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Buzz Lightyear appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
an action figure of Ralph appears in Big Hero 6 while Baymax, Hero, GoGo Tomago and Honey Lemon appears in  Ralph Breaks the Internet.

Wreck-It Ralph.game: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (Disney)
Wreck-It Ralph.description: Snow White and Grumpy appear in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Princess Aurora appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Ariel appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Belle appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Jasmine appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Pocahontas appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Mulan appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Tiana appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Merida appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Anna and Elsa appear in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Moana appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet; additionally an image of Ralph appears during the credits of the movie Moana..
Peter Pan's shadow and Tinker Bell make a cameo in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Eeyore appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Clarabelle Cow makes a cameo in Ralph Breaks the Internet while Mickey Mouse makes an appearance on a billboard in Wreck-It Ralph.
The movie Captain America: The First Avenger is mentioned in Ralph Breaks the Internet.
Baby Groot appears in Ralph Breaks the Internet, with Rocket Racoon also making a cameo.
Stormtroopers, C3PO and R2D2 appear in Ralph Breaks the Internet. A cabinet for the Star Wars arcade game can be seen in Wreck-It Ralph.
Nick Wilde and Judy Hopps make cameos in Ralph Breaks the Internet; a parody of Wreck-It Ralph titled "Wreck-It Rhino" makes a small appearance within the movie Zootopia.
Disney Magic Kingdoms features characters from the Wreck-It Ralph series.
Ralph Breaks the Internet and Fortnite have references to each other.
Wreck-It Ralph is mentioned in the episode "Adam West High"; Peter and Lois watch "Wreck-It Ralph 3: Ralph Wrecks the Toilet" in the Family Guy episode "Cutaway Land".
Hero’s Duty troops such as Sergeant Calhoun and Sugar Rush citizens from Wreck-It Ralph are fighters in Disney Sorcerer's Arena.
Litwak's Arcade is seen briefly in the short Us Again.
Wreck-It-Ralph appears in Disney Melee Mania.
Duncan and Wynnchel appear in Rescue Rangers (2022).
Characters and items from Wreck-It Ralph appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley.
Ralph appears in the credits for Wish.
Cards based on Wreck-it Ralph appear in Lorcana.
Characters from Wreck-It Ralph appear in Disney Speedstorm.
There will be a puzzle in Disney Solitare that shows a scene from Wreck-It Ralph.

Wrecking Crew.description: The Wrecking Crew series is a spin-off of the Mario series.
Foreman Spike from Wrecking Crew is unlockable in Mobile Golf.
Microgame versions of Wrecking Crew are featured in WarioWare: Twisted!, WarioWare: D.I.Y. Showcase and WarioWare Gold
Eggplant Man from Wrecking Crew makes an appearance in Chibi-Robo!
Dance Dance Revolution: Mario Mix includes a track from Wrecking Crew.
The Golden Hammer from Wrecking Crew is a usable item in Super Smash Bros. Brawl and its sequels, with Super Smash Bros. for Wii U also featuring a stage based on the game.
NES Remix includes challenges based on Wrecking Crew.
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of Wrecking Crew
Wrecking Crew is mentioned in Five Nights at Freddy's: Return to the Pit.

WrestleQuest.description: Invincible and Atom Eve appear in WrestleQuest as background characters.

X (A24).description: In X, A gas station called the "Pedlar Market" is a reference to the "Yankee Pedlar Inn" from The Innkeepers.

X (Nintendo).description: The Federation Army Special Ops Battleship VIXIV IV from the 2002 Metroid manga and the Galactic Federation Battleship VIXIV take their name from the VIXIV spaceship in X.
X-Scape features a reference to the F-Zero series.
The Commander from X appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; he also appears as a sticker in Brawl.

X-Men.description: Beast made his debut in X-Men (Vol. 1) #1
The X-Men appear in Avengers #3. Beast, Havok, Storm and Sunspot have also been members of the Avengers.
Bonanza is mentioned in X-Men #3.
Scarlet Witch made her debut appear in X-Men #4.
The X-Men appear in Fantastic Four #28.
Spider-Man appears in X-Men #35.
Hulk appears alongside the X-Men in X-Men #66.
Doctor Doom appears in X-Men (Vol. 1) #98.
Popeye the Sailor Man makes a cameo appearance in X-Men #125.
The X-Men appears with Silver Surfer in Marvel Feature #1.

The X-Men appear in Rom #17, #18, #65 and #66. The Brotherhood of Mutants from X-Men appears in Rom #31 and #32. The New Mutants and Professor X from X-Men appear in Rom Annual #3. Forge from X-Men appears in many issues of Rom. Rom can be seen on a screen in Uncanny X-Men #187.
Man-Thing appears in Uncanny X-Men #144.
Tigra appears in Uncanny X-Men #155-156.
The Uncanny X-Men and The New Teen Titans is a crossover between the two series.
The Wolverine series is a spin-off to the X-Men series.
X-Men and the Micronauts is a crossover between the two series.
The Uncategorizable X+Thems from Megaton Man are parodies of the X-Men.
Several X-Men appear in Christmas with Combat Colin.
Gambit made his debut in X-Men Annual #14.
The Punisher appears in Uncanny X-Men Vol. 1 #272.
Thanos appears alongside Cyclops and Wolverine in Infinity Gauntlet #3.
Wolverine mentions Terminator in the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "Days of Future Past, Part One".
One of the TV shows Mojo creates in the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "Mojovision" is called I Dream of Jean, the title being a parody of I Dream of Jeannie.
E.T. is mentioned in the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "Out of the Past - Part II".
Wolverine references the "do you feel lucky, punk?" speech from Dirty Harry in the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "The Dark Phoenix, Part II: The Inner Circle".
Wolverine uses the quote "Here's Johnny" from The Shining in the X-Men: The Aniamted Series episode "The Dark Phoenix, Part II: The Inner Circle".
Akuma appears as a secret character in X-Men: Children of the Atom; X-Men vs. Street Fighter is a crossover between the two series.
Members of "Technet" appear in the first part of the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "Proteus".
X-Men characters appear in the Marvel Super Heroes series.
Winnie the Pooh is mentioned in the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "A Deal with the Devil".
Mojo imitates Porky Pig from Looney Tunes in the X-Men: The Animated Series episode "Longshot".
Star Trek/X-Men is a crossover between the two series.
Shang-Chi appears in X-Men Vol. 2 #62-64 and Uncanny X-Men Vol. 5 #4. Nightcrawler from X-Men appears in Master of Kung Fu Vol. 2 #1.
Black Panther appears in various X-Men comics, while the X-Men appear several times in Black Panther Vol. 4.
X-Men characters are playable in all Marvel vs. Capcom games except Infinite.
The armor "Cyttoraks" (Psychometer in English) from Breath fo Fire IV is named after Cyttorak, the entity who gives power to X-Men villain Juggernaut.
Nightcrawler mentions the Twilight Zone in the 6th Episode of X-Men Evolution titled "Middleverse".
Digimon Toys appear in Ultimate X-Men #7.
X-Men is mentioned in the Malcolm in the Middle episode: "Hal Coaches".
X-Men UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Spider-Man and the X-Men crossover over with characters from Tutenstein in the comic, Tutenstein.
A character resembling Rorschach appears in Astonishing X-Men Vol. 3 #6.
A Zombie version of the X-Men first appear in Ultimate Fantastic Four #22 and in several Marvel Zombies comics.
Characters from X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse star in the "Save Me (Wake Up Call)" video of Video Mods.
Storm from the X-Men is mentioned in the English dub of the 6th episode of Ghost Stories.

Marvel: Ultimate Alliance is a spiritual sequel to X-Men Legends and features many playable characters from the X-Men series, including Cable, Colossus, Cyclops, Gambit, Iceman, Juggernaut, Magneto, Nightcrawler, Phoenix, Psylocke, Sabretooth and Storm, with "All New X-Men", "First Class X-Men", and "X-Men" being Team Bonuses.
X-Men is mentioned in Kick-Ass #1. The cover to "Uncanny X-Men #1" appears in Kick-Ass #7.
X-Men is mentioned in many episodes of The Big Bang Theory.
Linkara reviews Uncanny X-Men #423.
In the game X-Men Origins: Wolverine there's a cake based on the one from Portal.
The Angry Video Game Nerd reviews various X-Men games in the 69th episode of the series, and the HyperScan game X-Men in episode 131.
Jennifer compares her powers to the X-Men in Jennifer's Body.
There is a title achievement called "Quick Silver". Cyclops' Visor appears in the shop.
Mystique costume with X-Men heroes and Magneto later on are downloadable in LittleBigPlanet.
Blade appears in X-Men (Vol. 3) #2.
Rogue, Beast, Quicksilver, Silver Samurai, Scarlet Witch, Magneto, Apocalypse, and Phoenix have been subjects for Death Battle!
X-Men is parodied and has cameos in several issues of Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews the cartoon “X-Men”.
X-Men is parodied in the MAD sketch "The Clawfice".
X-Men is mentioned in the Ready Player One book; the fictional metal "adamantium" from X-Men is mentioned in Ready Player One; Wolverine can be seen in the movie.
A stick figure dresses up as Cyclops in the Dick Figures episode: "Terminate-Her".
Jake English has a poster of Mystique from X-Men in Homestuck.
The X-Men have been parodied multiple times on HISHE.
Charles Xavier's School for Gifted Children from X-Men is mentioned in Prep & Landing: Mansion Impossible.
A pinball table based on X-Men was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX 2 that features characters from the series.
The First 2012 wave of Lego Marvel Super Heroes included a X-Men set, LEGO would later release products based on X-Men '97.
Moon Knight appeared in X-Men Legacy Vol. 1 #266-267.
The Irate Gamer reviews Uncanny X-Men on NES
Geometry Dash features a skin based on Cyclops from the X-Men.
Magneto is mentioned in the Manhattan Love Story episode: "Sex Actually".
X-Men were mentioned in the episode The Princess Guide.
X-Men is parodied in Les Kassos.
Squirrel Girl appears in Uncanny X-Men #34.
The X-Men and several of its members are mentioned in Armada.
Team Express' cars found in Rocket League's Season Mode are named after X-Men characters Beast, Tusk and Sabretooth.
Quick Silver was playing Ms. Pac-Man in X-Men: Apocalypse.
Four children in the Mutant Academy watched Star Wars: Return of the Jedi.
An X-Men comic was mentioned in Chapter 1 of Stranger Things.
Dina mentions Professor X in Season 2, Episode 7 of Superstore, “Halloween Theft”.
Munchkin X-Men is a format crossover between the two series.
Magneto, Gambit, Juggernaut, Iceman, and Apocalypse have been subjects for DBX.
X-Men is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Dear Beloved Family", while Iceman is mentioned in the episode: "Did the Chicken Cross the Road?".
Pitch Meeting had episodes on the X-Men movies.
Gravity Falls: Lost Legends have parodies of the X-Men.
A VHS copy of X-Men (2000) can be seen in Comic Man's room.
Storm, Mystique, Wolverine, Dark Phoenix, Rogue, Gambit, Magneto, Cyclops, Colossus, Jubilee and Emma Frost appear in Fortnite.
Storm from X-Men appeared in Puzzle & Dragons during the Marvel collaboration event.
Quantum Leap is mentioned in "Last Annihilation: Wiccan & Hulkling #1".
Everett's dad mentions the X-Men in the Solar Opposites episode "A Very Solar Holiday Opposites Special".
A character dresses up as Jubilee in the 23rd episode of Close Enough.
X-Men is parodied in multiple Perfect Cell Vs episodes.
Cards based on characters from X-Men appear in Marvel Snap.
X-Men is mentioned in the Beef episode: "Just Not All at the Same Time".
The Marvel Studios series of Lego Minifigures includes Beast, Storm and Wolverine.
Professor X's School for the Gifted is mentioned in the Scott Pilgrim Takes Off episode "Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little Life".
X-Men game boxes are seen in the Melvins Macabre episode "NOSTALGIA".
Characters from X-Men appear in Monopoly Go!.
Characters from X-Men appears in the "Secret Lair x Marvel" release for Magic: The Gathering.
Wolverine, Luna Snow, Magik, Storm, Magneto, Emma Frost, Phoenix, Rogue and Gambit are playable characters in Marvel Rivals.
Godzilla vs. X-Men is a crossover between the two series.
Armor, Emma Frost, Juggernaut, Psylocke, Storm and Gambit are playable characters in Marvel Mystic Mayhem.
Storm and Phoenix are playable characters in Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Master Mold and Sauron also appear as bosses.
Storm is a playable character in Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.

X-O Manowar.description: The X-O Manowar armor first appears in Solar, Man of the Atom #6. Solar, Man of the Atom and X-O Manowar have appeared in many comics together.

Turok appears in several X-O Manowar comics. X-O Manowar appears in Turok, Dinosaur Hunter #1, #18 and #19, and Turok has a vision in which he sees X-O Manowar in Turok, Dinosaur Hunter #36 and #42. Additionally, Inquest from X-O Manowar appears in Turok #1 and #2.
Iron Man and X-O Manowar in Heavy Metal is a crossover between the two series.
A high school version of X-O Manowar appears in Valiant High.

X-Zone.description: X-Zone is compatible with the Super Scope and the main character is shown using it in the game.

XCOM.description: The Civ II: Fantastic Worlds expansion includes a scenario based on XCOM. Units from X-COM appear in Civilization V: Brave New World.
Team Fortress 2 features three promotional items based on XCOM: Enemy Unknown and unlocked by pre-ordering the game.
UFO: Enemy Unknown is part of Malina's collection in the Helltaker comic strip "Prologue".

XDefiant.description: The Cleaners from The Division appears as a faction in XDefiant.
Libertad, the Highwaymen and Blood Dragon from Far Cry appear as factions in XDefiant.
The Phantoms and the Wolves from Ghost Recon appear as factions in XDefiant.
Echelon from Splinter Cell appears as a faction in XDefiant.
DedSec from Watch Dogs appears as a faction in XDefiant.
GS-Kommando from Rainbow Six appears as a faction in XDefiant.
The Assassins from Assassin's Creed appears as a faction in XDefiant.
In XDefiant, the Enchanted Forest Map, as well as the game mode "Lum Hunt", are based on the Rayman series.

Xavier Riddle and the Secret Museum.description: There is a Xavier Riddle and the Secret Museum event in the game “Kart Kingdom”, featuring Xavier Riddle incarnations of historical figures.
Xavier and the others see Fred Rogers filming Mister Rogers' Neighborhood in the Xavier Riddles and the Secret Museum episode “I Am Fred Rogers”.

Xavier: Renegade Angel.description: The ending to Terminator 2: Judgment Day is parodied in the Xavier: Renegade Angel episode "Chief Beef Loco".
When throwing up bacon to travel to the future, Xavier ends up in the year 2112.

Xena.description: Xena is a spin-off of Hercules: The Legendary Journeys.
A Xena: Warrior Princess poster is seen in Small Soldiers.
Army of Darkness / Xena, Xena / Army of Darkness, and Army of Darkness / Xena: Warrior Princess: Forever... And a Day are direct crossovers between the two series.
Xena: Warrior Princess is mentioned in Little Britain USA.
Linkara reviews The Marriage of Xena and Hercules.
Xena appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #46.
Xebro is based on Xena from Xena: Warrior Princess.
Xena appears in Raid: Shadow Legends.
A pinball table based on Xena: Warrior Princess was added to the Pinball FX series starting with Pinball FX that features characters from the series.
Xena is a playable character in Funko Fusion.

Xenoblade.description: Xenoblade is a spiritual successor of Xenogears.
The English version of Xenoblade Chronicles references the "for great justice" line from Zero Wing.
Mii Plaza includes a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Xenoblade Chronicles.
Shulk from Xenoblade Chronicles appears as a playable character in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and for Wii U, with a stage based on the series.
Super Mario Maker features a costume based on Shulk from Xenoblade Chronicles.
Rex's salvager suit from Xenoblade Chronicles 2 is obtainable in The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.
KOS-MOS and T-ELOS from Xenosaga appear as Blades in Xenoblade Chronicles 2.
Xenoblade is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
Tetris 99 featured an Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition theme during a limited event.
The Monado from Xenoblade Chronicles can be found on display in a training hall in Nobody Saves the World.
Xenoblade is parodied in the Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episode "TAKE THE SHOT! TAKE THE F**KING SHOT!".

Xenogears.description: Xenogears is a spiritual successor of Chrono Trigger and Lucca from Chrono Trigger makes a cameo appearance in Xenogears.
A picture of two characters dressed as Elly and Margie from Xenogears can be obtained in Front Mission 3.
Xenosaga is a spiritual successor of Xenogears.
Statues resembling the Zohar from Xenogears appear in Soma Bringer.
Xenoblade is a spiritual successor of Xenogears.
Music from Xenogears is present in Theatrhythm Final Fantasy: Curtain Call and Theatrhythm Final Bar Line.

XG from Xenogears appears as a boss in World of Final Fantasy. Characters from Xenogears appeared in Final Fantasy Brave Exvius during special collaborations; there have also been other minor references between the two series.

Xenosaga.description: Xenosaga is a spiritual successor of Xenogears.
In Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail advertising Ace Combat 4.
In Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail advertising Smash Court Tennis Pro Tournament.
In Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail advertising a Pac-Man game.
In the Japanese version of Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail with an artwork of Klonoa, purpotedly coming from him as well.
In Xenosaga Episode 1 the character Mr. Holgar references the Drill Council and Susumu Hori from Mr. Driller.
In the English version of Xenosaga Episode 1 the player can receive an e-mail from Kazuya Mishima of Tekken 4, speaking about having won a battle and expecting his son Jin to be a better opponent.
The Magnus "Rare Action Figure" in Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean is based on KOS-MOS from Xenosaga.
Xenosaga Freaks includes a parody of the game titled Kotaba no Puzzle: Xenopittan.
Namco × Capcom features characters from Xenosaga.

A costume of KOS-MOS from Xenosaga is featured in Tales of the World: Narakiri Dungeon 3 with her actual attacks, Tales of the Abyss features a doll of KOS-MOS with her attacks as well, KOS-MOS appears as a support character in Tales of Hearts, Tales of Destiny for PlayStation has a "Gentleman" enemy wearing KOS-MOS's head gear while KOS-MOS's head gear also appears as the "Mechanical Doll Accessory" artifact in Tales of Arise.
Create-A-Soul mode in SoulCalibur III features character parts to create KOS-MOS from Xenosaga.

Famista Online, Famista DS, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match feature KOS-MOS from Xenosaga as a guest player, with Albedo also appearing in Famista Online 2010 and Shion appearing in Famista 2011 and Dream Match.
Several Xenosaga characters are featured in Super Robot Taisen OG Saga: Endless Frontier and its sequel.
A KOS-MOS costume from Xenosaga is unlockable in Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha A's Portable: The Gears of Destiny.
KOS-MOS appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #32.
KOS-MOS and T-ELOS from Xenosaga appear as Blades in Xenoblade Chronicles 2.

Xeodrifter.description: Xeodrifter is a playable character in Runbow.
Xeodrifter is a playable character in Mutant Mudds Super Challenge.

Xevious.description: The Terrazi enemy from Xevious is based on the Cylon Raiders from Battlestar Galactica.
The Kapi enemy from Xevious is based on the Millenium Falcon from Star Wars.
The Solvalou from Xevious is based on the Nostromo from Alien.
The Special Flag from Rally-X is a special item in Xevious and its sequels.
The Galaxian flagship is an enemy in Super Xevious, while the X68000 version of Galaga '88 features a bonus level with enemies from Xevious.
Bacuras from Xevious appear as enemies in Märchen Maze.
The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of the Solvalou from Xevious.
The Bacuras and Nasca lines from Xevious appear as enemies in Final Blaster.
A Kapi and the Solvalou from Xevious are secret bonus characters in Tinkle Pit.
The background music in the Onett Arcade in Earthbound features sample notes similar to Xevious.

The field in the Namco stadium in Super Famista 4, Super Famista 5 and Famista 64 features elements from Xevious, and the Solvalou ship, the Mothership Andor (under the name "Xevious") and the Bacura appear as guest players in Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and Famista Dream Match; additionally Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium and its sequels include players called "Solvalou" and "Xevious", while Famista Online 2010 and Famista Climax include one in the Rivals team based on the Mothership Andor.
Namco Classic Collection Vol. 1 includes Xevious.
Various Xevious games are featured in multiple Namco Museum titles.
One of the enemies in Super Xevious resembles the tanks from Tank Battalion series. Stage 42 in Namco Gallery Vol.1 version of Battle City is shaped after the Solvalou from Xevious.
Xevious and Super Xevious are featured in Namco History Vol.1.
Paul Phoenix and Heihachi Mishima appear as selectable ships in Xevious 3D/G+, while a small Solvalou is a customization item for Jack-5 in Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection.
Destroying all Sols in Area 1 and the red Sol in Area 2 of Xevious 3D/G+ makes the blue dragon from Dragon Spirit appear in Area 4.
Destroying all Sols in Area 1 and the red Sol in Area 2 of Xevious 3D/G+ makes a large Pooka from Dig Dug appear in Area 7, while Dig Dug: Digging Strike features a reference to Xevious.
One stage in GUNbare! Game Tengoku 2 features a boss parody of the Andor Genesis from Xevious.

A costume of a Grobda and a Bacuda from Xevious are featured on Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon with their actual techniques, while the Bacura appears as an enemy in Tales of Symphonia and Tales of Legendia while Tales of the World: Radiant Mythology 2 includes a DLC floating Solvalou hat.
Taiko no Tatsujin 4 and later games in the series feature music tracks from Xevious; music from Xevious is also featured in the Namcot Medley debuting in Taiko no Tatsujin 10.
Star Fox: Assault features Xevious as an unlockable game.
A song from Xevious is featured in Donkey Konga 3.

The Xevi language from Xevious is featured as the language of Aon in Druaga Online: The Story of Aon, while a picture of a Terrazi enemy from Xevious appears in the Museum area of The Return of Ishtar.
QuickSpot features one puzzle with the Solvalou from Xevious.

Pac-Man drives a modified Andor Genesis from Xevious in Ridge Racer 7 and a scaled-down Solvalou in Ridge Racer 3D, the Solvalou and Baracuda enemies can be seen flying by in the Mist Falls race track and the player can play a minigame of Xevious during loading screens. There are other minor references in several Ridge Racer games.

The Solvalou from Xevious is referenced in New Space Order Short Story, while a ship unit from the United Galaxy faction is based on the Solvalou and the Sacred Religious State's language is based on the Xevi language.
Pac-Man's "Soul Varoon" car in Mario Kart Arcade GP 2 is based on the Solvalou from Xevious.
The music theme "First Stage" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 04 is a remix of a theme from Xevious.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of a Bacura from Xevious with characters moving in the background.
The Mothership from Xevious appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Toroids and Bacuras from Xevious are enemies in Namco Chronicle.
Xevious is one of the games added to Namco Arcade.

Bacuras from Xevious started appearing in the Co-Op Mission "Tokyo Martial Law" from Ace Combat Infinity as part of a collaboration event, with Xevious-themed emblems being handed out at a later date; while city structures in Ace Combat 3: Electrosphere resemble the Andor Genesis from Xevious.
The Bacura from Xevious appears as an enemy in Smash Run mode in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS.

Pac-Man is selectable in Project Fardraut: Secondary Work of Xevious; additionally Xevious is included in Retro Arcade featuring Pac-Man, Pac-Man's Arcade Party, Pac-Man Connect and Play and Pac-Man's Pixel Bash; and a theme featuring Xevious characters appears in Pac-Man 99.
Wonder Momo is a playable character in Project Fardraut: Secondary Work of Xevious.
An army of enemy ships from Xevious appears in Kamen Rider × Super Sentai: Chou Super Hero Taisen.
An army of enemy ships from Xevious appears in Kamen Rider × Super Sentai: Chou Super Hero Taisen.
A cat based on the Solvalou from Xevious appears in Cat Busters as part of a Namco Catalog IP collaboration, alongside the Andor Genesis as a boss battle.
Xevious characters appear in The Knights of Avalon during the first Namco collaboration event.
The main theme of Xevious is part of the "Namcot Medley" BGM featured in Groove Coaster 4: Starlight Road.
Solvalou from Xevious and areas from the game appear in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers, various sprites from Xevious appear as treasures.
A human version of Xevious appears in 404 GAME RE:SET.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Xevious.

Xexex.description: The second level of Arcade Xexex appears as a playable game at the Amusement Park in Ganbare Goemon 2: Kiteretsu Shōgun Magginesu.
The stage "Sweet Land" in Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius is based on stage 2 of Xexex.
The FLINT-ROCK from Xexex is playable in Airforce Delta Strike.
The Flintlock ship and its weapon the Flint from Xexex appear as Yu-Gi-Oh cards.
Xexex puzzles are featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.

YIIK.description: In VA-11 Hall-A, Vella's cosplay group, YIIK, is a reference to the video game of the same name. One of the main characters is called Vella, whom this character is cosplaying as.
Travis can wear a YIIK: A Postmodern RPG t-shirt in Travis Strikes Again: No More Heroes.
Alex from YIIK is a DLC opponent in Rhythm Knights: Double Treble.
Alex from YIIK is a playable character and an assist in Cross Impact.

Yaiba (Shogakukan).description: Sunday VS Magazine: Shuuketsu! Choujou Daikessen! features characters from Yaiba.
There's a minor reference to Yaiba in episode 4 of Pop Team Epic.

Yakuman.description: Yakuman DS features many Mario characters, while a Majong Tile from Yakuman Houou is a costume in Super Mario Maker.
The Yakuman Player appears as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; he's also as a sticker in Brawl, while Yakuman DS is referenced in Toadsworth's trophy.

Yakuza.description: Yakuza 3 features a Virtua Fighter cabinet in one of its areas, while Yakuza 4 features a playable Virtual Fighter pachinko machine, Yakuza 5 features a playable Virtua Fighter pachislot machine and Yakuza 6 features a fully playable Virtua Fighter 5: Final Showdown arcade machine. Several character costumes and music from Yakuza are included in Virtua Fighter 5: Ultimate Showdown as part of the DLC "Yakuza Series Collaboration Pack".
There's a minor reference to Ryo Hazuki from Shenmue in Yakuza 4.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Portable DX features a music track from Yakuza: Dead Souls, while Yakuza 5 features playable Taiko no Tatsujin arcade cabinets.

In Yakuza 5 and it's remaster, an ice sculpture of Hatsune Miku can be found at Tsukimino. Haruka Sawamura, one of the playable characters, can also wear Hatsune Miku's signature outfit. In Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, songs from Hatsune Miku: Colorful Stage! are available to unlock and listen to.
Chapter 1 of the Initial D manga can be seen and read inside convenience stores in Yakuza 5 along with many other mangas. This was removed in the remastered version.
Kazuma Kiryu appears as a DLC golfer in the Japanese version of Hot Shots Golf: World Invitational.
Music from Yakuza was added to maimai in the maimai GreeN version.
Opa-Opa appears as a toy in a claw machine in Yakuza 0.
Goji Rokkaku, the main antagonist of Jet Set Radio appears in Yakuza Kiwami during the "Crisis on the Crapper" substory.
In Persona 5 one of the movies you can watch at the movie theater is a parody of Yakuza: Like a Dragon.
Yakuza 6 features playable Puyo Puyo arcade cabinets.
The English version of Yakuza 0 features a reference to JoJo's Bizarre Adventure.
An arcade cabinet of Virtual On can be played in Yakuza Kiwami 2.
Characters from Yakuza appear in Kyoutou Kotoba RPG: Kotodaman during a "Sega All Stars" collaboration.
Fist of the North Star: Lost Paradise is a spin-off of the Yakuza series, and Kazuma Kiryu from Yakuza appears as a downloadable skin.
Characters from Yakuza appear in Sega Heroes
Characters from the Yakuza series appear in LINE Rangers as part of a collaboration event.

A miniboss cat in the Nyakuza Metro DLC heavily resembles Goro Majima from Yakuza, investigating the manhole leading to this boss gives out the text "Kiwami means Extreme", after the subtitle of the Yakuza remakes.
There are several Dragon Quest references that are in Yakuza: Like a Dragon.
The "Sujimon" minigame in Yakuza: Like a Dragon is a parody of Pokémon.
Characters from Yakuza appear in Dragon Poker as part of a special collaboration.
Ichiban Kasuga from Yakuza: Like a Dragon appears in Earth UFO Catcher.
Outfits based on Kasuga, Majima and Saeko in her Matriarch outfit appears, along with cosmetics from Yakuza in Phantasy Star Online 2.
Characters from Yakuza appeared in Boku & Dragons as part of a special collaboration.
Woody Pop is playable in Lost Judgment.
Kiryu from Yakuza is playable in Super Monkey Ball: Banana Mania.
Outfits based on Kiryu, Majima and Kaoru and Cosmetics from Yakuza appears in Rainbow Six: Siege.
Yakuza is parodied in the Daitomodachi episode "Nessa Hits The Griddy After Ending My Nuzlocke".
The song "Bakamitai (Taxi Driver Edition)" from the Like a Dragon franchise is included as a part of the "Sega Music Pack" DLC for Samba de Amigo: Party Central.
A Bot based on Kazuma Kiryu from Yakuza can be found in Astro Bot.
Cosmetics based on the Like a Dragon series appeared in Among Us as part of a special collaboration.
Ichiban from Yakuza appears in Dave the Diver's Ichiban's Holiday DLC.
Ichiban Kasuga appears as a playable character in Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds.
Goro Majima appears in Shinobi: Art Of Vengeance as a part of "The SEGA Villains Stage DLC".

Yandere Simulator.description: Pippi, the mascot of Osu!, appears in Yandere Simulator.
Random Encounters has made a Yandere Simulator song, which featured Yandere Dev.
Characters from Yandere Simulator appear in the Daitomodachi episode "Yandere Chan Tortures Twitch".
Yandere-chan is a playable character in Go All Out!.

Yars.description: A Yar from Yars' Revenge makes a cameo in the game Raiders of the Lost Ark for Atari 2600.
A Yar from Yars' Revenge makes a cameo in the game E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial for Atari 2600.
Yars' Revenge is mentioned in Ready Player One.

Year Zero.description: "Capital G" from Year Zero appears in Rock Band.

Yellow Submarine.description: A cardboard cutout of The Phantom appears in Yellow Submarine.
A cardboard cutout of Mandrake the Magician appears in Yellow Submarine.
A cardboard cutout of Flash Gordon appears in Yellow Submarine.
A cardboard cutout of John Steed and Tara King appear in Yellow Submarine.
The Beatles: Rock Band features characters from Yellow Submarine.
The Blue Meanie appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #24.
Monopoly: The Beatles Yellow Submarine is a format crossover between the two series.
Yellow Submarine is mentioned in The Big Lez Show episodes "CHOOMAH ISLAND 2" and "PLAC-KEY".
Pepperland appears in The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen: The Tempest #2.

Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom.description: The version of Morio that looks like Goku can be seen in the Morio's Mind area of Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom.
The Bombeach area in Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom is a reference to Bob-omb Battlefield from Super Mario 64.
Yellow Taxi and Morio from Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom are playable in Move or Die.

Yertle the Turtle.game: The Wubbulous World of Dr. Seuss
Yertle the Turtle.description: The Wubbulous World of Dr. Seuss features characters from Yertle the Turtle.
Yertle the Turtle appears in Seussical.

Yie Ar Kung-Fu.description: Sexy Parodius features a stage based off Yie Ar Kung-Fu, including a cameo of its protagonist, Oolong.
Oolong is a selectable character in Jikkyō Power Pro Wrestling '96: Max Voltage  under the name "E R Kung-Fu".
Yie Ar Kung-Fu is included in Konami GB Collection Vol. 3.
Arino plays the NES port of Yie Ar Kung-Fu in episode 9. He also made it through a DVD-only revenge years later.
Yie Ar Kung-Fu was re-released as a part of the Oretachi Gēsen Zoku series.
La-Mulana features a collectible rom for Yie Ar Kung-Fu and Yie Ar Kung-Fu II.
Yie Ar Kung-Fu puzzles are featured in Pixel Puzzle Collection.
Lee from Yie Ar Kung-Fu makes an appearance in Kaettekita Pixel Crows.

Yin Yang Yo!.description: The Yin Yang Yo! episode "Attack of the Vidiots" features a reference to Super Mario Bros.

Yo Gabba Gabba!.description: The Aquabats! appear in the Yo Gabba Gabba episodes: "Summer", "Fun", "Superhero", and "Yo Gabba Gabba! LIVE! There's A Party In My City!".
Brobee appears in the Big Time Rush episode "Big Time Halloween" while he, Plex and Foofa appear in Big Time Rush episode "Big Time Cameo".
Songs from Yo Gabba Gabba! are featured in Just Dance Kids, Just Dance Kids 2, and Just Dance Kids 2014.
Yo Gabba Gabba! My First UNO is a format crossover between the two series.
Yo Gabba Gabba! is parodied in the MAD sketch "Yo Gagga Gagga!".
Yo! Fresh Beats Go Gabba Gabba! is a crossover between the two series.
Yo Gabba Gabba! is mentioned in the Modern Family episode: "Bringing Up Baby".
Yo Gabba Gabba! is shown in the South Park episode "Taming Strange".
Yo Gabba Gabba! is seen on TV in the WandaVision episode: "Breaking the Fourth Wall".
Yo Gabba Gabba! is parodied in the Robot Chicken episode "May Cause Light Cannibalism".
Bozo appears alongside Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.
Cheer Bear from Care Bears appears alongside Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.
H.R. Pufnstuf appears alongside Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.
A Steestak from Land of the Lost appears alongside Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.
Rainbow Connection from The Muppet Movie is covered by Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.
Strawberry Shortcake appears alongside Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.
The Teletubbies appears alongside Yo Gabba Gabba! in their Coachella Performance.

Yo-kai Watch.description: One of the tutorial chapters in Yo-Kai Watch features a minor reference to Metal Gear Solid.
In Yo-Kai Watch, one of the statues in the Gourd Pond Museum features a minor reference to Dark Souls.
Characters from Yo-Kai appear in Inazuma Eleven GO Galaxy as recruitable characters.
Episode 8 of Yo-Kai Watch features an allusion to Batman.
Episode 16 of Yo-Kai Watch features a reference to The Terminator.
Episode 19 of Yo-Kai Watch features a reference to Fist of the North Star.

Jibanyan from Yokai Watch is a party member in Taiko no Tatsujin: Don to Katsu no Jikuu Daibouken and Taiko no Tatsujin: Dokodon! Mystery Adventure, while Don-Chan appears in Yo-Kai Watch 2 and Yo-Kai Watch 3; additionally Taiko no Tatsujin Momoiro Version and later games in the series feature music tracks from Yokai Watch.
Episode 25 of Yo-Kai Watch features a parody of The Twilight Zone.
Episode 39 of the Yo-Kai Watch anime features a parody of Star Wars called "Space Wars", and there are minor references to the franchise in Yo-Kai Watch 2.
Episode 40 of Yo-Kai Watch features a reference to Yu-Gi-Oh .
Episode 42 of Yo-Kai Watch features references to The Walking Dead.
There's an Optimus Prime toy visible in episode 49 of the Yo-Kai Watch anime.
There's a references to Doraemon in Yo-Kai Watch: Tanjō no Himitsu da Nyan! .
Episode 60 of Yo-Kai Watch features a minor reference to The Ring.
Episode 68 of Yo-Kai Watch features a reference to Saint Seiya.

In episode 69 of Yo-Kai Watch when Gnomey reads a book about ghosts while hiding from Whisper, Jibanyan, and Hidabat, thinking they were monsters, the picture on a page he's reading resembles three ghosts that resembles the bodies of the Gastly, Haunter, and Gengar Pokémon.
Yo-Kai Watch Busters features several references to Ghostbusters.
Characters from Snack World appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Cinnamoroll characters appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Gudetama appears in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Hello Kitty characters appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Case Closed appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble. Dectective Conyan bears resemblance to Decetective Conan from Case Closed.
Characters from Ni No Kuni appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Monster Strike appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble. Characters from Yo-kai Watch appeared in Monster Strike during a special collaboration.
Characters from GeGeGe no Kitarō appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble. Kitarō makes an appearance in Yo-kai Watch Shadowside the Movie: The Return of the Oni King.
Characters from Inuyasha appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Kamen Rider appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Professor Layton appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Urusei Yatsura appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Magi appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Fantasy Life appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Ranma ½ appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Duel Masters appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Characters from Beyblade appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.
Mii Plaza includes a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Yo-Kai Watch.
Yo-Kai Watch Dance: Just Dance Special Version is a crossover between both series.
Music from Yo-Kai Watch was added to maimai in the maimai PiNK version.
Monopoly Junior: Yo-kai Watch Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
Yo-Kai Sangokushi is a format crossover between both series.
An episode of The Cat Mario Show promoting the release of Yo-Kai Watch featured a character from the series.

Thirteen Yokai from Yo-Kai Watch appear as minions in Final Fantasy XIV, during an event from July 26th to October 3rd, 2016, while Yo-Kai Watch 3 features a Yokai based on Moogle, and one riding a Chocobo from the Final Fantasy series.
Nintendo Badge Arcade features badges from the Yo-Kai Watch series.
Jinbanyan from Yo-Kai Watch appears in White Cat Tennis as part of its 1st Anniversary Gacha.
A mecha version of Jibanyan appears in Armored Girls.
Everybody's Golf features costumes based on Yo-Kai Watch as part of a Level-5 Collaboration event.
Characters from The Seven Deadly Sins appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble.

Characters from Yo-Kai Watch appeared in Puzzle & Dragons and Puzzle & Dragon Radar (with various characters appearing as leaders) during special collaborations, while characters from Puzzle & Dragons appeared in Yo-Kai Watch World during other collaborations.
Cells at Work! characters appear in Yo-Kai Sangokushi: Kunitori Wars as part of a special collaboration.

Eight members of Hololive Japan appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble as part of a collaboration event, while a character resembling and voiced by Korone makes a brief cameo in episode 94 of Yo-kai Watch♪.
Jibanyan from Yo-Kai Watch makes an appearance in Megaton Musashi X as part of a special collaboration.
Several characters from KonoSuba appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble as part of a collaboration event.
Characters from Frieren: Beyond Journey's End appear in Yo-kai Watch: Wibble Wobble as part of a collaboration event.

Yogi Bear.description: Yogi Bear debuted in a segment on The Huckleberry Hound Show; Huckleberry Hound appears in a number of Yogi Bear shows and movies; Yogi and Boo Boo Bear appear in The Good, The Bad, and the Huckleberry Hound.
Yogi Bear and Boo Boo appear in the Flintstones episode "Swedish Visitors".
Yogi Bear meet The Three Stooges in Yogi Bear and the Three Stooges Meet the Mad, Mad, Mad Dr. No-No.
Top Cat characters have appeared in several Yogi Bear shows and movies; Yogi Bear is seen on a comic book in the Top Cat episode "King For A Day".
Magilla Gorilla appears in Yogi's Ark Lark.
Peter Potamus and So-So appear in several Yogi Bear shows and movies.
Lambsy Divey appears in Yogi's Ark Lark.
Touché Turtle and Dum Dum appear in several Yogi Bear shows and movies.

Yogi Bear.game: Lippy The Lion and Hardy Har Har
Yogi Bear.description: Lippy the Lion and Hardy Har Har appear in several Yogi Bear shows and movies.
Quick Draw McGraw has appeared in several Yogi Bear shows.
Characters from Yogi Bear appear in Laff-A-Lympics.
Grape Ape appears in the Yogi's Space Race episode "Nebuloc - Prehistoric Planet".
Buzz Conroy and Frankenstein Jr. appear in the Yogi's Space Race episode "Race Through the Planet of the Monsters".
Yogi, Boo Boo and Snagglepuss from Yogi Bear appear in Casper's First Christmas.
Dick Dastardly and Muttley from Wacky Races appear as antagonists in Yogi's Treasure Hunt and Yo Yogi!.
A Yogi Bear toy is shown in episode 2129 of Sesame Street.
In the Full House episode "Return of Grandma" Yogi Bear is mentioned.
Yogi Bear appears in A Pup Named Scooby-Doo.
Yogi Bear and Ranger Smith appear on a TV screen in a The Further Adventures of SuperTed episode.
Loopy De Loop appears in Yo Yogi!.
In Stay Tuned there is a there is a reference to Yogi Bear in the form of “Yogi Beer”, a commercial concerning beer for children.
Yogi Bear and Boo-Boo also appear with the dogs in the Super Secret Secret Squirrel episode "Scirocco Mole", also as game show contestants.
Characters from Yogi Bear appear in I Am Weasel in the episode "I Am My Lifetime".
A corpse looking like Yogi Bear appears in Pico vs. Bear.
The Game Boy Color port of Pop n' Pop was altered into Yogi Bear: Great Balloon Blast for its North American release.

Yogi and Boo Boo from Yogi Bear appear in the Harvey Birdman episode "Death By Chocolate", with Boo Boo later becoming a recurring character in the series; Yakky Doodle appears in the Harvey Birdman episodes "Gone Efficien...t" and "Identity Theft".
Yogi Bear appears in the Powerpuff Girls episode "Shotgun Wedding".
In Little Britain, a character says to another that they’d better make sure the address on his card to Huggy Bear is right or else it might go to Yogi Bear.
Yogi and Boo Boo from Yogi Bear make cameos in the Duck Dodgers episode "K-9 Quarry".
Hanna-Barbera UNO is a format crossover that features Yogi Bear characters.
In Jimmy Timmy Power Hour, when Jimmy says he was not Timmy, Sanjay claims to be Yogi Bear.
In Jimmy Timmy Power Hour, when Jimmy says he was not Timmy, Sanjay claims to be Yogi Bear.

Yogi Bear.game: The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy
Yogi Bear.description: Characters from Yogi Bear appear in The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy.
Yogi Bear appears in the Johnny Bravo episode "Johnny Makeover".
Yogi Bear is referenced by Dean Winchester in Supernatural season 1 episode "Wendigo".

When Hermes was controlling the bear using his staff in the Class of the Titans episode "The Trojan Horse", he joked by telling it to find a picnic basket or park ranger. This is most likely a play on the popular cartoon "Yogi Bear".
Yogi Bear and Boo-Boo appear in the Family Guy episode "Hell Comes to Quahog".
Yogi Bear is mentioned in Bee Movie.
Yogi Bear is mentioned in The Thick of It.
Yogi Bear is parodied in the MAD sketch "Law & Ogre".
In the episode Paper Pete, when Pete showed Finn the Teddy Bear Joke Book, the characters on the cover resembles Yogi Bear, Boo-Boo and the Ranger from Yogi Bear.
Yogi is mentioned in the New Girl episode: "Fancyman: Part 2".
Happy Feet, Cats & Dogs: Revenge of Kitty Galore and Yogi Bear have been released on DVD together.
Happy Feet, Cats & Dogs: Revenge of Kitty Galore and Yogi Bear have been released on DVD together.
In The World’s End, the phrase "Let's Boo-Boo" is derived from Boo-Boo from Yogi Bear.
Yogi Bear appears in "Fun Dead".
Ranger Smith appears in Clássicos do Cinema - Turma da Mônica #48.
A character looking like Snagglepuss appears in a Heathcliff comic strip.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews “Yogi Bear (2010)”.

Yooka-Laylee.description: The pre-order "All-Stars" pack for Worms W.M.D. includes masks of Yooka-Laylee characters.
Yooka-Laylee is a spiritual successor to Banjo-Kazooie.
Shovel Knight appears as a character in the game Yooka-Laylee. A costume based on Shovel Knight also appears in Yooka-Replaylee.
Yooka-Laylee is a playable character in Brawlout.
Yooka & Laylee appear as guest characters in Mighty Fight Federation.
Yooka and Laylee from Yooka-Laylee make a cameo appearance in Demon Turf.
Yooka-Laylee appears as an assist character in Jitsu Squad.
Trowzer appears as a guest character in Clive 'N' Wrench.
Skins based on Yooka-Laylee appear in Fall Guys.
Yooka and Laylee appear as playable characters in Dunk Dunk.

Yosaku.description: Yosaku is included as a minigame in the NGPC game The King of Fighters: Battle de Paradise.
Arino plays the Cassette Vision game Kikori no Yosaku during the Aces of Hardware that Won't Appear segment.

Yoshi.description: The Yoshi series is a spinoff of the Mario series; the games Mario & Yoshi, Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island and Yoshi's Island: Super Mario Advance 3 are part of both series.
Mario uses the Super Scope in Yoshi's Safari.
Yoshi makes an appearance in Donkey Kong Country 2; a baby version of Donkey Kong, called Baby Donkey Kong, is playable in Yoshi's Island DS.
Yoshi no Panepon is a crossover between the two series.
The comic Blast Corps in Yoshis Knallkekse is a crossover between the two series.
Dr. Light from Mega Man makes a cameo in the comic Blast Corps in Yoshis Knallkekse.

The "Modern" versions of Vermin in Game & Watch Gallery 2, of Egg, Greenhouse, and Turtle Bridge in Game & Watch Gallery 3 and of Mario's Cement Factory in Game & Watch Gallery Advance feature elements from Yoshi games.
Croc: Legend of the Gobbos was originally meant to be a Yoshi game, but was then changed into an original IP.
Pikachu's name can be seen written on walls in Yoshi's Story.
A picture of Yoshi and Baby Mario referencing Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island appears in Game Boy Camera.
The Boo Blah from Yoshi's Island appears as an enemy in The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX.
Yoshi and places from the Yoshi series are featured in all Super Smash Bros. games.
Picross NP Vol. 2 includes images from the Yoshi series.
Yoshi appears in "Freeze Frame" and other N-Gang episodes.
Nintendo Puzzle Collection includes a remake of Yoshi's Cookie.
The box for Yoshi's Island can be seen in Dragon Ball Z: The Legacy of Goku II.
Nintendo UNO is a format crossover that features Yoshi's appearance from Yoshi's Story.
The tech demo for Yoshi Touch & Go was called Balloon Trip.
Musics from the Yoshi series are featured in Daigasso! Band Brothers.
Dance Dance Revolution: Mario Mix includes a track from Yoshi's Cookie.
Super Princess Peach takes many elements from Yoshi's Island.
Puzzle Mode of Tetris DS has a Yoshi's Cookie theme. Additionally the Western release of Yoshi no Panepon uses the name "Tetris Attack".

Baby Wario is playable in Yoshi's Island DS, while Wario characters directly interact with the "Yoshi's Story" microgame in WarioWare: Get It Together!; there also are other minor references between the two series.
A child looking like a baby Olimar makes an appearance in Yoshi's Island DS.
Files based on Yoshi's Island DS were obtainable by completing a level in UPIXO in Action: Mission in Snowdriftland.
Itadaki Street DS and Itadaki Street Wii feature references to the Yoshi series.
On the cover of Art Academy is shown a drawing of Yoshi.
Yoshi Egg and Yoshi hat head items appear in the shop.
Yoshi has been a subject for Death Battle!
Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games features a stage from Yoshi's Story; a Yoshi-themed zone also appears as a DLC in Sonic Lost World.
Metal Gear Solid: Snake Eater 3D features Yoshi dolls.
Nintendo Land features a minigame based on the Yoshi series.
The titular character from Era's Adventures 3D is based on Yoshi.
Mii Plaza features  a Puzzle Swap puzzle based on Yoshi's New Island.
Goat Simulator features a modifier called "Yoshi Goat", that lets the goat eat things and lay eggs.
Nintendo Badge Arcade features badges based on Yoshi's Woolly World.
Scanning an Amiibo in Amiibo Tap: Nintendo's Greatest Bits can give you access to playing a demo of Yoshi
Yoshi's Woolly World features Yoshi designs based on Inklings, unlocked by using the respective amiibo.
Poochi & Yoshi's Woolly World features Yoshi designs based on Animal Crossing characters, unlocked by using the respective amiibo.
Poochi & Yoshi's Woolly World features a Yoshi design based on Waddle Dee, unlocked by using the respective amiibo.
"Something About Yoshi's Island"  and "Something About Yoshi's Story" are parodies of Yoshi's Island and Yoshi's Story respectively.
Yoshi has been a subject for DBX.
Yoshi's Crafted World features cosmetics based on Nintendo Labo.
Yoshi can be seen in Animation vs. Super Mario Bros.
Petal Crash's gameplay takes inspiration from Yoshi's Cookie. Additionally, there are multiple other references to the Yoshi's Cookie.

Yoshi.game: Don't Toy with Me, Miss Nagatoro
Yoshi.description: The character Yoshi in a fantasy segment of Episode 6 of Don't Toy with Me, Miss Nagatoro appears out of an egg similar to Nintendo’s Yoshi.

Young Sheldon.description: Young Sheldon is a spin-off to The Big Bang Theory.
Ghost is mentioned in the Young Sheldon episode "Crisis Of Faith And Octopus Aliens".
ALF made an appearance in the ending credits of the Young Sheldon episode “A Race of Superhumans and a Letter to Alf”.
Melissa and George Cooper watch Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles in the episode "Quirky Eggheads and Texas Snow Globes".
Sheldon reads the Lord of the Rings triology.
Young Sheldon was mentioned in the Family Guy episode "Disney's The Reboot".
WarGames is mentioned in the Young Sheldon episode "Pongo Pygmaeus And A Culture That Encourages Spitting".
Georgie shows Missy Footloose in the Young Sheldon episode “Crappy Frozen Ice Cream and an Organ Grinder's Monkey”.
Sheldon mentioned The Simpsons in the Young Sheldon episode “A Pager, a Club and a Cranky Bag of Wrinkles”.
Missy watches Beauty and the Beast in the movie theater, which based on setting is most likely the Disney version, in the Young Sheldon episode “ A Virus, Heartbreak and a World of Possibilities”.
Hook is mentioned in the Young Sheldon episode "Money Laundering And A Cascade Of Hormones".
Connie and Dale watch Dinosaurs in the Young Sheldon episode “A Frat Party, a Sleepover and the Mother of All Blisters”.
Sheldon watches 90210 in the Young Sheldon episode  “A German Folk Song and an Actual Adult”.

Your Name..description: Taiko no Tatsujin Plus and later games in the series feature a music track from Your Name.
There's a reference to the poster of the anime film Your Name in episode 1 of Pop Team Epic.
Taki Tachibana and Mitsuha Miyamizu from Your Name appear in Weathering with You.
Your Name. is mentioned in Chapter 117 of Me & Roboco.

Ys.description: A parody of Ys called "Sauce" is featured within Segagaga.
Adol, Leah, and Feena from Ys I: Ancient Ys Vanished appear as characters in Vantage Master Online.
Ys Fortune is a format crossover featuring gameplay from Cleopatra Fortune but with Isha from Ys VI: The Ark of Napishtim replacing Patrako.
3D Dot Game Heroes features a loading screen based on the Ys series.
Ys vs. Trails in the Sky: Alternative Saga is a crossover between Ys and The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky.
Taiko no Tatsujin V Version, Taiko no Tatsujin White Version and Taiko no Tatsujin Plus feature a music track from Ys I & II Chronicles.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round features DLC costumes of characters from the Ys series as part of the "Falcom Mashup" costume set.
Ys VIII characters appear in Crusaders Quest for a collaboration event.
Music and skins based on Ys appears in DJMAX RESPECT V as part of the Falcom Pack DLC.

Yu-Gi-Oh.description: There's an entire series of Yu-Gi-Oh cards based around characters and items from Gradius.
Characters with Shiryu and Seiya's likeness make a brief appearance in Episode 54 of the Yu-Gi-Oh! anime.
Aitsu, Koitsu, Doitsu and Soitsu from Parodius appear as Yu-Gi-Oh cards.

The Yu-Gi-Oh cards "Getsu Fuhma" and "Ryu Kokki" are based on the protagonist and antagonist from Getsu Fuma Den.
In "Scary Board Game" Bo-bo-bo summons Yugi from his afro who summons Slifer The Sky Dragon.
Naruto characters appear in a crowd in Yu-Gi-Oh.
The Space Manbow enemy ship appears in the background of the "Space Manbo" Yu-Gi-Oh card, itself a reference as well.

Solid Snake from the Metal Gear series makes an uncredited cameo in Yu-Gi-Oh! 7 Trials to Glory: World Championship Tournament 2005, while the "Tactical Espionage Expert" Yu-Gi-Oh card is based on Solid Snake.
Yu-Gi-Oh is mentioned in Are We There Yet?
The Yu-Gi-Oh cards "Infernalvania" and "Vampire Hunter" ("Vampire Killer" in Japan) are references to the Castlevania series.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Tobikkiri! Anime Special and Taiko no Tatsujin V Version feature a music track from Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters GX.
Yugi is a playable character in the game.
The Hi Hi Puffy AmiYumi episode In the Cards focuses on “Stu-Pi-Doh” which is a spoof of Yu-Gi-Oh.
The Flintlock ship and its weapon the Flint from Xexex appear as Yu-Gi-Oh cards.
In The Fairly OddParents episode The End of the Universe-ity, one of the sailors that appeared at the end has a similar appearance to Bandit Keith.
The Lord British ship from Salamander appears as a Yu-Gi-Oh card.
Yu-Gi-Oh! is parodied in the MAD sketch "Grey's in Anime".
Linkara reviews Chapter 2 of Yu-Gi-Oh.
In the episode Hug Wolf, the table in the library where Jake found the book has a symbol like the Millennium Eye from Yu-Gi-Oh!. The episode Card Wars features a reference to Yu-Gi-Oh.
Episodes 1 and 9 feature references to Yu-Gi-Oh.
Episode 40 of Yo-Kai Watch features a reference to Yu-Gi-Oh .
Yu-Gi-Oh is parodied in Les Kassos.
Monster Hunter X features a downloadable costume from Yu-Gi-Oh.
Yu-Gi-Oh is parodied in multiple Daitomodachi episodes.
Monopoly: Yu-Gi-Oh Edition is a format crossover between the two series.
Characters from Yu-Gi-Oh are parodied in the Cell Vs episode "Cell Vs Yami Yugi".
The Monstermon cards in Kindergarten are modeled off of Yu-Gi-Oh cards.
Characters from Yu-Gi-Oh appeared in Monster Strike during a special collaboration.
Yu-Gi-Oh is parodied in multiple Perfect Cell Vs episodes.
Yu-Gi-Oh is parodied in the MeatCanyon episode "ITS TIME TO D-D-D-DUEL" and the Papa Meat episode "POV: You're About to Duel".
Characters from Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters appeared in Puzzle & Dragons during special collaborations.
The Pot of Greed is based on the card of the same name from Yu-Gi-Oh.
Magnificus' gameplay style in Inscryption is based on the Disc Duel style from Yu-Gi-Oh, and the creature Edaxio is a reference to Exodia and his summoning method.

Shugomaru gets distracted by a fresh-pack of Yu-Gi-Oh cards in Chapter 3 of Protect Me, Shugomaru!.  Later chapters feature different Yu-Gi-Oh references.  Also, the Pendulum Machine makes a physical appearance in Chapter 20 of Protect Me, Shugomaru!

Cards for Characters from the Power Pros series appeared in Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters during collaboration events. Additionally, the Yu-Gi-Oh card "Ultimate Baseball Kid" is inspired on the Power Pros series.
The Nostalgia Critic reviews “Yu-Gi-Oh”.

One of Sophie's outfits in "👗School Picnic outfit ideas!!🧺" is based on Dark Magician from Yu-Gi-Oh; Additionally, there are trading cards in "🚌I’m Just a Kid & 7 years later!!" and "🔮The Cards Decide Her Love Ending!!" that look similar to those from Yu-Gi-Oh. that look similar to those from Yu-Gi-Oh.
The worlds of Hello Kitty and Friends and Yu-Gi-Oh crossed over as part of a collaboration for McDonald's Happy Meal toys.
Kicks based on  Yu-Gi-Oh! appear in Fortnite.

YuYu Hakusho.description: Characters similar to Street Fighter characters appear in the crowd in Yu Yu Hakusho's episode "The Search Begins".
There is a minor visual reference to the polygonal look of early Virtua Fighter titles in chapter 168 of the Yu Yu Hakusho manga.
Yusuke is a playable character in the series.
In the episode Karate Island, Sandy's and Udon's muscle growth is loosely based on Toguro's 100% muscle growth in the manga and anime series Yu Yu Hakusho.
Bennett The Sage reviews “Yu Yu Hakusho: The Poltergeist Report”.
The Toguro Brothers from Yu Yu Hakusho make a brief cameo in Chapter 118 of the Assassination Classroom manga.
Hiei has been a subject for DBX.
Characters from Yu Yu Hakusho appeared in Monster Strike during special collaborations.
Yusuke Urameshi from Yu Yu Hakusho is parodied in the Cell Vs episode "Cell Vs Yusuke".
Characters from Yu Yu Hakusho appeared in Puzzle & Dragons and Puzzle & Dragons Radar (with various characters appearing as leaders) during special collaborations.
Yu Yu Hakusho is parodied in the MeatCanyon episode "URAMESHI".
The Nostalgia Critic's friends review Yu Yu Hakusho.
Yu Yu Hakusho characters make an appearance in Langrisser Mobile as part of a special collaboration.
Universal Fighting System includes a set of cards based on Yu Yu Hakusho.
Hiei from Yu Yu Hakusho has been a subject for Death Battle!
Characters from Yu Yu Hakusho appeared in Unison League during a special collaboration.
Yu Yu Hakusho characters appear in Grand Summoners for a collaboration event.
Bondo mentions Yu Yu Hakusho in Chapter 7 of Me & Roboco.
Botan's hair appears in the shop.
Yu Yu Hakusho characters appear in Kotodaman for a collaboration event.
Union Arena features cards based on Yu Yu Hakusho.

Wario Land II features a treasure based on the Big Face item from Yume Kojo: Doki Doki Panic.
Arino plays the Disk System game Yume Kojo: Doki Doki Panic in episode 15.
Birdo's trophy in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U mentions Doki Doki Panic.
Angry Video Game Nerd II: ASSimilation features a level called "Dookie Dookie Panic".

Yume Nikki.description: Madotsuki is a playable character in Indie Action.
An icon for Yume Nikki appears on the Entity's desktop in the original version of OneShot.
The Ao Oni makes a cameo appearance in Yume Nikki: Dream Diary.
Graffiti of Uboa can be found in Chapter 3 of FAITH: The Unholy Trinity.

Yume-100.description: Characters from Ensemble Stars! and 100 Sleeping Princes & the Kingdom of Dreams appear in each other’s game as special collaborations.
Characters from Black Butler Book of the Atlantic appear in 100 Sleeping Princes & the Kingdom of Dreams as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Yuri on Ice appear in 100 Sleeping Princes & the Kingdom of Dreams as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Fullmetal Alchemist appear in 100 Sleeping Princes & the Kingdom of Dreams as part of a special collaboration.
Characters from Bungo Stray Dogs appear in Yume 100 as part of a collaboration.

Yuri on Ice.description: Yuri on Ice is mentioned by TROLLTRACE.com in the South Park episode "The End of Serialization as We Know It".  Also, in the season finale of Yuri on Ice, there is a character that dresses up like Eric Cartman.
Characters from Yuri on Ice appeared in Rage of Bahamut as part of a special collaboration.
There's an official plush for Yurio in a Hello Kitty outfit.
Characters from Yuri on Ice appear in 100 Sleeping Princes & the Kingdom of Dreams as part of a special collaboration.
Yuri Katsuki from Yuri on Ice is mentioned in AI: The Somnium Files.
Music from Yuri on Ice can be played in WACCA.

YuruYuri.description: Characters and music from YuruYuri appear in Miracle Girls Festival.
Yuru Yuri characters appear in Re:Stage! Prism Step for a special collaboration.
Music from YuruYuri can be played in O.N.G.E.K.I. Summer Plus.

Yuyuki.description: Donbe, Kintaro and Tengu from Shin Onigashima make a cameo in Yuyuki.
Chao from Yuyuki appears in the Japanese version of Kirby's Dream Land 2 and with Goku in Kirby's Dream Land 3.
In Daigasso! Band Brothers DX, a theme from the game is played when the player chooses the Synth Bell.
Part Time UFO includes a costume based on Goku from Yuyuki.
Goku & Chao from Yuyuki appear as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

Y\u014dkai D\u014dch\u016bki.description: Tarosuke from Yōkai Dōchūki is a selectable character in the Japanese version of Rock 'n Ball.
The float parade bonus stage in Marvel Land features a float of Tarosuke and Monmotaro from Yōkai Dōchūki.
Valkyrie appears as an announcer in Kyūkai Dōchūki, and also appears among the crowd in stadiums of the Japan League.
Rick Taylor from Splatterhouse appears among the crowd in Japan League stadiums from Kyūkai Dōchūki.
A banner ad featuring Acha from Toy Pop appears in the Japan League stadiums from Kyūkai Dōchūki.
A banner ad featuring Wagan appears in the Japan League stadiums from Kyūkai Dōchūki.

The Namco Stars team from Family Statium is unlockable in Kyukai Dochuki, while Tarosuke from Shadow Land appears as a player in Famista Online, Pro Baseball Famista 2011 and its sequels, and Famista Dream Match; additionally one of the players in the Namco Stars team in Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium '87 and its sequels is called "Tarosuke".
Statues from the Spirit World in Yōkai Dōchūki make an appearance in Tales of Eternia.
Taiko no Tatsujin: Atsumare! Matsuri da!! Yondaime and later games in the series feature a music track from Yōkai Dōchūki.
Namco × Capcom features Torosuke from Yōkai Dōchūki as a playable character.
Arino plays the TurboGrafx-16 port of Yōkai Dōchūki in episode 36 of GameCenter CX.
The music theme "Mahou o Kakete!" from Famison 8-bit iDOLM@STER 03 is a remix of the main theme from Yōkai Dōchūki.
The Namco Special set in Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan Wii Deluxe includes a puzzle of an Oni from Yōkai Dōchūki with Tarosuke serving as assistant.
Tarosuke from Yōkai Dōchūki appears as a summon in Keroro RPG.
Tarosuke from Yōkai Dōchūki is a playable character in Namco Chronicle.
Tarosuke from Yōkai Dōchūki appears in Episode 9 of Mappy: The Beat.
A music track from Yōkai Dōchūki is featured in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.
Yōkai Dōchūki characters appear in The Knights of Avalon during the second Namco collaboration event.
Sprites from Yōkai Dōchūki appear as treasures in Treasure Hakkutsu! Diggers.
Yōkai Dōchūki is included in Namcot Collection.

A banner ad featuring Pac-Man appears in the Japan League stadiums from Kyūkai Dōchūki, and images of Pac-Man with a purple tie appear in after-match results; while a theme featuring characters from Yokai Dochuki appears in Pac-Man 99.
Picross S Namco Legendary Edition includes puzzles based off Yōkai Dōchūki.

ZONE (Zink Animation).description: One of the Indiegogo backer characters in the background of the Glass Canopy stage in Skullgirls is ZONE-Tan. One of the alternate color palettes in Skullgirls is based on ZONE-Tan.
ZONE-Tan is a playable character in Shady Lewd Kart.
ZONE-Tan has appeared next to Otachan multiple times.
ZONE-tan appears in the background of the Week 5 mall in Friday Night Funkin'.

Zack & Wiki.game: Princess Tomato in the Salad Kingdom
Zack & Wiki.description: The game is inspired by Princess Tomato in the Salad Kingdom and Dezeni Land.
One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the Vulgus sprite from Vulgus.

One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the Super Joe sprite from Commando.

One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the Arthur sprite from Ghouls 'n Ghosts, and one of the Bonelich's minigames songs is the Ghost 'n Goblins graveyard theme.
One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the Billy Bob sprite from Gun.Smoke.
One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the Lonely Astronaut sprite from Section Z.

One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the car sprite from The Speed Rumbler, and one of the Bonelich's minigames songs is the game's stage 1 theme.
Two of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure are trophies of the Lt. Henry and Mobi-chan sprites from Side Arms.

One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the Super Joe sprite from the Arcade version Bionic Commando, and one of the Bonelich's minigames songs is the game's stage 1 theme.

One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a Blodia mugshot from Armored Warriors.
One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a trophy of the P-38 Lightning sprite from 1941: Counter Attack.
One of the mysterious treasures in Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure is a Captain Commando mugshot.
A poster of Zack & Wiki is a collectible in the "Capcom Heroes" mode from Dead Rising 4: Frank's Big Package.

Zangeki no Reginleiv.description: Frey and Freya from Zangeki no Reginleiv appear as a spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; they are also a trophy in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U.

Zatch Bell!.description: Taiko no Tatsujin: Waku Waku anime Matsuri and later games in the series feature music tracks from Zatch Bell!.
Kiyo & Zatch, Brago & Sherry, Zeno & Dufort, and Victoream & Mohawk Ace appeared in Puzzle & Dragons during the second and third Weekly Shonen Magazine collaboration events.

Dale Davis from Zeke and Luther appears in the Pair of Kings episode "An Ice Girl for Boomer".

Zenless Zone Zero.description: Characters from Zenless Zone Zero appear in the Siege Tales episode "Zhu Yuan: Guardian girl of Zenless Zone Zero" as part of a sponsorship from miHoYo.
Characters from Zenless Zone Zero appear in the Kakyoin Waifu Connoisseur episode "GIVE ME THE DENNIES OR SHE GETS IT!" as part of a sponsorship from miHoYo.
Zenless Zone Zero is parodied in the Perfect Cell Vs episode "The Perfect Gacha Addiction".
Characters from Zenless Zone Zero appear in the Anime Weebs episode  "POV: The Anime forces itself on you" as part of a sponsorship from miHoYo.
Sophie and Maru interact with Yixuan from Zenless Zone Zero in the Sophie's Magic Diary short "🥋Sophie’s Special Training!!".

Zeno Clash.description: Zeno Clash is a mountable game for Garry's Mod and features characters and locations from the series.
A Rock of Ages crossover game mode was added as a free content update in Zeno Clash II.

Zero Escape.description: The North American version of 999: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors features a reference to the Zelda TV series.
Costumes based on Sigma Klin, Phi and Zero III from Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward appear in RESEARCH and DESTROY as part of the Costume Bundle DLC.

Zero Wing.description: Zero Wing is referenced in the Futurama episode "Anthology Of Interest II".
The English version of Phantasy Star Universe references the "All your base are belong to us" line from Zero Wing.

The Quest in Final Fantasy XI: Wings of the Goddess "A Nation On The Brink" features the dialogue "Then all your Jeuno are belong to us!" and "You are on way to destruction", referencing dialogue from Zero Wing.
The third episode of Sam & Max: The Devil's Playhouse, titled They Stole Max's Brain!, features a reference to the phrase "All your base are belong to us!"
Super Scribblenauts and its sequels feature the spawnable object "All Your Base Are Belong To Us".
The English version of Xenoblade Chronicles references the "for great justice" line from Zero Wing.
